128fn scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
129    scheduler_turn: u64,
130    virtual_nanoseconds: u64,
131    internal_io_poll: bool,
132    runtime_maps_read: bool,
133) -> String {
134    crate::detlog::record_suffix(crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommit {
135        scheduler_turn,
136        virtual_nanoseconds,
137        internal_io_poll,
138        runtime_maps_read,
139    })
140}

162/// The response from the scheduler that wakes back up a guest thread after a request.
163#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
164pub enum SchedResponse {
165    /// Keep running.
166    Go(Option<SchedValue>),
167
168    /// Keep running, and nothing else can run (`Scheduler::nothing_else_can_run`):
169    /// the answer to a polling turn that asked for it
170    /// (`Resources::waits_until_nothing_else_can_run`). The payload is `Go`'s.
171    GoAlone(Option<SchedValue>),
172
173    /// The guest was interupted by a signal while waiting on the scheduler, and will now execute
174    /// the handler.
175    Signaled(Option<Vec<SigWrapper>>),
176    ObserveSignal(Box<parked::AlarmControl>),
177    /// The original qualified in-guest sleep must stage its consumed SIGALRM.
178    InGuestFatalAlarm,
179    // TODO: Time to exit, or an exit is already under way
180    // Exit,
181}

183#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialOrd, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
184/// A value that the scheduler returns to the guest when resuming.  This is weakly typed in that it
185/// is only relevant to certain scheduler requests, and its meaning is dependent on what was
186/// requested of the scheduler.
187///
188/// It can be used to have the scheduler EMULATE behaviors (syscalls) that would normally happen in
189/// the guest. The first application for this is futexes.
190pub enum SchedValue {
191    /// The action timed out while waiting on the scheduler.
192    TimeOut,
193    /// A signal ended a futex wait (`SchedResponse::Signaled`), as distinct from a
194    /// wakeup or from the `EINTR` value some non-signal early returns carry
195    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>). It carries the
196    /// signals the scheduler committed to the waiter at the wake, as a kernel
197    /// signal set, which the waiter's own check may then count although it
198    /// holds them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005>).
199    Signaled(u64),
200    // TODO(T137799529) make this more strongly typed, an enum for different scenarios:
201    Value(u64),
202    /// The answer to a futex requeue (`FutexAction::RequeueRequest`): how many
203    /// waiters it woke and how many it moved to the other futex.
204    Requeued {
205        /// Waiters woken.
206        woken: u64,
207        /// Waiters moved onto the target futex.
208        moved: u64,
209    },
210}

257/// A thread waiting on a futex, including the bitset accepted by wake operations.

261    response: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
262    bitset: u32,
263    /// Where to read the kernel's view of this waiter's signal state, on a backend

269/// What a precise-mode futex waiter's backend tells the scheduler about the
270/// waiter's signals when the wait begins
271/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
272///
273/// Only the mask is captured. It belongs to the waiting thread, and only that
274/// thread can change it, so it cannot change while the thread is parked. The
275/// dispositions belong to the whole process and a sibling can change them with
276/// `rt_sigaction` at any time, so they are NOT captured here: the scheduler reads
277/// them from the kernel at the moment it commits a wake
278/// (`Scheduler::parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
279#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
280pub struct FutexSignalWatch {
281    /// Kernel sigset of the signals the waiter's mask leaves unblocked, without
282    /// the backend's own preemption signal.
283    pub unblocked: u64,
284    /// Whether a default `SIGTSTP`, `SIGTTIN`, or `SIGTTOU` leaves the wait parked:
285    /// set for a timed futex wait, whose restart would not keep its deadline
286    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`). Fixed by the call, so it
287    /// cannot change while the waiter is parked.
288    pub defers_default_stops: bool,
289    /// The waiter's process, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
290    pub pid: i32,
291    /// The waiter's thread, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
292    pub tid: i32,
293}

295/// Which processes a host-timed signal source can signal once a guest arms it

297#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
298pub enum HostTimedSignalScope {
299    /// Only the process of the thread that armed it.
300    Caller,
301    /// Any process of the container: the receiver can be another process, a
302    /// process group, or a process Hermit does not track.
303    Container,
304}

306/// The state of one other thread of a process, as a process-directed signal
307/// that a thread sends to its own process reads it
308/// (`Scheduler::own_process_signal_inputs`,
309/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034>).
310#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
311pub enum SiblingSignalState {
312    /// Its exit is granted: it never resumes guest code.
313    ExitGranted,
314    /// It runs or sleeps outside the schedule (a real kernel sleep: external
315    /// I/O, `rt_sigsuspend`, a vfork parent), so the moment it next dequeues
316    /// is host-timed.
317    OutOfSchedule,
318    /// It is stopped at a request, parked in a precise futex wait or polling
319    /// `rt_sigtimedwait`, with the mask a signal sent now meets; `None` when
320    /// that mask is unknown.
321    InSchedule(Option<u64>),
322}

324/// What the scheduler knows, in a thread's own turn, about the inputs to a
325/// process-directed signal that the thread sends to its own process
326/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034>). Every field is a function
327/// of the schedule.
328#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
329pub struct OwnProcessSignalInputs {
330    /// Every other thread of the process, in thread-ID order.
331    pub siblings: Vec<(DetTid, SiblingSignalState)>,
332    /// The host-timed signal record for the sender (`host_timed_signals`).
333    pub host_timed: u64,
334    /// The exit signals, other than 0 and SIGCHLD, of the process's unreaped
335    /// children, which the kernel sends itself at a host-timed moment.
336    pub foreign_exit_signals: u64,
337    /// Signals the scheduler sent to the process (`signal_guest`) that are
338    /// still in its shared queue (`ShdPnd`), so no thread has taken them yet.
339    pub undelivered_scheduler_signals: u64,
340    /// Whether an exec is in flight in the process (`exec_teardowns`).
341    pub exec_in_flight: bool,
342    /// Whether any guest has sent SIGSTKFLT, which Reverie also uses as its
343    /// timer marker (`Scheduler::record_guest_marker_signal`).
344    pub guest_marker_signal: bool,
345}

347/// The one-bit kernel sigset for a 1-based signal number, or 0 when out of range.
348pub(crate) fn kernel_signal_bit(raw_signal: i32) -> u64 {
349    if (1..=64).contains(&raw_signal) {
350        1_u64 << (raw_signal - 1)
351    } else {
352        0
353    }
354}
355
356/// The lowest signal number in the kernel sigset `set`, if any.
357pub(crate) fn first_signal(set: u64) -> Option<i32> {
358    (set != 0).then(|| set.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1)
359}

361/// Whether `signo` is SIGCONT or a stop signal. Generating SIGCONT flushes
362/// every pending stop signal, and generating a stop signal flushes SIGCONT,
363/// whoever sends it (`prepare_signal`), so a pending copy of one can never be
364/// proven a timer's own.
365fn is_job_control_signal(signo: i32) -> bool {
366    [
367        libc::SIGCONT,
368        libc::SIGSTOP,
369        libc::SIGTSTP,
370        libc::SIGTTIN,
371        libc::SIGTTOU,
372    ]
373    .contains(&signo)
374}

376/// The POSIX timer copies a successful exec flushes
377/// (`Scheduler::take_exec_timer_flush`; <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184>),
378/// as kernel sigsets. The exec's surviving thread takes each with a
379/// zero-timeout `rt_sigtimedwait` before its new image runs; a signal in both
380/// sets is taken twice, its own queue's copy first, as Linux dequeues them.
381#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
382pub struct ExecTimerFlush {
383    /// `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copies pending in the surviving thread's own queue.
384    pub own: u64,
385    /// `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copies pending in the process's shared queue.
386    pub shared: u64,
387}

389/// Every signal Linux sends because of a terminal, as a kernel sigset. Once a
390/// guest process may have the terminal as its controlling terminal, or be in
391/// the terminal's foreground process group, each can arrive at a moment set
392/// by host timing:
393///
394/// - SIGHUP and SIGCONT when the terminal hangs up, as when its other end
395///   closes, or when the session leader exits (`tty_vhangup_session`,
396///   `disassociate_ctty`).
397/// - SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the interrupt, quit and suspend
398///   characters (`isig`), sent to the foreground process group when the
399///   kernel processes the terminal's input, which it does on a kernel worker
400///   rather than inside the call that supplied the input.
401/// - SIGWINCH when the window size changes (`tty_do_resize`, which
402///   `pty_resize` reaches for a pseudoterminal), sent to the foreground
403///   process group: a terminal emulator outside the container changes the
404///   size when its user resizes the window.
405/// - SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU when a process of a background process group reads
406///   the terminal, or writes it or changes its settings while TOSTOP is set
407///   (`__tty_check_change`, `job_control`), sent to that process's group,
408///   which can hold a process Hermit does not schedule. Linux sends them
409///   inside the caller's call, so for a guest's own read or write the record
410///   holds them longer than needed.
411///
412/// The scheduler records the whole set at launch when the guest may start
413/// with a terminal (`startup_host_timed_signals`), and so does a guest call
414/// that gives a session a controlling terminal or names the terminal's
415/// foreground process group (`syscalls/files.rs`). From then on no gated wait
416/// ends for any of them, whoever sends it: each is held until the call
417/// returns, as before blocked waits decided interruption from the kernel's
418/// signal state (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>, and the
419/// round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
420/// interruption" of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
421pub(crate) fn terminal_signals() -> u64 {
422    [
423        libc::SIGHUP,
424        libc::SIGCONT,
425        libc::SIGINT,
426        libc::SIGQUIT,
427        libc::SIGTSTP,
428        libc::SIGWINCH,
429        libc::SIGTTIN,
430        libc::SIGTTOU,
431    ]
432    .into_iter()
433    .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal))
434}
435
436/// The signals recorded as host-timed for every process of the container
437/// before the guest's first instruction (`host_timed_signals_everywhere`):
438/// every signal a terminal sends (`terminal_signals`) when the guest may start
439/// with a terminal and blocked waits decide interruption from the kernel's
440/// signal state (`Config::guest_may_inherit_a_terminal`), and nothing
441/// otherwise. The guest makes no traced call that arms them, so no guest turn
442/// could record them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
443fn startup_host_timed_signals(cfg: &Config) -> u64 {
444    if cfg.backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption && cfg.guest_may_inherit_a_terminal {
445        terminal_signals()
446    } else {
447        0
448    }
449}

451/// Render an already-sorted thread list for a diagnostic, or `none`.
452fn render_tid_list(tids: &[DetTid]) -> String {
453    if tids.is_empty() {
454        "none".to_owned()
455    } else {
456        tids.iter()
457            .map(|t| format!("dtid {}", t))
458            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
459            .join(", ")
460    }
461}

463/// Deterministically pick one element from `choices` using the supplied PRNG,
464/// returning `None` for an empty slice. This is the single random-selection
465/// primitive used by the targeted-chaos scheduling points, so their choices stay
466/// reproducible under a fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
467fn chaos_pick<T: Copy>(prng: &mut Pcg64Mcg, choices: &[T]) -> Option<T> {
468    choices.choose(prng).copied()
469}
470
471fn take_matching_futex_waiters(waiters: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>, wake_mask: u32) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
472    let (matching, remaining) = std::mem::take(waiters)
473        .into_iter()
474        .partition(|waiter| waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0);
475    *waiters = remaining;
476    matching
477}

479/// The signals that wake a restartable internal IO poll at the drain, from the
480/// thread's kernel state (`state`), before the hold. Where the record of copies
481/// Linux discarded at send is kept (`records`, which equals
482/// `models_signal_targets`), a standard signal's fate was decided in the
483/// sender's turn: admission refused a discarded copy
484/// (`notify_signal_pending`), and a kept one wakes the poll whatever the
485/// disposition is now, since Linux's `TIF_SIGPENDING` is not cleared by a
486/// later flush. So a standard signal is filtered by the mask alone, never by
487/// the disposition read at the drain, which a sender's `SIG_IGN` in the same
488/// slice would otherwise turn against a wake Linux keeps (R2b-1 rule 1,
489/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273>). A real-time signal is
490/// outside the record (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4319>), so
491/// it keeps the disposition test. The backend's own preemption signal never
492/// wakes a poll.
493fn poll_wake_signals(state: &KernelSignalState, records: bool) -> u64 {
494    if !records {
495        return state.interrupting_wait(state.blocked, false);
496    }
497    let standard = discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS
498        & !kernel_signal_bit(reverie::PERF_EVENT_SIGNAL as libc::c_int);
499    (!state.blocked & standard)
500        | (state.interrupting_wait(state.blocked, false) & !discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS)
501}

503/// The kind of wait the drain of cross-task signals woke (`drain_woken_waiters`),

507    /// A parked precise-mode futex waiter.
508    FutexWaiter,
509    /// A restartable internal IO poll (`restartable_internal_io_signals`).
510    Poll,
511}

513/// A waiter the drain of cross-task signals woke, until its turn answers

515#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
516pub struct DrainWoken {
517    /// The kind of wait.

519    /// The scheduler sent the waiter a `SIGCHLD` at a commit point since the

523}

525/// Actions that are blocked on another internal action of the guest, such as a pipe communication,
526/// or are blocked on external conditions such as a network request.  These cannot consume a logical
527/// turn until a matching unblocking action is ready.
528///
529/// This structure will NOT include blocking operations that are implemented via polling.
530/// See NOTE [Blocking Syscalls via Internal Polling] in this folder.
531#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
532pub struct BlockedPool {
533    /// BLOCKED futex transactions, waiting for wakers. Multiple threads may be blocked on
534    /// the same futex.
535    ///
536    /// INVARIANT: because Futexes aren't currently modeled with `ResourceID`, a thread
537    /// waiting on a futex will have a request filled in `next_turns` but for zero resources.
538    pub futex_waiters: HashMap<FutexID, Vec<FutexWaiter>>,
539
540    /// Futex waiters whose deadlines expired and must receive `ETIMEDOUT` when scheduled.
541    /// Timed-out waiters are removed from `futex_waiters` before entering the run queue.
542    pub timed_out_futex_waiters: HashSet<DetTid>,
543
544    /// Threads whose next event is waiting on a point in time to proceed.
545    ///
546    /// This is sorted by soonest time of occurrence.
547    /// NOTE: futex waiters will ALSO appear in here if they have timeouts.
548    pub timed_waiters: TimedEvents,
549
550    /// Threads parked until a matching child process exits logically.
551    pub child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetTid, (DetPid, ChildWaitSpec)>,
552
553    /// Threads parked between logical process exit and a backend's final
554    /// physical-exit report.
555    pub physical_child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetPid, BTreeSet<DetTid>>,
556
557    /// Waiters whose deterministic physical-exit handoff is ready to commit.
558    pub physical_child_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
559
560    /// Blockers on external IO that are in the middle of executing (or have finished) and
561    /// are waiting for permission from the scheduler to resume.
562    ///
563    /// The protocol here is that the `(request,response)` pair (in `next_turns`) for
564    /// threads in `external_io_blockers` will have the request filled in with an
565    /// `BlockedExternalContinue` request when the thread is past its blocking action and
566    /// waiting for permission to resume. A failed operation governed by `BlockingVfork` instead
567    /// reports `VforkFailed`, which follows the same re-admission path after cancelling its
568    /// barrier. The request will stay empty while the thread is doing the blocking action. This is
569    /// different than the normal relationship
570    pub external_io_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
571
572    /// Threads executing the real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the runnable set.
573    /// These retain the kernel's atomic temporary-mask semantics, but unlike
574    /// arbitrary external IO they cannot complete without a signal.
575    pub rt_sigsuspend_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
576
577    /// The signal mask each thread in `external_io_blockers` or
578    /// `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` sleeps under, recorded when the scheduler
579    /// committed its blocking request: the call's own temporary mask
580    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`), or else the thread's mask read
581    /// while it was still stopped at that request. `None` records a mask that
582    /// could not be read. Such a thread runs outside the schedule, so its live
583    /// mask is host-timed; `kernel_sigchld_target` uses this record instead.
584    /// An entry lives exactly as long as the thread's blocking-pool entry.
585    pub out_of_scheduler_masks: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<u64>>,
586
587    /// Parents parked awaiting deterministic delivery of a host-async `SIGCHLD`.
588    ///
589    /// When a guest child process exits, the kernel raises `SIGCHLD` on the
590    /// parent at a moment decided purely by host timing. If the resulting
591    /// `InboundSignal` turn is committed as soon as it arrives, its position
592    /// races whatever guest work was already runnable -- classically a `make -jN`
593    /// jobserver `pselect6` continuation -- and `--strict --verify` diverges.
594    ///
595    /// Instead the parent is parked here, out of the run queue, and re-admitted
596    /// by `step2e_process_signal_deferred` only once no ordinary (non-poller)
597    /// guest work remains: the same deterministic-work-first policy that governs
598    /// `external_io_blockers`. The physical signal has already been delivered by
599    /// the kernel, so the handler's `wait4`/`waitpid` still reaps a real host
600    /// zombie and no synthetic signal is ever generated.
601    pub sigchld_deferred: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
602
603    /// Deferred `SIGCHLD` parents that `step2e_process_signal_deferred` has
604    /// re-admitted to the run queue, and threads whose `SIGCHLD` delivery the
605    /// scheduler already placed: a child-exit timer's commit of a deferred
606    /// delivery, and a thread sleeping outside the schedule that the
607    /// scheduler's `SIGCHLD` woke (`arm_signaled_background`). Their
608    /// `InboundSignal` turn must be granted rather than deferred (again) on the
609    /// turn the scheduler selects them.
610    pub sigchld_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
611
612    /// Threads whose `pause` or `nanosleep`, still queued or parked, the
613    /// scheduler woke for a signal it sent (`wake_signaled_guest`). That
614    /// synthetic `InboundSignal` turn is granted at once and consumes only this
615    /// mark; the real `SIGCHLD` delivery that may follow is admitted by its own
616    /// (`dequeue_sigchld`)
617    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126>).
618    pub woken_sleeps: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
619
620    /// Threads the scheduler woke, at a commit point, to take a `SIGCHLD` it
621    /// sent (`mark_placed_delivery`): a parked precise futex waiter whose wait
622    /// it interrupts, or a thread polling internal IO. The copy is
623    /// process-directed, and the kernel's `complete_signal` skips a
624    /// ptrace-stopped thread, so it goes to whichever thread resumes first:
625    /// step 3 resumes such a thread first, before any other, until its
626    /// delivery turn, while the copy is still pending and its mask does not
627    /// block it (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304>).
628    pub sigchld_takers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
629
630    /// Precise futex waiters and restartable internal IO polls the drain of
631    /// cross-task signals woke (`drain_pending_cross_task_signals`), until
632    /// their turn answers. A `SIGCHLD` in such a waiter's `WaitidSignals`
633    /// batch, put there by that wake or merged in later, is only a reason to
634    /// run, never a committed signal: `unblock_guest` leaves it out of the
635    /// answer, so the waiter's own check decides it, a futex waiter from the
636    /// schedule's record of a guest's private copy (`PrivatePending`), which
637    /// a flush clears, and a poll from the signals still pending at its turn.
638    /// A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sent since (`DrainWoken::scheduler_sent`) is
639    /// committed, and the answer names it
640    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132>,
641    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273>).
642    pub drain_woken_waiters: BTreeMap<DetTid, DrainWoken>,
643
644    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` that the
645    /// scheduler signaled at a committed point (`wake_signaled_guest`) while
646    /// they slept with no posted request. Their request was consumed when they
647    /// were backgrounded, so the scheduler cannot counterfeit one; it waits
648    /// for each one's own continuation (the InboundSignal its signal stop
649    /// posts) and requeues them all at the top of the next scheduler pass
650    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), so host delivery timing decides
651    /// only how long the scheduler spins, not where they enter the run queue.
652    pub signaled_background: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
653
654    /// Threads the scheduler signaled at a committed point while they were
655    /// still stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask
656    /// does not block the signal. The call's handler checked for a pending
657    /// signal before posting that request, so it could not see this one; the
658    /// thread's current mask may block it, so the kernel holds it pending until
659    /// the real `rt_sigsuspend` installs the temporary mask, and then delivers
660    /// it at once. Granting the request therefore arms the thread for the
661    /// release barrier (`arm_signaled_background`) as if the signal had been
662    /// sent one turn later, when it slept; otherwise the pool would hold a
663    /// sleeper the scheduler counts as unwakeable, and the next pass reports a
664    /// deadlock before the thread's signal stop is posted.
665    pub signaled_sigsuspend_requests: BTreeMap<DetTid, SigWrapper>,
666
667    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` whose call `hermit replay` serves
668    /// from the recording (`Resources::replay_served_from_log`). Such a call
669    /// cannot block, so `step2c_process_io_blockers` commits no turn until all
670    /// of them have finished, then readmits them, in thread order, before any
671    /// other background call. An entry lives exactly
672    /// as long as the thread's `external_io_blockers` entry.
673    pub replay_log_served: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
674}
675
676impl BlockedPool {
677    /// Returns true if there are NO blocked threads waiting outside the run-queue.
678    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
679        self.no_futex_waiters()
680            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
681            && self.child_waiters.is_empty()
682            && self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
683            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
684            && self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
685            && self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
686            && self.sigchld_deferred.is_empty()
687    }
688
689    /// True if there are no runnable threads, and the only blocked ones are externally-blocked.
690    fn only_external_blocked(&self) -> bool {
691        let has_external_wait = !self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
692            || !self.child_waiters.is_empty()
693            || !self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
694        self.no_futex_waiters()
695            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
696            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
697            && (has_external_wait || !self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty())
698    }
699
700    /// Returns true if there are zero threads blocked on futexes.
701    fn no_futex_waiters(&self) -> bool {
702        self.futex_waiters.iter().all(|(_, v)| v.is_empty())
703    }
704}
705
706/// Validate a request made by a thread executing outside the runnable set.
707/// A signal may interrupt a real blocking syscall before its ordinary
708/// continuation request is posted, so an inbound-signal request is ready too.
709/// `vfork` is excluded because a signal does not satisfy its child barrier.
710fn blocking_request_is_ready(
711    req: &Resources,
712    expected: ExternalOpId,
713    signal_can_complete: bool,
714) -> bool {
715    assert_eq!(req.resources.len(), 1);
716    let rsrc = req.resources.iter().next().unwrap().0;
717    match rsrc {
718        ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(op_id) => {
719            assert_eq!(*op_id, expected);
720            true
721        }
722        ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) if signal_can_complete => true,
723        other => panic!("expected external continue request, got {other:?}"),
724    }
725}
726
727/// Runtime state for enforcing a [`HappensBeforeProgram`] inside the scheduler.
728///
729/// The scheduler holds each edge's AFTER anchor -- removing that thread from the
730/// run queue -- until the edge's BEFORE anchor has *fired*, so an authored
731/// partial order deterministically reproduces a known race instead of relying on
732/// a seed lottery. An anchor "fires" when its thread is granted passage past the
733/// corresponding checkpoint (see [`Scheduler::hb_checkpoint`]).
734///
735/// Two position kinds are enforced: [`Position::SyscallCount`] and the syscall
736/// occurrence anchors (`Anchor::is_syscall_occurrence`, "the thread's Nth
737/// `writev` to fd 9"), which the guest counts per thread and names in its
738/// checkpoint ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]). A syscall-occurrence
739/// anchor with the posthook phase checks in after its call's result is final
740/// instead of at its entry, and an interrupted call that reached one is
741/// refused (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`,
742/// [`Scheduler::hb_posthook_interrupted`];
743/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>). Other position kinds are retained
744/// for diagnostics but never fire; [`HbRuntime::new`] warns about them so a run
745/// never silently ignores an ordering constraint. An anchor that never fires
746/// is refused by name (`HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED`, exit 122): a BEFORE
747/// anchor whose held thread can never proceed, at the terminal deadlock
748/// ([`HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal`]), and any syscall-occurrence anchor still
749/// unfired when the scheduler finishes ([`HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report`]).
750/// A gate that would hold a vfork child before its exec is refused when it
751/// closes (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD`). A version-2 program also bounds
752/// every hold by its budget (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`,
753/// [`Scheduler::hb_check_hold_budget`]) and refuses a non-leader exec on an
754/// identity a relative anchor names
755/// (`HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT`).
756#[derive(Debug)]
757struct HbRuntime {
758    /// The validated, normalized program (anchors indexed by name, plus edges).
759    program: HappensBeforeProgram,
760    /// Names of anchors that have fired. Monotonic: an anchor fires at most once,
761    /// when its thread is first granted passage past it.
762    fired: BTreeSet<String>,
763    /// Threads currently parked at an AFTER anchor, out of the run queue, awaiting
764    /// their gating BEFORE anchor(s). A `BTreeSet` keeps re-admission order
765    /// deterministic.
766    parked: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
767    /// Threads observed at creation time, in deterministic spawn order, so an
768    /// anchor addressed by `spawn_ordinal` resolves to a concrete `DetTid`.
769    /// Index 0 is the root thread; index N (1-based) is the Nth spawned child,
770    /// matching [`ThreadRef::spawn_ordinal`] semantics.
771    spawn_order: Vec<DetTid>,
772    /// Set when a newly fired anchor may have opened a parked thread's gate, so
773    /// [`Scheduler::hb_flush_wakes`] re-admits parked threads at the next
774    /// `step3` boundary. Re-admission is *deferred* to that boundary because it
775    /// pushes to the run queue, which is illegal while a `tentative_pop`
776    /// selection is in progress (as it is inside `block_for_one_resource`,
777    /// where anchors fire).
778    wake_pending: bool,
779    /// For each parked thread, the anchors it is held at (those whose gate was
780    /// closed when it reached them), so a gate that can never open is refused
781    /// by naming the BEFORE anchors it waits on. Kept in step with `parked`.
782    held_at: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<String>>,
783    /// The logical holds a version-2 budget is charged against: for each
784    /// thread whose gate is closed, the committed virtual time (ns) at which
785    /// it was first parked there and the anchors it is held at. Unlike
786    /// `parked` and `held_at`, which `hb_flush_wakes` clears whenever any
787    /// anchor fires, a hold ends only when the thread is granted passage or
788    /// removed, so a wake that leaves its gate closed does not reset the
789    /// budget.
790    holds: BTreeMap<DetTid, HbHold>,
791}
792
793/// One logical hold ([`HbRuntime::holds`]).
794#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
795struct HbHold {
796    /// Committed virtual time, in ns, when the hold began.
797    since_ns: u64,
798    /// The anchors the thread is held at.
799    anchors: Vec<String>,
800}
801
802impl HbRuntime {
803    /// Build runtime state from a normalized program, warning about any anchor
804    /// whose position kind this milestone does not enforce.
805    fn new(program: HappensBeforeProgram) -> Self {
806        for anchor in program.unenforced_positions() {
807            tracing::warn!(
808                "[happens-before] anchor {} uses position '{}', which the scheduler does not yet \
809                 enforce (only syscall counts and syscall occurrences are enforced); this \
810                 ordering constraint will NOT be applied",
811                anchor.name,
812                anchor.position,
813            );
814        }
815        Self {
816            program,
817            fired: BTreeSet::new(),
818            parked: BTreeSet::new(),
819            spawn_order: Vec::new(),
820            wake_pending: false,
821            held_at: BTreeMap::new(),
822            holds: BTreeMap::new(),
823        }
824    }
825
826    /// Record a thread at creation time for `spawn_ordinal` resolution. Idempotent
827    /// and cheap; the root thread lands at index 0, the Nth child at index N.
828    fn note_spawn(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
829        if !self.spawn_order.contains(&dettid) {
830            self.spawn_order.push(dettid);
831        }
832    }
833
834    /// True when `tref` resolves to `dettid`, by explicit `DetTid` or by
835    /// `spawn_ordinal` against the observed spawn order.
836    fn thread_matches(&self, tref: &ThreadRef, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
837        if let Some(d) = tref.dettid {
838            return d == dettid;
839        }
840        if let Some(ord) = tref.spawn_ordinal {
841            return self.spawn_order.get(ord as usize).copied() == Some(dettid);
842        }
843        false
844    }
845
846    /// Names of anchors on `dettid` whose enforced position is exactly
847    /// `SyscallCount(count)`.
848    fn anchors_at_syscall(&self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) -> Vec<String> {
849        self.program
850            .anchors
851            .values()
852            .filter(|a| {
853                matches!(a.position, Position::SyscallCount(n) if n == count)
854                    && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
855            })
856            .map(|a| a.name.clone())
857            .collect()
858    }
859
860    /// Of the syscall-occurrence anchors a checkpoint names (the guest counted
861    /// them reached on its thread), the ones that are syscall-occurrence
862    /// anchors on `dettid`: its own dettid, or a spawn ordinal that resolves to
863    /// it. A name that is not such an anchor on this thread is ignored.
864    fn occurrence_anchors_on(&self, dettid: DetTid, names: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
865        names
866            .iter()
867            .filter(|name| {
868                self.program.anchors.get(*name).is_some_and(|a| {
869                    a.is_syscall_occurrence() && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
870                })
871            })
872            .cloned()
873            .collect()
874    }
875
876    /// The refusal for a terminal state in which threads are held at gates that
877    /// can never open, or `None` when no thread is held. Names, for each held
878    /// thread, the unfired BEFORE anchors of the hard edges into the anchors it
879    /// is held at: those are the points the guest never reached, the likeliest
880    /// cause being a wrong count, `fd` or `nth` in the spec. Byte-stable.
881    fn held_gate_refusal(&self) -> Option<String> {
882        if self.parked.is_empty() {
883            return None;
884        }
885        let mut lines = Vec::new();
886        for dettid in &self.parked {
887            let held_at = self.held_at.get(dettid).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
888            for after in &held_at {
889                for edge in self.program.edges.iter().filter(|e| {
890                    &e.after == after
891                        && e.strength == Strength::Hard
892                        && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
893                }) {
894                    let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
895                    lines.push(format!(
896                        "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired; it holds dtid {} at anchor \
897                         '{}' (edge {} -> {})",
898                        before.name,
899                        before.thread.label,
900                        before.position,
901                        dettid,
902                        after,
903                        edge.before,
904                        edge.after
905                    ));
906                }
907            }
908        }
909        Some(format!(
910            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: happens-before BEFORE anchor(s) never fired, and the \
911             thread(s) they hold cannot proceed because nothing else can run:\n{}",
912            lines.join("\n")
913        ))
914    }
915
916    /// The refusal for syscall-occurrence anchors that never fired, or `None`
917    /// when every one fired. Such an anchor names a point the guest never
918    /// reached (or reached fewer than `nth` times), so an edge it is part of
919    /// was never exercised; the run must say so rather than pass. Lists the
920    /// anchors in name order, each with its position and the edges that use
921    /// it, and carries no host-dependent text, so it is byte-identical across
922    /// runs. Count anchors are not covered: an unreached count anchor is
923    /// silently ignored, as before.
924    fn unfired_occurrence_report(&self) -> Option<String> {
925        let unfired: Vec<String> = self
926            .program
927            .anchors
928            .values()
929            .filter(|a| a.is_syscall_occurrence() && !self.fired.contains(&a.name))
930            .map(|a| {
931                let edges: Vec<String> = self
932                    .program
933                    .edges
934                    .iter()
935                    .filter(|e| e.before == a.name || e.after == a.name)
936                    .map(|e| format!("{} -> {}", e.before, e.after))
937                    .collect();
938                // A relative anchor whose base never fired could not even
939                // start counting: name the base too.
940                let base = match &a.from {
941                    Some(base) if !self.fired.contains(base) => {
942                        format!("counted from '{}', which never fired either; ", base)
943                    }
944                    Some(base) => format!("counted from '{}'; ", base),
945                    None => String::new(),
946                };
947                format!(
948                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired ({}edges: {})",
949                    a.name,
950                    a.thread.label,
951                    a.position,
952                    base,
953                    if edges.is_empty() {
954                        "none".to_owned()
955                    } else {
956                        edges.join(", ")
957                    }
958                )
959            })
960            .collect();
961        if unfired.is_empty() {
962            return None;
963        }
964        Some(format!(
965            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: {} happens-before syscall-occurrence anchor(s) never \
966             fired before the guest finished, so the ordering they name was not exercised:\n{}",
967            unfired.len(),
968            unfired.join("\n")
969        ))
970    }
971
972    /// The unfired BEFORE anchors that hold a thread at `after`, one line each,
973    /// in the form the refusals use. Byte-stable.
974    fn unfired_befores(&self, after: &str) -> Vec<String> {
975        self.program
976            .edges
977            .iter()
978            .filter(|e| e.after == after && e.strength == Strength::Hard)
979            .filter(|e| !self.fired.contains(&e.before))
980            .map(|edge| {
981                let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
982                format!(
983                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired (edge {} -> {})",
984                    before.name, before.thread.label, before.position, edge.before, edge.after
985                )
986            })
987            .collect()
988    }
989
990    /// The refusal for a hold that has outlasted the version-2 budget at
991    /// committed time `now_ns`, or `None`. Holds are checked in `DetTid`
992    /// order; the first over budget is named, with the BEFORE anchors it
993    /// waits on. The text carries no time other than the budget, so it is
994    /// byte-identical across runs.
995    fn hold_budget_refusal(&self, now_ns: u64) -> Option<String> {
996        let budget = self.program.max_hold_ns?;
997        let (dettid, hold) = self.holds.iter().find(|(_, hold)| {
998            now_ns.saturating_sub(hold.since_ns) > budget
999                && hold.anchors.iter().any(|a| self.anchor_blocked(a))
1000        })?;
1001        let lines: Vec<String> = hold
1002            .anchors
1003            .iter()
1004            .flat_map(|after| self.unfired_befores(after))
1005            .collect();
1006        Some(format!(
1007            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid {} has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
1008             {:?} for more than max_hold_ns = {} virtual ns, waiting on:\n{}",
1009            dettid,
1010            hold.anchors,
1011            budget,
1012            lines.join("\n")
1013        ))
1014    }
1015
1016    /// The refusal for a non-leader exec in which `caller` takes over
1017    /// `leader`'s identity while a relative anchor, or the base of one, is on
1018    /// either thread, or `None`. Its activation state belongs to one task and
1019    /// is not carried across the replacement in this version.
1020    fn relative_identity_refusal(&self, caller: DetTid, leader: DetTid) -> Option<String> {
1021        let names: Vec<String> = self
1022            .program
1023            .relative_anchors()
1024            .filter(|(relative, _)| {
1025                self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, caller)
1026                    || self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, leader)
1027            })
1028            .map(|(relative, base)| format!("'{}' (from '{}')", relative.name, base.name))
1029            .collect();
1030        if names.is_empty() {
1031            return None;
1032        }
1033        Some(format!(
1034            "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {} execs and takes over the \
1035             identity of dtid {}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) {} are on these \
1036             threads; relative anchors are not carried across a non-leader exec.",
1037            caller,
1038            leader,
1039            names.join(", ")
1040        ))
1041    }
1042
1043    /// True when anchor `name` is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
1044    /// endpoint has not yet fired -- i.e. a thread reaching `name` must be held.
1045    fn anchor_blocked(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
1046        self.program.edges.iter().any(|e| {
1047            e.after == name && e.strength == Strength::Hard && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
1048        })
1049    }
1050}
1051
1052/// Which end of a thread's priority band a run-queue admission targets.
1053#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1054pub(crate) enum AdmitSide {
1055    /// Run before an equal-priority peer (`runqueue_push_front`).
1056    Front,
1057    /// Ordinary tail admission (`runqueue_push_back`).
1058    Back,
1059}
1060
1061/// How a run-queue admission's side is determined.
1062///
1063/// The side is *resolved* — not merely applied — at the deterministic drain
1064/// ([`Scheduler::drain_pending_run_queue_admissions`]). Buffering the *intent*
1065/// rather than an already-chosen `AdmitSide` is what keeps the admission a pure
1066/// function of deterministic scheduler state: any PRNG draw that picks the side
1067/// (`RunsPostFork::Random`) is consumed at the drain, in canonical `DetTid`
1068/// order, instead of in host RPC / lock-acquisition order at the handler. See
1069/// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`].
1070#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1071pub(crate) enum AdmitIntent {
1072    /// The side is fixed regardless of scheduler state; consumes no PRNG.
1073    Fixed(AdmitSide),
1074    /// The side follows the post-fork policy; `RunsPostFork::Random` draws from
1075    /// the scheduler PRNG at resolution time.
1076    PostFork(RunsPostFork),
1077}
1078
1079/// Why a raw TID must be removed from the physical run queue at the next
1080/// deterministic drain.
1081#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1082enum RemovalDisposition {
1083    /// The current thread incarnation is gone. Any admission recorded for the
1084    /// same raw TID is stale and must be cancelled.
1085    Retire,
1086    /// Linux nonleader exec destroyed the old process leader and reassigned
1087    /// its raw TID to the caller's replacement image. Remove the old physical
1088    /// queue slot, but preserve the one causally paired replacement admission.
1089    ReplaceThenAdmit,
1090}
1091
1092#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
1093enum WaitidSignalRequest {
1094    /// An in-flight wait that a pending signal should wake: either the legacy
1095    /// `waitid` kernel-polling loop or a scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle
1096    /// resource.
1097    ///
1098    /// Deliberately does NOT distinguish the two. Queue residency is not a
1099    /// property of the resource and must be decided at the drain, not inferred
1100    /// here: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its
1101    /// `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue` pushes a thread back before it
1102    /// issues its next request, so either request can be held by a thread that
1103    /// is already in the run queue.
1104    Parked,
1105    Pending(Vec<SigWrapper>),
1106}
1107
1108/// A thread released into a background call that sleeps under `mask`, a
1109/// temporary mask other than its own, whose entry the scheduler has not yet
1110/// seen (`Scheduler::background_entry_barriers`), and when it was released,
1111/// which bounds the wait (`Scheduler::background_entry_valve`).
1112#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
1113struct BackgroundEntry {
1114    mask: u64,
1115    since: std::time::Instant,
1116}
1117
1118/// A background read under record/replay (`Scheduler::background_reads`).
1119#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
1120struct BackgroundRead {
1121    /// Its call.
1122    op: ExternalOpId,
1123    /// The descriptor table it reads from.
1124    files: detcore_model::fd::FilesId,
1125    /// The descriptor number it reads.
1126    fd: i32,
1127    /// What that descriptor reads.
1128    signals: BackgroundReadSignals,
1129}
1130
1131/// What a background read's descriptor reads (`Scheduler::background_reads`).
1132#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1133enum BackgroundReadSignals {
1134    /// Not a signalfd.
1135    NotSignalfd,
1136    /// A signalfd for these signals (a kernel sigset).
1137    Signalfd(u64),
1138    /// Not known: it may be, or become before the read enters the kernel, a
1139    /// signalfd for any signal.
1140    Unknown,
1141}
1142
1143impl BackgroundReadSignals {
1144    /// Whether the read may take the signal `bit` (a kernel sigset bit).
1145    fn may_read(self, bit: u64) -> bool {
1146        match self {
1147            Self::NotSignalfd => false,
1148            Self::Signalfd(mask) => mask & bit != 0,
1149            Self::Unknown => true,
1150        }
1151    }
1152}
1153
1154/// The state for the deterministic scheduler.
1155#[derive(Debug)]
1156pub struct Scheduler {
1157    /// Monotonically count upwards.
1158    pub turn: u64,
1159
1160    /// The queue of logically UNBLOCKED guest threads waiting for a turn.  After a new
1161    /// thread is created, it should always have an entry in here, but it goes to the end
1162    /// of the line after its turn. Unblocked threads are dequed in priority order, then
1163    /// round-robin within a priority level.
1164    /// NB: Polling threads are considered unblocked, and their polling intervals are managed by the RunQueue
1165    pub run_queue: RunQueue,
1166
1167    /// Stores the communication endpoints for rendevous with each guest on its next turn.
1168    /// When the thread parks it provides its request for resources, and waits for a
1169    /// response.  After a new thread is created, it should always have an entry in here.
1170    ///
1171    /// Parked threads are READY, waiting only for the scheduler.
1172    ///
1173    /// (N.B.  This is a BTreeMap because we iterate over it, printing the
1174    /// contents, and BTreeMap gives us a predictable order, unlike HashMap.)
1175    pub next_turns: BTreeMap<DetTid, ThreadNextTurn>,
1176
1177    /// Thread pidfds for backends whose scheduler identities do not name host
1178    /// tasks directly. The address-space identity prevents stale exec cleanup
1179    /// from removing a replacement image's descriptor.
1180    physical_thread_pidfds: BTreeMap<DetTid, (MmId, i32, i32, OwnedFd)>,
1181
1182    /// The kernel's process and thread ids of each thread that registered
1183    /// them (`register_physical_thread`), kept after the thread exits, so a
1184    /// zombie's `/proc` directory is still found by its guest number
1185    /// (`procfs_ids`). Only what `/proc` lists is translated, so a reaped
1186    /// process's entry, kept until its number is taken again, names nothing.
1187    procfs_kernel_ids: BTreeMap<DetTid, (i32, i32)>,
1188
1189    /// Whole-process observations, one per process, each bound to the
1190    /// registration that armed it. The Arc identity distinguishes reused PIDs
1191    /// even when CLONE_VM shares MmId. Nothing arms one yet: the authenticated
1192    /// registration of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362> part 2
1193    /// will be its only caller (`arm_process_exit_watch`).
1194    process_exit_watches: BTreeMap<DetPid, Arc<ProcessExitWatch>>,
1195
1196    /// The current set of actions in the background.
1197    #[allow(dead_code)]
1198    pub bg_action_pool: HashMap<ActionID, Action>,
1199
1200    /// The logical, global time consumed by actions that have been committed already.
1201    pub committed_time: LogicalTime,
1202
1203    /// The thread of the last committed turn, so that `bump_global_time` can
1204    /// tell a signal delivery to the thread that was already running from one
1205    /// that switches threads (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139>).
1206    previous_turn_tid: Option<DetTid>,
1207
1208    /// INVARIANT: Thread IDs in `blocked` are absent from `run_queue`.
1209    pub blocked: BlockedPool,
1210
1211    /// Kernel-blocked vfork parents and their children, once registered.
1212    vfork_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<DetTid>>,
1213
1214    /// Exact parent address space captured when BlockingVfork is granted.
1215    /// A child self-registration can use this one-shot causal authority even
1216    /// when Linux reused a TID retired by an earlier transferred exec.
1217    vfork_registration_origins: BTreeMap<DetTid, MmId>,
1218
1219    /// Vfork parents that died, without an Exit grant, before their child
1220    /// registered: the barrier is cancelled so no other turn is excluded, but
1221    /// the child's still-outstanding `CreateVforkChildThread` must settle
1222    /// against this record instead of the barrier. A new vfork by the same
1223    /// TID clears a stale record ([`Scheduler::begin_vfork_barrier`]).
1224    dead_vfork_parents: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1225    /// Vfork parents that died while their registered child was still known
1226    /// to the scheduler. Their barrier is kept until the child's next release
1227    /// edge, which happens at a deterministic point: its `Exit` grant, its
1228    /// successful exec, or its logical kill
1229    /// ([`Scheduler::release_vfork_child`]). Dropping it at the
1230    /// parent's own retirement would let other threads be selected at a
1231    /// moment the host chooses: on ptrace a SIGKILL from another process
1232    /// retires its target only at the target's deregistration
1233    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984>).
1234    dead_parent_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1235    /// Vfork parents whose registered child reached a release edge (its
1236    /// `Exit` grant, its successful exec, or its logical kill) while the
1237    /// parent was alive. The barrier stays, and step2a waits without
1238    /// committing a turn until the parent's fate is known (its continuation
1239    /// or its retirement), then drops it. Recording the release whether or
1240    /// not the parent's death has been seen keeps the drop independent of the
1241    /// order in which those host-timed events arrive.
1242    released_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1243
1244    /// Processes a committed SIGKILL has doomed
1245    /// ([`Scheduler::record_committed_sigkill`]). They will die even if a
1246    /// thread of theirs is held at a happens-before gate, so a wait for one is
1247    /// never part of a deadlock. An entry is dropped when its process is
1248    /// reaped.
1249    sigkilled_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1250    /// Whether the backend reports every process's children
1251    /// (`BackendCapabilities::tracks_process_children`). Without it, a wait
1252    /// may have a child Detcore has no record of, so the children it knows
1253    /// being stuck does not make the wait stuck
1254    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`]).
1255    complete_child_lineage: bool,
1256    /// Threads granted their `Exit` (an `exit` or `exit_group`), inside their
1257    /// own committed turn. A thread that leaves the scheduler without one died
1258    /// of a signal or with its process, so its process is going down
1259    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`]). Cleared when
1260    /// the tid is registered again.
1261    committed_exits: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1262    /// Thread-group leaders retired at their own `exit` while a sibling still
1263    /// ran (`retire_exited_leader`). Linux keeps such a leader as a zombie
1264    /// until its group is empty, so its backend deregistration comes only
1265    /// then; that deregistration finds it here and changes nothing more
1266    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). Cleared when the tid
1267    /// is registered again.
1268    retired_exited_leaders: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1269    /// Leaders `retire_exited_leader` retired, until the kernel shows each
1270    /// one a zombie, and when it was retired, which bounds the wait
1271    /// (`exited_leader_valve`). The retirement comes before the leader's exit
1272    /// is injected, and the kernel's exit then releases its address space and
1273    /// files and moves its signal targeting; a sibling turn in that window
1274    /// would observe those changes at host-chosen points (Claude review of
1275    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245>). So step2 commits no
1276    /// turn while an entry is pending (`step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders`).
1277    exited_leader_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, std::time::Instant>,
1278    /// Threads that deregistered after their own `Exit` grant while the kernel
1279    /// had not yet carried out the exit, until the kernel shows each one
1280    /// exited (`ExitedThreadBarrier`). Only a backend whose scheduler
1281    /// identities do not name host tasks registers host thread pidfds
1282    /// (`physical_thread_pidfds`); DBT is one, and it reports a thread's exit
1283    /// before the native exit runs. That native exit walks the thread's robust
1284    /// list, stores 0 to its `clear_child_tid` word and wakes it, in that
1285    /// order, then releases its files, and a sibling turn before it finishes
1286    /// would observe those changes at host-chosen points
1287    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4246>). So step2 commits no
1288    /// turn while an entry is pending (`step2a_wait_for_exited_threads`).
1289    exited_thread_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExitedThreadBarrier>,
1290    /// How long an `exited_leader_barriers` entry may wait before the run
1291    /// ends with a named refusal.
1292    exited_leader_valve: Duration,
1293    /// Task states `read_task_state` reports in unit tests.
1294    #[cfg(test)]
1295    test_task_states: BTreeMap<DetTid, char>,
1296    /// Set by a SIGKILL whose victim the scheduler cannot name (a pidfd with
1297    /// no recorded process): from then on no child wait counts as part of a
1298    /// deadlock ([`Scheduler::record_unresolved_sigkill`]).
1299    unresolved_sigkill: bool,
1300    /// Under `--pipe-wake-latency`, the pollers each thread's actions readied
1301    /// since its last turn, which its hand-off moves it behind
1302    /// (`scheduler::pipe_wake`).
1303    pipe_handoff_pending: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1304    /// Processes a delivered signal with a fatal default action has doomed,
1305    /// read only by the `--pipe-wake-latency` scan (`scheduler::pipe_wake`).
1306    fatal_signal_doomed: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1307    /// Whether the `--pipe-wake-latency` hand-off has logged that it is inert.
1308    pipe_wake_inert_logged: bool,
1309
1310    /// Threads released into a background call that sleeps under a temporary
1311    /// mask other than their own (`rt_sigsuspend`, or a `ppoll` or `pselect6`
1312    /// whose mask the call's turn read), with that mask, until the kernel is
1313    /// seen to have installed it or the call has ended. Until then the thread
1314    /// still runs under its own mask on its way into the kernel, and a
1315    /// process-directed signal that its own mask leaves unblocked, such as the
1316    /// `SIGALRM` of an `ITIMER_REAL` that a timer wake sends, could be taken by
1317    /// it there or not, as host timing decides. So step2 commits no turn and
1318    /// pops no timer while an entry is pending
1319    /// (`step2a_wait_for_background_entry`,
1320    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3993>).
1321    background_entry_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, BackgroundEntry>,
1322    /// How long a `background_entry_barriers` entry may stay unproved, neither
1323    /// entered nor left, before the run ends with a named refusal
1324    /// (`step2a_wait_for_background_entry`).
1325    background_entry_valve: Duration,
1326
1327    /// Threads whose run-queue admission was recorded by a global-request
1328    /// handler while a `tentative_pop` transaction was live, deferred to the
1329    /// next deterministic drain point (`step2`) so it cannot mutate the run
1330    /// queue underneath the daemon's tentative selection. Keyed by `DetTid`
1331    /// so the drain order among co-pending admissions is canonical rather than
1332    /// lock-acquisition dependent. The stored value is the *unresolved*
1333    /// [`AdmitIntent`], so any side-selecting PRNG draw is deferred to the
1334    /// `DetTid`-ordered drain rather than performed in host RPC order. See
1335    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] and
1336    /// [`Scheduler::drain_pending_run_queue_admissions`].
1337    pending_run_queue_admissions: BTreeMap<DetTid, AdmitIntent>,
1338    /// The sequence number of the latest committed turn (`nothing_else_can_run`).
1339    progress_epoch: u64,
1340    /// The sequence number of the latest committed turn known to be progress:
1341    /// any turn but a guest-state-only poll's grant
1342    /// (`Resources::polls_guest_state_only`), and such a grant once the
1343    /// thread's next request shows its attempt moved something (it is not a
1344    /// retry, or is one with `previous_attempt_made_progress`).
1345    last_progress: u64,
1346    /// The sequence number of each guest-state-only poller's latest grant,
1347    /// until the thread commits a turn of another kind.
1348    guest_state_polled_at: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1349    /// The sequence number of each thread's latest committed turn: a poller's
1350    /// failed attempt came no earlier.
1351    last_commit_at: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1352    /// Set at the commit of a FIFO open's poll when nothing else can run but
1353    /// a timer is due at a finite deadline: the next pass moves global time
1354    /// to that deadline, as an empty run queue does, rather than letting the
1355    /// poll crawl there one turn charge at a time (`unblock_guest`).
1356    fast_forward_for_alone_poller: bool,
1357
1358    /// Run-queue *removals* requested by a global-request handler
1359    /// (`reconnect_after_exec` -> `logically_kill_thread`), deferred to the same
1360    /// deterministic drain point (`step2`). `RunQueue::remove_tid` carries the same
1361    /// `tentative_selection.is_none()` guard as the push operations, so a
1362    /// multi-threaded exec that reconnects on an asynchronous backend (DBT)
1363    /// inside the daemon's tentative window would otherwise trip it, poison the
1364    /// scheduler mutex, and hang the run.
1365    ///
1366    /// A `Retire` target is already logically dead (its `next_turns` entry is
1367    /// gone and its request is `ThreadExited`). `ReplaceThenAdmit` is the one
1368    /// Linux exception: a nonleader exec has installed a fresh registration at
1369    /// the destroyed leader's raw TID, but the old incarnation's physical queue
1370    /// slot must still be removed. Both are filtered from
1371    /// [`Scheduler::are_all_quiesced`] until this drain establishes the intended
1372    /// physical queue state.
1373    ///
1374    /// The map is drained before admissions. Ordinary retirement cancels a
1375    /// buffered admission for the same raw TID; the explicitly classified exec
1376    /// replacement preserves exactly one causally paired admission.
1377    pending_run_queue_removals: BTreeMap<DetTid, RemovalDisposition>,
1378
1379    /// Cross-task signals physically queued while their sole target was parked
1380    /// in waitid or restartable internal IO polling. Applied at step2, where
1381    /// run-queue mutation is safe.
1382    pending_cross_task_signals: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<SigWrapper>>,
1383
1384    /// Whether the scheduler models which thread the kernel gives a signal it
1385    /// sends, from the signal masks it reads from the kernel: set exactly when
1386    /// threads are serialized and the backend decides blocked-wait interruption
1387    /// from the kernel's signal state
1388    /// (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`). Under it the
1389    /// scheduler records the mask of each thread it releases into a call
1390    /// outside the schedule (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`), wakes such
1391    /// a thread at a fixed point when its own signal reaches it
1392    /// (`arm_signaled_background`), and sends a child-exit `SIGCHLD` to the
1393    /// thread the kernel would give it (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
1394    models_signal_targets: bool,
1395
1396    /// Signals that a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to a process,
1397    /// keyed by that process: no gated wait of the process ends for them
1398    /// (`host_timed_signals`). An entry is added in the turn of the call that
1399    /// arms the source and is never removed
1400    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
1401    host_timed_signals: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1402
1403    /// Signals that a host-timed source can post to any process of the
1404    /// container: one a guest armed (`HostTimedSignalScope::Container`), and
1405    /// from the start, a terminal the guest may have inherited
1406    /// (`startup_host_timed_signals`). Never removed.
1407    host_timed_signals_everywhere: u64,
1408
1409    /// Kernel signal states that tests install for parked futex waiters, in
1410    /// place of reading `/proc`.
1411    #[cfg(test)]
1412    test_kernel_signal_states: BTreeMap<DetTid, KernelSignalState>,
1413
1414    /// Read failures that tests install for emulated sleepers, in place of
1415    /// reading `/proc` (`sleep_signal`).
1416    #[cfg(test)]
1417    test_sleeper_read_failures: BTreeMap<DetTid, sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable>,
1418
1419    /// How many times `read_thread_blocked_mask` was asked for a thread's mask,
1420    /// so a test can show that a path which must not read `/proc` does not.
1421    #[cfg(test)]
1422    test_kernel_mask_reads: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize,
1423    /// Counts the drain's reads of a polling thread's kernel signal state
1424    /// (`restartable_internal_io_interrupting_signals`).
1425    #[cfg(test)]
1426    test_internal_io_signal_state_reads: std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize,
1427
1428    /// Child-TID futexes whose kernel clear may still be racing a guest join.
1429    cleared_child_tids: HashMap<FutexID, DetTid>,
1430
1431    /// The rendered report for a terminal deadlock, once one has been detected.
1432    ///
1433    /// Set instead of panicking, and consumed by `sched_loop_inner`, which
1434    /// prints it and exits the container. Panicking here does not end the run:
1435    /// the scheduler is a `tokio::spawn`ed task, so its panic is captured by the
1436    /// task harness while every guest stays parked on an
1437    /// `Ivar<SchedResponse>` that only the (now dead) scheduler could fill --
1438    /// the run then hangs until an external timeout. Unwinding would also
1439    /// poison the scheduler mutex on the way out.
1440    terminal_deadlock: Option<String>,
1441
1442    /// A scheduler turn refused because its configured charge would pass the
1443    /// end of representable virtual time (`--scheduler-turn-cost`). Like
1444    /// [`Scheduler::terminal_deadlock`], `bump_global_time` records it and
1445    /// `sched_loop_inner` prints it and exits, because a panic in the
1446    /// scheduler task would leave every guest parked. Both turn functions
1447    /// return as soon as it is set, before any maintenance, selection, grant
1448    /// or signal observation, so nothing new waits on a guest.
1449    terminal_clock_exhaustion: Option<String>,
1450
1451    /// Set when `terminal_deadlock` is a policy refusal of the happens-before
1452    /// spec (a gate that can never open, or a hold inside a vfork child) rather
1453    /// than a scheduler failure: the run then exits with
1454    /// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT` instead of the fatal status.
1455    terminal_is_refusal: bool,
1456
1457    /// The scheduler turn at which `step2d_handle_empty_queue` last logged
1458    /// "zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.", while that empty state lasts.
1459    ///
1460    /// The line reports a logical transition: every thread is dead or gone and
1461    /// nothing waits. Once logged, the daemon may pass through the empty-queue
1462    /// step again before it can exit, and how many extra passes it makes is
1463    /// host timing. It waits for a SaBRe supervisor to report a final wait
1464    /// status (`pending_physical_process_exits`), and it drains a removal that
1465    /// a dead thread's second, reactive exit hook queued
1466    /// (`pending_run_queue_removals`). Neither is a thread. This records that
1467    /// the current empty state was already reported, so those passes add no
1468    /// line. It is cleared as soon as the step sees a thread or a waiter again,
1469    /// and a committed turn makes the recorded turn stale.
1470    ///
1471    /// See <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360> and
1472    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223>.
1473    empty_queue_kick_turn: Option<u64>,
1474
1475    // A fatal backend result ends this run; it is never a guest response.
1476    // The event and run-queue transition share the grant/commit mutex. Every
1477    // callback and daemon wait clones its own subscriber, unlike an Ivar.
1478    backend_failure: Option<BackendFailureLocation>,
1479    backend_failure_sender: Option<oneshot::Sender<()>>,
1480    backend_failure_wake: Shared<oneshot::Receiver<()>>,
1481
1482    /// How the backend runs the guest. See [`Config::backend`].
1483    backend: BackendCapabilities,
1484    /// When the release barrier (`step2_release_signaled_background`) began
1485    /// waiting for the threads in `blocked.signaled_background` to post their
1486    /// continuations; `None` while the set is empty.
1487    signaled_background_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
1488    /// Set when the release barrier's watchdog expires; the scheduler loop
1489    /// ends the run with it (`exit_on_scheduler_refusal`).
1490    signaled_background_refusal: Option<SignaledBackgroundRefusal>,
1491    /// When step2a began skipping turns for vfork barriers that wait for a
1492    /// backend event (`Pending` or `Released` ones); `None` while none waits.
1493    vfork_barrier_wait_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
1494    /// Set when step2a's valve expires; `sched_loop_inner` ends the run with
1495    /// it (`exit_on_scheduler_refusal`).
1496    vfork_barrier_refusal: Option<VforkBarrierRefusal>,
1497
1498    /// When the SIGKILL fence started waiting for the current committed
1499    /// victims, in host time (`sigkill_retirement`).
1500    sigkill_fence_wait_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
1501
1502    /// A SIGKILL fence that waited past `SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE` for a death or
1503    /// a publication that never arrived: the run is refused.
1504    sigkill_fence_refusal: Option<sigkill_retirement::SigkillFenceRefusal>,
1505
1506    /// The bound on the SIGKILL fence and a sender's wait:
1507    /// `SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE`, shortened only by tests that expire it.
1508    pub(crate) sigkill_fence_valve: Duration,
1509
1510    /// A thread that, in its signal-delivery turn, decided that a fatal
1511    /// default action ends its thread group, and whose group `Exit` request
1512    /// is therefore granted at the very next turn, before any other thread
1513    /// runs (`hold_turn_for_group_exit`).
1514    group_exit_decider: Option<DetTid>,
1515    /// `hermit record`: where `step2c_process_io_blockers` logs each
1516    /// readmission of a backgrounded call (see `rejoin_log`).
1517    rejoin_writer: Option<RejoinWriter>,
1518    /// `hermit replay`: the logged readmissions not yet replayed. A log that
1519    /// cannot be read is refused when the scheduler is made, and one with
1520    /// readmissions left when the run ends is refused then
1521    /// (`unreplayed_rejoins`).
1522    rejoin_replay: Option<std::collections::VecDeque<Rejoin>>,
1523    /// Set when replay cannot follow the rejoin log; the scheduler loop ends
1524    /// the run with it (`exit_on_scheduler_refusal`).
1525    rejoin_refusal: Option<RejoinRefusal>,
1526    /// Per process, the signals the scheduler sent it that every thread
1527    /// blocked when sent, so they wait in its shared queue for the first
1528    /// thread that unblocks one (`note_signal_left_in_shared_queue`). Cleared
1529    /// when a thread of the process takes the signal
1530    /// (`note_process_signal_taken`). A call that begins under a mask that
1531    /// admits one of them is ended by it at once, so its readmission is fixed
1532    /// by the schedule (`arm_for_waiting_scheduler_signal`).
1533    shared_queue_scheduler_signals: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1534    /// When replay began waiting with nothing runnable and no readmission due
1535    /// (`step2c_replay_rejoin`); `None` otherwise.
1536    rejoin_stalled_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
1537    /// How many timed events `step2d_decide_empty_queue` has woken with the run

1539    /// rejoin log, because such a wake does not advance `turn`.

1541    #[cfg(test)]
1542    host_signal_attempts: u64,

1544    #[cfg(test)]
1545    controlled_turn_entries: u64,
1546    pub(crate) real_timers: real_timer::RealTimers,
1547    parked: parked::ParkedRequests,
1548
1549    /// Guest-handled SIGALRMs on a backend that runs Detcore inside each guest

1551    sigalrm: sigalrm::SigalrmLedger,
1552
1553    /// The determinism losses this scheduler recorded (`note_determinism_loss`).

1555    determinism_losses: Vec<String>,

1558    /// order (`reparent_orphans`).
1559    #[cfg(test)]
1560    reparentings: Vec<(DetPid, DetPid)>,
1561

1588

1590    /// process and the exec'ing thread, which survives as its leader: the

1594

1600    /// Tombstoned SaBRe threads whose final asynchronous deregistration statistics were merged.

1603

1613    /// deadlocked.

1615
1616    /// When the current wait for `namespace_zap_victims` began; reset once

1618    namespace_zap_wait_since: Option<std::time::Instant>,
1619
1620    /// `NAMESPACE_ZAP_VALVE`, shortened only by tests that expire it.
1621    pub(crate) namespace_zap_valve: Duration,
1622
1623    /// Logically exited child processes whose terminal wait status has not been consumed.
1624    logically_exited_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1625
1626    /// Logically exited processes whose parent reaped them automatically at
1627    /// exit (`ThreadTree::reaps_children_automatically`): no longer zombies,
1628    /// although no wait consumed them.

1630
1631    /// Reporting-backend children whose final physical exit has been observed.

1633

1635    /// classified None or Discard (`ChildExitNotification`), on a backend that

1637    /// guest turn runs until the backend reports that the kernel has published

1649    /// logically retired.

1664    posix_timer_arm_generations: BTreeMap<(DetPid, i32), u64>,

1669

1672    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4262>).

1674

1678

1681    /// have read since (`replay_unproven_copies`). A replayed signalfd read

1688

1693

1695    /// (`discarded_signal_control`), which runs rather than waits: a send it

1703

1707

1714    saved_guest_sigmasks: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1715

1717    /// thread of their process blocked them, by process

1719    /// signal, which then changes nothing until the process could observe it:
1720    /// a thread unblocks it, waits for it, or reads its pending set. Detcore
1721    /// does not deliver a real-time signal from a POSIX timer (it delivers one
1722    /// a thread or process sends since
1723    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/207>), so each of those
1724    /// points refuses the run by name (`pending_real_time_expirations`), and
1725    /// the process's exit, a change of the signal's disposition to `SIG_IGN`,
1726    /// or a successful exec, which flushes queued timer signals
1727    /// (`take_exec_timer_flush`), discards it, as Linux does.
1728    pending_real_time_expirations: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1729

1731    /// now (`send_child_exit_sigchld`), for `signal_guest` to enter in the

1733    sending_child_exit: Option<DetPid>,
1734

1738    /// (`WindowSend::ParentDeath`).
1739    sending_parent_death: bool,
1740

1742    /// process; a real-time timer expiration such a descriptor could read is
1743    /// never kept pending (`real_time_expiration_fate`).
1744    signalfd_masks: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,

1748    background_signalfd_reads: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
1749    /// Under record and replay, every thread's background read
1750    /// (`Resources::read_fd`, `BackgroundRead`): its op, descriptor table and
1751    /// number, and what that descriptor reads (`BackgroundReadSignals`),
1752    /// judged as the scheduler grants the read (`kernel_signalfd_read_mask`)

1754    /// (`register_signalfd`) or by a later `close`, `close_range`, `dup2` or

1760    background_reads: BTreeMap<DetTid, BackgroundRead>,
1761
1762    /// The real-time signals (a kernel sigset) that the mask a signal handler's
1763    /// return restores leaves unblocked, by process: the thread's mask when a
1764    /// caught signal was delivered to it, which `rt_sigreturn` restores without
1765    /// a stop that Detcore sees. While a handler runs, its `sa_mask` may block

1768    handler_restore_unblocked: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1769
1770    /// Processes one of whose threads has entered a call outside the schedule
1771    /// (`external_io_blockers`, `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`). Such a thread rejoins

1773    /// timer expires is not fixed by the schedule; a real-time expiration of
1774    /// such a process is never kept pending (`real_time_expiration_fate`).
1775    /// Recorded in the thread's own turn; never cleared.
1776    background_call_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1777
1778    /// Processes whose shared-queue SIGALRM dequeues the scheduler cannot

1780    /// `ITIMER_REAL` forwards at each pop instead of waiting for a dequeue

1782    alarm_unobservable: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1783
1784    /// Whether the last `send_guest_signal` landed: `Some(false)` when the

1786    guest_send_landed: Option<bool>,
1787
1788    /// `ITIMER_REAL` expiries that popped while their process's exec barrier
1789    /// was up, with the thread and signal to send, decided when the barrier
1790    /// ends (`finish_exec_alarm`).
1791    alarm_exec_deferred: BTreeMap<DetPid, (DetTid, Signal)>,
1792
1793    /// Unit tests: treat every guest send as landed without a host syscall.
1794    #[cfg(test)]
1795    test_guest_sends_land: bool,
1796
1797    /// When set, `send_guest_signal` records each send here (target, signal,
1798    /// siginfo, `thread_of`) and notes it to the discarded-at-send record as
1799    /// if it landed, instead of signalling a host task.
1800    #[cfg(test)]
1801    pub(crate) test_sent_signals: Option<Vec<TestSend>>,
1802
1803    /// The targets a captured send (`test_sent_signals`) would have woken
1804    /// (`send_wakes`).
1805    #[cfg(test)]
1806    pub(crate) test_send_wakes: Vec<DetTid>,
1807
1808    /// The set each thread polling `rt_sigtimedwait` waits for: a signal in
1809    /// it is taken at the thread's next poll whatever its mask, so the
1810    /// thread's effective mask is `blocked & !set`
1811    /// (`own_process_signal_inputs`).
1812    sigtimedwait_sets: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1813
1814    /// For each process, the signals the scheduler has sent to it
1815    /// (`signal_guest`). On ptrace the scheduler's copy is process-directed
1816    /// (`kill(pid)`), so it is outstanding exactly while its signal is in the
1817    /// process's shared queue; an admission counts only those
1818    /// (`own_process_signal_inputs`), whoever takes or merges the copy
1819    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122>).
1820    ///
1821    /// The record is never cleared. That is correct only because no other
1822    /// copy of a recorded signal that the sender does not block can sit in the
1823    /// shared queue at the sender's turn: such a copy would have been taken at
1824    /// the sender's last return to user mode, so one still there is the
1825    /// scheduler's, sent while the sender was stopped. The bit then names
1826    /// exactly the copy the kernel would dequeue before the send.
1827    undelivered_scheduler_signals: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1828
1829    /// For each thread and standard signal, the `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer whose
1830    /// expiration the scheduler sent it and that the thread has not consumed
1831    /// since (`fire_thread_timer`). While the entry stands, the pending copy of
1832    /// that signal on the thread is the timer's own queued signal, which Linux
1833    /// does not queue twice (an overrun). The entry goes when the copy is
