1838    thread_timer_copies: BTreeMap<(DetTid, i32), timed_waiters::SignalTimerId>,
1839
1840    /// Whether any guest has sent SIGSTKFLT, Reverie's timer marker
1841    /// (`record_guest_marker_signal`). Set in the sending call's turn and
1842    /// never cleared.
1843    guest_sent_marker_signal: bool,
1844
1845    /// Test-only stand-in for the /proc signal-mask fields, keyed by
1846    /// (process, thread, field). Unit tests use small fake pids that can name
1847    /// real host processes, so tests never read /proc: an absent entry reads
1848    /// as unavailable, which classifies a notification Undecided.
1849    #[cfg(test)]
1850    test_signal_masks: BTreeMap<(DetPid, Option<DetTid>, &'static str), u64>,
1851
1852    /// Ac table of "locks held": which action is using which resources.
1853    /// A given resource can be held by at most one action at a given time.
1854    #[allow(dead_code)]
1855    pub resources: HashMap<ResourceID, ActionID>,
1856
1857    /// Initially false, set to true when the first thread is running.
1858    /// Invariant: at the moment this becomes full, the queue is nonempty.
1859    pub started_up: Ivar<()>,
1860
1861    /// A model of the the raw ancestry tree of threads, based on parentage at the point
1862    /// of thread creation.  This establishes a mapping from each thread to the child
1863    /// threads it has spawned.
1864    //
1865    // FUTURE OPTION:
1866    // If this is not used for purposes *other* than `exit_group` handling in the future,
1867    // we could probably rip it out and just refer to the `/proc/pid/task/` directory
1868    // to determine what threads exit upon `exit_group`.
1869    pub thread_tree: ThreadTree,
1870
1871    /// Tracks the priorities of each thread. New threads should have an entry
1872    /// before being inserted into the runqueue.
1873    ///
1874    /// INVARIANT: Whenever the thread is normally in the run_queue, it's
1875    /// priority in the queue should match that stored here. "Abnormal"
1876    /// queueings include polling and eager IO polling.
1877    ///
1878    /// NB: BTreeMap over HashMap for deterministic printing.
1879    pub priorities: BTreeMap<DetTid, Priority>,
1880
1881    /// Tracks explicit optional timeslices to run for each thread.
1882    /// If a guest is to be unblocked on a thread the guest will receive this
1883    /// information and needs to "cooperate" and setup it's preemption for the amount
1884    pub timeslices: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<LogicalTime>>,
1885
1886    /// The virtual time that remained before the earliest pending deadline
1887    /// when each thread was last granted a turn ([`Scheduler::deadline_remaining`]),
1888    /// taken by the grant's reply so the thread can end its slice there
1889    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>).
1890    deadline_hints: BTreeMap<DetTid, Duration>,
1891
1892    /// Per-thread distribution of completed timeslice durations (virtual ns),
1893    /// collected from each thread as it deregisters at exit. Aggregated into the
1894    /// final run report. BTreeMap for deterministic iteration order.
1895    pub per_thread_timeslice: BTreeMap<DetTid, TimesliceStats>,
1896
1897    /// Final syscall count reported by each thread when it deregisters.
1898    pub per_thread_syscalls: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1899
1900    /// Counts already consumed from displaced leaders before the current
1901    /// transferred incarnation began reporting under the same leader TID.
1902    transferred_exec_syscall_offsets: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1903
1904    /// A record of which preemptions occured on each thread.  Only used IF `--record-preemptions`
1905    /// was specified in the Config, otherwise this remains empty.
1906    pub preemption_writer: Option<PreemptionWriter>,
1907
1908    /// An instance of replayer that is responsible for replaying events in case --replay-preemptions-from is specified
1909    pub replayer: Option<Replayer>,
1910
1911    /// Whether the replayed schedule's priorities were dropped when its
1912    /// recording ran out (`release_replay_priorities_if_exhausted`).
1913    replay_priorities_released: bool,
1914
1915    /// Count record_event calls which determines the event number if we're recording a schedule
1916    /// event trace.
1917    pub recorded_event_count: u64,
1918
1919    /// A copy of the `Config::stacktrace_event` vector.  This is MUTABLE,
1920    /// because we pop events off as we handle them.  The u64 is an index into
1921    /// the (original) replay_cursor trace.
1922    pub stacktrace_events: Option<StacktraceEventsIter>,
1923
1924    /// PRNG to drive any fuzzing of OS semantics (other than scheduling).
1925    fuzz_prng: Pcg64Mcg,
1926
1927    /// Independent scheduler-seeded stream for post-fork ordering choices.
1928    post_fork_prng: Pcg64Mcg,
1929
1930    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1931    stop_after_turn: Option<u64>,
1932    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1933    stop_after_iter: Option<u64>,
1934    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1935    recordreplay_modes: bool,
1936    /// Two scheduler turn charges ([`Config::scheduler_turn_charge`]): a
1937    /// periodic timer whose period is at most this hints no slice end
1938    /// (`deadline_remaining_from`). The exclusion predates the free delivery
1939    /// to the running thread (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139>)
1940    /// and is kept; lifting it is a separate change.
1941    fast_timer_period: LogicalTime,
1942    /// The timeout deadlines of backed-off pollers, in the order
1943    /// `step2b_restore_due_pollers` resolves them: once committed time passes
1944    /// a deadline, the poller's normal priority is restored so its next retry
1945    /// can return the timeout (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
1946    /// At most one entry per thread, mirrored by `poll_deadline_of`.
1947    poll_deadlines: BTreeSet<(LogicalTime, DetTid)>,
1948    /// Each thread's entry in `poll_deadlines`.
1949    poll_deadline_of: BTreeMap<DetTid, LogicalTime>,
1950    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1951    fuzz_futexes: bool,
1952    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config. When set (and only
1953    /// meaningful in chaos mode) the scheduler biases its nondeterminism points
1954    /// toward known race patterns rather than exploring uniformly.
1955    chaos_target_races: bool,
1956    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config. Under chaos a
1957    /// `sched_yield` opens or joins a yield epoch ([`Self::requeue_after`]).
1958    chaos: bool,
1959    /// Whether chaos change points are bounded
1960    /// ([`Self::bound_chaos_starvation`]): under `--chaos` with timer
1961    /// preemption and the default heuristic, and not replaying preemptions.
1962    /// There every change point is a random draw at a timer slice end. A
1963    /// preemption replay's change points carry the recorded priorities, which
1964    /// already hold any bound applied when they were recorded.
1965    chaos_bounds_starvation: bool,
1966    /// Under chaos, how many timer-slice change points have passed each runnable
1967    /// thread over since its last committed turn
1968    /// ([`Self::bound_chaos_starvation`]).
1969    chaos_passed_over: BTreeMap<DetTid, u32>,
1970
1971    /// Happens-before enforcement state, present only when the run carries a
1972    /// `HappensBeforeProgram`. Holds AFTER anchors until their BEFORE anchors
1973    /// fire, deterministically constructing an authored race ordering.
1974    happens_before: Option<HbRuntime>,
1975}
1976
1977type StacktraceEventsIter = Peekable<IntoIter<(u64, Option<SchedEvent>, Option<PathBuf>)>>;

1979// type ThreadTree = HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>;
1980#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
1981pub struct ThreadTree {
1982    /// Invariant: this is None only if `tree` is also empty.
1983    /// That is any ThreadTree of size zero or more has a root.
1984    root: Option<DetTid>,
1985    /// Invariant: every `DetTid` in the tree has an entry here, though if it is a leaf,
1986    /// it will have an empty children-vector.
1987    tree: HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1988
1989    /// The subset of threads that are also thread group leaders.  This tracks both the
1990    /// Tid, but it is (numerically) the same as Pid for group leaders in Linux.
1991    thread_group_leaders: HashSet<DetTid>,
1992
1993    /// Go from a Tid to the Pid/Tid of the containing process (i.e. a reverse view of a
1994    /// transitive closure of `thread_tree`).  Every thread should have an entry in
1995    /// here. If, however, a thread is a group leader, this will map back to itself.
1996    thread_to_leader: HashMap<DetTid, DetPid>,
1997
1998    /// Reverse map from a process (group-leader `DetPid`) to its effective Linux
1999    /// wait parent, including `CLONE_PARENT`. Populated when a new group leader
2000    /// is registered; the root process has no entry. Entries survive logical
2001    /// exit until the terminal status is consumed.
2002    process_parent: HashMap<DetPid, DetPid>,
2003
2004    /// Linux child-wait identity for each process leader. Unlike the thread
2005    /// tree edge, this records the effective wait parent after CLONE_PARENT,
2006    /// the exact creating task for __WNOTHREAD, clone exit-signal class, and
2007    /// mutable process-group/session membership.
2008    process_wait: HashMap<DetPid, ProcessWaitMetadata>,
2009
2010    /// How many times each process has exec'd successfully (Linux's
2011    /// `self_exec_id`), for the exit-signal rule a parent's exec applies
2012    /// (`ProcessWaitMetadata::parent_exec_generation`).
2013    exec_generations: HashMap<DetPid, u64>,
2014
2015    /// Processes that made themselves child subreapers with
2016    /// `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)` (Linux's
2017    /// `signal_struct::is_child_subreaper`). The flag survives exec, because
2018    /// the process keeps its pid, and a forked child does not inherit it.
2019    child_subreapers: HashSet<DetPid>,
2020
2021    /// The parent-death signal each task armed with `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)`
2022    /// that Detcore sends itself (`Scheduler::deliver_parent_death_signals`,
2023    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440>): Linux's per-task
2024    /// `pdeath_signal`. Every new task starts with none, as on Linux; exec
2025    /// keeps it.
2026    parent_death_signals: BTreeMap<DetTid, i32>,
2027
2028    /// For each process, the thread whose exit sends its tasks' parent-death
2029    /// signals: Linux's `real_parent`. It starts as the thread that created
2030    /// the process (its creator's for `CLONE_PARENT`, `wait_owner`), moves to
2031    /// a live sibling of that thread when it exits, and to the new reaper's
2032    /// thread when its whole process does (`reparent_child`). An orphan given
2033    /// to the container's init has none: init does not exit during the run.
2034    parent_death_parents: BTreeMap<DetPid, DetTid>,
2035
2036    /// Processes whose parent exited with no live child subreaper above it,
2037    /// so Linux gave them to the container's init (`reparent_orphans`). Their
2038    /// `process_parent` and wait metadata still name the dead parent, as
2039    /// before subreapers were modeled (exit classification reads that link),
2040    /// but a subreaper search must not climb past them: their real parent is
2041    /// init.
2042    init_orphans: HashSet<DetPid>,
2043
2044    /// Processes whose children Linux reaps automatically at exit, because the
2045    /// process set SIGCHLD to `SIG_IGN` or set `SA_NOCLDWAIT` on it
2046    /// (`do_notify_parent`'s autoreap test). The value is `(ignored,
2047    /// nocldwait)`; a process with neither has no entry. A forked child
2048    /// inherits it; exec keeps it only while SIGCHLD is ignored, because
2049    /// `flush_signal_handlers` resets a caught or default action and clears its
2050    /// flags (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091>).
2051    sigchld_autoreap: HashMap<DetPid, (bool, bool)>,
2052
2053    /// Processes whose exit the scheduler granted (`ResourceID::Exit` for the
2054    /// whole group, or for its last live thread), so that their logical exit
2055    /// is fixed between committed turns. A process that dies without one is
2056    /// recorded only at its host-timed deregistration (`reparent_orphans`).
2057    granted_exits: HashSet<DetPid>,
2058
2059    /// How many PID namespaces below the container's each process lives in;
2060    /// absent means zero. A child inherits its creator's depth and adds one
2061    /// for `CLONE_NEWPID` (`enter_new_pid_namespace`); `unshare` and `setns`
2062    /// are refused, so `clone` is the only way in. Linux's `find_new_reaper`
2063    /// looks for a subreaper only among ancestors at the exited process's
2064    /// own depth (`find_child_reaper`).
2065    pid_ns_depth: HashMap<DetPid, u32>,
2066    /// Processes created with `CLONE_NEWPID`: each is the init of a PID
2067    /// namespace, which Linux marks `SIGNAL_UNKILLABLE` against senders inside
2068    /// it (`sigkill_retirement`).
2069    pid_namespace_inits: HashSet<DetPid>,
2070    /// Each nested task's pid in each namespace it belongs to, recorded at its
2071    /// creation (`pid_namespaces`).
2072    pub(crate) pid_namespaces: pid_namespaces::PidNamespaces,
2073}
2074
2075#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
2076struct ProcessWaitMetadata {
2077    wait_parent: Option<DetPid>,
2078    wait_owner: DetTid,
2079    /// The child's exit signal as Linux keeps it (`task_struct::exit_signal`):
2080    /// the clone signal, its creator's for CLONE_PARENT, and SIGCHLD after the
2081    /// child's own successful exec. It decides the wait class (a child whose
2082    /// signal is not SIGCHLD is reaped only with __WCLONE or __WALL); the
2083    /// notification can differ (`ThreadTree::notification_signal`).
2084    exit_signal: libc::c_int,
2085    /// The wait parent's exec count when this child was created (Linux's
2086    /// `parent_exec_id`), or its creator's for CLONE_PARENT.
2087    parent_exec_generation: u64,
2088    process_group: DetPid,
2089    session: DetPid,
2090    /// Whether the process has not exec'd since it was created (Linux's
2091    /// `PF_FORKNOEXEC`): its parent may move it to another process group only
2092    /// until it execs (`ThreadTree::setpgid_decision`).
2093    forked_without_exec: bool,
2094}
2095
2096use pretty::Doc;
2097use pretty::RcDoc;
2098
2099/// The process group or session a process inherited from outside the
2100/// container's PID namespace: the root process's, until it calls `setsid` or
2101/// `setpgid`, and every descendant's that keeps it. Linux shows a process's
2102/// group or session from outside the reader's namespace as 0.
2103pub(crate) const OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE: DetPid = DetPid::from_raw(0);
2104
2105use self::replayer::DesyncStats;
2106use self::replayer::Replayer;
2107
2108impl ThreadTree {
2109    /// Internal helper. Add a [child] process to the tree, with the parent being `None`
2110    /// if it's the root of the tree.
2111    fn add_edge(&mut self, parent: Option<DetTid>, child: DetTid) {
2112        match parent {
2113            None => {
2114                self.root = Some(child);
2115                // Ensure an entry, even if the children vector is empty:
2116                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
2117            }
2118            Some(p) => {
2119                let vec = self.tree.entry(p).or_default();
2120                vec.push(child);
2121                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
2122            }
2123        }
2124    }
2125
2126    /// Read the children of a thread, which is assumed to have an entry in the tree.
2127    pub fn get_children(&self, parent: &DetTid) -> &Vec<DetTid> {
2128        self.tree
2129            .get(parent)
2130            .expect("Internal failure: tid was not found in ThreadTree")
2131    }
2132
2133    /// Convert to pretty-printed document.
2134    ///
2135    /// For example, a binary tree of depth two may print as `(1 (2 3 4) (5 6 7))`,
2136    /// showing each thread ID grouped with its children.
2137    ///
2138    /// The thread_group_leaders argument is used for additional context into account when
2139    /// pretty-printing a `ThreadTree`.  This will indicate which children are within new
2140    /// thread groups using square brackets:
2141    ///
2142    ///   `[1 [2 [3] 4] (5 6 7)]`
2143    // TODO: it would also be nice to store a fixed prefix of the binary name and listing
2144    // that along with the thread ID.
2145    pub fn pretty_print(&self) -> String {
2146        fn walk<'a>(
2147            tt: &'a HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
2148            tgl: &HashSet<DetTid>,
2149            current: &DetTid,
2150        ) -> RcDoc<'a, ()> {
2151            if let Some(children) = tt.get(current) {
2152                if tgl.contains(current) {
2153                    RcDoc::text("[")
2154                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
2155                        .append(if children.is_empty() {
2156                            RcDoc::text("")
2157                        } else {
2158                            RcDoc::text(" ").append(
2159                                RcDoc::intersperse(
2160                                    children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
2161                                    Doc::line(),
2162                                )
2163                                .nest(1)
2164                                .group(),
2165                            )
2166                        })
2167                        .append(RcDoc::text("]"))
2168                } else if children.is_empty() {
2169                    RcDoc::as_string(current)
2170                } else {
2171                    RcDoc::text("(")
2172                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
2173                        .append(RcDoc::text(" "))
2174                        .append(
2175                            RcDoc::intersperse(
2176                                children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
2177                                Doc::line(),
2178                            )
2179                            .nest(1)
2180                            .group(),
2181                        )
2182                        .append(RcDoc::text(")"))
2183                }
2184            } else {
2185                // This should be unreachable if the invariants are maintained:
2186                RcDoc::text("<ThreadTree corrupt, missing tid: ")
2187                    .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
2188                    .append(RcDoc::text(">"))
2189            }
2190        }
2191
2192        let root = match self.root {
2193            None => return "[]".into(),
2194            Some(root) => root,
2195        };
2196
2197        let doc = walk(&self.tree, &self.thread_group_leaders, &root);
2198        let width = 100;
2199        let mut vec = Vec::new();
2200        doc.render(width, &mut vec).unwrap();
2201        String::from_utf8(vec).unwrap()
2202    }
2203
2204    #[allow(dead_code)]
2205    /// Number of threads with entries in the tree.
2206    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
2207        self.tree.len()
2208    }
2209
2210    /// Simultaneously update the thread tree and leader tracking to reflect the creation
2211    /// of a new child thread.
2212    #[cfg(test)]
2213    pub fn add_child(
2214        &mut self,
2215        parent_dettid: DetTid,
2216        child_dettid: DetTid,
2217        is_group_leader: bool,
2218    ) {
2219        self.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
2220            parent_dettid,
2221            child_dettid,
2222            is_group_leader,
2223            false,
2224            libc::SIGCHLD,
2225        );
2226    }
2227
2228    /// Add a child while preserving the Linux identities used by wait-family
2229    /// selection. `clone_parent` changes the child's effective wait parent and
2230    /// owner to the caller's own parent task; threads never enter this process
2231    /// metadata table.
2232    pub fn add_child_with_wait_metadata(
2233        &mut self,
2234        parent_dettid: DetTid,
2235        child_dettid: DetTid,
2236        is_group_leader: bool,
2237        clone_parent: bool,
2238        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
2239    ) {
2240        // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
2241        if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
2242            self.add_edge(None, child_dettid);
2243        } else {
2244            self.add_edge(Some(parent_dettid), child_dettid);
2245        }
2246        // Linux's copy_process starts every new task with no parent-death
2247        // signal; a reused tid does not keep the old task's.
2248        self.parent_death_signals.remove(&child_dettid);
2249        if is_group_leader {
2250            self.thread_group_leaders.insert(child_dettid);
2251            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, child_dettid);
2252            // A reused pid starts with neither Linux attribute: the flag is
2253            // not inherited, and the new process has its own live parent.
2254            self.child_subreapers.remove(&child_dettid);
2255            self.init_orphans.remove(&child_dettid);
2256            self.granted_exits.remove(&child_dettid);
2257            // A forked child copies its creator's signal dispositions.
2258            let inherited = self
2259                .thread_to_leader
2260                .get(&parent_dettid)
2261                .filter(|_| parent_dettid != child_dettid)
2262                .and_then(|creator| self.sigchld_autoreap.get(creator))
2263                .copied();
2264            match inherited {
2265                Some(disposition) => self.sigchld_autoreap.insert(child_dettid, disposition),
2266                None => self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&child_dettid),
2267            };
2268            // The child lives in its creator's PID namespace until
2269            // `enter_new_pid_namespace` says otherwise.
2270            let creator_depth = self
2271                .thread_to_leader
2272                .get(&parent_dettid)
2273                .filter(|_| parent_dettid != child_dettid)
2274                .map_or(0, |creator| self.pid_ns_depth(*creator));
2275            if creator_depth == 0 {
2276                self.pid_ns_depth.remove(&child_dettid);
2277            } else {
2278                self.pid_ns_depth.insert(child_dettid, creator_depth);
2279            }
2280            // A reused pid is not a namespace init until registered as one.
2281            self.pid_namespace_inits.remove(&child_dettid);
2282            if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
2283                self.process_wait.insert(
2284                    child_dettid,
2285                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
2286                        wait_parent: None,
2287                        wait_owner: child_dettid,
2288                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
2289                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
2290                        // The root process inherits its process group and
2291                        // session from outside the container's PID namespace,
2292                        // as a process started by `unshare --pid --fork` does,
2293                        // and Linux shows such ids as 0 (`OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE`).
2294                        process_group: OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE,
2295                        session: OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE,
2296                        forked_without_exec: true,
2297                    },
2298                );
2299            } else {
2300                let parent_process = self
2301                    .thread_to_leader
2302                    .get(&parent_dettid)
2303                    .copied()
2304                    .expect("process child parent must have a thread-group leader");
2305                let parent_metadata = self.process_wait.get(&parent_process).copied().unwrap_or(
2306                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
2307                        wait_parent: None,
2308                        wait_owner: parent_dettid,
2309                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
2310                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
2311                        process_group: parent_process,
2312                        session: parent_process,
2313                        forked_without_exec: true,
2314                    },
2315                );
2316                // CLONE_PARENT makes the child a sibling of its creator: Linux
2317                // gives it the creator's parent, the creator's `parent_exec_id`
2318                // and the exit signal of the creator's process, whatever
2319                // signal the clone asked for (`copy_process`).
2320                let (wait_parent, wait_owner, exit_signal, parent_exec_generation) = if clone_parent
2321                {
2322                    (
2323                        parent_metadata.wait_parent,
2324                        parent_metadata.wait_owner,
2325                        parent_metadata.exit_signal,
2326                        parent_metadata.parent_exec_generation,
2327                    )
2328                } else {
2329                    (
2330                        Some(parent_process),
2331                        parent_dettid,
2332                        exit_signal,
2333                        self.exec_generation(parent_process),
2334                    )
2335                };
2336                if let Some(wait_parent) = wait_parent {
2337                    self.process_parent.insert(child_dettid, wait_parent);
2338                }
2339                // Linux's real_parent: the creating thread, or with
2340                // CLONE_PARENT the creator's own real parent, which
2341                // `parent_death_parents` keeps current where `wait_owner` may
2342                // name a thread that has since left.
2343                let real_parent = if clone_parent {
2344                    self.parent_death_parents.get(&parent_process).copied()
2345                } else {
2346                    Some(parent_dettid)
2347                };
2348                match real_parent {
2349                    Some(parent) => self.parent_death_parents.insert(child_dettid, parent),
2350                    None => self.parent_death_parents.remove(&child_dettid),
2351                };
2352                self.process_wait.insert(
2353                    child_dettid,
2354                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
2355                        wait_parent,
2356                        wait_owner,
2357                        exit_signal,
2358                        parent_exec_generation,
2359                        process_group: parent_metadata.process_group,
2360                        session: parent_metadata.session,
2361                        forked_without_exec: true,
2362                    },
2363                );
2364            }
2365        } else {
2366            let parent_leader: DetPid =
2367                    *self
2368                        .thread_to_leader
2369                        .get(&parent_dettid)
2370                        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
2371                            panic!("recv_create_child_thread: parent {} of child dtid {} does not exist in thread_to_leader map!",
2372                                   parent_dettid, child_dettid);
2373                        });
2374            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, parent_leader);
2375        }
2376    }
2377
2378    /// The process that created `pid` (its parent process), if `pid` is not the
2379    /// root process. Returns a possibly-stale parent if that process has since
2380    /// exited; callers deliver through `select_signal_target`, which drops a
2381    /// signal to a `Gone` target.
2382    pub fn parent_process(&self, pid: &DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2383        self.process_parent.get(pid).copied()
2384    }
2385
2386    /// The processes whose parent process is `parent` and that it has not
2387    /// reaped yet (`process_parent`), in pid order.
2388    pub fn unreaped_children_of(&self, parent: DetPid) -> Vec<DetPid> {
2389        let mut children: Vec<DetPid> = self
2390            .process_parent
2391            .iter()
2392            .filter(|(_, owner)| **owner == parent)
2393            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
2394            .collect();
2395        children.sort();
2396        children
2397    }
2398
2399    /// Preserve a surviving exec task's children when Linux replaces its TID
2400    /// with the process leader's. The creation tree remains historical; only
2401    /// the current task identity used by `__WNOTHREAD` changes. Scope the move
2402    /// to this effective parent so retained records from an older use of the
2403    /// same raw TID and `CLONE_PARENT` children keep their own wait identities.
2404    fn transfer_exec_wait_owner(&mut self, process: DetPid, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
2405        for metadata in self.process_wait.values_mut() {
2406            if metadata.wait_parent == Some(process) && metadata.wait_owner == former {
2407                metadata.wait_owner = leader;
2408            }
2409        }
2410    }
2411
2412    /// The parent-death bookkeeping of the exec'ing task `former`, which
2413    /// survives under the leader's tid `leader` (Linux's `exchange_tids`):
2414    /// the children whose parent it is keep it, and its own parent-death
2415    /// signal replaces the destroyed leader's.
2416    fn transfer_exec_parent_death(&mut self, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
2417        if former == leader {
2418            return;
2419        }
2420        for parent in self.parent_death_parents.values_mut() {
2421            if *parent == former {
2422                *parent = leader;
2423            }
2424        }
2425        match self.parent_death_signals.remove(&former) {
2426            Some(signal) => self.parent_death_signals.insert(leader, signal),
2427            None => self.parent_death_signals.remove(&leader),
2428        };
2429    }
2430
2431    /// `process`'s successful exec count (`exec_generations`).
2432    fn exec_generation(&self, process: DetPid) -> u64 {
2433        self.exec_generations.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
2434    }
2435
2436    /// Apply Linux's exit-signal rules for a successful exec by `process`: its
2437    /// own exit signal becomes SIGCHLD (so it leaves the clone wait class),
2438    /// and its exec count advances, which turns the notification of each child
2439    /// it created before this exec into SIGCHLD (`notification_signal`).
2440    pub fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
2441        *self.exec_generations.entry(process).or_insert(0) += 1;
2442        if self
2443            .sigchld_autoreap
2444            .get(&process)
2445            .is_some_and(|(ignored, _)| !ignored)
2446        {
2447            self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&process);
2448        }
2449        if let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&process) {
2450            metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
2451            metadata.forked_without_exec = false;
2452        }
2453    }
2454
2455    /// The signal Linux notifies `child`'s wait parent with when `child`
2456    /// exits (`do_notify_parent`): its exit signal, except that a signal other
2457    /// than SIGCHLD becomes SIGCHLD once the parent has exec'd since creating
2458    /// the child (its `parent_exec_id` no longer matches). 0 means none.
2459    /// `None` for a process without wait metadata.
2460    pub fn notification_signal(&self, child: DetPid) -> Option<libc::c_int> {
2461        let metadata = self.process_wait.get(&child)?;
2462        let parent_execed = metadata
2463            .wait_parent
2464            .is_some_and(|parent| self.exec_generation(parent) != metadata.parent_exec_generation);
2465        Some(if metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD && parent_execed {
2466            libc::SIGCHLD
2467        } else {
2468            metadata.exit_signal
2469        })
2470    }
2471
2472    pub fn process_group(&self, pid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2473        self.process_wait
2474            .get(&pid)
2475            .map(|metadata| metadata.process_group)
2476    }
2477
2478    /// The session of the process `pid`, as [`Self::process_group`].
2479    pub fn session(&self, pid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2480        self.process_wait.get(&pid).map(|metadata| metadata.session)
2481    }
2482
2483    /// Whether a process group `group` exists: whether any process of the
2484    /// model that Linux still has belongs to it, a zombie included. `gone`
2485    /// names the processes whose wait record outlived them: an automatically
2486    /// reaped child, an orphan the namespace's init reaped
2487    /// (`Scheduler::process_exists`).
2488    fn process_group_exists(&self, group: DetPid, gone: &dyn Fn(DetPid) -> bool) -> bool {
2489        self.process_wait
2490            .iter()
2491            .any(|(pid, metadata)| metadata.process_group == group && !gone(*pid))
2492    }
2493
2494    /// Linux's answer to `setsid()` by the process `process`
2495    /// (`ksys_setsid`): EPERM where a process group with its id exists, its
2496    /// own included, and otherwise success, which makes it the leader of a
2497    /// new session and process group (`Self::create_session` records that).
2498    /// `gone` as for `Self::process_group_exists`.
2499    pub fn setsid_decision(
2500        &self,
2501        process: DetPid,
2502        gone: &dyn Fn(DetPid) -> bool,
2503    ) -> Result<(), Errno> {
2504        if self.process_group_exists(process, gone) {
2505            return Err(Errno::EPERM);
2506        }
2507        if !self.process_wait.contains_key(&process) {
2508            return Err(Errno::ESRCH);
2509        }
2510        Ok(())
2511    }
2512
2513    /// Linux's answer to `setpgid(pid, pgid)` by the process `caller`
2514    /// (`sys_setpgid`), and on success the process to move and the group to
2515    /// move it to (`Self::set_process_group` records that):
2516    /// - `pid` 0 is the caller, and `pgid` 0 is the process `pid` names;
2517    ///   a negative `pgid` is EINVAL;
2518    /// - `pid` must name a process (EINVAL for another thread, ESRCH for
2519    ///   none), the caller or a child of it (ESRCH);
2520    /// - a child must be in the caller's session (EPERM) and not have
2521    ///   exec'd since it was created (EACCES);
2522    /// - a session leader cannot move (EPERM);
2523    /// - a group other than the process's own id must exist in the caller's
2524    ///   session (EPERM).
2525    ///
2526    /// `gone` names the processes Linux no longer has although their wait
2527    /// record remains (`Self::process_group_exists`), and `live_nonleader`
2528    /// the ids of live threads that lead no thread group
2529    /// (`Scheduler::signal_target_process`): EINVAL rather than ESRCH.
2530    pub fn setpgid_decision(
2531        &self,
2532        caller: DetPid,
2533        pid: libc::pid_t,
2534        pgid: libc::pid_t,
2535        gone: &dyn Fn(DetPid) -> bool,
2536        live_nonleader: &dyn Fn(DetPid) -> bool,
2537    ) -> Result<(DetPid, DetPid), Errno> {
2538        // In the kernel's order: a zero pid is the caller, a zero group is
2539        // then the pid, and only that group is checked for a negative value,
2540        // so `setpgid(-5, 0)` is EINVAL, not ESRCH.
2541        let pid = if pid == 0 { caller.as_raw() } else { pid };
2542        let pgid = if pgid == 0 { pid } else { pgid };
2543        if pgid < 0 {
2544            return Err(Errno::EINVAL);
2545        }
2546        let target = DetPid::from_raw(pid);
2547        let group = DetPid::from_raw(pgid);
2548        let Some(target_metadata) = self.process_wait.get(&target).filter(|_| !gone(target)) else {
2549            return Err(if live_nonleader(target) {
2550                Errno::EINVAL
2551            } else {
2552                Errno::ESRCH
2553            });
2554        };
2555        let caller_session = self
2556            .process_wait
2557            .get(&caller)
2558            .map(|metadata| metadata.session)
2559            .ok_or(Errno::ESRCH)?;
2560        if target != caller {
2561            if target_metadata.wait_parent != Some(caller) {
2562                return Err(Errno::ESRCH);
2563            }
2564            if target_metadata.session != caller_session {
2565                return Err(Errno::EPERM);
2566            }
2567            if !target_metadata.forked_without_exec {
2568                return Err(Errno::EACCES);
2569            }
2570        }
2571        if target_metadata.session == target {
2572            return Err(Errno::EPERM);
2573        }
2574        if group != target
2575            && !self.process_wait.iter().any(|(pid, metadata)| {
2576                metadata.process_group == group && metadata.session == caller_session && !gone(*pid)
2577            })
2578        {
2579            return Err(Errno::EPERM);
2580        }
2581        Ok((target, group))
2582    }
2583
2584    pub fn set_process_group(&mut self, pid: DetPid, process_group: DetPid) -> bool {
2585        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
2586            return false;
2587        };
2588        metadata.process_group = process_group;
2589        true
2590    }
2591
2592    /// Mirror a successful `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, on)` by `pid`.
2593    pub fn set_child_subreaper(&mut self, pid: DetPid, on: bool) {
2594        if on {
2595            self.child_subreapers.insert(pid);
2596        } else {
2597            self.child_subreapers.remove(&pid);
2598        }
2599    }
2600
2601    /// Whether `pid` is a child subreaper (`set_child_subreaper`).
2602    pub fn is_child_subreaper(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2603        self.child_subreapers.contains(&pid)
2604    }
2605
2606    /// Mirror a successful `rt_sigaction(SIGCHLD, ...)` by `pid`: whether its
2607    /// new action is `SIG_IGN`, and whether it carries `SA_NOCLDWAIT`.
2608    pub fn set_sigchld_disposition(&mut self, pid: DetPid, ignored: bool, nocldwait: bool) {
2609        if ignored || nocldwait {
2610            self.sigchld_autoreap.insert(pid, (ignored, nocldwait));
2611        } else {
2612            self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&pid);
2613        }
2614    }
2615
2616    /// Whether Linux reaps `pid`'s children automatically when they exit
2617    /// (`set_sigchld_disposition`).
2618    pub fn reaps_children_automatically(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2619        self.sigchld_autoreap.contains_key(&pid)
2620    }
2621
2622    /// Give `child` a new wait parent after its parent's process exited, as
2623    /// Linux's `reparent_leader` does: `reaper` and its thread `owner`. The
2624    /// exit signal becomes SIGCHLD, and the reaper's exec count is taken so
2625    /// that the notification is SIGCHLD too.
2626    fn reparent_child(&mut self, child: DetPid, reaper: DetPid, owner: DetTid) {
2627        let reaper_exec_generation = self.exec_generation(reaper);
2628        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&child) else {
2629            return;
2630        };
2631        metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
2632        metadata.wait_parent = Some(reaper);
2633        metadata.wait_owner = owner;
2634        metadata.parent_exec_generation = reaper_exec_generation;
2635        self.process_parent.insert(child, reaper);
2636        self.parent_death_parents.insert(child, owner);
2637    }
2638
2639    /// The children of `exited` whose new parent is still undecided: those
2640    /// whose wait parent is `exited` and that did not already go to init. In
2641    /// ascending pid order, because `process_wait` is a hash map and the
2642    /// order decides the order of the re-parenting records and wakes.
2643    fn undecided_orphans_of(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Vec<DetPid> {
2644        let mut orphans: Vec<DetPid> = self
2645            .process_wait
2646            .iter()
2647            .filter(|(child, metadata)| {
2648                metadata.wait_parent == Some(exited) && !self.is_init_orphan(**child)
2649            })
2650            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
2651            .collect();
2652        orphans.sort();
2653        orphans
2654    }
2655
2656    /// The process `tid` belongs to in the thread tree: its thread group's
2657    /// leader, or `None` for an unregistered thread.
2658    pub fn process_of(&self, tid: DetTid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2659        self.thread_to_leader.get(&tid).copied()
2660    }
2661
2662    /// `pid` was created with `CLONE_NEWPID`: it is the init of a PID
2663    /// namespace one level below its creator's (`pid_ns_depth`).
2664    pub fn enter_new_pid_namespace(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
2665        let depth = self.pid_ns_depth(pid) + 1;
2666        self.pid_ns_depth.insert(pid, depth);
2667    }
2668
2669    /// `pid_ns_depth` of `pid`.
2670    pub fn pid_ns_depth(&self, pid: DetPid) -> u32 {
2671        self.pid_ns_depth.get(&pid).copied().unwrap_or(0)
2672    }
2673
2674    /// Record that `child` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
2675    fn orphan_to_init(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
2676        self.init_orphans.insert(child);
2677        self.parent_death_parents.remove(&child);
2678    }
2679
2680    /// Whether `pid` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
2681    fn is_init_orphan(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2682        self.init_orphans.contains(&pid)
2683    }
2684
2685    /// `pid` was created with `CLONE_NEWPID` (`pid_namespace_inits`).
2686    pub fn mark_pid_namespace_init(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
2687        self.pid_namespace_inits.insert(pid);
2688    }
2689
2690    /// Whether `pid` is a PID namespace's init (`pid_namespace_inits`).
2691    pub fn is_pid_namespace_init(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2692        self.pid_namespace_inits.contains(&pid)
2693    }
2694
2695    pub fn create_session(&mut self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2696        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
2697            return false;
2698        };
2699        metadata.session = pid;
2700        metadata.process_group = pid;
2701        true
2702    }
2703
2704    /// Return the set of thread IDs in the "same process" as me (same TGID), including
2705    /// myself.
2706    ///
2707    /// Whether `tid` has been registered in the tree. A process the backend
2708    /// reports gone before it registers is not (asynchronous exit completion).
2709    pub fn contains(&self, tid: &DetTid) -> bool {
2710        self.thread_group_leaders.contains(tid) || self.thread_to_leader.contains_key(tid)
2711    }
2712
2713    /// Locks: takes scheduler lock.
2714    pub fn my_thread_group(&self, me: &DetTid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
2715        let root_tid: DetTid = if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(me) {
2716            *me
2717        } else {
2718            *self
2719                .thread_to_leader
2720                .get(me)
2721                .expect("thread must be in to_leader table")
2722        };
2723        let mut stack: Vec<DetTid> = vec![root_tid];
2724        let mut acc: Vec<DetTid> = vec![];
2725
2726        while let Some(first) = stack.pop() {
2727            if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(&first) && first != root_tid {
2728                continue; // Stop traversal when we walk into child processes.
2729            } else {
2730                acc.push(first);
2731            }
2732            let children = self.get_children(&first);
2733            stack.extend_from_slice(children);
2734        }
2735        assert!(acc.contains(me));
2736        acc
2737    }
2738}

2743        // this context:

2748// TODO (T137183027, T137184765)
2749/// A simple backoff strategy while we have any realtime/polling elements in the system.
2750/// When all external polling is removed, we can remove this.
2751struct Backoff {
2752    count: u64,
2753}
2754
2755impl Backoff {
2756    fn new() -> Self {
2757        Backoff { count: 0 }
2758    }
2759
2760    async fn further(&mut self, blocking: bool) {
2761        self.count += 1;
2762        const YIELDS_FIRST: u64 = 10;
2763        if blocking {
2764            if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
2765                std::thread::yield_now();
2766            } else {
2767                let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
2768                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros));
2769            }
2770        } else if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
2771            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
2772        } else {
2773            let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
2774            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros)).await;
2775        }
2776    }
2777
2778    fn reset(&mut self) {
2779        self.count = 0;
2780    }
2781}
2782
2783/// Sleep length for backoff round `round` (1-based): 2^round microseconds, capped at
2784/// 10 ms once 2^round would pass 8192 us.
2785fn backoff_sleep_micros(round: u64) -> u64 {
2786    if round > 13 { 10_000 } else { 1 << round }
2787}
2788
2789impl Default for Backoff {
2790    fn default() -> Self {
2791        Self::new()
2792    }
2793}

2811pub(crate) async fn sched_loop(sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>, timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) {
2812    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, false, None).await;
2813}
2814
2815pub(crate) async fn sched_loop_external(
2816    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2817    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2818    observer: SchedulerObserver,
2819) {
2820    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, true, Some(observer)).await;
2821}
2822
2823async fn sched_loop_inner(
2824    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2825    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2826    blocking_backoff: bool,
2827    observer: Option<SchedulerObserver>,
2828) {
2829    // The "daemon task starting up" INFO line is deliberately NOT emitted here.
2830    //
2831    // This body runs inside a `tokio::spawn`ed task (see
2832    // `GlobalState::initialize`), so the moment it is first polled is
2833    // unsynchronized with the spawning thread's continued bootstrap. That made
2834    // the line race the root thread's `USER RAND` / `CHAOSRAND` seeding lines
2835    // from `ThreadState::new`, and the L2 comparator reads the INFO stream as
2836    // ordered evidence: the two runs were identical as multisets and differed
2837    // only in this one line's position, which is a real `bitwise_parity: false`.
2838    //
2839    // The announcement is now emitted by whoever starts the daemon, in that
2840    // thread's program order, so it is deterministically sequenced after
2841    // `Scheduler::new`'s `SCHEDRAND` line and before the root `ThreadState`.
2842    // That is the order the ptrace backend already produced reliably.
2843    //
2844    // The observer callback stays here, at the point the task genuinely begins
2845    // executing, because it is a barrier signal for external backends and is
2846    // not part of the compared log stream. Moving the log does not cost us the
2847    // "it actually started" observation for the consumer that needs it.
2848    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2849        observer("daemon task starting; waiting for guest thread");
2850    }
2851    let (iv, stop_after_iter) = {
2852        // Block until queue is populated.
2853        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2854        (sched.started_up.clone(), sched.stop_after_iter)
2855    };
2856    if until_backend_failure(&sched, iv.get()).await.is_err() {
2857        return;
2858    }
2859    info!("[scheduler] guest in queue, scheduler proceeding..",);
2860    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2861        observer("guest registered; deterministic scheduler proceeding");
2862    }
2863    let mut iter: u64 = 0;
2864    // We keep track of whether the last turn was a SKIP:
2865    let mut last_res = Err(SkipTurn);
2866    let mut backoff = Backoff::new();
2867    let mut observed_turn = false;
2868
2869    loop {
2870        if sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failed() {
2871            return;
2872        }
2873        // TODO (T137183027, T137184765): as part of the current strategy for blocking IO ops (see
2874        // SPINNING below), we need to make sure that other threads can progress so we don't
2875        // busy-wait too tightly.
2876        if last_res.is_err() {
2877            backoff.further(blocking_backoff).await;
2878        } else {
2879            backoff.reset();
2880        }
2881
2882        trace!("[scheduler] loop iteration {}", iter);
2883        if stop_after_iter.is_some() && iter > stop_after_iter.unwrap() {
2884            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2885            tracing::warn!(
2886                "[scheduler] Early exit during sched loop iteration {} due to --stop-after-iter.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2887                iter,
2888                sched.full_summary()
2889            );
2890            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2891        }
2892        iter += 1;
2893
2894        // If there are NO threads left in the system, then we're truly done:
2895        {
2896            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2897            sched.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop);
2898            if sched.backend_failed() {
2899                return;
2900            }
2901            // A thread held at a happens-before gate is in neither the run queue
2902            // nor `blocked`, but it is still a live thread: without this the loop
2903            // exited while it waited and the guest hung with no scheduler and no
2904            // deadlock report (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
2905            if sched.run_queue.is_empty()
2906                && sched.blocked.is_empty()
2907                && sched
2908                    .happens_before
2909                    .as_ref()
2910                    .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty())
2911                && sched.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
2912                && sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty()
2913                && sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty()
2914                && !sched.control_barrier()
2915            {
2916                // A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired names an ordering
2917                // the run never exercised: refuse by name instead of passing.
2918                // Printed like the deadlock report (no timestamp), so it is
2919                // byte-identical across runs.
2920                if let Some(report) = sched
2921                    .happens_before
2922                    .as_ref()
2923                    .and_then(HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report)
2924                {
2925                    eprintln!("{}", report);
2926                    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2927                }
2928                info!("[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.");
2929                if let Some(refusal) = sched.unreplayed_rejoins() {
2930                    drop(sched);
2931                    exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2932                }
2933                if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2934                    observer("run queue empty; scheduler completed");
2935                }
2936                return;
2937            } else if let Some(stop) = sched.stop_after_turn
2938                && sched.turn > stop
2939            {
2940                tracing::warn!(
2941                    "[scheduler] Early exit during turn {} due to --stop-after-turn.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2942                    sched.turn,
2943                    sched.full_summary()
2944                );
2945                immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2946            }
2947        }
2948
2949        // Otherwise we trust the turn function to either choose a runnable thread or wait
2950        // until something blocked is ready to run again.
2951        last_res = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), timer.clone(), &last_res).await;
2952
2953        // A vfork barrier whose backend event never arrived. Taken here, after
2954        // either turn function, because both run step2a: the ordinary one
2955        // through `step2_process_blocked` and the signal-control one through
2956        // `step2_drain_prefix`.
2957        let vfork_refusal = sched.lock().unwrap().vfork_barrier_refusal.take();
2958        if let Some(refusal) = vfork_refusal {
2959            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2960        }
2961        // A SIGKILL whose victims' deaths or exit publications never arrived
2962        // (`Scheduler::SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE`).
2963        let sigkill_refusal = sched.lock().unwrap().sigkill_fence_refusal.take();
2964        if let Some(refusal) = sigkill_refusal {
2965            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2966        }
2967
2968        // A terminal deadlock ends the run here, alongside the two
2969        // `--stop-after-*` exits above, rather than by panicking out of the
2970        // scheduler task (see `report_terminal_deadlock`).
2971        //
2972        // Printed with `eprintln!` rather than `tracing::error!` on purpose: the
2973        // tracing writer prefixes a real wall-clock timestamp, and this report
2974        // is required to be byte-identical across runs of the same program.
2975        let terminal = {
2976            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2977            let is_refusal = sched.terminal_is_refusal;
2978            sched
2979                .take_terminal_deadlock()
2980                .map(|report| (report, is_refusal))
2981        };
2982        if let Some((report, is_refusal)) = terminal {
2983            eprintln!("{}", report);
2984            if is_refusal {
2985                // A happens-before spec the guest cannot satisfy: a policy
2986                // refusal, distinct from the guest's status and from a failure.
2987                std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2988            }
2989            report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(&report);
2990            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2991        }
2992        // Virtual time ran out under a configured --scheduler-turn-cost: end
2993        // the run the same way, rather than saturate the clock.
2994        if let Some(report) = sched.lock().unwrap().terminal_clock_exhaustion.take() {
2995            eprintln!("{}", report);
2996            immediate_fatal_exit();
2997        }
2998
2999        if last_res.is_ok() && !observed_turn {
3000            if let Some(observer) = &observer {
3001                observer("completed a deterministic scheduling turn");
3002            }
3003            observed_turn = true;
3004        }
3005    }
3006}
3007
3008/// A place in the daemon loop, inside one of its scheduler-lock holds, where a
3009/// test can land a host-timed backend report. Production builds compile
3010/// [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] to nothing.
3011///
3012/// Two reports reach the scheduler from backend threads at host-chosen times
3013/// near the end of a run: the SaBRe ptrace supervisor's
3014/// `complete_physical_process_exit` when the kernel delivers a process's final
3015/// wait status, and a dead thread's second, reactive `logically_kill_thread`
3016/// from its exit hook. Each can take the scheduler lock between any two of the
3017/// daemon's lock holds. These points sit before the top-of-loop exit check and
3018/// on both sides of the empty-queue step's decision, the two decisions that
3019/// read that state, so a test can land a report at each point in turn, with no
3020/// sleeps.
3021#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3022enum SchedLoopPoint {
3023    /// In the top-of-loop exit check's lock hold, before it reads any state.
3024    LoopTop,
3025    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, before it reads any state.
3026    BeforeEmptyQueue,
3027    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, after it has decided.
3028    AfterEmptyQueue,
3029}
3030
3031/// What the scheduler does with a child process's exit notification to its
3032/// parent, decided at the child's exit grant
3033/// (`Scheduler::classify_child_exit_notification`).
3034#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3035pub(crate) enum ChildExitNotification {
3036    /// Linux sends nothing: the parent explicitly ignores SIGCHLD, whether or
3037    /// not it blocks it.
3038    None,
3039    /// Linux discards the signal at generation: SIGCHLD is default-ignored and
3040    /// the receiving task does not block it.
3041    Discard,
3042    /// Linux delivers the signal: the parent catches it, or the receiving task
3043    /// blocks it (a blocked signal stays pending).
3044    Deliver,
3045    /// Hermit cannot classify the notification; the synthetic SIGCHLD path
3046    /// applies as before.
3047    Undecided,
3048}
3049
3050/// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order for an effective SIGCHLD: explicit SIG_IGN
3051/// suppresses it regardless of blocking; a blocked signal stays pending; a
3052/// caught one is delivered; a default-ignored, unblocked one is discarded.
3053pub(crate) fn classify_sigchld_notification(
3054    ignored: bool,
3055    caught: bool,
3056    blocked: bool,
3057) -> ChildExitNotification {
3058    if ignored {
3059        ChildExitNotification::None
3060    } else if blocked || caught {
3061        ChildExitNotification::Deliver
3062    } else {
3063        ChildExitNotification::Discard
3064    }
3065}
3066
3067/// A hex signal mask field (`SigIgn`, `SigCgt`, `SigBlk`) of
3068/// `/proc/<pid>/status`, or of `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/status` for a thread.
3069#[cfg_attr(test, allow(dead_code))]
3070fn proc_status_signal_mask(pid: DetPid, tid: Option<DetTid>, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
3071    // Refused, as `read_kernel_signal_state` is, where guest thread IDs do not
3072    // name host tasks.
3073    if crate::syscalls::host_signal_state_reads_refused() {
3074        return None;
3075    }
3076    let path = match tid {
3077        Some(tid) => format!("/proc/{}/task/{}/status", pid.as_raw(), tid.as_raw()),
3078        None => format!("/proc/{}/status", pid.as_raw()),
3079    };
3080    parse_proc_status_signal_mask(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?, field)
3081}
3082
3083fn parse_proc_status_signal_mask(status: &str, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
3084    status.lines().find_map(|line| {
3085        let value = line.strip_prefix(field)?.strip_prefix(':')?;
3086        u64::from_str_radix(value.trim(), 16).ok()
3087    })
3088}

3090/// Not an error, but simply a turn that cannot do productive work.
3091#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
3092pub struct SkipTurn;
3093
3094/// The release barrier's watchdog expired (`step2_release_signaled_background`):
3095/// committed signals armed these background threads, and they had still not
3096/// posted their continuations when it fired. Either the signal reached them
3097/// later than the barrier waits, or it never ended their calls (the arming
3098/// was wrong). Either way their admission point can no longer be fixed by the
3099/// scheduler, so the run is refused instead of being continued with an order
3100/// that host timing decides (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
3101#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
3102pub struct SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
3103    /// The armed threads that posted no continuation, in `DetTid` order.
3104    pub unposted: Vec<DetTid>,
3105    /// How long, in host time, the barrier had waited when it refused.
3106    pub waited: Duration,
3107}
3108
3109impl std::fmt::Display for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
3110    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
3111        write!(
3112            f,
3113            "hermit refused to continue the run: the signaled background threads {:?} \
3114             posted no continuation within {:?} of the release barrier (the signal \
3115             that armed them did not end their calls in that time), so their admission \
3116             order would depend on host timing",
3117            self.unposted.iter().map(|t| t.as_raw()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
3118            self.waited
3119        )
3120    }
3121}
3122
3123impl std::error::Error for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {}
3124
3125/// Which of its two waits a vfork barrier was in when step2a's valve expired
3126/// (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`).
3127#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
3128pub enum VforkBarrierState {
3129    /// The parent's vfork was granted and its child has not registered.
3130    Pending,
3131    /// The registered child reached a release edge (its `Exit` grant, its
3132    /// successful exec, or its logical kill) while its parent was alive.
3133    Released,
3134}
3135
3136/// One vfork barrier that was still waiting for a backend event when step2a's
3137/// valve expired.
3138#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
3139pub struct VforkBarrierWait {
3140    /// The vfork parent.
3141    pub parent: DetTid,
3142    /// Its registered child, or `None` while the barrier is `Pending`.
3143    pub child: Option<DetTid>,
3144    /// Which wait the barrier was in.
3145    pub state: VforkBarrierState,
3146}
3147
3148impl VforkBarrierWait {
3149    /// The backend event the barrier was waiting for.
3150    pub fn awaited(&self) -> &'static str {
3151        match self.state {
3152            VforkBarrierState::Pending => "the child's registration",
3153            VforkBarrierState::Released => "the parent's continuation or retirement",
3154        }
3155    }
3156}
3157
3158/// Step2a's valve expired (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`): a vfork
3159/// barrier waited, committing nothing, for a backend event that had not
3160/// arrived when it fired. Selecting other threads instead would let host
3161/// timing decide the schedule, so the run is refused
3162/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>).
3163#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
3164pub struct VforkBarrierRefusal {
3165    /// The barriers still waiting, in parent `DetTid` order.
3166    pub waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait>,
3167    /// How long, in host time, step2a had waited when it refused.
3168    pub waited: Duration,
3169}
3170
3171impl std::fmt::Display for VforkBarrierRefusal {
3172    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
3173        write!(
3174            f,
3175            "hermit refused to continue the run: vfork barriers waited {:?} for backend \
3176             events that never arrived:",
3177            self.waited
3178        )?;
3179        for wait in &self.waits {
3180            write!(f, " parent {}", wait.parent.as_raw())?;
3181            match wait.child {
3182                Some(child) => write!(f, " (child {})", child.as_raw())?,
3183                None => write!(f, " (no child registered)")?,
3184            }
3185            write!(f, " {:?}, awaiting {};", wait.state, wait.awaited())?;
3186        }
3187        Ok(())
3188    }
3189}
3190
3191impl std::error::Error for VforkBarrierRefusal {}
3192
3193/// End the run on a scheduler refusal: write it to stderr and exit with
3194/// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`, the status for "hermit examined the run and
3195/// refused it", as the network replay refusal does. Only the ptrace backend
3196/// arms the release barrier or runs record/replay, and a ptrace guest does not
3197/// outlive this process (Reverie sets `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`). A vfork barrier
3198/// refusal can come from any backend; it ends the run the way a terminal
3199/// deadlock refusal does. In Hermit's default container no guest outlives it:
3200/// the scheduler then runs in the init of the private PID namespace that
3201/// `Container::run` forks the guest into, and when a namespace init exits the
3202/// kernel `SIGKILL`s every remaining member (hermit-cli's container.rs,
3203/// `on_container_init_stop_signal`). That does not hold everywhere. With
3204/// `--no-namespace` the run gets no PID namespace, and hermit-cli's run.rs
3205/// (`log_cap_refusal`) names, for every backend, a way its guest can outlive an
3206/// exit like this one, ptrace's being the window before `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`
3207/// binds the guest. On DBT the scheduler runs in the DBT runtime
3208/// (`GlobalState::init_for_external_scheduler`), and the DynamoRIO guest is a
3209/// plain child of hermit that no PID namespace binds.
3210pub(crate) fn exit_on_scheduler_refusal(refusal: &dyn std::fmt::Display) -> ! {
3211    {
3212        use std::io::Write;
3213        let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
3214    }
3215    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
3216}

3218/// Refuse a fail-closed run at the point where the guest would observe an
3219/// expiration of a POSIX timer that notifies with real-time signal `signo`,
3220/// which Detcore does not deliver from a timer (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3893):
3221/// at the expiration itself, or later, where a pending one becomes observable
3222/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
3223/// What `Scheduler::fire_thread_timer` does with a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer's
3224/// expiration of a standard signal (`Scheduler::thread_timer_send`).
3225#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3226enum ThreadTimerSend {
3227    /// The signal is not pending on the thread: send it.
3228    Send,
3229    /// This timer's own earlier expiration is still pending there: Linux
3230    /// counts an overrun and queues nothing.
3231    Overrun,
3232    /// Another copy is pending there, which a send would merge into: refuse,
3233    /// naming why.
3234    Refuse(String),
3235}
3236
3237/// What Linux does with a real-time POSIX timer expiration, as far as the
3238/// guest could tell (`Scheduler::real_time_expiration_fate`).
3239#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3240pub(crate) enum RealTimeFate {
3241    /// Nothing can see it.
3242    Discarded,
3243    /// Queued where nothing can observe it yet: kept pending.
3244    Queued,
3245    /// The guest would see it now: the run refuses.
3246    Deliverable,
3247}
3248
3249/// Set, and never cleared, the first time a real-time timer expiration is
3250/// kept pending (`Scheduler::pending_real_time_expirations`). Until then no
3251/// call needs to ask the scheduler about pending ones, which keeps that
3252/// question off every signal-mask change and wait of a program that arms no
3253/// such timer. Only a backend that models signal targets keeps any pending,
3254/// and on it, ptrace, the tool and the scheduler share this process. It is set
3255/// at a timed pop and read by a thread in its own turn, so the schedule orders
3256/// the two.
3257static REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
3258    std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
3259
3260fn note_real_time_expiration_kept_pending() {
3261    REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
3262}
3263
3264/// A scheduler send a unit test captured (`Scheduler::test_sent_signals`):
3265/// target, signal, siginfo, and the process of a thread-directed send.
3266#[cfg(test)]
3267pub(crate) type TestSend = (
3268    DetTid,
3269    i32,
3270    Option<signal_lists::KernelSiginfo>,
3271    Option<DetPid>,
3272);
3273
3274/// Set once a POSIX timer is set or a timer's copy recorded
3275/// (`Scheduler::thread_timer_copies`), so a disposition change that flushes a
3276/// signal asks the scheduler to forget the copies, and an exec asks it what
3277/// its timer signals need (`take_exec_timer_flush`), only in a run that has
3278/// timers (`timer_copies_recorded`).
3279static TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
3280    std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
3281
3282/// Whether a POSIX timer's copy has been recorded in this run; see
3283/// [`TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED`].
3284pub(crate) fn timer_copies_recorded() -> bool {
3285    TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
3286}
3287
3288/// Whether any real-time timer expiration has been kept pending in this run;
3289/// see [`REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING`].
3290pub(crate) fn real_time_expiration_kept_pending() -> bool {
3291    REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
3292}
3293
3294pub(crate) fn refuse_real_time_expiration(signo: i32) -> ! {
3295    exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&format_args!(
3296        "hermit: a POSIX timer expired that notifies with real-time signal {signo}, which Detcore does not deliver from a timer; refusing the run rather than dropping the expiration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3893)"
3297    ))
3298}
