3300/// Scheduler-local attribution also represents process operations that have no
3301/// selected task. The public backend callback still supplies its actual task.
3302#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
3303struct BackendFailureLocation {
3304    pid: reverie::Pid,
3305    tid: Option<reverie::Tid>,
3306    phase: &'static str,
3307}
3308
3309/// Wait without manufacturing a normal scheduler request or response. The
3310/// caller must check the terminal state again under the mutex before mutation.
3311async fn until_backend_failure<T>(
3312    sched: &Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
3313    wait: impl std::future::Future<Output = T>,
3314) -> Result<T, SkipTurn> {
3315    let failure = {
3316        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
3317        if sched.backend_failed() {
3318            return Err(SkipTurn);
3319        }
3320        sched.backend_failure_waiter()
3321    };
3322    futures::pin_mut!(wait, failure);
3323    match futures::future::select(failure, wait).await {
3324        futures::future::Either::Left((notice, _)) => {
3325            notice.expect("scheduler owns the failure sender until publication");
3326            Err(SkipTurn)
3327        }
3328        futures::future::Either::Right((value, _)) => Ok(value),
3329    }
3330}
3331
3332/// Advance turn by 1 turn, blocking when necessary to make it happen.
3333/// Return the outcome of the turn as well as which resources were used, if any.
3334///
3335/// WARNING: this is duplicated with the non-blocking `step` function below.
3336/// TODO: this duplication is temporary and they should be either combined or one removed soon.
3337async fn do_ordinary_turn_blocking(
3338    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
3339    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3340    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
3341) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
3342    // Loop until all threads are parked, then proceed:
3343    //
3344    // TODO: First, this check can move after step2, before we commit the action. Second,
3345    // it can later grow more sophisticated to only check the completion of dependent
3346    // actions, not all outsanding guest actions.
3347    loop {
3348        // We must read the queue carefully, because it can grow in the background
3349        // everytime we await.  However, while it can *grow*, it cannot change order, as
3350        // only the scheduler thread (us) actually rotates entries from the front to the back.
3351        let req_ivar = {
3352            let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
3353            if mg.backend_failed() {
3354                return Err(SkipTurn);
3355            }
3356            let arc = global_time.clone();
3357
3358            let next_outstanding = mg.step1_check_quiescence(&arc, last_turn);
3359            // A refused charge ends the turn here, before any maintenance,
3360            // selection or grant; `sched_loop_inner` then reports it and exits.
3361            if mg.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
3362                return Err(SkipTurn);
3363            }
3364            match next_outstanding {
3365                None => {
3366                    trace!("Scheduler observed full quiescense, proceeding...");
3367                    break;
3368                }
3369                Some(iv) => iv.clone(),
3370            }
3371        };
3372        trace!("Scheduler wait for full quiescense, on {}...", req_ivar);
3373        let _ = until_backend_failure(&sched, req_ivar).await?;
3374    }
3375
3376    // Here we copy some information while holding the sched lock, and then release it so
3377    // we can `.await` below:
3378    let (next_dtid, req, resp) = {
3379        let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
3380        if sched.backend_failed() {
3381            return Err(SkipTurn);
3382        }
3383        let blocked = sched.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
3384        if let Some(refusal) = sched.signaled_background_refusal.take() {
3385            drop(sched);
3386            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
3387        }
3388        if let Some(refusal) = sched.rejoin_refusal.take() {
3389            drop(sched);
3390            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
3391        }
3392        blocked?;
3393        sched.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?
3394    };
3395
3396    finish_selected_turn(sched, global_time, next_dtid, req, resp).await
3397}
3398
3399pub async fn do_a_turn_blocking(
3400    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
3401    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3402    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
3403) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
3404    // Installed before the first guest thread registers, so every turn of a
3405    // run takes the same branch.
3406    let controlled = sched.lock().unwrap().signal_control_installed();
3407    if !controlled {
3408        return do_ordinary_turn_blocking(sched, global_time, last_turn).await;
3409    }
3410    #[cfg(test)]
3411    {
3412        sched.lock().unwrap().controlled_turn_entries += 1;
3413    }
3414    let result = async {
3415        // A control pause retains both its maintenance position and the unpaid
3416        // obligation of the preceding real turn. Transport messages never pay it.
3417        enum Action {
3418            Wait {
3419                request: Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>>,
3420                control: Ivar<()>,
3421                barrier: bool,
3422            },
3423            Select(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>),
3424        }
3425        let mut charged = false;
3426        let mut refresh = false;
3427        let mut maintenance = 0;
3428        // The reference admits one due event before a selection. Control
3429        // callbacks may refresh observed time, but must not spend that event
3430        // budget again and reverse ordinary sleepers' queue-front order.
3431        let mut timed_event_processed = false;
3432        let mut empty_queue_skip = false;
3433        loop {
3434            signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
3435            let action = {
3436                let mut state = sched.lock().unwrap();
3437                state.drain_control_intents();
3438                if state.backend_failed() {
3439                    return Err(SkipTurn);
3440                }
3441                let barrier = state.control_barrier();
3442                if empty_queue_skip && !barrier {
3443                    return Err(SkipTurn);
3444                }
3445                let request = state.are_all_quiesced();
3446                if !barrier && request.is_none() {
3447                    if !charged {
3448                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, last_turn);
3449                        charged = true;
3450                        // A refused charge ends the turn before maintenance,
3451                        // alarm selection, signal observations or grants can
3452                        // start; `sched_loop_inner` reports it and exits.
3453                        if state.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
3454                            return Err(SkipTurn);
3455                        }
3456                    } else if refresh {
3457                        // A hook can advance real observed logical time. Refresh
3458                        // eligibility without charging again. An earlier empty
3459                        // due check leaves the one-event budget available; an
3460                        // actual pop consumes it until this turn returns.
3461                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
3462                        if state.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
3463                            return Err(SkipTurn);
3464                        }
3465                        if !timed_event_processed {
3466                            timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
3467                        }
3468                        // Idempotent and spends no event budget, so it runs on
3469                        // every refresh.
3470                        state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
3471                        if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3472                            state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3473                            continue;
3474                        }
3475                    }
3476                    refresh = false;
3477                    if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
3478                        continue;
3479                    }
3480                    match maintenance {
3481                        0 => {
3482                            state.step2_drain_prefix()?;
3483                            maintenance = 1;
3484                            continue;
3485                        }
3486                        1 => {
3487                            if state.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
3488                                return Err(SkipTurn);
3489                            }
3490                            if !timed_event_processed {
3491                                timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
3492                            }
3493                            state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
3494                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3495                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3496                            }
3497                            maintenance = 2;
3498                            continue;
3499                        }
3500                        2 => {
3501                            state.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
3502                            maintenance = 3;
3503                            continue;
3504                        }
3505                        3 => {
3506                            state.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
3507                            maintenance = 4;
3508                            continue;
3509                        }
3510                        4 => {
3511                            empty_queue_skip =
3512                                state.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err();
3513                            // Select at the time to which the empty queue just
3514                            // advanced, before a later pass can advance again.
3515                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3516                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3517                            }
3518                            maintenance = 5;
3519                            continue;
3520                        }
3521                        _ => {
3522                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3523                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3524                                continue;
3525                            }
3526                            // Installing an observation creates an empty callback
3527                            // gate. Await its hook/finish before any tentative pop.
3528                            if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
3529                                continue;
3530                            }
3531                            let (tid, req, resp) = state.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?;
3532                            Action::Select(tid, req, resp)
3533                        }
3534                    }
3535                } else {
3536                    Action::Wait {
3537                        request,
3538                        control: state.control_waiter(),
3539                        barrier,
3540                    }
3541                }
3542            };
3543            match action {
3544                Action::Select(tid, req, resp) => {
3545                    return finish_selected_turn(
3546                        sched.clone(),
3547                        global_time.clone(),
3548                        tid,
3549                        req,
3550                        resp,
3551                    )
3552                    .await;
3553                }
3554                Action::Wait {
3555                    request,
3556                    control,
3557                    barrier,
3558                } => {
3559                    if barrier {
3560                        until_backend_failure(&sched, control).await?;
3561                    } else if let Some(request) = request {
3562                        let wait = async {
3563                            futures::pin_mut!(request, control);
3564                            let _ = futures::future::select(request, control).await;
3565                        };
3566                        until_backend_failure(&sched, wait).await?;
3567                    }
3568                    refresh = true;
3569                }
3570            }
3571        }
3572    }
3573    .await;
3574    signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
3575    result
3576}
3577
3578/// Complete the selected transaction. Keeping the await and post-await checks
3579/// together also lets native controls hold the real request wait open while
3580/// consuming cleanup races with the daemon.
3581pub(crate) async fn finish_selected_turn(
3582    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
3583    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3584    next_dtid: DetTid,
3585    req: Ivar<SchedRequest>,
3586    resp: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
3587) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
3588    // Step 1B: wait for the selected thread to make its request.
3589    trace!(
3590        "[sched-daemon] waiting for next thread (dtid {}) to park...",
3591        next_dtid
3592    );
3593    let rsrcs: Resources = match until_backend_failure(&sched, req.get()).await? {
3594        Err(ThreadExited) => {
3595            debug!(
3596                "[sched-daemon] woke up on request {}, but fizzling because next thread, {}, exited.",
3597                &req, &next_dtid
3598            );
3599            // The selected thread died while we awaited its request, so this turn
3600            // is skipped without reaching step4-6. `step3_peek` opened a
3601            // tentative_pop for `next_dtid`; close it here (undo, since the turn
3602            // did not commit) before returning. Otherwise the tentative selection
3603            // outlives the turn, and the next pass's step2 removal drain calls
3604            // `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is still `Some`, tripping
3605            // the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect panic moved one
3606            // pass" defect. The dead thread's buffered removal drains
3607            // deterministically on the next pass, once this undo has closed the
3608            // window.
3609            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
3610            if !sched.backend_failed() {
3611                sched.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
3612            }
3613            return Err(SkipTurn);
3614        }
3615        Ok(r) => r,
3616    };
3617    trace!("[sched-daemon] daemon woke up on {}...", &req);
3618
3619    // Since the scheduler is asynchronous, we need to check our assumptions.  Polling is
3620    // sufficient here because the thread cannot be racing with us to exit since we know
3621    // it is *already* parked.
3622    let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
3623    if mg.backend_failed() {
3624        return Err(SkipTurn);
3625    }
3626    mg.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(next_dtid)?;
3627    // A terminal verdict recorded while the lock was released (for example
3628    // by the exec reconnect handler) ends the run after this turn: do not
3629    // commit or grant it, so no guest runs concurrently with the exit.
3630    if mg.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
3631        mg.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
3632        return Err(SkipTurn);
3633    }
3634
3635    // The logical COMMIT point for the turn is during step4:
3636    mg.step4_resource_block(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
3637    mg.step5_guest_unblock(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
3638    let requeue = mg.requeue_after(&rsrcs);
3639    mg.step6_reenquue(next_dtid, requeue);
3640    if let Some(call) = rsrcs.as_exit_syscall() {
3641        mg.step7_simulate_exit_posthook(next_dtid, call, &global_time);
3642    }
3643    Ok(rsrcs)
3644}
3645
3646/// How [`Scheduler::step6_reenquue`] requeues the thread whose turn it was
3647/// ([`Scheduler::requeue_after`]).
3648#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
3649enum Requeue {
3650    /// At the back of its band.
3651    Back,
3652    /// At the back of its band, excluded from the next selection
3653    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded`]).
3654    OneTurnYield,
3655    /// At the back of its band, in the yield epoch
3656    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded_into_epoch`]).
3657    YieldEpoch,
3658}
3659
3660// A futex request contains only one resource request, for FutexWait.
3661fn assert_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) {
3662    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
3663        Some(Ok(req)) => {
3664            if !(req.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::FutexWait) && req.resources.len() == 1) {
3665                panic!(
3666                    "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected empty resource request, found: {:?}",
3667                    nextturn.dettid, req
3668                )
3669            }
3670        }
3671        _ => panic!(
3672            "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected request for zero resources, instead found no request.",
3673            nextturn.dettid
3674        ),
3675    }
3676}
3677
3678// Test if the request was from a futex_wait call.
3679fn is_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) -> bool {
3680    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
3681        Some(Ok(req)) => Scheduler::is_x_turn(&req, &ResourceID::FutexWait),
3682        _ => false,
3683    }
3684}

3686/// What a process that drives the scheduler in-process does with a terminal
3687/// deadlock report before the scheduler exits the process.
3688pub type TerminalDeadlockHook = Box<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>;
3689
3690static TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK: Mutex<Option<TerminalDeadlockHook>> = Mutex::new(None);
3691
3692/// Install (or, with `None`, remove) the hook a terminal deadlock report is
3693/// handed to just before the process exits. The exit cannot return an error to
3694/// a caller, so `run --verify` uses this to record the run as failed by a
3695/// deadlock instead of leaving its pending no-result stamp.
3696pub fn set_terminal_deadlock_hook(hook: Option<TerminalDeadlockHook>) {
3697    *TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK
3698        .lock()
3699        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()) = hook;
3700}
3701
3702fn report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(report: &str) {
3703    if let Some(hook) = TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK
3704        .lock()
3705        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())
3706        .as_ref()
3707    {
3708        hook(report);
3709    }
3710}

3718/// The result of consuming a SchedEvent during --replay-preemptions-from.  This represents some
3719/// decisions about what to do next, but are actions which we cannot implement inside
3720/// `consume_schedevent`.
3721pub struct ConsumeResult {
3722    /// Should we keep runnning this thread, if false we background the current thread after this schedevent to let the next thread run.
3723    pub keep_running: bool,
3724    /// A remaining (delta) timeslice this thread is required to run according to the replay schedule
3725    pub timeslice_remaining: Option<LogicalTime>,
3726    /// Should we print the stacktrace in the guest, as per --stacktrace-event
3727    pub print_stack: MaybePrintStack,
3728    /// The number of this event in the global total order of events.
3729    #[allow(dead_code)]
3730    pub event_ix: u64,
3731}
3732
3733/// Any non-None response means that the guest should print its stack trace before proceeding, and
3734/// a response that further includes a path means print to a file at that location.
3735pub type MaybePrintStack = Option<Option<PathBuf>>;

3737/// How many chaos timer-slice change points may pass a runnable thread over,
3738/// since its last committed turn, before the changing thread moves behind it
3739/// ([`Scheduler::bound_chaos_starvation`]). Each pass ends a slice, capped by
3740/// `--max-timeslice`, so a passed-over thread waits at most this many slices
3741/// of a thread that never blocks.
3742const CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND: u32 = 2;

3744enum ThreadStatus {
3745    // Not present in scheduler structures.
3746    Gone,
3747    Running,
3748    // Absent from run queue, but present in one of the blocked structures.
3749    NotRunning,
3750}

3756            Some(path) => {

3760
3761                let toprint = cfg
3762                    .stacktrace_event
3763                    .iter()

4003    pub(crate) fn register_physical_thread(
4004        &mut self,
4005        dettid: DetTid,
4006        mm: MmId,
4007        physical_pid: i32,
4008        physical_tid: i32,
4009    ) -> std::io::Result<()> {
4010        if physical_pid <= 0 || physical_tid <= 0 {
4011            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
4012                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
4013                "host process and thread IDs must be positive",
4014            ));
4015        }
4016        if let Some((known_mm, known_pid, known_tid, _)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid)
4017        {
4018            if *known_mm == mm && *known_pid == physical_pid && *known_tid == physical_tid {
4019                return Ok(());
4020            }
4021            if *known_mm == mm {
4022                return Err(std::io::Error::new(
4023                    std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
4024                    format!(
4025                        "scheduler identity {dettid} already names host process {known_pid} thread {known_tid}"
4026                    ),
4027                ));
4028            }
4029        }
4030        let raw_fd = unsafe {
4031            libc::syscall(
4032                libc::SYS_pidfd_open,
4033                physical_tid,
4034                libc::O_EXCL as libc::c_uint,
4035            )
4036        };
4037        if raw_fd < 0 {
4038            return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
4039        }
4040        // SAFETY: pidfd_open returned a new descriptor owned by this process.
4041        let pidfd = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(raw_fd as libc::c_int) };
4042        self.physical_thread_pidfds
4043            .insert(dettid, (mm, physical_pid, physical_tid, pidfd));
4044        self.procfs_kernel_ids
4045            .insert(dettid, (physical_pid, physical_tid));
4046        Ok(())
4047    }

4049    /// Arm `process`'s exit watch on `pidfd`, a process pidfd for its host
4050    /// process `physical_pid`, bound to address space `mm`; an earlier watch of
4051    /// the process stops being current. Nothing calls this in production yet:
4052    /// arming from unauthenticated numbers was the defect that got
4053    /// 2ee7190125 reverted, and the authenticated registration of
4054    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362> part 2 will be its caller.
4055    #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
4056    pub(crate) fn arm_process_exit_watch(
4057        &mut self,
4058        process: DetPid,
4059        mm: MmId,
4060        physical_pid: i32,
4061        pidfd: OwnedFd,
4062    ) -> Arc<ProcessExitWatch> {
4063        let watch = Arc::new(ProcessExitWatch {
4064            process,
4065            mm,
4066            physical_pid,
4067            pidfd,
4068        });
4069        self.process_exit_watches.insert(process, watch.clone());
4070        watch
4071    }
4072
4073    /// Called under the same mutex as registration, exec and deregistration.
4074    /// Normal leader exit leaves this process watch alive for its siblings.
4075    pub(crate) fn process_exit_watch_is_current(&self, watch: &Arc<ProcessExitWatch>) -> bool {
4076        self.process_exit_watches
4077            .get(&watch.process)
4078            .is_some_and(|current| Arc::ptr_eq(current, watch))
4079            && self.thread_tree.contains(&watch.process)
4080            && self
4081                .thread_tree
4082                .my_thread_group(&watch.process)
4083                .iter()
4084                .any(|tid| self.thread_mm(*tid) == Some(watch.mm))
4085    }
4086
4087    pub(crate) fn finish_process_exit_watch(&mut self, watch: &Arc<ProcessExitWatch>) {
4088        assert!(self.process_exit_watch_is_current(watch));
4089        self.process_exit_watches.remove(&watch.process);
4090    }
4091
4092    /// The host process ID registered for `dettid`'s host thread, if any.
4093    pub(crate) fn physical_process_of(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<i32> {
4094        self.physical_thread_pidfds
4095            .get(&dettid)
4096            .map(|(_, physical_pid, ..)| *physical_pid)
4097    }
4098
4099    /// Whether the host thread registered for `dettid` has exited, by a
4100    /// zero-timeout poll of the `PIDFD_THREAD` pidfd opened when it
4101    /// registered; `None` when it has no registration or the poll fails.
4102    pub(crate) fn registered_thread_has_exited(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<bool> {
4103        let (.., pidfd) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid)?;
4104        let mut poll = libc::pollfd {
4105            fd: pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
4106            events: libc::POLLIN,
4107            revents: 0,
4108        };
4109        // SAFETY: one valid pollfd, and a zero timeout never blocks.
4110        let ready = unsafe { libc::poll(&mut poll, 1, 0) };
4111        (ready >= 0).then_some(ready > 0)
4112    }

4114    /// Whether the scheduler granted the exit of process `detpid` and its
4115    /// parent has not reaped it: a zombie whose death the schedule fixed.
4116    pub(crate) fn process_exit_granted(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
4117        self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&detpid)
4118    }

4120    /// Record that the scheduler granted `detpid`'s exit, as its final Exit
4121    /// grant does.
4122    #[cfg(test)]
4123    pub(crate) fn grant_exit_for_test(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) {
4124        self.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(detpid);

4127    /// The registered thread through which a SIGKILL's victim `detpid` is
4128    /// known on the host: `named`, the thread the kill named, when it is
4129    /// registered, or else, for a kill that named the process
4130    /// (`process_directed`: kill or a pidfd), the victim's lowest registered
4131    /// thread. A pidfd names the victim's leader, which may have exited while
4132    /// its siblings run on (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
4133    /// A thread-directed SIGKILL (tkill, tgkill, rt_tgsigqueueinfo) to an
4134    /// exited thread gets no fallback: Linux does not end the group for it
4135    /// (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439, R1).
4136    pub(crate) fn sigkill_victim_registered_thread(
4137        &self,
4138        named: DetTid,
4139        detpid: DetPid,
4140        process_directed: bool,
4141    ) -> Option<DetTid> {
4142        if self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&named) {
4143            return Some(named);
4144        }
4145        if !process_directed {
4146            return None;
4147        }
4148        self.live_group_members(detpid)
4149            .into_iter()
4150            .find(|tid| self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(tid))
4151    }
4152
4153    /// The threads the thread tree lists in `detpid`'s group that still lead
4154    /// back to it, in DetTid order. The tree never drops an edge, so after a
4155    /// thread id is reused it can also be listed under its old group (Claude
4156    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439, R3).
4157    fn live_group_members(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4158        if !self.thread_tree.contains(&detpid) {
4159            return Vec::new();
4160        }
4161        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(detpid.as_raw());
4162        let mut group: Vec<DetTid> = self
4163            .thread_tree
4164            .my_thread_group(&detpid)
4165            .into_iter()
4166            .filter(|tid| {
4167                self.thread_tree
4168                    .thread_to_leader
4169                    .get(tid)
4170                    .is_none_or(|owner| *owner == leader)
4171            })
4172            .collect();
4173        group.sort();
4174        group
4175    }
4176
4177    fn remove_physical_thread(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid, mm: MmId) {
4178        if self
4179            .physical_thread_pidfds
4180            .get(dettid)
4181            .is_some_and(|(registered_mm, ..)| *registered_mm == mm)
4182        {
4183            self.physical_thread_pidfds.remove(dettid);
4184        }
4185    }

4187    #[cfg(test)]
4188    pub(crate) fn physical_thread_identity(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<(MmId, i32, i32)> {
4189        self.physical_thread_pidfds
4190            .get(&dettid)
4191            .map(|(mm, pid, tid, _)| (*mm, *pid, *tid))

4194    /// Record, in the sender's committed turn, that a SIGKILL to `dettid` (or
4195    /// to process `target_process`) succeeded. The process will die even
4196    /// while one of its threads is held at a happens-before gate, so
4197    /// [`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`] never counts a
4198    /// wait for it as part of a deadlock. On ptrace its retirement comes later,
4199    /// at its host-timed deregistration
4200    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994); this record is
4201    /// decided by the sender's syscall, so it is deterministic.
4202    pub(crate) fn record_committed_sigkill(
4203        &mut self,
4204        dettid: DetTid,
4205        target_process: Option<DetPid>,
4206    ) {
4207        let process = target_process.or_else(|| {
4208            self.thread_tree
4209                .thread_to_leader
4210                .get(&dettid)
4211                .map(|leader| DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw()))
4212        });
4213        match process {
4214            Some(process) => {
4215                self.sigkilled_processes.insert(process);
4216            }
4217            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
4218        }
4219    }
4220
4221    /// Record a successful SIGKILL the scheduler is not told about one victim
4222    /// at a time: every process now in process group `group`, or, for `None`
4223    /// (a pidfd whose process Detcore did not record), an unknown process.
4224    /// An unknown victim makes every child wait count as input that may still
4225    /// arrive for the rest of the run.
4226    pub(crate) fn record_unresolved_sigkill(&mut self, group: Option<DetPid>) {
4227        match group {
4228            Some(group) => {
4229                let members: Vec<DetPid> = self
4230                    .thread_tree
4231                    .process_wait
4232                    .iter()
4233                    .filter(|(_, metadata)| metadata.process_group == group)
4234                    .map(|(process, _)| *process)
4235                    .collect();
4236                self.sigkilled_processes.extend(members);
4237            }
4238            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
4239        }
4240    }
4241
4242    /// Whether a committed SIGKILL doomed `process`, and whether one with an
4243    /// unnamed victim was seen (test observation of the record above).
4244    #[cfg(test)]
4245    pub(crate) fn sigkill_recorded(&self, process: DetPid) -> (bool, bool) {
4246        (
4247            self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&process),
4248            self.unresolved_sigkill,
4249        )
4250    }
4251
4252    /// A thread is being registered on `dettid`: any committed exit recorded
4253    /// for an earlier thread with that tid no longer applies.
4254    pub(crate) fn forget_committed_exit(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
4255        self.forget_sigkill_receipt(dettid);
4256        self.committed_exits.remove(&dettid);
4257        self.retired_exited_leaders.remove(&dettid);
4258        // A reused pid names a new process, not one a namespace's end doomed.
4259        self.namespace_zap_victims.remove(&dettid);
4260    }
4261
4262    pub(crate) fn note_process_sigkill(
4263        &mut self,
4264        dettid: DetTid,
4265        detpid: DetPid,
4266        process_directed: bool,
4267    ) {
4268        if !self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
4269            return;
4270        }
4271        let threads: Vec<DetTid> = self
4272            .live_group_members(detpid)
4273            .into_iter()
4274            .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
4275            .collect();
4276        // A zombie whose exit the schedule granted has nothing left to retire:
4277        // Linux sends the signal and nothing changes
4278        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
4279        if process_directed && threads.is_empty() && self.process_exit_granted(detpid) {
4280            return;
4281        }
4282        let named_mm = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid).map(|(mm, ..)| *mm);
4283        // The named thread may be an exited leader, as a pidfd names it: for a
4284        // kill that named the process, any registered live thread of the
4285        // victim is enough to know it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
4286        // A thread-directed SIGKILL to an exited thread gets no such fallback
4287        // (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439, R1).
4288        if named_mm.is_none() && !process_directed {
4289            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
4290                format!(
4291                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot complete SIGKILL for dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
4292                    dettid,
4293                )
4294            });
4295            return;
4296        }
4297        if named_mm.is_none()
4298            && !threads
4299                .iter()
4300                .any(|tid| self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(tid))
4301        {
4302            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
4303                format!(
4304                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot complete SIGKILL for dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
4305                    dettid,
4306                )
4307            });
4308            return;
4309        }
4310        // SIGKILL ends the whole thread group, whichever thread it names.
4311        // Retire every live thread of the group, the named one first, then in
4312        // DetTid order, at this same committed point: none of them runs guest
4313        // code again, and on this backend a killed thread's pending request is
4314        // answered (`needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation`)
4315        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362).
4316        if let Some(mm) = named_mm {
4317            self.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, mm);
4318        }
4319        for tid in threads
4320            .into_iter()
4321            .filter(|tid| *tid != dettid || named_mm.is_none())
4322        {
4323            let mm = self
4324                .physical_thread_pidfds
4325                .get(&tid)
4326                .map(|(mm, ..)| *mm)
4327                .or_else(|| self.thread_mm(tid))
4328                .unwrap_or(MmId::initial(tid));
4329            self.logically_kill_thread(&tid, &detpid, mm);
4330        }
4331    }
4332
4333    fn should_synthesize_child_exit_signal(&self, parent: DetTid) -> bool {
4334        !self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&parent)
4335    }
4336
4337    /// Refuse the run (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`, exit 122) for a
4338    /// syscall entry of `dettid` that reached posthook `anchors` and returned
4339    /// the internal restart `code`: whether that entry returns `EINTR` or is
4340    /// restarted and never returns is decided by the kernel after this point
4341    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>).
4342    ///
4343    /// The guest names every spawn-ordinal anchor at its nth matching call on
4344    /// any thread, as for a completed call, so only the anchors that resolve
4345    /// to `dettid` count ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]); with none,
4346    /// the turn proceeds. Otherwise nothing fires, the verdict is recorded (an
4347    /// earlier pending verdict and its classification are kept), and the turn
4348    /// grants nothing, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit.
4349    fn hb_posthook_interrupted(
4350        &mut self,
4351        dettid: DetTid,
4352        count: u64,
4353        anchors: &[String],
4354        code: &str,
4355    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4356        let anchors = self
4357            .happens_before
4358            .as_ref()
4359            .expect("posthook refusal issued without a happens-before program")
4360            .occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, anchors);
4361        if anchors.is_empty() {
4362            return Ok(());
4363        }
4364        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
4365            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
4366                "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid {} reached posthook happens-before \
4367                 anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}, and the call was interrupted ({}); whether \
4368                 it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
4369                 checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook \
4370                 or on a call that is not interrupted.",
4371                dettid, anchors, count, code
4372            ));
4373            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
4374        }
4375        self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
4376    }
4377
4378    /// Handle a happens-before checkpoint issued by `dettid` after its `count`th
4379    /// intercepted syscall (see `Detcore::handle_syscall_event`).
4380    ///
4381    /// Grants passage (firing every anchor at `SyscallCount(count)` on this
4382    /// thread and re-admitting any parked threads whose gate may now be open)
4383    /// unless a reached anchor is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
4384    /// anchor has not fired, in which case the thread is parked out of the run
4385    /// queue until a later firing wakes it. Mirrors the `SleepUntil` park/skip
4386    /// protocol: the request/response ivars are left intact so the re-admitted
4387    /// thread re-evaluates this same checkpoint on its next turn.
4388    fn hb_checkpoint(
4389        &mut self,
4390        dettid: DetTid,
4391        count: u64,
4392        occurrence_anchors: &[String],
4393    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4394        let (reached, blocked) = {
4395            let hb = self
4396                .happens_before
4397                .as_ref()
4398                .expect("hb checkpoint issued without a happens-before program");
4399            let mut reached = hb.anchors_at_syscall(dettid, count);
4400            reached.extend(hb.occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, occurrence_anchors));
4401            let blocked = reached.iter().any(|name| hb.anchor_blocked(name));
4402            (reached, blocked)
4403        };
4404
4405        if reached.is_empty() {
4406            // No anchor addresses this (thread, count); nothing to gate or fire.
4407            return Ok(());
4408        }
4409
4410        if blocked {
4411            info!(
4412                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} held at happens-before \
4413                 anchor(s) {:?} (syscall count {}) awaiting a BEFORE anchor",
4414                self.turn, dettid, reached, count
4415            );
4416            if self
4417                .vfork_barriers
4418                .values()
4419                .any(|child| *child == Some(dettid))
4420            {
4421                // While a vfork child runs, no other thread can be selected
4422                // (`step3_peek`), so a BEFORE anchor could never fire and the run
4423                // would spin with no report
4424                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3930). Refuse instead.
4425                // Keep an earlier verdict, and its classification, if one is
4426                // already pending.
4427                if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
4428                    self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
4429                        "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD: happens-before anchor(s) {:?} would hold \
4430                         dtid {}, a vfork child that has not exec'd yet; while it runs no other \
4431                         thread can, so its gate could never open. Anchor the edge on a point \
4432                         before the vfork or after the child's exec.",
4433                        reached, dettid
4434                    ));
4435                    self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
4436                }
4437            }
4438            let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
4439            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
4440            hb.parked.insert(dettid);
4441            hb.held_at.insert(dettid, reached.clone());
4442            hb.holds.entry(dettid).or_insert_with(|| HbHold {
4443                since_ns: now_ns,
4444                anchors: reached.clone(),
4445            });
4446            return self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
4447        }
4448
4449        // Grant passage: fire the reached anchors. Only wake parked threads when a
4450        // new anchor actually fired, so an idempotent re-grant causes no churn.
4451        let mut newly_fired = false;
4452        {
4453            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
4454            // Passage granted: any hold of this thread is over.
4455            hb.holds.remove(&dettid);
4456            for name in &reached {
4457                if hb.fired.insert(name.clone()) {
4458                    newly_fired = true;
4459                }
4460            }
4461        }
4462        if newly_fired {
4463            debug!(
4464                "[happens-before] dettid {} fired anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}",
4465                dettid, reached, count
4466            );
4467            // Defer the actual re-admission: we are inside `block_for_one_resource`
4468            // with a `tentative_pop` selection live, and pushing to the run queue
4469            // now would trip the queue's transaction assertion. The next
4470            // `step2_drain_prefix` flushes (`step3_peek` as a backstop).
4471            self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().wake_pending = true;
4472        }
4473        Ok(())
4474    }
4475
4476    /// If a happens-before anchor fired since the last check, re-admit every
4477    /// parked thread to the run queue so it re-evaluates its gate on its next
4478    /// turn. Threads still blocked re-park; the request/response ivars are
4479    /// untouched, so no request needs re-filling. Deterministic: parked threads
4480    /// are iterated in `DetTid` order.
4481    ///
4482    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, with the other deferred run-queue
4483    /// admissions and before step2c and step2d look at the queue, and from
4484    /// `step3_peek` *before* the turn's `tentative_pop`. Both are points with no
4485    /// live selection transaction: anchors fire deep inside
4486    /// `block_for_one_resource` while a selection is live, so the actual
4487    /// re-admission must be deferred to one of them.
4488    fn hb_flush_wakes(&mut self) {
4489        match self.happens_before.as_mut() {
4490            Some(hb) if hb.wake_pending => hb.wake_pending = false,
4491            _ => return,
4492        }
4493        let parked: Vec<DetTid> = self
4494            .happens_before
4495            .as_ref()
4496            .map(|hb| hb.parked.iter().copied().collect())
4497            .unwrap_or_default();
4498        for dettid in parked {
4499            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
4500            hb.parked.remove(&dettid);
4501            hb.held_at.remove(&dettid);
4502            if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
4503                let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
4504                trace!(
4505                    "[happens-before] re-admitting parked dettid {} at queue position {}",
4506                    dettid, pos
4507                );
4508            }
4509        }
4510    }
4511
4512    /// Refuse the run when a held thread has outlasted a version-2 program's
4513    /// hold budget (`max_hold_ns`), charged in committed virtual time.
4514    ///
4515    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, so at every step2 pass of both turn
4516    /// loops, before selection. It reads only `committed_time` and the
4517    /// scheduler's own hold records, and it ends the run rather than releasing
4518    /// the thread, so it never decides which thread runs. A run with no
4519    /// version-2 program, or no hold, returns at once.
4520    fn hb_check_hold_budget(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
4521        let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
4522        let Some(refusal) = self
4523            .happens_before
4524            .as_ref()
4525            .and_then(|hb| hb.hold_budget_refusal(now_ns))
4526        else {
4527            return Ok(());
4528        };
4529        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
4530            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
4531            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
4532        }
4533        Err(SkipTurn)
4534    }
4535
4536    /// Fill in a resource request, which is exactly what might make the next logical
4537    /// step become unblocked.
4538    pub fn request_put(
4539        &mut self,
4540        req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>,
4541        rs: Resources,
4542        _global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
4543    ) {
4544        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4545        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1041): A guest resource-request RPC can race an
4546        // asynchronous signal delivery. `force_unblock_thread` replaces
4547        // `next_turns[tid].req` with an already-full Ivar carrying an
4548        // `InboundSignal` request (see the `Ivar::full` at the bottom of this
4549        // file). If the guest's own resource-request then lands on that same
4550        // turn, the previous unconditional `req.put()` panicked with "Ivar
4551        // multiple put" (observed intermittently on `timeout 5 echo hi` under
4552        // `--strict --verify`, where a 5s SIGALRM races the child's `wait4`).
4553        // Tolerate exactly that case: drop the late guest request and let the
4554        // signal turn win — the interrupted syscall (e.g. `rt_sigsuspend`)
4555        // restarts and re-issues a fresh request on the next turn. Any other
4556        // double-put still panics, preserving the write-once Ivar invariant.
4557        // Mirrors the `try_put` guard in `logically_kill_thread` (PR-845).
4558        if let Some(dropped) = req.try_put(Ok(rs)) {
4559            let tolerated = matches!(
4560                req.try_read(),
4561                Some(Ok(existing))
4562                    if existing
4563                        .resources
4564                        .keys()
4565                        .any(|r| {
4566                            matches!(
4567                                r,
4568                                ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) | ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_)
4569                            )
4570                        })
4571            );
4572            if tolerated {
4573                trace!(
4574                    "[request_put] dropping late guest request {:?}; an async inbound signal already filled the request for this turn (req {})",
4575                    dropped, req
4576                );
4577            } else {
4578                panic!(
4579                    "Ivar multiple put exception in request_put! Attempted to write {:?} to {}; existing content is not an inbound-signal request.",
4580                    dropped, req
4581                );
4582            }
4583        }
4584    }
4585
4586    /// Poll the resource request and *if* it is not currently observed to be full, return
4587    /// the IVar that *will* contain it in the future.
4588    fn check_request(&self, det_tid: &DetTid) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
4589        let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(det_tid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
4590            panic!(
4591                "[check_request] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
4592                det_tid
4593            )
4594        });
4595        if nextturn.req.is_empty() {
4596            Some(nextturn.req.clone())
4597        } else {
4598            None
4599        }
4600    }
4601
4602    /// Returns None if all are parked, otherwise the unfilled request of the next we're waiting on.
4603    fn are_all_quiesced(&self) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
4604        // Skip raw TIDs whose old run-queue incarnation is pending removal.
4605        // `Retire` targets have no `next_turns` entry, while
4606        // `ReplaceThenAdmit` targets have a fresh registration that must not be
4607        // waited on until the drain removes the old physical slot and admits
4608        // that replacement.
4609        self.run_queue
4610            .tids()
4611            .filter(|dt| !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(dt))
4612            .find_map(|dt| self.check_request(dt))
4613    }
