4615    /// Try to pop the next event from the sorted list of stacktrace_events, if it matches the given
4616    /// index.  This is idempotent, because subsequent attempts will just fizzle.
4617    fn try_pop_stacktrace_event(
4618        &mut self,
4619        current_ix: u64,
4620        observed: &SchedEvent,
4621    ) -> MaybePrintStack {
4622        let mut result = None;
4623        if let Some(iter) = &mut self.stacktrace_events
4624            && let Some((next_ix, event, m_path)) = iter.peek()
4625        {
4626            let go = if let Some(ev) = event {
4627                (*next_ix == current_ix && events_consistent(observed, ev))
4628                    || events_match(observed, ev)
4629            } else {
4630                *next_ix == current_ix
4631            };
4632            if go {
4633                info!(
4634                    "Now output stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
4635                    current_ix, observed,
4636                );
4637                if m_path.is_none() {
4638                    crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
4639                        "\nPrinting stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
4640                        current_ix,
4641                        observed,
4642                    );
4643                }
4644                result = Some(m_path.clone());
4645                let _ = iter.next();
4646            }
4647        }
4648        result
4649    }
4650
4651    /// Verify that the event we're replaying matches what just happened.  Set up the next
4652    /// (replayed) event to run.  Return true if the current thread will keep running and false if
4653    /// it needs to be descheduled.
4654    ///
4655    /// PreReq: we're running under --replay-schedule-from
4656    pub fn consume_schedevent(&mut self, observed: &SchedEvent) -> ConsumeResult {
4657        debug_assert!(self.replayer.is_some());
4658        let mytid = observed.dettid;
4659
4660        if let Some((ix, action)) = self.replayer.as_mut().map(|r| {
4661            let current_ix = r.traced_event_count;
4662            (current_ix, r.observe_event(observed))
4663        }) {
4664            let print_stack = self.try_pop_stacktrace_event(ix, observed);
4665            debug!("Next ReplayAction = {:?}", action);
4666            self.release_replay_priorities_if_exhausted();
4667
4668            match action {
4669                replayer::ReplayAction::Continue(timeslice_remaining) => {
4670                    return ConsumeResult {
4671                        keep_running: true,
4672                        print_stack,
4673                        event_ix: ix,
4674                        timeslice_remaining,
4675                    };
4676                }
4677                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::FatalDesync) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
4678                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::ReplayExausted) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
4679                replayer::ReplayAction::ContextSwitch(is_now, new_tid, timeslice_remaining) => {
4680                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(mytid, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
4681                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(new_tid, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
4682                    if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(new_tid) {
4683                        // If it is not yet in next_turns, that is because it was JUST spawned and
4684                        // hasn't showed up yet, but it will by the next scheduler turn.
4685                        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&new_tid) {
4686                            tracing::warn!(
4687                                "Attempted to context switch to tid {}, but it is not runnable atm. This could be legitimate if it is awoken by another thread exiting (futex wake).",
4688                                new_tid
4689                            );
4690                            // TODO(T138906107): make this a fatal error when RESYNC capability is robust enough.
4691                            // immediate_fatal_exit();
4692                        }
4693                    }
4694                    self.timeslices.insert(new_tid, timeslice_remaining);
4695                    return ConsumeResult {
4696                        keep_running: !is_now,
4697                        print_stack,
4698                        event_ix: ix,
4699                        timeslice_remaining,
4700                    };
4701                }
4702            };
4703        }
4704
4705        ConsumeResult {
4706            keep_running: true,
4707            print_stack: None,
4708            event_ix: 0,
4709            timeslice_remaining: None,
4710        }
4711    }
4712
4713    /// Updates the address Linux clears and wakes when this thread exits.
4714    ///
4715    /// `set_tid_address(2)` replaces the value supplied by clone. A zero
4716    /// address disables the exit-time store and wake.
4717    pub fn set_child_tid_address(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, address: usize) -> bool {
4718        let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
4719            return false;
4720        };
4721        next_turn.child_tid_addr = address;
4722        true
4723    }
4724
4725    /// Freeze the live sibling set at the caller's deterministic exec boundary.
4726    /// A failed exec must not kill these threads; only successful exec, or an
4727    /// actual exit receipt for a sibling, authorizes its eventual retirement.
4728    pub(crate) fn prepare_exec_teardown(
4729        &mut self,
4730        caller: DetTid,
4731        process: DetPid,
4732        mm: MmId,
4733    ) -> bool {
4734        if self.registered_process(caller) != Some(process)
4735            || !self.next_turns.contains_key(&caller)
4736            || !self.rpc_incarnation_matches(caller, mm)
4737            || self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&process)
4738        {
4739            return false;
4740        }
4741        let siblings = self
4742            .thread_tree
4743            .my_thread_group(&process)
4744            .into_iter()
4745            .filter(|tid| *tid != caller && self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
4746            .collect();
4747        self.exec_teardowns.insert(
4748            process,
4749            ExecTeardown {
4750                caller,
4751                mm,
4752                siblings,
4753                observed: BTreeSet::new(),
4754            },
4755        );
4756        true
4757    }
4758
4759    /// Account a physical exit without letting host callback order mutate the
4760    /// scheduler. The hook must return promptly: ptrace awaits the displaced
4761    /// leader's hook before invoking the survivor's successful exec callback.
4762    pub(crate) fn defer_exec_sibling_retirement(
4763        &mut self,
4764        tid: DetTid,
4765        process: DetPid,
4766        mm: MmId,
4767    ) -> bool {
4768        let Some(teardown) = self.exec_teardowns.get_mut(&process) else {
4769            return false;
4770        };
4771        if teardown.mm != mm || !teardown.siblings.contains(&tid) {
4772            return false;
4773        }
4774        teardown.observed.insert(tid);
4775        true
4776    }
4777
4778    /// The exact old-image receipt replaces absence of a scheduler registration
4779    /// as proof that a transferred exec's displaced leader was consumed.
4780    pub(crate) fn exec_sibling_retirement_observed(
4781        &self,
4782        tid: DetTid,
4783        process: DetPid,
4784        mm: MmId,
4785    ) -> bool {
4786        self.exec_teardowns
4787            .get(&process)
4788            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.mm == mm && teardown.observed.contains(&tid))
4789    }
4790
4791    /// Apply retirement in sorted order at the successful exec edge, or retire
4792    /// just physically consumed owners when an exec attempt fails. The caller
4793    /// remains registered with its empty request, so no turn can overtake the
4794    /// complete replacement registration. The ordinary removal path retains
4795    /// its INFO event, futex wakes and tentative-safe run-queue buffering.
4796    pub(crate) fn finish_exec_teardown(
4797        &mut self,
4798        caller: DetTid,
4799        process: DetPid,
4800        mm: MmId,
4801        succeeded: bool,
4802    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4803        if !self
4804            .exec_teardowns
4805            .get(&process)
4806            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.caller == caller && teardown.mm == mm)
4807        {
4808            return Vec::new();
4809        }
4810        let teardown = self.exec_teardowns.remove(&process).unwrap();
4811        let retired: Vec<_> = if succeeded {
4812            teardown.siblings
4813        } else {
4814            teardown.observed
4815        }
4816        .into_iter()
4817        .collect();
4818        // Only a successful exec's edge retires the others at a committed
4819        // point; a failed attempt retires the siblings that died meanwhile,
4820        // at moments host timing set.
4821        if succeeded {
4822            self.parent_death_exec_survivor = Some((process, caller));
4823        }
4824        for tid in &retired {
4825            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &process, mm);
4826            self.timeslices.remove(tid);
4827        }
4828        self.parent_death_exec_survivor = None;
4829        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
4830        self.finish_exec_alarm(process);
4831        retired
4832    }
4833
4834    /// Remove a thread from the deterministic scheduler.  In order to call this, the precondition
4835    /// is that this thread will execute no further (visible) instructions.
4836    ///
4837    /// This is called while the guest is running, not in the middle of a scheduler turn.
4838    ///
4839    /// This is IDEMPOTENT, and it may indeed be called twice, both to proactively remove a thread,
4840    /// and then reactively in response to an exit hook.
4841    pub fn logically_kill_thread(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid, detpid: &DetPid, mm: MmId) {
4842        if self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation {
4843            self.logically_killed_threads.insert(*dtid);
4844        }
4845        // Remove from the runnable queue at the next deterministic drain. This
4846        // is safe even if an asynchronous exec reconnect races a live
4847        // tentative_pop: the handler never reaches the run queue's mutation
4848        // guard and cannot poison the scheduler mutex.
4849        self.deschedule_or_defer(*dtid);
4850        // Remove from all non-runnable pools:
4851        self.remove_blocking_entries(dtid);
4852        self.retire_sigalrm_thread(*dtid, *detpid);
4853        // The process's last thread: its shared queue goes with it.
4854        if self
4855            .process_signal_targets(*detpid)
4856            .iter()
4857            .all(|thread| thread == dtid)
4858        {
4859            self.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.remove(detpid);
4860        }
4861        // Its own queue goes with it; a later thread with its tid starts empty.
4862        self.thread_timer_copies
4863            .retain(|(thread, _), _| thread != dtid);
4864        self.remove_physical_thread(dtid, mm);
4865        // A killed vfork parent must not leave its barrier behind: step2a
4866        // drops a barrier only when it can read the parent's pending request,
4867        // which `next_turns.remove` below discards, and while a barrier exists
4868        // `step3_peek` selects its child first, so a barrier left behind would
4869        // change the schedule after that child is gone
4870        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
4871        self.retire_vfork_parent(*dtid);
4872        // A killed vfork child is its own barrier's release edge.
4873        self.release_vfork_child(*dtid);
4874        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(dtid);
4875        self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(dtid);
4876        let retired = self
4877            .discarded_at_send
4878            .retire(discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(*dtid));
4879        self.note_private_entries_retired(retired);
4880        self.forget_pending_dequeue(*dtid);
4881        // Its private queue dies with it, and so does a raw-exit status its
4882        // grant never settled (a thread killed between its report and its
4883        // grant).
4884        self.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.remove(dtid);
4885        self.child_exit_sigchld.raw_exit_status.remove(dtid);
4886        self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(dtid);
4887        if dtid.as_raw() == detpid.as_raw() {
4888            self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(detpid);
4889        }
4890        self.real_timers.retire_task(*detpid, *dtid);
4891        self.retire_parked_requests(*dtid);
4892
4893        let _ = self.priorities.remove(dtid);
4894        let first_removal = self.next_turns.contains_key(dtid);
4895        match self.next_turns.remove(dtid) {
4896            None => {
4897                trace!(
4898                    "logically_kill_thread: thread already removed from scheduler: {}",
4899                    &dtid
4900                );
4901            }
4902            Some(nextturn) => {
4903                info!(
4904                    "logically_kill: Scheduler removing all knowledge of [det]tid {} in pid {}..",
4905                    dtid, detpid
4906                );
4907                // Put in a dummy request to unblock the scheduler that might be
4908                // waiting for the thread to park.
4909                //
4910                // WARNING: this try_put should potentially turn back into a put(), if we can narrow
4911                // down the exit scenarios and ensure that they happen when the guest is running and
4912                // has NOT filled its request to the scheduler yet.
4913                let request_was_pending = nextturn.req.try_put(Err(ThreadExited)).is_some();
4914                if request_was_pending
4915                    && self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
4916                    && !self.backend_failed()
4917                {
4918                    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4919                    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review killed-thread RPC cancellation.
4920                    nextturn.resp.try_put(SchedResponse::Signaled(None));
4921                }
4922                if nextturn.child_tid_addr != 0 {
4923                    self.wake_futex_child_cleartid(
4924                        FutexID::private(mm, nextturn.child_tid_addr),
4925                        *dtid,
4926                    );
4927                }
4928            }
4929        }
4930
4931        if first_removal {
4932            let process = self.registered_process(*dtid).unwrap_or(*detpid);
4933            self.deliver_parent_death_signals(*dtid, process);
4934        }
4935
4936        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4937        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
4938        let live_process_thread = self
4939            .thread_tree
4940            .my_thread_group(detpid)
4941            .into_iter()
4942            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
4943        // A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process
4944        // in the thread tree, although the backend reports its creator's pid
4945        // (`ResourceID::Exit` below makes the same distinction). Its exit
4946        // still decides its orphans, when its last thread leaves.
4947        if let Some(registered) = self.registered_process(*dtid)
4948            && registered != *detpid
4949            && !self
4950                .thread_tree
4951                .my_thread_group(&registered)
4952                .into_iter()
4953                .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid))
4954        {
4955            self.namespace_zap_victims.remove(&registered);
4956            self.reparent_orphans(registered);
4957        }
4958        if !live_process_thread {
4959            let _ = self.begin_physical_process_exit(*detpid);
4960            self.reparent_orphans(*detpid);
4961            self.logically_exited_processes.insert(*detpid);
4962            // The kill a namespace's end owed it has arrived.
4963            self.namespace_zap_victims.remove(detpid);
4964            // Linux decides at exit whether the parent reaps this child
4965            // automatically (do_notify_parent), and only for a child whose
4966            // exit signal is SIGCHLD; a later change of the parent's
4967            // disposition does not bring the child back.
4968            if self.thread_tree.notification_signal(*detpid) == Some(libc::SIGCHLD)
4969                && self
4970                    .thread_tree
4971                    .parent_process(detpid)
4972                    .is_some_and(|parent| self.thread_tree.reaps_children_automatically(parent))
4973            {
4974                self.autoreaped_exits.insert(*detpid);
4975            } else {
4976                self.autoreaped_exits.remove(detpid);
4977            }
4978            if let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(detpid) {
4979                self.wake_child_waiters(parent, *detpid);
4980            }
4981            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_process_timers(*detpid);
4982            self.real_timers.retire_process(*detpid);
4983            // A dying process discards its pending signals.
4984            self.pending_real_time_expirations.remove(detpid);
4985            self.child_exit_sigchld.forget_process(*detpid);
4986            self.discarded_at_send
4987                .retire(discarded_at_send::QueueId::Process(*detpid));
4988            self.posix_timer_arm_generations
4989                .retain(|(owner, _), _| owner != detpid);
4990            self.posix_timer_values
4991                .retain(|(owner, _), _| owner != detpid);
4992            self.posix_timer_overruns
4993                .retain(|(owner, _), _| owner != detpid);
4994            self.signal_unobservable
4995                .retain(|(owner, _)| owner != detpid);
4996            self.handler_masks.retain(|(owner, _), _| owner != detpid);
4997        }
4998    }
4999
5000    /// Record that task `tid` armed parent-death signal `signal` with
5001    /// `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)`, in its turn, for Detcore to send itself; 0
5002    /// disarms (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440>).
5003    pub fn set_parent_death_signal(&mut self, tid: DetTid, signal: i32) {
5004        if signal == 0 {
5005            self.thread_tree.parent_death_signals.remove(&tid);
5006        } else {
5007            self.thread_tree.parent_death_signals.insert(tid, signal);
5008        }
5009    }
5010
5011    /// The parent-death signal Detcore holds for task `tid`, or 0.
5012    pub fn parent_death_signal(&self, tid: DetTid) -> i32 {
5013        self.thread_tree
5014            .parent_death_signals
5015            .get(&tid)
5016            .copied()
5017            .unwrap_or(0)
5018    }
5019
5020    /// Send the parent-death signals of the children whose parent-death
5021    /// parent is `exited`, a thread of `process` that has just left, and give
5022    /// those children a new one, as Linux's `forget_original_parent` does
5023    /// when any thread exits (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440):
5024    /// for each such child, in pid order, each of its live tasks that armed a
5025    /// parent-death signal (leader first, then by tid) has it sent to the
5026    /// whole child process, through the scheduler's own send (`fire_alarm`)
5027    /// at the next drain (`flush_parent_death_signals`), which wakes a wait
5028    /// that admits it.
5029    ///
5030    /// This runs where `logically_kill_thread` first removes `exited`. For an
5031    /// `exit` or `exit_group` with sequentialized threads that follows the
5032    /// scheduler-ordered `ResourceID::Exit` grant and precedes the next
5033    /// committed turn, as re-parenting does (`reparent_orphans`), so the send
5034    /// is as deterministic as that turn; so are the threads an exit_group or a
5035    /// committed SIGKILL retires (their process's exit is granted) and those
5036    /// an exec's edge retires (`parent_death_exec_survivor`). A thread that
5037    /// died otherwise (a fatal signal) leaves at a moment host timing sets:
5038    /// its children's signals are posted then, as the kernel posted them
5039    /// before, and recorded as host-timed for their processes, so no gated
5040    /// wait ends for them (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146);
5041    /// that is a determinism loss, named here.
5042    fn deliver_parent_death_signals(&mut self, exited: DetTid, process: DetPid) {
5043        let children: Vec<DetPid> = self
5044            .thread_tree
5045            .parent_death_parents
5046            .iter()
5047            .filter(|(_, parent)| **parent == exited)
5048            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
5049            .collect();
5050        if children.is_empty() {
5051            return;
5052        }
5053        let heir = self.parent_death_heir(exited, process);
5054        for child in children {
5055            let mut tasks: Vec<DetTid> = self
5056                .thread_tree
5057                .my_thread_group(&DetTid::from_raw(child.as_raw()))
5058                .into_iter()
5059                .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
5060                .collect();
5061            tasks.sort_by_key(|tid| (tid.as_raw() != child.as_raw(), *tid));
5062            let signals: Vec<i32> = tasks
5063                .iter()
5064                .filter_map(|tid| self.thread_tree.parent_death_signals.get(tid).copied())
5065                .collect();
5066            let committed = self.committed_exits.contains(&exited)
5067                || self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&process)
5068                || self
5069                    .parent_death_exec_survivor
5070                    .map(|(survivor_process, _)| survivor_process)
5071                    == Some(process);
5072            for signal in signals {
5073                let Ok(signal) = Signal::try_from(signal) else {
5074                    warn!(
5075                        "[scheduler] parent-death signal {} of process {} is not one Detcore sends",
5076                        signal, child
5077                    );
5078                    continue;
5079                };
5080                if committed {
5081                    info!(
5082                        "[scheduler] thread {} left: parent-death signal {} to process {}",
5083                        exited, signal, child
5084                    );
5085                    self.pending_parent_death_signals.push((child, signal));
5086                } else {
5087                    // A thread that left at a host-timed moment (a fatal
5088                    // signal) sends at that moment, as the kernel did before:
5089                    // the signal is recorded as host-timed for the child's
5090                    // process, so that no gated wait of it ends for this copy,
5091                    // and posted without the scheduler's wake. Where the
5092                    // record lands is host-timed too, so say so.
5093                    self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
5094                        "parent-death signal {signal} of process {child} was posted when thread {exited}, which died without an Exit grant, left at a host-timed moment (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440)"
5095                    ));
5096                    info!(
5097                        "[scheduler] thread {} left at a host-timed moment: parent-death signal {} posted to process {} as host-timed",
5098                        exited, signal, child
5099                    );
5100                    self.record_host_timed_signals(
5101                        DetTid::from_raw(child.as_raw()),
5102                        HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
5103                        kernel_signal_bit(signal as libc::c_int),
5104                    );
5105                    let _ = signal::kill(Pid::from_raw(child.as_raw()), signal);
5106                }
5107            }
5108            match heir {
5109                Some(heir) => {
5110                    self.thread_tree.parent_death_parents.insert(child, heir);
5111                }
5112                None => {
5113                    self.thread_tree.parent_death_parents.remove(&child);
5114                }
5115            }
5116        }
5117    }
5118
5119    /// Send the parent-death signals decided since the last drain
5120    /// (`deliver_parent_death_signals`), in the order they were decided,
5121    /// through the scheduler's own send (`fire_alarm`), at this drain, where
5122    /// the run queue may change.
5123    fn flush_parent_death_signals(&mut self) {
5124        for (process, signal) in std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_parent_death_signals) {
5125            self.sending_parent_death = true;
5126            self.fire_alarm(process, DetTid::from_raw(process.as_raw()), signal);
5127            self.sending_parent_death = false;
5128        }
5129    }
5130
5131    /// The thread that becomes the parent-death parent of `exited`'s
5132    /// children: the first live thread of `process` that is not exiting
5133    /// (Linux's `find_alive_thread`, leader first, then by tid), or, when the
5134    /// whole process is going (its last thread, or an `exit_group` grant),
5135    /// the thread of the subreaper that adopts them (`find_child_reaper`).
5136    /// `None`: the container's init, which does not exit during the run.
5137    fn parent_death_heir(&self, exited: DetTid, process: DetPid) -> Option<DetTid> {
5138        // An exec's edge retires every other thread; the exec'ing one stays.
5139        if let Some((survivor_process, survivor)) = self.parent_death_exec_survivor
5140            && survivor_process == process
5141            && survivor != exited
5142        {
5143            return Some(survivor);
5144        }
5145        if !self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&process) {
5146            let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
5147                .thread_tree
5148                .my_thread_group(&DetTid::from_raw(process.as_raw()))
5149                .into_iter()
5150                .filter(|tid| {
5151                    *tid != exited
5152                        && self.next_turns.contains_key(tid)
5153                        && !self.committed_exits.contains(tid)
5154                })
5155                .collect();
5156            live.sort_by_key(|tid| (tid.as_raw() != process.as_raw(), *tid));
5157            if let Some(heir) = live.first() {
5158                return Some(*heir);
5159            }
5160        }
5161        self.find_child_reaper(process).map(|(_, owner)| owner)
5162    }
5163
5164    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-4000): orphan re-parenting to a child subreaper.
5165    /// Re-parent the children of `exited`, whose last thread just left the run
5166    /// set, as Linux's `forget_original_parent` does in `exit_notify`.
5167    ///
5168    /// The new parent is the nearest process on `exited`'s parent chain that
5169    /// is a child subreaper and still has a live thread (`find_new_reaper`).
5170    /// A child that has already exited becomes waitable by its new parent
5171    /// here. Without such a subreaper the child goes to the container's init,
5172    /// which no guest can wait for; its record is left as it was before
5173    /// subreapers were modeled, naming the dead parent, so a program that
5174    /// never sets the flag sees no change.
5175    ///
5176    /// This runs in the same scheduler critical section that makes `exited`
5177    /// itself waitable, so it is exactly as deterministic as that moment and
5178    /// never opens a window of its own. For an `exit` or `exit_group` with
5179    /// sequentialized threads (strict mode), that moment follows the
5180    /// scheduler-ordered `ResourceID::Exit` grant and precedes the next
5181    /// committed turn: the exiting thread goes back into the run queue with an
5182    /// empty request, and the quiesce wait (`are_all_quiesced`) selects no
5183    /// turn until its deregistration fills it. For a process killed by a
5184    /// signal it is the host-timed
5185    /// deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994), and the
5186    /// re-parent moves with it. On ptrace the kernel has already re-parented by
5187    /// then: the deregistration carries the final exit status, which the tracer
5188    /// sees only after `exit_notify`.
5189    ///
5190    /// The decision is made once per exit. `logically_kill_thread` can run
5191    /// again for the same dead process, from a thread's late exit hook at a
5192    /// moment the host chooses; by then every child has either moved to its
5193    /// subreaper or is an init orphan, and neither is collected again. A
5194    /// process that died without an Exit grant records a determinism loss
5195    /// when a subreaper adopts its orphans.
5196    ///
5197    /// Children are visited in pid order, so the waiters they wake join the
5198    /// run queue in an order that does not depend on hashing.
5199    fn reparent_orphans(&mut self, exited: DetPid) {
5200        let orphans = self.thread_tree.undecided_orphans_of(exited);
5201        if orphans.is_empty() {
5202            return;
5203        }
5204        let reaper = self.find_child_reaper(exited);
5205        if let Some((reaper, _)) = reaper
5206            && !self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&exited)
5207        {
5208            // Without an Exit grant (SIGKILL, another fatal signal, a fault)
5209            // the parent's exit is recorded at its host-timed deregistration,
5210            // and so is this adoption
5211            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). Say so rather
5212            // than let verification compare a schedule that host timing chose.
5213            self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
5214                "subreaper {reaper} adopted the orphans of process {exited}, which died without an Exit grant, at its host-timed deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994)"
5215            ));
5216        }
5217        for child in orphans {
5218            let Some((reaper, owner)) = reaper else {
5219                debug!(
5220                    "[scheduler] orphan {} of exited process {} goes to the container init",
5221                    child, exited
5222                );
5223                self.thread_tree.orphan_to_init(child);
5224                continue;
5225            };
5226            self.thread_tree.reparent_child(child, reaper, owner);
5227            #[cfg(test)]
5228            self.reparentings.push((child, reaper));
5229            info!(
5230                "[scheduler] re-parenting orphan {} of exited process {} to subreaper {}",
5231                child, exited, reaper
5232            );
5233            if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
5234                // Linux's reparent_leader makes the zombie's exit signal
5235                // SIGCHLD and notifies its new parent, which reaps it at once
5236                // if it reaps children automatically
5237                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091).
5238                if self.thread_tree.reaps_children_automatically(reaper) {
5239                    self.autoreaped_exits.insert(child);
5240                }
5241                self.wake_child_waiters(reaper, child);
5242            }
5243        }
5244    }

5290    /// Record a determinism loss for the run (`detlog::write_loss_notice`).
5291    /// Tests read the reasons this scheduler recorded, rather than the
5292    /// process-wide latch, which keeps whichever reason any test wrote first.

5299    /// The process and thread that inherit `exited`'s orphans
5300    /// (`reparent_orphans`): the nearest live child subreaper among its
5301    /// ancestors, and that process's first live thread, its leader if the
5302    /// leader is live (Linux's `find_alive_thread`). The search stops at a
5303    /// process that already went to the container's init: Linux's parent
5304    /// chain from there leads to init, whatever the stale record names. It
5305    /// also stops at a PID namespace boundary, as Linux's `find_new_reaper`
5306    /// does: an ancestor in an outer namespace never adopts. (Linux then gives
5307    /// the orphan to its own namespace's init; that adoption is not modeled,
5308    /// so such an orphan is left as before subreapers were.)
5309    fn find_child_reaper(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Option<(DetPid, DetTid)> {
5310        if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(exited) {
5311            return None;
5312        }
5313        let depth = self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(exited);
5314        let mut ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&exited);
5315        while let Some(candidate) = ancestor {
5316            if self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(candidate) != depth {
5317                return self.namespace_reaper(exited);
5318            }
5319            // A process killed by the SIGKILL being committed is dying, like a
5320            // subreaper with no live thread: the search passes it by.
5321            if self.thread_tree.is_child_subreaper(candidate)
5322                && !self.is_dying_sigkill_victim(candidate)
5323            {
5324                let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
5325                    .thread_tree
5326                    .my_thread_group(&candidate)
5327                    .into_iter()
5328                    .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
5329                    .collect();
5330                live.sort_by_key(|tid| (*tid != candidate, *tid));
5331                if let Some(owner) = live.first() {
5332                    return Some((candidate, *owner));
5333                }
5334            }
5335            if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(candidate) {
5336                return None;
5337            }
5338            ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&candidate);
5339        }
5340        self.namespace_reaper(exited)
5341    }
5342
5343    /// `exiting`'s exit was just granted. If it is a PID namespace's init, its
5344    /// namespace ends with it: Linux's `zap_pid_namespace` sends SIGKILL to
5345    /// every live process left in it, which then die at host-timed moments
5346    /// Detcore does not order, so that is a determinism loss, named here
5347    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155). Every other thread is
5348    /// stopped at a request or parked at this grant, so which members are
5349    /// live is fixed by the schedule. A zombie is already dead.
5350    fn note_pid_namespace_end(&mut self, exiting: DetPid) {
5351        if self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(exiting) != Some(exiting) {
5352            return;
5353        }
5354        let mut live: Vec<DetPid> = self
5355            .thread_tree
5356            .pid_namespaces
5357            .members(exiting)
5358            .into_iter()
5359            .filter(|task| self.next_turns.contains_key(task))
5360            .filter_map(|task| self.thread_tree.process_of(task))
5361            .filter(|process| *process != exiting)
5362            .collect();
5363        live.sort();
5364        live.dedup();
5365        if !live.is_empty() {
5366            self.namespace_zap_victims.extend(live.iter().copied());
5367            self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
5368                "PID namespace init {exiting} exited while its namespace still held live processes {live:?}; Linux kills them at host-timed moments (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155)"
5369            ));
5370        }
5371    }
5372
5373    /// `child`, a process just created, belongs to a PID namespace whose
5374    /// init's exit is already granted. Linux lets such a fork succeed until
5375    /// it starts killing the namespace (`zap_pid_namespace`), then kills the
5376    /// child with the rest, so it is a victim like those
5377    /// `note_pid_namespace_end` named.
5378    pub(crate) fn note_member_of_ended_namespace(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
5379        let chain = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.chain_of(child);
5380        if chain
5381            .iter()
5382            .any(|init| *init != child && self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(init))
5383        {
5384            self.namespace_zap_victims.insert(child);
5385        }
5386    }
5387
5388    /// Whether a process `note_pid_namespace_end` saw Linux about to kill
5389    /// still has a thread in the scheduler. Victims whose threads are all
5390    /// gone are dropped. The run already carries the determinism loss for
5391    /// them, so waiting here only lets the host's kill arrive; it cannot make
5392    /// a comparable run depend on host timing.
5393    fn awaiting_namespace_zap(&mut self) -> bool {
5394        let next_turns = &self.next_turns;
5395        let thread_tree = &self.thread_tree;
5396        self.namespace_zap_victims.retain(|victim| {
5397            next_turns
5398                .keys()
5399                .any(|tid| thread_tree.process_of(*tid) == Some(*victim))
5400        });
5401        !self.namespace_zap_victims.is_empty()
5402    }
5403
5404    /// The reaper Linux's `find_new_reaper` falls back to when no subreaper
5405    /// adopts: the init of `exited`'s own PID namespace
5406    /// (`pid_namespace::child_reaper`), with its first live thread, leader
5407    /// first (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4090). `None` in the
5408    /// container's namespace, whose init is Hermit (the orphan goes to it,
5409    /// `orphan_to_init`), and for the namespace's init itself, whose
5410    /// namespace ends with it.
5411    fn namespace_reaper(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Option<(DetPid, DetTid)> {
5412        let init = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(exited)?;
5413        if init == exited {
5414            return None;
5415        }
5416        let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
5417            .thread_tree
5418            .my_thread_group(&init)
5419            .into_iter()
5420            .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
5421            .collect();
5422        live.sort_by_key(|tid| (*tid != init, *tid));
5423        live.first().map(|owner| (init, *owner))
5424    }

5426    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
5427    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1173): Review SaBRe exec incarnation reconciliation.
5428    /// Apply Linux's successful-exec rule when a backend reloads its tool.
5429    ///
5430    /// Every sibling disappears. If a non-leader called exec, Linux also changes
5431    /// that surviving task's TID to the process leader's TID. In that case the old
5432    /// caller registration is retired and a fresh leader registration is installed
5433    /// before it is removed, so process-exit barriers cannot observe a transiently
5434    /// empty thread group.
5435    pub fn reconnect_after_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
5436        self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, None)
5437    }
5438
5439    /// Reconnect a non-leader exec whose backend preserved the caller's Tool
5440    /// state and PMU. The replay cursor, rather than the destroyed leader's
5441    /// pending duration, determines the replacement's next grant. The grant
5442    /// returns a relative duration; reconnect itself advances neither time nor
5443    /// the replay cursor and does not issue a scheduler turn.
5444    pub(crate) fn reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
5445        assert_ne!(reconnect.caller, reconnect.new_leader);
5446        let replay_resume = self.replayer.as_ref().and_then(Replayer::next_resume);
5447        let former = reconnect.caller;
5448        let leader = reconnect.new_leader;
5449        let consumed_syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.get(&leader).copied().unwrap_or(0);
5450        let retired = self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, replay_resume);
5451        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.insert(former);
5452        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
5453            .insert(leader, consumed_syscalls);
5454        retired
5455    }
5456
5457    fn reconnect_exec(
5458        &mut self,
5459        reconnect: ExecReconnect,
5460        replay_resume: Option<(DetTid, Option<LogicalTime>)>,
5461    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
5462        let ExecReconnect {
5463            caller,
5464            new_leader,
5465            detpid,
5466            pre_exec_mm,
5467            post_exec_mm,
5468            child_tid_addr,
5469            reconnect_priority,
5470        } = reconnect;
5471        let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
5472        assert!(group.contains(&caller));
5473        assert!(group.contains(&new_leader));
5474        self.exec_incarnations.insert(new_leader, post_exec_mm);
5475        self.thread_mms.insert(new_leader, post_exec_mm);
5476        // Reloading backends enter thread-start before handle_post_exec. Cancel
5477        // old POSIX deadlines before admitting the replacement's first turn.
5478        self.delete_exec_posix_timers(detpid);
5479
5480        let siblings = if self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&detpid) {
5481            let teardown = &self.exec_teardowns[&detpid];
5482            assert_eq!((teardown.caller, teardown.mm), (caller, pre_exec_mm));
5483            self.finish_exec_teardown(caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm, true)
5484        } else {
5485            // Reloading backends and older callers may already have retired
5486            // their siblings; retain their existing idempotent reconciliation.
5487            let mut siblings: Vec<_> = group.into_iter().filter(|tid| *tid != caller).collect();
5488            siblings.sort();
5489            self.parent_death_exec_survivor = Some((detpid, caller));
5490            for sibling in &siblings {
5491                self.logically_kill_thread(sibling, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
5492                self.timeslices.remove(sibling);
5493            }
5494            self.parent_death_exec_survivor = None;
5495            siblings
5496        };
5497        self.transfer_replay_copies(caller, new_leader, &siblings);
5498
5499        if caller == new_leader {
5500            self.next_turns
5501                .get_mut(&caller)
5502                .expect("exec caller must retain a scheduler registration")
5503                .child_tid_addr = child_tid_addr;
5504
5505            self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&siblings);
5506            return siblings;
5507        }
5508
5509        if let Some(refusal) = self
5510            .happens_before
5511            .as_ref()
5512            .and_then(|hb| hb.relative_identity_refusal(caller, new_leader))
5513            && self.terminal_deadlock.is_none()
5514        {
5515            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
5516            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
5517        }
5518
5519        self.thread_tree
5520            .transfer_exec_wait_owner(detpid, caller, new_leader);
5521        // The exec'ing thread survives as the leader, so its children keep
5522        // their parent, and its own parent-death signal goes with it.
5523        self.thread_tree
5524            .transfer_exec_parent_death(caller, new_leader);
5525        // The caller's own queue survives under the leader's tid; the
5526        // leader's went with the leader (`logically_kill_thread` above).
5527        self.transfer_thread_timer_copies(caller, new_leader);
5528        self.discarded_at_send.rekey_thread(caller, new_leader);
5529
5530        let survivor_priority = match replay_resume {
5531            Some((next_tid, _)) if next_tid == new_leader => REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY,
5532            Some(_) => REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY,
5533            None => self
5534                .priorities
5535                .get(&caller)
5536                .copied()
5537                .or(reconnect_priority)
5538                .expect("exec caller must have a scheduler priority"),
5539        };
5540        let mut retired = siblings;
5541
5542        // The leader identity was occupied by a thread the kernel destroyed as
5543        // part of this exec. This is the one intentional exception to permanent
5544        // raw-TID tombstones: the pending exec record proves why Linux reused it.
5545        self.logically_killed_threads.remove(&new_leader);
5546        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&new_leader);
5547        self.retired_exited_leaders.remove(&new_leader);
5548        // The new incarnation has not exited; whether the old one's exit was
5549        // granted decides its run-queue hand-over below.
5550        let old_leader_exit_granted = self.committed_exits.remove(&new_leader);
5551        self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
5552        assert!(
5553            self.next_turns
5554                .insert(
5555                    new_leader,
5556                    ThreadNextTurn {
5557                        dettid: new_leader,
5558                        child_tid_addr,
5559                        req: Ivar::new(),
5560                        resp: Ivar::new(),
5561                        protocol: Default::default(),
5562                    },
5563                )
5564                .is_none(),
5565            "retired exec leader still had a scheduler registration"
5566        );
5567        self.priorities.insert(new_leader, survivor_priority);
5568        if let Some((next_tid, timeslice)) = replay_resume
5569            && next_tid == new_leader
5570        {
5571            // Rebuild only the current cursor's decision. The removed entry
5572            // could have belonged to the displaced leader, while a prehook's
5573            // ContextSwitch(false, new_leader, ..) already refers to the
5574            // replacement. Neither priority nor the old entry distinguishes
5575            // those cases, and the cursor may have advanced in the meantime.
5576            self.timeslices.insert(new_leader, timeslice);
5577        }
5578        if let Some(writer) = &mut self.preemption_writer {
5579            writer.set_current(new_leader, survivor_priority);
5580        }
5581        // Post-exec reconnection can arrive asynchronously on backends whose
5582        // exec-child self-bootstraps outside a scheduler turn (DBT), so route
5583        // the new leader's admission (a run-queue *push*) through the
5584        // tentative-safe buffer rather than pushing directly.
5585        //
5586        // The exec caller's fresh next-turn request is the causal anchor. Step5
5587        // installed that empty Ivar before the caller began executing exec, so
5588        // the daemon cannot pass step1 while the successful exec is in flight.
5589        // This handler records the complete old-leader removal/replacement
5590        // admission pair before `logically_kill_thread(caller)` resolves that
5591        // request. The scheduler mutex then prevents step2 from observing only
5592        // half of the handoff. Host delay can move the handler relative to the
5593        // daemon's wait, but cannot change first-drain membership.
5594        //
5595        // The *removals* in this handler (`logically_kill_thread` ->
5596        // `run_queue.remove_tid`, for the exec caller and its siblings, above
5597        // and below) are likewise tentative-safe: `logically_kill_thread` now
5598        // routes the run-queue removal through `deschedule_or_defer`, which
5599        // buffers it to the same deterministic `step2` drain. The old leader's
5600        // removal is explicitly classified as `ReplaceThenAdmit`, so the drain
5601        // removes its physical queue slot without cancelling the new
5602        // incarnation. `are_all_quiesced` filters every pending removal key;
5603        // ordinary targets are logically dead, while the replacement key is not
5604        // runnable until that old slot has been removed and its admission
5605        // applied. No handler mutates the queue inside a tentative window.
5606        //
5607        // A leader retired at its own exit while its group lived on
5608        // (`retire_exited_leader`) left the run queue then, and a step2 drain
5609        // has usually consumed that removal already: there is no old slot left
5610        // to replace, so the new incarnation is only admitted. Its granted
5611        // exit (`committed_exits`, cleared only when the tid is registered
5612        // again) marks that case; the retirement record itself may already
5613        // be consumed by the zombie leader's deregistration, which the exec
5614        // delivers (Claude re-check of
5615        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245).
5616        if old_leader_exit_granted
5617            && !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&new_leader)
5618            && !self.run_queue.contains_tid(new_leader)
5619        {
5620            self.admit_to_run_queue(new_leader, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
5621        } else {
5622            self.replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(
5623                new_leader,
5624                AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back),
5625            );
5626        }
5627        self.started_up.try_put(());
5628
5629        self.logically_kill_thread(&caller, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
5630        self.timeslices.remove(&caller);
5631        retired.push(caller);
5632        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
5633        retired
5634    }
5635
5636    /// Install the barrier for a vfork parent whose `BlockingVfork` was just
5637    /// granted. State left by an earlier thread with the same TID is stale:
5638    /// that thread is gone, so a barrier it kept for its child, and a
5639    /// tombstone its child never settled, are dropped here, inside this
5640    /// committed turn.
5641    fn begin_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
5642        // The only barrier `parent` can still hold is one kept for a dead
5643        // thread with the same TID: a live parent's own barrier ends at its
5644        // continuation (step2a) before it can be granted another vfork.
5645        assert!(
5646            !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent)
5647                || self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent),
5648            "dettid {parent} began a vfork while its own live barrier stands"
5649        );
5650        self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
5651        self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent);
5652        self.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
5653    }
5654
5655    /// Remove `parent`'s barrier and every record about it.
5656    fn drop_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
5657        self.vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
5658        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
5659        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
5660        self.released_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
5661    }
5662
5663    /// `parent` is being logically killed. With no child registered yet, its
5664    /// barrier goes and a tombstone lets the child register as an orphan.
5665    /// With a registered child the barrier goes now if the child already
5666    /// reached a release edge or is gone, because then the child cannot be
5667    /// selected in its vfork role any more; otherwise it stays, marked
5668    /// parent-dead, until the child's next release edge. The outcome does not
5669    /// depend on whether this retirement arrives before or after that edge.
5670    fn retire_vfork_parent(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
5671        match self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent).copied() {
5672            None => {}
5673            Some(None) => {
5674                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
5675                self.dead_vfork_parents.insert(parent);
5676            }
5677            Some(Some(child))
5678                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
5679                    && !self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) =>
5680            {
5681                self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
5682            }
5683            Some(Some(_)) => self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent),
5684        }
5685    }
5686
5687    /// `child` reached a release edge: its `Exit` grant, its successful exec
5688    /// (`record_successful_exec`), or its logical kill. A barrier whose parent
5689    /// has died goes now. Otherwise the barrier is marked released, and step2a
5690    /// waits, committing nothing, until the parent's continuation or
5691    /// retirement, then drops it.
5692    pub(crate) fn release_vfork_child(&mut self, child: DetTid) {
5693        let parents: Vec<DetTid> = self
5694            .vfork_barriers
5695            .iter()
5696            .filter(|(_, registered)| **registered == Some(child))
5697            .map(|(parent, _)| *parent)
5698            .collect();
5699        for parent in parents {
5700            if self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) {
5701                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
5702            } else {
5703                self.released_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
5704            }
5705        }
5706    }
5707
5708    fn remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&mut self, retired: &[DetTid]) {
5709        self.vfork_barriers.retain(|parent, child| {
5710            !retired.contains(parent) && !child.is_some_and(|tid| retired.contains(&tid))
5711        });
5712        self.vfork_registration_origins
5713            .retain(|parent, _| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
5714        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers
5715            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
5716        self.released_vfork_barriers
5717            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
5718    }

5721    pub(crate) fn vfork_barrier_mentions(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5722        self.vfork_barriers
5723            .iter()
5724            .any(|(parent, child)| *parent == dettid || child == &Some(dettid))
5725    }

5754    /// Records `dettid` as the thread holding the serial grant, as
5755    /// `unblock_guest` does when it grants a turn.
5756    #[cfg(test)]
5757    pub(crate) fn set_running_for_test(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
5758        self.parked.running = Some(dettid);
5759    }

5762    pub(crate) fn select_test_turn(
5763        &mut self,

5768    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1023): Review fail-closed SaBRe thread tombstones.
5769    pub(crate) fn thread_is_logically_killed(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5770        self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
5771            && self.logically_killed_threads.contains(&dettid)
5772    }
5773
5774    /// Grant `dettid`'s next request, its group `Exit`, at the very next
5775    /// turn, before any other thread runs. Sent by a thread that holds the
5776    /// serial grant in its signal-delivery turn, after it read that the
5777    /// signal's default action ends the process. Linux commits that decision
5778    /// under the signal lock and queues SIGKILL to every other thread of the
5779    /// group at once (`complete_signal`), so no sibling runs another user
5780    /// instruction after it; here, no sibling takes a turn between the
5781    /// decision and the grant that ends the group
5782    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4278, Claude re-check of
5783    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4387). Returns whether
5784    /// `dettid` holds the grant; a thread that does not is ignored.
5785    pub(crate) fn hold_turn_for_group_exit(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5786        let holds = self.holds_serial_grant(dettid);
5787        if holds {
5788            self.group_exit_decider = Some(dettid);
5789        } else {
5790            tracing::warn!(
5791                "[scheduler] dettid {dettid} asked to keep its turn for a group exit without holding the serial grant"
5792            );
5793        }
5794        holds
5795    }
5796
5797    /// The thread whose group `Exit` must be granted next
5798    /// (`hold_turn_for_group_exit`), if it is queued with that request. A
5799    /// decider that left the run set otherwise is forgotten.
5800    fn queued_group_exit_decider(&mut self) -> Option<DetTid> {
5801        let decider = self.group_exit_decider?;
5802        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&decider) {
5803            self.group_exit_decider = None;
5804            return None;
5805        }
5806        self.run_queue
5807            .contains_non_polling_tid(decider)
5808            .then_some(decider)
5809    }
5810
5811    /// Whether `dettid` is running in a turn the scheduler granted it, now:
5812    /// - it is the thread last granted a turn (`parked.running`, set only by
5813    ///   `unblock_guest`), and neither a backend failure nor a logical kill
5814    ///   has ended its run;
5815    /// - it has not filed its next request yet. `unblock_guest` installs a
5816    ///   fresh, empty request slot at the grant, and the thread's next
5817    ///   request fills it, which surrenders the turn;
5818    /// - the grant did not release it into the background. A thread running a
5819    ///   blocking call outside the runnable set (`external_io_blockers`, which
5820    ///   includes a copying vfork's parent, or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or
5821    ///   one woken there by a signal (`signaled_background`), does not hold
5822    ///   the turn even before the next grant moves `parked.running` away.
5823    pub(crate) fn holds_serial_grant(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5824        !self.backend_failed()
5825            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
5826            && self.parked.running == Some(dettid)
5827            && self
5828                .next_turns
5829                .get(&dettid)
5830                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req.is_empty())
5831            && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
5832            && !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
5833            && !self.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&dettid)
5834    }

5836    /// Record the address-space identity `dettid` registered with
5837    /// (`thread_mms`).
5838    pub(crate) fn record_thread_mm(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
5839        self.thread_mms.insert(dettid, mm);
5840    }

5842    /// The address-space identity recorded for `dettid` (`thread_mms`).
5843    pub(crate) fn thread_mm(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<MmId> {
5844        self.thread_mms.get(&dettid).copied()
5845    }

5847    pub(crate) fn rpc_incarnation_matches(&self, dettid: DetTid, mm: MmId) -> bool {
5848        !self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&dettid)
5849            && self
5850                .exec_incarnations
5851                .get(&dettid)
5852                .is_none_or(|expected| *expected == mm)
5853    }
5854
5855    /// A newborn may reach StartNewThread before its parent registers it. It
5856    /// must wait without publishing a clock until registration consumes this
5857    /// marker; ordinary messages cannot use startup as authority to clear it.
5858    pub(crate) fn transferred_exec_tid_requires_registration(&self, tid: DetTid) -> bool {
5859        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid)
5860    }
5861
5862    /// Called only by authenticated fresh child registration. A raw Linux TID
5863    /// can be reused after exec retired its former owner; an ordinary RPC
5864    /// cannot reopen it. Bind the new address space in the same transaction so
5865    /// delayed messages from a different old image remain rejected.
5866    pub(crate) fn register_reused_transferred_exec_tid(&mut self, tid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
5867        if !self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid) {
5868            return;
5869        }
5870        assert!(
5871            !self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid),
5872            "a reused exec caller must not have a live registration"
5873        );
5874        self.exec_incarnations.insert(tid, mm);
5875        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&tid);
5876        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.remove(&tid);
5877        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.remove(&tid);
5878    }
