5880    pub(crate) fn backend_failed(&self) -> bool {
5881        self.backend_failure.is_some()
5882    }
5883
5884    pub(crate) fn backend_failure_waiter(&self) -> Shared<oneshot::Receiver<()>> {
5885        self.backend_failure_wake.clone()
5886    }
5887
5888    /// Linearize failure with ordinary grants. Close the transaction here,
5889    /// before any awakened Tool can run consuming clear-TID/futex cleanup.
5890    /// The daemon observes the terminal state and must not undo it a second
5891    /// time. The caller sends the notification after releasing this mutex.
5892    pub(crate) fn report_backend_failure(
5893        &mut self,
5894        event: reverie::BackendFailure,
5895    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
5896        self.report_backend_failure_location(BackendFailureLocation {
5897            pid: event.pid,
5898            tid: Some(event.tid),
5899            phase: event.phase,
5900        })
5901    }
5902
5903    fn report_backend_failure_location(
5904        &mut self,
5905        event: BackendFailureLocation,
5906    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
5907        if self.backend_failed() {
5908            return None;
5909        }
5910        if self.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress() {
5911            self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
5912        }
5913        tracing::error!(
5914            "backend failure for process {}, task {:?}, phase {}",
5915            event.pid,
5916            event.tid,
5917            event.phase
5918        );
5919        self.backend_failure = Some(event);
5920        self.backend_failure_sender.take()
5921    }
5922
5923    /// Construction does not imply scheduler registration: a backend may
5924    /// consume a child before its parent has sent CreateChildThread.
5925    pub(crate) fn thread_was_registered(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5926        self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.contains_key(&dettid)
5927    }
5928
5929    /// Retire the thread-group leader `leader` at its own `exit`, issued after
5930    /// its granted `Exit` and its last request, while another thread of its
5931    /// group is still registered. Linux leaves such a leader a zombie: it runs
5932    /// no more code, its group lives on, and the group's last thread ends the
5933    /// process. Its backend deregistration comes only when the whole group has
5934    /// gone (ptrace reports a leader's exit status after its last sibling's),
5935    /// so until then the scheduler would wait for a turn request that never
5936    /// comes (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). The leader
5937    /// leaves the scheduler here instead, in its own turn, and its later
5938    /// deregistration only accounts it (`take_retired_exited_leader`).
5939    /// Returns whether it was retired; a leader whose group has no other
5940    /// registered thread is left to its deregistration as before.
5941    ///
5942    /// No turn is committed from here until the kernel shows the leader a
5943    /// zombie (`exited_leader_barriers`): its exit, which the leader injects
5944    /// after this request, releases its address space and files, zeroes its
5945    /// `clear_child_tid` word and moves its signal targeting, and the
5946    /// siblings must see all of that done. Only where the scheduler models
5947    /// signal targets (ptrace) is a thread's `/proc` view its DetTid's, so
5948    /// only there is the leader retired here; elsewhere it is left to its
5949    /// deregistration, as before.
5950    pub(crate) fn retire_exited_leader(&mut self, leader: DetTid, mm: MmId) -> bool {
5951        if !self.leader_retires_at_exit(leader, mm) {
5952            return false;
5953        }
5954        let process = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
5955        self.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &process, mm);
5956        self.retired_exited_leaders.insert(leader);
5957        self.exited_leader_barriers
5958            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
5959        true
5960    }
5961
5962    /// Whether `retire_exited_leader` retires `leader`: on a backend whose
5963    /// `/proc` view is the scheduler's, a thread-group leader, of this
5964    /// incarnation, whose `Exit` was granted, while another thread of its
5965    /// group is registered.
5966    fn leader_retires_at_exit(&self, leader: DetTid, mm: MmId) -> bool {
5967        let process = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
5968        self.models_signal_targets
5969            && self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&process)
5970            && self.committed_exits.contains(&leader)
5971            && self.rpc_incarnation_matches(leader, mm)
5972            && self.next_turns.contains_key(&leader)
5973            && self
5974                .thread_tree
5975                .my_thread_group(&process)
5976                .into_iter()
5977                .any(|tid| tid != leader && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid))
5978    }
5979
5980    /// Whether `named` is a leader `retire_exited_leader` retired at its own
5981    /// exit while its group lives on, and that has not registered again. The
5982    /// scheduler commits no other turn until the kernel shows such a leader a
5983    /// zombie (`step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders`), so from any later turn it is
5984    /// one. Only a backend that models signal targets retires a leader so
5985    /// (`leader_retires_at_exit`); elsewhere this is always false
5986    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4445).
5987    pub(crate) fn names_a_retired_exited_leader(&self, named: DetTid) -> bool {
5988        self.retired_exited_leaders.contains(&named) && !self.next_turns.contains_key(&named)
5989    }
5990
5991    /// Whether `dettid` is a leader `retire_exited_leader` already retired;
5992    /// its deregistration then retires nothing more. Consumes the record.
5993    pub(crate) fn take_retired_exited_leader(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5994        self.retired_exited_leaders.remove(&dettid)
5995    }
5996
5997    /// Retire `dettid` at its accounted deregistration, unless an exec
5998    /// defers it or it is already logically killed. A leader retired at its
5999    /// own exit while its group lived on (`retire_exited_leader`) was retired
6000    /// then: by now its group may have ended, and retiring it again would run
6001    /// its process's end a second time, at this host-timed moment (deciding
6002    /// again whether its parent reaps it automatically, and waking the
6003    /// parent's waiters again).
6004    pub(crate) fn retire_deregistered_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, detpid: DetPid, mm: MmId) {
6005        if self.take_retired_exited_leader(dettid) {
6006            return;
6007        }
6008        self.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);
6009        if !self.defer_exec_sibling_retirement(dettid, detpid, mm)
6010            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
6011        {
6012            self.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, mm);
6013        }
6014    }
6015
6016    /// After `dettid`'s own `Exit` was granted, its deregistration may come
6017    /// before the kernel carries out the exit; on DBT it always does. Hold
6018    /// turns until the kernel shows the thread exited
6019    /// (`exited_thread_barriers`). The pidfd must name this incarnation: an
6020    /// exec's earlier image deregisters while the same host thread lives on.
6021    fn hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
6022        if !self.committed_exits.contains(&dettid) {
6023            return;
6024        }
6025        if self
6026            .physical_thread_pidfds
6027            .get(&dettid)
6028            .is_some_and(|(registered_mm, ..)| *registered_mm == mm)
6029        {
6030            self.hold_turns_until_gone(dettid);
6031        }
6032    }
6033
6034    /// Add an `exited_thread_barriers` entry for `thread`'s registered host
6035    /// thread, if it has one.
6036    fn hold_turns_until_gone(&mut self, thread: DetTid) {
6037        let Some((_, physical_pid, physical_tid, pidfd)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&thread)
6038        else {
6039            return;
6040        };
6041        match pidfd.try_clone() {
6042            Ok(pidfd) => {
6043                let barrier = ExitedThreadBarrier {
6044                    pidfd,
6045                    physical_pid: *physical_pid,
6046                    physical_tid: *physical_tid,
6047                    since: std::time::Instant::now(),
6048                };
6049                self.exited_thread_barriers.insert(thread, barrier);
6050            }
6051            Err(error) => {
6052                let reason = format!(
6053                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: cannot hold turns until exited thread {thread} is gone: \
6054                     duplicating its pidfd failed: {error}"
6055                );
6056                tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
6057                self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
6058            }
6059        }
6060    }
6061
6062    /// At an exit_group's grant, hold turns until the kernel has ended every
6063    /// thread of `process` whose host thread has a registered pidfd
6064    /// (`exited_thread_barriers`). The threads the grant kills have no Exit
6065    /// grant of their own, so their deregistrations add no hold.
6066    pub(crate) fn hold_turns_until_the_group_ends(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
6067        for thread in self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&process) {
6068            self.hold_turns_until_gone(thread);
6069        }
6070    }
6071
6072    /// Mark a physical exit cleanup as accounted. A transferred leader must
6073    /// consume each incarnation once even on a non-cancelling backend; other
6074    /// non-cancelling identities preserve their existing behavior.
6075    pub(crate) fn note_deregistration_accounted(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
6076        // Remember an owner accounted before a later peer failure as well.
6077        // Ordinary non-cancelling behavior still accepts its prior callbacks.
6078        let first = self.deregistration_accounted.insert(dettid);
6079        (!self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
6080            && !self.backend_failed()
6081            && !self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.contains_key(&dettid))
6082            || first
6083    }
6084
6085    /// Install a barrier between SaBRe's logical process-leader exit hook and the final ptrace
6086    /// wait status. Other backends retain their existing lifecycle behavior.
6087    pub(crate) fn begin_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6088        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
6089            && self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
6090        {
6091            // Monotone lifetime: an exit the backend already reported complete
6092            // (before its grant, or before a late deregistration) never
6093            // becomes pending again.
6094            return false;
6095        }
6096        if self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits
6097            || self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
6098        {
6099            self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
6100            let inserted = self.pending_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
6101            if inserted {
6102                trace!(
6103                    "[detcore, dpid {}] waiting for final physical process exit",
6104                    detpid
6105                );
6106            }
6107            inserted
6108        } else {
6109            false
6110        }
6111    }
6112
6113    /// Release the exact process barrier when the ptrace supervisor receives its final `Exited`
6114    /// or `Signaled` wait status. At that lifecycle point the process is physically waitable.
6115    /// The backend reports that the kernel has published `detpid`'s exit to
6116    /// its parent (`BackendCapabilities::reports_child_exit_publication`).
6117    /// Releases the hold the exit grant placed for a None or Discard
6118    /// notification; any other process is ignored. Returns whether a hold was
6119    /// released.
6120    pub(crate) fn complete_child_exit_publication(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6121        let released = self.child_exit_publications_pending.remove(&detpid);
6122        self.note_sigkill_publication(detpid);
6123        if !released {
6124            // No hold yet: the process was consumed before its Exit request
6125            // was granted (or has none). Remember it, so a stale grant does
6126            // not install a hold this report can no longer release.
6127            self.child_exit_publications_completed.insert(detpid);
6128        }
6129        released
6130    }
6131
6132    /// A successful exec by `process`, for the exit-signal rules it applies
6133    /// (`ThreadTree::record_successful_exec`).
6134    pub(crate) fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
6135        self.thread_tree.record_successful_exec(process);
6136        // The exec is a vfork child's release edge, while the exec caller
6137        // still owns its turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
6138        // A vfork child is a single-threaded process, so the caller is
6139        // `process`; an exec that retires a vfork child as a sibling or a
6140        // non-leader caller goes through `remove_exec_vfork_barriers`.
6141        self.release_vfork_child(process);
6142    }
6143
6144    /// Record (`Some`) or clear (`None`) the mask Linux's `blocked` holds for
6145    /// `dettid` while its kernel `SigBlk` differs (`saved_guest_sigmasks`).
6146    /// Returns false for a thread the scheduler no longer knows.
6147    pub(crate) fn set_saved_guest_sigmask(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mask: Option<u64>) -> bool {
6148        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) {
6149            return false;
6150        }
6151        match mask {
6152            Some(mask) => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.insert(dettid, mask),
6153            None => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(&dettid),
6154        };
6155        true
6156    }
6157
6158    /// Record (`Some`) or clear (`None`) the set `dettid` waits for in
6159    /// `rt_sigtimedwait`. Returns false for a thread the scheduler no longer
6160    /// knows.
6161    pub(crate) fn set_sigtimedwait_set(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, set: Option<u64>) -> bool {
6162        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) {
6163            return false;
6164        }
6165        // A poll of the set takes a pending copy of any signal in it, so a
6166        // timer's copy of one may be consumed from here until the call ends.
6167        let covered = match set {
6168            Some(set) => {
6169                self.sigtimedwait_sets.insert(dettid, set);
6170                set
6171            }
6172            None => self.sigtimedwait_sets.remove(&dettid).unwrap_or(0),
6173        };
6174
6175        self.thread_timer_copies.retain(|(thread, signo), _| {
6176            *thread != dettid || covered & kernel_signal_bit(*signo) == 0
6177        });
6178        true
6179    }
6180
6181    /// The inputs to a process-directed signal that `sender` sends to its own
6182    /// process, read in `sender`'s turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034).
6183    /// Every other thread is then stopped at a request, parked, or outside the
6184    /// schedule, so each mask read here is the one the schedule left it with
6185    /// (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
6186    pub(crate) fn own_process_signal_inputs(&self, sender: DetTid) -> OwnProcessSignalInputs {
6187        let process = self.sigchld_process(sender);
6188        // A thread is in `next_turns` from its creation to its removal
6189        // (`process_signal_targets`), so this is every live thread.
6190        let siblings = self
6191            .process_signal_targets(process)
6192            .into_iter()
6193            .filter(|thread| *thread != sender)
6194            .map(|thread| (thread, self.sibling_signal_state(thread)))
6195            .collect();
6196        let foreign_exit_signals = self
6197            .thread_tree
6198            .unreaped_children_of(process)
6199            .into_iter()
6200            .filter_map(|child| self.thread_tree.notification_signal(child))
6201            .filter(|signal| *signal != 0 && *signal != libc::SIGCHLD)
6202            .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal));
6203        OwnProcessSignalInputs {
6204            siblings,
6205            host_timed: self.host_timed_signals(sender),
6206            foreign_exit_signals,
6207            // Only a copy still in the process's shared queue can be dequeued
6208            // before the send; one taken by sigtimedwait, discarded by
6209            // SIG_IGN, or merged into an earlier copy of the same standard
6210            // signal (Hermit emulates a POSIX timer with kill(), so its copy
6211            // merges where Linux would queue the timer's own) is gone
6212            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122).
6213            undelivered_scheduler_signals: self
6214                .undelivered_scheduler_signals
6215                .get(&process)
6216                .copied()
6217                .unwrap_or(0)
6218                & self.read_shared_pending(sender).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
6219            exec_in_flight: self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&process),
6220            guest_marker_signal: self.guest_sent_marker_signal,
6221        }
6222    }
6223
6224    /// Record that a guest sent SIGSTKFLT. Reverie uses SIGSTKFLT as its timer
6225    /// marker, and a process-directed signal to the sender's own process
6226    /// excludes only Reverie's own copy from its check of the sender's queue,
6227    /// so it refuses once a guest copy may be pending
6228    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034).
6229    pub(crate) fn record_guest_marker_signal(&mut self) {
6230        self.guest_sent_marker_signal = true;
6231    }
6232
6233    /// The scheduler sent `signal` to `dettid`'s process (`signal_guest`;
6234    /// `undelivered_scheduler_signals`).
6235    fn note_scheduler_signal_sent(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: libc::c_int) {
6236        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
6237        *self
6238            .undelivered_scheduler_signals
6239            .entry(process)
6240            .or_default() |= kernel_signal_bit(signal);
6241    }
6242
6243    /// `thread`'s state for `own_process_signal_inputs`.
6244    fn sibling_signal_state(&self, thread: DetTid) -> SiblingSignalState {
6245        if self.parked.exit_fences.contains_key(&thread)
6246            || self.logically_killed_threads.contains(&thread)
6247        {
6248            return SiblingSignalState::ExitGranted;
6249        }
6250        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&thread)
6251            || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&thread)
6252        {
6253            return SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule;
6254        }
6255        // The kernel chooses by the thread's own mask (`SigBlk`), which a
6256        // stopped or parked thread cannot change, or by the guest's mask
6257        // while Detcore holds the thread under a private one
6258        // (`saved_guest_sigmasks`). A parked futex waiter's watch is the set
6259        // that ends its wait, not its mask.
6260        let mask = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&thread) {
6261            Some(saved) => Some(*saved),
6262            None => self.read_thread_blocked_mask(thread),
6263        };
6264        SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(mask.map(|mask| match self.sigtimedwait_sets.get(&thread) {
6265            Some(set) => mask & !set,
6266            None => mask,
6267        }))
6268    }
6269
6270    /// Classify `child`'s exit notification to `parent` at its exit grant, by
6271    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` rules (design: dev-hermit
6272    /// ignored/parity-green-sigchld/design-r7.md, design-r8.md).
6273    ///
6274    /// Only an effective SIGCHLD is classified: the child's clone exit signal
6275    /// must be SIGCHLD (a child created with another signal that later execs is
6276    /// left Undecided, conservatively). The receiving task is the creating
6277    /// thread Linux notifies (`wait_owner`); it must still belong to `parent`
6278    /// and be parked at the scheduler on an internal polling probe or a child
6279    /// wait, outside rt_sigsuspend and the temporary-mask syscalls (ppoll,
6280    /// pselect6, epoll_pwait), so its mask is stable and the guest's own. The parent's SIGCHLD disposition comes from
6281    /// /proc (ptrace guests are host processes whose dispositions Detcore
6282    /// passes through unchanged); the mask from the saved guest mask when
6283    /// Detcore holds a private one, else /proc. Anything unreadable is
6284    /// Undecided.
6285    pub(crate) fn classify_child_exit_notification(
6286        &self,
6287        child: DetPid,
6288        parent: DetPid,
6289    ) -> ChildExitNotification {
6290        let Some(wait) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
6291            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6292        };
6293        if self.thread_tree.notification_signal(child) != Some(libc::SIGCHLD) {
6294            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6295        }
6296        let receiving = wait.wait_owner;
6297        if self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&receiving) != Some(&parent) {
6298            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6299        }
6300        // Only the states the design covers (design-r8.md section 2): an
6301        // internal polling probe or a child wait, outside the temporary-mask
6302        // syscalls. Every other request (rt_sigsuspend, a signal in flight,
6303        // futexes, sleeps, external operations) and an unparked task stay
6304        // Undecided, with the synthetic SIGCHLD path as before.
6305        let covered = !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&receiving)
6306            && self
6307                .next_turns
6308                .get(&receiving)
6309                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
6310                .and_then(Result::ok)
6311                .is_some_and(|request| {
6312                    !request.resources.is_empty()
6313                        && request.resources.keys().all(|resource| {
6314                            matches!(
6315                                resource,
6316                                ResourceID::InternalIOPolling | ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }
6317                            )
6318                        })
6319                        && !matches!(request.fyi.as_str(), "ppoll" | "pselect6" | "epoll_pwait")
6320                });
6321        if !covered {
6322            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6323        }
6324        let Some(ignored) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigIgn") else {
6325            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6326        };
6327        let Some(caught) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigCgt") else {
6328            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
6329        };
6330        let blocked = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&receiving) {
6331            Some(mask) => *mask,
6332            None => match self.signal_mask_field(parent, Some(receiving), "SigBlk") {
6333                Some(mask) => mask,
6334                None => return ChildExitNotification::Undecided,
6335            },
6336        };
6337        let bit = 1_u64 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
6338        classify_sigchld_notification(ignored & bit != 0, caught & bit != 0, blocked & bit != 0)
6339    }
6340
6341    /// A /proc signal-mask field of a guest process or thread (the test-only
6342    /// table under `cfg(test)`).
6343    fn signal_mask_field(
6344        &self,
6345        pid: DetPid,
6346        tid: Option<DetTid>,
6347        field: &'static str,
6348    ) -> Option<u64> {
6349        #[cfg(test)]
6350        {
6351            self.test_signal_masks.get(&(pid, tid, field)).copied()
6352        }
6353        #[cfg(not(test))]
6354        {
6355            proc_status_signal_mask(pid, tid, field)
6356        }
6357    }

6359    pub(crate) fn complete_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6360        let removed = self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
6361        if removed {
6362            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
6363            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(detpid);
6364        } else if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
6365            // A completion that arrives before any grant (or after a death
6366            // without one) is kept, so a later begin is a no-op.
6367            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
6368        }
6369        removed
6370    }
6371
6372    /// The processes held between their exit grant and their physical exit,
6373    /// when exits complete asynchronously; otherwise none.
6374    pub(crate) fn pending_async_process_exits(&self) -> Vec<DetPid> {
6375        if !self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
6376            return Vec::new();
6377        }
6378        self.pending_physical_process_exits
6379            .iter()
6380            .copied()
6381            .collect()
6382    }
6383
6384    /// Whether the backend has reported `detpid` physically gone.
6385    pub(crate) fn process_physically_gone(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6386        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
6387    }
6388
6389    /// Begin the asynchronous-exit barrier for `process` at its Exit grant.
6390    /// The hold in `step2_drain_prefix` selects no further turn while any exit
6391    /// is pending, so a second grant cannot happen first: at most one process
6392    /// is ever pending.
6393    fn begin_exit_at_grant(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
6394        assert!(
6395            self.pending_physical_process_exits
6396                .iter()
6397                .all(|pending| *pending == process),
6398            "asynchronous exit completion: process {process} was granted an exit while {:?} is \
6399             still pending; the hold must allow at most one",
6400            self.pending_physical_process_exits
6401        );
6402        if self.begin_physical_process_exit(process) {
6403            trace!(
6404                "[detcore, dpid {}] holding turn selection until the exit completes",
6405                process
6406            );
6407        }
6408    }
6409
6410    /// Retire, at its completion, every registration of `detpid` that the
6411    /// process did not deregister itself: it died without finishing its exit
6412    /// hook (without an Exit grant, or between its grant and its
6413    /// `DeregisterThread`), at a moment the host chose. Returns whether anything
6414    /// was consumed; the caller then records determinism loss.
6415    ///
6416    /// A dead vfork parent's barrier is cancelled (by `logically_kill_thread`)
6417    /// so no other turn stays excluded. If its child has not registered yet, a
6418    /// tombstone lets the child's outstanding registration settle without the
6419    /// barrier.
6420    pub(crate) fn consume_unreported_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6421        // An admitted process can die before its parent's fork turn, or its
6422        // own startup, registers it. Then it has nothing to consume; the
6423        // completion still records it physically gone, so its registration
6424        // is refused when it arrives.
6425        if !self.thread_tree.contains(&detpid) {
6426            return false;
6427        }
6428        let unreported: Vec<DetTid> = self
6429            .thread_tree
6430            .my_thread_group(&detpid)
6431            .into_iter()
6432            .filter(|tid| {
6433                self.next_turns.contains_key(tid) && !self.deregistration_accounted.contains(tid)
6434            })
6435            .collect();
6436        for tid in &unreported {
6437            // A late DeregisterThread from the same incarnation, if one was
6438            // still in flight, is then acknowledged as already accounted.
6439            self.deregistration_accounted.insert(*tid);
6440            let mm = self
6441                .physical_thread_pidfds
6442                .get(tid)
6443                .map(|(mm, ..)| *mm)
6444                .unwrap_or(MmId::initial(*tid));
6445            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &detpid, mm);
6446        }
6447        !unreported.is_empty()
6448    }
6449
6450    pub(crate) fn has_unreported_exit(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
6451        self.thread_tree.contains(&detpid)
6452            && self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid).iter().any(|tid| {
6453                self.next_turns.contains_key(tid) && !self.deregistration_accounted.contains(tid)
6454            })
6455    }
6456
6457    /// Release every physical-exit barrier after the backend supervisor has drained all tracees.
6458    pub(crate) fn release_all_physical_process_exits(&mut self) -> usize {
6459        // Nothing can report a publication once every tracee is drained.
6460        self.child_exit_publications_pending.clear();
6461        self.child_exit_publications_completed.clear();
6462        let children = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_physical_process_exits);
6463        let released = children.len();
6464        for child in children {
6465            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(child);
6466            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(child);
6467        }
6468        released
6469    }
6470
6471    /// Remove entries from everywhere that non-runnable threads lurk.
6472    fn remove_blocking_entries(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid) {
6473        self.deadline_hints.remove(dtid);
6474        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(*dtid);
6475        let _ = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(dtid);
6476        self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(dtid);
6477        let _ = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(dtid);
6478        let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(dtid);
6479        let _ = self.background_entry_barriers.remove(dtid);
6480        self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(dtid);
6481        self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.remove(dtid);
6482        self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(dtid);
6483        self.blocked.woken_sleeps.remove(dtid);
6484        self.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.remove(dtid);
6485        self.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.remove(dtid);
6486        self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(dtid);
6487        let _ = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(dtid);
6488        self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(dtid);
6489        self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(dtid);
6490        self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
6491            waiters.remove(dtid);
6492            !waiters.is_empty()
6493        });
6494        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(dtid);
6495        self.parked.exits_awaiting_permit.remove(dtid);
6496        self.chaos_passed_over.remove(dtid);
6497        self.forget_poll_deadline(*dtid);
6498        let _ = self.remove_futex_waiter(dtid);
6499        // A killed thread must not keep the scheduler loop alive as a parked
6500        // happens-before thread. (`force_unblock_thread_at` never reaches here
6501        // for a parked thread: it leaves a held thread held.)
6502        if let Some(hb) = self.happens_before.as_mut() {
6503            hb.parked.remove(dtid);
6504            hb.held_at.remove(dtid);
6505            hb.holds.remove(dtid);
6506        }
6507    }
6508
6509    fn remove_futex_waiter(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid) -> bool {
6510        let mut removed = 0;
6511        self.blocked.futex_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
6512            let before = waiters.len();
6513            waiters.retain(|waiter| &waiter.dettid != dettid);
6514            removed += before - waiters.len();
6515            !waiters.is_empty()
6516        });
6517        assert!(removed <= 1, "thread was registered on multiple futexes");
6518        removed == 1
6519    }
6520
6521    /// Put a Futex waiter to sleep, to be awoken by `wake_futex_waiter`.
6522    pub fn sleep_futex_waiter(
6523        &mut self,
6524        dettid: &DetTid,
6525        futexid: FutexID,
6526        maybe_timeout: Option<LogicalTime>,
6527        bitset: u32,
6528        signal_watch: Option<FutexSignalWatch>,
6529    ) {
6530        let nxt = self
6531            .next_turns
6532            .get(dettid)
6533            .expect("Missing next_turns entry");
6534        let entry: &mut Vec<_> = self.blocked.futex_waiters.entry(futexid).or_default();
6535        entry.push(FutexWaiter {
6536            dettid: *dettid,
6537            response: nxt.resp.clone(),
6538            bitset,
6539            signal_watch,
6540        });
6541        // When we park, we use a resource request to signal WHAT we're blocking on.  But this is
6542        // not quite the same as when an active thread in the runqueue blocks on a resource, because
6543        // we're not actually waiting on the scheduler giving us the resource.  We're waiting in the
6544        // futex_waiters pool until a waker comes along.
6545        let mut rsrc = Resources::new(*dettid);
6546        rsrc.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
6547        nxt.req.put(Ok(rsrc));
6548        trace!(
6549            "[dtid {}] Waiter blocking on futex {:?}, now {} waiters, on {}",
6550            &dettid,
6551            &futexid,
6552            entry.len(),
6553            nxt.resp,
6554        );
6555        // A futex with timeout waits in both the futex_waiters and timed_events structures:
6556        if let Some(target_time) = maybe_timeout {
6557            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(target_time, *dettid);
6558        }
6559    }
6560
6561    /// Reschedule a single thread that has been blocked on futex.
6562    pub fn wake_futex_waiter(&mut self, waiter: FutexWaiter) {
6563        let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
6564        let waiter_ivar = waiter.response;
6565        debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(waiterid));
6566
6567        // If it was registered as a waiter-with-timeout, remove it:
6568        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
6569
6570        // Put the woken thread back into circulation:
6571        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waiterid);
6572        trace!(
6573            "[detcore] Woke one thread, dtid: {}, ivar {}, scheduled at position {}",
6574            &waiterid, &waiter_ivar, pos,
6575        );
6576        let nxt = self
6577            .next_turns
6578            .get_mut(&waiterid)
6579            .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
6580        assert_futex_request(nxt);
6581        // N.B. We don't write the response here.  That's for the scheduler to do.
6582        // But with a place in the queue, and a request filled, this thread
6583        // is ready to run in normal order.
6584    }
6585
6586    /// Move a waker to the back of its own priority band, under
6587    /// [`Config::yields_after_futex_wake`], so that it is behind the waiters
6588    /// its `FUTEX_WAKE` just queued when they share that band.
6589    ///
6590    /// The waker is the running thread, still in the run queue at the place
6591    /// its last committed turn left it, so ahead of the waiters
6592    /// [`Scheduler::wake_futex_waiter`] has just pushed. A yield request
6593    /// alone would be granted at once, and it would keep running. At the
6594    /// back of its band, its yield waits for the turns of every thread
6595    /// queued there, as at the end of any turn. It keeps its priority: a
6596    /// waiter in a lower-priority band still runs after it. (`--chaos`
6597    /// redraws priorities from the threads' chaos PRNGs, and a random
6598    /// heuristic does not select first in, first out.)
6599    /// The call comes in the waker's own wake request, in its turn, like the
6600    /// waiters' admission. A waker not in the run queue is left alone rather
6601    /// than asserted on: this runs with the scheduler locked, and a panic
6602    /// here would poison the lock.
6603    pub(crate) fn requeue_futex_waker(&mut self, waker: DetTid) {
6604        if !self.run_queue.remove_tid(waker) {
6605            warn!(
6606                "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} is not in the run queue; not requeued",
6607                waker
6608            );
6609            return;
6610        }
6611        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waker);
6612        trace!(
6613            "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} requeued to the back of its priority band at position {}",
6614            waker, pos
6615        );
6616    }
6617
6618    /// `--fuzz-futexes`: a random sample of `num_woken` of the matching waiters.
6619    fn choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(
6620        &mut self,
6621        vec: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>,
6622        num_woken: usize,
6623    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
6624        let rng = &mut self.fuzz_prng;
6625        debug!(
6626            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, pre shuffle: {:?}",
6627            num_woken,
6628            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
6629        );
6630
6631        // No need to actually use the results here since vec was mutated:
6632        let (_extracted, _remain) = &vec[..].partial_shuffle(rng, num_woken);
6633
6634        info!(
6635            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, post shuffle: {:?}",
6636            num_woken,
6637            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
6638        );
6639        // `partial_shuffle` leaves its random sample at the end of the slice.
6640        vec.split_off(vec.len() - num_woken)
6641    }
6642
6643    fn take_futex_wakees(
6644        &mut self,
6645        futexid: FutexID,
6646        max_to_wake: i32,
6647        wake_mask: u32,
6648    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
6649        // Linux's `futex_wake` (kernel/futex/waitwake.c) counts a matching waiter
6650        // before it compares the count, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`, and
6651        // `nr_wake` is the kernel's `int`. So a count of 0, or a `u32` count above
6652        // INT_MAX that is negative as an `int`, wakes one waiter, like a count of 1.
6653        // (Only futex2's FLAGS_STRICT returns early for a zero count, and futex2 is
6654        // refused before it reaches here.) FUTEX_WAKE_OP's two wakes share this
6655        // rule; FUTEX_REQUEUE's does not (0 wakes nobody), so
6656        // `requeue_futex_waiters` must never route its counts through here.
6657        let max_to_wake: usize = if max_to_wake <= 0 {
6658            1
6659        } else {
6660            max_to_wake as usize
6661        };
6662        let mut vec: Vec<FutexWaiter> = {
6663            match self.blocked.futex_waiters.get_mut(&futexid) {
6664                None => {
6665                    trace!(
6666                        "[detcore] Futex wake {} waiters FIZZLED -- none waiting",
6667                        max_to_wake
6668                    );
6669                    return Vec::new();
6670                }
6671                Some(r) => std::mem::take(r),
6672            }
6673        };
6674        trace!(
6675            "Waking up to {} Futex waiters, out of {} waiting.",
6676            max_to_wake,
6677            vec.len(),
6678        );
6679        let to_wake = if self.fuzz_futexes {
6680            let mut matching = take_matching_futex_waiters(&mut vec, wake_mask);
6681            let num_woken = std::cmp::min(matching.len(), max_to_wake);
6682            let to_wake = self.choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(&mut matching, num_woken);
6683            assert_eq!(to_wake.len(), num_woken);
6684            vec.extend(matching);
6685            to_wake
6686        } else {
6687            // Wake the longest waiters whose bitset matches first, as Linux does
6688            // for waiters of equal priority, and keep every other waiter in the
6689            // order it arrived: waiters are appended as their waits are committed,
6690            // so the list is in arrival order.
6691            let mut to_wake = Vec::new();
6692            let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(vec.len());
6693            for waiter in vec.drain(..) {
6694                if to_wake.len() < max_to_wake && waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0 {
6695                    to_wake.push(waiter);
6696                } else {
6697                    kept.push(waiter);
6698                }
6699            }
6700            vec = kept;
6701            to_wake
6702        };
6703        // Put back what wasn't woken up:
6704        if !vec.is_empty() {
6705            let junk = self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(futexid, vec);
6706            assert!(junk.unwrap().is_empty());
6707        }
6708        to_wake
6709    }
6710
6711    /// Reschedule all threads blocked on a particular futex.
6712    pub fn wake_futex_waiters(
6713        &mut self,
6714        _waker_dettid: DetTid,
6715        futexid: FutexID,
6716        max_to_wake: i32,
6717        wake_mask: u32,
6718    ) -> u64 {
6719        let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(futexid, max_to_wake, wake_mask);
6720        let num_woken = to_wake.len();
6721        for waiter in to_wake {
6722            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
6723        }
6724        num_woken as u64
6725    }
6726
6727    /// `FUTEX_REQUEUE` and `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE` on plain (non-PI) futexes, as
6728    /// Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) does them: walk the
6729    /// waiters of `from` in arrival order, stopping once
6730    /// `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`; wake the first `nr_wake`
6731    /// (`if (++task_count <= nr_wake)`) and move the rest onto `to`. Returns the
6732    /// numbers woken and moved; the call returns their sum. Bitsets are ignored,
6733    /// as `futex_requeue` ignores them. Unlike `futex_wake`, a `nr_wake` of 0
6734    /// wakes nobody here.
6735    ///
6736    /// A moved waiter joins the end of `to`'s waiters, in the order the moved
6737    /// waiters arrived, as `requeue_futex` appends it to the target hash chain
6738    /// with `plist_add`, so a later wake of `to` takes `to`'s earlier waiters
6739    /// first. Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody: `requeue_futex` only
6740    /// changes the waiter's key there. (When two different futexes share a Linux
6741    /// hash bucket the moved waiter keeps its place in the shared chain; that
6742    /// order depends on the kernel's hash of the addresses, which no guest can
6743    /// rely on, and Detcore uses the separate-bucket order.)
6744    ///
6745    /// The caller checks `nr_wake` and `nr_requeue` are not negative (`-EINVAL`)
6746    /// and, for `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE`, the futex word against `val3` (`-EAGAIN`).
6747    pub fn requeue_futex_waiters(
6748        &mut self,
6749        from: FutexID,
6750        to: FutexID,
6751        nr_wake: usize,
6752        nr_requeue: usize,
6753    ) -> (u64, u64) {
6754        let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.futex_waiters.remove(&from) else {
6755            return (0, 0);
6756        };
6757        let mut woken = Vec::new();
6758        let mut moved = Vec::new();
6759        let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(waiters.len());
6760        let mut task_count: usize = 0;
6761        for waiter in waiters {
6762            // `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`, in Linux's signed `int`s.
6763            if task_count as i128 - nr_wake as i128 >= nr_requeue as i128 {
6764                kept.push(waiter);
6765                continue;
6766            }
6767            task_count += 1;
6768            if task_count <= nr_wake {
6769                woken.push(waiter);
6770            } else if from == to {
6771                // Requeued onto the same key: it keeps its place.
6772                kept.push(waiter);
6773            } else {
6774                moved.push(waiter);
6775            }
6776        }
6777        let num_moved = (task_count - woken.len()) as u64;
6778        if !kept.is_empty() {
6779            self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(from, kept);
6780        }
6781        if !moved.is_empty() {
6782            self.blocked
6783                .futex_waiters
6784                .entry(to)
6785                .or_default()
6786                .extend(moved);
6787        }
6788        let num_woken = woken.len() as u64;
6789        for waiter in woken {
6790            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
6791        }
6792        trace!(
6793            "[detcore] futex requeue {:?} -> {:?}: woke {}, moved {}",
6794            from, to, num_woken, num_moved
6795        );
6796        (num_woken, num_moved)
6797    }
6798
6799    /// Whether `tid` waits for admission at the next deterministic drain.
6800    #[cfg(test)]
6801    pub(crate) fn admission_pending(&self, tid: DetTid) -> bool {
6802        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&tid)
6803    }

6805    /// Whether turns are held until the kernel has ended `tid`.
6806    #[cfg(test)]
6807    pub(crate) fn holds_turns_until_gone(&self, tid: DetTid) -> bool {
6808        self.exited_thread_barriers.contains_key(&tid)
6809    }

6811    /// Record futex wakes delivered by a physical-exit callback for the next
6812    /// deterministic run-queue drain.
6813    pub(crate) fn wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(
6814        &mut self,
6815        wakes: &[(DetTid, FutexID)],
6816    ) -> Vec<u64> {
6817        wakes
6818            .iter()
6819            .map(|(_owner, futexid)| {
6820                let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(*futexid, 1, u32::MAX);
6821                let num_woken = to_wake.len();
6822                for waiter in to_wake {
6823                    let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
6824                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
6825                    let next_turn = self
6826                        .next_turns
6827                        .get_mut(&waiterid)
6828                        .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
6829                    assert_futex_request(next_turn);
6830                    self.admit_to_run_queue(waiterid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
6831                }
6832                num_woken as u64
6833            })
6834            .collect()
6835    }

6837    /// Simulate the effect of CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID.
6838    pub fn wake_futex_child_cleartid(&mut self, futid: FutexID, dettid: DetTid) {
6839        self.cleared_child_tids.insert(futid, dettid);
6840        debug!(
6841            "simulate CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID on futex {:?}, wake one",
6842            futid
6843        );
6844        // Wakes only one thread, as per:
6845        // https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/set_tid_address.2.html
6846        if self.backend_failed() {
6847            // Failure closed the selection transaction permanently. Account
6848            // cleanup now: the stopped scheduler will never drain admissions,
6849            // and no waiter can receive another grant.
6850            assert!(!self.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
6851            self.wake_futex_waiters(dettid, futid, 1, u32::MAX);
6852        } else {
6853            // A thread's retirement can arrive while a tentative selection is
6854            // open, where a direct run-queue push is illegal. Keep the same
6855            // one-waiter choice, but admit it at the next drain, in DetTid
6856            // order with the admissions already pending
6857            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362, part 2 step 0b).
6858            self.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&[(dettid, futid)]);
6859        }
6860    }

6862    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6863    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review late CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID wait recovery.
6864    /// Whether a futex word still names the child that was logically cleared.
6865    pub(crate) fn child_tid_was_cleared(&self, futid: FutexID, observed: i32) -> bool {
6866        self.cleared_child_tids
6867            .get(&futid)
6868            .is_some_and(|dettid| dettid.as_raw() == observed)
6869    }
