6871    /// Step: Before we select which thread to run, first we check if some internal data
6872    /// structure maintenance is necessary, i.e. moving timed events from the waiting pool
6873    /// to the run queue. It manipulates scheduler data structures accordingly.
6874    fn step2_drain_prefix(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6875        // A terminal verdict recorded outside a turn (a global-request handler
6876        // such as the exec reconnect) ends the run once this turn returns:
6877        // select nothing, so no thread is granted a turn that would race the
6878        // exit.
6879        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
6880            return Err(SkipTurn);
6881        }
6882        self.flush_parent_death_signals();
6883        if self.sigkill_fence_holds() {
6884            // A SIGKILLed process was retired at the kill turn: select no
6885            // turn until its physical exit is accounted and published to its
6886            // parent; host timing decides only how long this lasts
6887            // (`sigkill_retirement`). Nothing is drained meanwhile either, so
6888            // no admission enters the run queue in an order that depends on
6889            // which victim's cleanup came first. Past the valve the run is
6890            // refused instead of hanging.
6891            let since = *self
6892                .sigkill_fence_wait_since
6893                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
6894            if since.elapsed() >= self.sigkill_fence_valve {
6895                self.refuse_unsettled_sigkill(since.elapsed());
6896            }
6897            std::thread::yield_now();
6898            return Err(SkipTurn);
6899        }
6900        self.sigkill_fence_wait_since = None;
6901        // The victims' owner-death wakes, held back until their cohort was
6902        // complete, run before the drains below, in a fixed order.
6903        self.run_retained_sigkill_wakes();
6904        // Apply run-queue mutations deferred by asynchronous global-request
6905        // handlers first, at this fixed deterministic point, before any early
6906        // return below and before step3 opens a tentative-pop window. Removals
6907        // drain before admissions so a thread killed while an admission was
6908        // still buffered is not re-enqueued.
6909        self.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
6910        self.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
6911        self.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
6912        // Re-admit happens-before threads whose gate a source opened in the
6913        // last committed turn, with the other deferred admissions: before
6914        // step2c harvests host-timed I/O continuations (so a ready one cannot
6915        // overtake a thread that is already runnable as far as the guest can
6916        // tell) and before step2d classifies an empty queue (so a source thread
6917        // that blocked right after firing is not reported as a futex deadlock,
6918        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
6919        self.hb_flush_wakes();
6920        self.hb_check_hold_budget()?;
6921        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
6922            && !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
6923        {
6924            // A granted exit has not completed physically yet: the exiting
6925            // process may still hold descriptors a peer would observe. Select
6926            // no turn until the backend reports it gone; the completion's host
6927            // timing decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
6928            std::thread::yield_now();
6929            return Err(SkipTurn);
6930        }
6931        if !self.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty() {
6932            // A child's exit grant left its notification to the kernel (None
6933            // or Discard). Select no turn until the backend reports the kernel
6934            // has published the exit to the parent; the report's host timing
6935            // decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
6936            std::thread::yield_now();
6937            return Err(SkipTurn);
6938        }
6939        if self
6940            .blocked
6941            .physical_child_waiters
6942            .keys()
6943            .any(|child| self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(child))
6944        {
6945            // A reaper has reached the deterministic logical-exit boundary.
6946            // Do not let runnable siblings advance while the backend catches
6947            // up to physical waitability; completion admits the waiter through
6948            // the next deterministic drain.
6949            std::thread::yield_now();
6950            return Err(SkipTurn);
6951        }
6952        self.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier()?;
6953        self.step2a_wait_for_background_entry()?;
6954        self.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders()?;
6955        self.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads()?;
6956        Ok(())
6957    }
6958
6959    /// Waits, committing no turn, until every thread that deregistered after
6960    /// its own `Exit` grant (`exited_thread_barriers`) has exited in the
6961    /// kernel (`ExitedThreadBarrier::settled`). Linux sets a thread's exit
6962    /// state in `exit_notify`, after `exit_mm` has walked the robust list,
6963    /// stored 0 to `clear_child_tid` and woken it, and after `exit_files`, so
6964    /// every sibling turn sees all of that done. When that happens is
6965    /// host-timed; waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler spins,
6966    /// never which turn comes next or what a sibling observes
6967    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4246>).
6968    fn step2a_wait_for_exited_threads(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6969        if self.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty() {
6970            return Ok(());
6971        }
6972        let mut settled = Vec::new();
6973        let mut stuck = None;
6974        for (thread, barrier) in &self.exited_thread_barriers {
6975            let observed = match barrier.settled() {
6976                Ok(()) => {
6977                    settled.push(*thread);
6978                    continue;
6979                }
6980                Err(observed) => observed,
6981            };
6982            if stuck.is_none() && barrier.since.elapsed() >= self.exited_leader_valve {
6983                stuck = Some(format!(
6984                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: thread {thread} deregistered after its exit was granted, \
6985                     and after {:?} the kernel has not ended it: {observed}",
6986                    self.exited_leader_valve
6987                ));
6988            }
6989        }
6990        for thread in settled {
6991            self.exited_thread_barriers.remove(&thread);
6992        }
6993        if let Some(reason) = stuck {
6994            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
6995            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
6996            return Err(SkipTurn);
6997        }
6998        if self.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty() {
6999            Ok(())
7000        } else {
7001            std::thread::yield_now();
7002            Err(SkipTurn)
7003        }
7004    }
7005
7006    /// Waits, committing no turn, until the kernel shows every leader
7007    /// retired at its own exit (`exited_leader_barriers`) a zombie, or dead,
7008    /// or gone. When the kernel finishes the leader's exit is host-timed;
7009    /// waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler spins, never which
7010    /// turn comes next or what a sibling observes
7011    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>).
7012    fn step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7013        if self.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty() {
7014            return Ok(());
7015        }
7016        let mut settled = Vec::new();
7017        let mut stuck = None;
7018        for (leader, since) in &self.exited_leader_barriers {
7019            let observed = match self.read_task_state(*leader) {
7020                Ok('Z' | 'X') => {
7021                    settled.push(*leader);
7022                    continue;
7023                }
7024                Ok(state) => format!("its state is {state}"),
7025                Err(errno) => {
7026                    let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
7027                    if thread_is_gone(pid, pid) {
7028                        settled.push(*leader);
7029                        continue;
7030                    }
7031                    format!("its state cannot be read ({errno}) although it is alive")
7032                }
7033            };
7034            if stuck.is_none() && since.elapsed() >= self.exited_leader_valve {
7035                stuck = Some(format!(
7036                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: thread-group leader {leader} was retired at its own exit, \
7037                     and after {:?} the kernel does not show it a zombie: {observed}",
7038                    self.exited_leader_valve
7039                ));
7040            }
7041        }
7042        for leader in settled {
7043            self.exited_leader_barriers.remove(&leader);
7044        }
7045        if let Some(reason) = stuck {
7046            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
7047            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
7048            return Err(SkipTurn);
7049        }
7050        if self.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty() {
7051            Ok(())
7052        } else {
7053            std::thread::yield_now();
7054            Err(SkipTurn)
7055        }
7056    }
7057
7058    /// The state letter of thread `thread` of its process, from
7059    /// `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` (the field after the command name).
7060    fn read_task_state(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Result<char, Errno> {
7061        #[cfg(test)]
7062        if let Some(state) = self.test_task_states.get(&thread) {
7063            return Ok(*state);
7064        }
7065        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
7066        let stat = std::fs::read(format!(
7067            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
7068            process.as_raw(),
7069            thread.as_raw()
7070        ))
7071        .map_err(|error| Errno::new(error.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(libc::EIO)))?;
7072        task_state_of_stat(&stat).ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
7073    }
7074
7075    /// Waits, committing no turn, until every thread released into a
7076    /// background call with a temporary mask (`background_entry_barriers`) has
7077    /// entered it, which its kernel mask shows, or has left it: its
7078    /// continuation is posted, or it is gone. When the kernel installed the
7079    /// mask is host-timed; waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler
7080    /// spins, never which turn comes next or which thread a later signal can
7081    /// reach (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3993).
7082    fn step2a_wait_for_background_entry(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7083        if self.background_entry_barriers.is_empty() {
7084            return Ok(());
7085        }
7086        let settled: Vec<DetTid> =
7087            self.background_entry_barriers
7088                .iter()
7089                .filter(|(thread, _)| {
7090                    let left = match self
7091                        .next_turns
7092                        .get(thread)
7093                        .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
7094                    {
7095                        Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => true,
7096                        Some(Ok(resources)) => resources.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
7097                            matches!(resource, ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_))
7098                        }),
7099                        _ => false,
7100                    };
7101                    left || !(self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(thread)
7102                        || self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(thread))
7103                })
7104                .map(|(thread, _)| *thread)
7105                .collect();
7106        for thread in settled {
7107            self.background_entry_barriers.remove(&thread);
7108        }
7109        // Otherwise the kernel's mask decides. A failed read proves nothing
7110        // about entry: only a thread confirmed gone releases its entry then
7111        // (Codex review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
7112        let mut entered = Vec::new();
7113        let mut unproved = None;
7114        for (thread, entry) in &self.background_entry_barriers {
7115            let observed = match self.read_thread_blocked_mask_result(*thread) {
7116                Ok(blocked) if blocked == entry.mask => {
7117                    entered.push(*thread);
7118                    continue;
7119                }
7120                Ok(blocked) => format!("its mask is {blocked:#x}"),
7121                Err(errno) => {
7122                    let process = self.sigchld_process(*thread);
7123                    if thread_is_gone(
7124                        reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
7125                        reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
7126                    ) {
7127                        entered.push(*thread);
7128                        continue;
7129                    }
7130                    format!("its mask cannot be read ({errno}) although it is alive")
7131                }
7132            };
7133            if unproved.is_none() && entry.since.elapsed() >= self.background_entry_valve {
7134                unproved = Some(format!(
7135                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: dettid {thread} was released into a background call \
7136                     that sleeps under mask {:#x}, and after {:?} it has neither entered it \
7137                     nor left it: {observed}",
7138                    entry.mask, self.background_entry_valve
7139                ));
7140            }
7141        }
7142        for thread in entered {
7143            self.background_entry_barriers.remove(&thread);
7144        }
7145        if let Some(reason) = unproved {
7146            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
7147            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
7148            return Err(SkipTurn);
7149        }
7150        if self.background_entry_barriers.is_empty() {
7151            Ok(())
7152        } else {
7153            std::thread::yield_now();
7154            Err(SkipTurn)
7155        }
7156    }
7157
7158    fn step2_process_blocked(
7159        &mut self,
7160        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
7161    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7162        // Before anything can return or pop a timer (`sigalrm`).
7163        self.step2_sigalrm_ledger();
7164        self.step2_release_signaled_background()?;
7165        self.step2_drain_prefix()?;
7166        // A signal the drain placed that armed a background thread ends the
7167        // pass before any timer pops: the release barrier requeues that thread
7168        // at the top of the next one. A `ChildExit` target is then chosen with
7169        // it no longer asleep, as the kernel would, which skips a sleeper that
7170        // already has a signal pending (`kernel_sigchld_target`); otherwise
7171        // the timer could name it while the kernel woke another sleeper that
7172        // nothing armed.
7173        if !self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty() {
7174            return Err(SkipTurn);
7175        }
7176        // Replay waits for a readmission due now before anything that changes
7177        // the schedule, so the pass that readmits does what record's did.
7178        if self.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
7179            return Err(SkipTurn);
7180        }
7181        if std::mem::take(&mut self.fast_forward_for_alone_poller) {
7182            self.fast_forward_to_next_finite_deadline(global_time);
7183        }
7184        self.step2b_process_timed(global_time);
7185        self.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
7186        // A timed signal that just armed a background thread is followed by an
7187        // empty pass, so the barrier above requeues it at the top of the next
7188        // one whether or not its continuation is already posted.
7189        if self.backend_failed()
7190            || self.control_barrier()
7191            || !self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty()
7192        {
7193            return Err(SkipTurn);
7194        }
7195        self.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
7196        self.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
7197        self.step2d_handle_empty_queue(global_time)
7198    }
7199
7200    /// Move global time to the earliest finite timed deadline, if it lies
7201    /// ahead, so that `step2b_process_timed` fires it once committed time
7202    /// catches up (the next pass, after step 1 updates committed time). Requested by a
7203    /// FIFO open's poll when nothing else can run but such a timer
7204    /// (`fast_forward_for_alone_poller`): as when the run queue is empty
7205    /// (`step2d_decide_empty_queue`), no thread could otherwise act before it.
7206    fn fast_forward_to_next_finite_deadline(&mut self, global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) {
7207        let Some(deadline) = self.blocked.timed_waiters.next_deadline() else {
7208            return;
7209        };
7210        if deadline.is_indefinite() {
7211            return;
7212        }
7213        let mut gt = global_time.lock().unwrap();
7214        let now = gt.as_nanos();
7215        if deadline > now {
7216            info!(
7217                "[scheduler] Nothing but a FIFO open's poll can run; skipping global time ahead to {}.",
7218                deadline
7219            );
7220            gt.add_extra_time(deadline.duration_since(now));
7221        }
7222    }
7223
7224    /// How long the release barrier waits for an armed thread's continuation
7225    /// before it refuses the run (see `step2_release_signaled_background`).
7226    const SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
7227
7228    /// How long step2a skips turns for a vfork barrier that waits for a
7229    /// backend event before it refuses the run (see
7230    /// `step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`). The same bound as the release
7231    /// barrier's.
7232    const VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
7233
7234    /// How long, in host time, the SIGKILL fence and a sender's `kill` wait
7235    /// for the victims' deaths and exit publications before the run is
7236    /// refused. Like `VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE`, it bounds the wait without ever
7237    /// deciding a turn: host timing decides only how long a pause lasts.
7238    pub(crate) const SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
7239
7240    /// How long, in host time, an empty run queue waits for Linux's kill of
7241    /// the processes of an ended PID namespace to be reported
7242    /// (`report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending`) before the run is
7243    /// stopped by name. A backend that never reports such a death (an
7244    /// in-guest tool that a SIGKILL gives no exit hook) would otherwise wait
7245    /// forever. Like the other valves, it decides no turn.
7246    pub(crate) const NAMESPACE_ZAP_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
7247
7248    /// Requeue, at a fixed point, the background-pool threads that a committed
7249    /// signal armed (`BlockedPool::signaled_background`, set by
7250    /// `arm_signaled_background`).
7251    ///
7252    /// This runs first in every scheduler pass: before the drain prefix, any
7253    /// timer pop, and any selection. While an armed thread is still in its pool
7254    /// with no posted request, the kernel is still delivering its signal, and
7255    /// the pass does nothing else: it returns `SkipTurn`. Once every armed
7256    /// thread has posted its continuation (or left its pool, or exited), all of
7257    /// them are requeued in `DetTid` order exactly as
7258    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers` requeues a ready backgrounded call. No
7259    /// guest turn and no other scheduler event can commit between the signal
7260    /// and the requeue, so host delivery time decides only how many empty
7261    /// passes spin, never where the threads enter the run queue.
7262    ///
7263    /// The watchdog (`SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE`) only bounds how long the
7264    /// barrier waits; it never decides an admission. An armed thread is woken
7265    /// because its recorded mask does not block the signal and a traced thread
7266    /// is never spared a signal at generation, so it always stops and posts. If
7267    /// that ever fails to happen before the watchdog fires, the barrier keeps
7268    /// every arm, records a `SignaledBackgroundRefusal`, and the scheduler loop
7269    /// ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`. Dropping the arms instead
7270    /// would leave the threads for `step2c` to harvest behind runnable siblings:
7271    /// an admission order that host delivery time decides.
7272    fn step2_release_signaled_background(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7273        if self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty() {
7274            self.signaled_background_since = None;
7275            return Ok(());
7276        }
7277        let armed: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.signaled_background.iter().copied().collect();
7278        let mut unposted = Vec::new();
7279        for dtid in armed {
7280            let in_pool = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
7281                || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid);
7282            match self.next_turns.get(&dtid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read()) {
7283                Some(Some(Ok(_))) if in_pool => {}
7284                Some(None) if in_pool => unposted.push(dtid),
7285                // Left its pool, exited, or unregistered: nothing to order.
7286                _ => {
7287                    self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(&dtid);
7288                }
7289            }
7290        }
7291        if !unposted.is_empty() {
7292            let since = *self
7293                .signaled_background_since
7294                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
7295            let waited = since.elapsed();
7296            if waited < Self::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE {
7297                trace!(
7298                    "[step2] waiting for signaled background dtids {:?} to post their continuations",
7299                    unposted
7300                );
7301                std::thread::yield_now();
7302                return Err(SkipTurn);
7303            }
7304            // Fail closed: keep every arm, so nothing is admitted at a
7305            // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
7306            if self.signaled_background_refusal.is_none() {
7307                let refusal = SignaledBackgroundRefusal { unposted, waited };
7308                tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
7309                self.signaled_background_refusal = Some(refusal);
7310            }
7311            return Err(SkipTurn);
7312        }
7313        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.signaled_background);
7314        self.signaled_background_since = None;
7315        for dtid in ready {
7316            info!(
7317                "[step2] Reschedule signaled background dtid {:?} at its fixed point",
7318                dtid
7319            );
7320            let external = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&dtid);
7321            self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(&dtid);
7322            let sigsuspend = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&dtid);
7323            let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(&dtid);
7324            assert!(
7325                external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
7326                "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
7327            );
7328            self.readmit_ready_thread(dtid);
7329        }
7330        Ok(())
7331    }
7332
7333    /// Re-admit parents whose host-async `SIGCHLD` was parked in
7334    /// `blocked.sigchld_deferred` (see `block_for_one_resource`). Uses the same
7335    /// deterministic-work-first gate as `step2c_process_io_blockers`: a deferred
7336    /// signal is delivered only once the run queue holds no ordinary (non-poller)
7337    /// guest work, so its commit order is fixed by the scheduler rather than by
7338    /// host signal-arrival timing. Runs after external-IO harvesting so a ready
7339    /// IO continuation is always ordered ahead of a deferred signal.
7340    fn step2e_process_signal_deferred(&mut self) {
7341        if self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty() {
7342            return;
7343        }
7344        let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
7345        if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
7346            return;
7347        }
7348        // BTreeSet drains in sorted DetTid order, giving a canonical admission
7349        // order when several parents are owed a signal at the same quiescence.
7350        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.sigchld_deferred);
7351        for dtid in ready {
7352            info!("[step2] Re-admit deferred SIGCHLD for dtid {:?}", dtid);
7353            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dtid);
7354            self.readmit_ready_thread(dtid);
7355        }
7356    }
7357
7358    /// Keep scheduling inside an active vfork until the parent can continue.
7359    /// Before child registration no guest may run; afterward step 3 selects the
7360    /// child first (see [`Self::step3_peek`]). A failed clone reaches the parent
7361    /// continuation without a child.
7362    ///
7363    /// On the ptrace backend the kernel keeps the vfork parent blocked inside the injected
7364    /// `clone(2)` until the child execs or exits, so a registered child (barrier `Some`) is always
7365    /// present by the time the parent posts its continuation; an unfulfilled barrier (`None`) at
7366    /// that point therefore means the clone failed and the barrier must be dropped. On a backend
7367    /// that defers the child spawn (see `defers_vfork_child_registration`, e.g. KVM) the
7368    /// child registers only *after* the parent posts its continuation, so an unfulfilled barrier at
7369    /// parent continuation means the child is still on its way and the barrier must be kept.
7370    ///
7371    /// Two states make every pass skip its turn until a backend event arrives:
7372    /// a `Pending` barrier waits for its child's registration, and a
7373    /// `Released` one for its parent's continuation or retirement. No turn
7374    /// commits meanwhile, so the event's host timing decides only how many
7375    /// passes skip, never which turn is next. Each skip yields the scheduler
7376    /// thread, as the other step2 prefix skips do. The valve
7377    /// (`VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE`) bounds the wait without ever deciding a
7378    /// selection: if the event has not arrived when it expires, every barrier
7379    /// is kept, a `VforkBarrierRefusal` names the waiting barriers, and
7380    /// `sched_loop_inner` ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`
7381    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>). Dropping the
7382    /// barriers instead would let other threads be selected at a moment the
7383    /// host chose.
7384    fn step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
7385        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
7386        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review deferred vfork child registration.
7387        let defers_registration = self.backend.defers_vfork_child_registration;
7388        let completed_parents: Vec<_> = self
7389            .vfork_barriers
7390            .iter()
7391            .filter_map(|(parent, registered_child)| {
7392                let child_registered = registered_child.is_some();
7393                let remove = match self
7394                    .next_turns
7395                    .get(parent)
7396                    .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
7397                {
7398                    // The parent exited: there will be no child; drop the barrier.
7399                    Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => true,
7400                    Some(Ok(resources)) => {
7401                        let vfork_failed = resources
7402                            .resources
7403                            .keys()
7404                            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::VforkFailed(_)));
7405                        let at_continue = resources.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
7406                            matches!(resource, ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_))
7407                        });
7408                        // A failed injected clone is an explicit deterministic outcome: no child
7409                        // can ever register, so cancel the barrier on every backend. Successful
7410                        // deferred spawns retain the ordinary continuation and keep waiting.
7411                        // At parent continuation, drop a fulfilled barrier as normal cleanup. An
7412                        // unfulfilled barrier is a failed clone only when the backend kept the
7413                        // parent blocked until the child registered; when the backend defers child
7414                        // registration the child is still coming, so keep waiting.
7415                        vfork_failed || (at_continue && (child_registered || !defers_registration))
7416                    }
7417                    _ => false,
7418                };
7419                remove.then_some(*parent)
7420            })
7421            .collect();
7422        for parent in completed_parents {
7423            self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
7424        }
7425
7426        // A pending barrier waits for its child's registration, a released one
7427        // for its parent's continuation or retirement; no turn commits
7428        // meanwhile, so when that host-timed event arrives cannot change the
7429        // schedule. A registered, unreleased barrier does not wait: step 3
7430        // admits its child.
7431        let waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait> = self
7432            .vfork_barriers
7433            .iter()
7434            .filter_map(|(parent, child)| {
7435                let state = if child.is_none() {
7436                    VforkBarrierState::Pending
7437                } else if self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(parent) {
7438                    VforkBarrierState::Released
7439                } else {
7440                    return None;
7441                };
7442                Some(VforkBarrierWait {
7443                    parent: *parent,
7444                    child: *child,
7445                    state,
7446                })
7447            })
7448            .collect();
7449        if waits.is_empty() {
7450            self.vfork_barrier_wait_since = None;
7451            return Ok(());
7452        }
7453        let since = *self
7454            .vfork_barrier_wait_since
7455            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
7456        let waited = since.elapsed();
7457        if waited < Self::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE {
7458            trace!("[step2a] waiting on vfork barriers {:?}", waits);
7459            std::thread::yield_now();
7460            return Err(SkipTurn);
7461        }
7462        // Fail closed: keep every barrier, so no other thread is selected at a
7463        // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
7464        if self.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none() {
7465            let refusal = VforkBarrierRefusal { waits, waited };
7466            tracing::error!("[step2a] {}", refusal);
7467            self.vfork_barrier_refusal = Some(refusal);
7468        }
7469        Err(SkipTurn)
7470    }
7471
7472    /// Record the timeout deadline of a poller that `step4_resource_block` just
7473    /// requeued backed off, replacing any earlier entry of the thread. Nothing
7474    /// is recorded under record/replay, whose schedule must not change, or
7475    /// under a heuristic that does not select in priority order (there a
7476    /// backed-off poller is never starved, and re-keying it would only remap
7477    /// seeds) (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
7478    fn note_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
7479        self.forget_poll_deadline(dettid);
7480        let Some(deadline) = rs.poll_deadline else {
7481            return;
7482        };
7483        if self.recordreplay_modes || !self.run_queue.is_priority_ordered() {
7484            return;
7485        }
7486        self.poll_deadlines.insert((deadline, dettid));
7487        self.poll_deadline_of.insert(dettid, deadline);
7488    }
7489
7490    fn forget_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
7491        if let Some(deadline) = self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid) {
7492            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
7493        }
7494    }
7495
7496    /// Restore the normal priority of every backed-off poller whose timeout
7497    /// deadline committed time has reached, so its next retry runs at the next
7498    /// selection and returns the timeout instead of waiting up to
7499    /// `POLLING_UPGRADE_INTERVAL` pushes for a poll upgrade
7500    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
7501    ///
7502    /// Each due entry resolves one of four ways:
7503    /// 1. the thread is gone, or its pending request no longer carries this
7504    ///    deadline (it ran, finished the call, or started another one): drop;
7505    /// 2. it is queued backed off: restore its priority, then drop;
7506    /// 3. it is queued but no longer backed off (`do_poll_upgrade`, or a
7507    ///    replayed priority change, restored it already): drop;
7508    /// 4. its request still carries the deadline but it is out of the run
7509    ///    queue: keep, so a later pass restores it once it is back. This is
7510    ///    defensive: the only suspension of a queued entry,
7511    ///    `take_validated_membership` for a parked alarm observation, accepts
7512    ///    no request that carries a poll deadline today.
7513    ///
7514    /// Deterministic: it reads only the deadlines threads computed in their own
7515    /// turns, `committed_time`, the run queue and the pending requests. It is
7516    /// idempotent for a given `committed_time` and monotone in it, so how many
7517    /// passes run between commits does not change its result; it is the same
7518    /// exposure `step2b_process_timed` already has to `committed_time`. A
7519    /// restore moves the entry to the back of its normal priority level: it
7520    /// takes a new back turn and counts toward the poll-upgrade interval
7521    /// (`RunQueue::restore_poller_priority`), so a poll upgrade can fire in the
7522    /// middle of this loop. Both are deterministic. It never admits or removes
7523    /// a thread.
7524    fn step2b_restore_due_pollers(&mut self) {
7525        let due: Vec<(LogicalTime, DetTid)> = self
7526            .poll_deadlines
7527            .iter()
7528            .take_while(|(deadline, _)| *deadline <= self.committed_time)
7529            .copied()
7530            .collect();
7531        for (deadline, dettid) in due {
7532            let still_waiting = self
7533                .next_turns
7534                .get(&dettid)
7535                .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
7536                .is_some_and(
7537                    |request| matches!(request, Ok(rs) if rs.poll_deadline == Some(deadline)),
7538                );
7539            if still_waiting {
7540                match self.run_queue.restore_poller_priority(dettid) {
7541                    PollerRestore::Restored => {
7542                        info!(
7543                            "[scheduler] dettid {} restored to its normal priority: its poll \
7544                             deadline {} has passed (committed time {})",
7545                            dettid, deadline, self.committed_time
7546                        );
7547                    }
7548                    PollerRestore::NotBackedOff => {}
7549                    PollerRestore::NotQueued => continue,
7550                }
7551            }
7552            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
7553            self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid);
7554        }
7555    }
7556
7557    /// Check whether it is time for the *earliest* time-based event to execute INSTEAD of
7558    /// dispatching from the normal run queue.  Manipulates scheduler data structures
7559    /// accordingly.
7560    /// Return whether an event was actually consumed, so a control refresh
7561    /// can distinguish an empty check from a spent maintenance budget.
7562    fn step2b_process_timed(&mut self, global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) -> bool {
7563        if let Some((time_ns, evt)) = self
7564            .blocked
7565            .timed_waiters
7566            .pop_if_before(self.committed_time)
7567        {
7568            match evt {
7569                TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(tid) => self.wake_timed_event(time_ns, tid),
7570                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, tid, sig) => {
7571                    let observed_now = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
7572                    self.dispatch_timed_signal(time_ns, id, tid, sig, true, observed_now)
7573                }
7574            }
7575            true
7576        } else {
7577            false
7578        }
7579    }

7581    /// Publish the actual ITIMER_REAL expiry through the common signal path.
7582    fn fire_itimer_real_copy(&mut self, process: DetPid, thread: DetTid, signal: Signal) -> bool {
7583        debug_assert_eq!(signal, Signal::SIGALRM);
7584        self.fire_process_alarm(
7585            process,
7586            thread,
7587            signal,
7588            None,
7589            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(Some(
7590                discarded_at_send::SignalProducer::ItimerReal,
7591            )),
7592        )
7593    }

7595    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
7596    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
7597    fn fire_alarm(&mut self, dpid: DetPid, dtid: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
7598        self.fire_alarm_with(dpid, dtid, sig, None);
7599    }
7600
7601    /// [`Self::fire_alarm`], sending the raw siginfo `info` when there is one
7602    /// (it must carry a negative `si_code`, as Linux requires of a sender's).
7603    /// Returns whether a signal was sent to a guest thread.
7604    fn fire_alarm_with(
7605        &mut self,
7606        dpid: DetPid,
7607        dtid: DetTid,
7608        sig: Signal,
7609        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
7610    ) -> bool {
7611        self.fire_process_alarm(
7612            dpid,
7613            dtid,
7614            sig,
7615            info,
7616            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(None),
7617        )
7618    }
7619
7620    /// The one body of every scheduler send of a process-directed timer
7621    /// signal (`fire_alarm_with`, `fire_process_timer`), so that both
7622    /// keep the shared-queue record (`note_signal_left_in_shared_queue`): a
7623    /// `SIGEV_SIGNAL` timer that once copied this body without it left a
7624    /// later `sigsuspend` unarmed behind a spinner (the Claude re-check of
7625    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4351, N1). `fate` says how
7626    /// the discarded-at-send record classifies it (`SendFate`).
7627    fn fire_process_alarm(
7628        &mut self,
7629        dpid: DetPid,
7630        dtid: DetTid,
7631        sig: Signal,
7632        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
7633        fate: discarded_at_send::SendFate,
7634    ) -> bool {
7635        // A guest-handled SIGALRM goes to the process's ledger, not the kernel.
7636        if self.divert_sigalrm(dpid, sig) {
7637            return false;
7638        }
7639        #[cfg(test)]
7640        {
7641            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
7642        }
7643        let target = self
7644            .select_signal_target(dpid, Some(dtid))
7645            .map(|preferred| self.timer_signal_target(dpid, preferred, sig));
7646        // Decided before the send, whose wake may change pools and masks.
7647        let every_thread_blocks = self.models_signal_targets
7648            && target.is_some_and(|target| {
7649                self.kernel_signal_target(dpid, target, sig as libc::c_int)
7650                    .is_none()
7651            });
7652        // Linux classifies the send against the leader, whatever thread
7653        // takes it: `it_real_fn` sends to the leader's pid, and a
7654        // `SIGEV_SIGNAL` timer to the leader (`posixtimer_get_target`).
7655        let sent = self.fire_alarm_at(dpid, target, sig, info, dpid, fate);
7656        if sent && every_thread_blocks {
7657            self.note_signal_left_in_shared_queue(dpid, sig as libc::c_int);
7658        }
7659        sent
7660    }
7661
7662    /// Record that the scheduler sent `process` the signal `signo` while
7663    /// every thread blocked it (`shared_queue_scheduler_signals`). Linux then
7664    /// keeps it in the process's shared queue, and the first thread to
7665    /// unblock it takes it.
7666    fn note_signal_left_in_shared_queue(&mut self, process: DetPid, signo: libc::c_int) {
7667        *self
7668            .shared_queue_scheduler_signals
7669            .entry(process)
7670            .or_default() |= kernel_signal_bit(signo);
7671    }
7672
7673    /// At the grant of a call outside the schedule whose sleeping mask is
7674    /// `mask`: if a signal the scheduler left in the process's shared queue
7675    /// (`shared_queue_scheduler_signals`) is still there, is one the mask
7676    /// admits and the process catches, and no `rt_sigtimedwait` set or
7677    /// signalfd could take it first, the call is ended by it as soon as it
7678    /// begins. Arm the thread so that the release barrier readmits it at a
7679    /// fixed point (`arm_signaled_background`), as when the signal is sent
7680    /// while the thread already sleeps.
7681    ///
7682    /// The record keeps the signal. Linux may end the call with another one
7683    /// (the thread's own queue is dequeued first, and the lowest-numbered
7684    /// signal within a queue), leaving this one pending to end the next call
7685    /// that admits it, which must be armed too; clearing the bit here held
7686    /// that call behind a spinner forever (Claude re-check of
7687    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314). No second grant comes
7688    /// before the armed call posts its continuation, since the barrier
7689    /// commits no turn until then, and if that call took the signal the next
7690    /// grant's read of the shared queue forgets it.
7691    ///
7692    /// Before, nothing armed it, so the call's end was a completion only the
7693    /// host observed, and run mode held it behind any runnable thread. Under
7694    /// `--chaos-target-races` the child-exit SIGCHLD often fires before the
7695    /// parent's `sigsuspend` begins, while every thread still blocks it, so a
7696    /// sibling spinning on `sched_yield` for the parent's wake kept it out
7697    /// forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4234).
7698    ///
7699    /// "Still there" is read from the process's shared pending set
7700    /// (`ShdPnd`), not assumed from the record. Linux removes a pending signal
7701    /// in many ways the scheduler does not see as a take: a disposition of
7702    /// SIG_IGN or a default-ignore SIG_DFL, `sigwaitinfo`, a signalfd read,
7703    /// the flush of a timer's signal at exec, and a sibling's dequeue before
7704    /// its delivery stop is granted. Arming for a signal one of them had
7705    /// already removed held the release barrier for a continuation that
7706    /// never came, and refused the run (Claude review of
7707    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314). The read is ordered by
7708    /// the scheduler lock: every thread in the schedule is stopped at its
7709    /// posted request, and the granted thread, already released, cannot issue
7710    /// its call until `finish_resource_response` takes the lock
7711    /// (`lock_rpc_scheduler`), which this step holds. So each of those
7712    /// removals, and every send the record counts, has happened by then, and
7713    /// none can happen during the read; moving the read out from under the
7714    /// lock would lose this. Threads in background calls do run meanwhile;
7715    /// those that could take the signal keep it from being armed
7716    /// (`another_call_may_take_waiting_signal`). A kernel
7717    /// SIGCHLD copy, raised when the host releases a child, coalesces with the
7718    /// scheduler's own while that one is pending, so it changes the read only
7719    /// after the scheduler's copy has gone, a residual of the host-timed copy.
7720    /// The record and the grant are committed points, and the caught set
7721    /// changes only in a guest turn, so the arming is a function of the
7722    /// schedule. The barrier waits with no deadline for the call to post its
7723    /// continuation, and refuses the run if it never does
7724    /// (`SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE`).
7725    fn arm_for_waiting_scheduler_signal(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mask: u64) {
7726        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
7727        let recorded = self
7728            .shared_queue_scheduler_signals
7729            .get(&process)
7730            .copied()
7731            .unwrap_or(0);
7732        if recorded == 0 {
7733            return;
7734        }
7735        // A signal no longer pending in the shared queue was removed
7736        // without a delivery: forget it.
7737        let Some(pending) = self.read_shared_pending(dettid) else {
7738            return;
7739        };
7740        let recorded = recorded & pending;
7741        self.shared_queue_scheduler_signals
7742            .insert(process, recorded);
7743        let Some(caught) = self.signal_mask_field(process, None, "SigCgt") else {
7744            return;
7745        };
7746        let Some(signo) = (1..=64).find(|signo: &i32| {
7747            let bit = kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
7748            recorded & !mask & caught & bit != 0
7749                && !self.another_call_may_take_waiting_signal(dettid, process, bit)
7750        }) else {
7751            return;
7752        };
7753        info!(
7754            "[dtid {}] its call begins with scheduler signal {} waiting in the shared queue",
7755            dettid, signo
7756        );
7757        self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, SigWrapper(signo));
7758    }
7759
7760    /// Whether a call other than `dettid`'s, by another thread of `process`,
7761    /// could take the shared-queue signal `bit` before `dettid`'s call does: a
7762    /// thread polling an `rt_sigtimedwait` set holding it, or a background call
7763    /// reading a signalfd (`background_signalfd_reads`) while a signalfd may
7764    /// read the signal. While the release barrier holds every turn, only a call
7765    /// already running outside the schedule can take it; and a signalfd read
7766    /// or `rt_sigtimedwait` dequeues from the caller's own process, so other
7767    /// processes' calls cannot. If one took the signal, the armed call would
7768    /// never post and the run would be refused, so `dettid`'s call is not
7769    /// armed then.
7770    ///
7771    /// The signalfd masks (`signalfd_may_read`) only accumulate, so they are
7772    /// only a filter. Counting them beside any background call, in any process,
7773    /// kept a wait from being armed beside a closed or unread signalfd and an
7774    /// unrelated `select` or vfork (Claude and Codex re-checks of
7775    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314). A read is tagged only
7776    /// on a descriptor Detcore's table still holds as a signalfd.
7777    fn another_call_may_take_waiting_signal(
7778        &self,
7779        dettid: DetTid,
7780        process: DetPid,
7781        bit: u64,
7782    ) -> bool {
7783        let sigtimedwait = self
7784            .thread_tree
7785            .my_thread_group(&process)
7786            .iter()
7787            .any(|thread| {
7788                *thread != dettid
7789                    && self
7790                        .sigtimedwait_sets
7791                        .get(thread)
7792                        .is_some_and(|set| set & bit != 0)
7793            });
7794        let signalfd_read = self.signalfd_may_read(bit)
7795            && self
7796                .thread_tree
7797                .my_thread_group(&process)
7798                .iter()
7799                .any(|thread| {
7800                    *thread != dettid
7801                        && self
7802                            .background_signalfd_reads
7803                            .get(thread)
7804                            .is_some_and(|op| {
7805                                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(thread) == Some(op)
7806                            })
7807                });
7808        sigtimedwait || signalfd_read
7809    }
7810
7811    /// What the descriptor `fd` of `thread` reads, asked of the kernel: if the
7812    /// kernel names it a signalfd (`anon_inode:[signalfd]`), the signals (a
7813    /// kernel sigset) in the `sigmask` line of its `fdinfo`, which only the
7814    /// guest's own `signalfd4` calls set. `Unknown` where the mask cannot be
7815    /// read, where the descriptor cannot be read at all, and where it is not
7816    /// open, since a later call may install a signalfd at that number before
7817    /// the read enters the kernel.
7818    fn kernel_signalfd_read_mask(&self, thread: DetTid, fd: i32) -> BackgroundReadSignals {
7819        if crate::syscalls::host_signal_state_reads_refused() {
7820            return BackgroundReadSignals::Unknown;
7821        }
7822        let task = format!(
7823            "/proc/{}/task/{}",
7824            self.sigchld_process(thread).as_raw(),
7825            thread.as_raw()
7826        );
7827        match std::fs::read_link(format!("{task}/fd/{fd}")) {
7828            Ok(target) if target == std::path::Path::new("anon_inode:[signalfd]") => {}
7829            Ok(_) => return BackgroundReadSignals::NotSignalfd,
7830            Err(_) => return BackgroundReadSignals::Unknown,
7831        }
7832        std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{task}/fdinfo/{fd}"))
7833            .ok()
7834            .and_then(|info| {
7835                info.lines()
7836                    .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("sigmask:"))
7837                    .and_then(|mask| u64::from_str_radix(mask.trim(), 16).ok())
7838            })
7839            .map_or(
7840                BackgroundReadSignals::Unknown,
7841                BackgroundReadSignals::Signalfd,
7842            )
7843    }
7844
7845    /// `close`, `close_range`, `dup2` or `dup3` released or replaced the
7846    /// descriptors `first..=last` of the descriptor table `files`, in its
7847    /// caller's turn: a background read of one of those numbers in that table
7848    /// that has not yet entered the kernel may now read another description,
7849    /// so what it reads becomes `Unknown` (`background_reads`,
7850    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4410). Every thread sharing
7851    /// the table (`CLONE_FILES`) names it by the same identity.
7852    pub(crate) fn note_descriptors_replaced(
7853        &mut self,
7854        files: detcore_model::fd::FilesId,
7855        first: u32,
7856        last: u32,
7857    ) {
7858        for read in self.background_reads.values_mut() {
7859            if read.files == files
7860                && u32::try_from(read.fd).is_ok_and(|fd| (first..=last).contains(&fd))
7861            {
7862                read.signals = BackgroundReadSignals::Unknown;
7863            }
7864        }
7865    }
7866
7867    /// Whether a thread of `dtid`'s process other than `dtid` sleeps outside the
7868    /// schedule in a call that could take its process's SIGCHLD at a moment
7869    /// host timing chooses: a call whose recorded mask
7870    /// (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`) leaves SIGCHLD unblocked or is
7871    /// unknown, so the kernel may deliver it there, or a background read whose
7872    /// descriptor may read SIGCHLD (`background_reads`). Membership is fixed
7873    /// at commit points: an entry is made when the call is granted and removed
7874    /// when it rejoins.
7875    ///
7876    /// Under record and replay, a woken sleep claims its SIGCHLD only when this
7877    /// is false (`ChildExitSigchldControl::WindowUnusable`). While such a call
7878    /// is out, whether it took the copy before the claim reads the pending bit
7879    /// is host-timed, in the recording and again in the replay, so the two
7880    /// could decide differently, and the replay then took a different branch
7881    /// or waited for ever for a signal the claim had taken
7882    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4343). Without the claim the
7883    /// sleep stays parked, and the outside call takes the copy as it did
7884    /// before the claim existed.
7885    pub(crate) fn outside_call_may_take_sigchld(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> bool {
7886        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
7887        let process = self.sigchld_process(dtid);
7888        self.thread_tree
7889            .my_thread_group(&process)
7890            .iter()
7891            .any(|thread| {
7892                *thread != dtid
7893                    && (self
7894                        .blocked
7895                        .out_of_scheduler_masks
7896                        .get(thread)
7897                        .is_some_and(|mask| mask.is_none_or(|mask| mask & bit == 0))
7898                        || self.background_reads.get(thread).is_some_and(|read| {
7899                            self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(thread) == Some(&read.op)
7900                                && read.signals.may_read(bit)
7901                        }))
7902            })
7903    }
7904
7905    /// The thread of `process` that a timer's process-directed `sig` is sent
7906    /// to, given the thread `select_signal_target` drew (`preferred`): the
7907    /// thread `kernel_signal_target` gives it (an `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper that
7908    /// does not block it, else `preferred` if it does not, else the first
7909    /// thread that does not), or `preferred` when every thread blocks it.
7910    ///
7911    /// The send names one thread, and the scheduler wakes that thread
7912    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`). Linux gives a process-directed signal only to
7913    /// a thread that does not block it (`complete_signal`), so naming a thread
7914    /// that blocks it woke the wrong thread: under `--chaos-target-races`, a
7915    /// SIGALRM drawn for a worker that blocks it left the thread in `pause`
7916    /// asleep forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320). A
7917    /// sleeper comes first because the kernel wakes it while the drawn thread
7918    /// is held in a ptrace stop, which `wants_signal` skips; naming the drawn
7919    /// thread then left which of the two took the signal to host timing
7920    /// (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4331, the same
7921    /// race https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237 fixed for SIGCHLD).
7922    /// When every thread blocks it, Linux keeps it in the shared queue for the
7923    /// first thread that unblocks it, which `kill` to any of them does too.
7924    ///
7925    /// Called only at a timed dispatch, where no guest thread holds the turn,
7926    /// so every mask read is a function of the schedule (see
7927    /// `kernel_sigchld_target`). Without signal-target modelling no mask is
7928    /// read, and `preferred` is kept.
7929    fn timer_signal_target(&self, process: DetPid, preferred: DetTid, sig: Signal) -> DetTid {
7930        if !self.models_signal_targets {
7931            return preferred;
7932        }
7933        match self.kernel_signal_target(process, preferred, sig as libc::c_int) {
7934            Some(thread) => {
7935                if thread != preferred {
7936                    info!(
7937                        "[dpid {}] sending {} to thread {} rather than the drawn thread {}.",
7938                        process, sig, thread, preferred
7939                    );
7940                }
7941                thread
7942            }
7943            None => preferred,
7944        }
7945    }
7946
7947    /// Send `sig` to `target` of `dpid`, classified against `named`, the task
7948    /// Linux names (`discarded_when_sent_to`), never inferred from `target`,
7949    /// which may be a thread Hermit chose. `fate`: how the discarded-at-send
7950    /// record classifies it.
7951    fn fire_alarm_at(
7952        &mut self,
7953        dpid: DetPid,
7954        target: Option<DetTid>,
7955        sig: Signal,
7956        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
7957        named: DetTid,
7958        fate: discarded_at_send::SendFate,
7959    ) -> bool {
7960        let Some(target) = target else {
7961            info!(
7962                "[dpid {}] Alarm expired after its target exited; ignoring.",
7963                dpid
7964            );
7965            return false;
7966        };
7967        info!(
7968            "[dtid {}] Alarm fired, delivering signal {} to guest.",
7969            target, sig
7970        );
7971        self.send_guest_signal(target, sig, None, info, named, fate);
7972        true
7973    }
7974
7975    /// Send an expiration of a `SIGEV_SIGNAL` POSIX timer of `process`
7976    /// (armed by `tid`) at its pop, as [`Self::fire_alarm`] does, with `info`
7977    /// its `SI_TIMER` siginfo where the scheduler models signal targets. The
7978    /// record's `SI_TIMER` code makes exec flush it, as Linux flushes a
7979    /// queued timer signal (`flush_itimer_signals`).
7980    pub(super) fn fire_process_timer(
7981        &mut self,
7982        process: DetPid,
7983        tid: DetTid,
7984        sig: Signal,
7985        producer: Option<discarded_at_send::TimerProducer>,
7986        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
7987    ) {
7988        // Only where the scheduler models signal targets (ptrace) is a
7989        // thread's `/proc` view its DetTid's.
7990        if !self.models_signal_targets {
7991            self.fire_alarm(process, tid, sig);
7992            return;
7993        }
7994        self.guest_send_landed = None;
7995        if !self.fire_process_alarm(
7996            process,
7997            tid,
7998            sig,
7999            info,
8000            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(
8001                producer.map(discarded_at_send::SignalProducer::Posix),
8002            ),
8003        ) {
8004            return;
8005        }
8006        self.note_replayed_timer_copy(
8007            discarded_at_send::QueueId::Process(process),
8008            sig as libc::c_int,
8009        );
8010        // Rule 4: a scheduler send of SIGALRM into the shared queue gives a
8011        // copy-less Inactive ITIMER_REAL its copy, whose dequeue restarts it
8012        // as on Linux (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
8013        if sig == Signal::SIGALRM && self.guest_send_landed != Some(false) {
8014            self.note_guest_sigalrm(tid, itimer_coalesce::GuestSigalrmTarget::Process(process));
8015        }
8016    }
8017
8018    /// Whether a signalfd could read the signal `bit` in some process. A
8019    /// signalfd's open description is shared with every process that
8020    /// inherited or received it, and any of them can change its mask
8021    /// (`signalfd(fd, mask)`), which Detcore sees only in the process that
8022    /// changed it; so the masks of every process count (Codex review of
8023    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
8024    fn signalfd_may_read(&self, bit: u64) -> bool {
8025        self.signalfd_masks.values().any(|mask| mask & bit != 0)
8026    }
8027
8028    /// `dettid` took a copy of `signo` at its delivery stop: if the shared
8029    /// queue no longer holds it, the record of a scheduler signal left there
8030    /// goes (`shared_queue_scheduler_signals`). The thread's own queue is
8031    /// dequeued first, so the copy taken may be another: a private take
8032    /// leaves the shared copy, and its record, in place (Codex review of
8033    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314).
8034    fn note_process_signal_taken(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signo: i32) {
8035        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
8036        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
8037        let recorded = self
8038            .shared_queue_scheduler_signals
8039            .get(&process)
8040            .is_some_and(|waiting| waiting & bit != 0);
8041        if recorded
8042            && self
8043                .read_shared_pending(dettid)
8044                .is_none_or(|pending| pending & bit == 0)
8045            && let Some(waiting) = self.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.get_mut(&process)
8046        {
8047            *waiting &= !bit;
8048        }
8049    }
8050
8051    /// A non-leader exec's caller `former` survives as `leader`
8052    /// (`reconnect_exec`): its own queue, and so its timer copy records, move
8053    /// to the leader's tid.
8054    fn transfer_thread_timer_copies(&mut self, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
8055        if former == leader {
8056            return;
8057        }
8058        let moved: Vec<_> = self
8059            .thread_timer_copies
8060            .iter()
8061            .filter(|((thread, _), _)| *thread == former)
8062            .map(|((_, signo), id)| (*signo, *id))
8063            .collect();
8064        self.thread_timer_copies
8065            .retain(|(thread, _), _| *thread != former && *thread != leader);
8066        for (signo, id) in moved {
8067            self.thread_timer_copies.insert((leader, signo), id);
8068        }
8069    }
8070
8071    /// What a successful exec of `process`, whose surviving thread is
8072    /// `survivor`, does to its pending timer signals, in the exec's turn
8073    /// before the new image runs. Linux removes every queued record whose
8074    /// `si_code` is `SI_TIMER`, from the survivor's own queue and the shared
8075    /// one (`flush_itimer_signals`), and keeps every other. Hermit sends each
8076    /// timer's record with `SI_TIMER`, so the kernel flushes those itself; a
8077    /// discarded copy carrying `SI_TIMER` goes too. What remains is where the
8078    /// physical records and Linux's entries differ (`SignalLists::exec`,
8079    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4262>): a `Proxy` ordinary
8080    /// entry whose `SI_TIMER` record was flushed is sent again here, and a
8081    /// kept record whose entry exec removed is returned for the survivor to
8082    /// take back. A shared record behind a copy of the same signal in the
8083    /// survivor's own queue cannot be taken alone: an `Err` names it.
8084    ///
8085    /// The exec retired every other thread with its queue
8086    /// (`logically_kill_thread`), and a non-leader caller's records moved to
8087    /// the leader's tid with its queue (`rekey_thread`).
8088    pub(crate) fn take_exec_timer_flush(
8089        &mut self,
8090        survivor: DetTid,
8091        process: DetPid,
8092    ) -> Result<ExecTimerFlush, String> {
8093        self.pending_real_time_expirations.remove(&process);
8094        self.thread_timer_copies
8095            .retain(|(thread, _), _| *thread != survivor);
8096        if let Some(refusal) = self.replay_exec_refusal(survivor, process) {
8097            return Err(refusal);
8098        }
8099        self.discarded_at_send.forget_parks_of(process);
8100        let (private, shared) = (
8101            discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(survivor),
8102            discarded_at_send::QueueId::Process(process),
8103        );
8104        for queue in [private, shared] {
8105            for signo in 1..32 {
8106                if self.discarded_at_send.discarded_is_si_timer(queue, signo) {
8107                    self.discarded_at_send.flush([queue], signo);
8108                }
8109            }
8110        }
8111        let outcome = self.discarded_at_send.lists.exec(&[private, shared]);
8112        // The survivor is running its exec: a re-send to it wakes nothing
8113        // (`send_wakes`).
8114        self.signal_control_caller = Some(survivor);
8115        for (queue, signo, _) in &outcome.resend {
8116            let Ok(sig) = Signal::try_from(*signo) else {
8117                continue;
8118            };
8119            info!(
8120                "[dtid {}] exec flushed the SI_TIMER record a kept signal {} stood on; sent again.",
8121                survivor, sig
8122            );
8123            let thread_of =
8124                matches!(queue, discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(_)).then_some(process);
8125            self.send_guest_signal(
8126                survivor,
8127                sig,
8128                thread_of,
8129                None,
8130                survivor,
8131                discarded_at_send::SendFate::Kept,
8132            );
8133        }
8134        self.signal_control_caller = None;
8135        let mut flush = ExecTimerFlush::default();
8136        for (queue, signo) in outcome.take_back {
8137            match queue {
8138                discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(_) => flush.own |= kernel_signal_bit(signo),
8139                discarded_at_send::QueueId::Process(_) => flush.shared |= kernel_signal_bit(signo),
8140            }
8141        }
8142        if flush.shared & !flush.own != 0 {
8143            let state = self
8144                .read_sleeper_signal_state(survivor)
8145                .map_err(|failure| {
8146                    format!(
8147                        "the pending signals of thread {survivor} could not be read ({failure:?})"
8148                    )
8149                })?;
8150            if let Some(signo) = first_signal(flush.shared & !flush.own & state.thread_pending) {
8151                return Err(format!(
8152                    "a POSIX timer's entry of signal {signo} stood on a record in the shared queue behind another copy in thread {survivor}'s own queue, which a dequeue would take first"
8153                ));
8154            }
8155        }
8156        Ok(flush)
8157    }
8158
8159    /// Deliver an expiration of a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` POSIX timer of `process`
8160    /// to exactly `thread`, as Linux queues it on that thread's own queue
8161    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164>). Unlike
8162    /// [`Self::fire_alarm`], no other thread stands in: once `thread` has
8163    /// exited, the expiration is dropped and the timer stays armed, as on
8164    /// Linux. Nothing goes through the in-guest SIGALRM ledger, which is
8165    /// process-wide: a POSIX timer notifying SIGALRM is refused while a
8166    /// handler is published (`SigalrmControl::ArmProducer`), and once armed it
8167    /// refuses a later handler, so the two never meet.
8168    ///
8169    /// A standard signal already pending on the thread
8170    /// (`thread_timer_send`): Linux queues the timer's own preallocated signal
8171    /// beside it (`posixtimer_send_sigqueue` skips `legacy_queue`), so the
8172    /// thread takes the signal twice, while a send from here merges into the
8173    /// pending copy. The run is refused by name rather than lose a delivery,
8174    /// unless the pending copy is this timer's own earlier expiration, which
8175    /// Linux counts as an overrun and does not queue again.
8176    fn fire_thread_timer(&mut self, id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId, thread: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
8177        let process = id.process();
8178        if !self.process_signal_targets(process).contains(&thread) {
8179            info!(
8180                "[dpid {}] Timer expired after its thread {} exited; dropped.",
8181                process, thread
8182            );
8183            return;
8184        }
8185        match self.thread_timer_send(id, thread, sig) {
8186            ThreadTimerSend::Send => {}
8187            ThreadTimerSend::Overrun => {
8188                info!(
8189                    "[dtid {}] Thread-directed timer fired while its own signal {} is still pending there; an overrun, nothing sent.",
8190                    thread, sig
8191                );
8192                return;
8193            }
8194            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) => exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&format_args!(
8195                "hermit: a SIGEV_THREAD_ID timer of process {process} expired for thread {thread} while signal {sig} was already pending there {reason}; Linux queues the timer's own signal beside it, a second delivery Detcore cannot produce, so the run is refused rather than lose it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4157)"
8196            )),
8197        }
8198        #[cfg(test)]
8199        {
8200            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
8201        }
8202        info!(
8203            "[dtid {}] Thread-directed timer fired, delivering signal {} to it.",
8204            thread, sig
8205        );
8206        let signo = sig as libc::c_int;
8207        TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
8208        // A job-control signal's copy can be flushed unobserved by any
8209        // sender's SIGCONT or stop signal.
8210        if self.thread_timer_copy_is_observable(thread, kernel_signal_bit(signo))
8211            && !is_job_control_signal(signo)
8212        {
8213            self.thread_timer_copies.insert((thread, signo), id);
8214        } else {
8215            self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(thread, signo));
8216        }
8217        self.note_replayed_timer_copy(discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(thread), signo);
8218        let producer = self.posix_timer_producer(id);
8219        // Its `SI_TIMER` record, with the overrun counted at the pop
8220        // (`fire_posix_timer_fallback`), which exec flushes.
8221        let info = match id {
8222            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(_, timer) if self.models_signal_targets => {
8223                let entry = self.timer_entry_now(process, timer);
8224                Some(self.timer_signal_info(
8225                    signo,
8226                    &entry,
8227                    self.posix_timer_overrun(process, timer),
8228                ))
8229            }
8230            _ => None,
8231        };
8232        self.send_guest_signal(
8233            thread,
8234            sig,
8235            Some(process),
8236            info,
8237            thread,
8238            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(
8239                producer.map(discarded_at_send::SignalProducer::Posix),
8240            ),
8241        );
8242    }
8243
8244    /// Whether timer `id`'s expiration can be sent to `thread` as signal
8245    /// `sig` (`fire_thread_timer`). It reads the thread's private pending
8246    /// set (`SigPnd`): the thread is stopped at a request, parked, or in a call
8247    /// outside the schedule, and no guest thread holds the turn at a timed
8248    /// dispatch, so only a host-timed signal could change it. A real-time
8249    /// signal queues every copy, so only a standard one can merge.
8250    fn thread_timer_send(
8251        &mut self,
8252        id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId,
8253        thread: DetTid,
8254        sig: Signal,
8255    ) -> ThreadTimerSend {
8256        let signo = sig as libc::c_int;
8257        // A pending copy Linux discarded when it was sent is not one: the
8258        // timer's copy is the only one Linux would hold
8259        // (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293>).
8260        let discarded = self
8261            .discarded_at_send
8262            .discarded(discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(thread));
8263        let pending = match self.read_sleeper_signal_state(thread) {
8264            Ok(state) => state.thread_pending & !discarded,
8265            Err(_) => {
8266                return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
8267                    "(its pending signals could not be read)".to_owned(),
8268                );
8269            }
8270        };
8271        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
8272        if pending & bit == 0 {
8273            // The timer's own earlier copy, if any, has been taken.
8274            self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(thread, signo));
8275            return ThreadTimerSend::Send;
8276        }
8277        // The terminal and the host can send these too.
8278        if is_job_control_signal(signo) {
8279            return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
8280                "(a job-control signal, which any sender's SIGCONT or stop signal may have flushed unobserved)"
8281                    .to_owned(),
8282            );
8283        }
8284        if !self.thread_timer_copy_is_observable(thread, bit) {
8285            return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
8286                "(a signalfd or an rt_sigtimedwait of the thread may have taken this timer's copy unobserved)"
8287                    .to_owned(),
8288            );
8289        }
8290        match self.thread_timer_copies.get(&(thread, signo)) {
8291            Some(sender) if *sender == id => ThreadTimerSend::Overrun,
8292            Some(sender) => ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(format!("(sent by another timer, {sender:?})")),
8293            None => ThreadTimerSend::Refuse("(not sent by this timer)".to_owned()),
8294        }
8295    }
8296
8297    /// The disposition of `signo` in `process` became one that ignores it:
8298    /// Linux flushes its pending copies from every thread (`do_sigaction`), so
8299    /// no timer's copy of it is pending anywhere in the process.
8300    pub(crate) fn forget_thread_timer_copies(&mut self, process: DetPid, signo: i32) {
8301        let threads: Vec<DetTid> = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&process);
8302        self.thread_timer_copies
8303            .retain(|(thread, signal), _| *signal != signo || !threads.contains(thread));
8304    }
8305
8306    /// Whether every consumption of a copy of the signal `bit` on `thread` is
8307    /// observed (`thread_timer_copies`): not while the thread polls a
8308    /// `rt_sigtimedwait` set holding it, nor while a signalfd could read it
8309    /// (`signalfd_may_read`).
8310    fn thread_timer_copy_is_observable(&self, thread: DetTid, bit: u64) -> bool {
8311        self.sigtimedwait_sets
8312            .get(&thread)
8313            .is_none_or(|set| set & bit == 0)
8314            && !self.signalfd_may_read(bit)
8315    }
8316
8317    /// Snapshot eligibility is local to the exact outstanding sleep request.
8318    /// Only a backend that keeps the guest's SIGALRM virtual
8319    /// (`virtualizes_guest_sigalrm`) has such a sleep; this reads that fact
8320    /// rather than comparing the whole capability set with one backend's.
8321    fn in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(
8322        &self,
8323        thread: DetTid,
8324    ) -> Option<(crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm, LogicalTime)> {
8325        if !self.backend.virtualizes_guest_sigalrm
8326            || self.registered_process(thread) != Some(thread)
8327            || self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) != [thread]
8328        {
8329            return None;
8330        }
8331        self.next_turns
8332            .get(&thread)?
8333            .req
8334            .try_read()?
8335            .ok()?
8336            .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
8337    }
8338
8339    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(&self, thread: DetTid) -> bool {
8340        self.next_turns
8341            .get(&thread)
8342            .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
8343            .is_some_and(|request| {
8344                request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
8345                    resources.resources.len() == 1
8346                        && resources.resources.get(&ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm)
8347                            == Some(&Permission::W)
8348                })
8349            })
8350    }
8351
8352    /// Only a consumed one-shot Alarm identity may replace a parked sleep.
8353    /// Dispatch supplies the event timestamp and observed GlobalTime, since
8354    /// empty-queue skips and control hooks can advance that clock before
8355    /// committed_time is refreshed.
8356    fn divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
8357        &mut self,
8358        event_ns: LogicalTime,
8359        id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId,
8360        thread: DetTid,
8361        signal: Signal,
8362        observed_now: LogicalTime,
8363    ) -> bool {
8364        let timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(process) = id else {
8365            return false;
8366        };
8367        if signal != Signal::SIGALRM
8368            || process != thread
8369            || self.sigalrm_handled(process)
8370            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_state(process).is_some()
8371            || !matches!(self.thread_status(thread), ThreadStatus::NotRunning)
8372            || self
8373                .happens_before
8374                .as_ref()
8375                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&thread))
8376        {
8377            return false;
8378        }
8379        let Some((snapshot, deadline)) = self.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(thread) else {
8380            return false;
8381        };
8382        if !snapshot.ends_process()
8383            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(thread) != Some(deadline)
8384            || deadline <= self.committed_time.max(event_ns).max(observed_now)
8385        {
8386            return false;
8387        }
8388        let mut wake = Resources::new(thread);
8389        wake.insert(ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm, Permission::W);
8390        info!(
8391            "[dtid {}] one-shot SIGALRM expired during an in-guest sleep; staging fatal delivery in the target's turn.",
8392            thread
8393        );
8394        self.force_unblock_thread(thread, wake);
8395        true
8396    }
8397
8398    /// Authenticate the retained caller request after the typed grant cleared
8399    /// its scheduler slot. This rejects a fabricated generic fatal resource,
8400    /// a stale address space, or a grant belonging to another task.
8401    pub(crate) fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
8402        &self,
8403        thread: DetTid,
8404        process: DetPid,
8405        mm: Option<MmId>,
8406        original: &Resources,
8407    ) -> bool {
8408        self.backend.virtualizes_guest_sigalrm
8409            && thread == process
8410            && original.tid == thread
8411            && original
8412                .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
8413                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| snapshot.ends_process())
8414            && self.registered_process(thread) == Some(process)
8415            && self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) == [thread]
8416            && mm.is_some_and(|mm| self.rpc_incarnation_matches(thread, mm))
8417            && self.holds_serial_grant(thread)
8418    }

8420    // Follow Linux semantics for delivering a signal to a thread within a process group.
8421    // Optionally take a hint on which tid detcore would *like* to deliver to, if it is available.
8422    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8423    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
8424    fn select_signal_target(&mut self, detpid: DetPid, m_dettid: Option<DetTid>) -> Option<DetTid> {
8425        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
8426            return None;
8427        }
8428
8429        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a process-directed signal may legally be
