8430        // handled by any thread in the group that does not block it. Instead of
8431        // always steering it to the hinted/leader thread, pick a random eligible
8432        // thread to surface signal-timing races. This stays reproducible under a
8433        // fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
8434        if let Some(chosen) = self.chaos_signal_target(detpid) {
8435            return Some(chosen);
8436        }
8437        self.live_signal_target(detpid, m_dettid)
8438    }
8439
8440    /// Under targeted chaos (`--chaos-target-races`), a random live thread of
8441    /// `detpid` to steer a process-directed signal to; `None` otherwise. Each
8442    /// call draws once from the fuzz PRNG.
8443    fn chaos_signal_target(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<DetTid> {
8444        if !self.chaos_target_races {
8445            return None;
8446        }
8447        let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
8448        let eligible: Vec<DetTid> = group
8449            .into_iter()
8450            .filter(|t| !matches!(self.thread_status(*t), ThreadStatus::Gone))
8451            .collect();
8452        let chosen = chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &eligible)?;
8453        info!(
8454            "[targeted-chaos] delivering process-directed signal to random group thread {} (of {:?})",
8455            chosen, eligible
8456        );
8457        Some(chosen)
8458    }
8459
8460    /// `select_signal_target` without targeted chaos: `m_dettid` if it is
8461    /// live, else the leader, else the process's first live thread.
8462    fn live_signal_target(&self, detpid: DetPid, m_dettid: Option<DetTid>) -> Option<DetTid> {
8463        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
8464            return None;
8465        }
8466        if let Some(dettid) = m_dettid {
8467            match self.thread_status(dettid) {
8468                ThreadStatus::Gone => {}
8469                ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
8470                    return Some(dettid);
8471                }
8472            }
8473        }
8474        // A thread whose exit waits for a sibling's delivery permit
8475        // (`exits_awaiting_permit`) is still live, and so still among
8476        // `process_signal_targets`, but it is exiting: the kernel passes it by
8477        // (`wants_signal` skips an exiting thread), and a signal sent to it
8478        // would never be delivered (`wake_signaled_guest`). So it is not chosen
8479        // here; a live sibling is (the Codex review of
8480        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4367).
8481        match self.thread_status(detpid) {
8482            ThreadStatus::Gone => self
8483                .process_signal_targets(detpid)
8484                .into_iter()
8485                .find(|thread| !self.parked.exits_awaiting_permit.contains(thread)),
8486            ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => Some(detpid),
8487        }
8488    }
8489
8490    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
8491    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
8492    /// Return the scheduler's live threads for a positive process ID.
8493    /// Is `dettid` a live thread, leader or not?
8494    ///
8495    /// `process_signal_targets` answers a DIFFERENT question and must not be
8496    /// reused for this one: it models `kill(2)`, so it returns nothing unless
8497    /// the id names a thread-group LEADER. `sched_setattr(2)` and its relatives
8498    /// resolve through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds any live task, so a
8499    /// non-leader thread's tid is a perfectly good target there. Answering that
8500    /// question with the kill resolver reports ESRCH for a thread that exists.
8501    ///
8502    /// Liveness is `next_turns`, the same membership `process_signal_targets`
8503    /// filters its own result by, so the two agree about what "live" means.
8504    pub fn thread_is_live(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
8505        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid)
8506    }
8507
8508    /// Whether `dettid` is the pid of a zombie child of `caller`'s process: a
8509    /// process that exited and that its parent, the caller's process, has not
8510    /// reaped. Linux keeps that pid until a wait in the caller's process
8511    /// consumes it (`consume_child_wait`), a committed turn, or the caller's
8512    /// process dies, which ends the caller too, so for the caller this answer
8513    /// cannot change at a host-timed moment. Another process's zombie can be
8514    /// freed when its parent dies without a granted exit, which Detcore learns
8515    /// at a host-timed deregistration. An autoreaped child or an orphan
8516    /// Hermit's init reaped is not a zombie (`exited_process_is_zombie`).
8517    pub(crate) fn id_is_a_zombie_child_of(&self, dettid: DetTid, caller: DetTid) -> bool {
8518        let pid = DetPid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw());
8519        self.exited_process_is_zombie(pid) == Some(true)
8520            && self.thread_tree.parent_process(&pid).is_some()
8521            && self.thread_tree.parent_process(&pid)
8522                == self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&caller).copied()
8523    }
8524
8525    /// Forget the exit of the process that last had pid `pid`, which a new
8526    /// process now has. Linux reuses a pid only once its last holder is
8527    /// gone, so its holder was reaped automatically or by init, and the
8528    /// record that it exited (`exited_process_is_zombie`) would otherwise
8529    /// describe the new process (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266>).
8530    pub fn forget_previous_process_exit(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
8531        self.logically_exited_processes.remove(&pid);
8532        self.autoreaped_exits.remove(&pid);
8533    }
8534
8535    /// The processes `/proc` lists, and, for `process`, the threads its
8536    /// `task` directory lists, as the container's PID namespace numbers them
8537    /// (`procfs::listing`). As on Linux, a process is listed from its
8538    /// creation until it is reaped, zombie included: while its wait record
8539    /// exists (every process gets one when created, the root and a
8540    /// `CLONE_PARENT` child of it included, and a reap removes it,
8541    /// `consume_child_wait`, before the backend has necessarily reported its
8542    /// threads' exits), unless it exited and is no zombie a guest can reap:
8543    /// an automatically reaped child, an orphan of the namespace's init
8544    /// (`exited_process_is_zombie`), or a process with no guest parent (the
8545    /// root process, a `CLONE_PARENT` child of it), which Hermit itself
8546    /// reaps. Its `task` lists its live threads and its leader while the
8547    /// process is listed.
8548    pub fn procfs_listing(&self, process: Option<DetPid>) -> crate::procfs::listing::ListingFacts {
8549        let listed = |leader: DetPid| self.process_exists(leader);
8550        let mut processes: Vec<i32> = self
8551            .thread_tree
8552            .thread_group_leaders
8553            .iter()
8554            .copied()
8555            .filter(|leader| listed(*leader))
8556            .map(|leader| leader.as_raw())
8557            .collect();
8558        processes.sort_unstable();
8559        let threads = match process {
8560            Some(process)
8561                if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&process) && listed(process) =>
8562            {
8563                let mut threads: Vec<i32> = self
8564                    .thread_tree
8565                    .my_thread_group(&process)
8566                    .into_iter()
8567                    .filter(|tid| *tid == process || self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
8568                    .map(|tid| tid.as_raw())
8569                    .collect();
8570                threads.sort_unstable();
8571                threads
8572            }
8573            _ => Vec::new(),
8574        };
8575        crate::procfs::listing::ListingFacts { processes, threads }
8576    }
8577
8578    /// Whether the task a per-process `/proc` file names exists, and whether
8579    /// the task it describes has exited without being reaped, for the
8580    /// top-level number `named` and the thread `thread` below its `task`, as
8581    /// the container's PID namespace numbers them: the lookup Linux makes of
8582    /// `/proc/<named>` (a listed process, a zombie until it is reaped, or a
8583    /// live thread of a listed process) and of its `task/<thread>`
8584    /// (`procfs::listing::task_exists`). The task the file describes is the
8585    /// thread, else the task `named` is; one that has exited (it has no turn
8586    /// left, `thread_is_live`) while its file exists has no memory map in
8587    /// Linux. Hermit's own init, pid 1 where no guest holds it, is live.
8588    pub fn procfs_task(&self, named: DetTid, thread: Option<DetTid>) -> (bool, bool) {
8589        let leader = self.signal_target_process(named);
8590        let facts = self.procfs_listing(leader);
8591        let task = crate::procfs::BoundTask {
8592            process: named.as_raw(),
8593            thread: thread.map(|thread| thread.as_raw()),
8594        };
8595        let exists =
8596            crate::procfs::listing::task_exists(task, leader.map(|leader| leader.as_raw()), &facts);
8597        if !exists {
8598            return (false, false);
8599        }
8600        let described = thread.unwrap_or(named);
8601        let hermit_init = described.as_raw() == 1 && leader.is_none();
8602        (true, !hermit_init && !self.thread_is_live(described))
8603    }
8604
8605    /// The kernel's number for each of `ids`, a guest process or thread
8606    /// number as `/proc` spells it (`to_kernel`), or the guest's for each
8607    /// kernel number (`!to_kernel`), where the backend's host threads
8608    /// registered their kernel ids (`register_physical_thread`; DBT, whose
8609    /// kernel numbers the container's processes otherwise than Detcore).
8610    /// `None` for a number of no process or live thread `/proc` lists
8611    /// (`procfs_listing`). Pid 1, the namespace's init, is Hermit's own
8612    /// process in both numberings unless a guest holds it. Where the
8613    /// numberings agree (no kernel ids registered, or each thread's is its
8614    /// own number), every number is its own.
8615    pub fn procfs_ids(&self, to_kernel: bool, ids: &[i32]) -> Vec<Option<i32>> {
8616        // Where every registered thread's kernel tid is its own number (an
8617        // in-guest native exec), or none registered, the numberings agree:
8618        // every number is its own.
8619        if self
8620            .procfs_kernel_ids
8621            .iter()
8622            .all(|(tid, (_, thread))| tid.as_raw() == *thread)
8623        {
8624            return ids.iter().map(|id| Some(*id)).collect();
8625        }
8626        let processes = self.procfs_listing(None).processes;
8627        // A process's leader while the process is listed (zombies too), and
8628        // any other thread while it lives.
8629        let listed = |tid: DetTid| {
8630            processes.binary_search(&tid.as_raw()).is_ok()
8631                || (self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid)
8632                    && self
8633                        .thread_tree
8634                        .thread_to_leader
8635                        .get(&tid)
8636                        .is_some_and(|leader| processes.binary_search(&leader.as_raw()).is_ok()))
8637        };
8638        let holds_one = |tid: DetTid| self.procfs_kernel_ids.contains_key(&tid);
8639        ids.iter()
8640            .map(|&id| {
8641                if to_kernel {
8642                    let tid = DetTid::from_raw(id);
8643                    match self.procfs_kernel_ids.get(&tid) {
8644                        Some((process, thread)) if listed(tid) => {
8645                            Some(if processes.binary_search(&id).is_ok() {
8646                                *process
8647                            } else {
8648                                *thread
8649                            })
8650                        }
8651                        _ if id == 1 && !holds_one(tid) => Some(1),
8652                        _ => None,
8653                    }
8654                } else {
8655                    self.procfs_kernel_ids
8656                        .iter()
8657                        .find(|(tid, (_, thread))| *thread == id && listed(**tid))
8658                        .map(|(tid, _)| tid.as_raw())
8659                        .or_else(|| (id == 1 && !holds_one(DetTid::from_raw(1))).then_some(1))
8660                }
8661            })
8662            .collect()
8663    }
8664
8665    /// Return scheduler-owned lifecycle state for an exact child-process wait.
8666    ///
8667    /// This deliberately models direct parentage and process liveness rather
8668    /// than `kill(2)` target resolution. It lets wait syscalls stop exposing
8669    /// the backend-dependent interval between logical exit and host waitability.
8670    pub fn exact_child_wait_state(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> ExactChildWaitState {
8671        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
8672            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
8673        }
8674
8675        let live = self
8676            .thread_tree
8677            .my_thread_group(&child)
8678            .into_iter()
8679            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
8680        if live {
8681            return ExactChildWaitState::Running;
8682        }
8683
8684        if !self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
8685            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
8686        }
8687
8688        if !self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits {
8689            ExactChildWaitState::LogicallyExited
8690        } else if self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(&child) {
8691            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicalExitPending
8692        } else {
8693            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicallyExited
8694        }
8695    }
8696
8697    fn child_matches_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
8698        let Some(metadata) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
8699            return false;
8700        };
8701        metadata.wait_parent == Some(parent)
8702            && spec.owner.is_none_or(|owner| metadata.wait_owner == owner)
8703            && match spec.exit_class {
8704                ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld => metadata.exit_signal == libc::SIGCHLD,
8705                ChildWaitExitClass::Clone => metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD,
8706                ChildWaitExitClass::Any => true,
8707            }
8708            && match spec.selector {
8709                ChildWaitSelector::Exact(expected) => child == expected,
8710                ChildWaitSelector::Any => true,
8711                ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group) => metadata.process_group == group,
8712            }
8713    }
8714
8715    /// True when there is at least one child wait and every one of them can
8716    /// only be satisfied by stuck children: children whose live threads are
8717    /// all held at happens-before gates, parked in a futex wait, waiting with
8718    /// no deadline (`pause`, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), or
8719    /// themselves in a child wait on stuck children. (A futex wait with a
8720    /// timeout counts too, but both callers decide only when no timer is
8721    /// reachable: any finite deadline fast-forwards the clock first.) None of these runs again
8722    /// until some other thread does (an anchor firing, a futex wake, a signal,
8723    /// a child exit), so with nothing runnable, no reachable timer and no
8724    /// outstanding external I/O, such waits can never end
8725    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904). A chain of waits
8726    /// down to a stuck child is stuck too, so an ancestor's ordinary wait does
8727    /// not hide the cycle below it. A wait with no matching child, a child
8728    /// with any other live thread or none, a child that has already exited,
8729    /// and a child a committed SIGKILL has doomed (it will die at a host-timed
8730    /// point, so its wait is real) are treated as able to end, as before.
8731    ///
8732    /// This held only in happens-before runs with a held thread until
8733    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430: elsewhere a parent
8734    /// waiting for a child in `pause()` (or in a futex wait nothing can wake)
8735    /// spun until the outer deadline, where the same child without the wait is
8736    /// reported as a deadlock at once. A signal from outside the container
8737    /// could end such a wait, as it could a lone `pause`, which is reported.
8738    ///
8739    /// Outside a happens-before run with a held thread (where it applied
8740    /// before 4430, and still does), it needs a backend that reports every
8741    /// child (`complete_child_lineage`): elsewhere a wait may match a child
8742    /// Detcore has no record of, which could still exit.
8743    fn child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children(&self) -> bool {
8744        let hb = self.happens_before.as_ref();
8745        if self.unresolved_sigkill || self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty() {
8746            return false;
8747        }
8748        if !self.complete_child_lineage && hb.is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty()) {
8749            return false;
8750        }
8751        // The stuck processes, as a least fixed point: a process becomes stuck
8752        // once each of its live threads is held, futex-parked, or waiting only
8753        // on processes already found stuck. Growing the set only makes more
8754        // processes qualify, so the iteration ends; the process tree has no
8755        // cycles, so a chain is found one level per round.
8756        let mut stuck: BTreeSet<DetPid> = BTreeSet::new();
8757        loop {
8758            let next: BTreeSet<DetPid> = self
8759                .thread_tree
8760                .process_wait
8761                .keys()
8762                .copied()
8763                .filter(|child| self.child_is_stuck(hb, *child, &stuck))
8764                .collect();
8765            if next == stuck {
8766                break;
8767            }
8768            stuck = next;
8769        }
8770        self.blocked
8771            .child_waiters
8772            .values()
8773            .all(|(parent, spec)| self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, &stuck))
8774    }
8775
8776    /// True when the child wait of `parent` with `spec` has at least one
8777    /// matching child and every matching child is in `stuck`.
8778    fn child_wait_is_stuck(
8779        &self,
8780        parent: DetPid,
8781        spec: ChildWaitSpec,
8782        stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>,
8783    ) -> bool {
8784        let mut children = self
8785            .thread_tree
8786            .process_wait
8787            .keys()
8788            .copied()
8789            .filter(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
8790            .peekable();
8791        children.peek().is_some() && children.all(|child| stuck.contains(&child))
8792    }
8793
8794    /// True when process `child` can run again only after some other thread
8795    /// does, given the processes already known to be `stuck`
8796    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`]).
8797    fn child_is_stuck(
8798        &self,
8799        hb: Option<&HbRuntime>,
8800        child: DetPid,
8801        stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>,
8802    ) -> bool {
8803        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(child.as_raw());
8804        // A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is killed by the
8805        // kernel when its parent thread exits, at a moment set by host
8806        // timing. The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the
8807        // caller's committed turn and never forgotten, so such a process
8808        // never counts as stuck (the second Claude re-check of
8809        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013). Another host-timed
8810        // signal is held off the stuck thread's wait, so it cannot end it
8811        // under Hermit; Linux would deliver a parent-death SIGTERM to a
8812        // paused child, which Hermit holds (a hang before
8813        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430, a deadlock report
8814        // since; https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440).
8815        if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child)
8816            || self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&child)
8817            || !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&leader)
8818            || self.host_timed_signals(leader) & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) != 0
8819        {
8820            return false;
8821        }
8822        // The thread tree keeps every thread a process ever had. A thread no
8823        // longer registered that left by its own committed exit is gone
8824        // harmlessly; one that left any other way died of a signal or with its
8825        // process, so the process is going down and its wait is real. The
8826        // dying thread's deregistration is ordered (the scheduler waits for a
8827        // running thread to quiesce); the held thread's is not, so only the
8828        // dying sibling can tell.
8829        let (live, gone): (Vec<DetTid>, Vec<DetTid>) = self
8830            .thread_tree
8831            .my_thread_group(&leader)
8832            .into_iter()
8833            .partition(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
8834        gone.iter().all(|tid| self.committed_exits.contains(tid))
8835            && !live.is_empty()
8836            && live.iter().all(|tid| {
8837                hb.is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(tid))
8838                    || self.parked_futex_waiter(*tid).is_some()
8839                    || self
8840                        .blocked
8841                        .timed_waiters
8842                        .thread_deadline(*tid)
8843                        .is_some_and(|deadline| deadline.is_indefinite())
8844                    || self
8845                        .blocked
8846                        .child_waiters
8847                        .get(tid)
8848                        .is_some_and(|(parent, spec)| {
8849                            self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, stuck)
8850                        })
8851            })
8852    }
8853
8854    pub fn ready_child_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> Option<DetPid> {
8855        self.logically_exited_processes
8856            .iter()
8857            .copied()
8858            .find(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
8859    }
8860
8861    pub fn has_child_wait_target(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
8862        self.thread_tree
8863            .process_wait
8864            .keys()
8865            .copied()
8866            .any(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, spec))
8867    }
8868
8869    /// Whether `process` exited and no wait has consumed it yet: a zombie.
8870    /// Linux still signals a zombie successfully, discarding the signal.
8871    #[cfg(test)]
8872    pub fn process_is_unreaped_zombie(&self, process: DetPid) -> bool {
8873        self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process)
8874    }
8875
8876    pub fn consume_child_wait(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> bool {
8877        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
8878            return false;
8879        }
8880        self.wake_child_waiters(parent, child);
8881        self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&child);
8882        self.sigkilled_processes.remove(&child);
8883        self.thread_tree.process_parent.remove(&child);
8884        self.thread_tree.process_wait.remove(&child);
8885        self.thread_tree.child_subreapers.remove(&child);
8886        self.thread_tree.init_orphans.remove(&child);
8887        self.thread_tree.granted_exits.remove(&child);
8888        self.autoreaped_exits.remove(&child);
8889        self.logically_exited_processes.remove(&child)
8890    }
8891
8892    fn wake_child_waiters(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) {
8893        let waiters: Vec<DetTid> = self
8894            .blocked
8895            .child_waiters
8896            .iter()
8897            .filter_map(|(dettid, (wait_parent, spec))| {
8898                (*wait_parent == parent && self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, *spec))
8899                    .then_some(*dettid)
8900            })
8901            .collect();
8902        for dettid in waiters {
8903            self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(&dettid);
8904            debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid));
8905            self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
8906        }
8907    }
8908
8909    fn wake_physical_child_waiters(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
8910        if let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.remove(&child) {
8911            for dettid in waiters {
8912                self.blocked.physical_child_ready.insert(dettid);
8913                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) && !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
8914                    self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
8915                }
8916            }
8917        }
8918    }
8919
8920    /// Whether Linux still has the process `leader`: from its creation until
8921    /// it is reaped, a zombie included, as `/proc` lists it
8922    /// (`Self::procfs_listing`). Its wait record can outlive it: an
8923    /// automatically reaped child, an orphan the namespace's init reaped, or
8924    /// a process with no guest parent, which Hermit itself reaps, is gone at
8925    /// its exit (`Self::exited_process_is_zombie`).
8926    pub fn process_exists(&self, leader: DetPid) -> bool {
8927        self.thread_tree.process_wait.contains_key(&leader)
8928            && match self.exited_process_is_zombie(leader) {
8929                None => true,
8930                Some(zombie) => zombie && self.thread_tree.parent_process(&leader).is_some(),
8931            }
8932    }
8933
8934    /// The process group (`session` false) or session (`session` true) of the
8935    /// task with id `pid`, as `getpgid` and `getsid` answer it: a live
8936    /// non-leader thread's id names its process, and an id Linux no longer
8937    /// has (an exited thread, a process that is gone, `Self::process_exists`)
8938    /// names nothing. Pid 1 is the namespace's init, Hermit's own process
8939    /// unless a guest holds it, whose group and session come from outside the
8940    /// namespace and read as 0, as `/proc` lists it.
8941    pub fn group_or_session_of(&self, pid: DetPid, session: bool) -> Option<DetPid> {
8942        let Some(process) = self.signal_target_process(pid) else {
8943            return (pid.as_raw() == 1).then_some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE);
8944        };
8945        if !self.process_exists(process) {
8946            return None;
8947        }
8948        if session {
8949            self.thread_tree.session(process)
8950        } else {
8951            self.thread_tree.process_group(process)
8952        }
8953    }
8954
8955    /// Linux's answer to `setsid()` by `process` (`ThreadTree::setsid_decision`),
8956    /// counting only processes Linux still has (`Self::process_exists`).
8957    pub fn setsid_decision(&self, process: DetPid) -> Result<(), Errno> {
8958        self.thread_tree
8959            .setsid_decision(process, &|pid| !self.process_exists(pid))
8960    }
8961
8962    /// Linux's answer to `setpgid(pid, pgid)` by `caller`
8963    /// (`ThreadTree::setpgid_decision`), naming and counting only tasks Linux
8964    /// still has.
8965    pub fn setpgid_decision(
8966        &self,
8967        caller: DetPid,
8968        pid: libc::pid_t,
8969        pgid: libc::pid_t,
8970    ) -> Result<(DetPid, DetPid), Errno> {
8971        self.thread_tree.setpgid_decision(
8972            caller,
8973            pid,
8974            pgid,
8975            &|pid| !self.process_exists(pid),
8976            &|tid| {
8977                !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&tid)
8978                    && self.signal_target_process(tid).is_some()
8979            },
8980        )
8981    }
8982
8983    /// The exit state of `detpid` as a signal sees it: `Some(true)` for a
8984    /// zombie, which has exited but whose status its parent can still wait
8985    /// for, so Linux still finds it and a signal to it succeeds;
8986    /// `Some(false)` for an exited process that is already gone (its parent
8987    /// reaped it automatically at exit, or it went to the container's init,
8988    /// which reaps it); `None` for a process not known to have exited
8989    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091>).
8990    pub fn exited_process_is_zombie(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<bool> {
8991        if !self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&detpid) {
8992            return None;
8993        }
8994        Some(!self.autoreaped_exits.contains(&detpid) && !self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(detpid))
8995    }
8996
8997    /// The process a process-directed signal naming `detpid` goes to. Linux's
8998    /// kill_pid_info looks the id up as a task, so a live non-leader thread's
8999    /// id names its whole thread group (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4094>).
9000    /// `None` when the id names neither a thread group nor a live thread: the
9001    /// id of an exited thread names nothing.
9002    pub fn signal_target_process(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
9003        if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
9004            return Some(detpid);
9005        }
9006        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&detpid) {
9007            return None;
9008        }
9009        self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&detpid).copied()
9010    }
9011
9012    /// What the `sigev_notify_thread_id` `named` of a `timer_create` in
9013    /// `process` names. Linux's `good_sigevent` accepts only a task of the
9014    /// caller's thread group, found by its pid in the caller's namespace, so
9015    /// anything else (no such task, another process, one of Hermit's own
9016    /// threads, which no guest group holds) is EINVAL
9017    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164>). A caller in a nested
9018    /// PID namespace names a pid of that namespace, which is not a DetTid.
9019    pub fn posix_timer_thread(&self, process: DetPid, named: i32) -> PosixTimerThread {
9020        if self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(process) > 0 {
9021            return PosixTimerThread::NestedNamespace;
9022        }
9023        if named <= 0 {
9024            return PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup;
9025        }
9026        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(named);
9027        if self.signal_target_process(thread) == Some(process) {
9028            PosixTimerThread::Thread(thread)
9029        } else {
9030            PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup
9031        }
9032    }
9033
9034    /// What the positive `pid`, named by the nested thread `caller` in its own
9035    /// PID namespace, names (`PidNamespaces::resolve_for`). For a task of the
9036    /// caller's own namespace's init, the answer carries the signals that init
9037    /// catches, read from a live thread of it in the caller's turn. The init's
9038    /// dispositions change only through its own scheduled `rt_sigaction`
9039    /// calls, with one exception: an `SA_RESETHAND` handler's reset at a
9040    /// delivery to a thread blocked outside the schedule (external I/O, a real
9041    /// `rt_sigsuspend`) happens at a host-timed moment.
9042    pub fn guest_pid(&self, caller: DetTid, pid: i32) -> pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer {
9043        use pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer;
9044        let answer = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.resolve_for(caller, pid);
9045        let GuestPidAnswer::Task { task, .. } = answer else {
9046            return answer;
9047        };
9048        let process = self.thread_tree.process_of(task).unwrap_or(task);
9049        let own_namespace = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(caller);
9050        if own_namespace != Some(process) || !self.thread_tree.is_pid_namespace_init(process) {
9051            return answer;
9052        }
9053        let Some(thread) = self.process_signal_targets(process).into_iter().next() else {
9054            return answer;
9055        };
9056        match crate::syscalls::read_kernel_signal_state(
9057            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
9058            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
9059        ) {
9060            Ok(state) => GuestPidAnswer::Task {
9061                task,
9062                own_init_caught: Some(state.caught),
9063            },
9064            Err(errno) => GuestPidAnswer::Untranslatable(format!(
9065                "cannot read the dispositions of PID namespace init {process}: {errno}"
9066            )),
9067        }
9068    }
9069
9070    pub fn process_signal_targets(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
9071        let Some(leader) = self.signal_target_process(detpid) else {
9072            return Vec::new();
9073        };
9074        let mut targets = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&leader);
9075        targets.retain(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
9076        targets.sort();
9077        targets
9078    }
9079
9080    fn wake_timed_event(&mut self, time_ns: LogicalTime, dettid: DetTid) {
9081        let futex_timed_out = {
9082            let next_turn = self
9083                .next_turns
9084                .get(&dettid)
9085                .expect("internal invariant broken");
9086            is_futex_request(next_turn)
9087        };
9088        if futex_timed_out {
9089            assert!(self.remove_futex_waiter(&dettid));
9090            assert!(self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid));
9091        }
9092
9093        if enabled!(Level::TRACE) {
9094            if futex_timed_out {
9095                info!(
9096                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}, committed time {}) - futex wait timed out!",
9097                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
9098                );
9099            } else {
9100                info!(
9101                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}) jumping back to the head of it's priority at global(committed) time {}",
9102                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
9103                );
9104            }
9105        }
9106        self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
9107    }
9108
9109    /// Send a signal to the guest. A scheduler-parked thread is made runnable immediately. SaBRe
9110    /// external syscalls remain blocked until the signal interrupts them and their real
9111    /// continuation RPC becomes visible; other backends retain their existing immediate requeue.
9112    /// `info`, when there is one, is the raw siginfo sent in place of the
9113    /// kernel's `SI_USER` (it must carry a negative `si_code`).
9114    #[cfg(test)]
9115    fn signal_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal, info: Option<[u8; 128]>) {
9116        self.send_guest_signal(
9117            dettid,
9118            signal,
9119            None,
9120            info,
9121            dettid,
9122            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(None),
9123        );
9124    }
9125
9126    /// [`Self::signal_guest`], or with `thread_of: Some(process)` a
9127    /// thread-directed send to `dettid` of `process`. A thread's pidfd
9128    /// (PIDFD_THREAD) sends thread-directed either way; without one,
9129    /// `kill(2)` would queue the signal for the whole process even when it
9130    /// names a non-leader thread, so a thread-directed send uses `tgkill(2)`.
9131    /// Only a process-directed copy enters the record of scheduler signals
9132    /// left in the shared queue (`undelivered_scheduler_signals`): a
9133    /// thread-directed one waits in its thread's own queue, where the sender's
9134    /// check of its own pending set sees it.
9135    ///
9136    /// The send is classified against `named`, the task Linux names
9137    /// (`discarded_when_sent_to`), and recorded once it succeeds
9138    /// (`discard_note_send`), with the actual timer source `producer`. A
9139    /// discarded send commits no wake (`wake_signaled_guest_as`).
9140    fn send_guest_signal(
9141        &mut self,
9142        dettid: DetTid,
9143        signal: Signal,
9144        thread_of: Option<DetPid>,
9145        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
9146        named: DetTid,
9147        fate: discarded_at_send::SendFate,
9148    ) {
9149        debug!(
9150            "[dtid {}] deliver signal {} physically to guest thread.",
9151            dettid, signal
9152        );
9153        #[cfg(test)]
9154        if self.test_guest_sends_land {
9155            self.guest_send_landed = Some(true);
9156            return;
9157        }
9158        // A thread's pidfd sends thread-directed either way.
9159        let queue = if thread_of.is_some() || self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&dettid) {
9160            discarded_at_send::QueueId::Thread(dettid)
9161        } else {
9162            discarded_at_send::QueueId::Process(self.sigchld_process(dettid))
9163        };
9164        let token = self.models_signal_targets.then(|| match fate {
9165            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(_) => {
9166                self.discard_pre_send(named, queue, signal as libc::c_int, None)
9167            }
9168            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Kept => {
9169                self.discard_kept_token(queue, signal as libc::c_int)
9170            }
9171        });
9172        // An ordinary send's record joins its list (A1): the siginfo it
9173        // carries, or Linux's `SI_KERNEL` for the scheduler's own signal
9174        // (`SEND_SIG_PRIV`). A timer entry's own record does not.
9175        let record = match fate {
9176            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(_) => Some(
9177                info.as_ref()
9178                    .map(signal_lists::KernelSiginfo::from_user)
9179                    .unwrap_or_else(|| {
9180                        signal_lists::ordinary_siginfo(signal as libc::c_int, 0x80, 0, 0)
9181                    }),
9182            ),
9183            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Kept => None,
9184        };
9185        // Unit tests capture the send, as if it landed.
9186        #[cfg(test)]
9187        if let Some(sent) = self.test_sent_signals.as_mut() {
9188            sent.push((
9189                dettid,
9190                signal as libc::c_int,
9191                info.as_ref().map(signal_lists::KernelSiginfo::from_user),
9192                thread_of,
9193            ));
9194            if let Some(token) = token {
9195                self.discard_note_fate(token, fate, record);
9196            }
9197            self.guest_send_landed = Some(true);
9198            if self.send_wakes(dettid) {
9199                self.test_send_wakes.push(dettid);
9200            }
9201            return;
9202        }
9203        // Whether a SIGCHLD is already pending in the shared queue, read before
9204        // the send: no guest thread holds the turn at a committed send, so
9205        // only a host-timed copy could change it (`fire_process_timer`).
9206        let sigchld_pending_before = signal == Signal::SIGCHLD
9207            && thread_of.is_none()
9208            && self.models_signal_targets
9209            && self
9210                .read_shared_pending(dettid)
9211                .is_some_and(|pending| pending & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) != 0);
9212        let info_ptr = info.as_ref().map_or(std::ptr::null(), |bytes| {
9213            bytes.as_ptr().cast::<libc::siginfo_t>()
9214        });
9215        let result = if let Some((_, _, _, pidfd)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid) {
9216            let rc = unsafe {
9217                libc::syscall(
9218                    libc::SYS_pidfd_send_signal,
9219                    pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
9220                    signal as libc::c_int,
9221                    info_ptr,
9222                    0,
9223                )
9224            };
9225            if rc < 0 {
9226                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
9227            } else {
9228                Ok(())
9229            }
9230        } else if self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
9231            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
9232                format!(
9233                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot deliver signal {} to dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
9234                    signal, dettid,
9235                )
9236            });
9237            self.guest_send_landed = Some(false);
9238            return;
9239        } else if let Some(process) = thread_of {
9240            // With a siginfo (a POSIX timer's `SI_TIMER` record), the
9241            // thread-directed form that carries it.
9242            let rc = unsafe {
9243                if info.is_some() {
9244                    libc::syscall(
9245                        libc::SYS_rt_tgsigqueueinfo,
9246                        process.as_raw(),
9247                        dettid.as_raw(),
9248                        signal as libc::c_int,
9249                        info_ptr,
9250                    )
9251                } else {
9252                    libc::syscall(
9253                        libc::SYS_tgkill,
9254                        process.as_raw(),
9255                        dettid.as_raw(),
9256                        signal as libc::c_int,
9257                    )
9258                }
9259            };
9260            if rc < 0 {
9261                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
9262            } else {
9263                Ok(())
9264            }
9265        } else if info.is_some() {
9266            let rc = unsafe {
9267                libc::syscall(
9268                    libc::SYS_rt_sigqueueinfo,
9269                    dettid.as_raw(),
9270                    signal as libc::c_int,
9271                    info_ptr,
9272                )
9273            };
9274            if rc < 0 {
9275                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
9276            } else {
9277                Ok(())
9278            }
9279        } else {
9280            let pid = Pid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()); // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
9281            signal::kill(pid, signal)
9282        };
9283        if result.is_ok()
9284            && let Some(token) = token
9285        {
9286            self.discard_note_fate(token, fate, record);
9287        }
9288        match result {
9289            Ok(()) if thread_of.is_none() => {
9290                if !self.note_group_send(dettid, signal, sigchld_pending_before) {
9291                    return;
9292                }
9293            }
9294            Ok(()) => {}
9295            // ⚠️ ESRCH IS AN EXPECTED OUTCOME HERE, NOT AN ERROR. The target
9296            // chose to exit between the moment it was selected and the moment
9297            // the signal was sent; that window is inherent and cannot be closed
9298            // by locking, because the thread's exit is the guest's decision.
9299            // There is no one left to signal and nothing left to wake, so the
9300            // correct behaviour is to say so and carry on.
9301            //
9302            // This is NOT a retry and NOT a widened catch: exactly ESRCH is
9303            // absorbed, and every other errno still panics, because a signal
9304            // rejected for any other reason means the scheduler's model of the
9305            // guest is wrong and continuing would compound it.
9306            //
9307            // WHY IT MATTERED. Before this, the unconditional `expect` turned
9308            // that ordinary race into a panic on the scheduler task -- and a
9309            // panicking scheduler does not fail the run, it HANGS it, because
9310            // every guest thread is waiting on a task that no longer exists.
9311            // Measured 2026-08-25: `hermit --backend kvm run --strict --verify`
9312            // on a bash process-substitution pipeline ran 420 s with empty
9313            // stdout and never exited. The pipeline's short-lived subshells hit
9314            // this window repeatedly. Found only once the 22 `run_kvm_` cli
9315            // tests were scheduled; nothing had ever run them.
9316            Err(nix::errno::Errno::ESRCH) => {
9317                info!(
9318                    "[dtid {}] signal {} not delivered: the thread exited before it landed. \
9319                     Expected race; nothing to deliver and nothing to wake.",
9320                    dettid, signal
9321                );
9322                self.guest_send_landed = Some(false);
9323                return;
9324            }
9325            Err(errno) => panic!("signal::kill to go through, got {errno}"),
9326        }
9327        let discarded = token.is_some_and(|token| token.discarded);
9328        if discarded {
9329            info!(
9330                "[dtid {}] signal {} is one Linux discards as sent to {}; committing no wake.",
9331                dettid, signal, named
9332            );
9333        }
9334        self.guest_send_landed = Some(true);
9335        if !self.send_wakes(dettid) {
9336            return;
9337        }
9338        self.wake_signaled_guest_as(dettid, signal, discarded);
9339    }
9340
9341    /// Whether a scheduler send to `dettid` wakes it. The thread whose own
9342    /// message caused the send (a promotion at its delivery stop or take, an
9343    /// exec re-send, `signal_control_caller`) is running, not parked: it
9344    /// meets the signal when it resumes, and a wake would assert that it is
9345    /// parked.
9346    fn send_wakes(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
9347        self.signal_control_caller != Some(dettid)
9348    }
9349
9350    /// Record a process-directed `signal` the scheduler just sent `dettid`
9351    /// at a committed point (`send_guest_signal`), with
9352    /// `sigchld_pending_before` whether a `SIGCHLD` was already pending in
9353    /// the process's shared queue. Returns whether the send can wake a thread
9354    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`): not a `SIGCHLD` that coalesced.
9355    fn note_group_send(
9356        &mut self,
9357        dettid: DetTid,
9358        signal: Signal,
9359        sigchld_pending_before: bool,
9360    ) -> bool {
9361        self.note_scheduler_signal_sent(dettid, signal as libc::c_int);
9362        // `kill` is a group send, into the process's shared queue: the
9363        // child-exit ledger's send window (`take_window`).
9364        if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD
9365            && self.models_signal_targets
9366            && !self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&dettid)
9367        {
9368            let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
9369            let child = self.sending_child_exit.take();
9370            if self.sigchld_window_usable(process) {
9371                let coalesced =
9372                    sigchld_pending_before && self.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(process);
9373                if self.sending_parent_death {
9374                    self.child_exit_sigchld.note_parent_death_send(process);
9375                } else {
9376                    self.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(process, child);
9377                }
9378                // Linux does not queue a standard signal already pending
9379                // (`legacy_queue`), so this send never reaches
9380                // `complete_signal`: it wakes no thread. Waking `dettid` would
9381                // interrupt a wait Linux leaves asleep, and marking it a taker
9382                // would hand it the copy that the first send's thread takes
9383                // (the Codex review of
9384                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Only where
9385                // the window holds a send and the queue shows the copy: the
9386                // two agree unless one is stale, and then the thread is woken,
9387                // as before.
9388                if coalesced {
9389                    info!(
9390                        "[dtid {}] SIGCHLD coalesced into the one pending in its process's shared queue; waking no thread.",
9391                        dettid
9392                    );
9393                    return false;
9394                }
9395            }
9396        }
9397        true
9398    }
9399
9400    /// Record `signal`, just sent at a committed point, for a thread still
9401    /// stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask does not
9402    /// block it (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`). A later signal
9403    /// of the same kind adds nothing: either one wakes the call.
9404    fn note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
9405        let Some(Some(Ok(request))) = self.next_turns.get(&dettid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read())
9406        else {
9407            return;
9408        };
9409        let suspends = request
9410            .resources
9411            .keys()
9412            .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)));
9413        let unblocked = matches!(
9414            request.blocked_signal_mask,
9415            Some(mask) if mask & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) == 0
9416        );
9417        if suspends && unblocked {
9418            self.blocked
9419                .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
9420                .entry(dettid)
9421                .or_insert(signal);
9422        }
9423    }
9424
9425    /// `wake_signaled_guest` for a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
9426    /// the run queue (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers` or `external_io_blockers`) on a
9427    /// traced backend, just sent `signal` at a committed point.
9428    ///
9429    /// Linux wakes a thread sleeping interruptibly when a signal it does not
9430    /// block is queued for it, and a traced thread is never spared one at
9431    /// generation (`sig_ignored` is false under ptrace), so it stops for
9432    /// delivery and the backend posts its `InboundSignal` continuation. Such a
9433    /// thread is armed for the release barrier
9434    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), which requeues it at the top of
9435    /// the next pass once that continuation is posted. A `SIGCHLD` target is
9436    /// also marked `sigchld_ready`, so its delivery commits rather than being
9437    /// deferred behind runnable siblings.
9438    ///
9439    /// Not armed, and left in its pool for `step2c` exactly as before, is a
9440    /// thread the signal does not wake at a known point: a vfork parent (it
9441    /// sleeps killable, so a non-fatal signal does not wake it) and a thread
9442    /// whose recorded sleeping mask is unknown or blocks the signal.
9443    fn arm_signaled_background(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
9444        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw());
9445        let wakes = !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&dettid)
9446            && matches!(
9447                self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&dettid),
9448                Some(Some(mask)) if mask & bit == 0
9449            );
9450        if !wakes {
9451            debug!(
9452                "[dtid {}] signal {} does not wake its background call at a known point; leaving it to step2c.",
9453                dettid, signal
9454            );
9455            return;
9456        }
9457        info!(
9458            "[dtid {}] signal {} armed signaled background thread; awaiting its continuation.",
9459            dettid, signal
9460        );
9461        self.blocked.signaled_background.insert(dettid);
9462        if signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
9463            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
9464        }
9465    }
9466
9467    /// Wake a scheduler-parked target after another guest has successfully
9468    /// queued a physical signal for it. The signal itself is not sent here;
9469    /// this only prevents an internal polling request from hiding a pending
9470    /// signal indefinitely.
9471    ///
9472    /// `signal` is the raw number (`SigWrapper`), so a realtime signal, which
9473    /// `nix`'s `Signal` cannot name, arms and notes a thread like a standard one
9474    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941>).
9475    fn wake_signaled_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: impl Into<SigWrapper>) {
9476        self.wake_signaled_guest_as(dettid, signal, false);
9477    }
9478
9479    /// [`Self::wake_signaled_guest`] for a send Linux `discarded`
9480    /// (`discarded_when_sent_to`): every branch that commits an
9481    /// `InboundSignal`, or counts the signal as committed, is skipped (an
9482    /// internal-IO poll, a queued sleep and its `woken_sleeps`, a drain-woken
9483    /// futex waiter's `scheduler_sent`, a parked futex waiter, whatever its own
9484    /// filter says, and a parked sleep or `waitid`). The physical copy still
9485    /// wakes a thread blocked outside the schedule or in a filed
9486    /// `rt_sigsuspend`, so `note_signaled_sigsuspend_request` and
9487    /// `arm_signaled_background` still fix where its continuation rejoins
9488    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293>).
9489    fn wake_signaled_guest_as(
9490        &mut self,
9491        dettid: DetTid,
9492        signal: impl Into<SigWrapper>,
9493        discarded: bool,
9494    ) {
9495        let signal = signal.into();
9496        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
9497            return;
9498        }
9499        // A thread whose exit waits for a sibling's delivery permit
9500        // (`exits_awaiting_permit`) has already made its exit call, and Linux
9501        // runs an exit to completion: a signal sent to an exiting thread is
9502        // never delivered to it, and process-directed signals pass it by
9503        // (`thread_status` reports it gone, so no target selection picks it).
9504        // Its retained `Exit` request is left as it is, and the permit's
9505        // release re-admits it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4367).
9506        // Before, it was found in no pool, and the send panicked.
9507        if self.parked.exits_awaiting_permit.contains(&dettid) {
9508            debug!(
9509                "[dtid {}] signal {} not woken: the thread is exiting.",
9510                dettid, signal
9511            );
9512            return;
9513        }
9514        // The physical send has already happened. Preserve its real kernel
9515        // pending/ignored semantics, but never invent an interrupted sleep
9516        // for an alarm this exact owner snapshot blocks or ignores. This
9517        // covers both filed requests and sleeps already outside the queue.
9518        if signal.raw() == libc::SIGALRM
9519            && self
9520                .in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(dettid)
9521                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| {
9522                    snapshot.blocked
9523                        || snapshot.disposition
9524                            == crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Ignored
9525                })
9526        {
9527            return;
9528        }
9529        debug!(
9530            "[dtid {}] make pending signal {} visible to the scheduler.",
9531            dettid, signal
9532        );
9533        // `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` joins `external_io_blockers` here per main's
9534        // rt_sigsuspend work; both mean the thread is parked outside the
9535        // scheduler and must await its own continuation.
9536        let has_external_blocker = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
9537            || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid);
9538        if self.models_signal_targets && !has_external_blocker {
9539            self.note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(dettid, signal);
9540        }
9541        let await_external_continuation =
9542            self.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls && has_external_blocker;
9543        // Where the scheduler models signal targets (`models_signal_targets`),
9544        // such a thread awaits its own continuation too. Its request was
9545        // consumed when it was backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited
9546        // for it; the scheduler orders the continuation the signal provokes
9547        // instead.
9548        if self.models_signal_targets && has_external_blocker && !await_external_continuation {
9549            self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
9550            return;
9551        }
9552        // A scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
9553        // DBT, KVM) has nothing to arm, and the thread still runs its call
9554        // outside the scheduler. Its request was consumed when it was
9555        // backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited for it either: it
9556        // rejoins through its own continuation (`BlockedExternalContinue`),
9557        // and the physical signal has already reached it. Before, a debug
9558        // build asserted below and a release build counterfeited a request
9559        // for a thread still in its pool, as
9560        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146 found for the traced
9561        // backend. In-guest LiteInst reached this when a vfork child's exit
9562        // signalled its parent, which the child had just killed, before the
9563        // parent's death was retired; host load widens that window.
9564        if has_external_blocker {
9565            return;
9566        }
9567        if cfg!(debug_assertions) && !await_external_continuation {
9568            let nxtturn = self
9569                .next_turns
9570                .get(&dettid)
9571                .expect("internal invariant broken");
9572            assert!(
9573                nxtturn.req.is_full(),
9574                "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler"
9575            );
9576        }
9577        if await_external_continuation || discarded {
9578            return;
9579        }
9580
9581        // A thread whose `SIGCHLD` delivery is deferred (`sigchld_deferred`)
9582        // is in the middle of that delivery, waiting for its turn, and the
9583        // kernel delivers the new signal after it. So the delivery is
9584        // re-admitted at this committed point, as step 2e would, and placed
9585        // (`sigchld_ready`) at the front of its band, with its request
9586        // untouched. Left deferred, a sibling that never stops running held
9587        // back both signals for ever (the Codex review of the fix of
9588        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4229). Before that,
9589        // `thread_status` found it in no pool and reported it gone, and the
9590        // send panicked.
9591        if self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.remove(&dettid) {
9592            info!(
9593                "[dtid {}] signal {} re-admits its deferred SIGCHLD delivery.",
9594                dettid, signal
9595            );
9596            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
9597            self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
9598            return;
9599        }
9600        // Now that the thread is signaled, it needs to be runnable for the scheduler to continue it.
9601        match self.thread_status(dettid) {
9602            ThreadStatus::Gone => {
9603                panic!(
9604                    "signal_guest: should not have just delivered a signal to a nonexistent thread..."
9605                );
9606            }
9607            ThreadStatus::Running => {
9608                let is_internal_io_polling = self
9609                    .next_turns
9610                    .get(&dettid)
9611                    .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
9612                    .is_some_and(|request| {
9613                        request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
9614                            resources
9615                                .resources
9616                                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
9617                        })
9618                    });
9619
9620                // A `pause` or `nanosleep` filed but not yet parked is still
9621                // queued. Granting it would park the thread with the signal
9622                // already gone by, and a pause would then never return: the run
9623                // ended in a false deadlock where Linux returns from the call
9624                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126). It is woken
9625                // as one already parked is (`NotRunning` below), at the front of
9626                // its band; its own turn decides whether the signal ends it
9627                // (`sleep_signal`): only if it is still pending for this thread,
9628                // unblocked, and caught or fatal. Only where the
9629                // backend reports the guest's signal state (`signal_sleep`):
9630                // elsewhere a woken sleep cannot tell, and every wake ends it.
9631                // A `nanosleep` whose deadline has passed completes at its
9632                // admission instead, as a parked one does at its timed pop.
9633                let is_queued_sleep = match self.signal_sleep(dettid) {
9634                    Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Pause) => true,
9635                    Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Nanosleep { deadline }) => {
9636                        deadline > self.committed_time
9637                    }
9638                    None => false,
9639                };
9640                if is_internal_io_polling {
9641                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
9642                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
9643                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
9644                    // At the front of its band and placed, as a parked futex
9645                    // waiter: the poller is the thread the scheduler chose to
9646                    // take the signal (the Claude review of
9647                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304).
9648                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
9649                    self.mark_placed_delivery(dettid, signal, woken);
9650                } else if is_queued_sleep && self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
9651                    // Read before the wake replaces the sleep request.
9652                    let ends = self.scheduler_sigchld_ends_sleep(dettid, signal);
9653                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
9654                    // The child-exit timer may already have marked the real
9655                    // delivery as placed (`sigchld_ready`); the requeue clears
9656                    // that mark, and the delivery after this wake needs it, or
9657                    // it is deferred behind any runnable sibling.
9658                    let delivery_placed = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&dettid);
9659                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
9660                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
9661                    // At the front of its band, as a cross-task signal requeues
9662                    // a sleep (`drain_sleep_signals`): the woken thread is the
9663                    // next to resume, so it is the one that dequeues a
9664                    // process-directed signal the kernel could not give a
9665                    // ptrace-stopped thread. Behind a running sibling, the
9666                    // sibling took the handler while the sleep still answered
9667                    // EINTR.
9668                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
9669                    if delivery_placed {
9670                        self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
9671                    }
9672                    // Resumed first, as a woken futex waiter is: at the front of
9673                    // its band it still followed a sibling of a higher band or a
9674                    // chaos draw, which took the process-directed copy
9675                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333). Only
9676                    // when the signal will end the sleep in its own turn: a sleep
9677                    // that parks again keeps no mark.
9678                    self.mark_woken_sleep_taker(dettid, signal, woken && ends);
9679                    // Granted at its turn without consuming `sigchld_ready`
9680                    // (`woken_sleeps`): deferred, a `nanosleep` the
9681                    // signal does not end never reached its deadline while a
9682                    // sibling kept running (the Codex review of
9683                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
9684                    self.blocked.woken_sleeps.insert(dettid);
9685                } else if let Some(woken) = self.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.get_mut(&dettid) {
9686                    // A futex waiter or poll the drain woke, still to run its
9687                    // turn: a `SIGCHLD` sent now at this commit point is
9688                    // committed to it, which the drain's own `SIGCHLD` is not
9689                    // (`drain_woken_waiters`). Its turn answers with it.
9690                    if signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
9691                        woken.scheduler_sent = true;
9692                    }
9693                }
9694                // TODO(T137242449): other runnable requests could be reprioritized to run
9695                // sooner, but for now we leave their priorities alone.
9696            }
9697            ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
9698                // This is a commit point. The only callers are a timed pop in
9699                // step2b (`dispatch_timed_signal` -> `fire_alarm` ->
9700                // `signal_guest`) or the empty-queue time skip, both on the
9701                // scheduler thread while no guest thread holds the turn. So the
9702                // dispositions read here are the ones in force at this point in
9703                // the global order, with the exceptions named at
9704                // `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`. That is where Linux
9705                // decides delivery: a caught, unblocked signal wakes the sleeper
9706                // with EINTR, and an ignored one is discarded and never wakes it.
9707                //
9708                // The woken waiter is queued to run next, so it is the first
9709                // thread to resume and dequeue the signal. Its futex handler
9710                // still checks, in its own turn, that an interrupting signal is
9711                // pending for it. If none is, because a sibling made the signal
9712                // ignored or, under a chaos schedule, resumed first and took it,
9713                // the waiter parks again with its original absolute deadline,
9714                // as a Linux waiter that the signal never reached would still be
9715                // waiting.
9716                if let Some(interrupting) =
9717                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()))
9718                {
9719                    if interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) == 0 {
9720                        // Blocked, ignored, or default-ignored for this waiter now,
9721                        // or a signal the wait holds until the call returns
9722                        // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`): the kernel
9723                        // discards an ignored signal or keeps the others pending,
9724                        // and the wait stays registered with its original
9725                        // absolute deadline. So does a default job-control stop
9726                        // that the wait defers (`FutexSignalWatch`), which the
9727                        // kernel delivers or discards when the call returns.
9728                        debug!(
9729                            "[dtid {}] signal {} does not interrupt its futex wait; leaving it parked.",
9730                            dettid, signal
9731                        );
9732                        return;
9733                    }
9734                    // The wake is committed for this signal. That commit is the
9735                    // deterministic delivery point; the woken waiter goes to the
9736                    // front of its band, so it is the next thread to resume and
9737                    // dequeue the signal (`force_unblock_thread_at`).
9738                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
9739                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
9740                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
9741                    self.mark_placed_delivery(dettid, signal, woken);
9742                    return;
9743                }
9744                // A parked `pause` or `nanosleep` woken for the scheduler's own
9745                // signal: its turn is granted at once, as a queued one's is
9746                // (`woken_sleeps`), so it decides in its own turn, not after a
9747                // sibling that never blocks. Like a woken futex waiter, it goes
9748                // to the front of its band and is resumed first for a `SIGCHLD`
9749                // (`mark_woken_sleep_taker`): behind a running sibling, the
9750                // sibling took the process-directed copy, and a `pause` that
9751                // found no signal for itself never returned
9752                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333).
9753                let parked_sleep = self.signal_sleep(dettid).is_some();
9754                let ends = parked_sleep && self.scheduler_sigchld_ends_sleep(dettid, signal);
9755                let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
9756                rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
9757                if parked_sleep {
9758                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
9759                    self.mark_woken_sleep_taker(dettid, signal, woken && ends);
9760                    self.blocked.woken_sleeps.insert(dettid);
9761                } else {
9762                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, rsrcs);
9763                }
9764            }
9765        }
9766    }
9767
9768    /// For a thread that `wake_signaled_guest` unblocked (`woken`) to take
9769    /// `signal`: a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sent it at this commit point is
9770    /// placed, so its woken turn is granted at its turn rather than deferred
9771    /// behind runnable siblings (`block_for_one_resource`), and it is a
9772    /// `sigchld_takers` thread, which step 3 resumes first. Deferred, or
9773    /// overtaken by a sibling of a higher band, a sibling resumed first and
9774    /// the kernel, which skips the ptrace-stopped waiter, gave it the signal
9775    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Marked only when the
9776    /// wake unblocked the thread: one left held (a happens-before gate) keeps
9777    /// no mark that a later, host-timed delivery could use.
9778    fn mark_placed_delivery(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper, woken: bool) {
9779        if woken && signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
9780            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
9781            self.blocked.sigchld_takers.insert(dettid);
9782        }
9783    }
9784
9785    /// For a `pause` or `nanosleep` that `wake_signaled_guest` unblocked and
9786    /// whose own turn takes the scheduler's `SIGCHLD`
9787    /// (`scheduler_sigchld_ends_sleep`, `takes`): it is a `sigchld_takers`
9788    /// thread, resumed first, as a woken futex waiter is
9789    /// (`mark_placed_delivery`). Its delivery is placed (`sigchld_ready`) only
9790    /// when the copy is committed to it (`committed_sigchld_pending`). Where
9791    /// host timing alone decides (SIGCHLD host-timed for it, with no committed
9792    /// copy), a thread outside the schedule may take the copy, no delivery
9793    /// follows the sleep's turn to consume the mark, and a later host-timed
9794    /// delivery would skip its deferral (the Codex review of the rebase of
9795    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333).
9796    fn mark_woken_sleep_taker(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper, takes: bool) {
9797        if takes && signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
9798            self.blocked.sigchld_takers.insert(dettid);
9799            if self.committed_sigchld_pending(dettid) {
9800                self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
9801            }
9802        }
9803    }
9804
9805    /// Whether a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sends `dettid` at this commit point,
9806    /// which wakes the `pause` or `nanosleep` its request is, ends that sleep in
9807    /// its own turn (`syscalls::signal::sleep_signal`). That turn ends it for a
9808    /// `SIGCHLD` it was woken for when the sleeper's mask leaves it interrupting
9809    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting`) and either the copy is committed to
9810    /// it by the schedule (`committed_sigchld_pending`, its `PlacedPending`
9811    /// answer) or `SIGCHLD` is host-timed for it, so the wake itself decides
9812    /// (`held_wake_ends_sleep`); and a `nanosleep`'s deadline must not have
9813    /// passed. Only such a sleep takes the signal. One that parks again must
9814    /// keep no `sigchld_ready` mark that a later, host-timed delivery could use
9815    /// (the Codex reviews of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333):
9816    /// a `SIGCHLD` the sleeper blocks or leaves at its ignoring default, or one
9817    /// with no committed copy (a process whose send window is unusable, a
9818    /// thread-directed send). Where the window is unusable, the sleep's own
9819    /// turn may instead claim the copy (`syscalls::signal::claim_pending_sigchld`);
9820    /// that claim places its own delivery (`ThreadState::claimed_sigchld`),
9821    /// not this mark. An unreadable state ends nothing here, so no mark
9822    /// is made. Read while no guest thread holds the turn, as
9823    /// `sleep_interrupting_signals` is. Any other signal: false, since only a
9824    /// `SIGCHLD` is marked.
9825    fn scheduler_sigchld_ends_sleep(&self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) -> bool {
9826        if signal.raw() != libc::SIGCHLD {
9827            return false;
9828        }
9829        let live = match self.signal_sleep(dettid) {
9830            Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Pause) => true,
9831            Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Nanosleep { deadline }) => {
9832                deadline > self.committed_time
9833            }
9834            None => false,
9835        };
9836        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
9837        let decided =
9838            self.host_timed_signals(dettid) & bit != 0 || self.committed_sigchld_pending(dettid);
9839        live && decided
9840            && self
9841                .read_sleeper_signal_state(dettid)
9842                .is_ok_and(|state| state.interrupting(state.blocked) & bit != 0)
9843    }
9844
9845    /// Whether `dettid`'s filed request is a `SIGCHLD` delivery
9846    /// (`InboundSignal`), or `None` while it has filed none.
9847    fn awaits_sigchld_delivery(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<bool> {
9848        let request = self.next_turns.get(&dettid)?.req.try_read()?;
9849        Some(request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
9850            resources
9851                .resources
9852                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)))
9853        }))
9854    }
9855
9856    /// The `sigchld_takers` thread step 3 resumes first, if any (see there).
9857    /// A taker leaves the set once its copy is gone from the shared queue
9858    /// (the send window is closed: it, or another thread, took it) and its
9859    /// request is not the delivery, so a stale entry cannot let a thread run
9860    /// first for ever. It is not first while its mask blocks `SIGCHLD`: it
9861    /// would not take the copy, which another thread may then take, as Linux
9862    /// retargets a shared signal.
9863    fn first_sigchld_taker(&mut self) -> Option<DetTid> {
9864        let stale: Vec<DetTid> = self
9865            .blocked
9866            .sigchld_takers
9867            .iter()
9868            .copied()
9869            .filter(|thread| {
9870                !self
9871                    .child_exit_sigchld
9872                    .window_open(self.sigchld_process(*thread))
9873                    && self.awaits_sigchld_delivery(*thread) != Some(true)
9874            })
9875            .collect();
9876        for thread in stale {
9877            self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(&thread);
9878        }
9879        let sigchld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
9880        self.blocked
9881            .sigchld_takers
9882            .iter()
9883            .find(|thread| {
9884                self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(**thread)
9885                    && self.awaits_sigchld_delivery(**thread).is_some()
9886                    && self
9887                        .thread_signal_mask(**thread)
9888                        .is_some_and(|mask| mask & sigchld == 0)
9889            })
9890            .copied()
9891    }
9892
9893    /// Classify a request that still represents the same in-flight waitid.
9894    /// A signal may arrive before its polling request is rewritten or after a prior
9895    /// notification has already materialized its scheduler wakeup.
9896    fn waitid_signal_request(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<WaitidSignalRequest> {
9897        let resources = self
9898            .next_turns
9899            .get(&dettid)
9900            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
9901            .and_then(Result::ok)?;
9902        // The two ways to be parked inside wait4/waitid: the legacy kernel
9903        // polling loop, and the scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle resource
9904        // added by the typed WaitChild work. Both must be woken; neither implies
9905        // anything about run-queue residency, which the drain decides.
9906        let waiting_on_child = resources
9907            .resources
9908            .keys()
9909            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }));
9910        let legacy_polling = resources.fyi == "waitid"
9911            && resources
9912                .resources
9913                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling);
9914        if legacy_polling || waiting_on_child {
9915            return Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked);
9916        }
9917        // Signals already materialized on this waitid request by an earlier
9918        // drain. A marked `WaitidSignals` resource instead belongs to an
9919        // interrupted InternalIOPolling request and is classified below.
9920        if resources.signal_interrupt_errno().is_some() {
9921            return None;
9922        }
9923        resources
9924            .resources
9925            .keys()
9926            .find_map(|resource| match resource {
9927                ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals) => {
9928                    Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(signals.clone()))
9929                }
9930                _ => None,
9931            })
9932    }
9933
9934    fn restartable_internal_io_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<SigWrapper>> {
