9935        if !self.backend.supports_parked_write_signal_interruption {
9936            return None;
9937        }
9938        self.next_turns
9939            .get(&dettid)
9940            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
9941            .and_then(Result::ok)
9942            .and_then(|resources| {
9943                if resources.resources.len() != 1
9944                    || resources.signal_interrupt_errno() != Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
9945                {
9946                    return None;
9947                }
9948                match resources.resources.keys().next() {
9949                    Some(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling) => Some(Vec::new()),
9950                    Some(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals)) => Some(signals.clone()),
9951                    _ => None,
9952                }
9953            })
9954    }
9955
9956    /// Whether `dettid` is asleep in a precise-mode futex wait: its request is the
9957    /// bare `FutexWait` park and it is still registered as a waiter. A waiter that
9958    /// a `FUTEX_WAKE` or its timeout already requeued is not: that outcome was
9959    /// committed first, so the wait completes with it and the kernel delivers the
9960    /// pending signal when the syscall returns, as Linux does after a wakeup.
9961    #[cfg(test)]
9962    fn is_parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
9963        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid).is_some()
9964    }
9965
9966    fn parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<&FutexWaiter> {
9967        if !self.next_turns.get(&dettid).is_some_and(is_futex_request) {
9968            return None;
9969        }
9970        self.blocked
9971            .futex_waiters
9972            .values()
9973            .find_map(|waiters| waiters.iter().find(|waiter| waiter.dettid == dettid))
9974    }
9975
9976    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter's mask leaves unblocked, when
9977    /// its backend reported them. A cross-task signal outside this set cannot
9978    /// interrupt the wait whatever the dispositions become, so it is not admitted
9979    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
9980    fn parked_futex_unblocked_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
9981        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)
9982            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
9983            .map(|watch| watch.unblocked)
9984    }
9985
9986    /// The signals that end a parked precise-mode futex waiter's wait NOW, when its
9987    /// backend reports the kernel's signal state: unblocked by its mask, and caught
9988    /// or fatal-by-default under the dispositions the kernel holds at this moment
9989    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Never `SIGCHLD`, which a
9990    /// gated wait holds until the call returns (`futex_wait_held_signals`),
9991    /// unless the scheduler sends it at this commit point (`committed`).
9992    ///
9993    /// ⚠️ CALL THIS ONLY WHERE A WAKE IS COMMITTED: the step2 drain of cross-task
9994    /// signals and the scheduler-sent signal paths in step2b and the empty-queue
9995    /// time skip. There no guest thread holds the turn: every thread the
9996    /// scheduler controls is stopped, its request filled or parked. A
9997    /// disposition changes only when a guest thread runs: `rt_sigaction` in its
9998    /// turn, or `exec`, or a fault or `SA_RESETHAND` delivery in its turn. So the
9999    /// value read here is a function of the deterministic schedule, not of when
10000    /// the host ran the read.
10001    ///
10002    /// Two kinds of thread are the exception. One blocked in a call the backend
10003    /// runs outside the scheduler (`external_io_blockers`, non-sequentialized
10004    /// IO) or in `rt_sigsuspend` (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) sits in the kernel,
10005    /// not in a ptrace stop, so a signal can be delivered to it at a host-timed
10006    /// moment. An `SA_RESETHAND` handler delivered that way resets its
10007    /// process's disposition outside any turn, and this read can race it. What
10008    /// such a race can change is bounded: a waiter woken for a signal that no
10009    /// longer interrupts it finds nothing pending when its futex handler checks
10010    /// in its own turn, and parks again with its original absolute deadline.
10011    ///
10012    /// Linux decides interruption the same way, from the disposition when the
10013    /// signal is delivered, and an ignored signal is discarded rather than ending
10014    /// the wait. A disposition changed after the wait began therefore counts: a
10015    /// signal that became caught wakes the waiter, and one that became ignored
10016    /// leaves it registered with its original absolute deadline. The earlier
10017    /// design, a disposition snapshot taken when the wait began, got both wrong:
10018    /// it could leave an untimed waiter parked forever with a ready handler, and
10019    /// it restarted a timed wait with a fresh relative timeout.
10020    ///
10021    /// A read error (the thread is gone, or the file is unparseable) falls back to
10022    /// every unblocked signal. A waiter woken that way reads its own signal state
10023    /// in its turn (`handle_futex_blocking`). If that read succeeds and finds no
10024    /// interrupting signal pending, it parks again with its original absolute
10025    /// deadline, so a false wake costs one extra turn. If that read fails too,
10026    /// it is handled as a wait's first read is (`read_wait_signal_state`): a
10027    /// thread that no longer exists ends the call with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which
10028    /// nothing observes, and otherwise the run ends with a diagnostic, never an
10029    /// errno the futex call cannot return. Leaving a waiter parked for a signal
10030    /// that does interrupt it could instead deadlock it.
10031    ///
10032    /// `committed` names a signal the scheduler sends at this commit point
10033    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, from `signal_guest`), such as a `SIGCHLD` from a
10034    /// child's child-exit timer, or from a POSIX timer whose signal is
10035    /// `SIGCHLD`: the wait does not hold it unless a
10036    /// host-timed source can post it too
10037    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). Nor does it hold a
10038    /// guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` recorded in the sender's committed
10039    /// turn (`private_sigchld`), which only this thread can take: the drain of
10040    /// that cross-task signal ends the wait as it ends a sleep
10041    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132). Only here, not in
10042    /// `futex_wait_held_signals`, which restartable internal IO polls share.
10043    fn parked_futex_interrupting_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid, committed: u64) -> Option<u64> {
10044        let watch = self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)?.signal_watch?;
10045        let held = self.futex_wait_held_signals(dettid)
10046            & !self.private_sigchld(dettid)
10047            & !(committed & !self.host_timed_signals(dettid));
10048        #[cfg(test)]
10049        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
10050            return Some(
10051                state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held,
10052            );
10053        }
10054        match read_kernel_signal_state(
10055            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.pid),
10056            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.tid),
10057        ) {
10058            Ok(state) => {
10059                Some(state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held)
10060            }
10061            Err(errno) => {
10062                debug!(
10063                    "[dtid {}] cannot read the signal state of parked futex waiter {}/{} ({}); \
10064                     treating every unblocked signal it does not hold as interrupting.",
10065                    dettid, watch.pid, watch.tid, errno
10066                );
10067                Some(watch.unblocked & !held)
10068            }
10069        }
10070    }
10071
10072    /// The signals that would interrupt the restartable internal IO poll of
10073    /// `dettid` (`restartable_internal_io_signals`), read from the thread the
10074    /// request names for `/proc` (`Resources::signal_state_task`; with none,
10075    /// no signal is filtered out). A poll that decides for itself
10076    /// (`Resources::decides_signal_interruption_itself`, a parked pipe
10077    /// `writev`, which polls with every ordinary signal blocked) is not
10078    /// passed here. The signals kept are those unblocked under its mask,
10079    /// and caught or acted on by default, as the kernel holds them now, at the
10080    /// step2 drain, with no guest thread holding the turn. `SIGCHLD` and the
10081    /// signals a host-timed source can post are held, as for a futex waiter
10082    /// (`futex_wait_held_signals`). A blocked signal must not end the poll:
10083    /// the call would return `ERESTARTSYS` with no signal for the kernel to
10084    /// deliver, and the guest would see the restart code itself
10085    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>). When the state
10086    /// cannot be read, every signal it does not hold is treated as
10087    /// interrupting, as before this filter. Where the record of copies Linux
10088    /// discarded at send is kept, a standard signal is filtered by the mask
10089    /// alone (`poll_wake_signals`).
10090    fn restartable_internal_io_interrupting_signals(
10091        &self,
10092        dettid: DetTid,
10093        task: Option<(i32, i32)>,
10094    ) -> u64 {
10095        let held = self.futex_wait_held_signals(dettid);
10096        // A guest thread ID names a host task only on a backend whose guest
10097        // runs as host tasks. Elsewhere (KVM) `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` is an
10098        // unrelated host task, if any, chosen by host thread-ID allocation, so
10099        // its state must never decide which signal ends the poll: keep every
10100        // signal the wait does not hold, and the woken call decides from the
10101        // backend's own state (a scalar pipe write checks the guest's mask and
10102        // disposition; a call with no progress returns ERESTARTSYS, which the
10103        // backend restarts unless a signal it would deliver is pending).
10104        if !crate::procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(&self.backend, None) {
10105            return !held;
10106        }
10107        // Unit tests script a thread's state; one with none scripted keeps
10108        // the unfiltered behaviour and never reads a host task's.
10109        #[cfg(test)]
10110        {
10111            let _ = task;
10112            self.test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
10113                .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10114            match self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
10115                Some(state) => poll_wake_signals(state, self.models_signal_targets) & !held,
10116                None => !held,
10117            }
10118        }
10119        #[cfg(not(test))]
10120        {
10121            let Some((pid, tid)) = task else {
10122                return !held;
10123            };
10124            match read_kernel_signal_state(reverie::Pid::from_raw(pid), reverie::Pid::from_raw(tid))
10125            {
10126                Ok(state) => poll_wake_signals(&state, self.models_signal_targets) & !held,
10127                Err(errno) => {
10128                    debug!(
10129                        "[dtid {}] cannot read the signal state of its internal IO poll ({}); \
10130                         treating every signal it does not hold as interrupting.",
10131                        dettid, errno
10132                    );
10133                    !held
10134                }
10135            }
10136        }
10137    }
10138
10139    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter holds until its call
10140    /// returns, whatever its mask and dispositions: `SIGCHLD`, whoever sent it,
10141    /// and every signal a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to its
10142    /// process (`host_timed_signals`). A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to
10143    /// the waiter at a commit point is the exception
10144    /// (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`' `committed`,
10145    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005), and so is a guest's
10146    /// thread-directed `SIGCHLD` the schedule recorded (`private_sigchld`),
10147    /// which the callers for sleeps and futex waits exempt at their own sites;
10148    /// the restartable internal IO polls that share this set do not
10149    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132). The kernel posts these at a moment set
10150    /// by host timing (`SIGCHLD` for a child's exit, stop or continue), and the
10151    /// waiter cannot tell that copy from one sent at a deterministic point. The
10152    /// guest side holds the same signals in its own checks (`KernelSignalWait`,
10153    /// and the futex pre-check in `handle_futex_blocking`)
10154    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
10155    fn futex_wait_held_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> u64 {
10156        kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | self.host_timed_signals(dettid)
10157    }
10158
10159    /// Records that `caller`, in its turn, armed a host-timed source of
10160    /// `signals`: a source the kernel fires at a moment set by host timing,
10161    /// such as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. From then on no gated wait of a process in
10162    /// `scope` ends for any of `signals`, whoever sends it
10163    /// (`host_timed_signals`). Returns what `caller`'s waits now hold.
10164    ///
10165    /// An entry is never removed: not when the guest disarms the source, nor
10166    /// at `exec`, nor when the source has fired. Hermit cannot tell a copy
10167    /// posted by the source from one a guest sends with `kill`, and a source
10168    /// that fired once may stay armed. Holding a signal too long keeps the
10169    /// behaviour gated waits had before signal interruption
10170    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>); ending a wait for a
10171    /// host-timed copy makes the run depend on host timing.
10172    ///
10173    /// The entry is keyed by the caller's process, so every thread of it is
10174    /// covered: Linux sends a parent-death signal process-directed, and the
10175    /// kernel picks the thread. A forked child starts with no entry, as it
10176    /// starts with no parent-death signal.
10177    pub fn record_host_timed_signals(
10178        &mut self,
10179        caller: DetTid,
10180        scope: HostTimedSignalScope,
10181        signals: u64,
10182    ) -> u64 {
10183        let processes = match scope {
10184            HostTimedSignalScope::Caller => {
10185                let process = self.sigchld_process(caller);
10186                *self.host_timed_signals.entry(process).or_default() |= signals;
10187                vec![process]
10188            }
10189            HostTimedSignalScope::Container => {
10190                self.host_timed_signals_everywhere |= signals;
10191                self.processes_with_timer_entries()
10192            }
10193        };
10194        // A host-timed source of a signal ends its pairs' observability,
10195        // decided in this turn, before the source can post (4262 design
10196        // §3.4, §4.11).
10197        for process in processes {
10198            for signal in (1..32).filter(|signal| signals & kernel_signal_bit(*signal) != 0) {
10199                if self.coalesces_alarms() {
10200                    self.lose_timer_observability(process, signal);
10201                }
10202            }
10203        }
10204        self.host_timed_signals(caller)
10205    }
10206
10207    /// The signals that no gated wait of `thread` ends for, because a
10208    /// host-timed source a guest armed can post them to its process
10209    /// (`record_host_timed_signals`), or a terminal the guest may have
10210    /// inherited can (`startup_host_timed_signals`). Gated waits read this in
10211    /// their own turn.
10212    pub fn host_timed_signals(&self, thread: DetTid) -> u64 {
10213        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
10214        self.host_timed_signals_everywhere
10215            | self.host_timed_signals.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
10216    }
10217
10218    // `SIGCHLD` AND GATED WAITS
10219    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146)
10220    //
10221    // A gated wait decides interruption from the kernel's pending set in
10222    // `/proc`: the precise futex pre-check and the parked waiter's wake
10223    // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`), and the polling waits that read
10224    // the kernel's signal state each turn (`KernelSignalWait`). None of them
10225    // ends for a `SIGCHLD` that only `/proc` reports. The kernel posts `SIGCHLD` to a
10226    // parent for a child's exit, stop or continue at a moment set by host
10227    // timing (under ptrace, when the tracer releases the dying child), and
10228    // `/proc` cannot tell that copy from one a guest or the scheduler sent at
10229    // a deterministic point. The signal stays pending in the kernel and is
10230    // delivered when the call returns for another reason. Linux would end the
10231    // wait; that part of the issue is given up until Reverie reports every
10232    // delivery it holds.
10233    //
10234    // The exception is a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to the thread at
10235    // a commit point through `signal_guest`, the one a child's `ChildExit`
10236    // timer sends, or a POSIX timer whose signal is `SIGCHLD`: the resume that
10237    // names it lifts the hold for that turn
10238    // alone, so the wait ends at a point the schedule fixes
10239    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). A death without that
10240    // timer (a child killed by a signal, or leaving through `exit` in its last
10241    // thread) still leaves the signal held.
10242    //
10243    // A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` (`tgkill`, `pthread_sigqueue`),
10244    // recorded in the sender's committed turn (`private_sigchld`), is the
10245    // other exception, for a `pause`, a `nanosleep` and a precise futex wait:
10246    // only the target can take that copy, so the drain of the cross-task
10247    // signal ends the wait, and a wait that checks before it parks asks the
10248    // schedule's record (`PrivatePending`, `PlacedPending`). A futex waiter's
10249    // turn after that drain is not committed the signal: its own check decides
10250    // from the record, which a flush clears (`drain_woken_waiters`). The
10251    // restartable internal IO polls and polling-mode futex waits still hold it
10252    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
10253    //
10254    // The waits of `select`, and of `pselect6` without a temporary mask, read
10255    // the same state but hold nothing (`KernelSignalWait::for_select`), so a
10256    // pending caught `SIGCHLD` still ends them at a turn host timing can
10257    // choose: a known gap that these waits had before.
10258    //
10259    // What follows models which thread of a process the kernel gives a
10260    // `SIGCHLD` that the scheduler sends for a child's exit
10261    // (`kernel_sigchld_target`), under `models_signal_targets`.
10262
10263    /// The process whose shared queue a `SIGCHLD` for `thread` joins.
10264    fn sigchld_process(&self, thread: DetTid) -> DetPid {
10265        self.registered_process(thread).unwrap_or(thread)
10266    }
10267
10268    /// The thread of `process` that the kernel gives a `SIGCHLD` queued on the
10269    /// process's shared queue, with `preferred` the thread it tries first (the
10270    /// child's creator).
10271    ///
10272    /// Linux's `complete_signal` takes `preferred` if it does not block the
10273    /// signal, and otherwise looks for another thread that does not. Under a
10274    /// tracer, a thread held in a ptrace stop does not qualify
10275    /// (`wants_signal`), and here every thread the scheduler holds is in one.
10276    /// So a thread in a real `rt_sigsuspend` (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) whose
10277    /// temporary mask does not block the signal comes first: if it is still
10278    /// asleep, the kernel queues the signal for it and wakes it. If it has
10279    /// already returned and stopped (its continuation posted), the kernel
10280    /// leaves the signal pending, and the thread takes it when it resumes:
10281    /// the temporary mask stays installed until a signal is delivered
10282    /// (`set_restore_sigmask`). Either way it is armed for the release barrier
10283    /// (`arm_signaled_background`), which admits it at the front of the run
10284    /// queue before any other thread takes a turn. Other calls outside the
10285    /// runnable set are not preferred: a `ppoll` or `pselect6` that returned
10286    /// restored the thread's own mask, which may block the signal, and a vfork
10287    /// parent's killable sleep is not woken. Only when there is no such
10288    /// `rt_sigsuspend` does the order below decide, over every thread that
10289    /// does not block the signal; when all of them are stopped, the kernel
10290    /// leaves the signal pending for whichever resumes first. The order is
10291    /// `preferred`, then the rest in thread-ID order, which stands in for the
10292    /// kernel's round-robin `curr_target`. Before, a stopped `preferred` was
10293    /// named ahead of a `sigsuspend` sibling the kernel woke: the sibling was
10294    /// not armed, so whether it took the signal before `preferred` resumed
10295    /// from a sleep that virtual time ended depended on host timing
10296    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237>). Only a chosen
10297    /// thread that sleeps outside the runnable set is woken
10298    /// (`arm_signaled_background`). A chosen parked futex waiter is not woken
10299    /// by the drain: its wait holds `SIGCHLD` until the call returns
10300    /// (`futex_wait_held_signals`), unless the `ChildExit` timer's own send
10301    /// names it (`wake_signaled_guest`).
10302    ///
10303    /// Every mask this uses is a function of the schedule, so the choice is
10304    /// too. Call this only at the step2 drain or a step2b timed pop, where no
10305    /// guest thread holds the turn. A thread then falls in one of two kinds:
10306    ///
10307    /// * One the scheduler controls is stopped at a request, filled or
10308    ///   parked. Its mask changes only when it runs, in its own turn, so the
10309    ///   mask read now is the one it stopped with.
10310    /// * One sleeping in a call outside the runnable set
10311    ///   (`external_io_blockers`, `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) is not stopped:
10312    ///   `rt_sigsuspend`, `ppoll` and `pselect6` install their temporary mask
10313    ///   after the scheduler released the thread, and a handler delivered to
10314    ///   it runs under a wider one, both at host-timed moments. Its live mask
10315    ///   is never read here; the mask recorded when the scheduler committed
10316    ///   its call is used instead (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`).
10317    ///
10318    /// A thread whose mask cannot be read is not a target, and only a thread
10319    /// that no longer exists has one: a stopped thread's `/proc` entry stays
10320    /// readable, and an out-of-scheduler thread's live mask is never read. A
10321    /// thread the guest kills is retired at the turn that kills it
10322    /// (`logically_kill_thread`), which takes it out of
10323    /// `process_signal_targets` before it dies. So an unreadable thread was
10324    /// killed from outside the container at a host-timed moment, the same
10325    /// envelope as any signal sent from outside; the kernel does not choose a
10326    /// dying thread either (`wants_signal` skips `PF_EXITING`). Returns `None`
10327    /// when every thread blocks the signal.
10328    fn kernel_sigchld_target(&self, process: DetPid, preferred: DetTid) -> Option<DetTid> {
10329        self.kernel_signal_target(process, preferred, libc::SIGCHLD)
10330    }
10331
10332    /// `kernel_sigchld_target` for any process-directed signal `signo`: an
10333    /// `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper that does not block it first, then `preferred`
10334    /// if it does not, then the first other thread that does not; `None` when
10335    /// every thread blocks it. A timer's signal is chosen with it too
10336    /// (`timer_signal_target`).
10337    fn kernel_signal_target(
10338        &self,
10339        process: DetPid,
10340        preferred: DetTid,
10341        signo: libc::c_int,
10342    ) -> Option<DetTid> {
10343        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
10344        let mut threads = self.process_signal_targets(process);
10345        // Stable, so the rest stay in thread-ID order.
10346        threads.sort_by_key(|thread| *thread != preferred);
10347        let unblocked = |thread: &DetTid| {
10348            self.thread_signal_mask(*thread)
10349                .is_some_and(|mask| mask & bit == 0)
10350        };
10351        threads
10352            .iter()
10353            .copied()
10354            .filter(|thread| self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(thread))
10355            .find(unblocked)
10356            .or_else(|| threads.iter().copied().find(unblocked))
10357    }
10358
10359    /// Send a `ChildExit` timer's `SIGCHLD` to `parent` (`info`: the siginfo
10360    /// to send instead of the kernel's `SI_USER`), and return the thread it
10361    /// was sent to. Where the scheduler models signal targets, that is the
10362    /// thread the kernel gives it (`kernel_sigchld_target`), trying first the
10363    /// child's `creator`, or under targeted chaos a random live thread of the
10364    /// process; the send then goes to exactly that thread, which
10365    /// `wake_signaled_guest` arms if it sleeps outside the schedule. Before,
10366    /// targeted chaos drew its random thread after the kernel's choice and
10367    /// replaced it, so it could name a stopped thread while the kernel woke an
10368    /// `rt_sigsuspend` sibling that nothing armed (the Codex review of
10369    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
10370    /// One chaos draw per send, as before.
10371    pub(super) fn fire_child_exit_alarm(
10372        &mut self,
10373        parent: DetPid,
10374        creator: DetTid,
10375        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
10376    ) -> Option<DetTid> {
10377        let sig = Signal::SIGCHLD;
10378        #[cfg(test)]
10379        {
10380            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
10381        }
10382        if !self.models_signal_targets {
10383            let target = self.select_signal_target(parent, Some(creator));
10384            return self
10385                .fire_alarm_at(
10386                    parent,
10387                    target,
10388                    sig,
10389                    info,
10390                    creator,
10391                    discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(None),
10392                )
10393                .then_some(target)?;
10394        }
10395        let every_thread_blocks = self.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator).is_none();
10396        let target = self.child_exit_sigchld_target(parent, creator);
10397        let target = self.live_signal_target(parent, Some(target));
10398        // Linux names the parent task (`do_notify_parent`): the creator, or,
10399        // once it exited, the first live thread of its process, which took
10400        // over its children (`forget_original_parent`, `find_alive_thread`).
10401        let named = if self.next_turns.contains_key(&creator) {
10402            creator
10403        } else {
10404            self.process_signal_targets(parent)
10405                .into_iter()
10406                .next()
10407                .unwrap_or(creator)
10408        };
10409        let sent = self.fire_alarm_at(
10410            parent,
10411            target,
10412            sig,
10413            info,
10414            named,
10415            discarded_at_send::SendFate::Classify(None),
10416        );
10417        if sent && every_thread_blocks {
10418            self.note_signal_left_in_shared_queue(parent, libc::SIGCHLD);
10419        }
10420        sent.then_some(target)?
10421    }
10422
10423    /// The thread of `parent` that a `ChildExit` timer's `SIGCHLD` is sent to
10424    /// where the scheduler models signal targets (`fire_child_exit_alarm`):
10425    /// the kernel's choice (`kernel_sigchld_target`), trying first `creator`,
10426    /// or under targeted chaos a random live thread of the process.
10427    fn child_exit_sigchld_target(&mut self, parent: DetPid, creator: DetTid) -> DetTid {
10428        let preferred = self.chaos_signal_target(parent).unwrap_or(creator);
10429        self.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, preferred)
10430            .unwrap_or(preferred)
10431    }
10432
10433    /// `thread`'s signal mask: the one its parked futex wait reported, which only
10434    /// it can change and so cannot change while it is parked; for a thread
10435    /// sleeping outside the runnable set, the one recorded when its call was
10436    /// committed (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`); and otherwise the
10437    /// kernel's (`SigBlk`) for a thread stopped at a request.
10438    fn thread_signal_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
10439        if let Some((receiver, mask)) = self.delivery_mask_override
10440            && receiver == thread
10441        {
10442            return Some(mask);
10443        }
10444        if let Some(watch) = self
10445            .parked_futex_waiter(thread)
10446            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
10447        {
10448            return Some(!watch.unblocked);
10449        }
10450        if let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&thread) {
10451            return *recorded;
10452        }
10453        self.read_thread_blocked_mask(thread)
10454    }
10455
10456    /// `thread`'s current signal mask (`SigBlk`), read from the kernel; `None`
10457    /// when it cannot be read. Ordered by the schedule only while `thread` is
10458    /// stopped at a request (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
10459    fn read_thread_blocked_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
10460        match self.read_thread_blocked_mask_result(thread) {
10461            Ok(blocked) => Some(blocked),
10462            Err(errno) => {
10463                debug!(
10464                    "[dtid {}] cannot read its signal mask ({}); it is not a SIGCHLD target.",
10465                    thread, errno
10466                );
10467                None
10468            }
10469        }
10470    }
10471
10472    /// The signals pending in the shared queue of `thread`'s process
10473    /// (`ShdPnd`), or `None` when it cannot be read.
10474    fn read_shared_pending(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
10475        // Unit tests script the queue; they never read a host task's.
10476        if cfg!(test) {
10477            #[cfg(test)]
10478            return self
10479                .test_kernel_signal_states
10480                .get(&thread)
10481                .map(|state| state.shared_pending);
10482        }
10483        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
10484        read_kernel_signal_state(
10485            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
10486            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
10487        )
10488        .ok()
10489        .map(|state| state.shared_pending)
10490    }
10491
10492    /// `read_thread_blocked_mask`, keeping the error, which says nothing about
10493    /// whether the thread still exists (`thread_is_gone` does).
10494    fn read_thread_blocked_mask_result(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
10495        #[cfg(test)]
10496        self.test_kernel_mask_reads
10497            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
10498        #[cfg(test)]
10499        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&thread) {
10500            return Ok(state.blocked);
10501        }
10502        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
10503        read_kernel_signal_state(
10504            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
10505            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
10506        )
10507        .map(|state| state.blocked)
10508    }
10509
10510    /// Record an unambiguous cross-task signal that was physically queued while
10511    /// its target was parked in waitid, restartable internal IO polling, or a
10512    /// precise-mode futex wait, or slept in a real `rt_sigsuspend` or waited
10513    /// for its grant (`in_rt_sigsuspend`), or in an emulated `pause` or
10514    /// `nanosleep` (`sleep_signal`). The
10515    /// request rewrite is deferred to step2 so an asynchronous backend cannot
10516    /// mutate beneath a tentative selection. A futex waiter is admitted on its
10517    /// mask and on what Linux does with the signal as it is sent (it discards
10518    /// one that is ignored, or ignored by default, then: `discarded_when_sent`),
10519    /// a `waitid` wait and an internal IO poll on that fate, and a sleep on its
10520    /// request alone; the drain, the commit point, decides on the rest.
10521    pub(crate) fn notify_signal_pending(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
10522        // A waitid wait is decided here too, in the sender's turn: its drain
10523        // works from a list with no queue identity (Claude N7 of
10524        // <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293>).
10525        if (self.waitid_signal_request(dettid).is_some()
10526            && !self.discarded_when_sent(dettid, signal))
10527            // A restartable internal IO poll decides at its own turn which
10528            // signals still interrupt it, so a copy Linux discarded at send,
10529            // or one the poll's mask blocks, does not end it either way;
10530            // refusing it here spares the poll a turn Linux does not have
10531            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273, R2b-1 rule 1).
10532            || (self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid).is_some()
10533                && !self.discarded_when_sent(dettid, signal)
10534                && self.poll_mask_admits(dettid, signal))
10535            || (self
10536                .parked_futex_unblocked_signals(dettid)
10537                .is_some_and(|signals| signals & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0)
10538                && !self.discarded_when_sent(dettid, signal))
10539            || self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid)
10540            || self.admits_sleep_signal(dettid, signal)
10541        {
10542            let signals = self.pending_cross_task_signals.entry(dettid).or_default();
10543            if !signals.contains(&signal) {
10544                signals.push(signal);
10545            }
10546        }
10547    }
10548
10549    /// Whether Linux discards `signal`, sent now to the parked futex waiter
10550    /// `dettid`, in the sender's turn: it is unblocked and ignored, or ignored
10551    /// by default with no handler (`discarded_at_generation`). A handler
10552    /// installed later does not bring it back. Read here, in the sender's turn,
10553    /// from the waiter's task as `parked_futex_interrupting_signals` reads it,
10554    /// because `rt_sigaction` takes no turn of its own, so by the drain a
10555    /// sibling may have installed one (the Claude review of
10556    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4290: a default SIGCHLD, then a
10557    /// handler, ended a futex wait with EINTR where Linux returns 0). A state
10558    /// that cannot be read is not discarded, and the drain decides.
10559    ///
10560    /// The sender recorded its send's fate in its turn, before this
10561    /// (`discarded_at_send`), against the mask and dispositions Linux reads.
10562    /// So `signal` is discarded for `dettid` when the record marks a queue it
10563    /// takes from and no queue it takes from holds a copy the record does not
10564    /// mark. Only standard signals are recorded, and only where the scheduler
10565    /// models signal targets; any other is never discarded here.
10566    fn discarded_when_sent(&self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) -> bool {
10567        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) & discarded_at_send::STANDARD_SIGNALS;
10568        let (thread_bits, process_bits) = self.discarded_bits(dettid);
10569        if (thread_bits | process_bits) & bit == 0 {
10570            return false;
10571        }
10572        let state = {
10573            #[cfg(test)]
10574            {
10575                self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid).copied()
10576            }
10577            #[cfg(not(test))]
10578            {
10579                None
10580            }
10581        };
10582        let state = state.or_else(|| {
10583            let (pid, tid) = match self
10584                .parked_futex_waiter(dettid)
10585                .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
10586            {
10587                Some(watch) => (watch.pid, watch.tid),
10588                None => (self.sigchld_process(dettid).as_raw(), dettid.as_raw()),
10589            };
10590            read_kernel_signal_state(reverie::Pid::from_raw(pid), reverie::Pid::from_raw(tid)).ok()
10591        });
10592        let Some(state) = state else {
10593            return false;
10594        };
10595        let kept = (state.thread_pending & !thread_bits) | (state.shared_pending & !process_bits);
10596        kept & bit == 0
10597    }
10598
10599    /// Whether the mask of the restartable internal IO poll `dettid` leaves
10600    /// `signal` unblocked, read in the sender's turn: the guest's own mask
10601    /// while Detcore holds the thread under a private one, as a pipe `writev`
10602    /// does (`saved_guest_sigmasks`), and otherwise the thread's kernel mask,
10603    /// which a parked thread cannot change. Where the record of copies Linux
10604    /// discarded at send is not kept (`models_signal_targets`), or the mask
10605    /// cannot be read, every signal is admitted, as before.
10606    fn poll_mask_admits(&self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) -> bool {
10607        if !self.models_signal_targets {
10608            return true;
10609        }
10610        let mask = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&dettid) {
10611            Some(saved) => Some(*saved),
10612            None => self.read_thread_blocked_mask(dettid),
10613        };
10614        mask.is_none_or(|mask| mask & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) == 0)
10615    }
10616
10617    /// Whether `dettid` sleeps in a real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the run queue
10618    /// (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or waits for the grant of that call's
10619    /// request, where a signal sent now still reaches the call
10620    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`).
10621    fn in_rt_sigsuspend(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
10622        self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
10623            || self
10624                .next_turns
10625                .get(&dettid)
10626                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
10627                .and_then(Result::ok)
10628                .is_some_and(|request| {
10629                    request
10630                        .resources
10631                        .keys()
10632                        .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)))
10633                })
10634    }
10635
10636    // Force a thread out blocking and into the runnable state, replacing its resource request.
10637    fn force_unblock_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources) {
10638        let _ = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, false);
10639    }
10640
10641    /// [`Scheduler::force_unblock_thread`], queuing the thread at the front of its
10642    /// priority band when `front` is set. A precise futex waiter woken for a
10643    /// signal goes to the front, so it is the next thread to resume and dequeue
10644    /// the signal it was woken for, which is the thread the scheduler chose for
10645    /// it (`kernel_sigchld_target`, and the cross-task sender's own target). A
10646    /// sibling queued ahead of it and not blocking the signal would otherwise
10647    /// resume first and take it, leaving the waiter a wake with nothing to be
10648    /// interrupted by (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
10649    ///
10650    /// A thread held at a happens-before gate is left held. Its pending
10651    /// request is the gate's checkpoint, and the guest does not re-check the
10652    /// gate after a substituted resume, so replacing that request would let
10653    /// the thread past a hard edge before its BEFORE anchor fired. A held
10654    /// thread is runnable as far as Linux is concerned, only not scheduled:
10655    /// the signal stays pending in the kernel and is delivered when the gate
10656    /// opens and the thread resumes, as for any runnable thread that is not
10657    /// running.
10658    ///
10659    /// Returns whether it unblocked the thread.
10660    fn force_unblock_thread_at(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources, front: bool) -> bool {
10661        // The consumed alarm already owns this exact response. A later
10662        // physical signal must not replace its fatal continuation.
10663        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
10664            return false;
10665        }
10666        if self
10667            .happens_before
10668            .as_ref()
10669            .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dettid))
10670        {
10671            info!(
10672                "[dtid {}] held at a happens-before gate; leaving it held, its signal pending",
10673                dettid
10674            );
10675            return false;
10676        }
10677        info!(
10678            "[dtid {}] removing blocking entries and requeuing thread",
10679            dettid
10680        );
10681        self.remove_blocking_entries(&dettid);
10682        // The substituted request resolves any polling wait the thread was in.
10683        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid);
10684
10685        if let Some(nxt) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) {
10686            // Counterfeit the entry as though the thread had requested this resource from the start:
10687            nxt.req = Ivar::full(Ok(rsrcs));
10688        }
10689
10690        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a force-unblocked thread (e.g. woken by a
10691        // signal or ready I/O) is normally requeued at the back of its priority
10692        // level, so it runs after everything already queued. Randomizing whether
10693        // it jumps to the front instead varies the order in which a just-woken
10694        // thread races the threads it was contending with -- surfacing
10695        // lock-ordering / wakeup-ordering races. Reproducible under `--fuzz-seed`.
10696        //
10697        // Chaos keeps its draw for a signal-woken futex waiter too, so the same
10698        // PRNG stream is consumed. A waiter that then resumes after a sibling
10699        // took its signal parks again with its original deadline.
10700        let to_front = if self.chaos_target_races {
10701            chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &[true, false]).unwrap_or(false)
10702        } else {
10703            front
10704        };
10705        if to_front {
10706            self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
10707        } else {
10708            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
10709        }
10710        true
10711    }
10712
10713    /// The backgrounded vfork child that step 3 waits for, and that step 2c
10714    /// readmits as soon as its call finishes.
10715    ///
10716    /// While a vfork barrier is in place, step 3 selects a barrier child that
10717    /// is queued to run a turn first. A child can instead be in the background
10718    /// pool (`external_io_blockers`): a vfork child that vforks again, as a
10719    /// double-spawning helper does, is backgrounded in its own `vfork` until
10720    /// its child execs (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4163>), and
10721    /// a child can call something whose completion the host times. Letting
10722    /// other threads run meanwhile would make how many turns they take before
10723    /// the child resumes depend on when its call finished, so step 3 selects
10724    /// nothing until it is readmitted
10725    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194>, Claude review of
10726    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205>). A child blocked on, or
10727    /// polling for, another thread is not here: only that thread's turn can
10728    /// wake it, so the other threads run.
10729    ///
10730    /// Returns `None` when a barrier child is queued to run a turn, or when no
10731    /// barrier child is backgrounded. Otherwise returns the innermost such
10732    /// child: the first backgrounded barrier child, in parent order (the order
10733    /// step 3 uses), that holds no barrier of its own. A child that does hold
10734    /// one is still inside its own `vfork`, so it cannot finish before its
10735    /// child does: with three levels (P vforks C, C vforks G, G vforks a child
10736    /// that execs), C waits for G, and only G, whose child has execed, can run.
10737    ///
10738    /// The choice does not depend on which background calls have finished, so
10739    /// waiting for that one child and readmitting it alone keeps the schedule
10740    /// independent of host timing: no turn can commit until it is readmitted.
10741    ///
10742    /// Under `hermit record` and `hermit replay` there is no such child: the
10743    /// rejoin log makes the turn of every readmission part of the recording
10744    /// (`log_rejoin`, `step2c_replay_rejoin`), so the child is readmitted like
10745    /// any other backgrounded call and other threads run meanwhile, as Linux
10746    /// runs every thread but the vfork parent. Waiting there instead hung a
10747    /// vfork child that polls a pipe another process writes: record
10748    /// backgrounds that poll, and the writer never ran
10749    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211>).
10750    fn vfork_gated_background_child(&self) -> Option<DetTid> {
10751        if self.vfork_barriers.is_empty()
10752            || self.rejoin_writer.is_some()
10753            || self.rejoin_replay.is_some()
10754        {
10755            return None;
10756        }
10757        let mut children = self.vfork_barriers.values().flatten();
10758        if children
10759            .clone()
10760            .any(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(*child))
10761        {
10762            return None;
10763        }
10764        children
10765            .find(|child| {
10766                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(*child)
10767                    && !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(*child)
10768            })
10769            .copied()
10770    }
10771
10772    /// The vfork barriers' children whose call runs in the background
10773    /// (`external_io_blockers`), in thread order. Under the rejoin log
10774    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers` readmits each as soon as its call finishes
10775    /// and logs the turn (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211>).
10776    fn backgrounded_vfork_children(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = DetTid> + '_ {
10777        let mut children: Vec<DetTid> = self
10778            .vfork_barriers
10779            .values()
10780            .flatten()
10781            .copied()
10782            .filter(|child| self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(child))
10783            .collect();
10784        children.sort();
10785        children.dedup();
10786        children.into_iter()
10787    }
10788
10789    /// Whether `dtid`'s backgrounded call, or signal-less wait, has finished,
10790    /// by the test `step2c_process_io_blockers` applies to each blocker.
10791    fn blocker_has_finished(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> bool {
10792        let (op_id, signal_can_complete) =
10793            if let Some(op_id) = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&dtid) {
10794                (*op_id, !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&dtid))
10795            } else if let Some(op_id) = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&dtid) {
10796                (*op_id, true)
10797            } else {
10798                return false;
10799            };
10800        self.next_turns.get(&dtid).is_some_and(|next| {
10801            matches!(next.req.try_read(), Some(Ok(req))
10802                if blocking_request_is_ready(&req, op_id, signal_can_complete))
10803        })
10804    }
10805
10806    /// `hermit replay`: whether this scheduler pass must wait, before it pops a
10807    /// timed event or restores a poller, for calls that replay readmits now
10808    /// but that have not finished on the host yet: the calls of a logged
10809    /// readmission due at this point, or a call replay serves from the
10810    /// recording (`replay_log_served`).
10811    ///
10812    /// Record readmits such a call in the first pass of its turn that finds it
10813    /// finished, so it pops at most one timed event before the readmission.
10814    /// Replay can reach that turn before the call finishes and then spins.
10815    /// If each spinning pass popped a timed event, several due events would
10816    /// fire at the same turn, where record fired one per turn (Claude review of
10817    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4298). Waiting here makes the
10818    /// pass that proceeds do what record's did: at most one pop, then the
10819    /// readmission.
10820    ///
10821    /// A logged call that is not parked as logged is left to
10822    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers`, which refuses it, and so is a wait past
10823    /// `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE`.
10824    fn replay_waits_before_maintenance(&mut self) -> bool {
10825        if self.rejoin_replay.is_none() {
10826            return false;
10827        }
10828        let log_served_waiting = self
10829            .blocked
10830            .replay_log_served
10831            .iter()
10832            .any(|dtid| !self.blocker_has_finished(*dtid));
10833        let point = (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes);
10834        let due_waiting = self
10835            .rejoin_replay
10836            .as_ref()
10837            .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
10838            .filter(|next| next.point() == point)
10839            .is_some_and(|next| {
10840                next.calls.iter().all(|(dtid, sequence)| {
10841                    self.blocked
10842                        .external_io_blockers
10843                        .get(dtid)
10844                        .map(|op| op.sequence)
10845                        == Some(*sequence)
10846                        || self
10847                            .blocked
10848                            .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
10849                            .get(dtid)
10850                            .map(|op| op.sequence)
10851                            == Some(*sequence)
10852                }) && next
10853                    .calls
10854                    .iter()
10855                    .any(|(dtid, _)| !self.blocker_has_finished(*dtid))
10856            });
10857        if due_waiting {
10858            let since = *self
10859                .rejoin_stalled_since
10860                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
10861            if since.elapsed() >= Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
10862                return false;
10863            }
10864        }
10865        if due_waiting || log_served_waiting {
10866            std::thread::yield_now();
10867            return true;
10868        }
10869        false
10870    }
10871
10872    /// `hermit replay`: whether the next logged readmission is due at this
10873    /// point of the schedule or already behind it, which
10874    /// `step2c_replay_rejoin` then applies or refuses.
10875    fn rejoin_due_now(&self) -> bool {
10876        self.rejoin_replay
10877            .as_ref()
10878            .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
10879            .is_some_and(|next| next.point() <= (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes))
10880    }
10881
10882    /// Whether a vfork barrier's child is queued to run a turn (not only
10883    /// polling): step 3 then selects it first. The deterministic-work-first
10884    /// gates count it as ordinary work even when its priority is in the last
10885    /// band, where `only_pollers` counts every entry as a poller, so that no
10886    /// background call or deferred signal is admitted between its turns at a
10887    /// moment the host chose. The fence that step 3 applies and the gates that
10888    /// admit host-timed completions then agree on what is runnable work (Codex
10889    /// re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
10890    fn vfork_child_runs_turn(&self) -> bool {
10891        self.vfork_barriers
10892            .values()
10893            .flatten()
10894            .any(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(*child))
10895    }
10896
10897    /// Check on threads executing blocking syscalls outside the runnable set.
10898    fn step2c_process_io_blockers(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10899        if !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
10900            || !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
10901        {
10902            // A nondeterministic snapshot of which backgrounded actions are ready right now:
10903            let mut blockers: Vec<(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)> = self
10904                .blocked
10905                .external_io_blockers
10906                .iter()
10907                .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(dtid)))
10908                .chain(
10909                    self.blocked
10910                        .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
10911                        .iter()
10912                        .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, true)),
10913                )
10914                .collect();
10915            blockers.sort_by_key(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid);
10916            let ready: Vec<DetTid> = blockers
10917                .iter()
10918                .filter(|(dtid, op_id, signal_can_complete)| {
10919                    let nt = self
10920                        .next_turns
10921                        .get(dtid)
10922                        .expect("internal invariant broken");
10923                    if let Some(Ok(req)) = nt.req.try_read() {
10924                        blocking_request_is_ready(&req, *op_id, *signal_can_complete)
10925                            // A race probe may report it unfinished for this check
10926                            // (docs/RACE_PROBES.md); off unless configured.
10927                            && !crate::race_probe::perturb(crate::race_probe::BG_HARVEST_SKIP)
10928                    } else {
10929                        false
10930                    }
10931                })
10932                .map(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid)
10933                .collect();
10934            debug!(
10935                "Nondeterministic status of backgrounded operations: out of {}, completed on {}, dtids: {:?}",
10936                blockers.len(),
10937                ready.len(),
10938                ready
10939            );
10940
10941            let requeue_ready = |scheduler: &mut Self, ready: &[DetTid]| {
10942                for ready_dtid in ready {
10943                    info!(
10944                        "[step2] Reschedule formerly backgrounded dtid {:?}",
10945                        ready_dtid
10946                    );
10947                    let external = scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
10948                    scheduler.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(ready_dtid);
10949                    let sigsuspend = scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
10950                    let _ = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(ready_dtid);
10951                    assert!(
10952                        external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
10953                        "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
10954                    );
10955                    scheduler.readmit_ready_thread(*ready_dtid);
10956                }
10957            };
10958
10959            // FIXME TODO (T137183027): for record/replay to work properly, we need to ALLOW the
10960            // "Nondeterminstic algorithm" below, but record & replay those scheduler events. In
10961            // the meantime, use a deterministic eager policy once there is no other runnable work.
10962            if self.recordreplay_modes {
10963                // A call that replay serves from the recording cannot block, but it
10964                // changes guest state while it runs: the stand-in for an accepted
10965                // connection takes a descriptor slot. Commit no other turn until every
10966                // such call has finished, so that each takes effect right after its own
10967                // turn rather than among other threads' turns at a host-timed point.
10968                // Waiting changes only how long the scheduler spins, not what it commits
10969                // next. It also makes the readiness of these calls below independent of
10970                // host timing.
10971                let log_served: Vec<DetTid> =
10972                    self.blocked.replay_log_served.iter().copied().collect();
10973                if log_served.iter().any(|dtid| !ready.contains(dtid)) {
10974                    trace!(
10975                        "[step2] waiting for background calls replay serves from the log, dtids {:?}",
10976                        log_served
10977                    );
10978                    std::thread::yield_now();
10979                    return Err(SkipTurn);
10980                }
10981
10982                // Only *real* deterministic work should defer external-IO harvesting.
10983                // Internal pollers sit at LAST_PRIORITY and are frequently spinning on
10984                // the very result an external-IO blocker will produce (e.g. the reader
10985                // side of `echo hi | cat`, where one stage uses InternalIOPolling while
10986                // its peer is backgrounded on BlockingExternalIO). Treat a run queue
10987                // that holds only pollers as "no deterministic work" so we still harvest
10988                // completed IO below; a queued poller must not starve a ready blocker.
10989                // Nor must a thread queued because it yielded: a sibling spinning
10990                // on `sched_yield` is always queued, and it starved a finished
10991                // background pselect6 forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4092).
10992                // Whether the call has finished is host-timed, as for a poller;
10993                // `log_rejoin` records the turn of the readmission for replay.
10994                // A vfork barrier's child that will run a turn is work too,
10995                // whatever its priority (see `vfork_child_runs_turn`).
10996                let only_pollers =
10997                    self.run_queue.only_pollers_or_yielders() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
10998
10999                // Deterministic work is runnable: let it proceed. Waiting here while such
11000                // work exists can deadlock thread creation -- the parent and new child
11001                // cannot complete clone while an existing worker blocks indefinitely in
11002                // epoll_wait.
11003                //
11004                // With the rejoin log active there is no vfork-gated child
11005                // (`vfork_gated_background_child`): a backgrounded vfork child
11006                // is readmitted below and logged like any other call. Without
11007                // it, the gated child is readmitted here unlogged: until then
11008                // no turn can commit (step 3 waits for it), so the turn of its
11009                // readmission does not depend on when its call finished.
11010                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
11011                    if let Some(child) = self.vfork_gated_background_child()
11012                        && ready.contains(&child)
11013                    {
11014                        requeue_ready(self, &[child]);
11015                    }
11016                    // With the rejoin log active, a backgrounded vfork child is
11017                    // readmitted as soon as its call finishes, even though other
11018                    // work is runnable, and the turn is logged: a sibling of the
11019                    // vfork parent can spin until the child is done, and deferring
11020                    // the child behind it would never readmit it. Replay follows
11021                    // the log here too, so a readmission due now is applied in the
11022                    // same branch the recording took (the schedules agree up to
11023                    // this turn, so the run queue is the same)
11024                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211).
11025                    if self.rejoin_replay.is_some() {
11026                        if self.rejoin_due_now() {
11027                            return self.step2c_replay_rejoin(&blockers, &ready, requeue_ready);
11028                        }
11029                    } else if self.rejoin_writer.is_some() {
11030                        let children: Vec<DetTid> = self
11031                            .backgrounded_vfork_children()
11032                            .filter(|child| ready.contains(child))
11033                            .collect();
11034                        if !children.is_empty() {
11035                            self.log_rejoin(&blockers, &children);
11036                            requeue_ready(self, &children);
11037                        }
11038                    }
11039                    return Ok(());
11040                }
11041
11042                // Replay readmits each call at the turn the recording logged, not when
11043                // it finishes (see `rejoin_log`).
11044                if self.rejoin_replay.is_some() {
11045                    return self.step2c_replay_rejoin(&blockers, &ready, requeue_ready);
11046                }
11047
11048                // Readmit those calls first, in thread order; every one has finished.
11049                // Other background calls are readmitted below once none of them remain.
11050                if !log_served.is_empty() {
11051                    requeue_ready(self, &log_served);
11052                    return Ok(());
11053                }
11054
11055                // Reschedule every blocker whose IO has completed so its continuation can
11056                // consume the recorded result. Harvesting all ready blockers (not just the
11057                // first) and doing so even when pollers are queued is what breaks the
11058                // record-mode pipe livelock: previously a queued poller made this branch
11059                // return early forever, so the completed read/write was never rescheduled
11060                // and the poller spun on data that never arrived.
11061                //
11062                // Which pass finds a call finished depends on host timing, so record
11063                // logs the turn of each readmission for replay to follow.
11064                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
11065                if !ready.is_empty() {
11066                    self.log_rejoin(&blockers, &ready);
11067                    requeue_ready(self, &ready);
11068                    return Ok(());
11069                }
11070
11071                // `rt_sigsuspend` has no spontaneous completion: with no real
11072                // external IO left, continue to step2d so a finite timer can
11073                // fire or the signal-less wait can receive a terminal verdict.
11074                if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
11075                    return Ok(());
11076                }
11077
11078                // No completed IO yet, but pollers are queued: let one poll. A poller
11079                // can be what the blocker waits for, not only the other way round: a
11080                // client's read on a TCP connection waits for the server's accept, and
11081                // the server polls that accept in turn
11082                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880). Spinning here would
11083                // never run it. Readiness is still checked, and a ready blocker
11084                // harvested, before every poll. Whether a call had finished before
11085                // this poll is host-timed; the rejoin log above makes replay agree.
11086                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() {
11087                    return Ok(());
11088                }
11089
11090                // No completed IO yet and nothing queued, but a thread sleeps
11091                // until a reachable deadline: let step2d move virtual time
11092                // there, as `hermit run` does below. The blocked call can wait
11093                // on that thread, a client that sleeps before it connects or
11094                // writes, and spinning would never wake it
11095                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3881). Whether the
11096                // call finished before this move is host-timed; the rejoin log
11097                // records the wake count with the turn so replay agrees.
11098                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
11099                if self.next_deadline_is_reachable() {
11100                    return Ok(());
11101                }
11102
11103                // No completed IO yet, and nothing to run. The
11104                // blocking syscalls are executing in the host kernel; go around the loop
11105                // and re-check readiness. (Still a busy-wait; see T137183027 for the
11106                // record-the-nondeterministic-event fix.)
11107                trace!(
11108                    "[step2] eagerly waiting on external IO for dtids {:?}. spinning.",
11109                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
11110                );
11111                std::thread::yield_now();
11112                return Err(SkipTurn);
11113            } // End region which should be deleted.
11114
11115            // Use the same deterministic-work-first policy as record/replay. Host
11116            // completion timing must not decide whether a ready continuation overtakes
11117            // guest work that was already runnable. Pollers are excluded because they
11118            // commonly wait for the completed operation and would otherwise starve it.
11119            let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
11120            if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
11121                if let Some(child) = self.vfork_gated_background_child()
11122                    && ready.contains(&child)
11123                {
11124                    requeue_ready(self, &[child]);
11125                }
11126                return Ok(());
11127            }
11128
11129            if !ready.is_empty() {
11130                requeue_ready(self, &ready);
11131            }
11132            if self.run_queue.is_empty()
11133                && self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty()
11134                && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
11135            {
11136                // TODO (T137184765): for now we just WAIT eagerly whenever there is blocking
11137                // external IO and else to do. We implement a busy-wait by going around the
11138                // scheduler loop again.
11139                trace!(
11140                    "[step2] TEMPORARY2: eagerly blocking on external IO for dtids {:?}.  SPINNING!",
11141                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
11142                );
11143                std::thread::yield_now();
11144                Err(SkipTurn)
11145            } else {
11146                // Productive work to do, irrespcetive of what's blocked, so let's get to it.
11147                Ok(())
11148            }
11149        } else {
11150            Ok(())
11151        }
11152    }
11153
11154    /// `hermit record`: log that `step2c_process_io_blockers` readmits the
11155    /// finished calls of `ready` at this turn (see `rejoin_log`).
11156    fn log_rejoin(&mut self, blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)], ready: &[DetTid]) {
11157        let Some(writer) = self.rejoin_writer.as_mut() else {
11158            return;
11159        };
11160        let rejoin = Rejoin {
11161            turn: self.turn,
11162            wakes: self.empty_queue_wakes,
11163            calls: ready
11164                .iter()
11165                .map(|dtid| {
11166                    let (_, op_id, _) = blockers
11167                        .iter()
11168                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
11169                        .expect("a ready thread is a blocker");
11170                    (*dtid, op_id.sequence)
11171                })
11172                .collect(),
11173        };
11174        writer
11175            .append(&rejoin)
11176            .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("cannot write the rejoin log: {err}"));
11177    }
11178
11179    /// How long replay waits, with nothing runnable and no readmission due, for
11180    /// work to appear, or at a logged readmission for its calls to finish,
11181    /// before it refuses (see `step2c_replay_rejoin`).
11182    const REJOIN_STALL_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
11183
11184    /// `hermit replay`: readmit backgrounded calls at the turns the recording
11185    /// logged (see `rejoin_log`). Called where record readmits finished calls,
11186    /// after the checks the two runs share.
11187    ///
11188    /// - A readmission logged for this turn waits until each of its calls has
11189    ///   finished, without committing a turn, then readmits them in the logged
11190    ///   order. Record readmitted them in a pass at this turn, before any other
11191    ///   turn could commit. A call still unfinished after `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE`
11192    ///   is refused rather than waited on forever.
11193    /// - Until then a finished call stays parked, and queued threads run as
11194    ///   they did in record.
11195    /// - Replay refuses if it reaches a later turn than a logged readmission,
11196    ///   or if the parked call is not the logged one.
11197    ///   With nothing runnable and no readmission due, record spun until a call
11198    ///   finished; replay waits `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE` for other work to appear
11199    ///   (a thread admission, say) and then refuses rather than hang.
11200    ///
11201    /// By induction on turns, the two schedules agree up to the next logged
11202    /// turn: everything host-timed before it (poll results, readmissions) is
11203    /// in the recording, so whatever let the call finish in record has also
11204    /// happened in replay by then.
11205    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
11206    fn step2c_replay_rejoin(
11207        &mut self,
11208        blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)],
11209        ready: &[DetTid],
11210        requeue_ready: impl Fn(&mut Self, &[DetTid]),
11211    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11212        let next = match self.rejoin_replay.as_ref() {
11213            Some(rejoins) => rejoins.front().cloned(),
11214            None => unreachable!("only replay follows the rejoin log"),
11215        };
11216        let describe = |rejoin: &Rejoin| {
11217            rejoin
11218                .calls
11219                .iter()
11220                .map(|(dtid, sequence)| format!("thread {} call {}", dtid.as_raw(), sequence))
11221                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
11222                .join(", ")
11223        };
11224        let point = (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes);
11225        if let Some(next) = next {
11226            if next.point() < point {
11227                let reason = format!(
11228                    "the recording readmitted {} at turn {} after {} timer wakes, and replay \
11229                     reached turn {} after {} first",
11230                    describe(&next),
11231                    next.turn,
11232                    next.wakes,
11233                    self.turn,
11234                    self.empty_queue_wakes
11235                );
11236                return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
11237            }
11238            if next.point() == point {
11239                for (dtid, sequence) in &next.calls {
11240                    let parked = blockers
11241                        .iter()
11242                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
11243                        .map(|(_, op_id, _)| op_id.sequence);
11244                    if parked != Some(*sequence) {
11245                        let reason = format!(
11246                            "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, but replay has {} parked there",
11247                            describe(&next),
11248                            next.turn,
11249                            parked.map_or("no such call".to_string(), |parked| format!(
11250                                "call {parked} of thread {}",
11251                                dtid.as_raw()
11252                            ))
11253                        );
11254                        return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
11255                    }
11256                }
11257                let due: Vec<DetTid> = next.calls.iter().map(|(dtid, _)| *dtid).collect();
11258                if due.iter().all(|dtid| ready.contains(dtid)) {
11259                    self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
11260                    if let Some(rejoins) = self.rejoin_replay.as_mut() {
11261                        rejoins.pop_front();
11262                    }
11263                    requeue_ready(self, &due);
11264                    return Ok(());
11265                }
11266                let since = *self
11267                    .rejoin_stalled_since
11268                    .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
11269                if since.elapsed() >= Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
11270                    let reason = format!(
11271                        "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, and replay waited {} s there \
11272                         for those calls to finish",
11273                        describe(&next),
11274                        next.turn,
11275                        Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE.as_secs()
11276                    );
11277                    return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
11278                }
11279                trace!(
11280                    "[step2] waiting at turn {} for the logged readmission of {:?}",
11281                    self.turn, due
11282                );
11283                std::thread::yield_now();
11284                return Err(SkipTurn);
11285            }
11286        }
11287        // Record readmitted nothing in this pass. `rt_sigsuspend` alone goes on
11288        // to step2d, queued pollers run, and step2d wakes a reachable timed
11289        // event, as in record.
11290        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
11291            || !self.run_queue.is_empty()
11292            || self.next_deadline_is_reachable()
11293        {
11294            self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
11295            return Ok(());
11296        }
11297        let since = *self
11298            .rejoin_stalled_since
11299            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
11300        if since.elapsed() < Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
11301            std::thread::yield_now();
11302            return Err(SkipTurn);
11303        }
11304        let reason = format!(
11305            "at turn {} nothing can run, and the next logged readmission is {}",
11306            self.turn,
11307            match self
11308                .rejoin_replay
11309                .as_ref()
11310                .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
11311            {
11312                Some(next) => format!("{} at turn {}", describe(next), next.turn),
11313                None => "none".to_string(),
11314            }
11315        );
11316        self.refuse_rejoin(reason)
11317    }
11318
11319    /// Whether step2d, with the run queue empty, would wake a timed event: one
11320    /// is pending, and the earliest is not `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`.
11321    fn next_deadline_is_reachable(&self) -> bool {
11322        self.blocked
11323            .timed_waiters
11324            .next_deadline()
11325            .is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_indefinite())
11326    }
11327
11328    /// Replay's refusal of a run that ends with logged readmissions it never
11329    /// reached: the recording's schedule went on past where replay's ended.
11330    fn unreplayed_rejoins(&self) -> Option<RejoinRefusal> {
11331        let rejoins = self.rejoin_replay.as_ref()?;
11332        let next = rejoins.front()?;
11333        Some(RejoinRefusal {
11334            reason: format!(
11335                "the run ended at turn {} with {} logged readmissions not replayed, the first at \
11336                 turn {}",
11337                self.turn,
11338                rejoins.len(),
11339                next.turn
11340            ),
11341        })
11342    }
11343
11344    /// Record a `RejoinRefusal` for the scheduler loop to end the run with.
11345    fn refuse_rejoin(&mut self, reason: String) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11346        if self.rejoin_refusal.is_none() {
11347            let refusal = RejoinRefusal { reason };
11348            tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
11349            self.rejoin_refusal = Some(refusal);
11350        }
11351        Err(SkipTurn)
11352    }
11353
11354    /// Render one blocked thread's pending request, with a stable resource order.
11355    ///
11356    /// `Resources::resources` is a `HashMap`, so its iteration order is not
11357    /// reproducible; sort the rendered entries. Reads the `Ivar`'s contents
11358    /// rather than `Debug`-printing the `Ivar`, whose parked `Waker` carries raw
11359    /// host pointers.
11360    fn render_pending_request(req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>) -> String {
11361        match req.try_read() {
11362            None => "<no request pending>".to_owned(),
11363            Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => "<thread exited>".to_owned(),
11364            Some(Ok(rsrc)) => {
11365                let mut held: Vec<String> = rsrc
11366                    .resources
11367                    .iter()
11368                    .map(|(rid, perm)| match rid {
11369                        // Spell the sentinel out. Its derived `Debug` is
11370                        // `SleepUntil(LogicalTime(18446744073709551615))`, and a
11371                        // reader who has to decode that number by hand is
11372                        // exactly the reader this report failed.
11373                        ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline) if deadline.is_indefinite() => {
11374                            format!("SleepUntil(INDEFINITE): {:?}", perm)
11375                        }
