11376                        _ => format!("{:?}: {:?}", rid, perm),
11377                    })
11378                    .collect();
11379                held.sort();
11380                let mut rendered = if held.is_empty() {
11381                    "<no resources>".to_owned()
11382                } else {
11383                    held.join(", ")
11384                };
11385                if rsrc.poll_attempt != 0 {
11386                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (poll_attempt {})", rsrc.poll_attempt);
11387                }
11388                if !rsrc.fyi.is_empty() {
11389                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (fyi {:?})", rsrc.fyi);
11390                }
11391                rendered
11392            }
11393        }
11394    }
11395
11396    /// Render a futex key with its guest address in hex.
11397    ///
11398    /// `FutexID`'s derived `Debug` prints the address in decimal, which is
11399    /// deterministic but unusable: a reader has to match it against a guest
11400    /// symbol or a `futex(...)` line in the DETLOG, and both are hex.
11401    fn render_futex_id(futex_id: &FutexID) -> String {
11402        match futex_id {
11403            FutexID::Private { mm, address } => {
11404                format!("private {:?} address {:#x}", mm, address)
11405            }
11406            FutexID::Shared { object, offset } => {
11407                format!("shared {:?} offset {:#x}", object, offset)
11408            }
11409        }
11410    }
11411
11412    /// Render a `LogicalTime` deadline, naming the no-deadline sentinel.
11413    fn render_deadline(deadline: LogicalTime) -> String {
11414        if deadline.is_indefinite() {
11415            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)".to_owned()
11416        } else {
11417            deadline.to_string()
11418        }
11419    }
11420
11421    /// Name every blocked class that is actually holding the run.
11422    ///
11423    /// Derived from state rather than passed in by the caller, so the headline
11424    /// cannot contradict the body it sits above. Branch order alone would
11425    /// mis-file a genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer
11426    /// registered: `step2d_handle_empty_queue` reaches the indefinite arm
11427    /// whenever *any* timed waiter exists, so a caller-supplied headline would
11428    /// read "waiting indefinitely" while the futex pool is the real story. The
11429    /// body always listed both; the headline is what lands in a bug report.
11430    fn describe_terminal_waiters(&self) -> String {
11431        let mut classes: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
11432        if !self.blocked.no_futex_waiters() {
11433            classes.push("thread(s) waiting on futex");
11434        }
11435        if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
11436            classes.push(
11437                "thread(s) waiting indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time)",
11438            );
11439        }
11440        if !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
11441            classes.push("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal");
11442        }
11443        // A deadlock is reported with child waits only when each waits for
11444        // children that cannot run again (`child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`).
11445        if !self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty() {
11446            classes.push("thread(s) waiting for a child that cannot exit");
11447        }
11448        if self
11449            .happens_before
11450            .as_ref()
11451            .is_some_and(|hb| !hb.parked.is_empty())
11452        {
11453            classes.push("thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire");
11454        }
11455        if classes.is_empty() {
11456            // Defensive: every caller fires with at least one class present.
11457            "thread(s) blocked with no possible wake".to_owned()
11458        } else {
11459            classes.join(", and ")
11460        }
11461    }
11462
11463    /// Build the deadlock report. **Must be byte-identical across runs of the
11464    /// same program**: this text reaches stderr, and emitting a
11465    /// host-dependent string from a deterministic execution engine is a defect
11466    /// in its own right, whether or not any comparator currently catches it.
11467    ///
11468    /// The obvious implementation -- `{:?}` of `run_queue`, `next_turns` and
11469    /// `blocked` -- is *not* reproducible. Three independent sources of
11470    /// run-to-run variation hide in those structures:
11471    ///
11472    /// 1. `ThreadNextTurn` and `FutexWaiter` hold [`Ivar`]s whose `Debug` prints
11473    ///    the parked waker as `Waker { data: 0x55.., vtable: 0x55.. }` -- raw
11474    ///    host pointers that move with ASLR on every run.
11475    /// 2. `BlockedPool::futex_waiters` is a `HashMap` and
11476    ///    `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, so both iterate in a
11477    ///    randomized order whenever they hold more than one entry.
11478    /// 3. `Resources::resources` is itself a `HashMap`, so even a single
11479    ///    thread's resource list is unordered.
11480    ///
11481    /// So every collection below is sorted on a stable key, and only
11482    /// guest-level identities are printed: dettids, resource ids, futex keys and
11483    /// logical deadlines, all of which Detcore already guarantees to be
11484    /// deterministic. No host pointer is emitted.
11485    fn format_terminal_deadlock(&self) -> String {
11486        // ⚠️ ADDING A SECTION HERE? RENDER `dtid` OR A STABLE ORDINAL, NEVER A
11487        // DEBUG-FORMATTED ID. The rule is stated in full in the doc comment above
11488        // and repeated here because that is not where authors edit: the doc
11489        // comment already warned that the obvious `{:?}` implementation is not
11490        // reproducible, and a later change added a section that did it anyway.
11491        //
11492        // A host-influenced counter is the failure that survives review, because
11493        // it LOOKS like a small integer. `{:?}` of a wrapper type, a raw thread
11494        // id, an allocation counter or anything seeded from host state will differ
11495        // run to run while reading like an ordinary index.
11496        //
11497        // Print only identities Detcore already determinizes: dettids, resource
11498        // ids, futex keys, logical deadlines, or a position computed by sorting on
11499        // one of those.
11500        //
11501        // ⚠️ AND EXTEND THE FIXTURE. The determinism test cannot see a section its
11502        // fixture never renders, so a section that only appears under state
11503        // `deadlocked_scheduler` does not build is UNGUARDED however good the
11504        // banned list is. If your section needs different scheduler state, add
11505        // that state to the fixture in the same change.
11506        let mut out = format!(
11507            "Deadlock detected: {}, but no runnable threads left.\n",
11508            self.describe_terminal_waiters()
11509        );
11510        let _ = writeln!(
11511            out,
11512            "  turn {}, committed time {}",
11513            self.turn, self.committed_time
11514        );
11515        let _ = writeln!(out, "  run queue: {} runnable", self.run_queue.len());
11516
11517        let _ = writeln!(out, "  threads ({}), by dettid:", self.next_turns.len());
11518        // `next_turns` is a BTreeMap, so this walk is already ordered.
11519        for (dettid, next_turn) in self.next_turns.iter() {
11520            let _ = writeln!(
11521                out,
11522                "    dtid {}: {}",
11523                dettid,
11524                Self::render_pending_request(&next_turn.req)
11525            );
11526        }
11527
11528        let mut futexes: Vec<String> = self
11529            .blocked
11530            .futex_waiters
11531            .iter()
11532            .filter(|(_, waiters)| !waiters.is_empty())
11533            .map(|(futex_id, waiters)| {
11534                let mut parked: Vec<String> = waiters
11535                    .iter()
11536                    .map(|w| format!("dtid {} (bitset {:#010x})", w.dettid, w.bitset))
11537                    .collect();
11538                parked.sort();
11539                format!(
11540                    "    {}: {}",
11541                    Self::render_futex_id(futex_id),
11542                    parked.join(", ")
11543                )
11544            })
11545            .collect();
11546        futexes.sort();
11547        if futexes.is_empty() {
11548            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters: none");
11549        } else {
11550            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters ({}), by futex:", futexes.len());
11551            for line in futexes {
11552                let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", line);
11553            }
11554        }
11555
11556        let mut timed_out: Vec<DetTid> = self
11557            .blocked
11558            .timed_out_futex_waiters
11559            .iter()
11560            .copied()
11561            .collect();
11562        timed_out.sort();
11563        let _ = writeln!(
11564            out,
11565            "  timed-out futex waiters: {}",
11566            render_tid_list(&timed_out)
11567        );
11568
11569        let timed: Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)> = self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect();
11570        if timed.is_empty() {
11571            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters: none");
11572        } else {
11573            // `TimedEvents` is backed by a BTreeMap keyed on the deadline, so
11574            // this is already in deadline order.
11575            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters ({}), by deadline:", timed.len());
11576            for (deadline, evt) in timed {
11577                let _ = writeln!(out, "    {}: {}", Self::render_deadline(deadline), evt);
11578            }
11579        }
11580
11581        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
11582            let _ = writeln!(out, "  external IO blockers: none");
11583        } else {
11584            // BTreeMap: already ordered by dettid.
11585            let _ = writeln!(
11586                out,
11587                "  external IO blockers ({}), by dettid:",
11588                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len()
11589            );
11590            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.external_io_blockers.iter() {
11591                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
11592            }
11593        }
11594
11595        if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
11596            let _ = writeln!(out, "  rt_sigsuspend blockers: none");
11597        } else {
11598            let _ = writeln!(
11599                out,
11600                "  rt_sigsuspend blockers ({}), by dettid:",
11601                self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len()
11602            );
11603            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.iter() {
11604                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
11605                // The mask recorded when the call was committed, when the
11606                // scheduler models signal targets: a signal it blocks cannot
11607                // end the wait, which is often why nothing can.
11608                if let Some(Some(mask)) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(dettid) {
11609                    let _ = writeln!(out, "      temporary mask {:#x}", mask);
11610                }
11611            }
11612        }
11613
11614        // Both are BTreeSets, so already ordered.
11615        let deferred: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.iter().copied().collect();
11616        let ready: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.iter().copied().collect();
11617        let _ = writeln!(
11618            out,
11619            "  sigchld deferred: {}; sigchld ready: {}",
11620            render_tid_list(&deferred),
11621            render_tid_list(&ready)
11622        );
11623        out
11624    }
11625
11626    /// Report a permanently blocked guest and abort the run.
11627    ///
11628    /// Reached only when the run queue is empty *and* every remaining thread is
11629    /// blocked on something no future scheduler turn can supply. In a
11630    /// sequentialized deterministic run the scheduler is the only source of
11631    /// wakeups, so "no thread can be woken now" is also "no thread can ever be
11632    /// woken": the condition is permanent, not transient. Linux would leave such
11633    /// a process hung forever; reporting it is strictly more useful than
11634    /// reproducing the hang, and it is the established Detcore behaviour for the
11635    /// futex case (`docs/ERROR_CATALOG.md`).
11636    ///
11637    /// `waiters` names *what* is blocked; everything else is shared, so every
11638    /// deadlock class prints the same reproducible shape.
11639    ///
11640    /// Records the report and returns [`SkipTurn`] rather than panicking.
11641    /// `sched_loop_inner` picks it up and exits the container, next to the two
11642    /// existing `--stop-after-*` fatal exits. A panic here would NOT end the
11643    /// run: the scheduler is a `tokio::spawn`ed task whose panic the harness
11644    /// captures, leaving every guest thread parked forever on an
11645    /// `Ivar<SchedResponse>` only the scheduler could fill, so the process hangs
11646    /// until an external timeout kills it. Unwinding out of
11647    /// `do_a_turn_blocking` would also poison the scheduler mutex.
11648    fn report_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> SkipTurn {
11649        let report = self.format_terminal_deadlock();
11650        // A terminal state with threads held at happens-before gates that can
11651        // never open is a fault of the spec, not of Hermit: refuse it by naming
11652        // the BEFORE anchors that never fired, with the deadlock report below
11653        // for diagnosis.
11654        let refusal = self
11655            .happens_before
11656            .as_ref()
11657            .and_then(HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal);
11658        // Keep the first verdict: it names the state that actually wedged.
11659        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
11660            if let Some(refusal) = refusal {
11661                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!("{}\n{}", refusal, report));
11662                self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
11663            } else {
11664                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(report);
11665            }
11666        }
11667        SkipTurn
11668    }
11669
11670    /// [`Self::report_terminal_deadlock`], except while a process Linux is
11671    /// killing for its namespace's end still has a thread
11672    /// ([`Self::awaiting_namespace_zap`]): that thread, often a `pause(2)`
11673    /// with no deadline, is about to die, so the state is not terminal. Spin
11674    /// until the backend reports the kill, as the external-IO wait does, but
11675    /// at most `namespace_zap_valve`: a backend that never reports the death
11676    /// gets a named deadlock instead of an unbounded wait.
11677    fn report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending(&mut self) -> SkipTurn {
11678        if !self.awaiting_namespace_zap() {
11679            self.namespace_zap_wait_since = None;
11680            return self.report_terminal_deadlock();
11681        }
11682        let since = *self
11683            .namespace_zap_wait_since
11684            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
11685        if since.elapsed() < self.namespace_zap_valve {
11686            trace!(
11687                "[scheduler] empty run-queue while Linux kills {:?} for their PID namespace's end. SPINNING!",
11688                &self.namespace_zap_victims
11689            );
11690            std::thread::yield_now();
11691            return SkipTurn;
11692        }
11693        // Past the valve: stop by name. The line carries only DetPids and
11694        // the configured bound, so it is the same on every run.
11695        let first_verdict = self.terminal_deadlock.is_none();
11696        let skip = self.report_terminal_deadlock();
11697        if first_verdict
11698            && !self.terminal_is_refusal
11699            && let Some(report) = self.terminal_deadlock.as_mut()
11700        {
11701            *report = format!(
11702                "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: processes {:?}, which Linux kills because their PID namespace's init exited, were not reported dead within {:?}\n{}",
11703                self.namespace_zap_victims, self.namespace_zap_valve, report
11704            );
11705        }
11706        skip
11707    }
11708
11709    /// Take the pending terminal-deadlock report, if the scheduler produced one.
11710    fn take_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
11711        self.terminal_deadlock.take()
11712    }
11713
11714    /// Test seam: see [`SchedLoopPoint`].
11715    #[cfg(not(test))]
11716    #[inline(always)]
11717    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, _point: SchedLoopPoint) {}
11718
11719    /// Test seam: run the current thread's installed loop probe, if any.
11720    #[cfg(test)]
11721    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, point: SchedLoopPoint) {
11722        test::fire_loop_probe(point, self);
11723    }
11724
11725    fn step2d_handle_empty_queue(
11726        &mut self,
11727        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
11728    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11729        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue);
11730        let decision = self.step2d_decide_empty_queue(global_time);
11731        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue);
11732        decision
11733    }
11734
11735    /// Whether no outstanding external wait can still produce input: none at
11736    /// all (`external_waits_empty`), or only child waits on children that
11737    /// cannot exit (`child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`). Called only
11738    /// where a deadlock verdict needs it, since that analysis walks every
11739    /// process.
11740    fn external_waits_settled(&self, external_waits_empty: bool) -> bool {
11741        external_waits_empty
11742            || (self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
11743                && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
11744                && self.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children())
11745    }
11746
11747    fn step2d_decide_empty_queue(
11748        &mut self,
11749        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
11750    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11751        // Threads whose gate opened were re-admitted by `step2_drain_prefix`;
11752        // threads still parked wait on a source that has not fired. They are
11753        // blocked, not gone: an empty queue with only them (and no timer or
11754        // external input that could let a source run) is a deadlock to report,
11755        // not an exit to fizzle into
11756        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149). A child wait counts
11757        // as input that may still arrive, unless every child it could reap is
11758        // held at a gate: such a child can only exit after it runs, so with
11759        // nothing runnable the wait is part of the deadlock
11760        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
11761        let hb_parked_empty = self
11762            .happens_before
11763            .as_ref()
11764            .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty());
11765        let timed_empty = self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty();
11766        let external_waits_empty = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
11767            && self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty()
11768            && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
11769        let rt_sigsuspend_empty = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty();
11770        let futex_empty = self.blocked.no_futex_waiters();
11771
11772        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
11773            let logically_empty = futex_empty
11774                && timed_empty
11775                && external_waits_empty
11776                && rt_sigsuspend_empty
11777                && hb_parked_empty;
11778            // Report the empty state from logical state alone, BEFORE the
11779            // physical-exit wait below and once per empty state. Both halves are
11780            // what make the line a function of Detcore scheduling.
11781            //
11782            // Before the physical-exit wait: that wait holds the loop for the
11783            // ptrace supervisor's final wait status, which arrives at a
11784            // host-chosen moment. When the report sat after the wait, it was
11785            // logged only if the status had landed before this step ran, and
11786            // otherwise the loop exited without it -- zero or one lines for the
11787            // same logical execution
11788            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360).
11789            //
11790            // Once per empty state: the loop can reach this step again before it
11791            // exits, while it waits for that status or drains a removal queued
11792            // by a dead thread's second, reactive exit hook. How many times it
11793            // does is host timing, and neither thing it waits for is a thread,
11794            // so the state it reports has not changed
11795            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223). See
11796            // `empty_queue_kick_turn`.
11797            //
11798            // The branch's control flow is unchanged: the wait still gates the
11799            // deadlock report and the timer fast-forward, and every path below
11800            // still skips this turn. Only where and how often the line is
11801            // logged changed; the guest cannot observe either.
11802            if !logically_empty {
11803                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
11804            } else if self.empty_queue_kick_turn != Some(self.turn) {
11805                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = Some(self.turn);
11806                // `info!`, and that level is load-bearing. Restored from `trace!`
11807                // by owner ruling after 08ff51a33e demoted it.
11808                //
11809                // THE DEMOTION'S ARGUMENT AND WHY IT WAS REJECTED. It ran: how
11810                // many times this branch is reached depends on when the host
11811                // delivers a child's final wait status, that is an external
11812                // real-time event, an INFO line driven by one is a determinism
11813                // hazard by construction, so keep the loop sub-INFO. The
11814                // measurement offered with it was real -- over 312 concurrent
11815                // SaBRe cell-runs, 4 diverged, and in each the whole difference
11816                // was this line plus one unrelated WARN.
11817                //
11818                // The owner's ruling: this fizzle is part of the deterministic
11819                // scheduling model, not record/replay external-IO terrain, so it
11820                // SHOULD be a deterministic function of detcore scheduling. If it
11821                // is not, that is a hermit DEFECT, and demoting the line hid the
11822                // defect instead of fixing it. The previous note ended "do not
11823                // promote this back without making the host's wait-status
11824                // delivery deterministic, which is not possible" -- but making it
11825                // deterministic is exactly the work owed, not a reason to stop
11826                // reporting it.
11827                //
11828                // AND THE DEFECT IS REAL AND LARGER THAN THIS LINE. Measured
11829                // 2026-08-24 on the CI-staged SaBRe artifact: a guest that forks
11830                // and reaps its child with `wait4(WNOHANG)` diverges 36 of 50
11831                // under `--verify-strict`, while ptrace is 0 of 50 on the same
11832                // guest. The divergence is not confined to logging -- the guest
11833                // ITSELF executes different work, 355 syscalls with 4 `wait4`
11834                // calls in one run against 354 with 3 in the other. The
11835                // scheduler's committed non-poll decisions are byte-identical
11836                // (68 in both), so what varies is how many times the parent is
11837                // told "not yet". Silencing this line would have left that
11838                // unreported.
11839                //
11840                // If this line is noisy again, the fix is to make a child's exit
11841                // become observable to its parent at a deterministic point, not
11842                // to lower the level.
11843                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
11844                    let record_suffix = crate::detlog::record_suffix(
11845                        crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerEmptyQueueKick,
11846                    );
11847                    info!(
11848                        "scheduler (step2_process_blocked): zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.{}",
11849                        record_suffix
11850                    );
11851                }
11852            }
11853            if !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty() {
11854                // The SaBRe plugin has run the child process's logical exit hook, but the ptrace
11855                // supervisor has not received its final wait status. Fast-forwarding the next
11856                // timer here can fire a parent's timeout before the child becomes waitable.
11857                trace!(
11858                    "waiting for physical process exits before empty-queue timer fast-forward: {:?}",
11859                    self.pending_physical_process_exits
11860                );
11861                std::thread::yield_now();
11862                return Err(SkipTurn);
11863            }
11864            // When the run queue is empty, we sometimes need to give things a kick.
11865            if logically_empty {
11866                return Err(SkipTurn);
11867            } else if timed_empty
11868                && (!futex_empty || !rt_sigsuspend_empty || !hb_parked_empty)
11869                && self.external_waits_settled(external_waits_empty)
11870            {
11871                return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending());
11872            } else if !timed_empty {
11873                // Only a *reachable* deadline justifies fast-forwarding the clock.
11874                // `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` is the sentinel a `pause(2)` (or a
11875                // far-future timer that saturated the clock) registers to mean "no
11876                // deadline; wake me on a signal". Because the map is ordered, an
11877                // indefinite front entry means every pending timed event is
11878                // indefinite, so no amount of virtual time can fire any of them.
11879                // Popping it anyway would jump global virtual time by ~584 years and
11880                // grant the sleep as a `ResumeStatus::Normal` wake, which is exactly
11881                // the internal violation `Detcore::handle_pause` refuses to accept.
11882                let next_deadline = self
11883                    .blocked
11884                    .timed_waiters
11885                    .next_deadline()
11886                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
11887                if next_deadline.is_indefinite() {
11888                    if !self.external_waits_settled(external_waits_empty) {
11889                        // Blocking external IO may still complete and produce the
11890                        // signal/wake the indefinite waiter needs, and a child
11891                        // that can still run may exit and end a child wait, so
11892                        // this is not a deadlock yet. Spin as step2c does for the
11893                        // same reason. A child wait on stuck children only
11894                        // (`child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children`) cannot end
11895                        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430).
11896                        trace!(
11897                            "[scheduler] empty run-queue with only indefinite waiters, but external IO is outstanding for dtids {:?}. SPINNING!",
11898                            &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
11899                        );
11900                        std::thread::yield_now();
11901                        return Err(SkipTurn);
11902                    }
11903                    return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending());
11904                }
11905                debug!(
11906                    "[scheduler] Deadlock avoidance! Empty run-queue, so waking next timed event."
11907                );
11908                let (event_ns, evt) = self
11909                    .blocked
11910                    .timed_waiters
11911                    .pop()
11912                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
11913                debug_assert_eq!(event_ns, next_deadline);
11914                self.empty_queue_wakes += 1;
11915                let observed_now = {
11916                    let mut gt = global_time.lock().unwrap();
11917                    let gt_now_ns = gt.as_nanos();
11918                    if event_ns > gt_now_ns {
11919                        info!("[scheduler] Skipping global time ahead to {}.", event_ns);
11920                        let delta = event_ns.duration_since(gt_now_ns);
11921                        detlog_debug!(
11922                            "[sched] add extra global time for deadlock avoidance {:?} on current time {}",
11923                            delta,
11924                            gt_now_ns,
11925                        );
11926                        gt.add_extra_time(delta);
11927                    } else {
11928                        // A control hook may have crossed this deadline after
11929                        // maintenance consumed its one event. Keep the separate
11930                        // empty-queue wake/SkipTurn, without rewinding the clock.
11931                        info!(
11932                            "[scheduler] Waking elapsed timed event at {} with global time {} unchanged.",
11933                            event_ns, gt_now_ns,
11934                        );
11935                    }
11936                    gt.as_nanos()
11937                };
11938
11939                match evt {
11940                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dtid) => self.wake_timed_event(event_ns, dtid),
11941                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, dtid, sig) => {
11942                        self.dispatch_timed_signal(event_ns, id, dtid, sig, false, observed_now)
11943                    }
11944                }
11945                return Err(SkipTurn);
11946            }
11947        } else {
11948            // A queued thread ends any empty state.
11949            self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
11950        }
11951        Ok(())
11952    }
11953
11954    /// Step: Find the next thread to run for this scheduling run.
11955    /// Sometimes the next thread is from the run queue, but it can also be a timed event.
11956    /// Return `None` if the queue is empty.
11957    ///
11958    /// This is a "peek" in the sense that it leaves the thread in the run queue.
11959    fn step3_peek(&mut self) -> Option<(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>)> {
11960        // Re-admit any happens-before threads whose gate opened since last turn.
11961        // Must precede `tentative_pop_next`: the run queue forbids pushes while a
11962        // selection transaction is live.
11963        self.hb_flush_wakes();
11964        debug!(
11965            "[sched-step3] Stepping scheduler, queue len {}, current turn {}, committed_time {}",
11966            self.run_queue.len(),
11967            self.turn,
11968            self.committed_time
11969        );
11970
11971        // Enable for FULL detail:
11972        {
11973            trace!(
11974                "[sched-step3] queue {:?}, io-blocked {:?}, next_turns: ",
11975                &self.run_queue, self.blocked.external_io_blockers
11976            );
11977            for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
11978                trace!(" ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}", dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp);
11979            }
11980            if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
11981                trace!("Timed events: {:?}", self.blocked.timed_waiters);
11982            }
11983        }
11984
11985        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
11986            None
11987        } else {
11988            // While a vfork barrier is in place its child runs first, so the
11989            // vfork interval is a run of the child's turns. A backgrounded
11990            // child is waited for (see `vfork_gated_background_child`), as its
11991            // call's completion is host-timed. When no barrier child is queued
11992            // to run a turn and none is backgrounded (each is blocked on
11993            // another thread or polling a call that is not ready), the queued
11994            // threads run as usual: Linux suspends only the vfork parent, and a
11995            // child that waits for a thread of its own or reads a pipe a sibling
11996            // writes must let that thread run
11997            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194). The parent
11998            // stays out of the run queue until step 2a has seen its release,
11999            // and such a child cannot exec or exit before another thread's turn
12000            // makes its call ready, so no host-timed event ends the interval.
12001            // Under `hermit record` and `hermit replay` a backgrounded child is
12002            // not waited for either: the other threads run, and the child's
12003            // host-timed completion ends the interval at a turn the rejoin log
12004            // records (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211).
12005            let gated_child = self
12006                .vfork_barriers
12007                .values()
12008                .flatten()
12009                .find(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(**child))
12010                .copied();
12011            // A thread woken to take the scheduler's SIGCHLD resumes first,
12012            // whatever its priority, chaos draw or selection heuristic, and
12013            // before even a vfork child (Linux suspends only the vfork
12014            // caller), so it is the thread that takes the process-directed
12015            // copy (`sigchld_takers`).
12016            let taker = self.first_sigchld_taker();
12017            let next_dtid = match self.queued_group_exit_decider().or(taker).or(gated_child) {
12018                Some(child) => self
12019                    .run_queue
12020                    .tentative_pop_tid(child)
12021                    .expect("selected thread disappeared from run queue"),
12022                None if self.vfork_gated_background_child().is_some() => return None,
12023                None => self.run_queue.tentative_pop_next().expect("impossible"),
12024            };
12025            let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
12026                panic!(
12027                "[sched-step3] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
12028                    next_dtid
12029            )
12030            });
12031            Some((next_dtid, nextturn.req.clone(), nextturn.resp.clone()))
12032        }
12033    }
12034
12035    /// Deschedule, but do not clear request/response. This should be used when
12036    /// the turn was skipped because the blocked-on resource is still blocking.
12037    fn skip_turn_blocked(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12038        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Started in step3.
12039        assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while we wait.
12040        trace!(
12041            "[dtid {}] after removal, run queue: {:?}",
12042            dettid, &self.run_queue
12043        );
12044        self.skip_turn()
12045    }
12046
12047    /// Post-await re-check: the selected thread parked (its request resolved
12048    /// `Ok`), but did its `next_turns` entry survive until the daemon got the
12049    /// lock back? If not, the turn must be abandoned.
12050    ///
12051    /// Returns `Err(SkipTurn)` for the abandoned case, after closing the
12052    /// tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Two things hang on that `Err`:
12053    ///
12054    /// * The tentative pop is undone rather than committed, so the selection
12055    ///   does not outlive the turn and the next pass's step2 removal drain does
12056    ///   not call `remove_tid` against a live `tentative_selection` (the same
12057    ///   hygiene the `Err(ThreadExited)` arm needs).
12058    /// * The caller reports a SKIP, not a completed turn. This branch bypasses
12059    ///   steps 4-7, so nothing is blocked, unblocked or re-enqueued -- yet
12060    ///   `bump_global_time` suppresses its advance only on `last_turn.is_err()`
12061    ///   ("if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped").
12062    ///   Reporting `Ok` here therefore added a DETLOG-visible virtual-time tick
12063    ///   for work that never happened, and whether this branch is reached at all
12064    ///   depends on whether teardown cleared `next_turns` inside the host-timed
12065    ///   gap between the await resolving and the re-lock -- so the same logical
12066    ///   execution could gain that tick in one run and not the next.
12067    fn abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12068        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&next_dtid) {
12069            return Ok(());
12070        }
12071        info!(
12072            "[sched-daemon] thread {} exited, skipping over...",
12073            &next_dtid
12074        );
12075        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
12076        Err(SkipTurn)
12077    }
12078
12079    /// Simply advance the turn. This does NOT remove any threads from the
12080    /// runqueue; callers must maintain `run_queue`/`blocking` invariants.
12081    fn skip_turn(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12082        self.turn += 1; // Skipping the turn advances the turn.
12083        Err(SkipTurn)
12084    }
12085
12086    /// Step: Determine if action will block based on current information.  E.g. will it block
12087    /// on a pipe read with no writer? If so, register it in the blocked_pool and issue a "skip".
12088    /// We can go ahead and take resource locks and physically issue the blocking effect if we
12089    /// like.  It's immaterial whether we do that now or later.
12090    ///
12091    /// Postcondition:
12092    ///  - If returning SkipTurn, this function ENDS the Scheduler turn, advancing to the
12093    ///    next (skipping subsequent steps within theturn).  Otherwise, it waits for a
12094    ///    later step end the turn.
12095    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)]
12096    fn step4_resource_block(
12097        &mut self,
12098        dettid: DetTid,
12099        rs: &Resources,
12100        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
12101    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12102        if rs.poll_attempt > 0 {
12103            // The thread is polling and hasn't been "remade" as runnable yet.
12104            info!(
12105                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} polling resource {:?}",
12106                self.turn, dettid, rs
12107            );
12108            // Requeue the thread as a poller
12109            let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
12110            assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
12111            self.run_queue
12112                .push_poller(dettid, self.get_priority(dettid), rs.poll_attempt);
12113            // Before the count reset below hides that this is a retry.
12114            self.note_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid, rs);
12115            trace!(
12116                "[dtid {}] after deprioritizing polling request, run queue: {:?}",
12117                dettid, &self.run_queue
12118            );
12119            self.upgrade_polled_to_runnable(dettid, rs); // Indicate the thread gets to run next time
12120            self.note_poll_deadline(dettid, rs);
12121            self.skip_turn()
12122        } else {
12123            match rs.resources.len() {
12124                0 => Ok(()),
12125                1 => {
12126                    let (rid, perm) = rs.resources.iter().next().unwrap();
12127                    let blocked = self.block_for_one_resource(
12128                        dettid,
12129                        rid,
12130                        perm,
12131                        rs.signal_interrupt_errno(),
12132                        rs.blocked_signal_mask,
12133                        resp,
12134                    );
12135                    if rs.replay_served_from_log
12136                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
12137                        && self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
12138                    {
12139                        self.blocked.replay_log_served.insert(dettid);
12140                    }
12141                    if let ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op) = rid {
12142                        if rs.reads_signalfd
12143                            && self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&dettid) == Some(op)
12144                        {
12145                            self.background_signalfd_reads.insert(dettid, *op);
12146                        } else {
12147                            self.background_signalfd_reads.remove(&dettid);
12148                        }
12149                        // Judged as the call is granted. Other threads' turns may
12150                        // run before the call enters the kernel; the ones that
12151                        // could change what the descriptor reads update the
12152                        // entry (`background_reads`).
12153                        match rs.read_fd.filter(|_| {
12154                            self.recordreplay_modes
12155                                && self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&dettid) == Some(op)
12156                        }) {
12157                            Some((files, fd)) => {
12158                                let signals = self.kernel_signalfd_read_mask(dettid, fd);
12159                                self.background_reads.insert(
12160                                    dettid,
12161                                    BackgroundRead {
12162                                        op: *op,
12163                                        files,
12164                                        fd,
12165                                        signals,
12166                                    },
12167                                );
12168                            }
12169                            None => {
12170                                self.background_reads.remove(&dettid);
12171                            }
12172                        }
12173                    }
12174                    if rs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown
12175                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
12176                        && let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get_mut(&dettid)
12177                    {
12178                        // The call sleeps under a mask this turn could not
12179                        // read faithfully (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`).
12180                        *recorded = None;
12181                    }
12182                    blocked
12183                }
12184                _ => {
12185                    panic!(
12186                        "Requests for more than one resource at a time are not supported yet: {:?}",
12187                        rs
12188                    )
12189                }
12190            }
12191        }
12192    }
12193
12194    /// Replace the request Ivar for `dettid` with a copy with `poll_attempt = 0`,
12195    /// indicating the poll request is runnable on the next trip through the run queue.
12196    ///
12197    /// Precondition: The guest is stopped, so that no one is potentially using the request Ivar.
12198    /// The request Ivar should also be full with the passed resources
12199    fn upgrade_polled_to_runnable(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
12200        // Still the same retry, though now runnable at once
12201        // (`nothing_else_can_run` reads it).
12202        let retry_rs = rs.upgraded_to_runnable();
12203        let runnable_req = Ivar::full(Ok(retry_rs.clone()));
12204        let req = &mut self
12205            .next_turns
12206            .get_mut(&dettid)
12207            .expect("nextturn present")
12208            .req;
12209        debug_assert!(req.try_read().unwrap().is_ok()); // Ivar should be full
12210        trace!(
12211            "[dtid {}] Upgrading polled resource request in {} to runnable non-polled in {}",
12212            dettid, req, runnable_req
12213        );
12214        let previous = std::mem::replace(req, runnable_req.clone());
12215        // This is the same logical operation with a fresh scheduler request.
12216        // Keep parked ownership attached while the daemon holds exclusive access.
12217        self.rebind_parked_request(dettid, &previous, &runnable_req, rs, &retry_rs);
12218    }
12219
12220    /// Helper function. Same postcondition as step4_resource_block
12221    fn block_for_one_resource(
12222        &mut self,
12223        dettid: DetTid,
12224        rid: &ResourceID,
12225        perm: &Permission,
12226        signal_interrupt_errno: Option<i32>,
12227        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
12228        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
12229    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12230        match rid {
12231            ResourceID::SleepUntil(target_ns) => {
12232                if *target_ns <= self.committed_time {
12233                    trace!(
12234                        "[dtid {}] time-based action ready to execute, target time {} is before committed global time {}",
12235                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
12236                    );
12237                    Ok(())
12238                } else if target_ns.is_indefinite() && self.admit_pause_with_due_sigalrm(dettid) {
12239                    // A pause admitted with a due guest-handled SIGALRM returns
12240                    // in this turn instead of parking (`sigalrm`).
12241                    Ok(())
12242                } else {
12243                    trace!(
12244                        "[dtid {}] time-based action not ready yet, registering waiter at future time {}. Current time is {}",
12245                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
12246                    );
12247                    info!(
12248                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} which wanted resource {:?} (blocking)",
12249                        self.turn, dettid, rid
12250                    );
12251                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(*target_ns, dettid);
12252                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
12253                }
12254            }
12255
12256            // Thread BEGINS a blocking syscall outside the runnable set.
12257            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id)
12258            | ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op_id)
12259            | ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id) => {
12260                if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingVfork(_)) {
12261                    self.begin_vfork_barrier(dettid);
12262                    if let Some(origin) = self.next_turns[&dettid].protocol.origin {
12263                        self.vfork_registration_origins.insert(dettid, origin.mm);
12264                    }
12265                }
12266                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(dettid.as_raw(), false);
12267                // A committed turn, as a step-5 grant is (`bound_chaos_starvation`).
12268                self.chaos_passed_over.remove(&dettid);
12269                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
12270                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
12271                        self.turn,
12272                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
12273                        false,
12274                        false,
12275                    );
12276                    info!(
12277                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, BACKGROUND dettid {} (maybe-blocking){}",
12278                        self.turn, dettid, record_suffix
12279                    );
12280                }
12281                // Here we allow the action to execute asynchrounously, in the
12282                // background. The protocol is that it must:
12283                //   (1) not interfere with other internal/external actions (independence),
12284                //   (2) Request a BlockedExternalContinue as the first thing after the external IO is complete.
12285                self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3
12286                assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while in background.
12287
12288                // TODO: Register the action that is occuring in the background:
12289                // let act = self.new_action(Ivar::new());
12290                // self.bg_action_pool.insert(act.action_id, act);
12291
12292                // Unblock guest so that potentially-blocking IO action can get
12293                // started. This intentionally races with subsequent turns the
12294                // scheduler commits, and thus it leans on an assumption of
12295                // non-interference, or on interference *only* affecting the external
12296                // actions that will be recorded anyway.
12297                //
12298                // Record the mask the thread will sleep under BEFORE releasing it:
12299                // its call's own temporary mask, read in its turn, or else its
12300                // current mask, which only it can change and cannot change while
12301                // it is still stopped at this request. Once released, its live
12302                // mask is host-timed (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
12303                //
12304                // Only a scheduler with `models_signal_targets` reads or records
12305                // that mask. Its two readers, `kernel_sigchld_target` (through
12306                // `thread_signal_mask`) and `arm_signaled_background`, run only
12307                // under that flag, and the flag needs
12308                // `supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`, which a
12309                // backend sets only when its `DetTid`s are the host thread IDs
12310                // that `/proc` names (`prepare_backend_config` in
12311                // `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs`). On a backend whose IDs are
12312                // guest-virtual, a `/proc` read of `dettid` would name an
12313                // unrelated host thread or none at all.
12314                let own_mask = self
12315                    .models_signal_targets
12316                    .then(|| self.read_thread_blocked_mask(dettid))
12317                    .flatten();
12318                let sleeping_mask = self
12319                    .models_signal_targets
12320                    .then_some(blocked_signal_mask.or(own_mask));
12321                // A call that will sleep under a temporary mask other than the
12322                // thread's own makes step2 wait until the kernel has installed
12323                // it (`background_entry_barriers`).
12324                // An unreadable own mask is not proof that the masks agree, so
12325                // it arms the barrier too (Codex review of
12326                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
12327                let entry_barrier = self
12328                    .models_signal_targets
12329                    .then_some(blocked_signal_mask)
12330                    .flatten()
12331                    .filter(|temporary| own_mask != Some(*temporary));
12332                // A background grant is this thread's turn: it ends the
12333                // one-turn exclusion and the yield epoch alike.
12334                self.run_queue.consume_yield_exclusion();
12335                self.run_queue.end_yield_epoch();
12336                // The call runs outside the schedule, so no timer signal of
12337                // its process stays observable: decided before it can run
12338                // (4262 design N8-6, `lose_timer_observability`).
12339                self.background_call_ends_timer_observability(self.sigchld_process(dettid));
12340                self.unblock_guest(dettid, resp)?;
12341
12342                // Only once the ivars are cleared and the guest is ready to issue
12343                // BlockedExternalContinue do we record which blocked pool owns it.
12344                let old = if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)) {
12345                    self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
12346                } else {
12347                    self.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
12348                };
12349                assert!(old.is_none(), "thread started a second external operation");
12350                self.background_call_processes
12351                    .insert(self.sigchld_process(dettid));
12352                if let Some(mask) = sleeping_mask {
12353                    self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.insert(dettid, mask);
12354                    let descriptors = !matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_));
12355                    self.note_outside_blocker(dettid, mask, descriptors);
12356                }
12357                if let Some(mask) = entry_barrier {
12358                    self.background_entry_barriers.insert(
12359                        dettid,
12360                        BackgroundEntry {
12361                            mask,
12362                            since: std::time::Instant::now(),
12363                        },
12364                    );
12365                }
12366                if let Some(signal) = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(&dettid) {
12367                    self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
12368                } else if let Some(Some(mask)) = sleeping_mask {
12369                    self.arm_for_waiting_scheduler_signal(dettid, mask);
12370                }
12371                Err(SkipTurn)
12372            }
12373
12374            // Thread CONTINUES after completing [potentially] blocking IO.
12375            ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(_) => {
12376                // We leave the thread out of the run-queue.  At the point we put it back
12377                // in, this resource request is immediately granted.
12378                Ok(())
12379            }
12380
12381            ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec } => {
12382                if self.ready_child_wait(*parent, *spec).is_some()
12383                    || !self.has_child_wait_target(*parent, *spec)
12384                {
12385                    Ok(())
12386                } else {
12387                    info!(
12388                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for child {:?}",
12389                        self.turn, dettid, spec
12390                    );
12391                    assert!(
12392                        self.blocked
12393                            .child_waiters
12394                            .insert(dettid, (*parent, *spec))
12395                            .is_none()
12396                    );
12397                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
12398                }
12399            }
12400
12401            ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child) => {
12402                if self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(&dettid) {
12403                    Ok(())
12404                } else {
12405                    info!(
12406                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for physical child {}",
12407                        self.turn, dettid, child
12408                    );
12409                    let completion_already_observed =
12410                        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(child);
12411                    assert!(
12412                        self.blocked
12413                            .physical_child_waiters
12414                            .entry(*child)
12415                            .or_default()
12416                            .insert(dettid)
12417                    );
12418                    let skipped = self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
12419                    if completion_already_observed {
12420                        self.wake_physical_child_waiters(*child);
12421                    }
12422                    skipped
12423                }
12424            }
12425
12426            // Thread requests change in priority
12427            ResourceID::PriorityChangePoint(prio, change_time, rcbs, epochs) => {
12428                self.perform_priority_changepoint(dettid, *prio, *change_time, *rcbs, epochs)
12429            }
12430
12431            // For now, all other resource types are immediately granted.
12432            // (TODO/FIXME: handle the entire set of resource requests.)
12433            ResourceID::FileContents(_) => Ok(()),
12434            ResourceID::FileMetadata(_) => Ok(()),
12435            ResourceID::DirectoryContents(_) => Ok(()),
12436            ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(_) => Ok(()),
12437            ResourceID::Path(_) => Ok(()),
12438            ResourceID::PathsTransitive(_) => Ok(()),
12439            ResourceID::Device(_) => Ok(()),
12440            // The scheduler-ordered `Exit` grant is the deterministic moment a
12441            // child process leaves the run set. Register a one-shot child-exit
12442            // `SIGCHLD` for the reaping parent, to be delivered at a deterministic
12443            // logical time by `step2b_process_timed`, instead of relying on the
12444            // host-async kernel `SIGCHLD` whose arrival time is host-timed (the
12445            // `make -jN` / redis `--strict --verify` nondeterminism source).
12446            // A backend that registered a PIDFD_THREAD already preserves the
12447            // kernel's native child-exit signal. Sending another SIGCHLD through
12448            // that pidfd would make the application observe both CLD_EXITED and
12449            // SI_TKILL for one child, so only the scheduler wait readiness is
12450            // synthesized on that path.
12451            ResourceID::Exit { group, process, mm } => {
12452                if self.group_exit_decider == Some(dettid) {
12453                    self.group_exit_decider = None;
12454                }
12455                if self.exit_awaits_sibling_permit(dettid, *process) {
12456                    info!(
12457                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {}'s exit behind a sibling's signal delivery",
12458                        self.turn, dettid
12459                    );
12460                    self.parked.exits_awaiting_permit.insert(dettid);
12461                    return self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
12462                }
12463                let reserve_mode = match self.reserve_exit_boundary(dettid, *process, *mm, *group) {
12464                    Ok(mode) => mode,
12465                    Err(failure) => {
12466                        self.fail_parked(dettid, failure);
12467                        // fail_parked linearizes terminal failure and closes
12468                        // the tentative selection. Do not undo it a second
12469                        // time through skip_turn_blocked.
12470                        return Err(SkipTurn);
12471                    }
12472                };
12473                // A grant that ends its process fixes the process's logical
12474                // exit between committed turns (`reparent_orphans`). The
12475                // process is the one the thread tree registered the exiting
12476                // thread in: for a raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit
12477                // signal, the backend's `process` names its creator instead.
12478                if let Some(exiting) = self.registered_process(dettid)
12479                    && (*group
12480                        || !self
12481                            .thread_tree
12482                            .my_thread_group(&exiting)
12483                            .into_iter()
12484                            .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid)))
12485                {
12486                    self.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(exiting);
12487                    self.note_pid_namespace_end(exiting);
12488                }
12489                // An exit_group ends every thread of the group, and on a
12490                // backend that reports exits before the kernel runs them each
12491                // thread's native exit walks its robust list and clears its
12492                // TID. No turn runs until all of them are done.
12493                if *group && let Some(exiting) = self.registered_process(dettid) {
12494                    self.hold_turns_until_the_group_ends(exiting);
12495                }
12496                // The grant is a vfork child's release edge: a barrier whose
12497                // parent has died ends here, inside this committed turn.
12498                self.release_vfork_child(dettid);
12499                // The thread leaves by its own committed exit, not by dying
12500                // with its process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
12501                self.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
12502                let last_live_thread = !self
12503                    .thread_tree
12504                    .my_thread_group(process)
12505                    .into_iter()
12506                    .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
12507                // An exit that ends its process leaves the host some time after
12508                // this grant. Hold turn selection from here until the backend
12509                // reports the process physically gone (asynchronous exit
12510                // completion), so no peer observes its descriptors still open.
12511                if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
12512                    && (*group || last_live_thread)
12513                {
12514                    self.begin_exit_at_grant(*process);
12515                }
12516                // Whether this grant ends `process`, as far as its parent's
12517                // notification goes: an `exit_group`, or the raw `exit` of its
12518                // last live thread, which Linux ends exactly as an
12519                // `exit_group` (statically linked busybox leaves that way).
12520                // A raw exit counts only where `process` is the exiting
12521                // thread's own process: for a raw clone child with a
12522                // non-SIGCHLD exit signal the backend names its creator
12523                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4012).
12524                let ends_process = *group
12525                    || (last_live_thread && self.registered_process(dettid) == Some(*process));
12526                self.child_exit_sigchld
12527                    .settle_exit_grant(dettid, *process, *group, ends_process);
12528                // The parent's child-exit notification is placed for every
12529                // grant that ends the process. Before, only an `exit_group`
12530                // registered the `ChildExit` timer, so a parent waiting in
12531                // `rt_sigsuspend` for the SIGCHLD of a child whose last thread
12532                // left through raw `exit` could be woken only by the kernel's
12533                // own copy, at a host-timed moment, and the empty run queue was
12534                // usually reported as a deadlock first
12535                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3895).
12536                if reserve_mode == signal_control::ExitReserveMode::Uncontrolled
12537                    && ends_process
12538                    && let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(process)
12539                    && self.should_synthesize_child_exit_signal(parent)
12540                {
12541                    // The hold waits for the backend's report that `process`
12542                    // is consumed, so it is sound only if this grant ends that
12543                    // process: the exiting thread must belong to it in the
12544                    // thread tree. A backend can name another process here
12545                    // (a raw clone child's exit_group named its creator before
12546                    // Reverie built such a child as its own process,
12547                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4012); such a
12548                    // grant keeps the synthetic timer it had before Phase A.
12549                    let ends_named_process =
12550                        if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&dettid) {
12551                            dettid == *process
12552                        } else {
12553                            self.registered_process(dettid) == Some(*process)
12554                        };
12555                    // A child whose exit signal is not SIGCHLD (a raw clone
12556                    // with exit signal 0 or SIGUSR1) is not notified with
12557                    // SIGCHLD: Linux sends its own exit signal, if any, and the
12558                    // kernel delivers that itself, so there is nothing to
12559                    // synthesize and nothing to hold.
12560                    let non_sigchld_exit_signal = ends_named_process
12561                        && matches!(
12562                            self.thread_tree.notification_signal(*process),
12563                            Some(signal) if signal != libc::SIGCHLD
12564                        );
12565                    let notification = if non_sigchld_exit_signal {
12566                        None
12567                    } else if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
12568                        Some(self.classify_child_exit_notification(*process, parent))
12569                    } else {
12570                        Some(ChildExitNotification::Undecided)
12571                    };
12572                    match notification {
12573                        None => {}
12574                        // Linux generates nothing (explicit SIG_IGN) or discards
12575                        // the signal at generation (default-ignored, unblocked),
12576                        // so the guest observes no SIGCHLD from Linux. Send no
12577                        // synthetic one: no alarm, no physical send, no wake of
12578                        // the parent. The traced parent still receives the
12579                        // kernel's own notification, which this hold places at
12580                        // the first scheduling pass after the backend reports its
12581                        // publication.
12582                        Some(ChildExitNotification::None | ChildExitNotification::Discard) => {
12583                            // A publication already reported (the process was
12584                            // consumed before this grant) needs no hold: the
12585                            // kernel has already notified the parent.
12586                            if !self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(process) {
12587                                self.child_exit_publications_pending.insert(*process);
12588                            }
12589                        }
12590                        // Caught, blocked and every state Hermit cannot classify
12591                        // keep the synthetic SIGCHLD.
12592                        Some(ChildExitNotification::Deliver | ChildExitNotification::Undecided) => {
12593                            // Fire strictly after the current committed time so the event
12594                            // is dispatched on a subsequent scheduler pass.
12595                            //
12596                            // Linux sends the child's exit signal to its parent thread,
12597                            // the one that created it, and prefers that thread when it
12598                            // picks which thread of the process takes the signal
12599                            // (`do_notify_parent` -> `complete_signal`). Where gated
12600                            // waits model interruption, the timer carries that thread
12601                            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146), so a
12602                            // creator that does not block `SIGCHLD` takes it and the
12603                            // leader's wait is left alone. Elsewhere it keeps naming
12604                            // the leader (DetTid == DetPid for a group leader).
12605                            let deadline = self.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
12606                            let parent_thread = if self.models_signal_targets {
12607                                self.thread_tree
12608                                    .process_wait
12609                                    .get(process)
12610                                    .map_or(parent, |metadata| metadata.wait_owner)
12611                            } else {
12612                                parent
12613                            };
12614                            // Where the kernel also sends its own, the first of the
12615                            // two delivered stands for the exit, the other is
12616                            // dropped, and the scheduler's gets Linux's siginfo
12617                            // (`child_exit_sigchld`).
12618                            if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
12619                                self.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, *process);
12620                            }
12621                            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
12622                                deadline,
12623                                *process,
12624                                parent,
12625                                parent_thread,
12626                            );
12627                        }
12628                    }
12629                }
12630                // The status reported for the process is consumed by a grant
12631                // that ends it (`settle_exit_grant` placed it, and `own` took
12632                // it if the notification is the scheduler's own).
12633                if ends_process {
12634                    self.child_exit_sigchld.forget_exit_status(*process);
12635                }
12636                Ok(())
12637            }
12638            ResourceID::ParentContinue { .. } => Ok(()),
12639            ResourceID::InternalIOPolling => Ok(()),
12640            ResourceID::FutexWait => Ok(()),
12641            ResourceID::TraceReplay => Ok(()),
12642            ResourceID::SchedYield => Ok(()),
12643            ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm => Ok(()),
12644
12645            // A guest thread checking in at a happens-before anchor point. Delegate
12646            // to the enforcement logic, which either grants passage (firing anchors)
12647            // or parks the thread until its gating BEFORE anchor fires.
12648            ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(count) => self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, &[]),
12649            ResourceID::HappensBeforeSyscallCheckpoint { count, anchors } => {
12650                self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, anchors)
12651            }
12652            ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
12653                count,
12654                anchors,
12655                code,
12656            } => self.hb_posthook_interrupted(dettid, *count, anchors, code),
12657
12658            // A host-async SIGCHLD (a guest child process exited) is delivered to
12659            // the parent at a moment decided by host timing. Committing that turn
12660            // immediately makes the signal race whatever guest work was already
12661            // runnable (e.g. a `make -jN` jobserver `pselect6` continuation),
12662            // which diverges under `--strict --verify`. Defer it deterministic-
12663            // work-first: park the parent out of the run queue and let
12664            // `step2e_process_signal_deferred` re-admit it once no ordinary guest
12665            // work remains, mirroring the `external_io_blockers` policy. Signals
12666            // that the scheduler itself synthesizes deterministically (timers via
12667            // `fire_alarm`) are never SIGCHLD and are unaffected.
12668            ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_) => Ok(()),
12669            // A still-queued sleep the scheduler woke for its own signal is
12670            // granted at once, and keeps `sigchld_ready` for the delivery
12671            // (`woken_sleeps`).
12672            ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) if self.blocked.woken_sleeps.remove(&dettid) => Ok(()),
12673            ResourceID::InboundSignal(sig) => {
12674                // The thread's own request at a delivery stop
12675                // (`handle_signal_event`, read-write) follows the kernel's
12676                // dequeue of this signal for it: a timer's copy of it there is
12677                // consumed. The scheduler's wakes of a signaled sleeper ask
12678                // for the same resource write-only, and deliver nothing.
12679                if *perm == Permission::RW {
12680                    self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(dettid, sig.raw()));
12681                    self.note_process_signal_taken(dettid, sig.raw());
12682                    if sig.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
12683                        self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(&dettid);
12684                    }
12685                }
12686                // `sigchld_ready` marks a parent step2e has already re-admitted,
12687                // or a delivery the scheduler already placed; grant it now rather
12688                // than deferring it (a second time). Where the scheduler models
12689                // signal targets, a delivery of a copy it sent is marked for the
12690                // very thread that took it (`dequeue_sigchld`).
12691                let already_readmitted = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&dettid);
12692                if sig.signal() == Some(Signal::SIGCHLD)
12693                    && signal_interrupt_errno.is_none()
12694                    && !already_readmitted
12695                    && self.run_queue.has_runnable_besides(dettid)
12696                {
12697                    self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
12698                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
12699                    self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(dettid);
12700                    Err(SkipTurn)
12701                } else {
12702                    Ok(())
12703                }
12704            }
12705        }
12706    }
12707
12708    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-868): Review the vfork registration scheduler barrier.
12709    pub(crate) fn complete_vfork_registration(&mut self, parent: DetTid, child: DetTid) {
12710        if self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent) {
12711            // The parent died before this registration; its barrier is already
12712            // cancelled. The child registers as any orphan does.
12713            self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
12714            return;
12715        }
12716        let registered_child = self
12717            .vfork_barriers
12718            .get_mut(&parent)
12719            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("vfork child registered without a pending parent {parent}"));
12720        assert!(registered_child.replace(child).is_none());
12721        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
12722    }
12723
12724    /// Authenticate the child address space against the exact parent grant,
12725    /// before a reused child TID has a registration of its own. The caller also
12726    /// checks the immutable RPC sender and the backend's vfork/serialized-fork
12727    /// mode; this predicate neither consumes the barrier nor opens admission.
12728    pub(crate) fn pending_vfork_registration_matches(
12729        &self,
12730        parent: DetTid,
12731        process: DetPid,
12732        child: DetTid,
12733        child_mm: MmId,
12734        shares_vm: bool,
12735    ) -> bool {
12736        let Some(parent_mm) = self.vfork_registration_origins.get(&parent).copied() else {
12737            return false;
12738        };
12739        parent != child
12740            && self.registered_process(parent) == Some(process)
12741            && self.next_turns.contains_key(&parent)
12742            && !self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
12743            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(parent)
12744            && self.rpc_incarnation_matches(parent, parent_mm)
12745            && self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent) == Some(&None)
12746            && MmId::for_clone(parent_mm, child, shares_vm) == child_mm
12747    }
12748
12749    /// Inner helper for just the core priority changing.
12750    fn requeue_with_new_priority(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, new_priority: Priority) {
12751        // TODO: do we want to record in preemption_writer if we are in schedule-trace-replay mode?
12752        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
12753        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
12754        let _old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
12755        let present = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
12756        if present {
12757            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
12758        }
12759        trace!(
12760            "[dettid {}] requeue: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
12761            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
12762        );
12763    }
12764
12765    /// Bound how long chaos priority change points can keep passing a runnable
12766    /// thread over (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4374).
12767    ///
12768    /// Under chaos a thread draws its priority at creation and redraws it only
12769    /// at the end of its own slice, so a thread that never runs never redraws.
12770    /// Behind a thread that never blocks (a busy-wait on non-blocking calls), a
12771    /// new thread with a poor draw waited until the spinner happened to draw
12772    /// worse still: at a priority of 9820 out of 10000, about 55 slices of
12773    /// 200 ms of virtual time on average, and on ptrace about 1 seed in 8 of a
12774    /// busy-wait guest hung for minutes.
12775    ///
12776    /// It applies only where every change point is a random draw at the end of
12777    /// a timer slice (`chaos_bounds_starvation`): under chaos with timer
