12778    /// preemption, a `sched_yield` takes the yield epoch or a weak yield, never
12779    /// a change point (`sched_yield_route`). It never rewrites a priority that
12780    /// was chosen rather than drawn: none under a preemption or schedule
12781    /// replay, and none under `--sched-heuristic=connectbind`, whose connect and
12782    /// bind set the first and last priorities. Under the random heuristics a
12783    /// priority does not decide the turn: each turn draws among the queued
12784    /// threads, so a thread that never runs is not held back by a draw it made
12785    /// once.
12786    ///
12787    /// Each runnable (non-polling) thread that `dettid`'s new priority still
12788    /// beats counts one more pass. A thread passed over at
12789    /// [`CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND`] such change points since its last committed
12790    /// turn moves ahead: `dettid` takes the priority one below it (numerically
12791    /// one greater, capped at `LAST_PRIORITY`), so the passed-over thread keeps
12792    /// the lead for all its turns until it blocks, or until `dettid`'s next
12793    /// change point draws again. A thread's count restarts at its committed
12794    /// turn and goes when its blocking entries are removed (it retires, or a
12795    /// forced wake requeues it).
12796    ///
12797    /// Deterministic: it reads only the priority map and run-queue membership
12798    /// at this change point, in thread-ID order, and counts change only at
12799    /// change points and committed turns; run-queue membership is the same
12800    /// input turn selection reads. The priority it returns is the one recorded
12801    /// for `dettid`, so a preemption replay restores it as a fixed priority.
12802    fn bound_chaos_starvation(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, drawn: Priority) -> Priority {
12803        if !self.chaos_bounds_starvation || self.replayer.is_some() {
12804            return drawn;
12805        }
12806        let queued: Vec<(DetTid, Priority)> = self
12807            .priorities
12808            .iter()
12809            .filter(|(tid, _)| **tid != dettid && self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(**tid))
12810            .map(|(tid, prio)| (*tid, *prio))
12811            .collect();
12812        let starving = queued
12813            .iter()
12814            .filter(|(tid, prio)| {
12815                *prio > drawn
12816                    && self.chaos_passed_over.get(tid).copied().unwrap_or(0) + 1
12817                        >= CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND
12818            })
12819            .map(|(_, prio)| *prio)
12820            .max();
12821        let priority = starving.map_or(drawn, |prio| (prio + 1).min(runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY));
12822        for (tid, prio) in queued {
12823            if prio > priority {
12824                *self.chaos_passed_over.entry(tid).or_insert(0) += 1;
12825            }
12826        }
12827        if priority != drawn {
12828            info!(
12829                "[scheduler] chaos change point of dettid {}: priority {} drawn, {} taken, behind a thread passed over at {} change points",
12830                dettid, drawn, priority, CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND
12831            );
12832        }
12833        priority
12834    }
12835
12836    /// Helper for priority changepoint logic
12837    ///
12838    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
12839    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
12840    ///
12841    /// Postcondition: Same as block_for_one_resource. However, always returns SkipTurn, because the
12842    /// priority changepoint may not allow the current thread to continue in a regular turn (i.e.
12843    /// doing actual work).
12844    fn perform_priority_changepoint(
12845        &mut self,
12846        dettid: DetTid,
12847
12848        new_priority: Priority,
12849        guest_time: LogicalTime,
12850        guest_rcbs: u64,
12851        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
12852        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1151)
12853        chaos_epochs: &[crate::resources::ChaosEpochTransition],
12854    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
12855        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
12856        let new_priority = self.bound_chaos_starvation(dettid, new_priority);
12857        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
12858        let old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
12859
12860        // Do not attempt to record preemptions/priorities when we're dictated by a raw schedule replay.
12861        if self.replayer.is_none()
12862            && let Some(pw) = &mut self.preemption_writer
12863        {
12864            let old_prio = old_priority.unwrap();
12865            debug!(
12866                "[dtid {}] Recording preemption point, current time {} prior priority {} (next priority {})",
12867                dettid, guest_time, old_prio, new_priority
12868            );
12869            for transition in chaos_epochs {
12870                pw.insert_chaos_epoch(dettid, *transition);
12871            }
12872            pw.insert_reprioritization(dettid, guest_time, guest_rcbs, old_prio, new_priority);
12873            pw.set_current(dettid, new_priority);
12874        }
12875
12876        let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
12877        // A change point ends any yield epoch. At a timer expiry the thread ran
12878        // the slice that just ended: a turn of a thread that did not yield. The
12879        // other source, a chaos `sched_yield` with the timer disabled (GH #81),
12880        // takes the change-point route instead of the epoch, so no epoch it
12881        // could end is open on its account.
12882        self.run_queue.end_yield_epoch();
12883        assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
12884        self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
12885        trace!(
12886            "[dettid {}] changepoint: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
12887            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
12888        );
12889
12890        // Update request to be empty so the thread is unconditionally
12891        // runnable when it next comes up in the queue.
12892        let empty_req = Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(dettid)));
12893        trace!(
12894            "[dettid {}] Priority change point emplaced empty resource request at new {}",
12895            dettid, empty_req
12896        );
12897        self.next_turns
12898            .get_mut(&dettid)
12899            .expect("nextturn present")
12900            .req = empty_req;
12901        info!(
12902            "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, dettid {} changed priority to {}",
12903            self.turn, dettid, new_priority
12904        );
12905        self.skip_turn() // The thread shouldn't run.
12906    }
12907
12908    fn step1_check_quiescence(
12909        &mut self,
12910        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
12911        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
12912    ) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
12913        // TODO: actually check resource availability to enable asynchronous background activities!
12914        let outstanding = self.are_all_quiesced();
12915        if outstanding.is_none() {
12916            self.bump_global_time(global_time, last_turn);
12917        }
12918        outstanding
12919    }
12920
12921    fn is_internal_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
12922        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::TraceReplay)
12923    }
12924
12925    /// A turn that only grants `InternalIOPolling`, i.e. a retry of a nonblocking
12926    /// poll/epoll/select/futex/recv/... injected by the blocking-via-polling machinery
12927    /// (see `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`). The *number* of such retries before a
12928    /// file descriptor becomes ready is wall-clock dependent when the readiness is driven
12929    /// by an external actor (e.g. a child linker process draining a pipe), so it varies
12930    /// between otherwise-identical runs.
12931    fn is_polling_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
12932        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
12933    }
12934
12935    /// Which retry of its call a request is: `poll_attempt`, or the one a
12936    /// skipped retry had before it was made runnable (`upgraded_from_attempt`).
12937    fn retry_number(rs: &Resources) -> u32 {
12938        rs.poll_attempt.max(rs.upgraded_from_attempt)
12939    }
12940
12941    /// A retry after an attempt that moved nothing: the thread waits on what
12942    /// another must do.
12943    fn waits_after_a_failed_attempt(rs: &Resources) -> bool {
12944        Self::retry_number(rs) > 0 && !rs.previous_attempt_made_progress
12945    }
12946
12947    /// A second or later retry of one call after an attempt that moved
12948    /// nothing: the thread's previous grant was for that same call, and its
12949    /// attempt moved nothing. A first retry (`1`) follows a grant in which the
12950    /// thread may have finished other calls first, which counts as progress.
12951    fn retries_its_call_without_progress(rs: &Resources) -> bool {
12952        Self::retry_number(rs) > 1 && !rs.previous_attempt_made_progress
12953    }
12954
12955    /// Whether no guest thread other than `dtid` can make progress unless a
12956    /// host acts or a timer fires, judged from scheduler state alone at
12957    /// `dtid`'s commit (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/2203>).
12958    /// Every other registered thread must be one of:
12959    ///
12960    /// - queued as a poller whose attempts depend only on guest actions
12961    ///   (`Resources::polls_guest_state_only`), whatever its backoff, whose
12962    ///   request retries after an attempt that moved nothing
12963    ///   (`waits_after_a_failed_attempt`), made no earlier than the latest
12964    ///   progress: its latest commit (`last_commit_at`) is at or after every
12965    ///   turn known to be progress (`last_progress`) and every other poller's
12966    ///   grant whose thread's request does not repeat that call without
12967    ///   progress (`retries_its_call_without_progress`);
12968    /// - parked as a futex waiter, a child waiter, an `rt_sigsuspend` waiter,
12969    ///   at a happens-before gate, in a timed wait, or in a call that waits on
12970    ///   a host (external IO): with nothing else able to run, only one of
12971    ///   those pollers, a host or a timer could wake it.
12972    ///
12973    /// A thread in neither state is runnable work, is running, or awaits
12974    /// admission to the run queue, so something else can run; so can a thread
12975    /// queued after `sched_yield` or polling what a host can change. The answer
12976    /// leans to "something else can run", which only keeps a FIFO open
12977    /// polling. When it is "nothing", the caller still waits for any timer due
12978    /// at a finite deadline first (`unblock_guest`).
12979    fn nothing_else_can_run(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> bool {
12980        // A grant counts as progress unless the thread's current request
12981        // repeats that grant's call after an attempt that moved nothing.
12982        let progress = self
12983            .guest_state_polled_at
12984            .iter()
12985            .filter(|&(&tid, _)| tid != dtid)
12986            .filter(|&(&tid, _)| {
12987                !self
12988                    .next_turns
12989                    .get(&tid)
12990                    .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
12991                    .is_some_and(
12992                        |req| matches!(req, Ok(rs) if Self::retries_its_call_without_progress(&rs)),
12993                    )
12994            })
12995            .map(|(_, &grant)| grant)
12996            .fold(self.last_progress, u64::max);
12997        self.next_turns
12998            .keys()
12999            .filter(|&&tid| tid != dtid)
13000            .all(|&tid| {
13001                let idle_poller = self.run_queue.contains_tid(tid)
13002                    && self
13003                        .last_commit_at
13004                        .get(&tid)
13005                        .is_some_and(|&commit| commit >= progress)
13006                    && self
13007                        .next_turns
13008                        .get(&tid)
13009                        .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
13010                        .is_some_and(|req| {
13011                            matches!(req, Ok(rs) if Self::is_polling_turn(&rs)
13012                            && rs.polls_guest_state_only
13013                            && Self::waits_after_a_failed_attempt(&rs))
13014                        });
13015                let parked_futex = self.next_turns.get(&tid).is_some_and(is_futex_request)
13016                    && self
13017                        .blocked
13018                        .futex_waiters
13019                        .values()
13020                        .any(|waiters| waiters.iter().any(|waiter| waiter.dettid == tid));
13021                let parked = parked_futex
13022                    || self.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&tid)
13023                    || self
13024                        .blocked
13025                        .physical_child_waiters
13026                        .values()
13027                        .any(|waiters| waiters.contains(&tid))
13028                    || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&tid)
13029                    || self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&tid)
13030                    || self.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(tid).is_some()
13031                    || self
13032                        .happens_before
13033                        .as_ref()
13034                        .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&tid));
13035                idle_poller || parked
13036            })
13037    }
13038
13039    /// A backend whose internal pipe turns are host-timed (today SaBRe) discovers an
13040    /// inherited stdio pipe as a device resource before the inner
13041    /// `InternalIOPolling` request. Both turns belong to one host-timing-sensitive pipe
13042    /// operation, so their logical-time logging must use the same retry normalization.
13043    fn is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
13044        rsrcs.fyi == HOST_TIMED_INTERNAL_PIPE_IO_FYI
13045    }
13046
13047    /// A strong yield issued, on a backend whose loopback pollers yield to their peers
13048    /// (today SaBRe), before a zero-timeout poll while the task owns a
13049    /// loopback connection. Its count is kernel-readiness timing, not guest-visible progress.
13050    fn is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
13051        rsrcs.fyi == LOOPBACK_POLL_YIELD_FYI
13052    }
13053
13054    /// A turn that commits only `InboundSignal` resources: a thread's signal
13055    /// stop asking to take the signal.
13056    fn is_inbound_signal_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
13057        !rsrcs.resources.is_empty()
13058            && rsrcs
13059                .resources
13060                .keys()
13061                .all(|id| matches!(id, ResourceID::InboundSignal(_)))
13062    }
13063
13064    fn is_x_turn(rsrcs: &Resources, x: &ResourceID) -> bool {
13065        if rsrcs.resources.contains_key(x) {
13066            if rsrcs.resources.len() > 1 {
13067                panic!(
13068                    "is_x_turn: not expecting an {:?} mixed in with other resource requests: {:?}",
13069                    x, rsrcs
13070                );
13071            }
13072            true
13073        } else {
13074            false
13075        }
13076    }
13077
13078    /// Tick global logical time due to represent the work of the scheduler itself.
13079    /// Also, update committed time.
13080    /// Prerequisite: all threads are parked, with their time contributions frozen.
13081    fn bump_global_time(
13082        &mut self,
13083        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
13084        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
13085    ) {
13086        // An internal IO-polling retry (see `is_polling_turn`) must still advance logical
13087        // time -- finite poll/epoll/select/futex timeouts are enforced by comparing observed
13088        // logical time against the deadline in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`, so freezing
13089        // time here would turn a timed wait into an infinite spin. But because the *count* of
13090        // these retries is host-timing nondeterministic, we keep their time-advance out of the
13091        // determinism log (DETLOG). This makes the `--verify` deterministic comparison
13092        // insensitive to retry count; the matching `{InternalIOPolling: ...}` COMMIT turn is
13093        // likewise excluded in `logdiff::is_internal_io_poll_commit`. Time values still shift
13094        // between runs, but those are numerically normalized before comparison.
13095        let last_turn_was_polling = last_turn
13096            .as_ref()
13097            .map(|resources| {
13098                Self::is_polling_turn(resources)
13099                    || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(resources)
13100                    || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(resources)
13101            })
13102            .unwrap_or(false);
13103
13104        // A turn that only delivers signals to the thread whose committed turn
13105        // came last, with no other thread in between, is not a context switch:
13106        // Linux runs the handler on the running thread's own timeslice.
13107        // Charging it a scheduler turn made a periodic timer whose period is at
13108        // most one turn charge expire again during every delivery, so the guest
13109        // ran nothing but its handler
13110        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). The previous turn
13111        // is the last committed one other than a host-timed polling retry
13112        // (`last_turn_was_polling`); skipped turns do not count. So the rule
13113        // also frees the signal wake of a thread asleep in pause, nanosleep or
13114        // a futex wait when that thread had the previous turn. Both inputs are
13115        // committed turns that both runs of --verify share, so they decide
13116        // alike. Record and replay keep the charge, as they keep the deadline
13117        // cap, so recordings keep their time stream and RECORD_VERSION is
13118        // unchanged.
13119        let own_signal_delivery = !self.recordreplay_modes
13120            && last_turn.as_ref().is_ok_and(|resources| {
13121                self.previous_turn_tid == Some(resources.tid)
13122                    && Self::is_inbound_signal_turn(resources)
13123            });
13124
13125        // At this moment, when threads are parked, we know that the global_time is
13126        // frozen and we can read it without any race.
13127        let snapshot: LogicalTime = {
13128            let mut gtime = global_time.lock().unwrap();
13129
13130            if self.run_queue.is_empty() && self.blocked.only_external_blocked() {
13131                // TODO(T112017687): rationalize the occurence of
13132                // BlockingExternalIO in strict runs. For example, we should
13133                // probably inject nanosleep and actually wait the intervening
13134                // time, so we don't appear too fast to external observers.
13135                trace!(
13136                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because we're ONLY waiting for external events"
13137                );
13138            } else if last_turn.is_err() {
13139                // Note: if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped. But since we
13140                // can't see the future, we just cancel out the bump by not doing a bump this turn.
13141                trace!(
13142                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn did not progress (i.e. SkipTurn)"
13143                );
13144            } else if last_turn
13145                .as_ref()
13146                .map(Self::is_internal_turn)
13147                .unwrap_or(false)
13148            {
13149                trace!(
13150                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn was an internal book-keeping one"
13151                );
13152            } else if !last_turn_was_polling
13153                && last_turn
13154                    .as_ref()
13155                    .map(|resources| resources.backend_runtime_bootstrap)
13156                    .unwrap_or(false)
13157            {
13158                // The turn served a syscall that a backend-resident runtime made
13159                // inside its bootstrap window and whose syscall cost is withheld
13160                // (`ThreadState::charge_syscall_time`). Per Reverie's
13161                // `Guest::is_backend_runtime_bootstrap` contract that work is not
13162                // the guest's, so its turn must not advance the guest's clock
13163                // either: a backend without such a runtime never makes this turn,
13164                // so charging it would add time that only one backend's guests
13165                // see. An IO-polling retry is
13166                // excluded above and still advances, because finite poll and
13167                // futex timeouts are enforced against this clock. The decision is
13168                // a function of the request alone, which the guest's own
13169                // execution determines, so both runs of --verify and a replay
13170                // make it identically.
13171                trace!(
13172                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld"
13173                );
13174            } else if own_signal_delivery {
13175                trace!(
13176                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn delivered a signal to the thread already running"
13177                );
13178            } else {
13179                let newtime = match gtime.add_scheduler_time() {
13180                    Ok(newtime) => newtime,
13181                    Err(exhausted) => {
13182                        // Keep the first report; the clock did not move.
13183                        self.terminal_clock_exhaustion
13184                            .get_or_insert_with(|| exhausted.to_string());
13185                        gtime.as_nanos()
13186                    }
13187                };
13188                if last_turn_was_polling {
13189                    // Advance time (needed for timeout enforcement) but keep it off the DETLOG.
13190                    trace!(
13191                        "[sched] advance global time for internal IO-polling retry (suppressed from detlog), new time {:?}",
13192                        newtime,
13193                    );
13194                } else {
13195                    detlog_debug!(
13196                        "[sched] advance global time for scheduler turn, new time {:?}",
13197                        newtime,
13198                    );
13199                }
13200            }
13201            gtime.as_nanos()
13202        };
13203        // A host-timed retry is not a turn that both runs of --verify share:
13204        // letting it set the previous turn's thread would make whether the
13205        // next signal delivery is charged depend on how many retries ran.
13206        if let Ok(resources) = last_turn
13207            && !last_turn_was_polling
13208        {
13209            self.previous_turn_tid = Some(resources.tid);
13210        }
13211
13212        match snapshot.cmp(&self.committed_time) {
13213            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
13214                panic!(
13215                    "bump_global_time: invariant broken, global time went backwards from {} to {}",
13216                    self.committed_time, snapshot
13217                );
13218            }
13219            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
13220            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
13221                // NB: `committed_time` still tracks the (host-timing-perturbed) global clock,
13222                // including the time advanced by suppressed IO-polling retries above, so this
13223                // line's presence is retry-count sensitive. It is therefore excluded from the
13224                // deterministic `--verify` comparison in `logdiff::is_scheduler_committed_time`
13225                // (it is redundant with the per-turn "advance global time" DETLOG anyway).
13226                detlog_debug!(
13227                    event = crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommittedTime;
13228                    "[sched-step1] advancing committed_time from {} to {}",
13229                    self.committed_time,
13230                    snapshot
13231                );
13232                self.committed_time = snapshot;
13233            }
13234        }
13235        // O3: every turn of an observable process has quiesced, and no pop or
13236        // grant of the next pass has run yet.
13237        self.reconcile_inactive_alarms(self.committed_time);
13238    }
13239
13240    /// Step 4: unblock enabled actions to actually, physically run.
13241    fn step5_guest_unblock(
13242        &mut self,
13243        next_dtid: DetTid,
13244        rsrcs: &Resources,
13245        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
13246    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
13247        match self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid) {
13248            None => {
13249                info!(
13250                    "Scheduler was about to schedule {} for a turn (resources {:?}), but it died first.",
13251                    &next_dtid, rsrcs.resources
13252                );
13253                Err(SkipTurn)
13254            }
13255            Some(nxt) => {
13256                assert_eq!(resp, &nxt.resp);
13257                // Refuse an exhausted transport identity before recording a
13258                // COMMIT or consuming any response state.
13259                if nxt.protocol.epoch.checked_add(1).is_none() {
13260                    self.fail_parked(next_dtid, parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow);
13261                    return Err(SkipTurn);
13262                }
13263                // N.B.: these prints themselves should be deterministic between
13264                // runs.  They are part of the "detlog".
13265                // The records this thread's in-guest Tool forwarded before the request
13266                // this turn serves go to the log here, at a point the schedule fixes
13267                // (the order rule at `detlog::set_forwarded_source`).
13268                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(next_dtid.as_raw(), true);
13269                self.chaos_passed_over.remove(&next_dtid);
13270                let normalization_marker = if self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs) {
13271                    " [sabre-internal-pipe-io]"
13272                } else if self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs) {
13273                    " [sabre-loopback-poll-zero-timeout]"
13274                } else {
13275                    ""
13276                };
13277                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
13278                    let internal_io_poll =
13279                        rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
13280                            || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs)
13281                            || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs);
13282                    let runtime_maps_read = rsrcs.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
13283                        matches!(
13284                            resource,
13285                            ResourceID::Path(path)
13286                                if path.as_path() == std::path::Path::new("/proc/self/maps")
13287                        )
13288                    });
13289                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
13290                        self.turn,
13291                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
13292                        internal_io_poll,
13293                        runtime_maps_read,
13294                    );
13295                    info!(
13296                        "[sched-step5] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, dettid {} using resources {:?}, on previously committed {}{}{}",
13297                        self.turn,
13298                        next_dtid,
13299                        rsrcs.resources,
13300                        self.committed_time,
13301                        normalization_marker,
13302                        record_suffix,
13303                    );
13304                }
13305                self.forget_pipe_handoff(next_dtid);
13306                self.unblock_guest(next_dtid, resp)?;
13307                Ok(())
13308            }
13309        }
13310    }
13311
13312    /// Unblock the guest to run, clear its ivars for the next turn, and increment the turn counter.
13313    ///
13314    /// Precondition: guest is stopped.
13315    /// Postcondition: guest is running concurrently with this scheduler/tracer thread.
13316    fn unblock_guest(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
13317        trace!(
13318            "[sched-step5] Guest unblocking (via {}); clear ivars for the next turn on dettid {}",
13319            &resp, &dtid
13320        );
13321        let mut signals = self.inbound_signals(dtid); // Peek before we clear the ivars.
13322        let signaled = !signals.is_empty();
13323        // A precise futex waiter or a poll the drain woke: a `SIGCHLD` its
13324        // batch carries is not committed to it, unless the scheduler sent one
13325        // since (`drain_woken_waiters`). The answer still says it was woken
13326        // for a signal, with an empty set if that was the only one.
13327        if let Some(woken) = self.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.remove(&dtid) {
13328            signals.retain(|signal| signal.raw() != libc::SIGCHLD);
13329            if woken.scheduler_sent {
13330                signals.push(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
13331                signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
13332            }
13333        }
13334        let fatal_alarm = self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dtid);
13335        let futex_timed_out = self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(&dtid);
13336        let (guest_state_poll, fruitless, wants_alone) = match self
13337            .next_turns
13338            .get(&dtid)
13339            .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
13340        {
13341            Some(Ok(rs)) => (
13342                Self::is_polling_turn(&rs) && rs.polls_guest_state_only,
13343                Self::retries_its_call_without_progress(&rs),
13344                rs.waits_until_nothing_else_can_run,
13345            ),
13346            _ => (false, false, false),
13347        };
13348        self.progress_epoch += 1;
13349        self.last_commit_at.insert(dtid, self.progress_epoch);
13350        let previous_grant = self.guest_state_polled_at.remove(&dtid);
13351        if guest_state_poll {
13352            // This thread's previous grant moved something unless this request
13353            // retries after an attempt that did not.
13354            if let Some(previous) = previous_grant
13355                && !fruitless
13356            {
13357                self.last_progress = self.last_progress.max(previous);
13358            }
13359            self.guest_state_polled_at.insert(dtid, self.progress_epoch);
13360        } else {
13361            self.last_progress = self.progress_epoch;
13362        }
13363        let mut alone = wants_alone && self.nothing_else_can_run(dtid);
13364        if alone
13365            && self
13366                .blocked
13367                .timed_waiters
13368                .next_deadline()
13369                .is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_indefinite())
13370        {
13371            // Only a timer can still let another thread run: move to it now.
13372            alone = false;
13373            self.fast_forward_for_alone_poller = true;
13374        }
13375        if let Err(error) = self.clear_nextturn(dtid) {
13376            self.fail_parked(dtid, error);
13377            return Err(SkipTurn);
13378        }
13379        self.turn += 1;
13380        let answer = if fatal_alarm {
13381            SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm
13382        } else if signaled {
13383            SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))
13384        } else if futex_timed_out {
13385            SchedResponse::Go(Some(SchedValue::TimeOut))
13386        } else {
13387            let timeslice = self.timeslices.remove(&dtid).flatten();
13388            // TODO(T137799529): use a more strongly typed representation rather than reusing
13389            // SchedValue/u64:
13390            let as_schedvalue = timeslice
13391                .as_ref()
13392                .map(LogicalTime::as_nanos)
13393                .map(SchedValue::Value);
13394            if alone {
13395                SchedResponse::GoAlone(as_schedvalue)
13396            } else {
13397                SchedResponse::Go(as_schedvalue)
13398            }
13399        };
13400        match self.deadline_remaining_from(dtid, self.committed_time) {
13401            Some(remaining) => self.deadline_hints.insert(dtid, remaining),
13402            None => self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid),
13403        };
13404        self.parked.running = Some(dtid);
13405        resp.put(answer);
13406        Ok(())
13407    }
13408
13409    /// The virtual time left, from `now`, before the earliest deadline a turn
13410    /// would act on (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>):
13411    ///   - a timed wait or timer (`timed_waiters`);
13412    ///   - a backed-off poller's timeout (`poll_deadlines`);
13413    ///   - the deadline of a sleep or poll another thread has requested but
13414    ///     not yet had a turn for. A sleep becomes a timed waiter only at the
13415    ///     turn that commits its request, so one queued behind the granted
13416    ///     thread would otherwise wait out that thread's whole slice.
13417    ///
13418    /// Only deadlines still ahead of `now` count, from threads that will take
13419    /// another turn: a passed one (including a yield's `SleepUntil(0)`) marks
13420    /// a request that is simply runnable or an entry kept past its time, and
13421    /// a thread pending removal or in a process a committed SIGKILL has
13422    /// doomed will never act on its deadline. A wait no longer than the time
13423    /// the scheduler charges for a turn has therefore passed by the grant and
13424    /// ends no slice: counting passed waits too would end the slice of every
13425    /// thread granted while another thread's sleep is over, a contended
13426    /// quantum this cap does not add (measured: 51% more virtual time for 8
13427    /// threads sleeping 1 ms between bursts of work, against 11%). `None`
13428    /// when nothing qualifies,
13429    /// and always under record/replay, which records no hint (as it records
13430    /// no poll deadline, `note_poll_deadline`).
13431    ///
13432    /// Deadlines are compared against `committed_time` at turns, and global
13433    /// time is the sum of every thread's local time, so while the granted
13434    /// thread runs alone global time advances exactly as its own clock does:
13435    /// a thread that ends its slice once this much of its own time has passed
13436    /// takes a turn no earlier than global time passes the deadline. That
13437    /// relies on serialized execution: one thread runs between turns.
13438    ///
13439    /// Determinism: every input is scheduler state fixed at a turn, after all
13440    /// threads have quiesced (`step1_check_quiescence`), so the hint is a
13441    /// function of the guest's execution. It inherits, and adds nothing to,
13442    /// the host-timed inputs that already reach `committed_time` and the
13443    /// timed waiters: internal IO-polling retries, background threads' time
13444    /// reports, and exit wakes from robust-list cleanup.
13445    fn deadline_remaining_from(&self, granted: DetTid, now: LogicalTime) -> Option<Duration> {
13446        if self.recordreplay_modes {
13447            return None;
13448        }
13449        // The granted thread's own timer signals count: they must end its
13450        // slice too. Only its own queued request (being granted) does not.
13451        let acts = |tid: DetTid| {
13452            !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&tid)
13453                && !self
13454                    .thread_tree
13455                    .process_of(tid)
13456                    .is_some_and(|process| self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&process))
13457        };
13458        let ahead = |deadline: &LogicalTime| *deadline > now && !deadline.is_indefinite();
13459        // Each expiry of a periodic timer that ends a slice costs a turn for
13460        // the slice end, and its delivery is charged again when it switches
13461        // threads (a delivery to the running thread is free since
13462        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). A timer whose period
13463        // is at most two turn charges could still spend more virtual time on
13464        // turns than on the guest. It hints nothing, as before this cap.
13465        let fast_periodic = |event: &TimedEvent| match event {
13466            TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, _, _) => self
13467                .blocked
13468                .timed_waiters
13469                .signal_timer_period(*id)
13470                .is_some_and(|period| period <= self.fast_timer_period),
13471            TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(_) => false,
13472        };
13473        let timed = self
13474            .blocked
13475            .timed_waiters
13476            .iter()
13477            .find(|(deadline, event)| {
13478                ahead(deadline)
13479                    && !fast_periodic(event)
13480                    && acts(match event {
13481                        TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(tid) => *tid,
13482                        TimedEvent::SignalEvt(_, target, _) => target.tid(),
13483                    })
13484            })
13485            .map(|(deadline, _)| deadline);
13486        let poll = self
13487            .poll_deadlines
13488            .iter()
13489            .find(|(deadline, tid)| ahead(deadline) && acts(*tid))
13490            .map(|(deadline, _)| *deadline);
13491        let queued = self
13492            .run_queue
13493            .tids()
13494            .filter(|tid| **tid != granted && acts(**tid))
13495            .filter_map(|tid| {
13496                self.next_turns
13497                    .get(tid)?
13498                    .req
13499                    .try_read_with(|request| request.as_ref().ok()?.queued_deadline())
13500                    .flatten()
13501            })
13502            .filter(ahead)
13503            .min();
13504        let earliest = [timed, poll, queued].into_iter().flatten().min()?;
13505        Some(Duration::from_nanos(
13506            earliest.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos()),
13507        ))
13508    }
13509
13510    /// Record the deadline hint for a thread that has just armed or re-armed
13511    /// a timer during its own turn, measured from the `now` the timer was
13512    /// armed against: the hint of the grant it runs under could not include
13513    /// that deadline. The reply to the arming request carries it.
13514    pub fn note_arming_hint(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, now: LogicalTime) {
13515        match self.deadline_remaining_from(dtid, now) {
13516            Some(remaining) => self.deadline_hints.insert(dtid, remaining),
13517            None => self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid),
13518        };
13519    }
13520
13521    /// Take the deadline hint recorded when `dtid` was last granted a turn or
13522    /// armed a timer. Every request clears it on arrival
13523    /// (`GlobalState::receive_rpc`), so a reply takes only a hint recorded
13524    /// while its own request was pending.
13525    pub fn take_deadline_hint(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) -> Option<Duration> {
13526        self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid)
13527    }
13528
13529    fn inbound_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Vec<SigWrapper> {
13530        let req = &self.next_turns.get(&dettid).unwrap().req;
13531        let mut signals = Vec::new();
13532        if let Some(Ok(resources)) = req.try_read() {
13533            for resource in resources.resources.keys() {
13534                match resource {
13535                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal) => signals.push(*signal),
13536                    ResourceID::WaitidSignals(batch) => signals.extend(batch.iter().copied()),
13537                    _ => {}
13538                }
13539            }
13540        }
13541        // A signal can legitimately appear in both an `InboundSignal` and a
13542        // merged `WaitidSignals` batch. Sort then dedup so the reported set is a
13543        // canonical function of WHICH signals are pending, not of how many
13544        // resources happen to carry each one or of the order they arrived in.
13545        signals.sort_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
13546        signals.dedup_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
13547        signals
13548    }
13549
13550    /// Clear the thread's nextturn, installing fresh ivars.
13551    ///
13552    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
13553    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
13554    fn clear_nextturn(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), parked::ProtocolFailure> {
13555        let epoch = self
13556            .next_turns
13557            .get(&dtid)
13558            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Identity)?
13559            .protocol
13560            .epoch
13561            .checked_add(1)
13562            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow)?;
13563        self.settle_parked_grant(dtid);
13564        self.clear_ready_polled_read(dtid);
13565        // The granted request is consumed; so is any polling wait it continued.
13566        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dtid);
13567        let nextturn = self
13568            .next_turns
13569            .get_mut(&dtid)
13570            .expect("clear_nextturn: Thread should be available in next_turns");
13571        nextturn.req = Ivar::new();
13572        nextturn.resp = Ivar::new();
13573        nextturn.protocol.epoch = epoch;
13574        nextturn.protocol.origin = None;
13575        Ok(())
13576    }
13577
13578    /// How [`Self::step6_reenquue`] requeues the thread whose granted request
13579    /// is `rsrcs`. A `SchedYield` turn is excluded from the next selection.
13580    /// Under chaos, a `sched_yield`'s `SchedYield` instead counts toward the
13581    /// yielder's streak, and after [`runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH`]
13582    /// plain yields it opens or joins a yield epoch, so the yielder is not
13583    /// selected again until a thread that did not yield has had a turn
13584    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded_into_epoch`]): chaos keeps each thread in its random band
13585    /// until its slice ends, which a `sched_yield` loop never reaches, so a
13586    /// one-turn exclusion lets two yielders take turns ahead of a thread in a
13587    /// later band forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4068). The
13588    /// zero-timeout loopback poll's `SchedYield` keeps the one-turn exclusion:
13589    /// how many of those a SaBRe task makes is host-timed.
13590    fn requeue_after(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> Requeue {
13591        if !rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::SchedYield) {
13592            Requeue::Back
13593        } else if self.chaos && !self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs) {
13594            Requeue::YieldEpoch
13595        } else {
13596            Requeue::OneTurnYield
13597        }
13598    }
13599
13600    /// Step: reenqueue the thread that just had a turn.
13601    fn step6_reenquue(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid, requeue: Requeue) {
13602        // We delay popping till here, so while holding the lock we "atomically" move the
13603        // thread from the front to the back of the queue.
13604        let dt2 = if requeue == Requeue::YieldEpoch {
13605            self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop_yield()
13606        } else {
13607            self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop_completed_turn()
13608        };
13609        assert_eq!(next_dtid, dt2);
13610        // A yield's queue placement is transient: the thread keeps its persistent priority
13611        // and its band.
13612        let pos = match requeue {
13613            Requeue::Back => self.runqueue_push_back(next_dtid),
13614            Requeue::OneTurnYield => {
13615                let priority = self.get_priority(next_dtid);
13616                self.run_queue.push_yielded(next_dtid, priority)
13617            }
13618            Requeue::YieldEpoch => {
13619                let priority = self.get_priority(next_dtid);
13620                self.run_queue.push_yielded_into_epoch(next_dtid, priority)
13621            }
13622        };
13623        debug!(
13624            "[sched-step6] dettid {} going back into queue at position {}.",
13625            next_dtid, pos
13626        );
13627    }
13628
13629    /// Add a simulated "post hook" for exit calls which we're about to let through.
13630    /// ALTERNATIVE: this could happen later when the thread_exit hook comes through.
13631    fn step7_simulate_exit_posthook(
13632        &mut self,
13633        dettid: DetTid,
13634        placeholder_syscall: Syscall,
13635        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
13636    ) {
13637        let replay = self.replayer.is_some();
13638        let record = self.preemption_writer.is_some();
13639        if !(replay || record) {
13640            return;
13641        }
13642        let thread_duration = global_time.lock().unwrap().threads_duration(dettid);
13643        debug!(
13644            "simulate exit posthook on tid {}, thread time {}: {:?}",
13645            dettid, thread_duration, placeholder_syscall
13646        );
13647
13648        let ev = SchedEvent::syscall(dettid, placeholder_syscall.number(), SyscallPhase::Posthook)
13649            .with_time(thread_duration);
13650        let print_stack1 = if replay {
13651            let ConsumeResult {
13652                keep_running,
13653                print_stack,
13654                event_ix: _,
13655                timeslice_remaining: _,
13656            } = self.consume_schedevent(&ev);
13657            // We should not ever need to background the thread when it is going to exit anyway.
13658            if !keep_running {
13659                tracing::warn!(
13660                    "simulate_exit_posthook: unexpectedly asked to background the current, exiting thread {}",
13661                    dettid
13662                );
13663            }
13664            print_stack
13665        } else {
13666            None
13667        };
13668        let print_stack2 = if record { self.record_event(&ev) } else { None };
13669        if print_stack1.is_some() || print_stack2.is_some() {
13670            crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
13671                ":: Guest tid {}, at thread time {}, backtrace requested but not available post-exit!\n",
13672                dettid,
13673                thread_duration
13674            );
13675        }
13676    }
13677
13678    /// Get the priority for a thread; panic if absent.
13679    fn get_priority(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Priority {
13680        *self
13681            .priorities
13682            .get(&dettid)
13683            .expect("get_priority: all threads should have a persistent priority")
13684    }
13685
13686    /// Push_back a thread onto the runqueue, respecting its persistent priority
13687    /// value. This should be the ordinary way threads are pushed onto the queue.
13688    pub fn runqueue_push_back(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
13689        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
13690        self.run_queue.push_back(dettid, priority)
13691    }
13692
13693    /// Under `--replay-schedule-from`, give a thread registering now its
13694    /// priority. A context switch to it that came before its registration
13695    /// has already set one. Otherwise it takes its `starting` priority:
13696    /// foreground for the root, deferred for any other thread, of whichever
13697    /// process, until the replayed schedule switches to it
13698    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472). Past the end of the
13699    /// recording (`release_replay_priorities_if_exhausted`) every thread has
13700    /// the default priority, so a new one does too: at the deferred priority
13701    /// it could wait for ever behind a parent that never blocks. Returns
13702    /// whether a thread other than the root took its starting priority
13703    /// unguided, a sign that the replay has left its recording.
13704    pub(crate) fn replay_registration_priority(
13705        &mut self,
13706        dettid: DetTid,
13707        starting: Priority,
13708    ) -> bool {
13709        if self.replay_priorities_released {
13710            self.priorities.insert(dettid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
13711            return false;
13712        }
13713        match self.priorities.entry(dettid) {
13714            std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
13715                entry.insert(starting);
13716                dettid != crate::consts::ROOT_DETPID
13717            }
13718            std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(_) => false,
13719        }
13720    }
13721
13722    /// Once the replayed schedule has no events left, give every thread the
13723    /// default priority, once. Nothing guides the run past that point, and a
13724    /// thread the schedule left at the deferred priority would otherwise wait
13725    /// for ever behind a foreground thread that never blocks, a thread the
13726    /// schedule readmitted at the deferred priority included
13727    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472). The point is the
13728    /// consumption of the last recorded event, a scheduled event of a running
13729    /// thread, so it is the same in every run.
13730    fn release_replay_priorities_if_exhausted(&mut self) {
13731        if self.replay_priorities_released
13732            || self.replayer.as_ref().is_none_or(Replayer::has_events_left)
13733        {
13734            return;
13735        }
13736        self.replay_priorities_released = true;
13737        info!("[sched] the replayed schedule ran out; every thread takes the default priority");
13738        let threads: Vec<DetTid> = self.priorities.keys().copied().collect();
13739        for dettid in threads {
13740            self.requeue_with_new_priority(dettid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
13741        }
13742    }
13743
13744    /// Readmit a thread whose blocking call finished, or whose deferred
13745    /// signal is due, ahead of all other work (`push_eager_io_repoll`).
13746    /// While `--replay-schedule-from` still has recorded events, the replayed
13747    /// schedule decides who runs next, through the priorities its context
13748    /// switches set, so the thread goes back at its own priority instead: an
13749    /// eager readmission outranked the thread the schedule had just switched
13750    /// to (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472). Past the end of
13751    /// the recording nothing guides the run, and a thread left at the
13752    /// deferred priority could wait behind a foreground one for ever, so
13753    /// readmission is eager again.
13754    fn readmit_ready_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
13755        if self
13756            .replayer
13757            .as_ref()
13758            .is_some_and(Replayer::has_events_left)
13759        {
13760            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
13761        } else {
13762            self.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(dettid);
13763        }
13764    }
13765
13766    /// Push a thread to the front of its persistent priority band.
13767    ///
13768    /// This is reserved for protocol handoffs where the queued thread must run
13769    /// before an equal-priority peer, such as ordinary clone child startup.
13770    pub(crate) fn runqueue_push_front(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
13771        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
13772        self.run_queue.push_front(dettid, priority)
13773    }
13774
13775    /// Record an intent to admit `dtid` to the run queue, applied by the daemon
13776    /// at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
13777    ///
13778    /// Global-request handlers (`recv_create_child_thread`,
13779    /// `reconnect_after_exec`) hold the scheduler lock but run on whichever
13780    /// backend worker fielded the RPC, not on the scheduler daemon's turn. The
13781    /// point in the daemon's loop at which such a handler acquires the lock is
13782    /// host-timing-dependent on asynchronous backends (e.g. DBT): it may land
13783    /// inside the tentative-pop window (between `step3_peek` and `step4`'s
13784    /// commit, where the lock is released across `req.get().await`) *or* outside
13785    /// it (during the quiescence-wait / backoff awaits at the top of
13786    /// `do_a_turn_blocking`, where `tentative_selection` is `None`). A design
13787    /// that pushed directly whenever the window happened to be closed would make
13788    /// the *admission order* — and, under `RunsPostFork::Random`, the PRNG draw
13789    /// order — a function of that host timing: two equal-priority admissions
13790    /// could enter the queue in either relative order across otherwise-identical
13791    /// runs, and a fixed seed could explore different schedules.
13792    ///
13793    /// So admission is *always* deferred, never applied directly here. Handlers
13794    /// only record the unresolved [`AdmitIntent`]; the daemon resolves the side
13795    /// (drawing any `RunsPostFork::Random` value) and pushes the run queue at the
13796    /// single `step2` drain, in canonical `DetTid` order, before `step3` opens a
13797    /// tentative window. Draining is also the only place `remove_tid`'s tentative
13798    /// guard is guaranteed to hold.
13799    ///
13800    /// # What this does and does not make deterministic
13801    ///
13802    /// **Synchronous backends (ptrace): fully deterministic, and byte-identical
13803    /// to the pre-deferral behavior.** Handlers run post-commit, one per turn, so
13804    /// at most one admission is buffered per turn and it drains at the next
13805    /// `step2` — before that turn's `step3` selection — yielding the same
13806    /// selection sequence and the same one-draw-per-fork PRNG order as an
13807    /// immediate push.
13808    ///
13809    /// **Asynchronous backends: every production admission site has a causal or
13810    /// explicit barrier that fixes its drain, and order within that drain is
13811    /// canonical.** A bare off-turn handler would still be insufficient: a
13812    /// `BTreeMap` only canonicalizes items already in one snapshot. The current
13813    /// sites additionally bind snapshot membership to deterministic scheduler
13814    /// state:
13815    ///
13816    /// * **Ordinary clone — anchored, causally.** `CreateChildThread` issues the
13817    ///   parent's `ParentContinue` request only *after* buffering the child's
13818    ///   admission, so no thread can run between the two and the admission
13819    ///   cannot straddle a drain boundary.
13820    /// * **`vfork` — anchored, by barrier.** `vfork_barriers` /
13821    ///   [`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`] hold the parent until the
13822    ///   child has registered, which fixes the drain.
13823    /// * **Multi-threaded exec reconnect — anchored, causally.** Step5 installs
13824    ///   the caller's empty next-turn request before it executes exec. The
13825    ///   reconnect handler atomically buffers the old-leader removal and new
13826    ///   incarnation admission, then retires the caller and resolves that
13827    ///   request. Step1 therefore cannot release step2 before the complete pair
13828    ///   exists. [`Scheduler::replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation`] binds the
13829    ///   same-raw-TID handoff explicitly.
13830    ///
13831    /// Thus both membership and within-drain resolution are functions of
13832    /// deterministic state for all current sites. The exec regression test
13833    /// forces the daemon to wait before reconnect, varies host yields, and
13834    /// compares the exact first-drain queue plus the next post-fork PRNG draw.
13835    pub(crate) fn admit_to_run_queue(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
13836        let prev = self.pending_run_queue_admissions.insert(dtid, intent);
13837        debug_assert!(
13838            prev.is_none(),
13839            "thread {:?} recorded for run-queue admission twice before draining",
13840            dtid
13841        );
13842    }
13843
13844    /// Atomically classify a same-raw-TID exec handoff and record its fresh
13845    /// admission. The scheduler mutex serializes this method with `step2`, so a
13846    /// drain can never observe only one half of the handoff.
13847    fn replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
13848        let disposition = self
13849            .pending_run_queue_removals
13850            .get_mut(&dtid)
13851            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
13852                panic!(
13853                    "exec replacement {:?} has no retired run-queue incarnation",
13854                    dtid
13855                )
13856            });
13857        assert_eq!(
13858            *disposition,
13859            RemovalDisposition::Retire,
13860            "exec replacement {:?} was classified more than once",
13861            dtid
13862        );
13863        *disposition = RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit;
13864        assert!(
13865            self.pending_run_queue_admissions
13866                .insert(dtid, intent)
13867                .is_none(),
13868            "exec replacement {:?} already had a pending admission",
13869            dtid
13870        );
13871    }
13872
13873    /// Resolve an [`AdmitIntent`] to a concrete [`AdmitSide`], consuming the
13874    /// post-fork PRNG draw for `RunsPostFork::Random`.
13875    ///
13876    /// Called at the drain rather than in the handler, so the draw is never
13877    /// consumed in host *RPC arrival* order, and the draws taken within one
13878    /// drain follow canonical `DetTid` order. This function only canonicalizes
13879    /// draws within a fixed drain; each admission site must separately bind its
13880    /// drain membership to deterministic scheduler state. See
13881    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the causal and explicit barriers
13882    /// that provide that binding for all current production sites.
13883    fn resolve_admit_intent(&mut self, intent: AdmitIntent) -> AdmitSide {
13884        match intent {
13885            AdmitIntent::Fixed(side) => side,
13886            AdmitIntent::PostFork(mode) => {
13887                if self.child_runs_first_post_fork(mode) {
13888                    AdmitSide::Front
13889                } else {
13890                    AdmitSide::Back
13891                }
13892            }
13893        }
13894    }
13895
13896    /// Record an intent to remove `dtid` from the run queue, applied by the
13897    /// daemon at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
13898    ///
13899    /// The mirror of [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the removal side, and
13900    /// deferred for the same reason: a global-request handler
13901    /// (`reconnect_after_exec` -> `logically_kill_thread`) runs on a backend
13902    /// worker and may hold the lock inside the daemon's tentative-pop window,
13903    /// where `RunQueue::remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` assert
13904    /// would trip and poison the scheduler mutex. Recording the removal and
13905    /// applying it at `step2` (window closed, guard holds) avoids that. The
13906    /// caller has already made the thread logically dead (cleared `next_turns`,
13907    /// resolved its request to `ThreadExited`), so leaving its stale run-queue
13908    /// entry in place until the drain is inert: the daemon skips it for any
13909    /// intervening turn (`step3`'s pick is validated against `next_turns`) and
13910    /// `are_all_quiesced` filters it out. On ptrace the drain runs at the next
13911    /// `step2`, before that turn's `step3` selection, so the removal is
13912    /// observationally immediate — the dead thread is never selected.
13913    fn deschedule_or_defer(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) {
13914        // A later logical death of a not-yet-drained exec replacement must
13915        // override `ReplaceThenAdmit`: `remove_blocking_entries` clears its
13916        // admission and this `Retire` disposition prevents resurrection.
13917        self.pending_run_queue_removals
13918            .insert(dtid, RemovalDisposition::Retire);
13919    }
13920
13921    /// Apply queued cross-task signal notifications at the deterministic
13922    /// run-queue mutation point. Re-check the request because a target may have
13923    /// exited or completed its wait before this drain.
13924    fn drain_pending_cross_task_signals(&mut self) {
13925        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_cross_task_signals);
13926        for (dettid, mut signals) in pending {
13927            if self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid) {
13928                // A guest's signal reached a thread asleep in a real
13929                // `rt_sigsuspend`, or stopped at that call's request, at host
13930                // speed. Linux wakes the call if its mask lets the signal
13931                // through, and the wake's signal stop is posted when the host
13932                // gets to it. Placing it here, at this fixed point, as for a
13933                // signal the scheduler sends (`wake_signaled_guest`: the release
13934                // barrier, or the record its grant arms), makes the scheduler
13935                // wait for that stop. Before, nothing did, and on a slow host
13936                // an empty run queue was reported as a deadlock first.
13937                signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
13938                signals.dedup();
13939                // Every signal, by its raw number: a realtime signal its mask
13940                // admits ends the call as a standard one does, and `nix`'s
13941                // `Signal` cannot name it, so filtering through it dropped the
13942                // wake (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941).
13943                for signal in signals {
13944                    self.wake_signaled_guest(dettid, signal);
13945                }
13946                continue;
13947            }
13948            match self.waitid_signal_request(dettid) {
13949                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked) => {
13950                    // This legacy wake completes the child-wait resource and
13951                    // replaces it with an ordinary signal grant. Retire its
13952                    // parked capability at the same ownership boundary; a
13953                    // shared alarm may become due later in this very pass.
13954                    if let Err(error) = self.retire_child_wait_signal_request(dettid) {
13955                        self.fail_parked(dettid, error);
13956                        continue;
13957                    }
13958                    // Decide run-queue residency HERE, by asking the queue, and
13959                    // never by inferring it from which resource the thread
13960                    // holds. A thread can hold either park request while already
13961                    // queued: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without
13962                    // clearing its `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue`
13963                    // pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues its
13964                    // next request. `force_unblock_thread` ends in
13965                    // `runqueue_push_*`, so pushing an already-queued thread
13966                    // trips the run-queue invariant under `debug_assertions`
13967                    // and, worse, SILENTLY double-enqueues in release — one
13968                    // thread selected twice. This mirrors `wake_signaled_guest`,
13969                    // which likewise consults `thread_status` before removing.
13970                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
13971                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
13972                        debug_assert!(
13973                            removed,
13974                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
13975                        );
13976                    }
13977                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
13978                    signals.dedup();
13979                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
13980                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
13981                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, resources);
13982                }
13983                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(existing)) => {
13984                    signals.extend(existing);
13985                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
13986                    signals.dedup();
13987                    // One resource, always. `step4_resource_block` and
13988                    // `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert a request carries
13989                    // exactly one, so this must replace the request rather than
13990                    // add to it. Only a request whose sole resource is already
13991                    // `WaitidSignals` reaches here, so nothing is discarded.
13992                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
13993                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
13994                    let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
13995                        continue;
13996                    };
13997                    next_turn.req = Ivar::full(Ok(resources));
13998                }
13999                None if let Some(interrupting) =
14000                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, 0) =>
14001                {
14002                    // A precise-mode futex waiter sleeps in `futex_waiters`, outside
14003                    // the run queue, so nothing else would ever let the physically
14004                    // pending signal interrupt it
14005                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Take it out
14006                    // of the futex and requeue it with the signal set, exactly as a
14007                    // scheduler-sent signal does in `wake_signaled_guest`: its turn
14008                    // answers `Signaled`, which the futex handler reports as the
14009                    // wait's restart errno, and the kernel then applies the guest's
14010                    // disposition. `WaitidSignals` is the one-resource form for a
14011                    // signal set, and later batches merge into it before it runs.
14012                    //
14013                    // This drain is the commit point. Admission checked only the
14014                    // waiter's mask; `interrupting` is computed from the
14015                    // dispositions the kernel holds now, with no guest thread
14016                    // holding the turn (see `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
14017                    // A signal that the sender, or a sibling later in the same
14018                    // turn, made ignored is dropped here, as the kernel drops it,
14019                    // and a waiter left with none stays registered with its
14020                    // original deadline.
14021                    signals.retain(|signal| interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0);
14022                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
14023                    signals.dedup();
14024                    if signals.is_empty() {
14025                        continue;
14026                    }
14027                    // The waiter runs next, so it is the thread that resumes
14028                    // and dequeues the signal. Its futex handler re-checks in
14029                    // its turn and parks again if nothing is pending for it.
14030                    // Marked after the unblock, which clears blocking entries:
14031                    // a `SIGCHLD` this batch carries is not committed to it
14032                    // (`drain_woken_waiters`).
14033                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
14034                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
14035                    if self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, resources, true) {
14036                        self.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.insert(
14037                            dettid,
14038                            DrainWoken {
14039                                waiter: DrainWokenWaiter::FutexWaiter,
14040                                scheduler_sent: false,
14041                            },
14042                        );
14043                    }
14044                }
14045                None if let Some(sleep) = self.signal_sleep(dettid) => {
14046                    // An emulated `pause` or `nanosleep`, parked in the timed
14047                    // waiters or still queued with its request
14048                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
14049                    self.drain_sleep_signals(dettid, sleep, signals);
14050                }
14051                None => {
14052                    let Some(existing) = self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid) else {
14053                        continue;
14054                    };
14055                    // ERESTARTSYS is the existing contract by which the kernel
14056                    // decides whether this physically pending signal restarts
14057                    // the syscall or interrupts it for a handler. Only a
14058                    // signal the kernel would deliver now ends the poll: a
14059                    // blocked, ignored or held one leaves it polling, with
14060                    // its request and place in the run queue unchanged.
14061                    let (task, decides_itself) = self
14062                        .next_turns
14063                        .get(&dettid)
14064                        .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
14065                        .and_then(Result::ok)
14066                        .map(|resources| {
14067                            (
14068                                resources.signal_state_task,
14069                                resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself,
14070                            )
14071                        })
14072                        .unwrap_or((None, false));
14073                    // A poll that checks the disposition itself after the
14074                    // wake (a parked pipe `writev`) keeps every signal.
14075                    let interrupting = if decides_itself {
14076                        !0
14077                    } else {
14078                        self.restartable_internal_io_interrupting_signals(dettid, task)
14079                    };
14080                    signals.retain(|signal| interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0);
14081                    signals.extend(existing);
14082                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
14083                    signals.dedup();
14084                    if signals.is_empty() {
14085                        continue;
14086                    }
14087                    // Replace the polling request rather than adding a second
14088                    // resource; step4 accepts exactly one.
14089                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
14090                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
14091                        debug_assert!(
14092                            removed,
14093                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
14094                        );
14095                    }
14096                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
14097                    // `WaitidSignals` is already the scheduler's one-resource
14098                    // representation for a complete signal identity set. The
14099                    // ERESTARTSYS marker distinguishes this write wakeup from a
14100                    // waitid request and survives later notification batches.
14101                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
14102                    resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
14103                    // A later batch merging into this wake is filtered by the
14104                    // same thread's state.
14105                    resources.signal_state_task = task;
14106                    resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = decides_itself;
14107                    // Marked after the unblock, which clears blocking entries,
14108                    // as for a futex waiter: a `SIGCHLD` this batch carries is
14109                    // not committed to the poll (`drain_woken_waiters`), whose
14110                    // turn decides from what is still pending then
14111                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273). It
14112                    // keeps its place at the back of the run queue. A parked
14113                    // pipe `writev` (`decides_itself`) is not marked: a guest's
14114                    // caught `SIGCHLD` still ends it as on Linux, until R2b-2
14115                    // decides the private `SIGCHLD` for every call.
14116                    if self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, resources, false) && !decides_itself {
14117                        self.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.insert(
14118                            dettid,
14119                            DrainWoken {
14120                                waiter: DrainWokenWaiter::Poll,
14121                                scheduler_sent: false,
14122                            },
14123                        );
14124                    }
14125                }
14126            }
14127        }
14128    }
14129
14130    /// Drain removals deferred by [`Scheduler::deschedule_or_defer`] at the same
14131    /// deterministic `step2` point as admissions, and *before* them, so a thread
14132    /// killed while an admission was still buffered is not re-enqueued. The
14133    /// window is closed here (`tentative_selection` is `None`), so
14134    /// `remove_tid`'s guard holds. The `BTreeMap` makes removal order canonical;
14135    /// each disposition determines whether a same-raw-TID admission is stale or
14136    /// is the explicitly paired exec replacement.
14137    fn drain_pending_run_queue_removals(&mut self) {
14138        if self.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty() {
14139            return;
14140        }
14141        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_removals);
14142        for (dtid, disposition) in pending {
14143            match disposition {
14144                RemovalDisposition::Retire => {
14145                    // Ordinary logical death cancels a buffered admission for
14146                    // the same thread incarnation.
14147                    self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(&dtid);
14148                }
14149                RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit => {
14150                    assert!(
14151                        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid),
14152                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its scheduler registration",
14153                        dtid
14154                    );
14155                    assert!(
14156                        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid),
14157                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its paired admission",
14158                        dtid
14159                    );
14160                    assert!(
14161                        !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid),
14162                        "logically dead exec replacement {:?} reached the drain",
14163                        dtid
14164                    );
14165                }
14166            }
14167            // Always remove the old physical queue slot before a replacement
14168            // admission is applied. This prevents the new image from inheriting
14169            // the destroyed leader's round-robin position.
14170            let _ = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dtid);
14171        }
14172    }
14173
14174    /// Push `dtid` onto the run queue immediately, idempotently: a thread
14175    /// already queued is left in place rather than enqueued twice.
14176    fn admit_now(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, side: AdmitSide) {
14177        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
14178            return;
14179        }
14180        match side {
14181            AdmitSide::Front => {
14182                let _ = self.runqueue_push_front(dtid);
14183            }
14184            AdmitSide::Back => {
14185                let _ = self.runqueue_push_back(dtid);
14186            }
14187        }
14188    }
14189
14190    /// Drain admissions deferred by [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] into the
14191    /// run queue at a single deterministic point: the very start of `step2`,
14192    /// before `step3_peek` opens a tentative window (so `tentative_selection` is
14193    /// guaranteed `None` here). Draining a `BTreeMap` visits `DetTid`s in sorted
14194    /// order, so the resulting run-queue state is a pure function of the
14195    /// deterministic schedule rather than of RPC/lock-acquisition timing.
14196    fn drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(&mut self) {
14197        if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty() {
14198            return;
14199        }
14200        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_admissions);
14201        // `pending` is a `BTreeMap`, so iteration visits `DetTid`s in sorted
14202        // order. Resolving each intent here (rather than at the racing handler)
14203        // means any `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw is consumed in this
14204        // canonical order, so both the admission order *and* the chosen side are
14205        // pure functions of deterministic state.
14206        for (dtid, intent) in pending {
14207            // A thread retired (exec/kill) between record and drain is skipped.
14208            // `remove_blocking_entries` also clears the buffer on teardown, so
14209            // this guard is defensive against any teardown path that does not.
14210            if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid) {
14211                trace!(
14212                    "[step2] skipping deferred admission of retired thread {:?}",
14213                    dtid
14214                );
14215                continue;
14216            }
