14217            let side = self.resolve_admit_intent(intent);
14218            self.admit_now(dtid, side);
14219        }
14220    }
14221
14222    /// Decide which side gets the first post-fork turn for an ordinary clone.
14223    pub(crate) fn child_runs_first_post_fork(&mut self, mode: RunsPostFork) -> bool {
14224        match mode {
14225            RunsPostFork::Child => true,
14226            RunsPostFork::Parent => false,
14227            RunsPostFork::Random => self.post_fork_prng.random(),
14228        }
14229    }
14230
14231    /// Check if a thread is alive, but removed from run queue.
14232    fn thread_status(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> ThreadStatus {
14233        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
14234            ThreadStatus::Running
14235        } else {
14236            // Check all the places a blocked thread could be hiding.
14237            // TODO: this O(N) search could be made more efficient with more indexing structures.
14238            for v in self.blocked.futex_waiters.values() {
14239                for waiter in v {
14240                    if waiter.dettid == dtid {
14241                        return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
14242                    }
14243                }
14244            }
14245            for (_, evt) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
14246                match evt {
14247                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dt) => {
14248                        if dt == dtid {
14249                            return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
14250                        }
14251                    }
14252                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(_, _, _) => {}
14253                }
14254            }
14255            if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid) {
14256                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
14257            }
14258            if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
14259                || self.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&dtid)
14260                || self
14261                    .blocked
14262                    .physical_child_waiters
14263                    .values()
14264                    .any(|waiters| waiters.contains(&dtid))
14265            {
14266                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
14267            }
14268            if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid) {
14269                return ThreadStatus::Running;
14270            }
14271            // Held at a happens-before gate: alive, out of the run queue until
14272            // a source fires. Reporting it as gone made a signal sent to it
14273            // (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) panic `wake_signaled_guest`.
14274            if self
14275                .happens_before
14276                .as_ref()
14277                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dtid))
14278            {
14279                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
14280            }
14281            ThreadStatus::Gone
14282        }
14283    }
14284
14285    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14286    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#252): Confirm completed and final partial slices belong in one distribution.
14287    /// Fold an exiting thread's completed-timeslice distribution into the
14288    /// scheduler's per-thread record, to be reported in the final run summary.
14289    pub fn record_timeslice_stats(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, stats: TimesliceStats) {
14290        if stats.is_empty() {
14291            return;
14292        }
14293        self.per_thread_timeslice
14294            .entry(dettid)
14295            .or_default()
14296            .merge(&stats);
14297    }
14298
14299    /// Record an exiting thread's final completed-syscall count.
14300    pub fn record_syscall_count(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) {
14301        let consumed = self
14302            .transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
14303            .get(&dettid)
14304            .copied()
14305            .unwrap_or(0);
14306        let total = consumed
14307            .checked_add(count)
14308            .expect("transferred exec syscall count overflow");
14309        self.per_thread_syscalls.insert(dettid, total);
14310    }
14311
14312    /// Summarize the run after completion, as a RunSummary. This is partial because the Scheduler
14313    /// does not have all the necessary information.
14314    ///
14315    /// Side Effects: This also flushes the in-memory PreemptionWriter to disk.
14316    #[cfg(test)]
14317    pub fn generate_partial_run_summary(
14318        &mut self,
14319        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
14320    ) -> anyhow::Result<RunSummary> {
14321        self.generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(preemptions_to)
14322            .map(|(summary, _)| summary)
14323    }
14324
14325    /// Build the full report and the INFO preemption description together.
14326    /// The latter retains counts/history but excludes the host output filename.
14327    /// This performs one generation and flush.
14328    pub(crate) fn generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(
14329        &mut self,
14330        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
14331    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RunSummary, Option<String>)> {
14332        let schedevent_replayed = self
14333            .replayer
14334            .as_ref()
14335            .map(|r| r.events_popped)
14336            .unwrap_or_default();
14337        let total_desync_stats = self
14338            .replayer
14339            .as_ref()
14340            .map(|r| {
14341                r.desync_counts
14342                    .values()
14343                    .fold(Default::default(), |x: DesyncStats, y: &DesyncStats| x + *y)
14344            })
14345            .unwrap_or_default();
14346
14347        let total_desyncs = total_desync_stats.soft + total_desync_stats.hard;
14348        let desync_descrip = if total_desyncs > 0 {
14349            let mut buf = String::new();
14350            write!(
14351                buf,
14352                "  Encountered {} soft desyncs, {} hard (with {} at context switch points), {} resyncs ({}/{} insertion/deletion).\n  Per thread (soft,hard,@switch,resync): ",
14353                total_desync_stats.soft,
14354                total_desync_stats.hard,
14355                total_desync_stats.at_context_switch,
14356                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions + total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
14357                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions,
14358                total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
14359            )?;
14360            if let Some(ref replayer) = self.replayer {
14361                for (tid, desync_stats) in replayer.desync_counts.iter() {
14362                    write!(
14363                        buf,
14364                        "{}=>({},{},{},{}) ",
14365                        tid,
14366                        desync_stats.soft,
14367                        desync_stats.hard,
14368                        desync_stats.at_context_switch,
14369                        desync_stats.resync_insertions + desync_stats.resync_deletions,
14370                    )?;
14371                }
14372            }
14373            writeln!(buf)?;
14374            Some(buf)
14375        } else {
14376            None
14377        };
14378
14379        let (reprio_descrip, info_reprio_descrip) = if let Some(pw) = self.preemption_writer.take()
14380        {
14381            let mut buf = String::new();
14382            writeln!(
14383                buf,
14384                "Record of {} preemption and reprioritization events:",
14385                pw.len()
14386            )?;
14387            let info_description;
14388            if let Some(path) = preemptions_to {
14389                // Preserve the full human/JSON description; build the INFO
14390                // description before adding the host artifact destination.
14391                info_description = buf.clone();
14392                writeln!(buf, "  (Writing to file {:?})", path)?;
14393                if let Err(str) = pw.flush() {
14394                    tracing::warn!("{}", str);
14395                }
14396            } else {
14397                // Recording, but not outputting to file, so this is the only (partial) record of it:
14398                writeln!(buf, "{}", truncated(200, pw.into_string()))?;
14399                info_description = buf.clone();
14400            }
14401            (Some(buf), Some(info_description))
14402        } else {
14403            (None, None)
14404        };
14405
14406        let num_processes = self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.len() as u64;
14407        let num_threads = self.thread_tree.size() as u64;
14408        let threads_descrip = format!("{}", self.thread_tree);
14409
14410        // Aggregate the per-thread timeslice distributions collected at thread
14411        // exit. BTreeMap gives a deterministic (dettid-sorted) ordering.
14412        let per_thread_timeslice: Vec<(DetTid, TimesliceStats)> = self
14413            .per_thread_timeslice
14414            .iter()
14415            .map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v))
14416            .collect();
14417        let mut timeslice_stats = TimesliceStats::default();
14418        for (_, st) in &per_thread_timeslice {
14419            timeslice_stats.merge(st);
14420        }
14421        let syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.values().copied().sum();
14422
14423        Ok((
14424            RunSummary {
14425                sched_turns: self.turn,
14426                schedevent_replayed,
14427                schedevent_recorded: self.recorded_event_count,
14428                schedevent_desynced: total_desyncs,
14429                // schedevent_desynced_at_context_switch: total_desyncs.at_context_switch,
14430                desync_descrip,
14431                reprio_descrip,
14432                threads_descrip,
14433                num_processes,
14434                num_threads,
14435                syscalls: Some(syscalls),
14436                virttime_elapsed: 0, // Cannot fill.
14437                virttime_final: 0,   // Cannot fill.
14438                realtime_elapsed: None,
14439                timeslice_stats,
14440                per_thread_timeslice,
14441                // The backend, not the scheduler, measures dispatch.
14442                dispatch_stats: None,
14443                // GlobalState records the effective run configuration.
14444                preemption: None,
14445            },
14446            info_reprio_descrip,
14447        ))
14448    }

14450    /// Summarize the state of the scheduler while executing (verbose).
14451    pub fn full_summary(&self) -> String {
14452        let mut buf = String::new();
14453        write!(&mut buf, "  {}", self.run_queue).unwrap();
14454
14455        let total_futex_blocked: usize = self.blocked.futex_waiters.iter().map(|v| v.1.len()).sum();
14456        writeln!(
14457            &mut buf,
14458            "\n  Futex-waiters, {} blocked on {} futexes:",
14459            total_futex_blocked,
14460            self.blocked.futex_waiters.len()
14461        )
14462        .unwrap();
14463        // Sorted, and no `Ivar` Debug. `format_terminal_deadlock` above already
14464        // documents the two sources this avoids, and this function had neither
14465        // guard: `futex_waiters` is a `HashMap`, so it iterates in a randomized
14466        // order once it holds more than one entry, and `FutexWaiter`'s derived
14467        // `Debug` prints its `Ivar`'s parked waker as raw host pointers.
14468        //
14469        // Measured before this change, three runs of
14470        // `--stop-after-turn=15 -- rustbin_futex_and_print`, which reaches this
14471        // function through the `--stop-after-turn` warning:
14472        //   Waker { data: 0x564ea2a82c80
14473        //   Waker { data: 0x55f2120b9c80
14474        //   Waker { data: 0x56163deeec80
14475        // Three runs, three host addresses, in a WARN record that
14476        // `--verify-strict` compares.
14477        //
14478        // Only guest-level identities are printed here: the futex key, the
14479        // waiting dettid and the bitset are all values Detcore already
14480        // determinizes.
14481        let mut futex_rows: Vec<String> = self
14482            .blocked
14483            .futex_waiters
14484            .iter()
14485            .map(|(futex, waiters)| {
14486                let mut dettids: Vec<String> =
14487                    waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid.to_string()).collect();
14488                dettids.sort();
14489                let mut bitsets: Vec<u32> = waiters.iter().map(|w| w.bitset).collect();
14490                bitsets.sort_unstable();
14491                format!(
14492                    "    {:?} => {} waiter(s), dettids [{}], bitsets {:?}",
14493                    futex,
14494                    waiters.len(),
14495                    dettids.join(", "),
14496                    bitsets
14497                )
14498            })
14499            .collect();
14500        futex_rows.sort();
14501        for row in futex_rows {
14502            writeln!(&mut buf, "{}", row).unwrap();
14503        }
14504
14505        writeln!(
14506            &mut buf,
14507            "\n  Timed-waiters, {}:",
14508            self.blocked.timed_waiters.len()
14509        )
14510        .unwrap();
14511        for (time, dtid) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
14512            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {} => {}", time, dtid).unwrap();
14513        }
14514
14515        writeln!(
14516            &mut buf,
14517            "\n  External-IO-blocked, {}:",
14518            self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len(),
14519        )
14520        .unwrap();
14521        for x in &self.blocked.external_io_blockers {
14522            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
14523        }
14524
14525        writeln!(
14526            &mut buf,
14527            "\n  Rt-sigsuspend-blocked, {}:",
14528            self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len(),
14529        )
14530        .unwrap();
14531        for x in &self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers {
14532            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
14533        }
14534
14535        writeln!(&mut buf, "\n  Next_turns: ").unwrap();
14536        for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
14537            writeln!(
14538                &mut buf,
14539                " ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}",
14540                dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp
14541            )
14542            .unwrap();
14543        }
14544        buf
14545    }

14547    // Return whether we should print the stacktrace after recording this event.
14548    // This is redundant with the consume_schedevent logic but allows us to print on either
14549    // recording or replay.
14550    pub fn record_event(&mut self, ev: &SchedEvent) -> MaybePrintStack {
14551        debug!(
14552            "[dtid {}] Record scheduled event #{}: {:?}",
14553            &ev.dettid, self.recorded_event_count, ev
14554        );
14555        let pw = self
14556            .preemption_writer
14557            .as_mut()
14558            .expect("trace_schedevent should be called only when preemption_writer is set");
14559        pw.insert_schedevent(ev.clone());
14560
14561        let print_stack = self.try_pop_stacktrace_event(self.recorded_event_count, ev);
14562        self.recorded_event_count += 1;
14563        print_stack
14564    }

14566    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14567    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
14568    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#869)
14569    // Returns the logical duration until any previously scheduled alarm, if any (zero otherwise).
14570    pub fn register_alarm(
14571        &mut self,
14572        detpid: DetPid,
14573        dettid: DetTid,
14574        now: LogicalTime,
14575        duration: LogicalTime,
14576        interval: LogicalTime,
14577        sig: Signal,
14578    ) -> (LogicalTime, LogicalTime) {
14579        let was_inactive = matches!(
14580            self.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_phase(detpid),
14581            Some(timed_waiters::AlarmPhase::Inactive { .. })
14582        );
14583        let old = if duration == LogicalTime::ZERO {
14584            // Alarm of 0 cancels any pending signal.
14585            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_alarm(detpid)
14586        } else {
14587            // POSIX timers' SIGALRM entries are not followed once ITIMER_REAL
14588            // is armed (4262 design §3.4), from this arm on.
14589            if self.coalesces_alarms() {
14590                self.lose_timer_observability(detpid, sig as libc::c_int);
14591            }
14592            let target_time = now + duration;
14593            self.blocked
14594                .timed_waiters
14595                .insert_alarm(target_time, detpid, dettid, sig, interval)
14596        };
14597        if let Some((old_target_time, old_interval)) = old {
14598            if was_inactive {
14599                // A timer waiting for the dequeue of its last expiry's copy
14600                // has no time left, as Linux's `itimer_get_remtime` reports
14601                // an inactive hrtimer (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
14602                return (LogicalTime::ZERO, old_interval);
14603            }
14604            let remain_ns = self.active_alarm_remaining_ns(old_target_time, now);
14605            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(remain_ns), old_interval)
14606        } else {
14607            // Return 0 if no previous alarm, as per https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/alarm.2.html
14608            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::ZERO)
14609        }
14610    }

14612    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14613    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#869)
14614    pub fn register_posix_timer(
14615        &mut self,
14616        detpid: DetPid,
14617        target: SignalTarget,
14618        timer_id: i32,
14619        deadline: Option<LogicalTime>,
14620        interval: LogicalTime,
14621        sig: timed_waiters::TimerSignal,
14622    ) {
14623        // Every set, arming or disarming, and the delete, which comes here
14624        // with no deadline, makes an earlier expiry stale
14625        // (`posix_timer_arm_generation`).
14626        *self
14627            .posix_timer_arm_generations
14628            .entry((detpid, timer_id))
14629            .or_default() += 1;
14630        if let Some(deadline) = deadline {
14631            self.blocked
14632                .timed_waiters
14633                .insert_posix_timer(deadline, detpid, target, timer_id, sig, interval);
14634        } else {
14635            self.blocked
14636                .timed_waiters
14637                .remove_posix_timer(detpid, timer_id);
14638        }
14639    }

14641    /// The arming generation of POSIX timer `timer_id` of `detpid`: how many
14642    /// times it has been set, by `timer_settime` (arming, rearming or
14643    /// disarming) or `timer_delete`, each of which reaches
14644    /// `register_posix_timer`; 0 for a timer never set. It is Linux's
14645    /// `it_signal_seq`, which `do_timer_settime` bumps so that an expiry queued
14646    /// before the set is dropped as stale at dequeue (kernel/time/posix-timers.c).
14647    /// An expiry recorded with a generation older than this one is stale. A
14648    /// process's generations are dropped when it is retired, so a reused
14649    /// timer id starts again at 0 in a new process.
14650    ///
14651    /// The one counter for every consumer that tells a current expiry from a
14652    /// stale one: the discarded-at-send record's parked expiries
14653    /// (`DiscardedAtSend::unignore`, <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4293>).
14654    /// A later consumer should read this rather than keep a counter of its own.
14655    pub(crate) fn posix_timer_arm_generation(&self, detpid: DetPid, timer_id: i32) -> u64 {
14656        self.posix_timer_arm_generations
14657            .get(&(detpid, timer_id))
14658            .copied()
14659            .unwrap_or(0)
14660    }
14661
14662    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
14663    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-841): Review logical ITIMER_REAL state queries.
14664    pub fn alarm_remaining(&self, detpid: DetPid, now: LogicalTime) -> LogicalTime {
14665        self.blocked
14666            .timed_waiters
14667            .alarm_time(detpid)
14668            .map(|deadline| LogicalTime::from_nanos(self.active_alarm_remaining_ns(deadline, now)))
14669            .unwrap_or(LogicalTime::ZERO)
14670    }
14671
14672    /// The time left before an Active `ITIMER_REAL` deadline. One whose
14673    /// deadline has already passed (its pop waits for a turn boundary) reads
14674    /// 1 us, as Linux's `itimer_get_remtime` floors an active hrtimer, so a
14675    /// running timer never reads as disarmed. Record and replay keep the
14676    /// saturating 0 they recorded with (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
14677    fn active_alarm_remaining_ns(&self, deadline: LogicalTime, now: LogicalTime) -> u64 {
14678        let remaining = deadline.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos());
14679        if remaining == 0 && !self.recordreplay_modes {
14680            1_000
14681        } else {
14682            remaining
14683        }
14684    }
14685}

14687/// An `exited_thread_barriers` entry: a duplicate of the thread's pidfd, its
14688/// host process and thread IDs, and when it deregistered, which bounds the
14689/// wait (`exited_leader_valve`).
14690#[derive(Debug)]
14691struct ExitedThreadBarrier {
14692    pidfd: OwnedFd,
14693    physical_pid: i32,
14694    physical_tid: i32,
14695    since: std::time::Instant,
14696}
14697
14698impl ExitedThreadBarrier {
14699    /// Whether the kernel shows the thread exited, or else what it shows.
14700    ///
14701    /// The pidfd polls readable once the thread is gone, or once it has an
14702    /// exit state, except for a thread-group leader whose group still has
14703    /// other threads (`pidfd_poll` checks `delay_group_leader`, fs/pidfs.c):
14704    /// that leader is a zombie, and its pidfd turns readable only when the
14705    /// group empties, which would need sibling turns this barrier withholds.
14706    /// So a zombie (`Z`) or dead (`X`) state in its `/proc` stat counts too, as
14707    /// for `step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders`. The pidfd is polled first: a
14708    /// thread already gone may have had its TID reused by another task, whose
14709    /// stat says nothing about this one.
14710    fn settled(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
14711        let mut poll = libc::pollfd {
14712            fd: self.pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
14713            events: libc::POLLIN,
14714            revents: 0,
14715        };
14716        // SAFETY: one valid pollfd, and a zero timeout never blocks.
14717        let ready = unsafe { libc::poll(&mut poll, 1, 0) };
14718        if ready > 0 {
14719            return Ok(());
14720        }
14721        let polled = if ready < 0 {
14722            format!(
14723                "polling its pidfd failed: {}",
14724                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
14725            )
14726        } else {
14727            "its pidfd does not report it exited".to_string()
14728        };
14729        match std::fs::read(format!(
14730            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
14731            self.physical_pid, self.physical_tid
14732        )) {
14733            Ok(stat) => match task_state_of_stat(&stat) {
14734                Some('Z' | 'X') => Ok(()),
14735                Some(state) => Err(format!("{polled}, and its state is {state}")),
14736                None => Err(format!("{polled}, and its stat cannot be parsed")),
14737            },
14738            Err(error) => Err(format!("{polled}, and its stat cannot be read ({error})")),
14739        }
14740    }
14741}
14742
14743/// The state letter in the contents of a `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` file:
14744/// the first non-blank byte after the last `)`. The command name before it is
14745/// raw bytes, not necessarily UTF-8 (`PR_SET_NAME`, or a UTF-8 name the
14746/// kernel cut at 15 bytes), and may itself contain `)`; only the state letter
14747/// is ASCII (Codex review of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245>).
14748fn task_state_of_stat(stat: &[u8]) -> Option<char> {
14749    let close = stat.iter().rposition(|byte| *byte == b')')?;
14750    stat[close + 1..]
14751        .iter()
14752        .find(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace())
14753        .filter(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphabetic())
14754        .map(|byte| *byte as char)
14755}

14803    #[test]
14804    fn chaos_pick_is_seed_deterministic_and_covers_all_choices() {
14805        let choices = [10, 20, 30, 40];
14806
14807        // Same seed => identical sequence of picks (the reproducibility that
14808        // targeted chaos relies on).
14809        let mut a = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
14810        let mut b = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
14811        for _ in 0..64 {
14812            assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut a, &choices), chaos_pick(&mut b, &choices));
14813        }
14814
14815        // Over enough draws every choice is reachable (the bias actually explores
14816        // the space rather than pinning one option).
14817        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(9);
14818        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
14819        for _ in 0..256 {
14820            seen.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &choices).unwrap());
14821        }
14822        assert_eq!(
14823            seen,
14824            choices.iter().copied().collect(),
14825            "chaos_pick should be able to return every choice"
14826        );
14827
14828        // An empty slice yields None rather than panicking.
14829        assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[] as &[i32]), None);
14830
14831        // The front/back coin flip used by force_unblock_thread reaches both.
14832        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(7);
14833        let mut both = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
14834        for _ in 0..64 {
14835            both.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[true, false]).unwrap());
14836        }
14837        assert_eq!(both, [false, true].into_iter().collect());
14838    }

14878    /// A queued polling thread whose request carries `polls_guest_state_only`
14879    /// as given and retries after an attempt that moved nothing, with its
14880    /// latest grant recorded as the latest committed turn.
14881    fn queued_poller(sched: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, guest_state_only: bool) {
14882        register_known_thread(sched, tid);
14883        let mut resources = Resources::new(tid);
14884        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
14885        resources.poll_attempt = 1;
14886        resources.polls_guest_state_only = guest_state_only;
14887        sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(resources));
14888        sched.run_queue.push_poller(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, 1);
14889        sched.last_commit_at.insert(tid, sched.progress_epoch);
14890        if guest_state_only {
14891            sched
14892                .guest_state_polled_at
14893                .insert(tid, sched.progress_epoch);
14894        }
14895    }

14910        register_known_thread(&mut sched, opener);
14911        queued_poller(&mut sched, DetTid::from_raw(5), true);
14912        // A turn committed after the poller's latest grant was progress; its
14913        // next attempt may succeed.
14914        sched.progress_epoch += 1;
14915        sched.last_progress = sched.progress_epoch;
14916        assert!(!sched.nothing_else_can_run(opener));
14917    }

14959    /// A reader's read moves data (its grant), then its next read waits: the
14960    /// first grant was progress after a writer's failed attempt, which the
14961    /// reader's next request shows and its commit records, even once the
14962    /// reader is a fruitless poller again (F1).
14963    #[test]
14964    fn a_poll_grant_whose_next_request_shows_progress_is_recorded() {
14965        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14966        let opener = DetTid::from_raw(3);
14967        register_known_thread(&mut sched, opener);
14968        // The writer waits for room since before the reader's read.
14969        queued_poller(&mut sched, DetTid::from_raw(5), true);
14970        let reader = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14971        register_known_thread(&mut sched, reader);
14972        let poll = |attempt: u32| {
14973            let mut resources = Resources::new(reader);
14974            resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
14975            resources.poll_attempt = attempt;
14976            resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
14977            resources
14978        };
14979        // The read that moves data, then the next read, which commits.
14980        sched.next_turns[&reader].req.put(Ok(poll(0)));
14981        let _ = turn_answer(&mut sched, reader);
14982        register_known_thread(&mut sched, reader);
14983        sched.next_turns[&reader].req.put(Ok(poll(0)));
14984        let _ = turn_answer(&mut sched, reader);
14985        // That read found nothing, its first retry found nothing, and it
14986        // retries again.
14987        register_known_thread(&mut sched, reader);
14988        sched.next_turns[&reader].req.put(Ok(poll(2)));
14989        sched.run_queue.push_poller(reader, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, 2);
14990        assert!(!sched.nothing_else_can_run(opener));
14991    }

14993    /// A poller's retry that step 4 skipped and made runnable
14994    /// (`upgrade_polled_to_runnable`, which sets `poll_attempt` to 0) is still
14995    /// a retry after an attempt that moved nothing. Granting it neither makes
14996    /// the thread's previous grant progress nor the thread runnable work, so
14997    /// beside it the FIFO open can still learn that nothing else can run
14998    /// (Claude re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4329, H1).
14999    #[test]
15000    fn an_upgraded_retry_is_still_fruitless() {
15001        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15002        let opener = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15003        register_known_thread(&mut sched, opener);
15004        // A waiting writer, idle since before the poller's grants.
15005        queued_poller(&mut sched, DetTid::from_raw(5), true);
15006        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(7);
15007        register_known_thread(&mut sched, poller);
15008        let retry = |attempt: u32| {
15009            let mut resources = Resources::new(poller);
15010            resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
15011            resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
15012            resources.poll_attempt = attempt;
15013            resources
15014        };
15015        // Its first retry is granted, and moves nothing.
15016        sched.next_turns[&poller].req.put(Ok(retry(1)));
15017        let _ = turn_answer(&mut sched, poller);
15018        // The second is skipped and made runnable, then granted.
15019        register_known_thread(&mut sched, poller);
15020        sched.next_turns[&poller].req.put(Ok(retry(2)));
15021        sched.upgrade_polled_to_runnable(poller, &retry(2));
15022        let _ = turn_answer(&mut sched, poller);
15023        // Its third waits again.
15024        register_known_thread(&mut sched, poller);
15025        sched.next_turns[&poller].req.put(Ok(retry(3)));
15026        sched.run_queue.push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, 3);
15027        assert!(sched.nothing_else_can_run(opener));
15028    }

15050    /// A FIFO open's polling request (`waits_until_nothing_else_can_run`).
15051    fn fifo_open_poll(sched: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
15052        register_known_thread(sched, tid);
15053        let mut resources = Resources::new(tid);
15054        resources.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
15055        resources.poll_attempt = 1;
15056        resources.polls_guest_state_only = true;
15057        resources.waits_until_nothing_else_can_run = true;
15058        sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(resources));
15059    }

15061    /// A sleeping thread cannot run before its deadline, so it does not keep a
15062    /// FIFO open polling; the open's commit moves time to the deadline first
15063    /// rather than answering that nothing else can run (Claude review of
15064    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4329, F3).
15065    #[test]
15066    fn a_fifo_open_beside_a_sleeper_moves_time_to_its_deadline() {
15067        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15068        let opener = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15069        fifo_open_poll(&mut sched, opener);
15070        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15071        register_known_thread(&mut sched, sleeper);
15072        sched
15073            .blocked
15074            .timed_waiters
15075            .insert(LogicalTime::from_nanos(2_000_000_000), sleeper);
15076        assert!(sched.nothing_else_can_run(opener));
15077        let answer = turn_answer(&mut sched, opener);
15078        assert!(matches!(answer, Some(SchedResponse::Go(_))), "{answer:?}");
15079        assert!(sched.fast_forward_for_alone_poller);
15080    }

15117    /// A thread that decided, in its own turn, that a default action ends its
15118    /// group runs its group `Exit` next, ahead of a thread queued before it;
15119    /// a thread that does not hold the turn cannot ask for that
15120    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4278).
15121    #[test]
15122    fn a_group_exit_decided_in_a_turn_is_granted_before_any_other_thread_runs() {
15123        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15124        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(41);
15125        let decider = DetTid::from_raw(43);
15126        for tid in [sibling, decider] {
15127            register_known_thread(&mut sched, tid);
15128        }
15129        sched.next_turns[&sibling]
15130            .req
15131            .put(Ok(Resources::new(sibling)));
15132        sched.run_queue.push_back(sibling, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15133        assert!(!sched.hold_turn_for_group_exit(decider));
15134        sched.set_running_for_test(decider);
15135        assert!(!sched.hold_turn_for_group_exit(sibling));
15136        assert!(sched.hold_turn_for_group_exit(decider));
15137        sched.next_turns[&decider]
15138            .req
15139            .put(Ok(Resources::new(decider)));
15140        sched.run_queue.push_back(decider, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15141        let (chosen, ..) = sched.select_test_turn().unwrap();
15142        assert_eq!(chosen, decider);
15143        sched.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
15144        // Once the decider has left the run set, it is forgotten.
15145        assert!(sched.run_queue.remove_tid(decider));
15146        sched.next_turns.remove(&decider);
15147        let (chosen, ..) = sched.select_test_turn().unwrap();
15148        assert_eq!(chosen, sibling);
15149        assert_eq!(sched.group_exit_decider, None);
15150    }

15218    /// A process's exit watch stays current through its leader's normal exit,
15219    /// for its siblings, and stops being current when a new registration
15220    /// replaces it (2ee7190125's test, with the watch armed directly).
15221    #[test]
15222    fn process_exit_watch_survives_leader_exit_and_rejects_reused_identity() {
15223        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15224        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(37);
15225        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(38);
15226        let mm = MmId::initial(leader);
15227        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
15228        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
15229        let (handle, stop, other_tid) = spawn_host_thread_until_told();
15230        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
15231        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, sibling, false);
15232        for (thread, physical) in [(leader, physical_tid), (sibling, other_tid)] {
15233            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
15234            scheduler.record_thread_mm(thread, mm);
15235            scheduler
15236                .register_physical_thread(thread, mm, physical_pid, physical)
15237                .unwrap();
15238        }
15239        let arm = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
15240            let pidfd = crate::tool_global::open_process_pidfd(physical_pid).unwrap();
15241            scheduler.arm_process_exit_watch(leader, mm, physical_pid, pidfd)
15242        };
15243        let old = arm(&mut scheduler);
15244        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, mm);
15245        assert!(scheduler.process_exit_watch_is_current(&old));
15246        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&sibling));
15247        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&sibling, &leader, mm);
15248        assert!(
15249            scheduler.process_exit_watch_is_current(&old),
15250            "normal death still needs cleanup"
15251        );
15252        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
15253        scheduler
15254            .register_physical_thread(leader, mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
15255            .unwrap();
15256        let replacement = arm(&mut scheduler);
15257        assert!(!Arc::ptr_eq(&old, &replacement));
15258        assert!(!scheduler.process_exit_watch_is_current(&old));
15259        assert!(scheduler.process_exit_watch_is_current(&replacement));
15260        stop.send(()).unwrap();
15261        handle.join().unwrap();
15262    }

15264    /// A host thread that reports its TID and then waits until it is told to
15265    /// exit, for the exited-thread barrier tests.
15266    fn spawn_host_thread_until_told() -> (
15267        std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
15268        std::sync::mpsc::Sender<()>,
15269        i32,
15270    ) {
15271        let (tid_tx, tid_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
15272        let (exit_tx, exit_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
15273        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
15274            tid_tx
15275                .send(unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 })
15276                .unwrap();
15277            let _ = exit_rx.recv();
15278        });
15279        let tid = tid_rx.recv().unwrap();
15280        (handle, exit_tx, tid)
15281    }

15283    #[test]
15284    fn turns_wait_until_the_kernel_ends_a_thread_that_exited_by_its_own_grant() {
15285        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15286        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(36);
15287        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(37);
15288        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(36);
15289        let mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
15290        let (handle, exit_tx, tid) = spawn_host_thread_until_told();
15291        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
15292        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, dettid, false);
15293        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
15294        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, dettid);
15295        scheduler
15296            .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, std::process::id() as i32, tid)
15297            .unwrap();
15298        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
15299
15300        // The backend reports the exit before the kernel carries it out.
15301        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(dettid, detpid, mm);
15302        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid));
15303        assert!(!scheduler.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&dettid));
15304        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.contains_key(&dettid));
15305        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err());
15306        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err());
15307
15308        exit_tx.send(()).unwrap();
15309        handle.join().unwrap();
15310        // The join returns at the CLEARTID wake; the kernel sets the exit
15311        // state, which the pidfd reports, a little later.
15312        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
15313        while scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err() {
15314            assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10));
15315        }
15316        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15317        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
15318    }

15320    /// The body of the helper process's second thread: it waits for a signal
15321    /// until the test kills the process.
15322    extern "C" fn pause_forever(_: *mut libc::c_void) -> libc::c_int {
15323        loop {
15324            // SAFETY: pause has no arguments and only waits for a signal.
15325            unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pause) };
15326        }
15327    }
15328
15329    /// A thread-group leader that exits while another thread of its group
15330    /// lives is a zombie whose pidfd stays unreadable until the group empties
15331    /// (`delay_group_leader` in fs/pidfs.c). Its siblings need turns to empty
15332    /// it, so the zombie state itself must settle the barrier, or a DBT
15333    /// `pthread_exit` from main deadlocks (Claude re-review of
15334    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4315 at 4c08c669).
15335    #[test]
15336    fn a_zombie_leader_with_a_live_sibling_settles_its_exit_barrier() {
15337        // SAFETY: the child runs only raw system calls and the clone wrapper
15338        // before it exits, never returning into the test harness.
15339        let child = unsafe { libc::fork() };
15340        assert!(child >= 0, "fork failed");
15341        if child == 0 {
15342            unsafe {
15343                let stack_size = 64 * 1024;
15344                let stack = libc::mmap(
15345                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
15346                    stack_size,
15347                    libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
15348                    libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS,
15349                    -1,
15350                    0,
15351                );
15352                if stack == libc::MAP_FAILED {
15353                    libc::_exit(2);
15354                }
15355                let flags = libc::CLONE_VM
15356                    | libc::CLONE_FS
15357                    | libc::CLONE_FILES
15358                    | libc::CLONE_SIGHAND
15359                    | libc::CLONE_THREAD
15360                    | libc::CLONE_SYSVSEM;
15361                if libc::clone(
15362                    pause_forever,
15363                    stack.cast::<u8>().add(stack_size).cast(),
15364                    flags,
15365                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
15366                ) < 0
15367                {
15368                    libc::_exit(3);
15369                }
15370                // The leader alone exits; its sibling keeps the group alive.
15371                libc::syscall(libc::SYS_exit, 0);
15372            }
15373            unreachable!();
15374        }
15375        /// Kills and reaps the helper even when an assertion fails first.
15376        struct Reap(libc::pid_t);
15377        impl Drop for Reap {
15378            fn drop(&mut self) {
15379                // SAFETY: the helper is this test's own child.
15380                unsafe {
15381                    libc::kill(self.0, libc::SIGKILL);
15382                    libc::waitpid(self.0, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
15383                }
15384            }
15385        }
15386        let _reap = Reap(child);
15387        let process_pidfd = crate::tool_global::open_process_pidfd(child).unwrap();
15388        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
15389        loop {
15390            let stat = std::fs::read(format!("/proc/{child}/task/{child}/stat")).unwrap();
15391            if task_state_of_stat(&stat) == Some('Z') {
15392                break;
15393            }
15394            assert!(
15395                started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10),
15396                "the leader never exited"
15397            );
15398            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
15399        }
15400
15401        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15402        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(37);
15403        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(37));
15404        scheduler
15405            .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, child, child)
15406            .unwrap();
15407        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
15408        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);
15409        let barrier = &scheduler.exited_thread_barriers[&dettid];
15410        let mut poll = libc::pollfd {
15411            fd: barrier.pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
15412            events: libc::POLLIN,
15413            revents: 0,
15414        };
15415        // The pidfd alone would hold the barrier.
15416        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::poll(&mut poll, 1, 0) }, 0);
15417        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_ok());
15418        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15419        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
15420        let mut process_poll = libc::pollfd {
15421            fd: process_pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
15422            events: libc::POLLIN,
15423            revents: 0,
15424        };
15425        assert_eq!(
15426            unsafe { libc::poll(&mut process_poll, 1, 0) },
15427            0,
15428            "leader-only exit is not whole-process death"
15429        );
15430        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::kill(child, libc::SIGKILL) }, 0);
15431        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::poll(&mut process_poll, 1, 5000) }, 1);
15432        assert_ne!(process_poll.revents & libc::POLLIN, 0);
15433    }

15435    /// An exit_group's grant ends every thread of the group, and the threads it
15436    /// kills have no Exit grant of their own, so the grant itself holds turns
15437    /// until the kernel has ended each thread of the group that has a host
15438    /// pidfd, and no other process's (Claude review of
15439    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4277 at 65138a17, N3).
15440    #[test]
15441    fn an_exit_group_grant_holds_turns_for_every_thread_of_its_group() {
15442        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15443        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(36);
15444        let process = DetPid::from_raw(36);
15445        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(37);
15446        let other = DetTid::from_raw(40);
15447        let mm = MmId::initial(process);
15448        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
15449        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, sibling, false);
15450        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(other, other, true);
15451        let mut host_threads = Vec::new();
15452        for (tid, tid_mm) in [(leader, mm), (sibling, mm), (other, MmId::initial(other))] {
15453            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
15454            let (handle, exit_tx, host_tid) = spawn_host_thread_until_told();
15455            scheduler
15456                .register_physical_thread(tid, tid_mm, std::process::id() as i32, host_tid)
15457                .unwrap();
15458            host_threads.push((handle, exit_tx));
15459        }
15460
15461        assert!(
15462            scheduler
15463                .block_for_one_resource(
15464                    sibling,
15465                    &ResourceID::Exit {
15466                        group: true,
15467                        process,
15468                        mm,
15469                    },
15470                    &Permission::RW,
15471                    None,
15472                    None,
15473                    &Ivar::new(),
15474                )
15475                .is_ok()
15476        );
15477        assert_eq!(
15478            scheduler
15479                .exited_thread_barriers
15480                .keys()
15481                .copied()
15482                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15483            vec![leader, sibling]
15484        );
15485        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err());
15486
15487        for (handle, exit_tx) in host_threads {
15488            exit_tx.send(()).unwrap();
15489            handle.join().unwrap();
15490        }
15491        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
15492        while scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err() {
15493            assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10));
15494        }
15495        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15496        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
15497    }

15499    #[test]
15500    fn turns_are_not_held_for_a_thread_without_its_own_grant_or_of_another_image() {
15501        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15502        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(37);
15503        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(37);
15504        let mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
15505        let (handle, exit_tx, tid) = spawn_host_thread_until_told();
15506        scheduler
15507            .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, std::process::id() as i32, tid)
15508            .unwrap();
15509
15510        // Killed with its group, or by a signal: no Exit grant of its own.
15511        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);
15512        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15513        // An exec's earlier image deregisters while the host thread lives on.
15514        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
15515        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm.for_exec(detpid));
15516        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15517        // No host thread is registered for it (ptrace).
15518        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(DetTid::from_raw(38), mm);
15519        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
15520        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_ok());
15521
15522        exit_tx.send(()).unwrap();
15523        handle.join().unwrap();
15524    }

15527    fn a_thread_the_kernel_never_ends_is_refused_by_name_past_the_valve() {

15552    fn required_physical_thread_pidfd_does_not_fall_back_to_virtual_tid() {

15566    /// A four-generation chain of single-threaded processes, each live in the
15567    /// run set: root 1, its child 2, grandchild 3 and great-grandchild 4.
15568    /// Process 4 is a clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal.
15569    fn process_chain() -> Scheduler {
15570        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15571        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15572        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
15573        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
15574        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
15575        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
15576            middle,
15577            orphan,
15578            true,
15579            false,
15580            libc::SIGUSR1,
15581        );
15582        for pid in [root, inner, middle, orphan] {
15583            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
15584        }
15585        scheduler
15586    }
15587
15588    /// The exit of single-threaded `pid` after its Exit grant: what an
15589    /// `exit_group` does.
15590    fn exit_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, pid: DetPid) {
15591        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(pid);
15592        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&pid, &pid, MmId::initial(pid));
15593    }

15595    /// Detcore's process groups and sessions answer as Linux's
15596    /// (`setsid_decision`, `setpgid_decision`; slice B3a-4c of
15597    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266).
15598    #[test]
15599    fn process_groups_and_sessions_follow_linux() {
15600        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15601        let root = DetPid::from_raw(3);
15602        let child = DetPid::from_raw(5);
15603        let other = DetPid::from_raw(7);
15604        for pid in [root, child, other] {
15605            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, pid, true);
15606        }
15607        // The root's group and session come from outside the namespace.
15608        assert_eq!(
15609            scheduler.thread_tree.process_group(root),
15610            Some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE)
15611        );
15612        assert_eq!(
15613            scheduler.thread_tree.session(child),
15614            Some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE)
15615        );
15616        // A child may lead its own group, and a sibling may join it.
15617        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(child, 0, 0), Ok((child, child)));
15618        scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(child, child);
15619        assert_eq!(
15620            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, other.as_raw(), child.as_raw()),
15621            Ok((other, child))
15622        );
15623        // No such group, a negative group, no such process.
15624        assert_eq!(
15625            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, other.as_raw(), 99),
15626            Err(Errno::EPERM)
15627        );
15628        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, 0, -1), Err(Errno::EINVAL));
15629        // The kernel takes a zero group as the pid before checking its sign.
15630        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, -5, 0), Err(Errno::EINVAL));
15631        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, 42, 0), Err(Errno::ESRCH));
15632        // Not the caller's child.
15633        assert_eq!(
15634            scheduler.setpgid_decision(child, other.as_raw(), 0),
15635            Err(Errno::ESRCH)
15636        );
15637        // A group with the caller's id exists: setsid is EPERM.
15638        assert_eq!(scheduler.setsid_decision(child), Err(Errno::EPERM));
15639        // The root leads no group: setsid succeeds, and it then leads both.
15640        assert_eq!(scheduler.setsid_decision(root), Ok(()));
15641        scheduler.thread_tree.create_session(root);
15642        assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_tree.process_group(root), Some(root));
15643        assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_tree.session(root), Some(root));
15644        // A session leader cannot move; a child in another session cannot be
15645        // moved.
15646        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, 0, 0), Err(Errno::EPERM));
15647        assert_eq!(
15648            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, other.as_raw(), 0),
15649            Err(Errno::EPERM)
15650        );
15651        // A child that exec'd cannot be moved by its parent.
15652        let late = DetPid::from_raw(9);
15653        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, late, true);
15654        scheduler.thread_tree.record_successful_exec(late);
15655        assert_eq!(
15656            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, late.as_raw(), 0),
15657            Err(Errno::EACCES)
15658        );
15659        assert_eq!(scheduler.setpgid_decision(late, 0, 0), Ok((late, late)));
15660    }
15661
15662    /// A process Linux no longer has, although its wait record remains (a
15663    /// child its parent reaps automatically, here), has no group or session,
15664    /// is no member of its group, and cannot be moved; a live thread's id
15665    /// names its process, and pid 1 is the namespace's init
15666    /// (`group_or_session_of`, `process_exists`).
15667    #[test]
15668    fn process_groups_count_only_processes_linux_still_has() {
15669        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15670        let root = DetPid::from_raw(3);
15671        let child = DetPid::from_raw(5);
15672        let late = DetPid::from_raw(7);
15673        for pid in [root, child, late] {
15674            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, pid, true);
15675        }
15676        assert_eq!(
15677            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, child.as_raw(), 0),
15678            Ok((child, child))
15679        );
15680        scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(child, child);
15681        assert_eq!(scheduler.group_or_session_of(child, false), Some(child));
15682        assert_eq!(
15683            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, late.as_raw(), child.as_raw()),
15684            Ok((late, child))
15685        );
15686        // The root ignores SIGCHLD, so its child is gone at its exit.
15687        scheduler
15688            .thread_tree
15689            .set_sigchld_disposition(root, true, false);
15690        exit_process(&mut scheduler, child);
15691        assert!(!scheduler.process_exists(child));
15692        assert_eq!(scheduler.group_or_session_of(child, false), None);
15693        assert_eq!(scheduler.group_or_session_of(child, true), None);
15694        // Its group had no other member, so it no longer exists.
15695        assert_eq!(
15696            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, late.as_raw(), child.as_raw()),
15697            Err(Errno::EPERM)
15698        );
15699        assert_eq!(
15700            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, child.as_raw(), 0),
15701            Err(Errno::ESRCH)
15702        );
15703        // A live thread's id names its process; setpgid names a process, so
15704        // another thread's id is EINVAL. Once the thread exits, its id names
15705        // nothing.
15706        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(9);
15707        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(late, thread, false);
15708        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
15709        assert_eq!(
15710            scheduler.group_or_session_of(thread, false),
15711            Some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE)
15712        );
15713        assert_eq!(
15714            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, thread.as_raw(), 0),
15715            Err(Errno::EINVAL)
15716        );
15717        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&thread, &late, MmId::initial(late));
15718        assert_eq!(scheduler.group_or_session_of(thread, false), None);
15719        assert_eq!(
15720            scheduler.setpgid_decision(root, thread.as_raw(), 0),
15721            Err(Errno::ESRCH)
15722        );
15723        // The namespace's init, which no guest holds here.
15724        let init = DetPid::from_raw(1);
15725        assert_eq!(
15726            scheduler.group_or_session_of(init, false),
15727            Some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE)
15728        );
15729        assert_eq!(
15730            scheduler.group_or_session_of(init, true),
15731            Some(OUTSIDE_NAMESPACE)
15732        );
15733        assert_eq!(
15734            scheduler.group_or_session_of(DetPid::from_raw(42), false),
15735            None
15736        );
15737    }

15739    /// Where the backend registers the kernel's ids (DBT), the guest's and
15740    /// the kernel's numbers translate both ways for what `/proc` lists, a
15741    /// zombie included, and for nothing else (`procfs_ids`, slice B3a-4 of
15742    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266).
15743    #[test]
15744    fn procfs_numbers_translate_for_what_proc_lists() {
15745        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15746        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15747        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15748        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, thread, false);
15749        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
15750        for (tid, kernel) in [(2, (12, 12)), (3, (13, 13)), (4, (14, 14)), (5, (12, 15))] {
15751            scheduler
15752                .procfs_kernel_ids
15753                .insert(DetTid::from_raw(tid), kernel);
15754        }
15755        // A process's number is its kernel pid; another thread's, its tid.
15756        // The root, pid 1 here with no registration, is 1 in both.
15757        assert_eq!(
15758            scheduler.procfs_ids(true, &[1, 2, 3, 5, 9]),
15759            [Some(1), Some(12), Some(13), Some(15), None]
15760        );
15761        assert_eq!(
15762            scheduler.procfs_ids(false, &[1, 12, 13, 15, 99]),
15763            [Some(1), Some(2), Some(3), Some(5), None]
15764        );
15765        // A zombie is translated until it is reaped.
15766        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
15767        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_ids(true, &[4]), [Some(14)]);
15768        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_ids(false, &[14]), [Some(4)]);
15769        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(middle, orphan));
15770        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_ids(true, &[4]), [None]);
15771        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_ids(false, &[14]), [None]);
15772        // Where no kernel ids are registered (ptrace), or each is its
15773        // thread's own number (an in-guest native exec), every number is its
15774        // own.
15775        let mut agreeing = process_chain();
15776        assert_eq!(
15777            agreeing.procfs_ids(true, &[2, 3, 9]),
15778            [Some(2), Some(3), Some(9)]
15779        );
15780        agreeing
15781            .procfs_kernel_ids
15782            .insert(DetTid::from_raw(2), (2, 2));
15783        assert_eq!(agreeing.procfs_ids(false, &[2, 9]), [Some(2), Some(9)]);
15784    }

15786    /// The process table's answer for a per-process `/proc` file
15787    /// (`procfs_task`): a live process's file exists and its task has its
15788    /// memory map; a zombie's exists without one; a reaped process's and an
15789    /// unused number's do not; a live thread's below its process's `task`
15790    /// exists, and not below another process's; Hermit's init, pid 1 with
15791    /// no guest holding it, is live.
15792    #[test]
15793    fn procfs_task_answers_from_the_process_table() {
15794        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15795        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15796        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15797        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, thread, false);
15798        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
15799        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(orphan, None), (true, false));
15800        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(inner, Some(thread)), (true, false));
15801        assert_eq!(
15802            scheduler.procfs_task(thread, None),
15803            (true, false),
15804            "/proc/<tid>"
15805        );
15806        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(middle, Some(thread)), (false, false));
15807        assert_eq!(
15808            scheduler.procfs_task(DetTid::from_raw(9), None),
15809            (false, false)
15810        );
15811        // A zombie: its file exists, owned as a task without a memory map.
15812        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
15813        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(orphan, None), (true, true));
15814        // Reaped: gone.
15815        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(middle, orphan));
15816        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(orphan, None), (false, false));
15817        // A process that takes the pid again is live.
15818        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, orphan, true);
15819        scheduler.forget_previous_process_exit(orphan);
15820        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, orphan);
15821        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_task(orphan, None), (true, false));
15822        // Hermit's own init, where no guest holds pid 1.
15823        let empty = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15824        assert_eq!(
15825            empty.procfs_task(DetTid::from_raw(1), Some(DetTid::from_raw(1))),
15826            (true, false)
15827        );
15828    }
15829
15830    /// `/proc` lists every process from its creation until it is reaped,
15831    /// zombie included, and none of the threads that lead no process; a
15832    /// process's `task` lists its threads (`procfs_listing`,
15833    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4266).
15834    #[test]
15835    fn procfs_lists_processes_until_they_are_reaped_and_their_threads() {
15836        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15837        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15838        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15839        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, thread, false);
15840        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
15841        let listing = scheduler.procfs_listing(Some(inner));
15842        assert_eq!(listing.processes, [1, 2, 3, 4]);
15843        assert_eq!(listing.threads, [2, 5]);
15844        // A zombie is listed until its parent reaps it.
15845        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
15846        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes, [1, 2, 3, 4]);
15847        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(middle, orphan));
15848        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes, [1, 2, 3]);
15849        assert!(scheduler.procfs_listing(Some(orphan)).threads.is_empty());
15850        // Not a process: no `task`.
15851        assert!(scheduler.procfs_listing(Some(thread)).threads.is_empty());
15852        // A child reaped automatically is gone at its exit, before any wait.
15853        let ignored = DetPid::from_raw(6);
15854        scheduler
15855            .thread_tree
15856            .set_sigchld_disposition(inner, true, false);
15857        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, ignored, true);
15858        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, ignored);
15859        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes, [1, 2, 3, 6]);
15860        exit_process(&mut scheduler, ignored);
15861        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes, [1, 2, 3]);
15862        // A new process that reuses its pid is listed.
15863        scheduler
15864            .thread_tree
15865            .set_sigchld_disposition(inner, false, false);
15866        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, ignored, true);
15867        scheduler.forget_previous_process_exit(ignored);
15868        assert_eq!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes, [1, 2, 3, 6]);
15869        // So is an orphan of the namespace's init once it exits.
15870        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(7);
15871        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, grandchild, true);
15872        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, grandchild);
15873        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
15874        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(grandchild));
15875        assert!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes.contains(&7));
15876        exit_process(&mut scheduler, grandchild);
15877        assert!(!scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes.contains(&7));
15878        // A `CLONE_PARENT` child of the root has no guest parent: Hermit
15879        // reaps it, so it is gone at its exit; so is the root itself.
15880        let root = DetPid::from_raw(1);
15881        let sibling = DetPid::from_raw(8);
15882        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
15883            root,
15884            sibling,
15885            true,
15886            true,
15887            libc::SIGCHLD,
15888        );
15889        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
15890        assert!(scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes.contains(&8));
15891        exit_process(&mut scheduler, sibling);
15892        assert!(!scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes.contains(&8));
15893        exit_process(&mut scheduler, root);
15894        assert!(!scheduler.procfs_listing(None).processes.contains(&1));
15895    }

15897    /// `logically_kill_thread` runs again for a process that is already dead,
15898    /// from a thread's late exit hook at a moment the host chooses. An orphan
15899    /// already given to init is not searched for a subreaper again, even if a
15900    /// subreaper has appeared since, so the outcome is the first decision's.
15901    #[test]
15902    fn a_late_second_exit_record_does_not_re_decide_an_init_orphan() {
15903        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15904        let [root, _, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15905        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
15906        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
15907
15908        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
15909        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
15910
15911        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
15912        assert_eq!(
15913            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
15914            Some(middle)
15915        );
15916        assert!(
15917            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
15918        );
15919    }

15921    /// A parent that died without an Exit grant (killed) is recorded at its
15922    /// host-timed deregistration, and so is a subreaper's adoption of its
15923    /// orphans (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). The adoption
15924    /// records a determinism loss instead of passing as deterministic.
15925    #[test]
15926    fn adopting_the_orphans_of_a_killed_parent_records_a_determinism_loss() {
15927        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15928        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15929        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
15930        assert!(!scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&middle));
15931
15932        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
15933
15934        assert_eq!(
15935            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
15936            Some(inner)
15937        );
15938        assert_eq!(scheduler.determinism_losses.len(), 1);
15939        assert!(
15940            scheduler.determinism_losses[0].contains("without an Exit grant"),
15941            "{:?}",
15942            scheduler.determinism_losses
15943        );
15944    }
15945
15946    /// One SIGKILL kills a subreaper (5) and, in the same send, its child (3),
15947    /// whose own child (7) survives; the surviving subreaper root (1) sends.
15948    /// The victims retire in tid order, so 3 goes first while 5 is still
15949    /// registered. Its orphan must pass over the dying 5 to the root, and the
15950    /// adoption happens at the committed send, so it is no determinism loss
15951    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994).
15952    #[test]
15953    fn a_sigkill_cohort_subreaper_adopts_none_of_its_fellow_victims_orphans() {
15954        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15955        let [root, subreaper, middle, orphan] = [1, 5, 3, 7].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15956        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
15957        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, subreaper, true);
15958        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(subreaper, middle, true);
15959        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, orphan, true);
15960        for pid in [root, subreaper, middle, orphan] {
15961            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
15962            scheduler.record_thread_mm(pid, MmId::initial(pid));
15963        }
15964        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
15965        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(subreaper, true);
15966        let group = DetPid::from_raw(77);
15967        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(subreaper, group));
15968        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(middle, group));
15969
15970        let reserved = scheduler.reserve_sigkill_group(root, group, 0).unwrap();
15971        let victims = scheduler.commit_sigkill(reserved.token, true);
15972
15973        assert_eq!(
15974            victims.iter().map(|v| v.tid.as_raw()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
15975            [3, 5]
15976        );
15977        // 7 goes straight to the root: the dying 5 never adopts it. Then 5's
15978        // own exit gives the dead 3 to the root.
15979        assert_eq!(scheduler.reparentings, [(orphan, root), (middle, root)]);
15980        assert_eq!(
15981            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
15982            Some(root)
15983        );
15984        assert!(
15985            scheduler.determinism_losses.is_empty(),
15986            "{:?}",
15987            scheduler.determinism_losses
15988        );
15989        assert!(!scheduler.is_dying_sigkill_victim(subreaper));
15990    }
15991
15992    /// A subreaper outside a PID namespace never adopts from inside it: the
15993    /// search stops where the depth changes. An inner process's orphan, and
15994    /// the orphan of the namespace's own init, are left to init.
15995    #[test]
15996    fn a_subreaper_does_not_adopt_across_a_pid_namespace_boundary() {
15997        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
15998        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
15999        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
16000        // `inner` is a namespace init; `middle` and `orphan` live inside it.
16001        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
16002        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
16003        tree.add_child(root, root, true);
16004        tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
16005        tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
16006        tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
16007        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(inner), 1);
16008        assert_eq!(
16009            tree.pid_ns_depth(middle),
16010            1,
16011            "a child inherits its creator's depth"
16012        );
16013        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(root), 0);
16014        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
16015        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
16016
16017        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16018        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
16019        assert!(
16020            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
16021        );
16022
16023        // The namespace init itself dies: its children are not adopted by the
16024        // outer subreaper either.
16025        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
16026        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
16027        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
16028        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
16029        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16030        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
16031    }

16033    /// Orphans are decided in ascending pid order whatever order the hash map
16034    /// holds them in: 64 children, so a hash order that happens to be sorted
16035    /// is out of the question.
16036    #[test]
16037    fn orphans_are_decided_in_pid_order() {
16038        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
16039        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(1);
16040        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16041        let children: Vec<DetPid> = (0..64).map(|i| DetPid::from_raw(1000 - 7 * i)).collect();
16042        for child in &children {
16043            tree.add_child(parent, *child, true);
16044        }
16045        let mut expected = children.clone();
16046        expected.sort();
16047        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected);
16048        tree.orphan_to_init(expected[0]);
16049        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected[1..]);
16050    }

16062    /// A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process in
16063    /// the thread tree, but the backend reports its exit with its creator's
16064    /// pid. Its orphans are still decided when its last thread leaves.

16070        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, creator, true);

16072            creator,
16073            raw,
16074            true,
16075            false,

16089            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,

16124    /// A reused pid starts without the old process's subreaper flag, init

16145    /// When its parent's process exits, an orphan's wait parent becomes the
16146    /// nearest live child subreaper, as Linux's `forget_original_parent`
16147    /// does, with SIGCHLD as its exit signal (`reparent_leader`)
16148    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3997).
16149    #[test]
16150    fn an_orphan_goes_to_its_nearest_live_child_subreaper() {
16151        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
16152        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
16153        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
16154        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
16155        let orphan_wait = normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan));
16156        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
16157
16158        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16159
16160        assert!(scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
16161
16162        let metadata = scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan];
16163        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_parent, Some(inner));
16164        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_owner, inner);
16165        assert_eq!(metadata.exit_signal, libc::SIGCHLD);
16166        assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_tree.parent_process(&orphan), Some(inner));
16167        assert_eq!(
16168            scheduler.thread_tree.notification_signal(orphan),
16169            Some(libc::SIGCHLD)
16170        );
16171        assert_eq!(
16172            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(inner, orphan),
16173            ExactChildWaitState::Running
16174        );
16175        assert_eq!(
16176            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(middle, orphan),
16177            ExactChildWaitState::Unknown
16178        );
16179
16180        // The orphan exits: its new parent can wait for it.
16181        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
16182        assert_eq!(
16183            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
16184            Some(middle),
16185            "the exited child, the lower pid, is selected first"
16186        );
16187        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, middle));
16188        assert_eq!(
16189            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
16190            Some(orphan)
16191        );
16192        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, orphan));
16193        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)));
16194    }

16196    /// An orphan that has already exited when its parent does becomes
16197    /// waitable by the subreaper at that moment.
16198    #[test]
16199    fn an_exited_orphan_becomes_waitable_by_the_subreaper() {
16200        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
16201        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
16202        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
16203        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
16204        assert_eq!(
16205            scheduler.ready_child_wait(middle, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
16206            None,
16207            "a clone child does not match a SIGCHLD-class wait"
16208        );
16209
16210        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16211
16212        assert_eq!(
16213            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
16214            Some(orphan),
16215            "re-parenting made it a SIGCHLD child of the subreaper"
16216        );
16217    }
