16219    /// Without a live subreaper among its ancestors an orphan has no guest
16220    /// parent (the container's init). A subreaper with no live thread is
16221    /// skipped, and clearing the flag takes a process out of the search.
16222    #[test]
16223    fn an_orphan_without_a_live_subreaper_has_no_guest_parent() {
16224        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
16225        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
16226        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
16227        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, false);
16228        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16229        // The record still names the dead parent, as before subreapers were
16230        // modeled, and no live process can wait for the orphan.
16231        assert_eq!(
16232            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
16233            Some(middle)
16234        );
16235        assert_eq!(
16236            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].exit_signal,
16237            libc::SIGUSR1
16238        );
16239        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
16240        for parent in [root, inner] {
16241            assert!(
16242                !scheduler
16243                    .has_child_wait_target(parent, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
16244            );
16245        }
16246
16247        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
16248        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
16249        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
16250        // The inner subreaper has left the run set but is still its parent
16251        // in the record.
16252        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&inner);
16253        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
16254        assert_eq!(
16255            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
16256            Some(root)
16257        );
16258    }

16261    /// parent, but its real parent is init. So when it exits in turn, its own
16262    /// children go to init too, even if a process above the dead parent has

16288    /// When a subreaper itself exits, the orphans it had inherited move on to

16331    #[test]
16332    fn dbt_process_sigkill_completes_registered_child_lifecycle() {
16333        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16334            backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
16335        });
16336        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16337        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(37);
16338        let child = DetTid::from_raw(38);
16339        let child_mm = MmId::for_clone(MmId::initial(parent), child, false);
16340        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
16341        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
16342        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16343        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
16344        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
16345        scheduler
16346            .register_physical_thread(child, child_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
16347            .expect("PIDFD_THREAD must bind the current test thread");
16348
16349        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(child, child, true);
16350
16351        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&child));
16352        assert!(!scheduler.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&child));
16353        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child));
16354    }

16356    /// SIGKILL ends a whole thread group, so the DBT kill notice retires every
16357    /// live thread of the target's group, not only the thread it names, and a
16358    /// sibling's filed request is answered so that it runs no more guest code
16359    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362).
16360    #[test]
16361    fn dbt_process_sigkill_retires_every_thread_of_the_target_group() {
16362        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16363            *backend = reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT;
16364        });
16365        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16366        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(37);
16367        let child = DetTid::from_raw(38);
16368        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(39);
16369        let child_mm = MmId::for_clone(MmId::initial(parent), child, false);
16370        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
16371        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
16372        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16373        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
16374        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, sibling, false);
16375        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
16376        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
16377        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
16378        scheduler.record_thread_mm(sibling, child_mm);
16379        scheduler
16380            .register_physical_thread(child, child_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
16381            .expect("PIDFD_THREAD must bind the current test thread");
16382        scheduler.next_turns[&sibling]
16383            .req
16384            .put(Ok(Resources::new(sibling)));
16385        let sibling_response = scheduler.next_turns[&sibling].resp.clone();
16386
16387        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(child, child, true);
16388
16389        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&child));
16390        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&sibling));
16391        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&parent));
16392        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child));
16393        assert!(matches!(
16394            sibling_response.try_read(),
16395            Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(None))
16396        ));
16397    }

16399    /// A pidfd SIGKILL names the victim's leader. When that leader has exited
16400    /// while a sibling runs on, the kill notice retires the group through the
16401    /// sibling's registration; when the victim is a zombie whose exit was
16402    /// granted, there is nothing to retire and no deadlock
16403    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4411).
16404    #[test]
16405    fn dbt_process_sigkill_finds_an_exited_leaders_group_and_leaves_a_zombie_alone() {
16406        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16407            *backend = reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT;
16408        });
16409        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16410        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(37);
16411        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(38);
16412        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(39);
16413        let child_mm = MmId::for_clone(MmId::initial(parent), leader, false);
16414        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
16415        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
16416        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16417        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, leader, true);
16418        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, sibling, false);
16419        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
16420        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
16421        scheduler
16422            .register_physical_thread(sibling, child_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
16423            .expect("PIDFD_THREAD must bind the current test thread");
16424        let leader_process = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
16425
16426        // A thread-directed SIGKILL to the exited leader does not end the
16427        // group (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439,
16428        // R1): nothing is retired, and the notice reports it loudly.
16429        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(leader, leader_process, false);
16430        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&sibling));
16431        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.take().is_some());
16432
16433        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(leader, leader_process, true);
16434
16435        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
16436        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&sibling));
16437        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&parent));
16438
16439        let zombie = DetTid::from_raw(41);
16440        let zombie_process = DetPid::from_raw(zombie.as_raw());
16441        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, zombie, true);
16442        scheduler.grant_exit_for_test(zombie_process);
16443        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(zombie, zombie_process, true);
16444        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
16445
16446        // Without a granted exit, a victim no registration names stays the
16447        // loud false deadlock it was.
16448        let unknown = DetTid::from_raw(43);
16449        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, unknown, true);
16450        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(unknown, DetPid::from_raw(unknown.as_raw()), true);
16451        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_some());
16452    }
16453
16454    /// The thread tree never drops an edge, so a thread id reused by another
16455    /// process stays listed under the group it left. A process-directed
16456    /// SIGKILL to that old, exited group must not find the reused thread and
16457    /// retire it (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4439,
16458    /// R3; re-check N2).
16459    #[test]
16460    fn a_process_sigkill_does_not_take_a_reused_thread_id_from_another_group() {
16461        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
16462            *backend = reverie::BackendCapabilities::DBT;
16463        });
16464        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
16465        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(37);
16466        let old_leader = DetTid::from_raw(38);
16467        let reused = DetTid::from_raw(39);
16468        let new_leader = DetTid::from_raw(50);
16469        let new_mm = MmId::for_clone(MmId::initial(parent), new_leader, false);
16470        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
16471        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, old_leader, true);
16472        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(old_leader, reused, false);
16473        // The old group has exited; its thread id now names a thread of 50.
16474        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, new_leader, true);
16475        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(new_leader, reused, false);
16476        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
16477        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, reused);
16478        scheduler
16479            .register_physical_thread(reused, new_mm, std::process::id() as i32, unsafe {
16480                libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32
16481            })
16482            .expect("PIDFD_THREAD must bind the current test thread");
16483        let old_process = DetPid::from_raw(old_leader.as_raw());
16484        assert!(
16485            scheduler
16486                .thread_tree
16487                .my_thread_group(&old_process)
16488                .contains(&reused),
16489            "the stale edge this test is about must exist"
16490        );
16491
16492        assert_eq!(
16493            scheduler.sigkill_victim_registered_thread(old_leader, old_process, true),
16494            None
16495        );
16496        scheduler.note_process_sigkill(old_leader, old_process, true);
16497        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&reused));
16498        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_some());
16499    }

16501    fn install_runnable_exec_group(
16502        sched: &mut Scheduler,
16503        leader: DetTid,
16504        caller: DetTid,
16505    ) -> (DetPid, MmId, Ivar<SchedRequest>) {
16506        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
16507        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
16508        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
16509        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
16510        register_known_thread(sched, leader);
16511        register_known_thread(sched, caller);
16512        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
16513        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
16514        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
16515        (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request)
16516    }

16518    fn reconnect_nonleader_exec(
16519        sched: &mut Scheduler,
16520        leader: DetTid,
16521        caller: DetTid,
16522        detpid: DetPid,
16523        pre_exec_mm: MmId,
16524    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
16525        sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
16526            caller,
16527            new_leader: leader,
16528            detpid,
16529            pre_exec_mm,
16530            post_exec_mm: pre_exec_mm.for_exec(detpid),
16531            child_tid_addr: 0,
16532            reconnect_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
16533        })
16534    }

16536    fn reconnect_transferred_exec(
16537        sched: &mut Scheduler,

16539        caller: DetTid,
16540        detpid: DetPid,
16541        pre_exec_mm: MmId,
16542    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {

16550            reconnect_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
16551        })

16554    /// A readmitted thread keeps the priority the replayed schedule gave it
16555    /// while the schedule has events left, and is readmitted eagerly once it
16556    /// has run out (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472).
16557    #[test]
16558    fn a_readmission_keeps_its_replay_priority_until_the_schedule_runs_out() {
16559        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16560        let foreground = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16561        let readmitted = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16562        let event = SchedEvent::syscall(foreground, Sysno::getpid, SyscallPhase::Prehook);
16563        sched.replayer = Some(Replayer::new(vec![event.clone()]));
16564        sched
16565            .priorities
16566            .insert(foreground, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
16567        sched
16568            .priorities
16569            .insert(readmitted, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
16570
16571        sched.readmit_ready_thread(readmitted);
16572        assert_eq!(
16573            sched.run_queue.queued_priority(readmitted),
16574            Some(REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY)
16575        );
16576
16577        assert!(sched.run_queue.remove_tid(readmitted));
16578        let _ = sched.replayer.as_mut().unwrap().observe_event(&event);
16579        sched.readmit_ready_thread(readmitted);
16580        let eager = sched.run_queue.queued_priority(readmitted).unwrap();
16581        assert!(eager < REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY, "{eager}");
16582
16583        // Outside a schedule replay, readmission is always eager.
16584        sched.replayer = None;
16585        assert!(sched.run_queue.remove_tid(readmitted));
16586        sched.readmit_ready_thread(readmitted);
16587        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.queued_priority(readmitted), Some(eager));
16588    }
16589
16590    /// A thread queued at the deferred replay priority when the recording
16591    /// runs out does not stay behind the foreground thread: consuming the
16592    /// last recorded event gives every thread the default priority
16593    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472).
16594    #[test]
16595    fn the_last_replayed_event_releases_the_replay_priorities() {
16596        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16597        let foreground = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16598        let deferred = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16599        let first = SchedEvent::syscall(foreground, Sysno::getpid, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
16600            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000));
16601        let last = SchedEvent::syscall(foreground, Sysno::getppid, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
16602            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(20_000));
16603        sched.replayer = Some(Replayer::new(vec![first.clone(), last.clone()]));
16604        sched
16605            .priorities
16606            .insert(foreground, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
16607        sched.priorities.insert(deferred, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
16608        sched.readmit_ready_thread(deferred);
16609
16610        let _ = sched.consume_schedevent(&first);
16611        assert_eq!(
16612            sched.run_queue.queued_priority(deferred),
16613            Some(REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY)
16614        );
16615
16616        let _ = sched.consume_schedevent(&last);
16617        assert_eq!(
16618            sched.run_queue.queued_priority(deferred),
16619            Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY)
16620        );
16621        assert_eq!(sched.priorities.get(&foreground), Some(&DEFAULT_PRIORITY));
16622    }
16623
16624    /// A thread registering after the replayed schedule ran out takes the
16625    /// default priority like every other thread, not the deferred one; one
16626    /// registering earlier with no context switch to it takes its starting
16627    /// priority (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4472).
16628    #[test]
16629    fn a_thread_registering_after_the_replay_ran_out_takes_the_default_priority() {
16630        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16631        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16632        let early = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16633        let late = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16634        let last = SchedEvent::syscall(parent, Sysno::getpid, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
16635            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000));
16636        sched.replayer = Some(Replayer::new(vec![last.clone()]));
16637        sched.priorities.insert(parent, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
16638
16639        assert!(sched.replay_registration_priority(early, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY));
16640        assert_eq!(
16641            sched.priorities.get(&early),
16642            Some(&REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY)
16643        );
16644
16645        let _ = sched.consume_schedevent(&last);
16646        assert!(!sched.replay_registration_priority(late, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY));
16647        assert_eq!(sched.priorities.get(&late), Some(&DEFAULT_PRIORITY));
16648        assert_eq!(sched.priorities.get(&early), Some(&DEFAULT_PRIORITY));
16649    }

16651    /// Only a leader retired at its own exit while its group lives on counts
16652    /// as a retired exited leader; one that merely left `next_turns`, as at a
16653    /// host-timed deregistration on DBT, does not
16654    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4445).
16655    #[test]
16656    fn only_a_leader_retired_at_its_exit_names_a_retired_exited_leader() {
16657        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16658        let retired = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16659        let deregistered = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16660        sched.retired_exited_leaders.insert(retired);
16661        assert!(sched.names_a_retired_exited_leader(retired));
16662        assert!(!sched.names_a_retired_exited_leader(deregistered));
16663        // Registered again under the same tid: live, so no longer retired.
16664        register_known_thread(&mut sched, retired);
16665        assert!(!sched.names_a_retired_exited_leader(retired));
16666    }
16667
16668    fn exec_replay(
16669        caller: DetTid,
16670        next: DetTid,
16671        following: DetTid,
16672        branches: Option<u32>,
16673    ) -> (Replayer, SchedEvent) {
16674        let prehook = SchedEvent::syscall(caller, Sysno::execve, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
16675            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000));
16676        let mut events = vec![prehook.clone()];
16677        if let Some(count) = branches {
16678            let branch = SchedEvent::branches(next, count)
16679                .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000) + LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
16680            let other = SchedEvent {
16681                op: detcore_model::schedule::Op::OtherInstructions,
16682                count: 1,
16683                ..branch.clone()
16684            };
16685            events.extend([branch, other]);
16686        } else {
16687            events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
16688                next,
16689                Sysno::getpid,
16690                SyscallPhase::Prehook,
16691            ));
16692        }
16693        events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
16694            following,
16695            Sysno::getpid,
16696            SyscallPhase::Prehook,
16697        ));
16698        (Replayer::new(events), prehook)
16699    }

16701    #[tokio::test]
16702    async fn transferred_exec_reconnect_restores_replay_pre_hook_continuation_grant() {
16703        for branches in [Some(123), None] {
16704            let config = Config::default();
16705            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
16706            let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
16707            let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
16708            let unrelated = DetTid::from_raw(31);
16709            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request) =
16710                install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
16711            register_known_thread(&mut sched, unrelated);
16712            sched.runqueue_push_back(unrelated);
16713            let (replayer, prehook) = exec_replay(caller, leader, unrelated, branches);
16714            sched.replayer = Some(replayer);
16715            let duration = branches.map(|count| LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
16716
16717            // Exercise the actual prehook ContextSwitch(false, leader, ..),
16718            // including the priority and pending duration it stages.
16719            let consumed = sched.consume_schedevent(&prehook);
16720            assert!(consumed.keep_running);
16721            assert_eq!(consumed.event_ix, 0);
16722            assert_eq!(consumed.timeslice_remaining, duration);
16723            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&caller], REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
16724            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
16725            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
16726
16727            // The backend consumes the displaced leader before post-exec.
16728            // That removes its priority, but not its pending timeslice.
16729            sched.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
16730            let caller_request = sched.next_turns[&caller].req.clone();
16731            sched.turn = 41;
16732            sched.committed_time = GlobalTime::new(&config).as_nanos();
16733            let before = (sched.turn, sched.committed_time);
16734            let next_event = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap().cursor.peek().cloned();
16735            reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
16736
16737            assert_eq!((sched.turn, sched.committed_time), before);
16738            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
16739            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
16740            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&caller));
16741            assert!(matches!(caller_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
16742            assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
16743            assert_ne!(sched.next_turns[&leader].req, old_leader_request);
16744            let replayer = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap();
16745            assert_eq!(replayer.traced_event_count, 1);
16746            assert_eq!(replayer.events_popped, 1);
16747            assert_eq!(replayer.cursor.peek(), next_event.as_ref());
16748            assert_eq!(
16749                replayer.desync_counts,
16750                BTreeMap::from([(caller, replayer::DesyncStats::default())])
16751            );
16752
16753            for tid in [leader, unrelated] {
16754                let mut resources = Resources::new(tid);
16755                resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(tid), Permission::RW);
16756                sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(resources));
16757            }
16758            let continuation = sched.next_turns[&leader].resp.clone();
16759            let unrelated_response = sched.next_turns[&unrelated].resp.clone();
16760            assert!(continuation.try_read().is_none());
16761            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
16762            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16763            let granted = tokio::time::timeout(
16764                Duration::from_secs(5),
16765                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
16766            )
16767            .await
16768            .expect("the continuation grant must not stall")
16769            .expect("the replay continuation must be runnable");
16770            assert_eq!(granted.tid, leader);
16771            let Some(SchedResponse::Go(granted_duration)) = continuation.try_read() else {
16772                panic!("replacement did not receive an ordinary continuation grant");
16773            };
16774            assert_eq!(
16775                granted_duration,
16776                duration.map(|time| SchedValue::Value(time.as_nanos()))
16777            );
16778            assert!(unrelated_response.try_read().is_none());
16779            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
16780            assert_eq!(sched.turn, before.0 + 1);
16781            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&leader));
16782            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
16783            assert_eq!(
16784                sched.run_queue.tids().filter(|tid| **tid == leader).count(),
16785                1
16786            );
16787        }
16788    }

16825        let granted = tokio::time::timeout(

16830        .expect("the unrelated task's grant must not stall")
16831        .expect("the other replay task must retain its grant");
16832        assert_eq!(granted.tid, unrelated);
16833        assert!(continuation.try_read().is_none());
16834        let Some(SchedResponse::Go(Some(SchedValue::Value(duration)))) =
16835            unrelated_response.try_read()
16836        else {
16837            panic!("the other replay task lost its pending duration");
16838        };
16839        assert_eq!(duration, LogicalTime::from_rcbs(123).as_nanos());

16879            register_known_thread(&mut sched, unrelated);
16880            let unrelated_mm = MmId::initial(unrelated);
16881            assert!(sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(caller, pre_exec_mm));
16882
16883            if transfer {
16884                reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
16885            } else {
16886                reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
16887            }
16888
16889            // A transferred caller must not regain a clock component or merge
16890            // final statistics through a late ordinary RPC, in any address
16891            // space. The legacy reload mode's admission policy is unchanged.
16892            for mm in [pre_exec_mm, post_exec_mm, unrelated_mm] {
16893                assert_eq!(sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(caller, mm), !transfer);
16894            }
16895            assert!(!sched.thread_is_logically_killed(caller));
16896            assert!(sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(leader, post_exec_mm));
16897            assert!(!sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(leader, pre_exec_mm));
16898            assert!(sched.rpc_incarnation_matches(unrelated, unrelated_mm));
16899            assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&unrelated));
16900        }
16901    }

17076                child_tid_addr: 0,

17099    /// F1/F2: an admission deferred while a tentative_pop window is live must
17100    /// resolve its side -- including the `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw -- at
17101    /// the `DetTid`-ordered drain, so the drained run queue is a pure function of
17102    /// deterministic state, independent of the order in which racing handlers
17103    /// buffered the admissions.
17104    #[test]
17105    fn deferred_admission_side_is_arrival_order_independent() {
17106        let config = Config {
17107            sched_seed: Some(0xABCD),
17108            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
17109            ..Default::default()
17110        };
17111        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
17112        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
17113
17114        // Buffer the two children in `order`, optionally while a tentative
17115        // window is live, then drain. Return the drained relative order of the
17116        // two children (the anchor is filtered out because it is consumed by the
17117        // window in the `open_window` case but not otherwise -- what must be
17118        // deterministic is the children's order and chosen sides).
17119        let drained_order = |order: [DetTid; 2], open_window: bool| -> Vec<DetTid> {
17120            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17121            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17122            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
17123            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
17124            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
17125            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
17126
17127            if open_window {
17128                assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
17129                assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17130            }
17131            for tid in order {
17132                sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
17133            }
17134            // Admission ALWAYS defers -- window or not -- so nothing is pushed or
17135            // resolved (no side chosen, no PRNG drawn) until the drain.
17136            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&lower));
17137            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&higher));
17138            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(lower));
17139            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(higher));
17140
17141            if open_window {
17142                let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
17143            }
17144            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
17145            sched
17146                .run_queue
17147                .tids()
17148                .copied()
17149                .filter(|t| *t == lower || *t == higher)
17150                .collect()
17151        };
17152
17153        // The drained order/side is independent of BOTH host-timing inputs the
17154        // old immediate path was sensitive to: the arrival (buffering) order of
17155        // the racing handlers, and whether a tentative window happened to be
17156        // live when each handler ran.
17157        let baseline = drained_order([lower, higher], true);
17158        assert_eq!(
17159            baseline,
17160            drained_order([higher, lower], true),
17161            "arrival order"
17162        );
17163        assert_eq!(
17164            baseline,
17165            drained_order([lower, higher], false),
17166            "window state"
17167        );
17168        assert_eq!(baseline, drained_order([higher, lower], false), "both");
17169        assert!(baseline.contains(&lower) && baseline.contains(&higher));
17170    }

17172    #[test]
17173    fn robust_list_wake_batches_are_arrival_order_independent() {
17174        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
17175        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
17176        let first_owner = DetTid::from_raw(31);
17177        let second_owner = DetTid::from_raw(33);
17178        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(5));
17179        let lower_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100);
17180        let higher_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200);
17181
17182        let deliver = |reverse: bool| {
17183            let mut first = ThreadState::<()>::new(first_owner, &Config::default(), ());
17184            let mut second = first.clone();
17185            second.dettid = second_owner;
17186            first.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404100));
17187            second.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404200));
17188            first.stage_robust_list_wakes(
17189                RobustListExit::ExitGroup,
17190                vec![
17191                    (
17192                        second_owner,
17193                        vec![RobustListWake {
17194                            futex: higher_futex,
17195                        }],
17196                    ),
17197                    (first_owner, vec![RobustListWake { futex: lower_futex }]),
17198                ],
17199            );
17200            let first_time = DetTime::default();
17201            let mut second_time = first_time.clone();
17202            second_time.add_syscall();
17203            let ready = if reverse {
17204                assert_eq!(
17205                    second.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time.clone()),
17206                    None,
17207                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
17208                );
17209                first
17210                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time)
17211                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
17212                    .1
17213            } else {
17214                assert_eq!(
17215                    first.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time),
17216                    None,
17217                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
17218                );
17219                second
17220                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time)
17221                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
17222                    .1
17223            };
17224            let request: Vec<_> = ready
17225                .into_iter()
17226                .map(|(owner, wake)| (owner, wake.futex))
17227                .collect();
17228            assert_eq!(
17229                request,
17230                vec![(first_owner, lower_futex), (second_owner, higher_futex)],
17231                "one owner/futex-sorted request must carry the complete group"
17232            );
17233
17234            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17235            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17236            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
17237            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
17238            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
17239            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
17240            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&lower, lower_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
17241            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&higher, higher_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
17242
17243            assert_eq!(sched.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&request), vec![1, 1]);
17244
17245            let pending: Vec<_> = sched
17246                .pending_run_queue_admissions
17247                .iter()
17248                .map(|(tid, intent)| (*tid, *intent))
17249                .collect();
17250            assert_eq!(
17251                pending,
17252                vec![
17253                    (lower, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
17254                    (higher, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
17255                ]
17256            );
17257            assert_eq!(
17258                sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
17259                vec![anchor],
17260                "physical-exit wakes must wait for the deterministic drain"
17261            );
17262
17263            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
17264            let drained = sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>();
17265            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
17266            (pending, drained)
17267        };
17268
17269        let forward = deliver(false);
17270        let reverse = deliver(true);
17271        assert_eq!(forward, reverse);
17272        assert_eq!(forward.1, vec![DetTid::from_raw(5), lower, higher]);
17273    }

17275    /// F3: a run-queue removal requested while a tentative_pop window is live
17276    /// (an asynchronous exec reconnect racing the daemon) must be deferred, not
17277    /// applied through `remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` guard, and
17278    /// a pending-removal thread whose `next_turns` entry is already gone must not
17279    /// crash `are_all_quiesced`. The removal lands at the next drain.
17280    /// ITEM 1 REGRESSION: whether a thread is live and whether an id names a
17281    /// signal target are different questions.
17282    ///
17283    /// `process_signal_targets` models `kill(2)`: Linux's `kill_pid_info` looks
17284    /// the id up as a task and signals its whole thread group, so a live
17285    /// non-leader thread's id names its process
17286    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4094>; this test used to
17287    /// assert the opposite). `sched_setattr(2)` and its relatives resolve
17288    /// through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds the live task itself. The two
17289    /// still differ for a group whose leader has exited while a member lives:
17290    /// the leader's id names a process with one live thread, but the leader is
17291    /// not live. This test fails the moment `thread_is_live` is reduced to the
17292    /// kill resolver.
17293    #[test]
17294    fn a_non_leader_thread_is_live_without_being_a_kill_target() {
17295        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17296        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(11);
17297        let member = DetTid::from_raw(12);
17298        let stranger = DetTid::from_raw(13);
17299        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
17300        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, member, false);
17301        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
17302        register_known_thread(&mut sched, member);
17303
17304        assert!(sched.thread_is_live(leader), "the leader is obviously live");
17305        assert!(
17306            sched.thread_is_live(member),
17307            "a non-leader thread of a live group is live; sched_setattr must reach it"
17308        );
17309        assert!(
17310            !sched.thread_is_live(stranger),
17311            "a tid that was never registered is not live"
17312        );
17313
17314        // kill(2) names a process by any of its live threads' ids.
17315        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(member), Some(leader));
17316        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(leader), Some(leader));
17317        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(stranger), None);
17318        assert_eq!(sched.process_signal_targets(member), vec![leader, member]);
17319        assert_eq!(sched.process_signal_targets(leader), vec![leader, member]);
17320        assert!(sched.process_signal_targets(stranger).is_empty());
17321
17322        // The distinction being preserved: once the leader has exited, its id
17323        // still names the process (one live thread), but it is not live.
17324        sched.next_turns.remove(&leader);
17325        assert!(
17326            !sched.thread_is_live(leader),
17327            "an exited leader is not live; sched_setattr must not reach it"
17328        );
17329        assert_eq!(
17330            sched.process_signal_targets(leader),
17331            vec![member],
17332            "kill(2) to the exited leader's id reaches its live member"
17333        );
17334        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(leader), Some(leader));
17335        assert!(sched.thread_is_live(member));
17336    }
17337
17338    #[test]
17339    fn deferred_removal_survives_tentative_window_and_drains() {
17340        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17341        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
17342        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
17343        register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
17344        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
17345        sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
17346        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim);
17347
17348        // Daemon peeks the anchor and releases the lock (window open).
17349        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
17350        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17351
17352        // A racing handler descheduling the victim must buffer, not panic.
17353        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
17354        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
17355        assert!(
17356            sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim),
17357            "removal is deferred, so the stale entry lingers until the drain"
17358        );
17359
17360        // The handler has also made the victim logically dead: its next_turns
17361        // entry is gone. Iterating quiescence must SKIP the victim (filtered by
17362        // pending_run_queue_removals) rather than panic in check_request on the
17363        // missing next_turns entry -- without the filter this call panics.
17364        sched.next_turns.remove(&victim);
17365        let _ = sched.are_all_quiesced();
17366
17367        // Close the window and drain: the victim is gone, the anchor remains.
17368        let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
17369        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
17370        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17371        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
17372    }
17373
17374    /// Always-defer invariant (codex finding 1/2): even with NO tentative window
17375    /// live, a global-request handler NEVER pushes or pops the run queue
17376    /// directly -- both admission and removal are buffered and take effect only
17377    /// at the deterministic step2 drain. This removes the host-timing-dependent
17378    /// immediate path: whichever daemon phase a handler happened to race, it only
17379    /// records intent, so the run-queue mutation is applied at one fixed point in
17380    /// DetTid order regardless of host arrival timing.
17381    #[test]
17382    fn run_queue_mutations_always_defer_to_the_drain() {
17383        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17384        let keep = DetTid::from_raw(7);
17385        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
17386        register_known_thread(&mut sched, keep);
17387        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
17388        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim); // already queued; to be removed
17389        assert!(!sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17390
17391        // No window live, yet both mutations buffer rather than apply.
17392        sched.admit_to_run_queue(keep, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
17393        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
17394        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&keep));
17395        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
17396        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep), "admission deferred");
17397        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim), "removal deferred");
17398
17399        // The daemon applies them at the drain (removals first, then admissions).
17400        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
17401        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
17402        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep));
17403        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
17404        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
17405        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17406    }

17408    /// A thread admitted and then killed before the drain must end up neither
17409    /// queued nor pending: removals drain first and the retired-thread skip in
17410    /// the admission drain drops the buffered admission for a thread with no
17411    /// next_turns entry.
17412    #[test]
17413    fn buffered_admission_cancelled_by_buffered_removal() {
17414        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17415        let tid = DetTid::from_raw(11);
17416        register_known_thread(&mut sched, tid);
17417
17418        sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
17419        sched.deschedule_or_defer(tid);
17420
17421        // The thread is retired before the drain: its next_turns entry is gone.
17422        sched.next_turns.remove(&tid);
17423        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
17424        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
17425
17426        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(tid));
17427        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
17428        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17429    }

17431    /// A successful nonleader exec retires the old process leader and reuses
17432    /// its raw TID for the caller's replacement image.  The old-leader removal
17433    /// and replacement-leader admission therefore share a `DetTid`, but they do
17434    /// not name the same thread incarnation: the drain must remove the former
17435    /// without cancelling the latter.
17436    #[test]
17437    fn nonleader_exec_removal_preserves_replacement_admission() {
17438        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
17439            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
17440            backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
17441        });
17442        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17443        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
17444        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
17445        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
17446        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
17447
17448        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
17449        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
17450        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
17451        register_known_thread(&mut sched, caller);
17452        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
17453        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
17454
17455        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
17456        let post_exec_mm = pre_exec_mm.for_exec(detpid);
17457        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
17458        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
17459        sched
17460            .register_physical_thread(leader, pre_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
17461            .expect("old leader PIDFD_THREAD registration must succeed");
17462        sched
17463            .register_physical_thread(leader, post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
17464            .expect("post-exec PIDFD_THREAD registration must replace the old address space");
17465        let retired = sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
17466            caller,
17467            new_leader: leader,
17468            detpid,
17469            pre_exec_mm,
17470            post_exec_mm,
17471            child_tid_addr: 0,
17472            reconnect_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
17473        });
17474
17475        assert_eq!(retired, vec![leader, caller]);
17476        assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
17477        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
17478        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&leader));
17479        assert_eq!(
17480            sched.physical_thread_identity(leader),
17481            Some((post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)),
17482            "old-leader cleanup must not remove the replacement leader's PIDFD_THREAD"
17483        );
17484
17485        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
17486        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
17487
17488        assert_eq!(
17489            sched
17490                .run_queue
17491                .tids()
17492                .filter(|dettid| **dettid == leader)
17493                .count(),
17494            1,
17495            "the first eligible drain must contain exactly one replacement leader"
17496        );
17497        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
17498        assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
17499        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
17500        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17501    }

17504    fn exec_replacement_killed_before_drain_is_not_resurrected() {

17535    #[test]
17536    fn exec_reconnect_only_buffers_while_tentative_selection_is_live() {
17537        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
17538            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;

17544        register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
17545        sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);

17548        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
17549        let queue_during_window = sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>();
17550
17551        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);

17558        );

17560            sched.pending_run_queue_removals.get(&leader),
17561            Some(&RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit)

17580    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
17581    enum ExecReconnectTiming {
17582        BeforeDaemon,
17583        AfterCallerWait { yields: usize },
17584        CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect,
17585    }
17586
17587    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
17588    struct ExecDrainObservation {
17589        queue: Vec<DetTid>,
17590        next_post_fork_draw: bool,
17591        turn: u64,
17592        old_leader_registration_survived: bool,
17593    }
17594
17595    async fn observe_exec_reconnect_drain(timing: ExecReconnectTiming) -> ExecDrainObservation {
17596        let config = Config {
17597            sched_seed: Some(0x5107),
17598            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
17599            ..Config::default()
17600        }
17601        .with_backend(|backend| {
17602            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
17603        });
17604        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
17605        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17606        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
17607        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
17608        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(31);
17609        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(37);
17610        let barrier_parent = DetTid::from_raw(99);
17611        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
17612        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
17613
17614        let (caller_request, old_leader_request) = {
17615            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17616            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
17617            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
17618            register_known_thread(&mut s, leader);
17619            register_known_thread(&mut s, caller);
17620            // Give the destroyed leader a visibly different queue band. The
17621            // replacement must use the caller's priority at the ordinary tail.
17622            s.priorities.insert(leader, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17623            s.runqueue_push_back(leader);
17624            s.runqueue_push_back(caller);
17625            s.next_turns
17626                .get(&leader)
17627                .unwrap()
17628                .req
17629                .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
17630
17631            register_known_thread(&mut s, lower);
17632            register_known_thread(&mut s, higher);
17633            s.admit_to_run_queue(lower, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
17634            s.admit_to_run_queue(higher, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
17635            // `step2` drains first, then this unresolved barrier returns
17636            // `SkipTurn`, exposing the exact first-drain queue before step3 can
17637            // tentatively select or rotate it.
17638            s.vfork_barriers.insert(barrier_parent, None);
17639            (
17640                s.next_turns.get(&caller).unwrap().req.clone(),
17641                s.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone(),
17642            )
17643        };
17644
17645        if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon) {
17646            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
17647                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
17648                leader,
17649                caller,
17650                detpid,
17651                pre_exec_mm,
17652            );
17653        } else if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
17654            caller_request.put(Ok(Resources::new(caller)));
17655        }
17656
17657        let turn_sched = sched.clone();
17658        let turn_time = global_time.clone();
17659        let turn = tokio::spawn(async move {
17660            let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
17661            do_a_turn_blocking(turn_sched, turn_time, &last).await
17662        });
17663
17664        if let ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields } = timing {
17665            let mut saw_waiter = false;
17666            for _ in 0..1_000 {
17667                if caller_request.to_string() == "<ivar HasWaiter>" {
17668                    saw_waiter = true;
17669                    break;
17670                }
17671                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
17672            }
17673            assert!(saw_waiter, "daemon never waited on the exec caller request");
17674            for _ in 0..yields {
17675                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
17676            }
17677            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
17678                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
17679                leader,
17680                caller,
17681                detpid,
17682                pre_exec_mm,
17683            );
17684        }
17685
17686        assert!(turn.await.expect("scheduler task panicked").is_err());
17687        let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17688        let observation = ExecDrainObservation {
17689            queue: s.run_queue.tids().copied().collect(),
17690            next_post_fork_draw: s.child_runs_first_post_fork(RunsPostFork::Random),
17691            turn: s.turn,
17692            old_leader_registration_survived: s
17693                .next_turns
17694                .get(&leader)
17695                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req == old_leader_request),
17696        };
17697        if !matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
17698            assert_eq!(
17699                observation
17700                    .queue
17701                    .iter()
17702                    .filter(|tid| **tid == leader)
17703                    .count(),
17704                1
17705            );
17706            assert!(!observation.queue.contains(&caller));
17707            assert!(!observation.old_leader_registration_survived);
17708            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
17709            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17710        }
17711        observation
17712    }
17713
17714    #[tokio::test]
17715    async fn exec_reconnect_caller_gate_fixes_first_drain_membership_and_prng() {
17716        let canonical = observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon).await;
17717        for yields in [0, 1, 64] {
17718            assert_eq!(
17719                canonical,
17720                observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields }).await,
17721                "host delay of {yields} yields changed the first eligible drain"
17722            );
17723        }
17724
17725        let broken =
17726            observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect).await;
17727        assert!(broken.old_leader_registration_survived);
17728        assert_ne!(
17729            canonical.queue, broken.queue,
17730            "the deliberate caller-gate violation was inert"
17731        );
17732    }
17733
17734    /// With `--scheduler-turn-cost`, a charge refused because it would pass the
17735    /// end of representable virtual time ends an ordinary turn at once: the
17736    /// runnable thread is not selected or granted, so the terminal report can
17737    /// exit without waiting on any guest
17738    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3885). Before the fix the turn
17739    /// went on to select and grant thread 100.
17740    #[tokio::test]
17741    async fn a_refused_turn_charge_returns_before_an_ordinary_grant() {
17742        let config = Config {
17743            sequentialize_threads: true,
17744            epoch: "2554-07-21T23:34:32.709051615Z".parse().unwrap(),
17745            scheduler_turn_cost: std::num::NonZeroU64::new(1_000_000_000),
17746            ..Config::default()
17747        };
17748        let mut s = Scheduler::new(&config);
17749        let ready = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17750        register_known_thread(&mut s, ready);
17751        s.next_turns[&ready].req.put(Ok(Resources::new(ready)));
17752        s.runqueue_push_back(ready);
17753        let mut time = GlobalTime::new(&config);
17754        // One accepted charge leaves 500,615 ns of representable time.
17755        let now = time.add_scheduler_time().unwrap();
17756        assert_eq!(now.as_nanos(), u64::MAX - 500_615);
17757        s.committed_time = now;
17758        let response = s.next_turns[&ready].resp.clone();
17759        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(s));
17760        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(time));
17761
17762        let outcome = do_a_turn_blocking(
17763            sched.clone(),
17764            global_time.clone(),
17765            &Ok(Resources::new(ready)),
17766        )
17767        .await;
17768        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17769        assert!(s.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some());
17770        assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(SkipTurn)), "{outcome:?}");
17771        assert_eq!(
17772            global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
17773            now,
17774            "a refused charge adds nothing"
17775        );
17776        assert!(
17777            response.try_read().is_none(),
17778            "the runnable thread was not granted"
17779        );
17780        assert!(!s.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17781        assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(ready));
17782    }
17783
17784    /// F6 (real-path regression): when the thread `step3_peek` tentatively
17785    /// selected dies while the daemon awaits its request, `do_a_turn_blocking`
17786    /// takes the `Err(ThreadExited)` fizzle arm. That arm MUST undo the tentative
17787    /// pop so the selection does not outlive the turn; otherwise the next pass's
17788    /// step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is
17789    /// still `Some`, tripping the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect
17790    /// panic moved one pass" defect (reachable in NORMAL async-DBT operation, not
17791    /// just the reviewed edge case: any thread that exits during the await window
17792    /// races here). This drives the ACTUAL async daemon function end to end
17793    /// rather than poking `RunQueue` directly, which is the coverage gap the
17794    /// pre-existing tests left. Positive control: after the fizzle the window is
17795    /// closed and the following real step2 removal drain does not panic.
17796    #[tokio::test]
17797    async fn reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_safe() {
17798        let config = Config::default();
17799        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
17800        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
17801        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
17802        {
17803            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17804            s.priorities.insert(dead, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17805            s.next_turns.insert(
17806                dead,
17807                ThreadNextTurn {
17808                    dettid: dead,
17809                    child_tid_addr: 0,
17810                    // Request already resolved to `ThreadExited`: the daemon will
17811                    // observe the thread died the moment it awaits `req.get()`.
17812                    req: Ivar::full(Err(ThreadExited)),
17813                    resp: Ivar::new(),
17814                    protocol: Default::default(),
17815                },
17816            );
17817            s.runqueue_push_back(dead);
17818        }
17819        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
17820
17821        // Pass 1: step1 sees a filled request (quiescent), step3 tentatively
17822        // pops `dead`, then `req.get().await` yields `Err(ThreadExited)`. The
17823        // fizzle arm returns `SkipTurn` and undoes the tentative pop.
17824        let first = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
17825        assert!(first.is_err(), "fizzled reconnect turn skips");
17826        assert!(
17827            !sched.lock().unwrap().run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
17828            "the ThreadExited arm must undo the tentative pop"
17829        );
17830
17831        // Pass 2: the dead thread's run-queue removal is now buffered, exactly
17832        // as a reconnect/kill handler would leave it. Because pass 1 closed the
17833        // window, the real step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` with
17834        // `tentative_selection == None` and does NOT trip the guard. Pre-fix
17835        // (window left open) this call panicked.
17836        {
17837            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
17838            s.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
17839            s.next_turns.remove(&dead);
17840            let _ = s.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
17841            assert!(!s.run_queue.contains_tid(dead), "dead thread drained out");
17842            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
17843        }
17844    }
17845
17846    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle), part 1: the branch itself, both ways.
17847    ///
17848    /// NEGATIVE -- the defect. A selected thread whose `next_turns` entry
17849    /// vanished during the daemon's post-await window must abandon the turn:
17850    /// report `SkipTurn` (it commits nothing -- steps 4-7 are bypassed) AND
17851    /// close the tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Before the fix this
17852    /// branch fell through to `Ok(rsrcs)`, which `bump_global_time` reads as a
17853    /// completed turn and answers with a virtual-time advance.
17854    /// POSITIVE -- not inert. A thread that is still registered proceeds: `Ok`,
17855    /// with its tentative selection left open for step4 to commit. Without this
17856    /// side an `abort_turn_if_thread_vanished` that simply always skipped would
17857    /// pass the negative and silently stall the scheduler.
17858    #[test]
17859    fn a_vanished_thread_aborts_its_turn_and_a_live_one_does_not() {
17860        let config = Config::default();
17861        let vanishing = DetTid::from_raw(11);
17862        let live = DetTid::from_raw(13);
17863
17864        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17865        register_known_thread(&mut sched, vanishing);
17866        register_known_thread(&mut sched, live);
17867        sched.runqueue_push_back(vanishing);
17868        sched.runqueue_push_back(live);
17869
17870        // NEGATIVE: retire `vanishing` after its selection was tentatively
17871        // popped, exactly as teardown does inside the post-await window.
17872        assert_eq!(
17873            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(vanishing),
17874            Some(vanishing)
17875        );
17876        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17877        sched.next_turns.remove(&vanishing);
17878        assert!(
17879            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(vanishing).is_err(),
17880            "a turn that bypasses steps 4-7 must report SkipTurn, never success: \
17881             reporting Ok lets bump_global_time advance virtual time for a turn \
17882             that committed nothing"
17883        );
17884        assert!(
17885            !sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
17886            "the abandoned turn must also close its tentative window"
17887        );
17888
17889        // POSITIVE: a still-registered thread is untouched and proceeds to
17890        // step4 with its selection still open to commit.
17891        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(live), Some(live));
17892        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
17893        assert!(
17894            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(live).is_ok(),
17895            "a live thread's turn must proceed"
17896        );
17897        assert!(
17898            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
17899            "a proceeding turn must keep its tentative selection open for step4"
17900        );
17901    }
17902
17903    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle must not advance virtual time): both sides of
17904    /// the consequence, stated directly against `bump_global_time` -- the code
17905    /// that turns a turn's returned `Result` into a virtual-time decision.
17906    ///
17907    /// The defect: the fizzle arm where `req.get()` resolved `Ok` but the
17908    /// thread's `next_turns` entry vanished before the daemon re-acquired the
17909    /// lock skips steps 4-7, commits nothing, and used to fall through to
17910    /// `Ok(rsrcs)` -- landing in the advancing branch below and adding a
17911    /// DETLOG-visible tick for work that never happened. It now reports
17912    /// `Err(SkipTurn)` like its `ThreadExited` sibling, so this pair of
17913    /// assertions is what that fix buys.
17914    ///
17915    /// Deliberately NOT an end-to-end test of that arm. Reaching it requires
17916    /// teardown to clear `next_turns` inside the host-scheduling gap between the
17917    /// await resolving and the re-lock, and that gap is not constructible from a
17918    /// test: the daemon quiescence check only proceeds once every thread's request
17919    /// is already filled, so `req.get()` never suspends and there is no window a
17920    /// test can hold open. An attempt to win the lock in that gap is a genuine
17921    /// race that would usually lose (and deadlocks outright on a current-thread
17922    /// runtime, where the daemon's blocking `sched.lock()` stalls the whole
17923    /// executor). F6's `reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_
17924    /// safe` does drive the real `do_a_turn_blocking` for the sibling arm.
17925    ///
17926    /// NEGATIVE: a skipped turn leaves virtual time exactly where it was. That is
17927    /// what the F8 fix buys; before it, the non-committing arm reported `Ok` and
17928    /// landed in the advancing branch.
17929    /// POSITIVE: a committed, non-internal turn *does* advance it. Without this
17930    /// side the negative would pass vacuously for a `bump_global_time` that had
17931    /// simply stopped advancing time at all.
17932    #[test]
17933    fn virtual_time_advances_for_a_committed_turn_and_not_for_a_skipped_one() {
17934        let config = Config::default();
17935        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
17936
17937        // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external events"
17938        // guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
17939        let mut advancing = Scheduler::new(&config);
17940        advancing.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17941        advancing.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
17942        let advancing_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
17943        let before_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
17944        advancing.bump_global_time(&advancing_time, &Ok(Resources::new(runnable)));
17945        let after_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
17946        assert!(
17947            after_commit > before_commit,
17948            "a committed turn must advance virtual time ({before_commit:?} -> {after_commit:?})"
17949        );
17950
17951        let mut skipping = Scheduler::new(&config);
17952        skipping.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17953        skipping.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
17954        let skipping_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
17955        let before_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
17956        skipping.bump_global_time(&skipping_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
17957        let after_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
17958        assert_eq!(
17959            after_skip, before_skip,
17960            "a skipped turn must not advance virtual time"
17961        );
17962    }

17964    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139: a turn that delivers a
17965    /// signal to the thread whose turn came last is not charged a scheduler
17966    /// turn. The same delivery to another thread is, an ordinary turn of the
17967    /// same thread is, a waitid turn is, and under record/replay the delivery
17968    /// is too. A host-timed polling retry in between does not count as the
17969    /// previous turn.
17970    #[test]
17971    fn a_signal_delivered_to_the_running_thread_is_not_charged_a_turn() {
17972        let config = Config::default();
17973        let running = DetTid::from_raw(13);
17974        let other = DetTid::from_raw(14);
17975        let delivery = |tid: DetTid| {
17976            let mut request = Resources::new(tid);
17977            request.insert(
17978                ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGALRM)),
17979                Permission::W,
17980            );
17981            request
17982        };
17983        let retry = |tid: DetTid| {
17984            let mut request = Resources::new(tid);
17985            request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
17986            request
17987        };
17988        // The advance of the last of `turns`, committed in order.
17989        let advance = |record_replay: bool, turns: &[Resources]| {
17990            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
17991            sched.recordreplay_modes = record_replay;
17992            for tid in [running, other] {
17993                sched.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
17994                sched.runqueue_push_back(tid);
17995            }
17996            let time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
17997            let (last, earlier) = turns.split_last().unwrap();
17998            for turn in earlier {
17999                sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(turn.clone()));
18000            }
18001            let before = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
18002            sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(last.clone()));
18003            let after = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
18004            after.duration_since(before)
18005        };
18006        let charge = advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), Resources::new(running)]);
18007        assert!(charge > Duration::ZERO, "an ordinary turn is charged");
18008        assert_eq!(
18009            advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), delivery(running)]),
18010            Duration::ZERO,
18011            "a delivery to the thread whose turn came last"
18012        );
18013        assert_eq!(
18014            advance(false, &[delivery(running), delivery(running)]),
18015            Duration::ZERO,
18016            "a second delivery in a row to the same thread"
18017        );
18018        assert_eq!(
18019            advance(false, &[Resources::new(other), delivery(running)]),
18020            charge,
18021            "a delivery that switches threads"
18022        );
18023        assert_eq!(
18024            advance(true, &[Resources::new(running), delivery(running)]),
18025            charge,
18026            "a delivery under record/replay"
18027        );
18028        let mut waitid = Resources::new(running);
18029        waitid.insert(
18030            ResourceID::WaitidSignals(vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)]),
18031            Permission::W,
18032        );
18033        assert_eq!(
18034            advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), waitid]),
18035            charge,
18036            "a waitid turn is not a signal delivery"
18037        );
18038        // A host-timed polling retry does not count as the previous turn, so
18039        // the charge cannot depend on how many retries ran.
18040        assert_eq!(
18041            advance(
18042                false,
18043                &[Resources::new(other), retry(running), delivery(running)]
18044            ),
18045            charge,
18046            "a retry between another thread's turn and the delivery"
18047        );
18048        assert_eq!(
18049            advance(
18050                false,
18051                &[Resources::new(running), retry(running), delivery(running)]
18052            ),
18053            Duration::ZERO,
18054            "a retry between the same thread's turn and the delivery"
18055        );
18056    }

18058    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3517: a committed turn that
18059    /// served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld does not
18060    /// advance virtual time. The identical request without the mark does, so the
18061    /// negative is not vacuous, and a marked IO-polling retry still does, because
18062    /// finite poll and futex timeouts are enforced against this clock.
18063    #[test]
18064    fn bootstrap_syscall_turn_withholds_scheduler_time_except_for_polling_retries() {
18065        let config = Config::default();
18066        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
18067        let advance = |request: Resources| {
18068            // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external
18069            // events" guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
18070            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
18071            sched.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
18072            sched.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
18073            let time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
18074            let before = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
18075            sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(request));
18076            let after = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
18077            assert_eq!(sched.committed_time, after);
18078            (before, after)
18079        };
18080        let file = ResourceID::Path("/proc/self/maps".into());
18081
18082        let mut guest_turn = Resources::new(runnable);
18083        guest_turn.resources.insert(file.clone(), Permission::R);
18084        let (before, after) = advance(guest_turn.clone());
18085        assert!(
18086            after > before,
18087            "an unmarked committed turn must advance virtual time ({before:?} -> {after:?})"
18088        );
18089        let per_turn = after - before;
18090
18091        let mut bootstrap_turn = guest_turn;
18092        bootstrap_turn.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
18093        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_turn);
18094        assert_eq!(
18095            after, before,
18096            "a turn serving an uncharged bootstrap syscall must not advance virtual time"
18097        );
18098
18099        let mut bootstrap_poll = Resources::new(runnable);
18100        bootstrap_poll
18101            .resources
18102            .insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
18103        bootstrap_poll.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
18104        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_poll);
18105        assert_eq!(
18106            after - before,
18107            per_turn,
18108            "a marked IO-polling retry must still advance virtual time by one turn"
18109        );
18110    }

18112    /// Liveness (negative control) for the F6 fix above: proves the guard the
18113    /// fizzle arm protects is real, so the positive test is not vacuous. If a
18114    /// fizzled turn does NOT undo its tentative pop (the pre-fix behavior), the
18115    /// next pass's step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while
18116    /// `tentative_selection` is `Some`, and the run queue's transaction guard
18117    /// panics. This is precisely the panic `undo_tentative_pop` prevents.
18118    #[test]
18119    #[should_panic(expected = "tentative_selection.is_none()")]
18120    fn removal_drain_panics_if_tentative_window_left_open() {
18121        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
18122        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
18123        register_known_thread(&mut sched, dead);
18124        sched.runqueue_push_back(dead);
18125
18126        // Simulate step3_peek selecting `dead` with the turn neither committing
18127        // nor undoing -- i.e., the fizzle arm WITHOUT its undo.
18128        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(dead));
18129        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
18130
18131        // Next pass buffers the removal and drains: remove_tid trips the guard.
18132        sched.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
18133        sched.next_turns.remove(&dead);
18134        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
18135    }
