20625    /// A handler a sibling installs over `SIG_IGN` after the wait began ends the
20626    /// wait when the signal arrives, as on Linux. The earlier design read the
20627    /// dispositions when the wait began and left this waiter parked; an untimed
20628    /// wait then never ended (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
20629    #[test]
20630    fn a_signal_caught_after_a_futex_wait_began_ends_it() {
20631        // Through the step2 drain of a cross-task signal.
20632        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20633        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
20634        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20635        scheduler
20636            .test_kernel_signal_states
20637            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
20638        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
20639        // The sibling's `rt_sigaction` runs in its turn, before it signals.
20640        scheduler
20641            .test_kernel_signal_states
20642            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
20643        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
20644        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
20645
20646        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
20647        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
20648        assert_eq!(
20649            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
20650            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
20651        );
20652
20653        // Through a scheduler send (a timer), for SIGWINCH, which is ignored by
20654        // default until a handler is installed. A SIGCHLD ends the wait only
20655        // when the scheduler sends it
20656        // (`a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it`).
20657        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20658        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
20659        let winch = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH);
20660        scheduler
20661            .test_kernel_signal_states
20662            .insert(target, signal_state(0, 0));
20663        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(winch)));
20664        scheduler
20665            .test_kernel_signal_states
20666            .insert(target, signal_state(winch, 0));
20667        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGWINCH);
20668
20669        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
20670        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
20671        assert_eq!(
20672            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
20673            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
20674        );
20675    }
20676
20677    /// A signal a sibling sets to `SIG_IGN` after the wait began leaves the waiter
20678    /// parked, registered with its original absolute deadline, because Linux
20679    /// discards an ignored signal without ending the wait. The earlier design woke
20680    /// the waiter, and the restarted `FUTEX_WAIT` began a fresh relative timeout
20681    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
20682    #[test]
20683    fn a_signal_ignored_after_a_futex_wait_began_keeps_its_deadline() {
20684        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20685        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
20686        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20687        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
20688        scheduler
20689            .test_kernel_signal_states
20690            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
20691        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
20692            &target,
20693            futex,
20694            Some(deadline),
20695            u32::MAX,
20696            Some(signal_watch(usr1)),
20697        );
20698        scheduler
20699            .test_kernel_signal_states
20700            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
20701
20702        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
20703        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
20704        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
20705
20706        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
20707        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
20708        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
20709        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
20710        assert_eq!(
20711            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
20712            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
20713        );
20714        // A FUTEX_WAKE still finds the waiter.
20715        assert_eq!(
20716            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(101), futex, 1, u32::MAX),
20717            1
20718        );
20719    }

20721    /// When the waiter's signal state cannot be read at the commit point, every
20722    /// signal its mask leaves unblocked ends the wait. A needless wake costs one
20723    /// turn: the waiter re-checks its signals in its own turn and parks again
20724    /// with its original absolute deadline. A missed wake can leave the waiter
20725    /// parked forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
20726    #[test]
20727    fn an_unreadable_signal_state_ends_a_parked_futex_wait() {
20728        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20729        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
20730        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
20731            &target,
20732            futex,
20733            None,
20734            u32::MAX,
20735            Some(signal_watch(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH))),
20736        );
20737        assert!(!scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.contains_key(&target));
20738
20739        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH));
20740        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
20741
20742        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
20743        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
20744        assert_eq!(
20745            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
20746            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
20747        );
20748    }

20750    /// A backend that does not report the guest's signal state keeps the base
20751    /// behavior: no cross-task wakeup for a parked futex waiter.

20768    /// A futex waiter that a wake already requeued completes as woken; the signal
20769    /// does not rewrite its request.

20771    fn pending_signal_does_not_rewrite_a_woken_futex_waiter() {

20799    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of one waiter wakes the longest waiter, as Linux does for
20800    /// waiters of equal priority. Waking the newest one let a thread that re-waits
20801    /// after every wake take every wake, and an older waiter never ran
20802    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3917).
20803    #[test]
20804    fn a_futex_wake_takes_the_longest_waiter_first() {
20805        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20806        let waiters = [100, 101, 102].map(DetTid::from_raw);
20807        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
20808        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
20809        for waiter in waiters {
20810            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
20811            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
20812        }
20813        for (woken, waiter) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
20814            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
20815            for (index, other) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
20816                assert_eq!(
20817                    scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(other),
20818                    index > woken,
20819                    "after wake {woken}, waiter {other:?}"
20820                );
20821            }
20822            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
20823        }
20824    }
20825
20826    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` count of 0, or a count that is negative as the kernel's
20827    /// `int nr_wake` (-1, which is `u32::MAX` as the guest passes it), wakes one
20828    /// waiter, the longest one, as Linux's `futex_wake` does: it counts a waiter
20829    /// before comparing, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`
20830    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3957). A count of 0 used to wake
20831    /// nobody, and a negative count panicked the scheduler.
20832    #[test]
20833    fn a_futex_wake_count_of_zero_or_below_wakes_one_waiter() {
20834        for count in [0, -1, u32::MAX as i32, i32::MIN] {
20835            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20836            let waiters = [100, 101].map(DetTid::from_raw);
20837            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
20838            for waiter in waiters {
20839                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
20840                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
20841            }
20842            assert_eq!(
20843                scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, count, u32::MAX),
20844                1,
20845                "count {count}"
20846            );
20847            assert!(
20848                !scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[0]),
20849                "count {count}"
20850            );
20851            assert!(
20852                scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[1]),
20853                "count {count}"
20854            );
20855        }
20856        // With no waiter, such a wake still wakes nobody.
20857        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20858        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
20859        assert_eq!(
20860            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, 0, u32::MAX),
20861            0
20862        );
20863    }
20864
20865    /// A count of 0 still skips waiters whose bitset does not match, and wakes
20866    /// the first one that does, as `futex_wake`'s `continue` before `++ret`.
20867    #[test]
20868    fn a_futex_wake_bitset_count_of_zero_wakes_the_first_matching_waiter() {
20869        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20870        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
20871        let waiters = [(100, 0b10), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b01)]
20872            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
20873        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
20874            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
20875            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
20876        }
20877        assert_eq!(
20878            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(103), futex, 0, 0b01),
20879            1
20880        );
20881        let parked = waiters.map(|(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
20882        assert_eq!(parked, [true, false, true]);
20883    }
20884
20885    /// Helper: `n` waiters (raw tids from `first`) parked on `futex` with `bitset`.
20886    fn park_futex_waiters(
20887        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
20888        futex: FutexID,
20889        first: i32,
20890        n: i32,
20891        bitset: u32,
20892    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
20893        (first..first + n)
20894            .map(|raw| {
20895                let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(raw);
20896                register_known_thread(scheduler, waiter);
20897                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
20898                waiter
20899            })
20900            .collect()
20901    }
20902
20903    fn futex_waiter_order(scheduler: &Scheduler, futex: FutexID) -> Vec<DetTid> {
20904        scheduler
20905            .blocked
20906            .futex_waiters
20907            .get(&futex)
20908            .map(|waiters| waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid).collect())
20909            .unwrap_or_default()
20910    }
20911
20912    /// FUTEX_REQUEUE wakes the first `nr_wake` waiters in arrival order and moves
20913    /// the next `nr_requeue`, which join the end of the target's waiters in their
20914    /// arrival order, as Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) with
20915    /// `requeue_futex` appending to the target chain
20916    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3958).
20917    #[test]
20918    fn a_futex_requeue_wakes_the_oldest_and_moves_the_next_in_order() {
20919        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20920        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
20921        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
20922        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
20923        let on_to = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, to, 100, 1, u32::MAX);
20924        let on_from = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 101, 4, u32::MAX);
20925        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, 1, 2), (1, 2));
20926        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_from[0]));
20927        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, from), vec![on_from[3]]);
20928        assert_eq!(
20929            futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
20930            vec![on_to[0], on_from[1], on_from[2]]
20931        );
20932        // A later wake of the target takes its own earlier waiter first.
20933        assert_eq!(
20934            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(99), to, 1, u32::MAX),
20935            1
20936        );
20937        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_to[0]));
20938    }
20939
20940    /// `futex_requeue`'s loop: `if (task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue) break;`
20941    /// before counting, and `if (++task_count <= nr_wake)` to wake. So nothing is
20942    /// done for 0 and 0, a `nr_wake` of 0 wakes nobody (unlike `futex_wake`), and
20943    /// bitsets do not matter.
20944    #[test]
20945    fn futex_requeue_counts_follow_linux() {
20946        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
20947        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
20948        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
20949        for (nr_wake, nr_requeue, expected) in [
20950            (0, 0, (0, 0)),
20951            (0, 1, (0, 1)),
20952            (2, 0, (2, 0)),
20953            (5, 5, (3, 0)),
20954        ] {
20955            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20956            let waiters = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 100, 3, 0b01);
20957            assert_eq!(
20958                scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, nr_wake, nr_requeue),
20959                expected,
20960                "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue}"
20961            );
20962            let (woken, moved) = expected;
20963            let (woken, moved) = (woken as usize, moved as usize);
20964            for (index, &waiter) in waiters.iter().enumerate() {
20965                assert_eq!(
20966                    scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter),
20967                    index < woken,
20968                    "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue} waiter {index}"
20969                );
20970            }
20971            assert_eq!(
20972                futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
20973                waiters[woken..woken + moved].to_vec()
20974            );
20975        }
20976    }

20978    /// Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody (`requeue_futex` only rewrites
20979    /// the key): the counted waiters keep their places, and only the woken leave.

20986            scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 0, i32::MAX as usize),

20988        );
20989        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters);
20990        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 1, 1), (1, 1));
20991        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters[1..].to_vec());

20994    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of several wakes the longest waiters, and they join the
20995    /// run queue in the order they started waiting.
20996    #[test]
20997    fn a_futex_wake_of_several_takes_the_longest_waiters_in_order() {
20998        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
20999        let waiters = [100, 101, 102, 103].map(DetTid::from_raw);
21000        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
21001        for waiter in waiters {
21002            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
21003            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
21004        }
21005        assert_eq!(
21006            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(104), futex, 2, u32::MAX),
21007            2
21008        );

21010            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21011            waiters[..2]
21012        );

21014            waiters[2..]
21015                .iter()
21016                .all(|&waiter| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter))
21017        );

21020    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE_BITSET` that matches only some waiters leaves the others
21021    /// in the order they arrived, so a later wake still takes the longest
21022    /// waiter (Linux `futex_wake` walks one list in arrival order and skips
21023    /// the waiters whose bitset does not match).
21024    #[test]
21025    fn a_partial_bitset_wake_keeps_the_other_waiters_in_arrival_order() {
21026        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21027        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
21028        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
21029        let waiters = [(100, 0b01), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b10)]
21030            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
21031        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
21032            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
21033            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
21034        }
21035        let parked = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
21036            waiters
21037                .iter()
21038                .map(|&(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter))
21039                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
21040        };
21041        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, 0b01), 1);
21042        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, true, true]);
21043        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
21044        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, true]);
21045        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
21046        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, false]);
21047    }

21049    /// The wakes Detcore issues for an exiting thread also take the longest
21050    /// waiter: the one-waiter wake of `CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID` (several threads
21051    /// joining one) and the one-waiter wake of a robust-list futex.
21052    #[test]
21053    fn exit_wakes_take_the_longest_waiter_first() {
21054        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21055        let exiting = DetTid::from_raw(99);
21056        let waiters = [100, 101, 102].map(DetTid::from_raw);
21057        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(99)), 0x404110);
21058        for waiter in waiters {
21059            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
21060            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
21061        }
21062        scheduler.wake_futex_child_cleartid(futex, exiting);
21063        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[0]));

21067            vec![1]

21070        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[2]));

21073    /// Under `--futex-wake-yields` a waker that woke a waiter goes
21074    /// behind it, and behind every thread already queued, so its yield at the
21075    /// syscall's post-hook is granted only after their turns
21076    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3874). By default the waker
21077    /// keeps its place ahead of the waiter it woke.
21078    #[test]
21079    fn a_futex_waker_is_requeued_behind_the_waiters_it_woke() {
21080        for requeue in [false, true] {
21081            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21082            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21083            let waker = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21084            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21085            for tid in [waiter, waker, runnable] {
21086                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21087            }
21088            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waker);
21089            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
21090            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
21091            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
21092
21093            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
21094            if requeue {
21095                scheduler.requeue_futex_waker(waker);
21096            }
21097            let expected = if requeue {
21098                vec![runnable, waiter, waker]
21099            } else {
21100                vec![waker, runnable, waiter]
21101            };
21102            assert_eq!(
21103                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21104                expected
21105            );
21106        }
21107    }

21109    /// A chaos scheduler with three threads in consecutive bands, the first
21110    /// two put into the yield epoch through real `SchedYield` turns.
21111    fn scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch() -> (Scheduler, [DetTid; 3]) {
21112        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21113            chaos: true,
21114            ..Config::default()
21115        });
21116        let tids = [
21117            DetTid::from_raw(100),
21118            DetTid::from_raw(101),
21119            DetTid::from_raw(102),
21120        ];
21121        for (index, tid) in tids.into_iter().enumerate() {
21122            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21123            scheduler
21124                .priorities
21125                .insert(tid, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + index as u64);
21126            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
21127        }
21128        for yielder in [tids[0], tids[1]] {
21129            for _ in 0..=runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH {
21130                let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
21131                request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
21132                let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&yielder).unwrap();
21133                next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
21134                let response = next.resp.clone();
21135                assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21136                assert!(
21137                    scheduler
21138                        .step4_resource_block(yielder, &request, &response)
21139                        .is_ok()
21140                );
21141                assert!(
21142                    scheduler
21143                        .step5_guest_unblock(yielder, &request, &response)
21144                        .is_ok()
21145                );
21146                assert!(matches!(response.try_read(), Some(SchedResponse::Go(_))));
21147                let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
21148                assert_eq!(requeue, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
21149                scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
21150            }
21151        }
21152        (scheduler, tids)
21153    }
21154
21155    /// A poller's non-committing backoff grants no turn, so the yielders stay
21156    /// excluded and the poller, in a later band, is selected again. Written by
21157    /// the Codex reviewer of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4080
21158    /// (round 2), as are the next two tests.
21159    #[test]
21160    fn a_noncommitting_poll_backoff_keeps_the_yield_epoch() {
21161        let (mut scheduler, tids) = scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch();
21162        let poller = tids[2];
21163        let mut request = Resources::new(poller);
21164        request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
21165        request.poll_attempt = 1;
21166        let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&poller).unwrap();
21167        next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
21168        let response = next.resp.clone();
21169        let committed_time = scheduler.committed_time;
21170        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(poller));
21171        assert!(
21172            scheduler
21173                .step4_resource_block(poller, &request, &response)
21174                .is_err()
21175        );
21176        assert!(
21177            response.try_read().is_none(),
21178            "NONCOMMIT cannot grant this retry"
21179        );
21180        assert_eq!(scheduler.committed_time, committed_time);
21181        assert_eq!(
21182            scheduler
21183                .next_turns
21184                .get(&poller)
21185                .unwrap()
21186                .req
21187                .try_read()
21188                .unwrap()
21189                .unwrap()
21190                .poll_attempt,
21191            0,
21192            "the real backoff path must remake its pending request as runnable"
21193        );
21194        assert_eq!(
21195            scheduler.run_queue.queued_priority(poller),
21196            Some(2 * (runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 2))
21197        );
21198        assert_eq!(
21199            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(),
21200            Some(poller),
21201            "poll bookkeeping grants no non-yield turn, so the earlier yielders must remain excluded"
21202        );
21203    }

21205    /// A completed guest turn of a thread that did not yield ends the epoch.
21206    #[test]
21207    fn a_completed_non_yield_turn_ends_the_yield_epoch() {
21208        let (mut scheduler, tids) = scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch();
21209        let worker = tids[2];
21210        let request = Resources::new(worker);

21212        next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));

21214        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(worker));
21215        assert!(
21216            scheduler
21217                .step4_resource_block(worker, &request, &response)
21218                .is_ok()
21219        );
21220        assert!(
21221            scheduler
21222                .step5_guest_unblock(worker, &request, &response)
21223                .is_ok()

21232    /// When the last thread outside the epoch yields too, the epoch covers the
21233    /// queue and ends, and the bands decide again.
21234    #[test]
21235    fn the_last_thread_outside_yielding_ends_the_yield_epoch() {
21236        let (mut scheduler, tids) = scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch();
21237        let last = tids[2];
21238        // Its plain yield, then the one that joins the epoch and covers it.
21239        for _ in 0..=runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH {
21240            let mut request = Resources::new(last);
21241            request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
21242            let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&last).unwrap();
21243            next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
21244            let response = next.resp.clone();
21245            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(last));
21246            assert!(
21247                scheduler
21248                    .step4_resource_block(last, &request, &response)
21249                    .is_ok()
21250            );
21251            assert!(
21252                scheduler
21253                    .step5_guest_unblock(last, &request, &response)
21254                    .is_ok()
21255            );
21256            assert!(matches!(response.try_read(), Some(SchedResponse::Go(_))));
21257            let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
21258            assert_eq!(requeue, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
21259            scheduler.step6_reenquue(last, requeue);
21260        }
21261        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(tids[0]));
21262    }

21264    /// A `SchedYield` turn opens or joins a yield epoch only under `--chaos`,
21265    /// and only when it is a `sched_yield`: the zero-timeout loopback poll's
21266    /// yield, whose count is host-timed, keeps the one-turn exclusion
21267    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4068).
21268    #[test]
21269    fn only_a_chaos_sched_yield_opens_a_yield_epoch() {
21270        let tid = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21271        let mut sched_yield = Resources::new(tid);
21272        sched_yield.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
21273        let mut loopback = sched_yield.clone();
21274        loopback.fyi(LOOPBACK_POLL_YIELD_FYI);
21275        let other = Resources::new(tid);
21276        for chaos in [false, true] {
21277            let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21278                chaos,
21279                ..Config::default()
21280            });
21281            let expected = if chaos {
21282                Requeue::YieldEpoch
21283            } else {
21284                Requeue::OneTurnYield
21285            };
21286            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&sched_yield), expected);
21287            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&loopback), Requeue::OneTurnYield);
21288            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&other), Requeue::Back);
21289        }
21290    }

21292    /// Through `step6_reenquue`, two chaos `sched_yield` callers cannot take
21293    /// turns ahead of a thread in a later band, and both keep their persistent
21294    /// priorities. Without chaos the one-turn exclusion lets the first yielder
21295    /// run again after the second.
21296    #[test]
21297    fn two_chaos_yielders_cannot_shut_out_a_thread_in_a_later_band() {
21298        for chaos in [false, true] {
21299            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21300                chaos,
21301                ..Config::default()
21302            });
21303            let first = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21304            let second = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21305            let awaited = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21306            for tid in [first, second, awaited] {
21307                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21308            }
21309            scheduler.priorities.insert(first, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21310            scheduler
21311                .priorities
21312                .insert(second, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 1);
21313            scheduler
21314                .priorities
21315                .insert(awaited, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
21316            for tid in [first, second, awaited] {
21317                scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
21318            }
21319            // Under chaos each yielder's first yield is a plain one; its second
21320            // joins the epoch.
21321            let yields_each = if chaos {
21322                runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH + 1
21323            } else {
21324                1
21325            };
21326            for yielder in [first, second] {
21327                let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
21328                request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
21329                let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
21330                for _ in 0..yields_each {
21331                    assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21332                    scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
21333                }
21334            }
21335            let expected = if chaos { awaited } else { first };
21336            assert_eq!(
21337                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(),
21338                Some(expected),
21339                "chaos={chaos}"
21340            );
21341            assert_eq!(scheduler.get_priority(first), runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21342            assert_eq!(scheduler.get_priority(second), runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 1);
21343        }
21344    }

21346    /// Put `yielder` into a yield epoch through `step6_reenquue`, with the
21347    /// chaos `sched_yield` turns that take it there: its plain yields, then
21348    /// the one that joins.
21349    fn chaos_yield_turn(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, yielder: DetTid) {
21350        let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
21351        request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
21352        let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
21353        assert_eq!(requeue, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
21354        for _ in 0..=runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH {
21355            assert_eq!(
21356                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(yielder),
21357                Some(yielder)
21358            );
21359            scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
21360        }
21361    }

21363    /// A priority change point is a turn of a thread that did not yield, so,
21364    /// through the scheduler's own change-point path, it ends the yield epoch:
21365    /// the yielder in the first band runs next, not the third thread.
21366    #[test]
21367    fn a_priority_change_point_ends_the_yield_epoch() {
21368        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21369            chaos: true,
21370            ..Config::default()
21371        });
21372        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21373        let preempted = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21374        let third = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21375        for tid in [yielder, preempted, third] {
21376            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21377        }
21378        scheduler
21379            .priorities
21380            .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21381        scheduler.priorities.insert(third, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
21382        for tid in [yielder, preempted, third] {
21383            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
21384        }
21385        chaos_yield_turn(&mut scheduler, yielder);
21386
21387        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(preempted));
21388        // A change point never commits the turn: it always reports a skip.
21389        assert!(
21390            scheduler
21391                .perform_priority_changepoint(
21392                    preempted,
21393                    DEFAULT_PRIORITY,
21394                    LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
21395                    1,
21396                    &[]
21397                )
21398                .is_err()
21399        );
21400        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21401    }

21403    /// Two threads, spinner and waiter, at the given priorities, both queued,
21404    /// on a chaos scheduler.
21405    fn chaos_spinner_and_waiter(
21406        cfg: Config,
21407        spinner_priority: Priority,
21408        waiter_priority: Priority,
21409    ) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid) {
21410        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&cfg);
21411        let spinner = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21412        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21413        for tid in [spinner, waiter] {
21414            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21415        }
21416        scheduler.priorities.insert(spinner, spinner_priority);
21417        scheduler.priorities.insert(waiter, waiter_priority);
21418        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(spinner);
21419        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waiter);
21420        (scheduler, spinner, waiter)
21421    }
21422
21423    /// The spinner's change point, through the scheduler's own path, with
21424    /// `drawn` as its new random priority.
21425    fn spinner_changepoint(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, spinner: DetTid, drawn: Priority, at: u64) {
21426        assert_eq!(
21427            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(spinner),
21428            Some(spinner)
21429        );
21430        assert!(
21431            scheduler
21432                .perform_priority_changepoint(spinner, drawn, LogicalTime::from_nanos(at), at, &[])
21433                .is_err()
21434        );
21435    }
21436
21437    /// One committed turn of `tid`, through steps 4 to 6: it must be the next
21438    /// thread, and it is requeued at the back of its band.
21439    fn commit_a_turn(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
21440        let request = Resources::new(tid);
21441        let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&tid).unwrap();
21442        next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
21443        let response = next.resp.clone();
21444        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(tid));
21445        assert!(
21446            scheduler
21447                .step4_resource_block(tid, &request, &response)
21448                .is_ok()
21449        );
21450        assert!(
21451            scheduler
21452                .step5_guest_unblock(tid, &request, &response)
21453                .is_ok()
21454        );
21455        let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
21456        scheduler.step6_reenquue(tid, requeue);
21457    }
21458
21459    /// Under chaos, a thread that never blocks redraws its priority at each
21460    /// slice end, but a thread that never runs never redraws. A new thread
21461    /// with a poor draw (9820 here) waited behind a busy-wait until the spinner
21462    /// drew worse still (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4374). Now a
21463    /// thread passed over at `CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND` slice ends moves ahead:
21464    /// the spinner takes the priority one below it, so it keeps the lead for
21465    /// every turn it takes, not only the first.
21466    #[test]
21467    fn a_chaos_change_point_yields_to_a_thread_it_keeps_passing_over() {
21468        let (mut scheduler, spinner, waiter) = chaos_spinner_and_waiter(
21469            Config {
21470                chaos: true,
21471                ..Config::default()
21472            },
21473            500,
21474            9820,
21475        );
21476        assert_eq!(CHAOS_PASSOVER_BOUND, 2);
21477        let next = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
21478            let next = scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next();
21479            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
21480            next
21481        };
21482        assert_eq!(next(&mut scheduler), Some(spinner));
21483        // The first pass: the spinner keeps its draw and runs again.
21484        spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, 136, 1);
21485        assert_eq!(scheduler.priorities[&spinner], 136);
21486        assert_eq!(scheduler.chaos_passed_over.get(&waiter), Some(&1));
21487        assert_eq!(next(&mut scheduler), Some(spinner));
21488        // The second: it takes the priority one below the waiter's, not 7043.
21489        spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, 7043, 2);
21490        assert_eq!(scheduler.priorities[&spinner], 9821);
21491        // The waiter runs, and keeps running ahead of the spinner turn after
21492        // turn; its count restarted at its first committed turn.
21493        for _ in 0..3 {
21494            commit_a_turn(&mut scheduler, waiter);
21495            assert!(!scheduler.chaos_passed_over.contains_key(&waiter));
21496        }
21497        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(waiter));
21498        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
21499        // A thread whose blocking entries are removed leaves no count behind.
21500        scheduler.chaos_passed_over.insert(waiter, 1);
21501        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&waiter);
21502        assert!(!scheduler.chaos_passed_over.contains_key(&waiter));
21503    }
21504
21505    /// A waiter at the last priority has no band below it: the spinner shares
21506    /// it and is requeued behind it.
21507    #[test]
21508    fn a_chaos_change_point_behind_a_last_priority_thread_shares_its_band() {
21509        let (mut scheduler, spinner, waiter) = chaos_spinner_and_waiter(
21510            Config {
21511                chaos: true,
21512                ..Config::default()
21513            },
21514            500,
21515            runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY,
21516        );
21517        spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, 136, 1);
21518        spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, 7043, 2);
21519        assert_eq!(scheduler.priorities[&spinner], runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
21520        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(waiter));
21521    }

21523    /// The bound counts only a thread the new priority still beats, and only
21524    /// where every change point is a random draw at a timer slice end: under
21525    /// chaos with timer preemption and the default heuristic. Without timer
21526    /// preemption (a chaos `sched_yield` is then a change point), under
21527    /// `connectbind` (which sets chosen priorities), a preemption replay, a raw
21528    /// schedule replay or a random heuristic, and for a polling waiter, every
21529    /// change point keeps its draw.
21530    #[test]
21531    fn a_chaos_change_point_bounds_only_timer_slices_on_the_default_queue() {
21532        let chaos = || Config {
21533            chaos: true,
21534            ..Config::default()
21535        };
21536        assert!(chaos().max_timeslice.is_some());
21537        // A waiter the spinner's draws never beat is never counted.
21538        let (mut scheduler, spinner, waiter) = chaos_spinner_and_waiter(chaos(), 500, 9820);
21539        for (at, drawn) in [(1, 9900), (2, 9950), (3, 9990)] {
21540            spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, drawn, at);
21541            assert_eq!(scheduler.priorities[&spinner], drawn);
21542            assert!(!scheduler.chaos_passed_over.contains_key(&waiter));
21543            scheduler.priorities.insert(spinner, 500);
21544            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(spinner));
21545            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(spinner);
21546        }
21547
21548        let unbounded = |name: &str, cfg: Config, setup: &dyn Fn(&mut Scheduler)| {
21549            let (mut scheduler, spinner, _waiter) = chaos_spinner_and_waiter(cfg, 500, 9820);
21550            setup(&mut scheduler);
21551            for (at, drawn) in [(1, 136), (2, 7043), (3, 4756)] {
21552                spinner_changepoint(&mut scheduler, spinner, drawn, at);
21553                assert_eq!(scheduler.priorities[&spinner], drawn, "{name}");
21554            }
21555            assert!(scheduler.chaos_passed_over.is_empty(), "{name}");
21556        };
21557        unbounded(
21558            "no timer preemption",
21559            Config {
21560                max_timeslice: None,
21561                ..chaos()
21562            },
21563            &|_| {},
21564        );
21565        unbounded(
21566            "connectbind",
21567            Config {
21568                sched_heuristic: crate::config::SchedHeuristic::ConnectBind,
21569                ..chaos()
21570            },
21571            &|_| {},
21572        );
21573        unbounded(
21574            "random heuristic",
21575            Config {
21576                sched_heuristic: crate::config::SchedHeuristic::Random,
21577                ..chaos()
21578            },
21579            &|_| {},
21580        );
21581        unbounded(
21582            "preemption replay",
21583            Config {
21584                replay_preemptions_from: Some(PathBuf::from("/nonexistent/preemptions.json")),
21585                ..chaos()
21586            },
21587            &|_| {},
21588        );
21589        unbounded("schedule replay", chaos(), &|scheduler| {
21590            scheduler.replayer = Some(replayer::Replayer::new(Vec::new()));
21591        });
21592        unbounded("polling waiter", chaos(), &|scheduler| {
21593            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21594            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(waiter));
21595            scheduler.run_queue.push_poller(waiter, 9820, u32::MAX);
21596        });
21597    }

21599    /// A background grant (here `BlockingExternalIO`) is a turn of a thread
21600    /// that did not yield, so it ends the yield epoch as well as the one-turn
21601    /// exclusion: the yielder in the first band runs next.
21602    #[test]
21603    fn a_background_grant_ends_the_yield_epoch() {
21604        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21605            chaos: true,
21606            ..Config::default()
21607        });
21608        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21609        let background = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21610        let third = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21611        for tid in [yielder, background, third] {
21612            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21613        }
21614        scheduler
21615            .priorities
21616            .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21617        scheduler.priorities.insert(third, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
21618        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(yielder);
21619        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(third);
21620        chaos_yield_turn(&mut scheduler, yielder);
21621
21622        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
21623            &mut scheduler,
21624            background,
21625            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(background, 1)),
21626            None,
21627        );
21628        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(background));
21629        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21630    }

21632    /// A chaos `sched_yield` keeps the yielder ordinary work: the
21633    /// deterministic-work-first gate stays closed to an external continuation
21634    /// whose readiness is host-timed while it is runnable. A first version of
21635    /// the hermit#4068 fix moved the yielder into the last band, where it
21636    /// counted as a poller (review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4080,
21637    /// whose Codex reviewer wrote this test).
21638    #[test]
21639    fn a_chaos_yield_keeps_ordinary_work_ahead_of_host_ready_io() {
21640        for finished in [false, true] {
21641            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21642                chaos: true,
21643                ..Config::default()
21644            });
21645            let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21646            let poller = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21647            let background = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21648            for tid in [yielder, poller, background] {
21649                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21650            }
21651            scheduler
21652                .priorities
21653                .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21654            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(yielder);
21655            scheduler
21656                .run_queue
21657                .push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
21658            let op = ExternalOpId::new(background, 7);
21659            scheduler
21660                .blocked
21661                .external_io_blockers
21662                .insert(background, op);
21663            if finished {
21664                let mut continuation = Resources::new(background);
21665                continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op), Permission::RW);
21666                scheduler
21667                    .next_turns
21668                    .get(&background)
21669                    .unwrap()
21670                    .req
21671                    .put(Ok(continuation));
21672            }
21673            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21674            scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
21675            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
21676            assert_eq!(
21677                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&background),
21678                Some(&op),
21679                "ordinary yielding work must defer host-ready admission; finished={finished}"
21680            );
21681            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(background));
21682
21683            // Adjacent positive: with the ordinary yielder gone, a real all-poller
21684            // queue admits exactly a posted continuation, preserving useful IO progress.
21685            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(yielder));
21686            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
21687            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(background), finished);
21688        }
21689    }

21691    /// The `InboundSignal` branch defers a host-asynchronous `SIGCHLD` behind
21692    /// ordinary work, and a chaos `sched_yield` must not turn that work into a
21693    /// poller and release the signal (same review and author as above).
21694    #[test]
21695    fn a_chaos_yield_keeps_ordinary_work_ahead_of_a_deferred_sigchld() {
21696        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
21697            chaos: true,
21698            ..Config::default()
21699        });
21700        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21701        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21702        let signaled = DetTid::from_raw(102);
21703        for tid in [yielder, poller, signaled] {
21704            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
21705        }
21706        scheduler
21707            .priorities
21708            .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
21709        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(yielder);
21710        scheduler
21711            .run_queue
21712            .push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
21713        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(signaled);
21714        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
21715        assert_eq!(
21716            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(signaled),
21717            Some(signaled)
21718        );
21719        assert!(
21720            scheduler
21721                .block_for_one_resource(
21722                    signaled,
21723                    &inbound,
21724                    &Permission::W,
21725                    None,
21726                    None,
21727                    &Ivar::new()
21728                )
21729                .is_err()
21730        );
21731        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled));
21732        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
21733        scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
21734        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
21735        assert!(
21736            scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled),
21737            "ordinary yielding work must defer host-async SIGCHLD admission"
21738        );
21739        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(signaled));
21740
21741        // Adjacent positive: removing the only ordinary thread leaves real
21742        // pollers and makes the same deferred signal eligible for readmission.
21743        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(yielder));
21744        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
21745        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled));
21746        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(signaled));
21747    }

21750    /// admits ready IO and a deferred signal, as the progress policy needs.
21751    #[test]
21752    fn a_poller_only_queue_still_admits_ready_io_and_a_deferred_sigchld() {
21753        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {

21756        });

21764            .run_queue
21765            .push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);

21772        let op = ExternalOpId::new(background, 7);

21779        scheduler

21790    /// The scheduler under the condition that turns on its model of which thread
21791    /// a signal reaches (`models_signal_targets`): serialized threads and a
21792    /// backend that decides blocked-wait interruption from the kernel's signal
21793    /// state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
21794    fn gated_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
21795        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(
21796            &Config {
21797                sequentialize_threads: true,
21798                ..Config::default()
21799            }
21800            .with_backend(|backend| {
21801                backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = true;
21802                backend.delivers_preemption_timer_events = false;
21803                backend.runs_guest_code_between_injections = false;
21804            }),
21805        );
21806        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
21807        scheduler
21808    }
21809
21810    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` ends a parked precise-mode futex wait only when the
21811    /// scheduler sends it to the waiter at a commit point (`wake_signaled_guest`,
21812    /// as a `ChildExit` timer does): the waiter is woken with the signal, as
21813    /// Linux ends the wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
21814    /// Through the drain of a cross-task signal, which only says a `SIGCHLD` is
21815    /// pending, or when a host-timed source a guest armed can post `SIGCHLD`
21816    /// too, the waiter stays parked with its original deadline, and the signal
21817    /// stays pending in the kernel until the call returns for another reason:
21818    /// `/proc` cannot tell a `SIGCHLD` sent at a deterministic point from the
21819    /// one the kernel posts for a child event at a moment set by host timing
21820    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). A caught `SIGUSR1`
21821    /// still ends the same wait.
21822    #[test]
21823    fn a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it() {
21824        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
21825        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
21826        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
21827        for (scheduler_send, host_timed) in [(false, false), (true, false), (true, true)] {
21828            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
21829            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
21830            if host_timed {
21831                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
21832            }
21833            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
21834                &target,
21835                futex,
21836                Some(deadline),
21837                u32::MAX,
21838                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
21839            );
21840            scheduler
21841                .test_kernel_signal_states
21842                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
21843            assert_eq!(
21844                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(target, 0),
21845                Some(usr1),
21846                "a caught SIGCHLD is not among the signals that end the wait"
21847            );
21848
21849            if scheduler_send {
21850                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
21851            } else {
21852                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
21853                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21854            }
21855            let case = format!("scheduler_send={scheduler_send} host_timed={host_timed}");
21856            if scheduler_send && !host_timed {
21857                assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
21858                assert_eq!(
21859                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
21860                    vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)],
21861                    "{case}"
21862                );
21863                continue;
21864            }
21865            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
21866            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
21867            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{case}");
21868            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
21869            assert_eq!(
21870                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21871                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
21872                "{case}"
21873            );
21874
21875            if scheduler_send {
21876                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
21877            } else {
21878                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21879                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21880            }
21881            assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
21882            assert_eq!(
21883                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
21884                vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
21885                "{case}"
21886            );
21887        }
21888    }
21889
21890    /// A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sends a parked precise-mode futex waiter at a
21891    /// commit point (a `ChildExit` timer) wakes it to the front of its band and
21892    /// marks the delivery as placed (`sigchld_ready`), so its turn is granted
21893    /// ahead of a runnable sibling rather than deferred behind it. Deferred,
21894    /// the sibling resumed first, and the kernel, which skips the
21895    /// ptrace-stopped waiter, gave the sibling the signal: the handler ran on
21896    /// the sibling and the wait did not end with EINTR, where Linux ends it
21897    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Without the mark the
21898    /// same turn is deferred, and a `SIGUSR1`, which is never deferred, sets
21899    /// no mark.
21900    #[test]
21901    fn a_scheduler_sigchld_wakes_a_parked_futex_waiter_ahead_of_a_runnable_sibling() {
21902        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
21903        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
21904        for (signal, marked) in [
21905            (Signal::SIGCHLD, true),
21906            (Signal::SIGCHLD, false),
21907            (Signal::SIGUSR1, false),
21908        ] {
21909            let case = format!("{signal:?}, marked={marked}");
21910            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
21911            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
21912            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
21913                &target,
21914                futex,
21915                None,
21916                u32::MAX,
21917                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
21918            );
21919            scheduler
21920                .test_kernel_signal_states
21921                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
21922            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21923            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
21924            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
21925
21926            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, signal);
21927            assert_eq!(
21928                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21929                vec![target, sibling],
21930                "{case}"
21931            );
21932            assert_eq!(
21933                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
21934                signal == Signal::SIGCHLD,
21935                "{case}"
21936            );
21937            if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD && !marked {
21938                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&target);
21939            }
21940            let resources = scheduler
21941                .next_turns
21942                .get(&target)
21943                .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
21944                .and_then(Result::ok)
21945                .expect("the waiter holds its signal request");
21946            let (selected, _, response) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
21947            assert_eq!(selected, target, "{case}");
21948            let granted = scheduler
21949                .step4_resource_block(target, &resources, &response)
21950                .is_ok();
21951            let deferred = signal == Signal::SIGCHLD && !marked;
21952            assert_eq!(granted, !deferred, "{case}");
21953            assert_eq!(
21954                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&target),
21955                deferred,
21956                "{case}"
21957            );
21958        }
21959    }
21960
21961    /// A waiter the wake leaves held at a happens-before gate gets no
21962    /// `sigchld_ready` mark, which a later, host-timed `SIGCHLD` delivery could
21963    /// otherwise use to skip its deferral (the Codex and Claude reviews of
21964    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304); nor
21965    /// is it made a thread step 3 resumes first. Where the wake does unblock it,
21966    /// both hold.
21967    #[test]
21968    fn a_held_futex_waiter_is_not_marked_for_a_scheduler_sigchld() {
21969        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
21970        for held in [false, true] {
21971            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
21972            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
21973            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
21974            scheduler
21975                .test_kernel_signal_states
21976                .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
21977            if held {
21978                let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
21979                hb.parked.insert(target);
21980                scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
21981            }
21982            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
21983            assert_eq!(
21984                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
21985                !held,
21986                "held={held}"
21987            );
21988            assert_eq!(
21989                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target),
21990                !held,
21991                "held={held}"
21992            );
21993        }
21994    }
21995
21996    /// A thread polling internal IO that the scheduler sends a `SIGCHLD` it
21997    /// does not block is woken to the front of its band and marked, so it is
21998    /// the next thread to resume and takes the signal. Before, it went to the
21999    /// back, its turn was deferred,
22000    /// and a spinning sibling took the signal: a `read` of an empty pipe
22001    /// returned the sibling's byte where Linux returns EINTR (the Claude
22002    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304).
22003    #[test]
22004    fn a_scheduler_sigchld_wakes_an_internal_io_poller_ahead_of_a_runnable_sibling() {
22005        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22006        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22007        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, poller);
22008        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
22009        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
22010        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
22011        let mut polling = Resources::new(poller);
22012        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::RW);
22013        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&poller).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
22014        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(poller);
22015        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(poller, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22016        assert_eq!(
22017            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
22018            vec![poller, sibling]
22019        );
22020        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&poller));
22021        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&poller));
22022        assert_eq!(
22023            scheduler.inbound_signals(poller),
22024            vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)]
22025        );
22026    }
22027
22028    /// A thread woken to take the scheduler's `SIGCHLD` is the next selected,
22029    /// whatever its priority or the selection heuristic, and before a runnable
22030    /// vfork child, so it is the thread that resumes first and takes the
22031    /// process-directed copy: chosen over a sibling in a higher band and over
22032    /// the vfork child (the Claude and Codex reviews of
22033    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Not while its mask
22034    /// blocks `SIGCHLD`; and it leaves the set once its copy is gone from the
22035    /// shared queue and its request is not the delivery.
22036    #[test]
22037    fn a_sigchld_taker_is_selected_first_whatever_its_priority() {
22038        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22039        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22040        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
22041        scheduler
22042            .priorities
22043            .insert(target, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY - 1);
22044        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
22045        scheduler
22046            .test_kernel_signal_states
22047            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
22048        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
22049        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
22050        scheduler
22051            .priorities
22052            .insert(sibling, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
22053        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
22054        // A runnable vfork child, which step 3 otherwise selects first.
22055        let vfork_parent = DetTid::from_raw(102);
22056        let vfork_child = DetTid::from_raw(103);
22057        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, vfork_child);
22058        scheduler
22059            .vfork_barriers
22060            .insert(vfork_parent, Some(vfork_child));
22061        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(vfork_child);
22062        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22063        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target));
22064        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
22065        assert_eq!(selected, target);
22066        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
22067
22068        // Not while its mask blocks SIGCHLD.
22069        scheduler
22070            .test_kernel_signal_states
22071            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, chld));
22072        scheduler
22073            .blocked
22074            .out_of_scheduler_masks
22075            .insert(target, Some(chld));
22076        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
22077        assert_eq!(selected, vfork_child);
22078        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
22079        scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(&target);
22080
22081        // Its copy gone (no send in the window) and its request something
22082        // else: it leaves the set.
22083        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(target)));
22084        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
22085        assert_eq!(selected, vfork_child);
22086        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
22087        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target));
22088    }
