22090    /// A second `SIGCHLD` sent while the first is still pending in the
22091    /// process's shared queue coalesces, as Linux does not queue a standard
22092    /// signal already pending (`legacy_queue`): it wakes no thread and makes
22093    /// none a taker, so the thread the first send woke takes the one copy.
22094    /// Before, the second send woke its own target and marked it too, and the
22095    /// lower-numbered target was resumed first and took the copy (the Codex
22096    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Where the
22097    /// window and the queue disagree, one is stale and the thread is woken,
22098    /// as before.
22099    #[test]
22100    fn a_coalesced_sigchld_wakes_no_thread() {
22101        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22102        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22103        let first = DetTid::from_raw(101);
22104        for (pending_before, window_open, coalesces) in [
22105            (true, true, true),
22106            (false, true, false),
22107            (true, false, false),
22108        ] {
22109            let case = format!("pending_before={pending_before} window_open={window_open}");
22110            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22111            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
22112            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
22113            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, first, false);
22114            for thread in [leader, first] {
22115                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
22116                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22117                    &thread,
22118                    futex,
22119                    None,
22120                    u32::MAX,
22121                    Some(signal_watch(chld)),
22122                );
22123                scheduler
22124                    .test_kernel_signal_states
22125                    .insert(thread, signal_state(chld, 0));
22126            }
22127            if window_open {
22128                // The first send, to `first`, as `send_guest_signal` makes it.
22129                assert!(
22130                    scheduler.note_group_send(first, Signal::SIGCHLD, false),
22131                    "{case}"
22132                );
22133                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(first, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22134                assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&first), "{case}");
22135            }
22136            let wakes = scheduler.note_group_send(leader, Signal::SIGCHLD, pending_before);
22137            assert_eq!(wakes, !coalesces, "{case}");
22138            if wakes {
22139                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(leader, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22140            }
22141            assert_eq!(
22142                scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(leader),
22143                coalesces,
22144                "{case}"
22145            );
22146            assert_eq!(
22147                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&leader),
22148                !coalesces,
22149                "{case}"
22150            );
22151            if coalesces {
22152                let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
22153                assert_eq!(selected, first, "{case}");
22154                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
22155            }
22156        }
22157    }
22158
22159    /// The answer a woken thread's turn gets (`unblock_guest`).
22160    fn turn_answer(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid) -> Option<SchedResponse> {
22161        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
22162        assert!(scheduler.unblock_guest(target, &response).is_ok());
22163        response.try_read()
22164    }
22165
22166    /// A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD`, recorded in the sender's turn
22167    /// (`PrivateSent`), ends a parked precise-mode futex wait through the
22168    /// drain of the cross-task signal, as Linux ends the wait for a caught,
22169    /// unblocked signal pending for the thread. The waiter's turn says it was
22170    /// woken for a signal but commits no `SIGCHLD` to it, so its own check
22171    /// decides from the record (`PrivatePending`), which a flush clears. The
22172    /// wait stays parked for an unrecorded copy, a recorded one a host-timed
22173    /// source could also have posted, a recorded one that is default-ignored
22174    /// (under ptrace the kernel queues a copy Linux discards at generation,
22175    /// and the sender's turn records it), and one whose record a flush
22176    /// cleared (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
22177    #[test]
22178    fn a_private_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_through_the_drain() {
22179        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
22180        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22181        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
22182        for case in ["recorded", "unrecorded", "host-timed", "default", "flushed"] {
22183            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22184            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
22185            if case == "host-timed" {
22186                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
22187            }
22188            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22189                &target,
22190                futex,
22191                Some(deadline),
22192                u32::MAX,
22193                Some(signal_watch(chld)),
22194            );
22195            let caught = if case == "default" { 0 } else { chld };
22196            scheduler
22197                .test_kernel_signal_states
22198                .insert(target, signal_state(caught, 0));
22199            if case != "unrecorded" {
22200                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
22201                    target,
22202                    ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
22203                );
22204            }
22205            if case == "flushed" {
22206                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
22207            }
22208            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
22209            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22210            if case == "recorded" {
22211                assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
22212                assert_eq!(
22213                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
22214                    vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)],
22215                    "{case}"
22216                );
22217                assert!(
22218                    matches!(
22219                        turn_answer(&mut scheduler, target),
22220                        Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))) if signals.is_empty()
22221                    ),
22222                    "{case}: woken for a signal, with no SIGCHLD committed"
22223                );
22224                assert!(scheduler.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.is_empty());
22225                continue;
22226            }
22227            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
22228            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
22229            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{case}");
22230            assert_eq!(
22231                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
22232                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
22233                "{case}"
22234            );
22235        }
22236    }
22237
22238    /// The drain marks a futex waiter only when it actually unblocked it: a
22239    /// thread held at a happens-before gate is left held
22240    /// (`force_unblock_thread_at`), and a mark left on it would outlive the
22241    /// wake it describes (the Claude re-check of
22242    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
22243    #[test]
22244    fn a_futex_waiter_held_at_a_gate_is_not_marked_as_drain_woken() {
22245        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
22246        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22247        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22248        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
22249        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
22250        scheduler
22251            .test_kernel_signal_states
22252            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
22253        scheduler
22254            .child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target });
22255        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
22256        hb.parked.insert(target);
22257        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
22258        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
22259        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22260        assert!(scheduler.blocked.drain_woken_waiters.is_empty());
22261    }
22262
22263    /// A `SIGCHLD` the drain merges into the batch of a futex waiter it
22264    /// already woke (`WaitidSignalRequest::Pending`) is not committed either:
22265    /// the waiter's turn carries the `SIGUSR1` it was woken for and no
22266    /// `SIGCHLD`. A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sends at a commit point
22267    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005)
22268    /// is committed, to a parked waiter and to one the drain already woke,
22269    /// for `SIGUSR1` or for a guest's recorded private `SIGCHLD`, that has not
22270    /// yet run its turn (the Claude re-check of
22271    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132: that commit was lost).
22272    #[test]
22273    fn only_a_scheduler_sent_sigchld_is_committed_to_a_woken_futex_waiter() {
22274        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
22275        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22276        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
22277        let usr1_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
22278        let chld_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD);
22279        for case in [
22280            "merged",
22281            "parked",
22282            "woken for SIGUSR1",
22283            "woken for a private SIGCHLD",
22284        ] {
22285            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22286            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
22287            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22288                &target,
22289                futex,
22290                None,
22291                u32::MAX,
22292                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
22293            );
22294            scheduler
22295                .test_kernel_signal_states
22296                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
22297            let expected = match case {
22298                "merged" => {
22299                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1_signal);
22300                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22301                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, chld_signal);
22302                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22303                    assert_eq!(
22304                        scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
22305                        vec![usr1_signal, chld_signal],
22306                        "the merge put SIGCHLD in the batch"
22307                    );
22308                    vec![usr1_signal]
22309                }
22310                "parked" => {
22311                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22312                    vec![chld_signal]
22313                }
22314                "woken for SIGUSR1" => {
22315                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1_signal);
22316                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22317                    assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
22318                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22319                    vec![usr1_signal, chld_signal]
22320                }
22321                _ => {
22322                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
22323                        target,
22324                        ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
22325                    );
22326                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, chld_signal);
22327                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22328                    assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
22329                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22330                    vec![chld_signal]
22331                }
22332            };
22333            let answer = turn_answer(&mut scheduler, target);
22334            assert!(
22335                matches!(&answer, Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))) if *signals == expected),
22336                "{case}: {answer:?}"
22337            );
22338        }
22339    }

22341    /// A recorded private `SIGCHLD` does not end a restartable internal IO
22342    /// poll: R2 exempts it only for precise futex waits, and
22343    /// `futex_wait_held_signals`, which the poll shares, still holds it
22344    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
22345    #[test]
22346    fn a_recorded_private_sigchld_does_not_end_a_restartable_internal_read_poll() {
22347        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
22348        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22349        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
22350        assert!(scheduler.restartable_internal_io_signals(target).is_some());
22351        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
22352            target,
22353            KernelSignalState {
22354                caught: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
22355                ..Default::default()
22356            },
22357        );
22358        scheduler
22359            .child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target });
22360        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
22361        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22362        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
22363        let resources = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
22364            .req
22365            .try_read()
22366            .and_then(Result::ok)
22367            .expect("the poller keeps its request");
22368        assert!(
22369            resources
22370                .resources
22371                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
22372        );

22375    /// A signal recorded as host-timed for a process, as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`
22376    /// records its signal in the arming thread's turn, never ends a parked
22377    /// precise-mode futex wait of any thread of that process, although the
22378    /// waiter catches it, and a later disarm does not remove the record. A
22379    /// forked child's wait still ends for it; a container-wide record holds
22380    /// it in every process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
22381    #[test]
22382    fn a_host_timed_signal_never_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_of_its_process() {
22383        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
22384        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
22385        let term = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM);
22386        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22387        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
22388            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), 0, "nothing armed yet");
22389        }
22390
22391        // The creator, not its process's leader, arms SIGUSR1.
22392        assert_eq!(
22393            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(creator, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr1),
22394            usr1
22395        );
22396        assert_eq!(
22397            scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent),
22398            usr1,
22399            "the record covers every thread of the arming process"
22400        );
22401        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(creator), usr1);
22402        assert_eq!(
22403            scheduler.host_timed_signals(child),
22404            0,
22405            "a forked child starts without its parent's record"
22406        );
22407        // A disarm (signal 0) records nothing and removes nothing.
22408        assert_eq!(
22409            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(parent, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, 0),
22410            usr1
22411        );
22412        // A container-wide source holds its signal in every process.
22413        assert_eq!(
22414            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(child, HostTimedSignalScope::Container, usr2),
22415            usr2
22416        );
22417        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), usr1 | usr2);
22418        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(child), usr2);
22419
22420        // Parked futex waiters that catch all three signals: only SIGTERM ends
22421        // the parent's wait, and SIGUSR1 and SIGTERM end the child's.
22422        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
22423            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22424                &thread,
22425                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
22426                None,
22427                u32::MAX,
22428                Some(signal_watch(usr1 | usr2 | term)),
22429            );
22430            scheduler
22431                .test_kernel_signal_states
22432                .insert(thread, signal_state(usr1 | usr2 | term, 0));
22433        }
22434        assert_eq!(
22435            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(parent, 0),
22436            Some(term)
22437        );
22438        assert_eq!(
22439            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(child, 0),
22440            Some(usr1 | term)
22441        );
22442    }
22443
22444    /// A launch that may pass the guest a terminal records every signal a
22445    /// terminal sends as host-timed for every process before the guest runs:
22446    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT for a hangup, SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the
22447    /// interrupt, quit and suspend characters, SIGWINCH for a resize, and
22448    /// SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU for a background read or write. So a parked
22449    /// precise-mode futex wait that catches all of them ends for none, in the
22450    /// first process and in a forked child alike. Nothing is recorded without
22451    /// that terminal, or on a backend whose blocked waits do not read the
22452    /// kernel's signal state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
22453    /// Round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
22454    /// interruption" on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361: only
22455    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT were recorded, so a resize ended such a wait at a
22456    /// turn the host chose.
22457    #[test]
22458    fn a_launch_that_may_pass_a_terminal_holds_the_terminal_signals_from_the_start() {
22459        let terminal = [
22460            libc::SIGHUP,
22461            libc::SIGCONT,
22462            libc::SIGINT,
22463            libc::SIGQUIT,
22464            libc::SIGTSTP,
22465            libc::SIGWINCH,
22466            libc::SIGTTIN,
22467            libc::SIGTTOU,
22468        ]
22469        .into_iter()
22470        .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal));
22471        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
22472        let gated = |guest_may_inherit_a_terminal| {
22473            Config {
22474                sequentialize_threads: true,
22475                guest_may_inherit_a_terminal,
22476                ..Config::default()
22477            }
22478            .with_backend(|backend| {
22479                backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = true;
22480                backend.delivers_preemption_timer_events = false;
22481                backend.runs_guest_code_between_injections = false;
22482            })
22483        };
22484        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(true)), terminal);
22485        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(false)), 0);
22486        assert_eq!(
22487            startup_host_timed_signals(
22488                &Config {
22489                    guest_may_inherit_a_terminal: true,
22490                    ..Config::default()
22491                }
22492                .with_backend(|backend| backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = false)
22493            ),
22494            0,
22495            "a backend whose waits do not read the kernel's signal state records nothing"
22496        );
22497
22498        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(true));
22499        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
22500        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22501        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
22502        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
22503        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
22504        for thread in [parent, child] {
22505            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
22506        }
22507        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
22508            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), terminal);
22509            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22510                &thread,
22511                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
22512                None,
22513                u32::MAX,
22514                Some(signal_watch(terminal | usr1)),
22515            );
22516            scheduler
22517                .test_kernel_signal_states
22518                .insert(thread, signal_state(terminal | usr1, 0));
22519            assert_eq!(
22520                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(thread, 0),
22521                Some(usr1),
22522                "only SIGUSR1 ends the wait of {thread:?}"
22523            );
22524        }
22525
22526        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(false));
22527        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), 0);
22528    }
22529
22530    /// A parent process 100 whose second thread 101 created child process 200
22531    /// with `exit_signal`, on the gated scheduler.
22532    fn sigchld_family(exit_signal: libc::c_int) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid, DetTid) {
22533        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
22534        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22535        let creator = DetTid::from_raw(101);
22536        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
22537        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
22538        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, creator, false);
22539        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
22540            creator,
22541            child,
22542            true,
22543            false,
22544            exit_signal,
22545        );
22546        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
22547            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
22548        }
22549        (scheduler, parent, creator, child)
22550    }
22551
22552    /// The inputs of a process-directed signal the leader sends to its own
22553    /// process read each sibling from the schedule
22554    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034): a stopped thread's
22555    /// `SigBlk`; the guest's own mask while Detcore holds the thread under a
22556    /// private one (`saved_guest_sigmasks`); `blocked & !set` for an
22557    /// `rt_sigtimedwait` poller; external I/O and a real `rt_sigsuspend` as
22558    /// outside the schedule; and a logically killed thread as exit-granted.
22559    #[test]
22560    fn own_process_signal_inputs_read_each_sibling_from_the_schedule() {
22561        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
22562        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
22563        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22564        let state = |scheduler: &Scheduler| scheduler.own_process_signal_inputs(parent).siblings;
22565        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
22566            creator,
22567            KernelSignalState {
22568                blocked: usr1 | usr2,
22569                ..Default::default()
22570            },
22571        );
22572        assert_eq!(
22573            state(&scheduler),
22574            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr1 | usr2)))]
22575        );
22576        assert!(scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, Some(usr1)));
22577        assert_eq!(
22578            state(&scheduler),
22579            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr2)))],
22580            "a poller takes a signal in its set whatever its mask"
22581        );
22582        assert!(scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, None));
22583        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(creator, Some(usr2)));
22584        assert_eq!(
22585            state(&scheduler),
22586            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr2)))],
22587            "the guest's own mask, not Detcore's private one"
22588        );
22589        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(creator, None));
22590        let op = ExternalOpId {
22591            tid: creator,
22592            sequence: 1,
22593        };
22594        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(creator, op);
22595        assert_eq!(
22596            state(&scheduler),
22597            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule)]
22598        );
22599        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&creator);
22600        scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.insert(creator, op);
22601        assert_eq!(
22602            state(&scheduler),
22603            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule)]
22604        );
22605        scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&creator);
22606        scheduler.logically_killed_threads.insert(creator);
22607        assert_eq!(
22608            state(&scheduler),
22609            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::ExitGranted)]
22610        );
22611    }

22613    /// An unreaped child whose exit signal is neither 0 nor SIGCHLD names that
22614    /// signal in its parent's inputs, and a SIGCHLD child names nothing.
22615    #[test]
22616    fn own_process_signal_inputs_name_a_childs_foreign_exit_signal() {
22617        let (scheduler, parent, _creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGUSR2);
22618        assert_eq!(
22619            scheduler
22620                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
22621                .foreign_exit_signals,
22622            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2)
22623        );
22624        let (scheduler, parent, _creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22625        assert_eq!(
22626            scheduler
22627                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
22628                .foreign_exit_signals,
22629            0
22630        );
22631    }

22633    /// A signal the scheduler sent to a process counts for its own-process
22634    /// admission only while it is in the process's shared queue, where its
22635    /// process-directed copy waits: a guest's copy of the same number taken
22636    /// from a thread's own queue does not settle it, and a copy merged into an
22637    /// earlier one (Hermit's `kill()` copy for a POSIX timer merges with a
22638    /// pending standard signal), taken by sigtimedwait or discarded by
22639    /// SIG_IGN, gone from the queue, refuses nothing. An unreadable queue keeps the record
22640    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122).
22641    #[test]
22642    fn a_scheduler_sent_signal_counts_while_it_is_in_the_shared_queue() {
22643        let hup = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGHUP);
22644        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22645        let shared = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, pending: u64| {
22646            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
22647                parent,
22648                KernelSignalState {
22649                    shared_pending: pending,
22650                    ..Default::default()
22651                },
22652            );
22653        };
22654        let undelivered = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
22655            scheduler
22656                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
22657                .undelivered_scheduler_signals
22658        };
22659        shared(&mut scheduler, hup);
22660        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), 0, "nothing sent yet");
22661        scheduler.note_scheduler_signal_sent(creator, libc::SIGHUP);
22662        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup);
22663        shared(&mut scheduler, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | hup);
22664        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup, "only what the scheduler sent");
22665        shared(&mut scheduler, 0);
22666        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), 0, "gone from the shared queue");
22667        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.clear();
22668        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup, "an unreadable queue keeps it");
22669    }

22672    /// every process and never forgotten.
22673    #[test]
22674    fn a_guest_marker_signal_send_is_recorded_for_every_process() {
22675        let (mut scheduler, parent, _creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22676        assert!(
22677            !scheduler

22694    fn park_for_sigchld(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, unblocked: u64) {
22695        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
22696        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
22697            &thread,
22698            futex,
22699            None,
22700            u32::MAX,
22701            Some(signal_watch(unblocked)),
22702        );
22703        scheduler
22704            .test_kernel_signal_states
22705            .insert(thread, signal_state(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0));
22706    }
22707
22708    /// A child's death itself wakes no parked futex waiter of its parent,
22709    /// although the waiter catches `SIGCHLD`: a child killed by a signal, or
22710    /// leaving through `exit` in its last thread, has no `ChildExit` timer, and
22711    /// the kernel posts its own `SIGCHLD` at a moment set by host timing, so the
22712    /// signal stays pending until the waiter's call returns for another reason.
22713    /// Before, the death made the signal eligible and the drain woke that
22714    /// waiter (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The scheduler
22715    /// still names the thread Linux would give it to (`kernel_sigchld_target`),
22716    /// the child's creator first, and the `SIGCHLD` a `ChildExit` timer sends to
22717    /// that thread wakes it, and only it
22718    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
22719    #[test]
22720    fn a_child_exit_wakes_only_the_parked_futex_waiter_its_timer_signals() {
22721        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22722        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22723        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
22724        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, chld);
22725        assert_eq!(
22726            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
22727            Some(creator)
22728        );
22729
22730        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
22731        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22732        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
22733        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
22734        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
22735        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
22736        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(creator).is_empty());
22737
22738        // The SIGCHLD a `ChildExit` timer sends to the creator wakes it, and
22739        // leaves the leader parked.
22740        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
22741        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
22742        assert_eq!(
22743            scheduler.inbound_signals(creator),
22744            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)]
22745        );
22746        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
22747        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
22748    }
22749
22750    /// The kernel gives a shared-queue `SIGCHLD` to the first thread that does
22751    /// not block it, the child's creator first, whether that thread is parked or
22752    /// running, and `kernel_sigchld_target` names that thread: a `ChildExit`
22753    /// timer signals it. No parked waiter is woken for the child's death,
22754    /// whichever thread is the target (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
22755    #[test]
22756    fn a_child_exit_sigchld_goes_to_the_first_thread_that_does_not_block_it() {
22757        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22758
22759        // The creator runs and does not block SIGCHLD: it takes the signal, and
22760        // the leader's wait is left alone.
22761        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22762        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
22763        scheduler
22764            .test_kernel_signal_states
22765            .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
22766        assert_eq!(
22767            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
22768            Some(creator)
22769        );
22770        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
22771        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22772        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
22773        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
22774
22775        // The creator blocks SIGCHLD and the leader runs without blocking it: the
22776        // leader comes first in thread-ID order and takes it, so a waiter after
22777        // it is not woken.
22778        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22779        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(102);
22780        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, waiter, false);
22781        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
22782        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, waiter, chld);
22783        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
22784        scheduler
22785            .test_kernel_signal_states
22786            .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
22787        assert_eq!(
22788            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
22789            Some(parent)
22790        );
22791        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
22792        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22793        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
22794        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
22795
22796        // Every thread blocks it: nobody is chosen and nobody is woken.
22797        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22798        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
22799        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
22800            parent,
22801            KernelSignalState {
22802                blocked: chld,
22803                ..signal_state(chld, 0)
22804            },
22805        );
22806        assert_eq!(scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator), None);
22807        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
22808        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22809        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
22810    }
22811
22812    /// A timer's process-directed signal is sent to a thread that does not
22813    /// block it, since Linux gives it to no other, and the scheduler wakes the
22814    /// thread it names. The thread `select_signal_target` drew keeps it if it
22815    /// does not block it; when every thread blocks it, the drawn thread is
22816    /// kept, and `kill` leaves it in the shared queue. Before, a SIGALRM drawn
22817    /// under `--chaos-target-races` for a worker that blocks it woke that
22818    /// worker, and the thread in `pause` slept forever
22819    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320).
22820    #[test]
22821    fn a_timer_signal_goes_to_a_thread_that_does_not_block_it() {
22822        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
22823        let state = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
22824            blocked,
22825            ..signal_state(alrm, 0)
22826        };
22827        let (mut scheduler, leader, worker, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22828        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
22829        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(leader, state(0));
22830        scheduler
22831            .test_kernel_signal_states
22832            .insert(worker, state(alrm));
22833        assert_eq!(
22834            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22835            leader,
22836            "the worker blocks SIGALRM, the leader does not"
22837        );
22838        assert_eq!(
22839            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, leader, Signal::SIGALRM),
22840            leader
22841        );
22842
22843        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(worker, state(0));
22844        assert_eq!(
22845            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22846            worker,
22847            "a drawn thread that does not block it keeps it"
22848        );
22849
22850        scheduler
22851            .test_kernel_signal_states
22852            .insert(leader, state(alrm));
22853        scheduler
22854            .test_kernel_signal_states
22855            .insert(worker, state(alrm));
22856        assert_eq!(
22857            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22858            worker,
22859            "every thread blocks it: the drawn thread is kept"
22860        );
22861
22862        // A second candidate: the fallback takes the lowest thread ID that
22863        // does not block it.
22864        let third = DetTid::from_raw(102);
22865        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, third, false);
22866        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, third);
22867        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(leader, state(0));
22868        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(third, state(0));
22869        assert_eq!(
22870            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22871            leader,
22872            "the lowest thread that does not block it"
22873        );
22874
22875        // A thread asleep in rt_sigsuspend whose mask admits the signal comes
22876        // first, ahead of a drawn thread that does not block it either: the
22877        // kernel wakes the sleeper while the drawn thread is held in a ptrace
22878        // stop (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4331).
22879        let op = ExternalOpId::new(third, 1);
22880        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
22881            &mut scheduler,
22882            third,
22883            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
22884            Some(0),
22885        );
22886        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(worker, state(0));
22887        assert_eq!(
22888            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22889            third,
22890            "the rt_sigsuspend sleeper, not the drawn worker"
22891        );
22892        assert_eq!(
22893            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, leader, Signal::SIGALRM),
22894            third,
22895            "nor the drawn leader"
22896        );
22897
22898        scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
22899        let reads = scheduler
22900            .test_kernel_mask_reads
22901            .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
22902        assert_eq!(
22903            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
22904            worker,
22905            "without signal-target modelling the drawn thread is kept"
22906        );
22907        assert_eq!(
22908            scheduler
22909                .test_kernel_mask_reads
22910                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
22911            reads,
22912            "and no mask is read"
22913        );
22914    }
22915
22916    /// A signal the scheduler sent while every thread blocked it waits in the
22917    /// process's shared queue, and a call that begins under a mask admitting
22918    /// it is ended by it at once. Such a call is armed for the release
22919    /// barrier, so it rejoins at a fixed point rather than as a completion
22920    /// only the host observes, which run mode held behind a thread spinning
22921    /// on `sched_yield` (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4234).
22922    ///
22923    /// Not armed:
22924    /// - when the call's mask blocks the signal;
22925    /// - when the process does not catch it (it does not end `sigsuspend`);
22926    /// - when a thread has taken it, or the shared queue no longer holds it,
22927    ///   as after SIG_IGN, `sigwaitinfo`, a signalfd read, an exec or a
22928    ///   sibling's dequeue; arming then held the barrier for a continuation
22929    ///   that never came (Claude review of
22930    ///   https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314);
22931    /// - when a sibling's `rt_sigtimedwait` set could take it first, or a
22932    ///   signalfd covers it and a sibling's background call reads a signalfd.
22933    ///   A signalfd that only exists, a background call that reads none, an
22934    ///   ended read, or another process's read does not count (Claude and
22935    ///   Codex re-checks of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4314);
22936    /// - for a later call once the armed call took it.
22937    ///
22938    /// Still armed after a thread took a copy from its own queue, which Linux
22939    /// dequeues first: the shared copy remains (Codex review of the same). And
22940    /// a later call is armed again while the signal is still pending, as when
22941    /// another signal ended the first (Claude re-check of the same).
22942    #[test]
22943    fn a_call_that_begins_with_a_scheduler_signal_waiting_is_armed() {
22944        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
22945        let family = |caught: u64, pending: u64| {
22946            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
22947            scheduler
22948                .test_signal_masks
22949                .insert((parent, None, "SigCgt"), caught);
22950            for thread in [parent, creator] {
22951                scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
22952                    thread,
22953                    KernelSignalState {
22954                        blocked: chld,
22955                        shared_pending: pending,
22956                        ..signal_state(caught, 0)
22957                    },
22958                );
22959            }
22960            scheduler.note_signal_left_in_shared_queue(parent, libc::SIGCHLD);
22961            (scheduler, parent, creator)
22962        };
22963        let begin = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, mask: u64| {
22964            let op = ExternalOpId::new(thread, 1);
22965            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
22966                scheduler,
22967                thread,
22968                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
22969                Some(mask),
22970            );
22971            assert_eq!(
22972                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&thread),
22973                Some(&op)
22974            );
22975            let armed = scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&thread);
22976            assert_eq!(armed, scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&thread));
22977            armed
22978        };
22979
22980        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
22981        assert!(
22982            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
22983            "caught, admitted, pending: armed"
22984        );
22985        for thread in [parent, creator] {
22986            if let Some(state) = scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.get_mut(&thread) {
22987                state.shared_pending = 0;
22988            }
22989        }
22990        assert!(
22991            !begin(&mut scheduler, parent, 0),
22992            "the armed call took the signal: a later call is not armed"
22993        );
22994        assert_eq!(
22995            scheduler.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.get(&parent),
22996            Some(&0),
22997            "and the record forgets it"
22998        );
22999
23000        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23001        assert!(begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0), "armed");
23002        assert!(
23003            begin(&mut scheduler, parent, 0),
23004            "another signal ended the armed call and this one is still pending: \
23005             the later call it ends is armed too"
23006        );
23007
23008        let (mut scheduler, _, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23009        assert!(
23010            !begin(&mut scheduler, creator, chld),
23011            "its mask blocks the signal"
23012        );
23013
23014        let (mut scheduler, _, creator) = family(0, chld);
23015        assert!(
23016            !begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23017            "not caught: it does not end sigsuspend"
23018        );
23019
23020        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23021        for thread in [parent, creator] {
23022            if let Some(state) = scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.get_mut(&thread) {
23023                state.shared_pending = 0;
23024            }
23025        }
23026        scheduler.note_process_signal_taken(parent, libc::SIGCHLD);
23027        assert_eq!(
23028            scheduler.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.get(&parent),
23029            Some(&0),
23030            "a thread has taken it from the shared queue: the record forgets it"
23031        );
23032        assert!(!begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0), "a thread has taken it");
23033
23034        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23035        scheduler.note_process_signal_taken(parent, libc::SIGCHLD);
23036        assert_eq!(
23037            scheduler.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.get(&parent),
23038            Some(&chld),
23039            "a thread took its own copy: the shared one, and the record, remain"
23040        );
23041        assert!(
23042            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23043            "after a private take the shared copy still ends the call: armed"
23044        );
23045
23046        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, 0);
23047        assert!(
23048            !begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23049            "the shared queue no longer holds it"
23050        );
23051        assert_eq!(
23052            scheduler.shared_queue_scheduler_signals.get(&parent),
23053            Some(&0),
23054            "and the record forgets it"
23055        );
23056
23057        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23058        scheduler.sigtimedwait_sets.insert(parent, chld);
23059        assert!(
23060            !begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23061            "an rt_sigtimedwait set could take it first"
23062        );
23063
23064        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23065        scheduler.signalfd_masks.insert(parent, chld);
23066        assert!(
23067            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23068            "a signalfd covers it, but no other call runs outside the schedule: armed"
23069        );
23070
23071        let reading = |tagged: bool, live: bool| {
23072            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23073            scheduler.signalfd_masks.insert(parent, chld);
23074            let op = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
23075            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(parent, op);
23076            if tagged {
23077                let tag = if live {
23078                    op
23079                } else {
23080                    ExternalOpId::new(parent, 6)
23081                };
23082                scheduler.background_signalfd_reads.insert(parent, tag);
23083            }
23084            (scheduler, creator)
23085        };
23086        let (mut scheduler, creator) = reading(true, true);
23087        assert!(
23088            !begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23089            "a signalfd covers it and a sibling's background call reads a signalfd"
23090        );
23091        let (mut scheduler, creator) = reading(false, false);
23092        assert!(
23093            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23094            "a sibling's background call that reads no signalfd (a select, a vfork): armed"
23095        );
23096        let (mut scheduler, creator) = reading(true, false);
23097        assert!(
23098            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23099            "a signalfd read that has ended, the sibling now in another call: armed"
23100        );
23101
23102        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator) = family(chld, chld);
23103        let other_process = DetTid::from_raw(parent.as_raw() + 100);
23104        let op = ExternalOpId::new(other_process, 7);
23105        scheduler.signalfd_masks.insert(other_process, chld);
23106        scheduler
23107            .blocked
23108            .external_io_blockers
23109            .insert(other_process, op);
23110        scheduler
23111            .background_signalfd_reads
23112            .insert(other_process, op);
23113        assert!(
23114            begin(&mut scheduler, creator, 0),
23115            "another process's signalfd read takes from its own queue: armed"
23116        );
23117    }
23118
23119    /// Commit `thread`'s request to begin a blocking call outside the runnable
23120    /// set, as step3 does, with `mask` the call's own temporary mask.
23121    fn commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23122        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
23123        thread: DetTid,
23124        rid: ResourceID,
23125        mask: Option<u64>,
23126    ) {
23127        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(thread);
23128        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(thread), Some(thread));
23129        assert!(
23130            scheduler
23131                .block_for_one_resource(thread, &rid, &Permission::RW, None, mask, &Ivar::new())
23132                .is_err()
23133        );
23134    }
23135
23136    /// A thread sleeping in `rt_sigsuspend` or in other IO outside the runnable
23137    /// set is not stopped, so its live mask changes at host-timed moments:
23138    /// `rt_sigsuspend` installs its temporary mask only after the scheduler
23139    /// released the thread. The `SIGCHLD` target is chosen from the mask the
23140    /// scheduler recorded when it committed the call, the call's own mask or
23141    /// else the mask read while the thread was still stopped at its request.
23142    /// Before, the live mask was read when the child died, so whether the
23143    /// creator or a sibling parked in a precise futex wait took the signal
23144    /// depended on host timing; the target is also the thread a `ChildExit`
23145    /// timer signals (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
23146    #[test]
23147    fn a_sigchld_target_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_uses_the_mask_recorded_at_its_commit() {
23148        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
23149        let blocking = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
23150            blocked,
23151            ..signal_state(chld, 0)
23152        };
23153        let family_with_parked_sibling = || {
23154            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23155            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
23156            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
23157            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
23158            park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, sibling, chld);
23159            // The leader runs with SIGCHLD blocked, and so does the creator
23160            // until its call installs a mask of its own.
23161            scheduler
23162                .test_kernel_signal_states
23163                .insert(parent, blocking(chld));
23164            scheduler
23165                .test_kernel_signal_states
23166                .insert(creator, blocking(chld));
23167            (scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling)
23168        };
23169
23170        // The creator suspends with an rt_sigsuspend mask that unblocks SIGCHLD.
23171        // Whether or not the host has installed that mask yet, the creator takes
23172        // the signal, so the sibling's precise futex wait is left alone.
23173        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
23174        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23175        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23176            &mut scheduler,
23177            creator,
23178            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
23179            Some(0),
23180        );
23181        assert_eq!(
23182            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
23183            Some(&op)
23184        );
23185        assert_eq!(
23186            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
23187            Some(&Some(0))
23188        );
23189        for live in [chld, 0] {
23190            scheduler
23191                .test_kernel_signal_states
23192                .insert(creator, blocking(live));
23193            assert_eq!(
23194                scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23195                Some(creator)
23196            );
23197        }
23198        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
23199        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
23200        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
23201
23202        // Other external IO sleeps under the thread's own mask, read while it is
23203        // still stopped at its request: SIGCHLD blocked. A later change of its
23204        // live mask does not make it the target. The sibling is the target, but
23205        // its wait holds SIGCHLD, so it stays parked.
23206        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
23207        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23208            &mut scheduler,
23209            creator,
23210            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 2)),
23211            None,
23212        );
23213        assert_eq!(
23214            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
23215            Some(&Some(chld))
23216        );
23217        scheduler
23218            .test_kernel_signal_states
23219            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
23220        assert_eq!(
23221            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23222            Some(sibling)
23223        );
23224        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
23225        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
23226        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
23227        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(sibling).is_empty());
23228
23229        // A mask that could not be recorded is not a target, whatever the live
23230        // one says, and the record goes when the thread leaves its pool.
23231        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
23232        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23233            &mut scheduler,
23234            creator,
23235            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 3)),
23236            Some(0),
23237        );
23238        scheduler
23239            .blocked
23240            .out_of_scheduler_masks
23241            .insert(creator, None);
23242        scheduler
23243            .test_kernel_signal_states
23244            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
23245        assert_eq!(
23246            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23247            Some(sibling)
23248        );
23249        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&creator);
23250        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
23251        assert_eq!(
23252            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23253            Some(creator)
23254        );
23255    }
23256
23257    /// The creator is stopped at a request without blocking `SIGCHLD` while a
23258    /// sibling sleeps in an `rt_sigsuspend` whose mask lets it through. The
23259    /// kernel passes over a thread in a ptrace stop, so it gives the signal to
23260    /// the sibling and wakes it: the sibling is the target, and the signal the
23261    /// `ChildExit` timer sends it arms it for the release barrier. Before, the
23262    /// creator was named and the sibling not armed, so whether it took the
23263    /// signal before the creator resumed from a sleep virtual time ended was
23264    /// host-timed (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237>). The
23265    /// creator is named as before when the sibling's mask blocks `SIGCHLD`,
23266    /// and when the sibling is in other external IO: a `ppoll` that returned
23267    /// has restored its own mask, and a vfork parent's sleep is not woken.
23268    #[test]
23269    fn a_sigchld_goes_to_a_sibling_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_before_a_stopped_creator() {
23270        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
23271        for (sigsuspend, sleeping_mask, sibling_takes) in
23272            [(true, 0, true), (true, chld, false), (false, 0, false)]
23273        {
23274            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23275            scheduler
23276                .test_kernel_signal_states
23277                .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
23278            scheduler
23279                .test_kernel_signal_states
23280                .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
23281            let op = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1);
23282            let rid = if sigsuspend {
23283                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op)
23284            } else {
23285                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
23286            };
23287            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, parent, rid, Some(sleeping_mask));
23288            let expected = if sibling_takes { parent } else { creator };
23289            assert_eq!(
23290                scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23291                Some(expected),
23292                "rt_sigsuspend {sigsuspend}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
23293            );
23294            if sibling_takes {
23295                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(parent, Signal::SIGCHLD);
23296                assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&parent));
23297                assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
23298            }
23299        }
23300    }
23301
23302    /// Under targeted chaos, the random thread is only the one the kernel
23303    /// tries first: a `ChildExit` send still goes to the `rt_sigsuspend`
23304    /// sibling the kernel wakes, whichever thread chaos draws. Before, the
23305    /// draw replaced the kernel's choice, so it could name the stopped creator
23306    /// while the kernel woke the sibling, which nothing armed. With the
23307    /// sibling's mask blocking `SIGCHLD`, every draw ends at the creator (the
23308    /// Codex review of
23309    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
23310    #[test]
23311    fn targeted_chaos_does_not_replace_the_kernels_child_exit_target() {
23312        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
23313        for (sleeping_mask, sibling_takes) in [(0, true), (chld, false)] {
23314            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23315            scheduler.chaos_target_races = true;
23316            scheduler
23317                .test_kernel_signal_states
23318                .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
23319            scheduler
23320                .test_kernel_signal_states
23321                .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
23322            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23323                &mut scheduler,
23324                parent,
23325                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1)),
23326                Some(sleeping_mask),
23327            );
23328            let expected = if sibling_takes { parent } else { creator };
23329            for draw in 0..16 {
23330                assert_eq!(
23331                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
23332                    expected,
23333                    "draw {draw}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
23334                );
23335            }
23336        }
23337    }
23338
23339    /// A guest's signal that the drain places on an `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper
23340    /// arms it, and the pass then ends before a due `ChildExit` timer pops:
23341    /// the timer chooses its target only after the release barrier has
23342    /// requeued that thread. Otherwise the timer could name the sleeper, which
23343    /// the kernel skips because a signal is already pending for it, while the
23344    /// kernel woke another sleeper that nothing armed (the Codex review of
23345    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
23346    #[test]
23347    fn a_drain_that_arms_a_sleeper_ends_the_pass_before_a_child_exit_timer() {
23348        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
23349        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23350        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23351            &mut scheduler,
23352            parent,
23353            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1)),
23354            Some(0),
23355        );
23356        let deadline = scheduler.committed_time;
23357        scheduler
23358            .blocked
23359            .timed_waiters
23360            .insert_child_exit(deadline, child, parent, creator);
23361        scheduler.committed_time = deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
23362        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(parent, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
23363
23364        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
23365        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&parent));
23366        assert_eq!(
23367            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(),
23368            1,
23369            "the ChildExit timer must not pop in the pass that armed the sleeper"
23370        );
23371    }
23372
23373    /// A signal the scheduler sends while a thread is still stopped at its
23374    /// `rt_sigsuspend` request reaches the call: the thread may block it now,
23375    /// but the call's temporary mask does not, so the kernel delivers it as
23376    /// soon as the call starts. Committing the call arms the thread for the
23377    /// release barrier, which waits for its signal stop, as for a signal sent
23378    /// after the commit. Before, the thread entered the pool as a sleeper no
23379    /// signal could reach, and the next pass reported a deadlock. That is how
23380    /// dash's `wait` failed: a `ChildExit` timer fired between its
23381    /// `wait4(WNOHANG)` and its `rt_sigsuspend`, while it blocked every signal.
23382    /// A signal the temporary mask blocks arms nothing.
23383    #[test]
23384    fn a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
23385        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
23386        for (temporary_mask, armed) in [(0, true), (chld, false)] {
23387            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23388            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
23389            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
23390            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
23391            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
23392            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
23393            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
23394            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
23395
23396            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
23397            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
23398            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23399                &mut scheduler,
23400                creator,
23401                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
23402                Some(temporary_mask),
23403            );
23404            assert_eq!(
23405                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
23406                Some(&op)
23407            );
23408            assert_eq!(
23409                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
23410                armed,
23411                "temporary mask {temporary_mask:#x}"
23412            );
23413            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator), armed);
23414            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty());
23415        }
23416    }
23417
23418    /// A guest's signal to a thread asleep in a real `rt_sigsuspend`
23419    /// (`kill`, `tgkill` and `tkill` report it with `notify_signal_pending`)
23420    /// is placed at the next drain as a signal the scheduler sends is: the
23421    /// thread is armed for the release barrier when its sleeping mask lets the
23422    /// signal through, and not when it blocks it; a thread still stopped at
23423    /// its `rt_sigsuspend` request gets the record its grant arms. Before, such
23424    /// a signal was not recorded at all, the scheduler did not wait for the
23425    /// wake's signal stop, and on a slow host it reported a deadlock first.
23426    ///
23427    /// A realtime signal is placed the same way: `nix` cannot name it, and the
23428    /// drain used to drop it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941).
23429    /// SIGKILL arms too, although it has no delivery stop under ptrace: the
23430    /// arm is cleared when the thread's exit is processed
23431    /// (`a_sigkill_arm_on_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_ends_with_its_exit`), and
23432    /// without it the killed sleeper would count as unwakeable until then.
23433    #[test]
23434    fn a_guest_signal_to_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_arms_the_release_barrier() {
23435        let usr1 = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
23436        let realtime = SigWrapper(35);
23437        let kill = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL);
23438        for (signal, sleeping_mask, armed) in [
23439            (usr1, 0, true),
23440            (usr1, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1), false),
23441            (realtime, 0, true),
23442            (realtime, kernel_signal_bit(35), false),
23443            (kill, 0, true),
23444        ] {
23445            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23446            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23447                &mut scheduler,
23448                creator,
23449                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 5)),
23450                Some(sleeping_mask),
23451            );
23452            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
23453            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
23454            assert_eq!(
23455                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
23456                armed,
23457                "signal {signal}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
23458            );
23459        }
23460
23461        for signal in [usr1, realtime, kill] {
23462            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23463            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
23464            request.insert(
23465                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 6)),
23466                Permission::RW,
23467            );
23468            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
23469            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
23470            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
23471            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
23472            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
23473            assert_eq!(
23474                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
23475                Some(&signal),
23476                "signal {signal}"
23477            );
23478        }
23479    }
23480
23481    /// The SIGKILL policy of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941: a
23482    /// guest's SIGKILL to a thread asleep in `rt_sigsuspend` arms it like any
23483    /// signal its mask admits (the installed mask can never block SIGKILL).
23484    /// There is no delivery stop to wait for; the thread exits, and processing
23485    /// that exit clears the arm (`remove_blocking_entries`), so the release
23486    /// barrier does not wait past it.
23487    #[test]
23488    fn a_sigkill_arm_on_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_ends_with_its_exit() {
23489        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23490        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23491            &mut scheduler,
23492            creator,
23493            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 5)),
23494            Some(0),
23495        );
23496        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL));
23497        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
23498        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
23499        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&creator);
23500        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
23501        assert!(
23502            !scheduler
23503                .blocked
23504                .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
23505                .contains_key(&creator)
23506        );
23507    }
23508
23509    /// A scheduler that does not model signal targets (`models_signal_targets`)
23510    /// neither reads a committed thread's sleeping mask from `/proc` nor records
23511    /// one. Nothing on such a scheduler consumes the record, and on a backend
23512    /// whose `DetTid` is not a host thread ID the read would name an unrelated
23513    /// host thread or none. The gated scheduler, for contrast, records the
23514    /// call's own mask, or else reads the thread's
23515    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
23516    /// A background call whose temporary mask its turn cannot vouch for
23517    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`: a pselect6 in record and
23518    /// replay) has no recorded sleeping mask, so a committed signal never arms
23519    /// it, whatever the thread's ordinary mask, and it is not a `SIGCHLD`
23520    /// target. Taking the ordinary mask for such a call armed it for a SIGALRM
23521    /// the call's own mask blocks, and the release barrier waited for a wake
23522    /// Linux never delivers (Codex review of
23523    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3989). The same call without the
23524    /// flag is armed, from the ordinary mask read while it was stopped.
23525    #[test]
23526    fn a_background_call_with_an_unknown_sleeping_mask_is_never_armed() {
23527        for unknown in [false, true] {
23528            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23529            // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
23530            scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
23531            scheduler
23532                .test_kernel_signal_states
23533                .insert(creator, signal_state(0, 0));
23534            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23535            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
23536            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op), Permission::RW);
23537            request.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = unknown;
23538            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
23539            assert_eq!(
23540                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
23541                Some(creator)
23542            );
23543            assert!(
23544                scheduler
23545                    .step4_resource_block(creator, &request, &Ivar::new())
23546                    .is_err()
23547            );
23548            assert_eq!(
23549                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
23550                Some(&op)
23551            );
23552            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGALRM);
23553            let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
23554            let armed = scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator);
23555            if unknown {
23556                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&None));
23557                assert!(!armed);
23558                assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_signal_mask(creator), None);
23559            } else {
23560                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(0)));
23561                assert!(armed);
23562            }
23563        }
23564    }

23566    /// A thread released into a background `rt_sigsuspend` whose temporary
23567    /// mask differs from its own holds every later turn and timer pop until
23568    /// its kernel mask shows the temporary one, or its call has left the
23569    /// blocked pool. Before, the scheduler went on at once, and the
23570    /// process-directed `SIGALRM` of a timer wake, which the thread's own mask
23571    /// leaves unblocked, could reach it on its way into the kernel or not, as
23572    /// host timing decided (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3993).
23573    /// A call that sleeps under the thread's own mask needs no barrier.
23574    #[test]
23575    fn a_background_call_with_a_temporary_mask_holds_the_schedule_until_the_kernel_installs_it() {
23576        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
23577        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
23578        let masked = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
23579            blocked,
23580            ..signal_state(0, 0)
23581        };
23582        for (own, installed_then_left) in [(alrm, None), (usr1, Some(true)), (usr1, Some(false))] {
23583            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23584            scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
23585            scheduler
23586                .test_kernel_signal_states
23587                .insert(creator, masked(own));
23588            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23589            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23590                &mut scheduler,
23591                creator,
23592                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
23593                Some(alrm),
23594            );
23595            let case = format!("own={own:#x} installed_then_left={installed_then_left:?}");
23596            let Some(installed) = installed_then_left else {
23597                assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.is_empty(), "{case}");
23598                assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{case}");
23599                continue;
23600            };
23601            // Still on its way into the kernel, under its own mask.
23602            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{case}");
23603            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{case}");
23604            if installed {
23605                scheduler
23606                    .test_kernel_signal_states
23607                    .insert(creator, masked(alrm));
23608            } else {
23609                // The call ended before the mask was seen, as when a pending
23610                // signal ended it at once and its continuation was granted.
23611                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&creator);
23612            }
23613            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{case}");
23614            assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.is_empty(), "{case}");
23615        }
23616    }

23618    /// A live thread released into a background call whose kernel mask cannot
23619    /// be read has not proved its entry, and holds its barrier: a read error
23620    /// is not evidence that the thread is gone (Codex review of
23621    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053, whose regression this is).
23622    /// The test thread is a real, live identity; one read returns EIO through
23623    /// the read seam.
23624    #[test]
23625    fn a_live_thread_whose_mask_cannot_be_read_holds_its_background_entry() {
23626        use std::cell::Cell;
23627        use std::rc::Rc;
23628
23629        use crate::syscalls::signal_state_read_seam;
23630
23631        let (mut scheduler, thread, own, temporary) = live_background_entry_scheduler(None);
23632        assert_eq!(
23633            scheduler
23634                .background_entry_barriers
23635                .get(&thread)
23636                .map(|entry| entry.mask),
23637            Some(temporary)
23638        );
23639        let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(std::process::id() as i32);
23640        let tid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw());
23641        let reads = Rc::new(Cell::new(0));
23642        let observed = reads.clone();
23643        let seam = signal_state_read_seam::install(move |_, _| {
23644            observed.set(observed.get() + 1);
23645            Some(Err(reverie::Errno::EIO))
23646        });
23647        let result = scheduler.step2_drain_prefix();
23648        drop(seam);
23649        assert_eq!(
23650            reads.get(),
23651            1,
23652            "the entry proof read takes the injected error"
23653        );
23654        assert!(!thread_is_gone(pid, tid));
23655        assert_eq!(read_kernel_signal_state(pid, tid).unwrap().blocked, own);
23656        assert!(
23657            result.is_err(),
23658            "a live thread with no observed temporary mask keeps the barrier"
23659        );
23660        assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.contains_key(&thread));
23661        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
23662    }

23664    /// An own mask that cannot be read when the scheduler grants the call is no
23665    /// proof that it equals the temporary mask, so the barrier is armed (Codex
23666    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
23667    #[test]
23668    fn an_unreadable_own_mask_at_the_grant_still_arms_the_entry_barrier() {
23669        let (scheduler, thread, _own, temporary) =
23670            live_background_entry_scheduler(Some(reverie::Errno::EIO));
23671        assert_eq!(
23672            scheduler
23673                .background_entry_barriers
23674                .get(&thread)
23675                .map(|entry| entry.mask),
23676            Some(temporary)
23677        );
23678    }
