23680    /// An entry that stays unproved, neither entered nor left, past
23681    /// `background_entry_valve` ends the run with a named refusal instead of
23682    /// holding every turn forever (Codex review of
23683    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
23684    #[test]
23685    fn an_unproved_background_entry_ends_the_run_by_name_after_the_valve() {
23686        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
23687        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
23688        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23689        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
23690        scheduler.background_entry_valve = Duration::ZERO;
23691        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
23692            creator,
23693            KernelSignalState {
23694                blocked: usr1,
23695                ..signal_state(0, 0)
23696            },
23697        );
23698        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23699            &mut scheduler,
23700            creator,
23701            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
23702            Some(alrm),
23703        );
23704        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
23705        let reason = scheduler
23706            .terminal_deadlock
23707            .clone()
23708            .expect("the unproved entry ends the run");
23709        assert!(reason.starts_with("HERMIT_DEADLOCK:"), "{reason}");
23710        assert!(reason.contains("neither entered it"), "{reason}");
23711    }

23713    /// A scheduler with the calling test thread, a real and live identity,
23714    /// granted a background `rt_sigsuspend` under a temporary mask that differs
23715    /// from its actual one. `own_read_error` makes the grant's own-mask read
23716    /// fail. Returns the scheduler, the thread, its actual mask and the
23717    /// temporary mask.
23718    fn live_background_entry_scheduler(
23719        own_read_error: Option<reverie::Errno>,
23720    ) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, u64, u64) {
23721        use crate::syscalls::signal_state_read_seam;
23722
23723        let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(std::process::id() as i32);
23724        // SAFETY: gettid takes no arguments and changes nothing.
23725        let tid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 });
23726        assert!(!thread_is_gone(pid, tid));
23727        let own = read_kernel_signal_state(pid, tid)
23728            .expect("the test thread's signal state is readable")
23729            .blocked;
23730        let temporary = own ^ kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
23731        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(pid.as_raw());
23732        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(tid.as_raw());
23733        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
23734        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
23735        if thread != leader {
23736            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, thread, false);
23737        }
23738        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
23739        let seam = own_read_error
23740            .map(|errno| signal_state_read_seam::install(move |_, _| Some(Err(errno))));
23741        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23742            &mut scheduler,
23743            thread,
23744            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(thread, 1)),
23745            Some(temporary),
23746        );
23747        drop(seam);
23748        (scheduler, thread, own, temporary)
23749    }

23751    #[test]
23752    fn a_scheduler_that_does_not_model_signal_targets_reads_and_records_no_sleeping_mask() {
23753        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
23754        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
23755        for models in [false, true] {
23756            for (seq, rt_sigsuspend, call_mask) in [(1, false, None), (2, true, Some(0))] {
23757                let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23758                scheduler.models_signal_targets = models;
23759                scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
23760                    creator,
23761                    KernelSignalState {
23762                        blocked: chld,
23763                        ..signal_state(chld, 0)
23764                    },
23765                );
23766                let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, seq);
23767                let rid = if rt_sigsuspend {
23768                    ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op)
23769                } else {
23770                    ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
23771                };
23772                let before = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
23773                commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, call_mask);
23774                let reads = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed) - before;
23775                let case = format!("models={models} rt_sigsuspend={rt_sigsuspend}");
23776
23777                // Either way the thread sleeps in its pool.
23778                let pool = if rt_sigsuspend {
23779                    &scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers
23780                } else {
23781                    &scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers
23782                };
23783                assert_eq!(pool.get(&creator), Some(&op), "{case}");
23784                let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
23785                if models {
23786                    assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(call_mask.unwrap_or(chld))), "{case}");
23787                    // The thread's own mask, read once: it is the sleeping mask
23788                    // of a call without one, and decides whether a call with
23789                    // one needs an entry barrier.
23790                    assert_eq!(reads, 1, "{case}");
23791                } else {
23792                    assert_eq!(recorded, None, "{case}");
23793                    assert!(
23794                        scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty(),
23795                        "{case}"
23796                    );
23797                    assert_eq!(reads, 0, "{case}");
23798                }
23799            }
23800        }
23801    }
23802
23803    /// Post `signal`'s delivery stop for `thread`, as its backend does when the
23804    /// kernel wakes it for the signal.
23805    fn post_inbound_signal(
23806        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
23807        thread: DetTid,
23808        signal: libc::c_int,
23809        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
23810    ) {
23811        let req = scheduler.next_turns.get(&thread).unwrap().req.clone();
23812        let mut delivered = Resources::new(thread);
23813        delivered.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(signal)), Permission::W);
23814        scheduler.request_put(&req, delivered, global_time);
23815    }
23816
23817    /// A committed signal to a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
23818    /// the run queue, on a traced backend, counterfeits no request for it: its
23819    /// request was consumed when it was backgrounded. The thread is armed, and
23820    /// every scheduler pass is empty until the delivery stop the signal
23821    /// provokes is posted; the next pass then requeues it, before anything
23822    /// else, and its `SIGCHLD` delivery is granted rather than deferred behind
23823    /// a runnable sibling. Before, a debug build asserted here and a release
23824    /// build counterfeited a request for a thread still in its pool
23825    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
23826    #[test]
23827    fn a_signal_to_a_thread_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_is_requeued_after_its_own_stop() {
23828        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
23829        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23830        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23831        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23832            &mut scheduler,
23833            creator,
23834            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
23835            Some(0),
23836        );
23837        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
23838
23839        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
23840        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
23841        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
23842        assert!(
23843            scheduler
23844                .next_turns
23845                .get(&creator)
23846                .unwrap()
23847                .req
23848                .try_read()
23849                .is_none()
23850        );
23851        assert_eq!(
23852            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
23853            Some(&op)
23854        );
23855        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
23856
23857        // The kernel has not delivered yet: every pass is empty.
23858        for _ in 0..3 {
23859            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
23860            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
23861        }
23862
23863        // The thread's own stop posts its continuation; the next pass requeues it.
23864        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
23865        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
23866        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
23867        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
23868        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
23869        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
23870        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
23871
23872        // Its delivery commits although the leader is runnable.
23873        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
23874        assert_eq!(
23875            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
23876            Some(creator)
23877        );
23878        assert!(
23879            scheduler
23880                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
23881                .is_ok()
23882        );
23883        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
23884    }
23885
23886    /// On a scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
23887    /// DBT, KVM), a committed signal to a thread asleep in a call outside the
23888    /// scheduler (a blocking external call, or a vfork parent waiting for its
23889    /// child) neither arms the thread nor counterfeits a request: the thread
23890    /// stays in its pool, awaiting its own continuation. Before, a debug build
23891    /// panicked here ("thread should be parked in the scheduler"). In-guest
23892    /// LiteInst hit it when a vfork child's exit signalled the parent it had
23893    /// just killed, and the panic poisoned the scheduler and hung the run.
23894    #[test]
23895    fn a_signal_to_a_backgrounded_thread_on_a_scheduler_without_signal_targets_waits_for_its_continuation()
23896     {
23897        for vfork in [false, true] {
23898            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23899            scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
23900            assert!(!scheduler.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls);
23901            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23902            let rid = if vfork {
23903                ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op)
23904            } else {
23905                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
23906            };
23907            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, None);
23908            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
23909
23910            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
23911            let case = format!("vfork={vfork}");
23912            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
23913            assert!(
23914                scheduler
23915                    .next_turns
23916                    .get(&creator)
23917                    .unwrap()
23918                    .req
23919                    .try_read()
23920                    .is_none(),
23921                "{case}: a request was counterfeited"
23922            );
23923            assert_eq!(
23924                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
23925                Some(&op),
23926                "{case}"
23927            );
23928            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
23929            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent), "{case}");
23930        }
23931    }

23933    /// When the release barrier's watchdog expires with an armed thread that
23934    /// has still not posted its continuation, the barrier must not drop the
23935    /// arm and resume scheduling: that would leave the thread for `step2c` to
23936    /// harvest behind runnable siblings, an admission order that host delivery
23937    /// time decides. The watchdog's start is backdated here (an injected clock),
23938    /// so the production bound needs no test knob.
23939    #[test]
23940    fn an_expired_release_barrier_keeps_the_arm_and_refuses_the_run() {
23941        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
23942        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
23943        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
23944            &mut scheduler,
23945            creator,
23946            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
23947            Some(0),
23948        );
23949        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
23950        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
23951        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
23952
23953        // The first empty pass starts the watchdog.
23954        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
23955        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
23956        scheduler.signaled_background_since = Some(
23957            std::time::Instant::now()
23958                .checked_sub(Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE + Duration::from_secs(1))
23959                .expect("the monotonic clock has run longer than the watchdog bound"),
23960        );
23961
23962        // Expired: the pass is still refused, the arm and the pool entry stay,
23963        // and nothing is requeued for a later harvest.
23964        for _ in 0..2 {
23965            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
23966            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
23967            assert_eq!(
23968                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
23969                Some(&op)
23970            );
23971            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
23972        }
23973        // The typed refusal names the thread, and the scheduler loop ends the
23974        // run with it rather than scheduling on.
23975        let refusal = scheduler
23976            .signaled_background_refusal
23977            .take()
23978            .expect("an expired barrier records a typed refusal");
23979        assert_eq!(refusal.unposted, vec![creator]);
23980        assert!(refusal.waited >= Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE);
23981        assert!(
23982            refusal
23983                .to_string()
23984                .starts_with("hermit refused to continue the run")
23985        );
23986        // A whole pass is refused as well, so step2c cannot harvest the thread.
23987        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
23988        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
23989        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
23990        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_refusal.is_some());
23991    }
23992
23993    /// Armed threads are released together, only once every one has posted,
23994    /// in an order fixed by thread ID alone: the barrier pushes them in
23995    /// ascending DetTid order to the front of the run queue (as `step2e` admits
23996    /// deferred parents), so the highest DetTid runs first. Which stop the host
23997    /// reports first does not decide the order: both posting orders give the
23998    /// same run-queue order. A thread that leaves its pool another way (here it
23999    /// exits) is dropped rather than waited for.
24000    #[test]
24001    fn signaled_background_threads_are_released_together_in_thread_id_order() {
24002        for creator_posts_first in [false, true] {
24003            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
24004            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24005            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
24006            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
24007            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
24008            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24009                &mut scheduler,
24010                creator,
24011                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
24012                Some(0),
24013            );
24014            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24015                &mut scheduler,
24016                sibling,
24017                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(sibling, 1)),
24018                Some(0),
24019            );
24020            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24021                &mut scheduler,
24022                child,
24023                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(child, 1)),
24024                Some(0),
24025            );
24026            for thread in [sibling, child, creator] {
24027                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(thread, Signal::SIGUSR1);
24028            }
24029            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.len(), 3);
24030            assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.is_empty());
24031
24032            let (first, last) = if creator_posts_first {
24033                (creator, sibling)
24034            } else {
24035                (sibling, creator)
24036            };
24037            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, first, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
24038            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
24039            scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
24040            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
24041            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(first));
24042            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
24043
24044            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, last, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
24045            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
24046            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
24047            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
24048            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(sibling));
24049            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), sibling);
24050            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(creator));
24051            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), creator);
24052            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(child));
24053            assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
24054            assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
24055            assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
24056        }
24057    }
24058
24059    /// A signal that does not wake a background call at a known point arms
24060    /// nothing and counterfeits nothing: the thread stays in its pool for
24061    /// `step2c` to harvest. That is a vfork parent, which sleeps killable, and
24062    /// a thread whose recorded sleeping mask blocks the signal or is unknown.
24063    #[test]
24064    fn a_signal_that_cannot_wake_a_background_call_leaves_it_in_its_pool() {
24065        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
24066        let cases: [(&str, Option<u64>, bool); 3] = [
24067            ("vfork parent", Some(0), true),
24068            ("blocked", Some(chld), false),
24069            ("unknown mask", None, false),
24070        ];
24071        for (case, mask, vfork_parent) in cases {
24072            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24073            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
24074            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24075                &mut scheduler,
24076                creator,
24077                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
24078                Some(0),
24079            );
24080            scheduler
24081                .blocked
24082                .out_of_scheduler_masks
24083                .insert(creator, mask);
24084            if vfork_parent {
24085                scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
24086            }
24087            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
24088            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
24089            assert!(
24090                !scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator),
24091                "{case}"
24092            );
24093            assert_eq!(
24094                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
24095                Some(&op),
24096                "{case}"
24097            );
24098            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
24099            assert!(
24100                scheduler
24101                    .next_turns
24102                    .get(&creator)
24103                    .unwrap()
24104                    .req
24105                    .try_read()
24106                    .is_none(),
24107                "{case}"
24108            );
24109            assert!(
24110                scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok(),
24111                "{case}"
24112            );
24113        }
24114    }
24115
24116    /// A signal another guest sends in its own turn (`notify_signal_pending`)
24117    /// while a thread is still stopped at its posted `rt_sigsuspend` request
24118    /// reaches the call, as a timer's send at that point does
24119    /// (`a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes`):
24120    /// the send is queued, the step2 drain notes it without arming anything,
24121    /// and committing the call arms the thread for the release barrier. A
24122    /// signal the temporary mask blocks is not noted, and nothing arms. Coverage
24123    /// of main: its drain notes the send
24124    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
24125    /// note.
24126    #[test]
24127    fn a_sibling_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
24128        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
24129        // Realtime signals and SIGKILL follow the policy of
24130        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941: a realtime signal the
24131        // mask admits is noted and armed like a standard one; SIGKILL is too.
24132        for (case, signal, temporary_mask, armed) in [
24133            ("admitted", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1), 0, true),
24134            ("realtime admitted", SigWrapper(35), 0, true),
24135            (
24136                "realtime blocked",
24137                SigWrapper(35),
24138                kernel_signal_bit(35),
24139                false,
24140            ),
24141            ("blocked", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1), usr1, false),
24142            ("SIGKILL", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL), 0, true),
24143        ] {
24144            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24145            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
24146            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
24147            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
24148            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
24149            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
24150            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
24151            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
24152
24153            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
24154            assert_eq!(
24155                scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.get(&creator),
24156                Some(&vec![signal]),
24157                "{case}"
24158            );
24159            assert!(
24160                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
24161                "{case}"
24162            );
24163            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
24164            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
24165            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
24166            assert_eq!(
24167                scheduler
24168                    .blocked
24169                    .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
24170                    .get(&creator)
24171                    .copied(),
24172                armed.then_some(signal),
24173                "{case}"
24174            );
24175            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator), "{case}");
24176            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24177                &mut scheduler,
24178                creator,
24179                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
24180                Some(temporary_mask),
24181            );
24182            assert_eq!(
24183                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
24184                Some(&op),
24185                "{case}"
24186            );
24187            assert_eq!(
24188                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
24189                armed,
24190                "{case}"
24191            );
24192            assert!(
24193                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
24194                "{case}"
24195            );
24196        }
24197    }
24198
24199    /// A signal a sibling sends while the waiter's `rt_sigsuspend` request is
24200    /// posted but not yet granted is delivered by the kernel as soon as the
24201    /// granted call installs its temporary mask, and the waiter's delivery stop
24202    /// is its report. The step2 drain notes the send and granting the request
24203    /// arms the waiter, so every pass is empty until that stop is posted, and
24204    /// the release barrier then requeues the waiter ahead of the runnable
24205    /// sibling: no sibling runs between the grant and the waiter's return.
24206    /// Coverage of main: its drain notes the send
24207    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
24208    /// note. Adapted from https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3224, where a
24209    /// hold on every other thread gave this order.
24210    #[tokio::test]
24211    async fn a_sibling_signal_sent_before_the_rt_sigsuspend_grant_requeues_the_waiter_first() {
24212        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
24213        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24214        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
24215        let rid = ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op);
24216        let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
24217        request.insert(rid.clone(), Permission::RW);
24218        request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
24219        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&creator].req.clone();
24220        scheduler.request_put(&req, request, &global_time);
24221        // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
24222        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
24223
24224        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1));
24225        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
24226        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
24227        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
24228        assert_eq!(
24229            scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
24230            Some(&SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1))
24231        );
24232
24233        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
24234        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, Some(0));
24235        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&parent].req.clone();
24236        scheduler.request_put(&req, Resources::new(parent), &global_time);
24237        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
24238        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(scheduler));
24239        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
24240
24241        for _ in 0..3 {
24242            let pass = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
24243            assert!(pass.is_err(), "the sibling ran before the waiter reported");
24244            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24245            assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
24246            assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
24247        }
24248        post_inbound_signal(
24249            &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
24250            creator,
24251            libc::SIGUSR1,
24252            &global_time,
24253        );
24254        let turn = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last)
24255            .await
24256            .expect("the waiter's delivery turn");
24257        assert_eq!(turn.tid, creator);
24258        assert!(
24259            turn.resources
24260                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1)))
24261        );
24262        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24263        assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
24264        assert!(s.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
24265        assert!(s.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
24266    }

24268    /// The invariant that guards the counterfeit request still holds for every
24269    /// thread outside the background pools: a signaled thread there must be
24270    /// parked at a posted request.
24271    #[test]
24272    #[should_panic(expected = "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler")]
24273    fn a_signal_to_an_unposted_thread_outside_the_background_pools_still_asserts() {
24274        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24275        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
24276    }

24278    /// The resources of `thread`'s posted request, or `None` while it has
24279    /// posted nothing.
24280    fn request_resources(scheduler: &Scheduler, thread: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<ResourceID>> {
24281        scheduler.next_turns[&thread]
24282            .req
24283            .try_read()
24284            .map(|request| request.unwrap().resources.keys().cloned().collect())
24285    }

24287    /// A synthesized `SIGCHLD` that reaches a vfork parent still inside its real
24288    /// vfork (its request is empty) arms nothing and counterfeits nothing. A
24289    /// vfork parent sleeps killable, so the signal stays pending; a counterfeit
24290    /// request would put a thread that cannot answer on the run queue and lose
24291    /// the continuation that releases the vfork barrier. Once the child has
24292    /// exited, the parent's own continuation arrives and the ordinary barrier
24293    /// and blocker paths return it to the run queue.
24294    #[test]
24295    fn child_exit_signal_leaves_vfork_parent_waiting_for_its_continuation() {
24296        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24297        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
24298        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24299            &mut scheduler,
24300            creator,
24301            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
24302            Some(0),
24303        );
24304        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
24305
24306        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
24307
24308        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
24309        assert_eq!(
24310            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
24311            Some(&op)
24312        );
24313        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
24314        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, creator), None);
24315
24316        let mut continuation = Resources::new(creator);
24317        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op), Permission::RW);
24318        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
24319        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
24320        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
24321        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
24322        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
24323        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
24324        assert_eq!(
24325            request_resources(&scheduler, creator),
24326            Some(vec![ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op)])
24327        );
24328    }

24331    /// posted neither replaces that continuation nor requeues the parent ahead

24391    /// `rt_sigsuspend` completes only through a signal. A signal its recorded
24392    /// mask admits arms the waiter without counterfeiting a request: the waiter
24393    /// rejoins the run queue only with the `InboundSignal` report it posts
24394    /// itself, and that report is what it runs with.

24425    /// Only a backend whose blocked waits are interrupted by the kernel's
24426    /// signal state (`supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`)

24429    /// RPC, the waiter stays in its pool, unarmed, with its request empty.
24430    #[test]

24432        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {

24436        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24437        assert!(!scheduler.models_signal_targets);

24440        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
24441        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24442            &mut scheduler,

24445            Some(0),

24459    /// A signal the waiter's temporary mask blocks cannot end its
24460    /// `rt_sigsuspend`, so it must not arm the waiter: the scheduler would then
24461    /// wait for a report that never comes. Left in its pool, a waiter that
24462    /// nothing else can wake gets the terminal deadlock verdict instead of a
24463    /// hang, and the verdict names the mask.
24464    #[test]
24465    fn signal_blocked_by_the_rt_sigsuspend_mask_leaves_the_wait_in_its_pool() {
24466        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
24467        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
24468        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
24469        let op = ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291);
24470        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
24471        let alarm_bit = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
24472        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24473            &mut scheduler,
24474            waiter,
24475            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
24476            Some(alarm_bit),
24477        );
24478
24479        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, Signal::SIGALRM);
24480
24481        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
24482        assert_eq!(
24483            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&waiter),
24484            Some(&op)
24485        );
24486        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
24487        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, waiter), None);
24488        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
24489        let report = scheduler
24490            .take_terminal_deadlock()
24491            .expect("a waiter whose mask blocks the only signal is a terminal deadlock");
24492        assert!(
24493            report.contains("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal"),
24494            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
24495        );
24496        assert!(
24497            report.contains(&format!("temporary mask {:#x}", alarm_bit)),
24498            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
24499        );
24500    }
24501
24502    /// The scheduler's sigset bits are the kernel's: signal n is bit n - 1, so
24503    /// realtime signal 64 is bit 63, and a number outside 1..=64 has no bit.
24504    /// The mask recorded for an `rt_sigsuspend` waiter is the one the kernel
24505    /// installs, which never blocks SIGKILL or SIGSTOP (the syscall layer's
24506    /// `kernel_installed_signal_mask`, tested with it). A signal that mask
24507    /// admits arms the waiter; one it blocks does not.
24508    #[test]
24509    fn rt_sigsuspend_mask_uses_kernel_sigset_bits_and_cannot_block_kill_or_stop() {
24510        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
24511        assert_eq!(usr1, 1_u64 << (libc::SIGUSR1 - 1));
24512        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(64), 1_u64 << 63);
24513        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(63), 1_u64 << 62);
24514        for out_of_range in [0, 65, -1, i32::MIN] {
24515            assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(out_of_range), 0, "{out_of_range}");
24516        }
24517        // The widest mask the kernel installs.
24518        let everything = !(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP));
24519        assert_ne!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM), 0);
24520        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL), 0);
24521        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP), 0);
24522
24523        let cases = [
24524            (usr1, Signal::SIGUSR1, false),
24525            (usr1, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
24526            (0, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
24527            (everything, Signal::SIGALRM, false),
24528        ];
24529        for (mask, signal, armed) in cases {
24530            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
24531            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
24532            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
24533            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
24534                &mut scheduler,
24535                waiter,
24536                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291)),
24537                Some(mask),
24538            );
24539            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, signal);
24540            assert_eq!(
24541                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&waiter),
24542                armed,
24543                "mask {mask:#x}, signal {signal}"
24544            );
24545        }
24546    }

24548    /// A child-exit timer whose creator already dequeued the kernel's own
24549    /// `SIGCHLD` for the process, and had that delivery deferred, commits that
24550    /// delivery instead of sending a second signal. Before, only the leader was
24551    /// looked up, so the timer sent again and found the deferred creator in no
24552    /// pool (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
24553    #[test]
24554    fn a_child_exit_timer_commits_a_deferred_creator_delivery_without_sending() {
24555        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
24556        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24557        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
24558        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
24559        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
24560        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
24561        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
24562        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
24563        assert_eq!(
24564            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
24565            Some(creator)
24566        );
24567        assert!(
24568            scheduler
24569                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
24570                .is_err()
24571        );
24572        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&creator));
24573        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
24574
24575        let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
24576        scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
24577            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
24578            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
24579            SignalTarget::Process(creator),
24580            Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
24581            true,
24582            scheduler.committed_time,
24583        );
24584        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, attempts);
24585        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
24586        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
24587        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
24588        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
24589    }

24591    /// What happens to a real-time POSIX timer expiration
24592    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089): kept pending only
24593    /// when every live thread blocks it by a mask the schedule fixes and
24594    /// nothing can observe it, discarded where Linux discards it, and refused
24595    /// otherwise.
24596    fn real_time_family() -> (Scheduler, DetPid, DetTid, DetTid, u64) {
24597        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24598        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
24599        let rt = kernel_signal_bit(35);
24600        for thread in [parent, creator] {
24601            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
24602                thread,
24603                KernelSignalState {
24604                    blocked: rt,
24605                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
24606                },
24607            );
24608        }
24609        (
24610            scheduler,
24611            DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw()),
24612            parent,
24613            creator,
24614            rt,
24615        )
24616    }
24617
24618    #[test]
24619    fn a_real_time_expiration_every_thread_blocks_is_kept_pending() {
24620        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, _creator, rt) = real_time_family();
24621        assert_eq!(
24622            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, SignalTarget::Process(parent), 35),
24623            RealTimeFate::Queued
24624        );
24625        for at in [1, 2] {
24626            scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
24627                LogicalTime::from_nanos(at),
24628                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0),
24629                SignalTarget::Process(parent),
24630                timed_waiters::TimerSignal::RefuseRealTime(35),
24631                true,
24632                scheduler.committed_time,
24633            );
24634        }
24635        // A second expiration of the same signal coalesces into the same bit.
24636        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), rt);
24637        assert_eq!(
24638            scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
24639            0
24640        );
24641        assert!(real_time_expiration_kept_pending());
24642    }

24644    #[test]
24645    fn a_real_time_expiration_one_thread_unblocks_is_deliverable() {
24646        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, creator, _rt) = real_time_family();
24647        scheduler
24648            .test_kernel_signal_states
24649            .insert(creator, signal_state(0, 0));
24650        assert_eq!(
24651            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, SignalTarget::Process(parent), 35),
24652            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
24653        );
24654    }

24656    /// A thread-directed real-time expiration
24657    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164) is judged by its named
24658    /// thread alone: kept pending while that thread blocks it, whatever its
24659    /// siblings do; deliverable when it does not; discarded once it is gone.
24660    #[test]
24661    fn a_thread_directed_real_time_expiration_is_judged_by_its_thread_alone() {
24662        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, creator, _rt) = real_time_family();
24663        scheduler
24664            .test_kernel_signal_states
24665            .insert(parent, signal_state(0, 0));
24666        let fate = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target| {
24667            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, target, 35)
24668        };
24669        assert_eq!(
24670            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Process(creator)),
24671            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
24672        );
24673        assert_eq!(
24674            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(creator)),
24675            RealTimeFate::Queued
24676        );
24677        assert_eq!(
24678            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(parent)),
24679            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
24680        );
24681        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
24682        assert_eq!(
24683            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(creator)),
24684            RealTimeFate::Discarded
24685        );
24686    }

24688    /// `timer_create`'s `sigev_notify_thread_id` must name a live thread of the
24689    /// caller's process, as Linux's `good_sigevent` requires; a caller in a
24690    /// nested PID namespace is answered apart, since its ids are not DetTids
24691    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
24692    #[test]
24693    fn a_sigev_thread_id_timer_names_only_a_live_thread_of_its_process() {
24694        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24695        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
24696        assert_eq!(
24697            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, creator.as_raw()),
24698            PosixTimerThread::Thread(creator)
24699        );
24700        assert_eq!(
24701            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, parent.as_raw()),
24702            PosixTimerThread::Thread(parent)
24703        );
24704        for named in [child.as_raw(), 0, -1, 999] {
24705            assert_eq!(
24706                scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, named),
24707                PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup,
24708                "{named}"
24709            );
24710        }
24711        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
24712        assert_eq!(
24713            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, creator.as_raw()),
24714            PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup
24715        );
24716        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(process);
24717        assert_eq!(
24718            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, parent.as_raw()),
24719            PosixTimerThread::NestedNamespace
24720        );
24721    }

24723    /// A `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` expiration of a standard signal pending on its
24724    /// thread: an overrun when the pending copy is this timer's own and not
24725    /// consumed since, a refusal when it is another source's (another timer,
24726    /// no record) or a poll of the signal may have consumed it unobserved
24727    /// (an `rt_sigtimedwait` set, which also clears the record), and a send
24728    /// once the copy has been taken
24729    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
24730    #[test]
24731    fn a_thread_timer_expiration_beside_a_pending_copy_is_an_overrun_or_a_refusal() {
24732        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24733        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
24734        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
24735        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
24736        let other = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 1);
24737        let pending = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, bits: u64| {
24738            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
24739                creator,
24740                KernelSignalState {
24741                    thread_pending: bits,
24742                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
24743                },
24744            );
24745        };
24746        pending(&mut scheduler, 0);
24747        assert_eq!(
24748            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24749            ThreadTimerSend::Send
24750        );
24751        scheduler
24752            .thread_timer_copies
24753            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
24754        pending(&mut scheduler, usr1);
24755        assert_eq!(
24756            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24757            ThreadTimerSend::Overrun
24758        );
24759        assert!(matches!(
24760            scheduler.thread_timer_send(other, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24761            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("another timer")
24762        ));
24763        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, Some(usr1));
24764        assert!(matches!(
24765            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24766            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("rt_sigtimedwait")
24767        ));
24768        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, None);
24769        assert!(matches!(
24770            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24771            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("not sent by this timer")
24772        ));
24773        scheduler
24774            .thread_timer_copies
24775            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
24776        pending(&mut scheduler, 0);
24777        assert_eq!(
24778            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
24779            ThreadTimerSend::Send
24780        );
24781        assert!(scheduler.thread_timer_copies.is_empty());
24782    }

24784    /// A thread's timer-copy records go with it, so a later thread given
24785    /// its tid starts with none (Claude review of
24786    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
24787    #[test]
24788    fn a_dead_threads_timer_copy_records_go_with_it() {
24789        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24790        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
24791        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
24792        scheduler
24793            .thread_timer_copies
24794            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
24795        scheduler
24796            .thread_timer_copies
24797            .insert((parent, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
24798        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&creator, &process, MmId::initial(process));
24799        assert_eq!(
24800            scheduler.thread_timer_copies.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
24801            vec![&(parent, libc::SIGUSR1)]

24805    /// An expiration of a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer whose thread has exited is
24806    /// dropped, with no signal sent to any other thread and nothing recorded
24807    /// as left in the shared queue, and the periodic timer stays armed, as on
24808    /// Linux (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
24809    #[test]
24810    fn a_sigev_thread_id_expiration_after_its_thread_exited_is_dropped() {
24811        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
24812        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
24813        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
24814        let period = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
24815        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
24816            process,
24817            SignalTarget::Thread(creator),
24818            0,
24819            Some(period),
24820            period,
24821            Signal::SIGUSR1.into(),
24822        );
24823        let (at, event) = scheduler
24824            .blocked
24825            .timed_waiters
24826            .pop_if_before(period)
24827            .expect("the timer is due");
24828        let TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, target, signal) = event else {
24829            panic!("a timer event, not {event}");
24830        };
24831        assert_eq!(target, SignalTarget::Thread(creator));
24832        scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(at, id, target, signal, true, at);
24833        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
24834        assert!(scheduler.undelivered_scheduler_signals.is_empty());
24835        assert_eq!(
24836            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
24837            vec![(
24838                LogicalTime::from_nanos(20),
24839                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, SignalTarget::Thread(creator), signal)
24840            )]
24841        );
24842    }

24945        // later re-parenting changes nothing.
24946        let (mut scheduler, _parent_process, _parent, _creator, rt) = real_time_family();
24947        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);

24964            RealTimeFate::Queued

24969            RealTimeFate::Deliverable

25015    fn a_pending_real_time_expiration_is_discarded_by_ignore_and_by_exit() {

25019            .pending_real_time_expirations

25021        scheduler.discard_pending_real_time_expirations(process, rt);
25022        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), other);
25023        scheduler.discard_pending_real_time_expirations(process, other);
25024        assert!(
25025            !scheduler
25026                .pending_real_time_expirations
25027                .contains_key(&process)
25028        );
25029        // The process's exit discards what is left, once its last thread goes.
25030        scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations.insert(process, rt);
25031        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&creator, &process, MmId::initial(process));
25032        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), rt);
25033        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &process, MmId::initial(process));
25034        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), 0);

25037    /// The barrier runs before anything else in a pass: while an armed thread
25038    /// has posted nothing, a due timer is not popped and the pass is empty;
25039    /// once it has posted, the pass requeues it first and then goes on.
25040    #[test]
25041    fn the_signaled_background_barrier_runs_before_any_timer_pop() {
25042        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
25043        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
25044        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
25045        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
25046        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
25047            &mut scheduler,
25048            creator,
25049            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
25050            Some(0),
25051        );
25052        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGUSR1);
25053        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
25054            LogicalTime::from_nanos(0),
25055            child,
25056            parent,
25057            creator,
25058        );
25059        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
25060        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 1);
25061        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
25062
25063        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
25064        let _ = scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
25065        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
25066        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
25067        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
25068        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 0);
25069    }

25071    /// A `SIGCHLD` delivery that no scheduler decision placed is deferred behind
25072    /// a runnable sibling, as a host-async signal is, so the sibling's work runs
25073    /// first. A committed futex wake no longer places one: no `SIGCHLD` ends a
25074    /// gated wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
25075    #[test]
25076    fn an_unplaced_sigchld_delivery_is_deferred_behind_a_runnable_sibling() {
25077        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
25078        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
25079        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
25080        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
25081        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
25082        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(parent), Some(parent));
25083        assert!(
25084            scheduler
25085                .block_for_one_resource(parent, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
25086                .is_err()
25087        );
25088        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&parent));
25089        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
25090        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
25091    }

25093    /// A precise futex waiter woken for a signal is queued ahead of a thread that
25094    /// was already runnable, so it is the thread that resumes and dequeues the
25095    /// signal (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
25096    #[test]
25097    fn a_signal_woken_futex_waiter_runs_before_an_already_runnable_thread() {
25098        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
25099        for scheduler_send in [false, true] {
25100            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25101            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
25102            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(101);
25103            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, runnable);
25104            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
25105            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
25106            scheduler
25107                .test_kernel_signal_states
25108                .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
25109            if scheduler_send {
25110                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
25111            } else {
25112                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25113                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25114            }
25115            assert_eq!(
25116                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
25117                vec![target, runnable]
25118            );
25119        }
25120    }

25122    /// A child whose `exit_group` was granted has a `ChildExit` timer that sends
25123    /// the parent's `SIGCHLD` at a fixed logical time. Its logical death leaves
25124    /// the timer armed and sends nothing itself, and the timer names the thread
25125    /// that created the child, the one Linux prefers
25126    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
25127    #[test]
25128    fn a_child_exit_timer_names_the_thread_that_created_the_child() {
25129        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
25130        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD));
25131        let child_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
25132        let deadline = scheduler.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
25133        assert!(
25134            scheduler
25135                .block_for_one_resource(
25136                    child,
25137                    &ResourceID::Exit {
25138                        group: true,
25139                        process: child_process,
25140                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
25141                    },
25142                    &Permission::RW,
25143                    None,
25144                    None,
25145                    &Ivar::new(),
25146                )
25147                .is_ok()
25148        );
25149
25150        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
25151
25152        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
25153        assert_eq!(
25154            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
25155            vec![(
25156                deadline,
25157                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(
25158                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit {
25159                        child: child_process,
25160                        parent,
25161                    },
25162                    SignalTarget::Process(creator),
25163                    Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
25164                ),
25165            )]
25166        );
25167    }

25169    /// The first `SIGCHLD` delivered for an owned child's exit stands for it
25170    /// (`child_exit_sigchld`): once the kernel's copy was delivered, the
25171    /// child's `ChildExit` timer sends none, which before was a second
25172    /// `SIGCHLD` for that exit. Without that delivery the timer sends its own.
25173    #[test]
25174    fn a_child_exit_timer_sends_nothing_after_the_kernels_copy() {
25175        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25176        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25177        for kernel_copy_first in [false, true] {
25178            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25179            let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
25180            let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
25181            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
25182            assert_eq!(
25183                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
25184                    child,
25185                    ChildExitSigchldControl::ExitStatus {
25186                        code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
25187                        status: 7,
25188                        uid: 0,
25189                    },
25190                ),
25191                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
25192            );
25193            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
25194            if kernel_copy_first {
25195                assert_eq!(
25196                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
25197                        parent,
25198                        ChildExitSigchldControl::ClaimKernelCopy { child },
25199                    ),
25200                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(false),
25201                    "the kernel's copy is the first, and is delivered"
25202                );
25203            }
25204            let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
25205            scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
25206                scheduler.committed_time,
25207                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
25208                SignalTarget::Process(parent),
25209                Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
25210                true,
25211                scheduler.committed_time,
25212            );
25213            assert_eq!(
25214                scheduler.host_signal_attempts - attempts,
25215                u64::from(!kernel_copy_first),
25216                "kernel copy first: {kernel_copy_first}"
25217            );
25218        }
25219    }

25221    /// A nested parent names its children by its own namespace's pids
25222    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155). The kernel's copy of
25223    /// a child's exit `SIGCHLD` carries the child's nested pid, which claims
25224    /// that child's exit, so its `ChildExit` timer then sends nothing. The
25225    /// scheduler's own copy is delivered with the nested pid, not the DetPid.
25226    /// A dequeue of a kernel copy whose pid names no task there is taken as
25227    /// another copy.
25228    #[test]
25229    fn a_nested_parents_child_exit_sigchld_is_answered_in_its_namespace() {
25230        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25231        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25232        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
25233        use child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy;
25234        use child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend;
25235        for kernel_copy_first in [false, true] {
25236            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25237            let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
25238            let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
25239            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
25240            let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
25241            namespaces.record(parent, &[parent], &[100, 1]).unwrap();
25242            namespaces.record(child, &[parent], &[200, 2]).unwrap();
25243            assert_eq!(
25244                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
25245                    child,
25246                    ChildExitSigchldControl::ExitStatus {
25247                        code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
25248                        status: 7,
25249                        uid: 0,
25250                    },
25251                ),
25252                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
25253            );
25254            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
25255            if kernel_copy_first {
25256                assert_eq!(
25257                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
25258                        parent,
25259                        ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
25260                            copy: DequeuedCopy::Kernel {
25261                                child: DetPid::from_raw(99),
25262                            },
25263                            admits: true,
25264                        },
25265                    ),
25266                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded,
25267                    "a pid that names no task in the namespace"
25268                );
25269                assert_eq!(
25270                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
25271                        parent,
25272                        ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
25273                            copy: DequeuedCopy::Kernel {
25274                                child: DetPid::from_raw(2),
25275                            },
25276                            admits: true,
25277                        },
25278                    ),
25279                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(false)
25280                );
25281                assert_eq!(
25282                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
25283                    Some(TimerSend::Nothing),
25284                    "the nested pid claimed the child's exit"
25285                );
25286            } else {
25287                assert_eq!(
25288                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
25289                    Some(TimerSend::Send)
25290                );
25291                match scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
25292                    parent,
25293                    ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
25294                        copy: DequeuedCopy::Scheduler,
25295                        admits: true,
25296                    },
25297                ) {
25298                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(OwnCopy::Deliver(info)) => {
25299                        assert_eq!(info.pid, 2, "the own copy names the child's nested pid")
25300                    }
25301                    other => panic!("the own copy is delivered, not {other:?}"),
25302                }
25303            }
25304        }
25305    }

25413    /// A restartable internal read poller, as `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`
25414    /// marks one, with SIGUSR1 blocked and SIGUSR2 caught.
25415    /// A restartable internal IO poll is admitted, in the sender's turn, only
25416    /// for a signal its mask leaves unblocked: the kernel's mask, or the
25417    /// guest's own while Detcore holds the thread under a private one, as a
25418    /// pipe `writev` does (`saved_guest_sigmasks`; R2b-1 rule 1, the Claude
25419    /// implementation review, F5).
25420    #[test]
25421    fn a_poll_is_admitted_only_for_a_signal_its_mask_leaves_unblocked() {
25422        let usr1 = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
25423        let usr2 = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2);
25424        let admitted = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target| {
25425            scheduler
25426                .pending_cross_task_signals
25427                .get(&target)
25428                .cloned()
25429                .unwrap_or_default()
25430        };
25431        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25432        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
25433        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1);
25434        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr2);
25435        assert_eq!(
25436            admitted(&scheduler, target),
25437            vec![usr2],
25438            "the kernel's mask blocks SIGUSR1"
25439        );
25440
25441        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25442        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
25443        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(target, Some(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2))));
25444        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1);
25445        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr2);
25446        assert_eq!(
25447            admitted(&scheduler, target),
25448            vec![usr1],
25449            "the guest's saved mask decides while a private one is installed"
25450        );
25451    }

25453    /// A poll the drain woke is marked (`DrainWokenWaiter::Poll`): a
25454    /// `SIGCHLD` the drain merges into its batch is not committed to it, and
25455    /// its turn decides from what is still pending then. A `SIGCHLD` the
25456    /// scheduler sends at a commit point (`wake_signaled_guest`, such as a
25457    /// child-exit timer's) is committed, to a drain-woken poll and to a queued
25458    /// one, and the answer names it (R2b-1 rule 7; the Claude implementation
25459    /// review, F4).
25460    #[test]
25461    fn only_a_scheduler_sent_sigchld_is_committed_to_a_woken_poll() {
25462        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
25463        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
25464        let usr2_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2);
25465        let chld_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD);
25466        for case in ["merged", "woken for SIGUSR2", "queued"] {
25467            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25468            let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
25469            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
25470                target,
25471                KernelSignalState {
25472                    caught: chld | usr2,
25473                    ..Default::default()
25474                },
25475            );
25476            let expected = match case {
25477                "merged" => {
25478                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr2_signal);
25479                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25480                    assert_eq!(
25481                        scheduler
25482                            .blocked
25483                            .drain_woken_waiters
25484                            .get(&target)
25485                            .map(|woken| woken.waiter),
25486                        Some(DrainWokenWaiter::Poll),
25487                        "the drain marks the poll it woke"
25488                    );
25489                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, chld_signal);
25490                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25491                    vec![usr2_signal]
25492                }
25493                "woken for SIGUSR2" => {
25494                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr2_signal);
25495                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25496                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
25497                    vec![usr2_signal, chld_signal]
25498                }
25499                _ => {
25500                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
25501                    vec![chld_signal]
25502                }
25503            };
25504            let answer = turn_answer(&mut scheduler, target);
25505            assert!(
25506                matches!(&answer, Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))) if *signals == expected),
25507                "{case}: {answer:?}"
25508            );
25509        }
25510    }

25512    fn restartable_read_poller(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) -> DetTid {
25513        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25514        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
25515        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
25516        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
25517        polling.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
25518        polling.fyi("read");
25519        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
25520        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25521        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
25522            target,
25523            KernelSignalState {
25524                caught: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
25525                blocked: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
25526                ..Default::default()
25527            },
25528        );
25529        target
25530    }

25533    /// read poll: the blocked SIGUSR1 is dropped, and the caught SIGUSR2
25534    /// rewrites the request to its `ERESTARTSYS` wake

25596    /// On a backend that owns process signal control (KVM) a guest thread ID
25597    /// is not a host task, so the drain never reads kernel signal state for
25598    /// it: `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` would describe an unrelated host task,
25599    /// chosen by host thread-ID allocation. Every signal the wait does not
25600    /// hold wakes the poll, which decides for itself: here the SIGUSR1 that
25601    /// the (never consulted) scripted state blocks still wakes it. On ptrace
25602    /// the same poll is filtered by that state.
25603    #[test]
25604    fn the_drain_never_reads_kernel_signal_state_under_process_signal_control() {
25605        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
25606        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
25607            backend.provides_process_signal_control = true;
25608            backend.supports_parked_write_signal_interruption = true;
25609        });
25610        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
25611        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
25612
25613        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25614        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25615
25616        assert_eq!(
25617            scheduler
25618                .test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
25619                .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
25620            0,
25621            "the drain read a guest thread's kernel signal state"
25622        );
25623        assert_eq!(
25624            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25625            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
25626        );
25627
25628        let mut ptrace = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25629        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut ptrace);
25630        ptrace.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25631        ptrace.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25632        assert_eq!(
25633            ptrace
25634                .test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
25635                .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
25636            1
25637        );
25638        assert!(ptrace.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
25639    }

25641    /// A poll that decides for itself whether a signal interrupts it (a
25642    /// parked pipe `writev`, which polls with every ordinary signal blocked)
25643    /// is not filtered by the drain: with its scripted kernel state blocking
25644    /// SIGUSR1, the caught SIGUSR1 still wakes it, and the rewritten request
25645    /// keeps the marker for a later batch
25646    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187).
25647    #[test]
25648    fn the_drain_does_not_filter_a_poll_that_decides_signal_interruption_itself() {
25649        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25650        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25651        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
25652        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
25653        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
25654        polling.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
25655        polling.decides_signal_interruption_itself = true;
25656        polling.fyi("writev");
25657        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
25658        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25659        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
25660            target,
25661            KernelSignalState {
25662                caught: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
25663                blocked: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
25664                ..Default::default()
25665            },
25666        );
25667
25668        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25669        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25670
25671        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
25672        assert_eq!(
25673            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25674            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
25675        );
25676        let resources = scheduler
25677            .next_turns
25678            .get(&target)
25679            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
25680            .and_then(Result::ok)
25681            .expect("the target should hold its signal interruption request");
25682        assert!(resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself);
25683        assert_eq!(
25684            resources.signal_interrupt_errno(),
25685            Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
25686        );
25687    }

25690    fn pending_signals_preserve_a_restartable_internal_write_pollers_signal_set() {
25691        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25692        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);

25694        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
25695        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
25696        polling.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);

25699        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25700
25701        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
25702        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25703        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25704
25705        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
25706        assert_eq!(
25707            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25708            vec![
25709                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
25710                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
25711            ]
25712        );
