25714            .next_turns
25715            .get(&target)
25716            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
25717            .and_then(Result::ok)
25718            .expect("the target should hold its signal interruption request");
25719        assert_eq!(resources.resources.len(), 1);
25720        assert!(
25721            resources
25722                .resources
25723                .contains_key(&ResourceID::WaitidSignals(vec![
25724                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
25725                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
25726                ]))
25727        );

25729            resources.signal_interrupt_errno(),
25730            Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
25731        );

25733        // A signal arriving after the request was rewritten must remain part
25734        // of the same one-resource response rather than being dropped.
25735        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM));
25736        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25737        assert_eq!(
25738            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25739            vec![
25740                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
25741                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2),
25742                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM),
25743            ]
25744        );
25745
25746        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
25747        let (selected, _, selected_response) = scheduler.step3_peek().unwrap();
25748        assert_eq!(selected, target);
25749        assert!(
25750            scheduler
25751                .step4_resource_block(target, &resources, &selected_response)
25752                .is_ok()
25753        );
25754        assert!(
25755            scheduler
25756                .step5_guest_unblock(target, &resources, &selected_response)
25757                .is_ok()
25758        );
25759        assert!(matches!(
25760            response.try_read(),
25761            Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals)))
25762                if signals == vec![
25763                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
25764                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2),
25765                    SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM),
25766                ]
25767        ));
25768    }

25812    /// `step4_resource_block` and `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert that a
25813    /// request carries exactly one resource. The drain must never violate that.
25814    ///
25815    /// An earlier revision merged a pending signal into a request that already
25816    /// held an `InboundSignal`, producing a two-resource request. The scheduler
25817    /// daemon then panicked and the container hung — on a guest containing no
25818    /// `waitid` at all, because `{InboundSignal}` is exactly what `signal_guest`
25819    /// installs for an ordinary cross-thread signal.
25820    #[test]
25821    fn drain_never_builds_a_multi_resource_request() {
25822        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25823        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25824        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
25825        // The shape that crashed: an ordinary delivered signal, nothing to do
25826        // with waitid.
25827        let mut inbound = Resources::new(target);
25828        inbound.insert(
25829            ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)),
25830            Permission::W,
25831        );
25832        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(inbound));
25833        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25834
25835        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
25836        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25837
25838        let resources = scheduler
25839            .next_turns
25840            .get(&target)
25841            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
25842            .and_then(Result::ok)
25843            .expect("the target should still hold a request");
25844        assert!(
25845            resources.resources.len() <= 1,
25846            "the drain produced a {}-resource request, which step4 asserts against: {:?}",
25847            resources.resources.len(),
25848            resources.resources,
25849        );
25850    }

25852    /// A thread can hold a `WaitChild` request while ALREADY in the run queue:
25853    /// `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its request, and
25854    /// `step6_reenqueue` pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues
25855    /// its next request. An earlier revision inferred "blocked" from the
25856    /// resource and skipped the run-queue removal, so the drain pushed a
25857    /// second copy of the thread.
25858    ///
25859    /// That failure is worse than it looks: `RunQueue`'s duplicate check is
25860    /// `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, so debug builds panic with "Invariant
25861    /// violation! Tried to add ... already present" while RELEASE builds
25862    /// silently enqueue the thread twice and select it twice.
25863    #[test]
25864    fn pending_signal_does_not_double_queue_a_runnable_child_waiter() {
25865        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25866        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25867        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
25868        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
25869        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
25870            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
25871            owner: None,
25872            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
25873        };
25874        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
25875        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
25876        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
25877        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
25878        // The distinguishing state: holds WaitChild AND is runnable, with no
25879        // `child_waiters` entry -- exactly what a just-woken waiter looks like.
25880        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25881        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
25882        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target));
25883
25884        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25885        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25886
25887        let occurrences = scheduler
25888            .run_queue
25889            .tids()
25890            .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
25891            .count();
25892        assert_eq!(
25893            occurrences, 1,
25894            "the signalled child waiter must appear in the run queue exactly once"
25895        );
25896    }
25897
25898    /// A thread parked on a scheduler-managed child wait is blocked in
25899    /// `child_waiters`, never in the run queue, so the run-queue removal the
25900    /// polling disposition performs does not apply to it. Before this case was
25901    /// handled, a signal aimed at such a thread was recorded nowhere and a wait
25902    /// on a child that never exits could not be interrupted at all.
25903    #[test]
25904    fn pending_signal_unblocks_a_managed_child_waiter() {
25905        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25906        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25907        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
25908        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
25909        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
25910            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
25911            owner: None,
25912            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
25913        };
25914        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
25915        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
25916        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
25917        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
25918        // Parked, not runnable: exactly how `WaitChild` leaves a thread.
25919        scheduler
25920            .blocked
25921            .child_waiters
25922            .insert(target, (parent, spec));
25923        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
25924
25925        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
25926        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
25927
25928        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25929
25930        assert!(
25931            scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target),
25932            "the signalled child waiter must be requeued"
25933        );
25934        assert!(
25935            !scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target),
25936            "its child-wait blocking entry must be cleared"
25937        );
25938        assert_eq!(
25939            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25940            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
25941            "the resume must name the signal that woke it"
25942        );
25943    }

25979    /// A scheduler for a backend whose process exits complete asynchronously
25980    /// (in-guest LiteInst), with killed-thread RPC cancellation as that backend
25981    /// has it.
25982    fn async_exit_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
25983        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
25984            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
25985            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
25986        });
25987        Scheduler::new(&config)
25988    }

25990    /// Registers single-threaded process `tid` with an empty pending request.
25991    fn register_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
25992        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
25993        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
25994            tid,
25995            ThreadNextTurn {
25996                dettid: tid,
25997                child_tid_addr: 0,
25998                req: Ivar::new(),
25999                resp: Ivar::new(),
26000                protocol: Default::default(),
26001            },
26002        );
26003    }
26004
26005    #[test]
26006    fn async_exit_holds_selection_from_the_grant_until_completion() {
26007        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
26008        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26009        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
26010        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
26011        assert_eq!(
26012            scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits,
26013            BTreeSet::from([process])
26014        );
26015        // What the backend's watchdog reads.
26016        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits(), [process]);
26017        // Every pass skips while the exit is pending, however many there are.
26018        for _ in 0..3 {
26019            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
26020        }
26021        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
26022        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
26023        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
26024        assert!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits().is_empty());
26025    }

26027    #[test]
26028    fn without_async_exit_completion_the_grant_holds_nothing() {
26029        let config = Config::default();
26030        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26031        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26032        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(process));
26033        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
26034        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
26035        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
26036        assert!(!scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
26037    }

26039    #[test]
26040    fn async_exit_lifetime_is_monotone() {
26041        // A completion that arrives first is kept, and a later begin, from the
26042        // grant or from a late deregistration, is a no-op.
26043        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
26044        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26045        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
26046        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
26047        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
26048        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(process));
26049        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
26050        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
26051
26052        // After a grant and its completion, a late begin is a no-op too.
26053        let other = DetPid::from_raw(200);
26054        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(other);
26055        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(other));
26056        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(other));
26057        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
26058    }

26060    #[test]
26061    #[should_panic(expected = "the hold must allow at most one")]
26062    fn a_second_exit_grant_while_one_is_pending_is_an_invariant_violation() {
26063        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
26064        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(DetPid::from_raw(100));
26065        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(DetPid::from_raw(200));
26066    }

26068    #[test]
26069    fn completion_consumes_only_registrations_the_process_did_not_deregister() {
26070        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
26071        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(100);
26072        let deregistered = DetTid::from_raw(200);
26073        register_process(&mut scheduler, dead);
26074        register_process(&mut scheduler, deregistered);
26075        // `deregistered` finished its exit hook before exiting.
26076        assert!(scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(deregistered));
26077        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&deregistered, &deregistered, MmId::initial(deregistered));
26078
26079        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(deregistered));
26080        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
26081        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&dead));
26082        // A late DeregisterThread for the consumed thread is already accounted.
26083        assert!(!scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(dead));
26084        // Consuming twice is a no-op.
26085        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
26086    }

26088    /// A joiner woken by a thread's CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID is admitted at the
26089    /// next drain, in DetTid order with the other admissions of that drain,
26090    /// whichever arrived first; it is not pushed at once. On the base code it
26091    /// was pushed at the wake, so it ran ahead of a lower DetTid
26092    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4362, part 2 step 0b). The
26093    /// joiner here has the higher DetTid: with a lower one, both orders agree
26094    /// and the case could not tell them apart (Claude review of
26095    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4453, F2).
26096    #[test]
26097    fn a_cleartid_joiner_is_admitted_in_dettid_order_with_pending_admissions() {
26098        for wake_first in [false, true] {
26099            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
26100            let lower = DetTid::from_raw(5);
26101            let dead = DetTid::from_raw(9);
26102            let joiner = DetTid::from_raw(11);
26103            let mm = MmId::initial(dead);
26104            let address = 0x404100;
26105            let futex = FutexID::private(mm, address);
26106            for tid in [lower, dead, joiner] {
26107                scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
26108                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
26109                scheduler.record_thread_mm(tid, mm);
26110            }
26111            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&dead).unwrap().child_tid_addr = address;
26112            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&joiner, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
26113            if wake_first {
26114                scheduler.wake_futex_child_cleartid(futex, dead);
26115                scheduler.admit_to_run_queue(lower, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
26116            } else {
26117                scheduler.admit_to_run_queue(lower, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
26118                scheduler.wake_futex_child_cleartid(futex, dead);
26119            }
26120            assert!(
26121                scheduler.admission_pending(joiner),
26122                "wake_first={wake_first}"
26123            );
26124            scheduler.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
26125
26126            assert_eq!(
26127                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26128                vec![lower, joiner],
26129                "wake_first={wake_first}"
26130            );
26131        }
26132    }
26133
26134    /// A thread retired while a tentative selection is open wakes its
26135    /// clear-TID joiner by admission, which is legal there, instead of a run
26136    /// queue push, which panics (2ee7190125's test).
26137    #[test]
26138    fn unreported_exit_defers_clear_tid_wake_during_tentative_selection() {
26139        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
26140        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
26141        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(9);
26142        let waiters = [11, 12].map(DetTid::from_raw);
26143        let mm = MmId::initial(dead);
26144        let address = 0x404100;
26145        let futex = FutexID::private(mm, address);
26146        for process in [anchor, dead, waiters[0]] {
26147            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(process, process, true);
26148        }
26149        scheduler
26150            .thread_tree
26151            .add_child(waiters[0], waiters[1], false);
26152        for tid in [anchor, dead, waiters[0], waiters[1]] {
26153            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
26154            scheduler.record_thread_mm(tid, mm);
26155        }
26156        // A CLONE_VM process can leave a clear-TID waiter in a different,
26157        // surviving thread group that shares its address space.
26158        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&dead).unwrap().child_tid_addr = address;
26159        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
26160        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(dead);
26161        for waiter in waiters {
26162            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
26163        }
26164        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
26165        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
26166        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
26167        assert!(scheduler.child_tid_was_cleared(futex, dead.as_raw()));
26168        assert!(scheduler.admission_pending(waiters[0]));
26169        assert!(!scheduler.admission_pending(waiters[1]));
26170        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[0]));
26171        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[1]));
26172        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
26173        scheduler.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
26174        scheduler.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
26175        assert_eq!(
26176            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26177            vec![anchor, waiters[0]]
26178        );
26179    }

26182    fn a_dead_vfork_parent_cancels_its_barrier_and_settles_a_late_child() {
26183        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
26184        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
26185        let child = DetTid::from_raw(101);
26186        register_process(&mut scheduler, parent);
26187        // The parent is in vfork; its child has not registered yet.
26188        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
26189        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(parent));
26190        assert!(!scheduler.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent));
26191        // The child's outstanding registration settles without a barrier,
26192        // without panicking.
26193        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
26194        assert!(!scheduler.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent));
26195        assert!(!scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.contains(&parent));
26196    }

26357    #[test]
26358    fn alarm_deadline_uses_observed_logical_time() {
26359        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
26360        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26361        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(101);
26362        let now = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
26363        let duration = LogicalTime::from_nanos(250);
26364
26365        assert_eq!(
26366            scheduler.register_alarm(
26367                detpid,
26368                dettid,
26369                now,
26370                duration,
26371                LogicalTime::ZERO,
26372                Signal::SIGALRM,
26373            ),
26374            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::ZERO)
26375        );
26376        assert_eq!(
26377            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26378            vec![(
26379                LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_250),
26380                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(
26381                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(detpid),
26382                    SignalTarget::Process(dettid),
26383                    Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
26384                )
26385            )]
26386        );
26387        assert_eq!(
26388            scheduler.alarm_remaining(detpid, LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_100)),
26389            LogicalTime::from_nanos(150)
26390        );
26391        // Overdue but not yet popped: an active timer reads 1 us, as Linux's
26392        // `itimer_get_remtime` floors it, not 0 (which means a disarmed or
26393        // inactive timer; https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139).
26394        assert_eq!(
26395            scheduler.alarm_remaining(detpid, LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_300)),
26396            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000)
26397        );
26398
26399        let cancel_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_100);
26400        assert_eq!(
26401            scheduler.register_alarm(
26402                detpid,
26403                dettid,
26404                cancel_time,
26405                LogicalTime::ZERO,
26406                LogicalTime::ZERO,
26407                Signal::SIGALRM
26408            ),
26409            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(150), LogicalTime::ZERO)
26410        );
26411        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
26412    }

26438    #[test]
26439    fn physical_exit_barrier_precedes_empty_queue_timer_fast_forward() {
26440        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
26441            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
26442            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
26443        });
26444        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26445        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
26446        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
26447        let exit_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
26448        let first_process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26449        let second_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
26450        let unrelated_process = DetPid::from_raw(300);
26451
26452        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
26453        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
26454        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(second_process));
26455        scheduler.register_alarm(
26456            first_process,
26457            first_process,
26458            initial_time,
26459            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
26460            LogicalTime::ZERO,
26461            Signal::SIGALRM,
26462        );
26463
26464        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26465        assert_eq!(
26466            scheduler
26467                .blocked
26468                .timed_waiters
26469                .iter()
26470                .map(|(time, _)| time)
26471                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26472            vec![exit_deadline]
26473        );
26474        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
26475
26476        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(unrelated_process));
26477        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
26478        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
26479        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26480        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
26481        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
26482
26483        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(second_process));
26484        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26485        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
26486        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), exit_deadline);
26487    }

26489    fn physical_wait_handoff_queue(completion_before_wait: bool) -> Vec<DetTid> {
26490        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
26491            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
26492            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
26493        });
26494        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
26495        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26496        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
26497        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(200);
26498        let child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
26499        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
26500        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
26501        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waiter);
26502        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
26503
26504        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
26505        if completion_before_wait {
26506            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
26507        }
26508
26509        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(waiter), Some(waiter));
26510        assert!(
26511            scheduler
26512                .block_for_one_resource(
26513                    waiter,
26514                    &ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child),
26515                    &Permission::W,
26516                    None,
26517                    None,
26518                    &Ivar::new(),
26519                )
26520                .is_err()
26521        );
26522        assert_eq!(
26523            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26524            vec![sibling]
26525        );
26526
26527        if !completion_before_wait {
26528            assert!(
26529                scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err(),
26530                "a runnable sibling must not pass the pending physical-exit barrier"
26531            );
26532            assert_eq!(
26533                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26534                vec![sibling]
26535            );
26536            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
26537        }
26538
26539        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_ok());
26540        assert!(scheduler.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
26541        assert!(scheduler.blocked.physical_child_ready.contains(&waiter));
26542        scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect()
26543    }
26544
26545    #[test]
26546    fn physical_wait_handoff_is_identical_before_or_after_backend_completion() {
26547        let completion_before = physical_wait_handoff_queue(true);
26548        let completion_after = physical_wait_handoff_queue(false);
26549
26550        assert_eq!(completion_before, completion_after);
26551        assert_eq!(
26552            completion_before,
26553            vec![DetTid::from_raw(200), DetTid::from_raw(100)]
26554        );
26555    }

26580    #[test]
26581    fn terminal_wait_selects_group_owner_and_clone_class() {
26582        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
26583        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
26584        let owner_a = DetTid::from_raw(101);
26585        let owner_b = DetTid::from_raw(102);
26586        let normal = DetPid::from_raw(200);
26587        let clone_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
26588        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
26589        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, owner_a, false);
26590        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, owner_b, false);
26591        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
26592            owner_a,
26593            normal,
26594            true,
26595            false,
26596            libc::SIGCHLD,
26597        );
26598        scheduler
26599            .thread_tree
26600            .add_child_with_wait_metadata(owner_b, clone_child, true, false, 0);
26601        let group = DetPid::from_raw(77);
26602        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(normal, group));
26603        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(clone_child, group));
26604        scheduler.logically_exited_processes.insert(normal);
26605        scheduler.logically_exited_processes.insert(clone_child);
26606
26607        assert_eq!(
26608            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
26609                parent,
26610                ChildWaitSpec {
26611                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(DetPid::from_raw(78)),
26612                    owner: Some(owner_a),
26613                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
26614                },
26615            ),
26616            None,
26617            "a different process group must not match"
26618        );
26619        assert_eq!(
26620            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
26621                parent,
26622                ChildWaitSpec {
26623                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(normal),
26624                    owner: Some(owner_b),
26625                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
26626                },
26627            ),
26628            None,
26629            "__WNOTHREAD must exclude a child created by another task"
26630        );
26631        assert_eq!(
26632            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
26633                parent,
26634                ChildWaitSpec {
26635                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(clone_child),
26636                    owner: Some(owner_b),
26637                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
26638                },
26639            ),
26640            None,
26641            "a clone child must not enter the ordinary SIGCHLD population"
26642        );
26643        assert_eq!(
26644            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
26645                parent,
26646                ChildWaitSpec {
26647                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group),
26648                    owner: Some(owner_b),
26649                    exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Clone,
26650                },
26651            ),
26652            Some(clone_child)
26653        );
26654        assert_eq!(
26655            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
26656                parent,
26657                ChildWaitSpec {
26658                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
26659                    owner: Some(owner_a),
26660                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
26661                },
26662            ),
26663            Some(normal)
26664        );
26665    }

26696
26697    /// Populate a scheduler with a deadlock's worth of blocked state, inserting
26698    /// each collection in the caller's chosen order.
26699    ///
26700    /// `reverse` exists so the same logical state can be built two ways: the
26701    /// report must not depend on insertion order, because `futex_waiters` is a
26702    /// `HashMap`, `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, and
26703    /// `Resources::resources` a `HashMap`.
26704    fn deadlocked_scheduler(config: &Config, reverse: bool) -> Scheduler {
26705        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(config);
26706        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
26707        let mut futexes = vec![
26708            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100), 5),
26709            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200), 7),
26710            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404300), 9),
26711        ];
26712        let mut tids = vec![3, 5, 7, 9];
26713        if reverse {
26714            futexes.reverse();
26715            tids.reverse();
26716        }
26717
26718        for (futex_id, dettid) in futexes {
26719            scheduler
26720                .blocked
26721                .futex_waiters
26722                .entry(futex_id)
26723                .or_default()
26724                .push(futex_waiter(dettid, u32::MAX));
26725        }
26726        for dettid in tids {
26727            let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(dettid);
26728            // A request carrying several resources: `Resources::resources` is a
26729            // HashMap, so an unsorted render would vary here too.
26730            let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
26731            resources.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
26732            resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(dettid), Permission::RW);
26733            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
26734                dettid,
26735                ThreadNextTurn {
26736                    dettid,
26737                    child_tid_addr: 0,
26738                    // A FULL ivar: `Debug` on this prints the parked waker's raw
26739                    // host pointers, which is exactly what must not reach stderr.
26740                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(resources)),
26741                    resp: Ivar::new(),
26742                    protocol: Default::default(),
26743                },
26744            );
26745            scheduler.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid);
26746        }
26747        scheduler
26748            .blocked
26749            .timed_waiters
26750            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(11));
26751        // A thread held at a happens-before gate, which adds a headline class
26752        // and renders its checkpoint request in the per-thread list.
26753        let held = DetTid::from_raw(13);
26754        let mut gate = Resources::new(held);
26755        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50), Permission::R);
26756        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
26757            held,
26758            ThreadNextTurn {
26759                dettid: held,
26760                child_tid_addr: 0,
26761                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
26762                resp: Ivar::new(),
26763                protocol: Default::default(),
26764            },
26765        );
26766        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
26767            r#"{"version": 1,
26768                "events": {"never": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
26769                           "gate": {"thread": "13", "syscalls": 50}},
26770                "edges": [{"before": "never", "after": "gate", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
26771        );
26772        hb.parked.insert(held);
26773        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
26774        scheduler
26775    }
26776
26777    /// The terminal deadlock exit hands its report to the installed hook first
26778    /// (`run --verify` records the run as failed by a deadlock), and nothing
26779    /// once the hook is removed.
26780    #[test]
26781    fn a_terminal_deadlock_report_reaches_the_installed_hook_until_it_is_removed() {
26782        let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
26783        let sink = Arc::clone(&seen);
26784        set_terminal_deadlock_hook(Some(Box::new(move |report: &str| {
26785            sink.lock().unwrap().push(report.to_owned());
26786        })));
26787        let config = Config::default();
26788        let report = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, false).format_terminal_deadlock();
26789        report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(&report);
26790        set_terminal_deadlock_hook(None);
26791        report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook("after removal");
26792        assert_eq!(*seen.lock().unwrap(), vec![report]);
26793    }
26794
26795    /// The deadlock report reaches stderr, so it must be byte-identical across
26796    /// runs of the same program. Codex measured the unguarded `{:?}` dump
26797    /// emitting `Waker { data: 0x557e90a74680, .. }` in one run and
26798    /// `Waker { data: 0x5654e2b08680, .. }` in the next: raw host pointers that
26799    /// move with ASLR. Assert the render carries no host pointer and no
26800    /// insertion-order dependence.
26801    #[test]
26802    fn deadlock_report_is_deterministic_and_carries_no_host_pointer() {
26803        let config = Config::default();
26804        let forward = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, false).format_terminal_deadlock();
26805        let reversed = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, true).format_terminal_deadlock();
26806
26807        // Same logical state built in two insertion orders must render
26808        // identically: no HashMap/HashSet iteration order may leak.
26809        assert_eq!(forward, reversed);
26810
26811        // No `Debug` of an Ivar/Waker, and so no host pointer.
26812        //
26813        // ⚠️ THIS LIST CANNOT SEE A SECTION THE FIXTURE NEVER RENDERS. It only
26814        // inspects the text `deadlocked_scheduler` happens to produce. When you
26815        // add a section to `format_terminal_deadlock`, add the state that triggers
26816        // it to the fixture in the same change, or this test will pass and say
26817        // nothing about your section.
26818        //
26819        // These tokens catch host POINTERS and raw thread ids. The subtler failure
26820        // is a host-influenced COUNTER, which looks like an ordinary small integer
26821        // and matches no banned word -- which is why the byte-identical assertion
26822        // above is the load-bearing check and this list is only a backstop.
26823        for banned in [
26824            "Waker", "Ivar", "vtable", "Mutex", "poisoned", "ThreadId", "0x7f",
26825        ] {
26826            assert!(
26827                !forward.contains(banned),
26828                "deadlock report leaked {banned:?}; it must print only guest-level \
26829                 identities.\n{forward}"
26830            );
26831        }
26832
26833        // The report is still substantive: it names every blocked thread, the
26834        // futex keys, and the indefinite deadline.
26835        for expected in [
26836            // This fixture holds BOTH pools and a held thread, so the
26837            // state-derived headline must name all three rather than whichever
26838            // branch happened to fire.
26839            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
26840             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), and \
26841             thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire, \
26842             but no runnable threads left.",
26843            "dtid 13: HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50): R",
26844            "dtid 3",
26845            "dtid 9",
26846            "0x404100",
26847            "0x404300",
26848            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)",
26849            "FutexWait: R, MemAddrSpace(DetPid(3)): RW",
26850        ] {
26851            assert!(
26852                forward.contains(expected),
26853                "deadlock report lost {expected:?}:\n{forward}"
26854            );
26855        }
26856    }
26857
26858    /// A `pause(2)` registers `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`, which is a sentinel for
26859    /// "no deadline", not a deadline. With nothing else left to run, the guest is
26860    /// permanently blocked and must be reported as such -- never woken.
26861    #[test]
26862    fn indefinite_waiter_alone_is_reported_as_a_deadlock() {
26863        let config = Config::default();
26864        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26865        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
26866        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
26867
26868        scheduler
26869            .blocked
26870            .timed_waiters
26871            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(100));
26872
26873        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26874
26875        // Asserting the verdict by value, not by catching a panic: the report is
26876        // recorded for `sched_loop_inner` to print and exit on, so the text is
26877        // checkable here rather than only through `#[should_panic]`.
26878        let report = scheduler
26879            .take_terminal_deadlock()
26880            .expect("an indefinite waiter with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
26881        assert!(
26882            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
26883            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
26884        );
26885        // Taking it is destructive, and the indefinite waiter is never woken.
26886        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
26887        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
26888        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
26889    }

26891    /// A nested namespace's init exits beside a child in `pause(2)`. Linux
26892    /// kills the child (`zap_pid_namespace`) at a moment the host chooses, so
26893    /// until the backend reports that kill the empty run queue is waiting for
26894    /// it, not deadlocked; a deadlock verdict here ended the run before its
26895    /// determinism loss could be reported
26896    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155).
26897    #[test]
26898    fn a_pause_in_an_ended_pid_namespace_waits_for_the_kill_not_a_deadlock() {
26899        let config = Config::default();
26900        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26901        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
26902        let [root, init, child] = [3, 5, 7].map(DetTid::from_raw);
26903        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
26904        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, init, true);
26905        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(init);
26906        scheduler.thread_tree.mark_pid_namespace_init(init);
26907        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(init, child, true);
26908        let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
26909        namespaces.record(init, &[init], &[5, 1]).unwrap();
26910        namespaces.record(child, &[init], &[7, 2]).unwrap();
26911        for tid in [init, child] {
26912            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
26913        }
26914
26915        scheduler.note_pid_namespace_end(init);
26916        assert_eq!(scheduler.determinism_losses.len(), 1);
26917        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&init);
26918        scheduler
26919            .blocked
26920            .timed_waiters
26921            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
26922
26923        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26924        assert!(
26925            scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none(),
26926            "a thread Linux is killing is not a deadlock"
26927        );
26928
26929        // The backend reports the kill: nothing is left, and nothing waits.
26930        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
26931        assert!(scheduler.namespace_zap_victims.is_empty());
26932        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26933        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
26934
26935        // Without a namespace end, the same pause is still a deadlock.
26936        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
26937        scheduler
26938            .blocked
26939            .timed_waiters
26940            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
26941        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26942        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_some());
26943    }
26944
26945    /// A namespace whose init exited, with its member `child` in `pause(2)`
26946    /// and nothing else left: the state `note_pid_namespace_end` leaves.
26947    fn ended_namespace_with_a_paused_member(child: DetTid) -> Scheduler {
26948        let config = Config::default();
26949        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
26950        let [root, init] = [3, 5].map(DetTid::from_raw);
26951        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
26952        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, init, true);
26953        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(init);
26954        scheduler.thread_tree.mark_pid_namespace_init(init);
26955        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(init, child, true);
26956        let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
26957        namespaces.record(init, &[init], &[5, 1]).unwrap();
26958        namespaces
26959            .record(child, &[init], &[child.as_raw(), 2])
26960            .unwrap();
26961        for tid in [init, child] {
26962            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
26963        }
26964        scheduler.note_pid_namespace_end(init);
26965        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&init);
26966        scheduler
26967            .blocked
26968            .timed_waiters
26969            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
26970        scheduler
26971    }

26973    /// A backend that never reports the killed member's death (an in-guest
26974    /// tool gets no exit hook for a SIGKILL) must not wait forever: past the
26975    /// valve the run stops on a deadlock that names the victims, and the
26976    /// report is the same text every time.
26977    #[test]
26978    fn a_namespace_kill_never_reported_ends_in_a_named_deadlock() {
26979        let child = DetTid::from_raw(7);
26980        let mut scheduler = ended_namespace_with_a_paused_member(child);
26981        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
26982        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26983        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
26984
26985        scheduler.namespace_zap_valve = Duration::ZERO;
26986        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
26987        let report = scheduler
26988            .take_terminal_deadlock()
26989            .expect("past the valve the wait ends in a report");
26990        assert!(
26991            report.starts_with(
26992                "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: processes {DetPid(7)}, which Linux kills because their PID namespace's init exited, were not reported dead within 0ns\n"
26993            ),
26994            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
26995        );
26996        assert!(
26997            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
26998            "{report}"
26999        );
27000    }

27002    /// A process forked into the namespace after its init's Exit grant, but
27003    /// before Linux starts killing the namespace, dies with it too, so it is
27004    /// waited for like the members named at the grant. A process outside the
27005    /// ended namespace is not.

27007    fn a_process_forked_into_an_ended_namespace_is_a_victim() {

27013        namespaces.record(late, &[init], &[9, 3]).unwrap();
27014        scheduler.note_member_of_ended_namespace(late);

27017            scheduler.namespace_zap_victims,

27137    /// The `SignalEvt` arm is the sub-case whose behaviour this change actually
27138    /// alters, and it is reachable with no `pause` anywhere.
27139    ///
27140    /// `handle_timer_settime` adds a guest-supplied duration to now, and
27141    /// `LogicalTime`'s `Add` saturates, so an absurdly far-future POSIX timer
27142    /// (issue #219, the Java case) lands on `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` and
27143    /// `register_posix_timer` inserts it verbatim. Previously `step2d` popped it,
27144    /// fast-forwarded the clock ~584 years, and dispatched to `fire_alarm`, which
27145    /// -- unlike the `ThreadEvt` arm -- does NOT abort: it delivered a bogus
27146    /// year-2554 signal and the guest carried on. That is now a terminal
27147    /// deadlock, which is the faithful answer, because Linux will not fire that
27148    /// timer either and those threads genuinely hang.
27149    #[test]
27150    fn saturated_posix_timer_alone_is_a_deadlock_not_a_bogus_signal() {
27151        let config = Config::default();
27152        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27153        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27154        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
27155        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
27156
27157        // The real production entry point, with the deadline a saturating add
27158        // produces. No `pause`, no `ThreadEvt`.
27159        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
27160            process,
27161            SignalTarget::Process(process),
27162            7,
27163            Some(LogicalTime::MAX - LogicalTime::from_nanos(0)),
27164            LogicalTime::ZERO,
27165            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
27166        );
27167        assert_eq!(
27168            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.next_deadline(),
27169            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
27170            "a saturated timer must land on the no-deadline sentinel"
27171        );
27172
27173        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27174
27175        let report = scheduler
27176            .take_terminal_deadlock()
27177            .expect("a saturated timer with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
27178        assert!(
27179            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
27180            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
27181        );
27182        // The signal was NOT delivered and the clock did NOT jump to the end of
27183        // logical time: both are what the old fast-forward did here.
27184        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
27185        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.is_empty());
27186        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
27187    }
27188
27189    /// The headline is derived from state, not from the branch that fired, so a
27190    /// genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer registered names
27191    /// both classes rather than being filed as an indefinite-wait bug.
27192    #[test]
27193    fn a_futex_deadlock_holding_a_saturated_timer_names_both_classes() {
27194        let config = Config::default();
27195        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27196        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27197        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
27198        scheduler
27199            .blocked
27200            .futex_waiters
27201            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
27202            .or_default()
27203            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
27204        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
27205            DetPid::from_raw(100),
27206            SignalTarget::Process(DetPid::from_raw(100)),
27207            7,
27208            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
27209            LogicalTime::ZERO,
27210            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
27211        );
27212
27213        // Branch order sends this to the indefinite arm, because a timed waiter
27214        // exists; the headline must still say the futex pool is blocked.
27215        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27216        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().expect("terminal");
27217        let headline = report.lines().next().expect("a headline");
27218        assert_eq!(
27219            headline,
27220            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
27221             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), but no \
27222             runnable threads left.",
27223            "full report:\n{report}"
27224        );
27225    }

27227    /// The futex class shares `report_terminal_deadlock`, so it must record a
27228    /// verdict too -- otherwise fixing the teardown for one class silently
27229    /// leaves the other wedged.
27230    #[test]
27231    fn futex_deadlock_records_the_same_terminal_verdict() {
27232        let config = Config::default();
27233        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27234        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27235        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
27236        scheduler
27237            .blocked
27238            .futex_waiters
27239            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
27240            .or_default()
27241            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
27242
27243        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27244
27245        let report = scheduler
27246            .take_terminal_deadlock()
27247            .expect("futex waiters with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
27248        assert!(
27249            report.contains("thread(s) waiting on futex"),
27250            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
27251        );
27252    }

27254    /// The positive half of the bracket: refusing to fast-forward onto an
27255    /// indefinite waiter must not make the fast-forward machinery inert. A real
27256    /// deadline still fires, the clock still advances to exactly that deadline
27257    /// (not to the end of logical time), and the indefinite waiter stays parked.
27258    #[test]
27259    fn finite_deadline_still_fast_forwards_alongside_an_indefinite_waiter() {
27260        let config = Config::default();
27261        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27262        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27263        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
27264        let alarm_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
27265        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
27266        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(200);
27267
27268        scheduler
27269            .blocked
27270            .timed_waiters
27271            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
27272        scheduler.register_alarm(
27273            process,
27274            process,
27275            initial_time,
27276            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
27277            LogicalTime::ZERO,
27278            Signal::SIGALRM,
27279        );
27280
27281        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27282        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), alarm_deadline);
27283        assert_eq!(
27284            scheduler
27285                .blocked
27286                .timed_waiters
27287                .iter()
27288                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
27289            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
27290        );
27291    }

27293    /// Outstanding blocking external IO can still deliver the signal an
27294    /// indefinite waiter is waiting for, so the deadlock verdict must be
27295    /// deferred rather than reported. `step2c` does not cover this case: it only
27296    /// spins when `timed_waiters` is *empty*, and an indefinite waiter is an
27297    /// entry.
27298    #[test]
27299    fn outstanding_external_io_defers_the_indefinite_wait_verdict() {
27300        let config = Config::default();
27301        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27302        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27303        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
27304        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(100);
27305        let io_thread = DetTid::from_raw(101);
27306
27307        scheduler
27308            .blocked
27309            .timed_waiters
27310            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
27311        scheduler
27312            .blocked
27313            .external_io_blockers
27314            .insert(io_thread, ExternalOpId::new(io_thread, 0));
27315
27316        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27317        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
27318        assert_eq!(
27319            scheduler
27320                .blocked
27321                .timed_waiters
27322                .iter()
27323                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
27324            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
27325        );
27326    }

27404    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order: explicit SIG_IGN wins over blocking,
27405    /// blocking over default-ignore, and only a default-ignored, unblocked
27406    /// SIGCHLD is discarded.
27407    #[test]
27408    fn sigchld_notification_classification_follows_do_notify_parent() {
27409        use ChildExitNotification::*;
27410        for (ignored, caught, blocked, expected) in [
27411            (true, false, false, None),
27412            (true, false, true, None),
27413            (false, false, false, Discard),
27414            (false, false, true, Deliver),
27415            (false, true, false, Deliver),
27416            (false, true, true, Deliver),
27417        ] {
27418            assert_eq!(
27419                classify_sigchld_notification(ignored, caught, blocked),
27420                expected,
27421                "ignored {ignored}, caught {caught}, blocked {blocked}"
27422            );
27423        }
27424    }

27447    const SIGCHLD_BIT: u64 = 1 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
27448
27449    /// A parent process 100 and its child 200 (exit signal `exit_signal`),
27450    /// the parent parked on a request labelled `fyi`, with /proc reporting
27451    /// `ignored`, `caught` and `blocked` as SIGCHLD's state for the parent.
27452    fn child_exit_fixture(
27453        reports_publication: bool,
27454        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
27455        fyi: Option<&str>,
27456        masks: Option<(bool, bool, bool)>,
27457    ) -> (Scheduler, DetPid, DetPid) {
27458        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
27459            backend.reports_child_exit_publication = reports_publication;
27460        });
27461        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27462        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
27463        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
27464        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
27465        scheduler
27466            .thread_tree
27467            .add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, child, true, false, exit_signal);
27468        let req = match fyi {
27469            Some(label) => {
27470                let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
27471                request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
27472                request.fyi(label);
27473                Ivar::full(Ok(request))
27474            }
27475            Option::None => Ivar::new(),
27476        };
27477        for tid in [parent, child] {
27478            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
27479                tid,
27480                ThreadNextTurn {
27481                    dettid: tid,
27482                    child_tid_addr: 0,
27483                    req: if tid == parent {
27484                        req.clone()
27485                    } else {
27486                        Ivar::new()
27487                    },
27488                    resp: Ivar::new(),
27489                    protocol: Default::default(),
27490                },
27491            );
27492            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
27493        }
27494        if let Some((ignored, caught, blocked)) = masks {
27495            let bit = |set: bool| if set { SIGCHLD_BIT } else { 0 };
27496            scheduler
27497                .test_signal_masks
27498                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigIgn"), bit(ignored));
27499            scheduler
27500                .test_signal_masks
27501                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigCgt"), bit(caught));
27502            scheduler
27503                .test_signal_masks
27504                .insert((parent, Some(parent), "SigBlk"), bit(blocked));
27505        }
27506        (scheduler, parent, child)
27507    }
27508
27509    #[test]
27510    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_when_every_input_is_known() {
27511        use ChildExitNotification::*;
27512        let classify = |exit_signal, fyi, masks| {
27513            let (scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(true, exit_signal, fyi, masks);
27514            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
27515        };
27516        let read = Some("read");
27517        assert_eq!(
27518            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((true, false, true))),
27519            None
27520        );
27521        assert_eq!(
27522            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, false))),
27523            Discard
27524        );
27525        assert_eq!(
27526            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, true, false))),
27527            Deliver
27528        );
27529        assert_eq!(
27530            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, true))),
27531            Deliver
27532        );
27533        // Not an effective SIGCHLD, the receiving task not parked, a
27534        // temporary-mask syscall, or /proc unreadable: Undecided.
27535        assert_eq!(
27536            classify(libc::SIGUSR1, read, Some((false, false, false))),
27537            Undecided
27538        );
27539        assert_eq!(classify(0, read, Some((false, false, false))), Undecided);
27540        assert_eq!(
27541            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Option::None, Some((false, false, false))),
27542            Undecided
27543        );
27544        for label in ["ppoll", "pselect6", "epoll_pwait"] {
27545            assert_eq!(
27546                classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Some(label), Some((false, false, false))),
27547                Undecided,
27548                "{label}"
27549            );
27550        }
27551        assert_eq!(classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Option::None), Undecided);
27552    }

27554    /// A managed wait installs Detcore's private blocking mask, which /proc
27555    /// then reports; the saved guest mask decides instead.
27556    #[test]
27557    fn child_exit_notification_reads_the_saved_guest_mask() {
27558        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27559            true,
27560            libc::SIGCHLD,
27561            Some("wait-child-lifecycle"),
27562            Some((false, false, true)),
27563        );
27564        assert_eq!(
27565            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
27566            ChildExitNotification::Deliver
27567        );
27568        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Some(0)));
27569        assert_eq!(
27570            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
27571            ChildExitNotification::Discard
27572        );
27573        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Some(SIGCHLD_BIT)));
27574        assert_eq!(
27575            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
27576            ChildExitNotification::Deliver
27577        );
27578        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Option::None));
27579        assert!(!scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(DetPid::from_raw(999), Some(0)));
27580    }

27582    fn child_exit_timer_armed(scheduler: &Scheduler, child: DetPid) -> bool {
27583        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().any(|(_, event)| {
27584            matches!(
27585                event,
27586                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child: exited, .. }, ..)
27587                    if exited == child
27588            )
27589        })
27590    }

27592    fn grant_group_exit(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, child: DetPid) {
27593        grant_group_exit_from(scheduler, child, child);
27594    }

27596    /// Grants `thread` an exit_group request that names `child` as its process.
27597    fn grant_group_exit_from(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, child: DetPid) {
27598        assert!(
27599            scheduler
27600                .block_for_one_resource(
27601                    thread,
27602                    &ResourceID::Exit {
27603                        group: true,
27604                        process: child,
27605                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
27606                    },
27607                    &Permission::RW,
27608                    Option::None,
27609                    Option::None,
27610                    &Ivar::new(),
27611                )
27612                .is_ok()
27613        );
27614    }

27616    /// A child's effective exit signal follows Linux: the clone's signal; its
27617    /// creator's process's signal under CLONE_PARENT; SIGCHLD after the child's
27618    /// own successful exec, which also moves it out of the clone wait class.
27619    /// The parent's exec changes only the notification of the children it
27620    /// created before (`parent_exec_id`), not their wait class, and not that of
27621    /// a child it creates afterwards. Before, the clone's requested signal was
27622    /// kept for good (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3895).
27623    #[test]
27624    fn a_childs_effective_exit_signal_follows_exec_and_clone_parent() {
27625        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
27626        let creator = DetPid::from_raw(200);
27627        let usr1_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
27628        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(400);
27629        let late_child = DetPid::from_raw(500);
27630        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
27631        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
27632        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, creator, true, false, libc::SIGCHLD);
27633        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, usr1_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
27634        // CLONE_PARENT with SIGUSR1 requested: the creator's SIGCHLD, and the
27635        // creator's parent.
27636        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(creator, grandchild, true, true, libc::SIGUSR1);
27637        let exit_signal = |tree: &ThreadTree, pid| tree.process_wait[&pid].exit_signal;
27638        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, grandchild), libc::SIGCHLD);
27639        assert_eq!(tree.process_wait[&grandchild].wait_parent, Some(parent));
27640        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
27641
27642        // The parent's exec: the existing SIGUSR1 child still waits as a clone
27643        // child but notifies with SIGCHLD; one created afterwards does not.
27644        tree.record_successful_exec(parent);
27645        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, late_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
27646        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, usr1_child), libc::SIGUSR1);
27647        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
27648        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
27649
27650        // The child's own exec: SIGCHLD for both.
27651        tree.record_successful_exec(late_child);
27652        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, late_child), libc::SIGCHLD);
27653        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
27654        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(DetPid::from_raw(999)), None);
27655    }
27656
27657    /// The exit-notification classifier reads the effective notification
27658    /// signal: a clone(SIGUSR1) child that exec'd notifies with SIGCHLD, so an
27659    /// ignored SIGCHLD is classified (here Discard) rather than left Undecided.
27660    #[test]
27661    fn child_exit_notification_uses_the_effective_exit_signal() {
27662        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27663            true,
27664            libc::SIGUSR1,
27665            Some("read"),
27666            Some((false, false, false)),
27667        );
27668        assert_eq!(
27669            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
27670            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
27671        );
27672        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
27673        assert_eq!(
27674            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
27675            ChildExitNotification::Discard
27676        );
27677    }

27679    /// For an ignored notification the exit grant arms no synthetic SIGCHLD
27680    /// and holds every turn until the backend reports the kernel published
27681    /// the exit; caught, blocked and unclassifiable notifications keep the
27682    /// timer, as does a backend that makes no publication report.
27683    #[test]
27684    fn ignored_child_exit_holds_turns_instead_of_arming_the_timer() {
27685        for masks in [(true, false, false), (false, false, false)] {
27686            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
27687                child_exit_fixture(true, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), Some(masks));
27688            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
27689            assert!(!child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child), "{masks:?}");
27690            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
27691            assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(DetPid::from_raw(999)));
27692            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
27693            assert!(scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
27694            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{masks:?}");
27695        }
27696        for (reports, masks) in [
27697            (true, Some((false, true, false))),
27698            (true, Some((false, false, true))),
27699            (true, Option::None),
27700            (false, Some((false, false, false))),
27701        ] {
27702            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
27703                child_exit_fixture(reports, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), masks);
27704            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
27705            assert!(
27706                child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child),
27707                "{reports} {masks:?}"
27708            );
27709            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
27710        }
27711    }

27713    /// An exit_group from a thread that, in the thread tree, leads its own
27714    /// process but names another process (as ptrace did for a raw clone child
27715    /// with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal, naming it by its creator's pid, before
27716    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/992) does not end the named
27717    /// process, which is never reported consumed. It must keep the synthetic
27718    /// timer and install no hold, which would stop every turn for good.
27719    #[test]
27720    fn an_exit_that_names_another_process_installs_no_hold() {
27721        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27722            true,
27723            libc::SIGCHLD,
27724            Some("read"),
27725            Some((false, false, false)),
27726        );
27727        let clone_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
27728        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
27729            child,
27730            clone_child,
27731            true,
27732            false,
27733            libc::SIGUSR1,
27734        );
27735        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
27736            clone_child,
27737            ThreadNextTurn {
27738                dettid: clone_child,
27739                child_tid_addr: 0,
27740                req: Ivar::new(),
27741                resp: Ivar::new(),
27742                protocol: Default::default(),
27743            },
27744        );
27745        scheduler.priorities.insert(clone_child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
27746        grant_group_exit_from(&mut scheduler, clone_child, child);
27747        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
27748        assert!(child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child));
27749        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());

27752    /// A process consumed before its Exit request is granted (killed while
27753    /// the request is queued) is reported first. The stale grant must install
27754    /// no hold, since no report is left to release it; a retired leader's
27755    /// early report is forgotten.
27756    #[test]
27757    fn a_publication_reported_before_the_grant_installs_no_hold() {
27758        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27759            true,
27760            libc::SIGCHLD,
27761            Some("read"),
27762            Some((false, false, false)),
27763        );
27764        assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
27765        grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
27766        assert!(!child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child));
27767        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
27768        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_completed.is_empty());
27769        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
27770
27771        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27772            true,
27773            libc::SIGCHLD,
27774            Some("read"),
27775            Some((false, false, false)),
27776        );
27777        assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
27778        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
27779        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_completed.is_empty());
27780    }

27782    /// The victim of a committed SIGKILL has a parent that catches SIGCHLD, so
27783    /// the kernel will send the parent its own copy. The commit installs the
27784    /// publication hold and arms the scheduler's CLD_KILLED copy, and the
27785    /// sender's `kill` is not settled once the victim's exit is accounted, only
27786    /// once the kernel's publication is reported too
27787    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994).
27788    #[test]
27789    fn a_delivered_sigkill_notification_waits_for_the_kernels_publication() {
27790        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27791            true,
27792            libc::SIGCHLD,
27793            Some("read"),
27794            Some((false, true, false)),
27795        );
27796        scheduler.record_thread_mm(child, MmId::initial(child));
27797        let token = scheduler
27798            .reserve_sigkill(parent, child, 1000)
27799            .unwrap()
27800            .token;
27801        let victims = scheduler.commit_sigkill(token, true);
27802        assert!(
27803            scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.contains(&child),
27804            "no publication hold"
27805        );
27806        assert!(
27807            child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child),
27808            "no CLD_KILLED copy"
27809        );
27810
27811        assert_eq!(
27812            scheduler.route_sigkill_receipt(child),
27813            sigkill_retirement::SigkillReceipt::Committed
27814        );
27815        assert!(
27816            !scheduler.sigkill_settled(&victims),
27817            "settled before the kernel's publication"
27818        );
27819        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
27820        assert!(scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
27821        assert!(scheduler.sigkill_settled(&victims));
27822        // When its timer fires, the scheduler's copy is sent and, delivered,
27823        // carries the siginfo Linux gives the parent.
27824        assert_eq!(
27825            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
27826            Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send)
27827        );
27828        let answer = scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
27829            parent,
27830            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl::TakeOwnCopy,
27831        );
27832        assert!(
27833            matches!(
27834                answer,
27835                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(
27836                    child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Deliver(info)
27837                ) if info == child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
27838                    code: libc::CLD_KILLED,
27839                    pid: child.as_raw(),
27840                    uid: 1000,
27841                    status: libc::SIGKILL,
27842                }
27843            ),
27844            "{answer:?}"
27845        );
27846    }

27848    #[test]
27849    fn a_publication_reported_before_a_sigkill_commit_installs_no_hold() {

27869    /// Only an internal polling probe or a child wait is classified; a parent
27870    /// in rt_sigsuspend, with a signal in flight, or in any other wait is
27871    /// Undecided and keeps the synthetic SIGCHLD.
27872    #[test]
27873    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_in_covered_parent_states() {
27874        let classify_with = |resource: ResourceID, fyi: &str, sigsuspend: bool| {
27875            let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
27876                true,
27877                libc::SIGCHLD,
27878                Some("read"),
27879                Some((false, false, false)),
27880            );
27881            let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
27882            request.insert(resource, Permission::W);
27883            request.fyi(fyi);
27884            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
27885            if sigsuspend {
27886                scheduler
27887                    .blocked
27888                    .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
27889                    .insert(parent, crate::resources::ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1));
27890            }
27891            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
27892        };
27893        let wait = ResourceID::WaitChild {
27894            parent: DetPid::from_raw(100),
27895            spec: crate::types::ChildWaitSpec {
27896                selector: crate::types::ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
27897                owner: Option::None,
27898                exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
27899            },
27900        };
27901        assert_eq!(
27902            classify_with(wait, "wait-child-lifecycle", false),
27903            ChildExitNotification::Discard
27904        );
27905        assert_eq!(
27906            classify_with(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, "read", true),
27907            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
27908        );
27909        assert_eq!(
27910            classify_with(
27911                ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)),
27912                "",
27913                false
27914            ),
27915            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
27916        );
27917        assert_eq!(
27918            classify_with(ResourceID::FutexWait, "futex_wait", false),
27919            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
