27923    #[test]
27924    fn final_child_exit_does_not_block_parent_timer() {
27925        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
27926            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
27927            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
27928        });
27929        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
27930        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
27931        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
27932        let deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
27933        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
27934        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
27935        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
27936        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
27937        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
27938            parent,
27939            ThreadNextTurn {
27940                dettid: parent,
27941                child_tid_addr: 0,
27942                req: Ivar::new(),
27943                resp: Ivar::new(),
27944                protocol: Default::default(),
27945            },
27946        );
27947        scheduler.priorities.insert(parent, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
27948        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, parent);
27949
27950        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
27951        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27952        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
27953        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
27954        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
27955        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
27956        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
27957    }

27959    type LoopProbe = Box<dyn FnMut(SchedLoopPoint, &mut Scheduler)>;
27960
27961    thread_local! {
27962        static LOOP_PROBE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<LoopProbe>> =
27963            const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
27964    }
27965
27966    /// Called by [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] in test builds. The probe is
27967    /// thread-local, so only a daemon loop polled on the installing test's own
27968    /// thread (a current-thread runtime) reaches it.
27969    pub(super) fn fire_loop_probe(point: SchedLoopPoint, sched: &mut Scheduler) {
27970        // Taken out while it runs, so the probe may use the scheduler freely.
27971        let Some(mut probe) = LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take()) else {
27972            return;
27973        };
27974        probe(point, sched);
27975        LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| {
27976            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
27977            if slot.is_none() {
27978                *slot = Some(probe);
27979            }
27980        });
27981    }
27982
27983    /// Uninstalls the loop probe when the test ends, including by panic.
27984    struct LoopProbeGuard;
27985
27986    impl LoopProbeGuard {
27987        fn install(probe: LoopProbe) -> Self {
27988            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| *slot.borrow_mut() = Some(probe));
27989            LoopProbeGuard
27990        }
27991    }
27992
27993    impl Drop for LoopProbeGuard {
27994        fn drop(&mut self) {
27995            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take());
27996        }
27997    }
27998
27999    /// Records, in order, the text of every INFO event from
28000    /// `detcore::scheduler`: the stream the L2 verify comparator reads.
28001    ///
28002    /// It is a thread-scoped subscriber, so a test that reads it must start
28003    /// with `exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test`. `tracing` caches
28004    /// callsite interest for the whole process, and a parallel in-process test
28005    /// that reaches a scheduler callsite with no subscriber can cache `never`
28006    /// and drop a real record from this capture
28007    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3366).
28008    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
28009    struct SchedulerInfoLog(Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>);
28010
28011    struct MessageText(Option<String>);
28012
28013    impl tracing::field::Visit for MessageText {
28014        fn record_debug(&mut self, field: &tracing::field::Field, value: &dyn std::fmt::Debug) {
28015            if field.name() == "message" {
28016                self.0 = Some(format!("{value:?}"));
28017            }
28018        }
28019    }
28020
28021    impl tracing::Subscriber for SchedulerInfoLog {
28022        fn register_callsite(
28023            &self,
28024            _: &'static tracing::Metadata<'static>,
28025        ) -> tracing::subscriber::Interest {
28026            tracing::subscriber::Interest::sometimes()
28027        }
28028
28029        fn enabled(&self, metadata: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
28030            *metadata.level() == Level::INFO
28031        }
28032
28033        fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
28034            tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
28035        }
28036
28037        fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
28038
28039        fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
28040
28041        fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
28042            if !event.metadata().target().starts_with("detcore::scheduler") {
28043                return;
28044            }
28045            let mut text = MessageText(None);
28046            event.record(&mut text);
28047            if let Some(text) = text.0 {
28048                self.0.lock().unwrap().push(text);
28049            }
28050        }
28051
28052        fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
28053
28054        fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
28055    }
28056
28057    /// What one daemon run to shutdown shows: its scheduler INFO lines, in
28058    /// order, and the logical state it leaves.
28059    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
28060    struct ShutdownObservation {
28061        scheduler_info: Vec<String>,
28062        turn: u64,
28063        global_time: LogicalTime,
28064    }
28065
28066    const FIZZLE: &str = "zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.";
28067    const SCHED_LOOP_EXIT: &str = "[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.";
28068
28069    /// Run the real daemon loop, `sched_loop`, from the state `setup` builds
28070    /// until it exits. When the loop reaches `landing` -- (pass number, point)
28071    /// -- run `report` there, inside that lock hold, as a backend thread that
28072    /// took the scheduler lock at that moment would. Returns the observation
28073    /// and whether `report` ran.
28074    async fn run_daemon_to_shutdown(
28075        config: &Config,
28076        setup: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler),
28077        landing: Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>,
28078        report: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler) + 'static,
28079    ) -> (ShutdownObservation, bool) {
28080        let log = SchedulerInfoLog::default();
28081        let _subscriber = tracing::subscriber::set_default(log.clone());
28082        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(config)));
28083        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(config)));
28084        {
28085            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
28086            setup(&mut s);
28087            s.started_up.try_put(());
28088        }
28089
28090        let landed = std::rc::Rc::new(std::cell::Cell::new(false));
28091        let probe: LoopProbe = {
28092            let landed = landed.clone();
28093            let mut report = Some(report);
28094            let mut pass = 0u64;
28095            Box::new(move |point, s| {
28096                if point == SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop {
28097                    pass += 1;
28098                    // A hang guard, not a timing assumption: every schedule
28099                    // here exits by its third pass.
28100                    assert!(pass <= 8, "the daemon loop did not exit in 8 passes");
28101                }
28102                if landing == Some((pass, point))
28103                    && let Some(report) = report.take()
28104                {
28105                    report(s);
28106                    landed.set(true);
28107                }
28108            })
28109        };
28110        let _probe = LoopProbeGuard::install(probe);
28111        sched_loop(sched.clone(), global_time.clone()).await;
28112
28113        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
28114        assert!(s.run_queue.is_empty());
28115        assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
28116        assert!(s.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
28117        let observation = ShutdownObservation {
28118            scheduler_info: log.0.lock().unwrap().clone(),
28119            turn: s.turn,
28120            global_time: global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
28121        };
28122        (observation, landed.get())
28123    }
28124
28125    /// Each point a host-timed report can land in the daemon's last two passes:
28126    /// the pass that drains the last thread's removal, and the pass after it.
28127    const SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS: [(u64, SchedLoopPoint); 6] = [
28128        (1, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
28129        (1, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
28130        (1, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
28131        (2, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
28132        (2, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
28133        (2, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
28134    ];
28135
28136    /// Every run must match the first exactly, and the first must report the
28137    /// empty state once, as its last line before the loop exits.
28138    fn assert_one_shutdown_log(runs: &[(Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>, ShutdownObservation)]) {
28139        let fizzles = |observation: &ShutdownObservation| {
28140            observation
28141                .scheduler_info
28142                .iter()
28143                .filter(|line| line.contains(FIZZLE))
28144                .count()
28145        };
28146        // Every landing's count, so a failure shows the whole pattern.
28147        let counts = runs
28148            .iter()
28149            .map(|(landing, observation)| (*landing, fizzles(observation)))
28150            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
28151        let (first, canonical) = &runs[0];
28152        assert_eq!(
28153            fizzles(canonical),
28154            1,
28155            "landing at {first:?} must log the empty state once; fizzle lines per landing: \
28156             {counts:?}; {canonical:#?}"
28157        );
28158        let tail = &canonical.scheduler_info[canonical.scheduler_info.len() - 2..];
28159        assert!(
28160            tail[0].contains(FIZZLE) && tail[1] == SCHED_LOOP_EXIT,
28161            "the empty state must be reported just before the loop exits: {canonical:#?}"
28162        );
28163        for (landing, observation) in &runs[1..] {
28164            assert_eq!(
28165                observation, canonical,
28166                "a report landing at {landing:?} instead of {first:?} changed the scheduler's \
28167                 INFO log or logical state; fizzle lines per landing: {counts:?}"
28168            );
28169        }
28170    }
28171
28172    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360: on SaBRe the last
28173    /// thread's logical exit opens a physical-exit barrier, and the ptrace
28174    /// supervisor closes it when the kernel's final wait status arrives -- a
28175    /// host-timed moment. Before the fix the empty-queue step logged its
28176    /// "fizzling" line only when that status had already landed by the time the
28177    /// step ran, so the line appeared zero or one times depending on the host.
28178    /// Land it at every point of the last two passes; the scheduler's INFO log
28179    /// and state must not change.
28180    #[tokio::test]
28181    async fn sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands() {
28182        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
28183        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
28184            module_path!(),
28185            "sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands",
28186        ) {
28187            return;
28188        }
28189        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
28190            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
28191            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
28192        });
28193        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28194        let mut runs = Vec::new();
28195        for landing in SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS {
28196            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
28197                &config,
28198                |s| {
28199                    s.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
28200                    register_known_thread(s, root);
28201                    // step6 re-enqueued the thread after its committed
28202                    // `exit_group` turn; then its exit hook ran.
28203                    s.runqueue_push_back(root);
28204                    s.logically_kill_thread(&root, &root, MmId::initial(root));
28205                    assert_eq!(s.pending_physical_process_exits, BTreeSet::from([root]));
28206                },
28207                Some(landing),
28208                move |s| assert!(s.complete_physical_process_exit(root)),
28209            )
28210            .await;
28211            assert!(landed, "the final wait status never landed at {landing:?}");
28212            runs.push((Some(landing), observation));
28213        }
28214        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
28215    }
28216
28217    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223, the same defect on
28218    /// ptrace: a worker's `exit_group` logically kills its parked sibling at
28219    /// once, and the kernel's physical kill later runs the sibling's exit hook,
28220    /// which calls `logically_kill_thread` again. The second call finds nothing
28221    /// to remove but still queues a removal, which the daemon must drain
28222    /// before it may exit. Before the fix, if that arrived after the empty-queue
28223    /// step had logged its line, the drain pass logged it a second time. Land
28224    /// it at every reachable point, and after the loop has exited (`None`); the
28225    /// scheduler's INFO log and state must not change.
28226    #[tokio::test]
28227    async fn redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands() {
28228        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
28229        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
28230            module_path!(),
28231            "redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands",
28232        ) {
28233            return;
28234        }
28235        let config = Config::default();
28236        assert!(!config.backend.reports_physical_process_exits);
28237        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28238        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(4);
28239        // With no physical-exit barrier the loop exits at the top of pass 2,
28240        // before pass 2's empty-queue step, so those two points are unreachable.
28241        let landings = SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS[..4]
28242            .iter()
28243            .copied()
28244            .map(Some)
28245            .chain([None]);
28246        let mut runs = Vec::new();
28247        for landing in landings {
28248            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
28249                &config,
28250                |s| {
28251                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
28252                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
28253                    register_known_thread(s, leader);
28254                    register_known_thread(s, worker);
28255                    // step6 re-enqueued the worker after its committed
28256                    // `exit_group` turn. The leader is parked, not queued.
28257                    s.runqueue_push_back(worker);
28258                    // After granting the exit, `finish_resource_response`
28259                    // logically kills the sibling; then the worker's own exit
28260                    // hook kills the worker.
28261                    s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
28262                    s.logically_kill_thread(&worker, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
28263                },
28264                landing,
28265                // The kernel's kill of the leader runs its exit hook.
28266                move |s| s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader)),
28267            )
28268            .await;
28269            assert_eq!(
28270                landed,
28271                landing.is_some(),
28272                "the redundant exit hook landed wrongly for {landing:?}"
28273            );
28274            runs.push((landing, observation));
28275        }
28276        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
28277    }

28282            .unwrap()

28284            .unwrap();
28285        HbRuntime::new(program)

28288    /// A spec whose only edge gates dettid 5 on dettid 3, for the empty-queue
28289    /// tests below.
28290    const HB_GATE_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
28291        "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
28292                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
28293        "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;

28295    /// A source fired and opened a parked thread's gate (`wake_pending`), and
28296    /// the source thread then left the run queue: the maintenance prefix must
28297    /// re-admit the parked thread before the empty-queue step classifies the
28298    /// state, not leave it to be reported as a deadlock
28299    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
28300    #[test]
28301    fn empty_queue_step_readmits_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_opened() {
28302        let config = Config::default();
28303        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
28304        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
28305        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28306        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
28307        hb.fired.insert("src".to_owned());
28308        hb.parked.insert(target);
28309        hb.wake_pending = true;
28310        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
28311        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
28312
28313        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28314        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_ok());
28315        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
28316        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
28317        assert!(hb.parked.is_empty() && !hb.wake_pending);
28318        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28319    }

28321    /// The nearby case that must NOT wake: the target is parked and no source
28322    /// has fired, nothing else can run, so no anchor can ever fire. The
28323    /// empty-queue step must report a terminal deadlock naming the gate rather
28324    /// than treat the scheduler as empty (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
28325    #[test]
28326    fn empty_queue_step_reports_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_cannot_open() {
28327        let config = Config::default();
28328        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
28329        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
28330        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28331        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
28332        hb.parked.insert(target);
28333        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
28334
28335        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
28336        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
28337        let report = scheduler
28338            .take_terminal_deadlock()
28339            .expect("a parked thread with no possible source must be a reported deadlock");
28340        assert!(
28341            report.contains("held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire"),
28342            "{report}"
28343        );
28344    }

28346    /// A signal the scheduler sends to a thread held at a happens-before gate
28347    /// (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) must leave the thread held, with its
28348    /// gate's checkpoint request intact. The held thread used to be reported as
28349    /// gone, which panicked `wake_signaled_guest` and hung the run; and had it
28350    /// been force-unblocked, the substituted request would have let it past
28351    /// its gate before the source fired.
28352    #[test]
28353    fn signal_to_a_thread_held_at_a_gate_leaves_it_held() {
28354        let config = Config::default();
28355        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
28356        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28357        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
28358        hb.parked.insert(target);
28359        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
28360        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
28361        let mut gate = Resources::new(target);
28362        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43), Permission::R);
28363        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
28364            target,
28365            ThreadNextTurn {
28366                dettid: target,
28367                child_tid_addr: 0,
28368                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
28369                resp: Ivar::new(),
28370                protocol: Default::default(),
28371            },
28372        );
28373
28374        assert!(matches!(
28375            scheduler.thread_status(target),
28376            ThreadStatus::NotRunning
28377        ));
28378        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
28379
28380        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
28381        assert!(
28382            scheduler
28383                .happens_before
28384                .as_ref()
28385                .unwrap()
28386                .parked
28387                .contains(&target)
28388        );
28389        let request = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
28390            .req
28391            .try_read()
28392            .expect("the held thread's request is still filled")
28393            .expect("the held thread's request is not an error");
28394        assert!(
28395            request
28396                .resources
28397                .contains_key(&ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43))
28398                && request.resources.len() == 1,
28399            "the gate's checkpoint request was replaced: {:?}",
28400            request.resources.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()
28401        );
28402    }

28404    /// One syscall can reach a count anchor and a syscall-occurrence anchor at
28405    /// once (the commit claims both are evaluated): the checkpoint must fire
28406    /// both. Of the occurrence anchors the guest names, only those on this
28407    /// thread fire; a spawn-ordinal anchor that resolves to another thread, and
28408    /// a name that is not an anchor, are ignored.
28409    #[test]
28410    fn checkpoint_fires_count_and_occurrence_anchors_reached_at_one_syscall() {
28411        let config = Config::default();
28412        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
28413        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
28414            r#"{"version": 1,
28415                "threads": {"S2": {"spawn_ordinal": 2}},
28416                "events": {"count": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 13},
28417                           "occ": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2},
28418                           "other": {"thread": "S2", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}}}"#,
28419        ));
28420        let named = ["occ", "other", "missing"].map(str::to_owned);
28421        assert!(
28422            scheduler
28423                .hb_checkpoint(DetTid::from_raw(5), 13, &named)
28424                .is_ok()
28425        );
28426        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
28427        let fired: Vec<&str> = hb.fired.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
28428        assert_eq!(fired, ["count", "occ"]);
28429        assert!(hb.wake_pending);
28430    }

28432    /// A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired is refused by name when the
28433    /// run finishes, with its position and the edges that use it. A count
28434    /// anchor that never fired is not part of the refusal (unchanged behavior),
28435    /// and once every occurrence anchor has fired there is nothing to refuse.
28436    #[test]
28437    fn unfired_occurrence_anchor_is_reported_by_name() {
28438        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
28439            r#"{"version": 1,
28440                "events": {"c": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
28441                           "w": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}},
28442                "edges": [{"before": "c", "after": "w", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
28443        );
28444        let report = hb
28445            .unfired_occurrence_report()
28446            .expect("an unfired occurrence anchor must be refused");
28447        assert!(
28448            report.starts_with("HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: 1 happens-before"),
28449            "{report}"
28450        );
28451        assert!(
28452            report.contains("anchor 'w' on thread 5: writev(fd=9)#2 never fired (edges: c -> w)"),
28453            "{report}"
28454        );
28455        assert!(!report.contains("anchor 'c'"), "{report}");
28456        hb.fired.insert("w".to_owned());
28457        assert!(hb.unfired_occurrence_report().is_none());
28458    }

28460    /// A version-2 spec that holds dettid 5 at its 43rd syscall until both
28461    /// sources fire, with an unrelated anchor on dettid 7 and a 1000 ns budget.
28462    const HB_BUDGET_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,
28463        "events": {"src1": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
28464                   "src2": {"thread": "4", "syscalls": 42},
28465                   "other": {"thread": "7", "syscalls": 9},
28466                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
28467        "edges": [{"before": "src1", "after": "dst"},
28468                  {"before": "src2", "after": "dst"}]}"#;
28469
28470    /// Select `dettid` as step3 would and let it reach its checkpoint at
28471    /// syscall `count`, at committed time `now_ns`.
28472    fn hb_reach(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, dettid: DetTid, count: u64, now_ns: u64) -> bool {
28473        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(now_ns);
28474        scheduler
28475            .priorities
28476            .entry(dettid)
28477            .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
28478        if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
28479            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
28480        }
28481        scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(dettid).unwrap();
28482        let granted = scheduler.hb_checkpoint(dettid, count, &[]).is_ok();
28483        if granted {
28484            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
28485        }
28486        granted
28487    }
28488
28489    /// A posthook anchor on the same thread as an entry that returned an
28490    /// internal restart code is refused by name and does not fire, the turn
28491    /// grants nothing (the thread leaves the run queue), and the thread it
28492    /// gates stays held; an earlier pending verdict is kept. A spawn-ordinal
28493    /// anchor the guest named at another thread's interrupted call is not on
28494    /// that thread, and its turn proceeds (the Claude review of
28495    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048). A completed entry's
28496    /// posthook checkpoint fires it like a prehook one
28497    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929).
28498    #[test]
28499    fn an_interrupted_posthook_anchor_is_refused_and_does_not_fire() {
28500        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
28501            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
28502            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
28503                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
28504                                       "phase": "posthook"},
28505                       "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
28506            "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;
28507        let source = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28508        let anchors = ["src".to_owned()];
28509        let interrupt = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, anchors: &[String]| {
28510            scheduler
28511                .priorities
28512                .entry(source)
28513                .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
28514            if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source) {
28515                scheduler.runqueue_push_back(source);
28516            }
28517            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(source).unwrap();
28518            let granted = scheduler
28519                .hb_posthook_interrupted(source, 9, anchors, "ERESTARTSYS")
28520                .is_ok();
28521            if granted {
28522                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
28523            }
28524            granted
28525        };
28526        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28527        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
28528        // The helper's spawn-ordinal anchor, named at dtid 3's call: not on
28529        // dtid 3, so nothing is refused and the turn proceeds.
28530        assert!(interrupt(&mut scheduler, &["helper_wait".to_owned()]));
28531        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
28532        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
28533        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source));
28534        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
28535        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().fired.is_empty());
28536        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
28537        assert_eq!(
28538            scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(),
28539            "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid 3 reached posthook happens-before anchor(s) \
28540             [\"src\"] at syscall count 9, and the call was interrupted (ERESTARTSYS); whether \
28541             it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
28542             checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook or \
28543             on a call that is not interrupted."
28544        );
28545
28546        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28547        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
28548        scheduler.terminal_deadlock = Some("earlier".to_owned());
28549        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
28550        assert_eq!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(), "earlier");
28551
28552        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28553        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
28554        assert!(scheduler.hb_checkpoint(source, 9, &anchors).is_ok());
28555        assert!(
28556            scheduler
28557                .happens_before
28558                .as_ref()
28559                .unwrap()
28560                .fired
28561                .contains("src")
28562        );
28563        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
28564    }
28565
28566    /// Through a whole turn (`block_for_one_resource`): an interrupted entry
28567    /// whose posthook anchor is on its thread commits no turn and gets no
28568    /// response, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit; one whose
28569    /// only anchor is another thread's spawn-ordinal anchor is an ordinary
28570    /// turn (the Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048).
28571    #[tokio::test]
28572    async fn an_interrupted_posthook_refusal_grants_no_turn() {
28573        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
28574            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
28575            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
28576                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
28577                                       "phase": "posthook"}}}"#;
28578        for (anchor, refused) in [("helper_wait", false), ("src", true)] {
28579            let config = Config::default();
28580            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
28581            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
28582            let thread = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28583            register_known_thread(&mut sched, thread);
28584            sched.runqueue_push_back(thread);
28585            let mut request = Resources::new(thread);
28586            request.insert(
28587                ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
28588                    count: 9,
28589                    anchors: vec![anchor.to_owned()],
28590                    code: "ERESTARTSYS".to_owned(),
28591                },
28592                Permission::R,
28593            );
28594            sched.next_turns[&thread].req.put(Ok(request));
28595            let response = sched.next_turns[&thread].resp.clone();
28596            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
28597            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
28598            let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
28599                Duration::from_secs(5),
28600                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
28601            )
28602            .await
28603            .expect("the turn must not stall");
28604            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
28605            assert_eq!(outcome.is_err(), refused, "{anchor}: {outcome:?}");
28606            assert_eq!(response.try_read().is_none(), refused, "{anchor}");
28607            assert_eq!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some(), refused, "{anchor}");
28608        }
28609    }
28610
28611    /// The hold budget is charged in committed virtual time from the moment
28612    /// the thread is first parked. A wake caused by an unrelated anchor, and a
28613    /// gate only partly opened, re-park the thread without restarting its
28614    /// hold; past the budget the run is refused by name, naming the BEFORE
28615    /// anchor still missing. The check runs in `step2_drain_prefix`, which both
28616    /// turn loops call before selection.
28617    #[test]
28618    fn a_hold_is_charged_from_its_first_park_and_refused_past_its_budget() {
28619        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28620        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
28621        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28622        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
28623        let hold = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held].clone();
28624        assert_eq!(hold.since_ns, 5000);
28625
28626        // An unrelated anchor fires: the wake re-admits and clears the
28627        // physical park, and the thread re-parks; the hold is unchanged.
28628        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(7), 9, 5200));
28629        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28630        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().parked.is_empty());
28631        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5500));
28632        // One of two sources fires: still held, still the same hold.
28633        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5600));
28634        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28635        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5700));
28636        assert_eq!(
28637            scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held],
28638            hold
28639        );
28640
28641        // Exactly the budget is not over it.
28642        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6000);
28643        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28644        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28645        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6001);
28646        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
28647        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
28648        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
28649        assert_eq!(
28650            report,
28651            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid 5 has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
28652             [\"dst\"] for more than max_hold_ns = 1000 virtual ns, waiting on:\n  anchor 'src2' \
28653             on thread 4: after 42 syscalls never fired (edge src2 -> dst)"
28654        );
28655    }
28656
28657    /// A hold that ends inside its budget is gone: once the gate opens and the
28658    /// thread passes, no later committed time can refuse it. A version-1 spec
28659    /// has no budget at all.
28660    #[test]
28661    fn a_released_hold_and_a_version_1_hold_are_never_refused() {
28662        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28663        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
28664        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28665        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
28666        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
28667        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
28668        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28669        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5300));
28670        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
28671        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
28672        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28673        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28674
28675        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28676        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
28677            &HB_BUDGET_SPEC.replace(r#""version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,"#, r#""version": 1,"#),
28678        ));
28679        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
28680        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(u64::MAX / 2);
28681        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28682        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28683    }

28685    /// A non-leader exec hands the caller's task the leader's identity. When a
28686    /// relative anchor (with its base, on the same thread) is on either
28687    /// identity, the handoff is refused by name; any other exec is unaffected.
28688    #[test]
28689    fn a_non_leader_exec_on_a_relative_anchors_thread_is_refused() {
28690        let hb = hb_runtime(
28691            r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
28692                "m": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 2},
28693                "r": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"},
28694                "x": {"thread": "8", "syscall": "getppid"}}}"#,
28695        );
28696        let tid = DetTid::from_raw;
28697        let expected = |caller: i32, leader: i32| {
28698            format!(
28699                "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {caller} execs and takes \
28700                 over the identity of dtid {leader}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' \
28701                 (from 'm') are on these threads; relative anchors are not carried across a \
28702                 non-leader exec."
28703            )
28704        };
28705        // The relative anchor's thread is the leader that is replaced...
28706        assert_eq!(
28707            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(7), tid(5)),
28708            Some(expected(7, 5))
28709        );
28710        // ...or the worker whose task takes over.
28711        assert_eq!(
28712            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(5), tid(9)),
28713            Some(expected(5, 9))
28714        );
28715        // An absolute anchor alone on either thread is not affected.
28716        assert_eq!(hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(8), tid(9)), None);
28717    }
28718
28719    /// A version-2 spec with a relative anchor (and its base) on dettid 17.
28720    const HB_RELATIVE_ON_17: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
28721        "m": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 1},
28722        "r": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"}}}"#;
28723
28724    /// The refusal goes through the real exec-reconnect handlers: a non-leader
28725    /// exec on the relative anchor's identity is recorded as a policy refusal
28726    /// on both the ordinary and the transferred path, while a same-identity
28727    /// exec (the leader itself execs) keeps the anchor and is not refused.
28728    #[test]
28729    fn exec_reconnect_refuses_a_relative_anchor_only_across_a_non_leader_exec() {
28730        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
28731        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
28732        for transferred in [false, true] {
28733            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28734            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
28735            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
28736            if transferred {
28737                reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
28738            } else {
28739                reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
28740            }
28741            assert!(sched.terminal_is_refusal, "transferred: {transferred}");
28742            let report = sched.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
28743            assert!(
28744                report.starts_with(
28745                    "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid 18 execs and takes over \
28746                     the identity of dtid 17, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' (from 'm')"
28747                ),
28748                "transferred: {transferred}: {report}"
28749            );
28750        }
28751
28752        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28753        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
28754        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
28755        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, leader, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
28756        assert!(sched.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28757        assert!(!sched.terminal_is_refusal);
28758    }
28759
28760    /// Once the exec reconnect has recorded the identity refusal, the next
28761    /// turn grants nothing: an unrelated thread waiting at an ordinary request
28762    /// gets no response, so no guest runs concurrently with the policy exit.
28763    /// (Adopted from the review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4004.)
28764    #[tokio::test]
28765    async fn the_identity_refusal_grants_no_further_turn() {
28766        let config = Config::default();
28767        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
28768        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
28769        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
28770        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
28771        let other = DetTid::from_raw(31);
28772        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
28773        register_known_thread(&mut sched, other);
28774        sched.runqueue_push_back(other);
28775        let mut pending = Resources::new(other);
28776        pending.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(other), Permission::RW);
28777        sched.next_turns[&other].req.put(Ok(pending));
28778        let other_response = sched.next_turns[&other].resp.clone();
28779
28780        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
28781        assert!(sched.terminal_deadlock.is_some() && sched.terminal_is_refusal);
28782        sched.next_turns[&leader]
28783            .req
28784            .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
28785
28786        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
28787        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
28788        let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
28789            Duration::from_secs(5),
28790            do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
28791        )
28792        .await
28793        .expect("the turn must not stall");
28794        assert!(outcome.is_err(), "a turn was committed: {outcome:?}");
28795        assert!(
28796            other_response.try_read().is_none(),
28797            "dtid 31 was granted a turn after the identity refusal was recorded"
28798        );
28799        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
28800        assert_eq!(s.turn, 0);
28801        assert!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some());
28802    }
28803
28804    /// A held thread that is removed (killed) leaves no hold behind, so a
28805    /// later committed time cannot refuse the run for it.
28806    #[test]
28807    fn a_removed_held_thread_leaves_no_hold_behind() {
28808        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28809        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
28810        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28811        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
28812        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&held);
28813        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
28814        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
28815        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28816        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28817    }

28819    /// A hold whose gate has opened is not refused while the re-admitted
28820    /// thread waits to be selected again, however late that is.
28821    #[test]
28822    fn an_opened_gate_is_not_refused_before_its_thread_runs_again() {
28823        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28824        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
28825        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28826        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
28827        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
28828        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
28829        // The hold record stays until the thread passes its checkpoint.
28830        assert!(
28831            scheduler
28832                .happens_before
28833                .as_ref()
28834                .unwrap()
28835                .holds
28836                .contains_key(&held)
28837        );
28838        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
28839        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
28840        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
28841    }

28843    /// A relative anchor that never fired is reported with its base, and the
28844    /// report says when that base never fired either.

28846    fn an_unfired_relative_anchor_names_its_base() {

28865            ),

28870    /// A thread-group leader's own `exit` retires it while its group lives on,
28871    /// so the scheduler stops waiting for a turn request from a zombie that
28872    /// makes none (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100). Only
28873    /// where the scheduler models signal targets (ptrace), only a leader of
28874    /// this incarnation that is still registered, only after its exit was
28875    /// granted, and only while another thread of its group is registered. It
28876    /// then holds turns until the kernel shows it a zombie; its process does
28877    /// not end there, and its later deregistration finds it retired once. A
28878    /// leader alone in its group is left to its deregistration, and a new
28879    /// thread on its tid starts clean.
28880    #[test]
28881    fn an_exited_leader_with_a_live_sibling_leaves_the_scheduler_at_its_exit() {
28882        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28883        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
28884        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28885        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
28886        let process = DetPid::from_raw(3);
28887        let mm = MmId::initial(process);
28888        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
28889        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
28890        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
28891        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, worker);
28892
28893        // No granted exit yet.
28894        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
28895        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
28896        // A non-leader is not retired here, even with its exit granted.
28897        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(worker);
28898        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(worker, mm));
28899        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&worker));
28900        scheduler.committed_exits.remove(&worker);
28901        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(leader);
28902        // Not where the scheduler does not model signal targets.
28903        scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
28904        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
28905        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
28906        // Not from another incarnation of the leader's tid.
28907        let other_image = mm.for_exec(leader);
28908        scheduler.exec_incarnations.insert(leader, other_image);
28909        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
28910        scheduler.exec_incarnations.remove(&leader);
28911        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty());
28912
28913        assert!(scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
28914        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
28915        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&worker));
28916        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.contains_key(&leader));
28917        assert!(!scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
28918        // A leader no longer registered is not retired again.
28919        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
28920        assert!(scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
28921        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
28922
28923        // The worker's own exit then ends the process.
28924        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&worker, &process, mm);
28925        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
28926
28927        // A leader alone in its group is left to its deregistration.
28928        let alone = DetTid::from_raw(7);
28929        let alone_mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(7));
28930        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, alone, true);
28931        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, alone);
28932        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(alone);
28933        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(alone, alone_mm));
28934        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&alone));
28935
28936        // A retired leader's tid registered again starts with no record.
28937        scheduler.retired_exited_leaders.insert(alone);
28938        scheduler.forget_committed_exit(alone);
28939        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(alone));
28940    }
28941
28942    /// After retiring a leader at its own exit, the scheduler commits no turn
28943    /// until the kernel shows the leader a zombie (or dead): its exit, injected
28944    /// after the retirement, releases what a sibling could observe
28945    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100, Claude review of
28946    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245). A leader that never gets
28947    /// there ends the run with a named refusal after the valve.
28948    #[test]
28949    fn turns_wait_until_a_retired_leader_is_a_zombie() {
28950        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
28951        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
28952        scheduler
28953            .exited_leader_barriers
28954            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
28955        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'R');
28956        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_err());
28957        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
28958        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'Z');
28959        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_ok());
28960        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty());
28961
28962        scheduler
28963            .exited_leader_barriers
28964            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
28965        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'X');
28966        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_ok());
28967
28968        scheduler
28969            .exited_leader_barriers
28970            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
28971        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'S');
28972        scheduler.exited_leader_valve = Duration::ZERO;
28973        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_err());
28974        let reason = scheduler.terminal_deadlock.clone().unwrap();
28975        assert!(
28976            reason.contains("thread-group leader 3 was retired at its own exit")
28977                && reason.contains("its state is S"),
28978            "{reason}"
28979        );
28980    }

28982    /// The state letter of a task's stat file is found after the last `)`,
28983    /// whatever bytes the command name holds (Codex review of
28984    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245): an ASCII name, a name
28985    /// with raw non-UTF-8 bytes, and a name containing `)` itself.
28986    #[test]
28987    fn a_task_state_is_read_after_any_command_name() {
28988        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (leader) Z 2 3 3 0 -1"), Some('Z'));
28989        assert_eq!(
28990            task_state_of_stat(b"3 (\xff\xfe\x80) Z 2 3 3 0 -1"),
28991            Some('Z')
28992        );
28993        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (a) b)) S 2 3 3 0"), Some('S'));
28994        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (no state)"), None);
28995        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 leader Z"), None);
28996        // The production reader decodes this process's own stat file.
28997        let own = std::fs::read(format!(
28998            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
28999            std::process::id(),
29000            unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) }
29001        ))
29002        .unwrap();
29003        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(&own), Some('R'));
29004    }

29006    /// A surviving thread that execs after its leader was retired at its own
29007    /// exit takes over the leader's tid with a plain admission: the retired
29008    /// leader's run-queue removal was already drained, so there is no old slot
29009    /// to replace (Claude re-check of
29010    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245; before, the exec
29011    /// hand-over panicked).
29012    #[test]
29013    fn an_exec_after_the_leader_was_retired_at_exit_admits_the_new_leader() {
29014        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29015        sched.models_signal_targets = true;
29016        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
29017        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
29018        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
29019        sched.committed_exits.insert(leader);
29020        assert!(sched.retire_exited_leader(leader, pre_exec_mm));
29021        // The step2 drain after the retirement, and the kernel showing the
29022        // leader a zombie.
29023        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
29024        sched.exited_leader_barriers.clear();
29025        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(leader));
29026
29027        // The exec reaps the zombie leader first, whose deregistration
29028        // consumes its retirement record.
29029        assert!(sched.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
29030
29031        assert!(!sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
29032        // The exec prepares its teardown, which lists only the registered
29033        // siblings: the retired leader is not one.
29034        assert!(sched.prepare_exec_teardown(caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm));
29035
29036        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
29037        // A plain admission: no old slot to replace.
29038        assert!(!sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
29039        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&leader));
29040        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
29041        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
29042        assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
29043        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(leader));
29044        assert!(!sched.next_turns.contains_key(&caller));
29045        // The new incarnation has not exited.
29046        assert!(!sched.committed_exits.contains(&leader));
29047    }
29048
29049    /// The late deregistration of a leader retired at its own exit, which
29050    /// ptrace delivers only after its group has ended, does not end its
29051    /// process again (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). Linux
29052    /// decides at the group's end whether the parent reaps the child
29053    /// automatically, and a later change of the parent's SIGCHLD disposition
29054    /// does not change that.
29055    #[test]
29056    fn a_retired_leaders_late_deregistration_does_not_end_its_process_again() {
29057        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29058        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
29059        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(2);
29060        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29061        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29062        let process = DetPid::from_raw(3);
29063        let mm = MmId::initial(process);
29064        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
29065        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, leader, true);
29066        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
29067        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
29068        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
29069        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, worker);
29070        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(leader);
29071        assert!(scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
29072        // The worker's exit ends the process; the parent does not reap
29073        // automatically.
29074        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(worker, process, mm);
29075        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
29076        assert!(!scheduler.autoreaped_exits.contains(&process));
29077        // The parent then ignores SIGCHLD, and the leader's deregistration
29078        // arrives.
29079        scheduler
29080            .thread_tree
29081            .set_sigchld_disposition(DetPid::from_raw(2), true, false);
29082        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(leader, process, mm);
29083        assert!(!scheduler.autoreaped_exits.contains(&process));
29084        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
29085    }
29086
29087    /// A child wait is part of a deadlock only when every child it could reap
29088    /// has all its live threads held at gates, parked in a futex wait, or
29089    /// waiting with no deadline (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904,
29090    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430). A child thread doing
29091    /// anything else (a wait with a deadline included), an exited child, a
29092    /// child a committed SIGKILL has doomed, a wait with no matching child,
29093    /// and an unnamed SIGKILL keep the wait counted as input that may still
29094    /// arrive; a thread that has exited no longer counts. Whether a thread is
29095    /// held elsewhere in the run does not matter (it did until 4430).
29096    #[test]
29097    fn a_child_wait_settles_only_on_children_held_or_in_futex_waits() {
29098        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29099        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
29100        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29101        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29102        let child_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
29103        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
29104        // The root inherits its process group from outside the namespace; this
29105        // test's root leads its own, as after setpgid(0, 0), so its children's
29106        // group is its pid.
29107        scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(parent, parent);
29108        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
29109        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
29110        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
29111            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
29112            owner: None,
29113            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
29114        };
29115        scheduler
29116            .blocked
29117            .child_waiters
29118            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
29119        let park_in_futex = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, addr: usize| {
29120            let mut futex_request = Resources::new(tid);
29121            futex_request.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::RW);
29122            s.next_turns.get_mut(&tid).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(futex_request));
29123            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(5)), addr);
29124            s.blocked
29125                .futex_waiters
29126                .entry(futex)
29127                .or_default()
29128                .push(futex_waiter(tid.as_raw(), u32::MAX));
29129        };
29130        // No held thread: the child's only thread parked in a futex wait
29131        // settles the wait, as it would with a held thread elsewhere; the
29132        // child's state decides (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430).
29133        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child, 0x404000);
29134        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29135        scheduler.blocked.futex_waiters.clear();
29136        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&child).unwrap().req = Ivar::new();
29137        // Doing anything else, it could still run.
29138        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29139        // Waiting with no deadline (`pause`) it is stuck; with a deadline it
29140        // will wake.
29141        scheduler
29142            .blocked
29143            .timed_waiters
29144            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
29145        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29146        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(child);
29147        scheduler
29148            .blocked
29149            .timed_waiters
29150            .insert(LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000), child);
29151        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29152        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(child);
29153        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29154        let hold = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid| {
29155            s.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().parked.insert(tid);
29156        };
29157        hold(&mut scheduler, child);
29158        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29159
29160        // A thread the child had that is no longer registered: if it left by
29161        // its own committed exit it is gone harmlessly; if it left without one
29162        // (a fatal signal, or a kill of its process), the process is going
29163        // down and the wait is real.
29164        let gone = DetTid::from_raw(8);
29165        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, gone, false);
29166        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29167        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
29168        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29169        // A new thread on that tid has not exited.
29170        scheduler.forget_committed_exit(gone);
29171        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29172        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
29173
29174        // A committed SIGKILL dooms the child: it will die, so the wait is
29175        // real, whenever its host-timed retirement arrives.
29176        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29177        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29178        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
29179        // A SIGKILL named by thread maps to its process.
29180        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, None);
29181        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29182        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
29183        // A process-group kill dooms every process in the group.
29184        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(Some(DetPid::from_raw(3)));
29185        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29186        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29187        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
29188        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29189
29190        // A second child thread that is neither held nor in a futex wait could
29191        // still run.
29192        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, child_worker, false);
29193        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child_worker);
29194        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29195        // Parked in a futex wait, it can only be woken by another thread.
29196        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child_worker, 0x404110);
29197        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29198
29199        // A child that has exited logically is reapable.
29200        scheduler
29201            .logically_exited_processes
29202            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5));
29203        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29204        scheduler
29205            .logically_exited_processes
29206            .remove(&DetPid::from_raw(5));
29207
29208        // A wait that matches no child is left alone.
29209        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
29210            parent,
29211            (
29212                DetPid::from_raw(3),
29213                ChildWaitSpec {
29214                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
29215                    ..spec
29216                },
29217            ),
29218        );
29219        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29220
29221        // A SIGKILL whose victim cannot be named disables settling for good.
29222        scheduler
29223            .blocked
29224            .child_waiters
29225            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
29226        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29227        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(None);
29228        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29229
29230        // Reaping a doomed process drops its record (last: reaping also drops
29231        // the child's wait entry).
29232        scheduler
29233            .thread_tree
29234            .process_parent
29235            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5), DetPid::from_raw(3));
29236        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29237        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29238        scheduler.consume_child_wait(DetPid::from_raw(3), DetPid::from_raw(5));
29239        assert!(!scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29240    }

29242    /// Without a happens-before runtime, a child wait settles on a child whose
29243    /// only thread waits with no deadline or in a futex wait, and not on one
29244    /// that could run (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4430).
29245    #[test]
29246    fn a_child_wait_settles_without_happens_before_on_a_paused_child() {
29247        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29248        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.is_none());
29249        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29250        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29251        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
29252        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
29253        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
29254        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
29255            parent,
29256            (
29257                DetPid::from_raw(3),
29258                ChildWaitSpec {
29259                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(5)),
29260                    owner: None,
29261                    exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
29262                },
29263            ),
29264        );
29265        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29266        // In rt_sigsuspend it runs the real call, which a host-timed signal
29267        // can end, so it is not stuck.
29268        scheduler
29269            .blocked
29270            .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
29271            .insert(child, ExternalOpId::new(child, 1));
29272        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29273        scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.clear();
29274        scheduler
29275            .blocked
29276            .timed_waiters
29277            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
29278        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29279        assert!(
29280            scheduler
29281                .describe_terminal_waiters()
29282                .contains("thread(s) waiting for a child that cannot exit")
29283        );
29284        // A parent-death SIGKILL may still end it at a host-timed moment.
29285        scheduler
29286            .host_timed_signals
29287            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5), kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL));
29288        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29289        scheduler.host_timed_signals.clear();
29290        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29291        // On a backend that does not report every child, the wait may have
29292        // one Detcore does not know of.
29293        scheduler.complete_child_lineage = false;
29294        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29295        scheduler.complete_child_lineage = true;
29296        // A committed SIGKILL dooms it, so the wait will end.
29297        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
29298        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29299    }

29301    /// A parent-death signal follows Linux's `forget_original_parent`
29302    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440): a child's
29303    /// parent-death parent is the thread that created it; when that thread
29304    /// leaves while its process lives on, the child moves to the process's
29305    /// first live thread (leader first); when the whole process goes (an
29306    /// `exit_group` grant), to the reaper, here the container's init (none).
29307    /// A new task starts with no signal, a disarm clears it, and a reused tid
29308    /// does not keep the old task's.
29309    #[test]
29310    fn a_parent_death_parent_moves_as_linux_moves_real_parent() {
29311        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29312        let (leader, worker, child) = (
29313            DetTid::from_raw(3),
29314            DetTid::from_raw(4),
29315            DetTid::from_raw(5),
29316        );
29317        let process = DetPid::from_raw(3);
29318        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
29319        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
29320        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(worker, child, true);
29321        for tid in [leader, worker, child] {
29322            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
29323        }
29324        assert_eq!(
29325            scheduler
29326                .thread_tree
29327                .parent_death_parents
29328                .get(&DetPid::from_raw(5)),
29329            Some(&worker)
29330        );
29331        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(child), 0);
29332        scheduler.set_parent_death_signal(child, libc::SIGTERM);
29333        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(child), libc::SIGTERM);
29334        // The worker leaves; the leader lives on and becomes the parent.
29335        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_heir(worker, process), Some(leader));
29336        // A thread with a committed exit is leaving too, and is passed by.
29337        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(leader);
29338        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_heir(worker, process), None);
29339        scheduler.committed_exits.remove(&leader);
29340        // An exit_group grant ends the whole process: the reaper adopts.
29341        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(process);
29342        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_heir(worker, process), None);
29343        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.remove(&process);
29344        // An exec by the worker: it survives under the leader's tid, so the
29345        // child keeps its parent there, and the worker's own signal replaces
29346        // the destroyed leader's.
29347        scheduler.set_parent_death_signal(worker, libc::SIGUSR2);
29348        scheduler.set_parent_death_signal(leader, libc::SIGHUP);
29349        scheduler
29350            .thread_tree
29351            .transfer_exec_parent_death(worker, leader);
29352        assert_eq!(
29353            scheduler
29354                .thread_tree
29355                .parent_death_parents
29356                .get(&DetPid::from_raw(5)),
29357            Some(&leader)
29358        );
29359        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(leader), libc::SIGUSR2);
29360        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(worker), 0);
29361        // A disarm clears it; a reused tid starts with none.
29362        scheduler.set_parent_death_signal(child, 0);
29363        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(child), 0);
29364        scheduler.set_parent_death_signal(child, libc::SIGUSR1);
29365        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(worker, child, true);
29366        assert_eq!(scheduler.parent_death_signal(child), 0);
29367    }
