29369    /// A chain of child waits down to a held child is stuck: the root waits
29370    /// for its child, which waits for a grandchild held at a gate, and the
29371    /// root's ordinary wait does not hide the cycle below it (the Codex design
29372    /// re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929). A middle
29373    /// process that could still run, or a wait in the chain that matches no
29374    /// child, keeps the chain counted as input that may still arrive.
29375    #[test]
29376    fn a_chain_of_child_waits_down_to_a_held_child_settles() {
29377        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29378        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
29379        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29380        let middle = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29381        let leaf = DetTid::from_raw(7);
29382        let middle_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
29383        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
29384        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, middle, true);
29385        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, leaf, true);
29386        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle);
29387        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
29388        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
29389            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
29390            owner: None,
29391            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
29392        };
29393        scheduler
29394            .blocked
29395            .child_waiters
29396            .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
29397        scheduler
29398            .blocked
29399            .child_waiters
29400            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
29401        // The leaf runs: nothing is stuck.
29402        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29403        scheduler
29404            .happens_before
29405            .as_mut()
29406            .unwrap()
29407            .parked
29408            .insert(leaf);
29409        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29410
29411        // The middle process's wait matches no child: it may still end.
29412        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
29413            middle,
29414            (
29415                DetPid::from_raw(5),
29416                ChildWaitSpec {
29417                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
29418                    ..any
29419                },
29420            ),
29421        );
29422        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29423        scheduler
29424            .blocked
29425            .child_waiters
29426            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
29427        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29428
29429        // A second middle thread that could run keeps the root's wait open.
29430        scheduler
29431            .thread_tree
29432            .add_child(middle, middle_worker, false);
29433        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle_worker);
29434        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29435    }
29436
29437    /// A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is never stuck: the
29438    /// kernel kills it at a host-timed moment when its parent thread exits.
29439    /// The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the caller's turn
29440    /// (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` in `syscalls/misc.rs`). Another parent-death signal
29441    /// is held off a gated wait like any host-timed signal, so it does not
29442    /// change the answer (the second Claude re-check of
29443    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013).
29444    #[test]
29445    fn a_process_armed_with_a_parent_death_sigkill_is_not_stuck() {
29446        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
29447            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
29448            owner: None,
29449            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
29450        };
29451        // The held child, and the middle of a chain down to a held child.
29452        for armed in [5, 7] {
29453            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
29454            scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
29455            let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29456            let (child, leaf) = (DetTid::from_raw(5), DetTid::from_raw(7));
29457            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
29458            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, child, true);
29459            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
29460            scheduler
29461                .blocked
29462                .child_waiters
29463                .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
29464            let held = if armed == 7 {
29465                scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, leaf, true);
29466                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
29467                scheduler
29468                    .blocked
29469                    .child_waiters
29470                    .insert(child, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
29471                leaf
29472            } else {
29473                child
29474            };
29475            scheduler
29476                .happens_before
29477                .as_mut()
29478                .unwrap()
29479                .parked
29480                .insert(held);
29481            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29482            let doomed = if armed == 7 { child } else { held };
29483            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
29484                doomed,
29485                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
29486                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM),
29487            );
29488            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29489            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
29490                doomed,
29491                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
29492                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL),
29493            );
29494            assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_stuck_children());
29495        }
29496    }
29497
29498    /// The enforcement predicates that drive `hb_checkpoint`: an anchor is
29499    /// reached at exactly its `SyscallCount` on the right thread, an AFTER anchor
29500    /// of a Hard edge is blocked until its BEFORE anchor fires, and firing the
29501    /// BEFORE anchor opens the gate. This mirrors the two-thread race validated
29502    /// end-to-end (main_write < worker_write forcing A before B).
29503    #[test]
29504    fn hb_runtime_gate_opens_only_after_before_anchor_fires() {
29505        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
29506            r#"{
29507              "version": 1,
29508              "threads": { "main": {"dettid": 3}, "worker": {"dettid": 5} },
29509              "events": {
29510                "main_write":   {"thread": "main",   "syscalls": 47},
29511                "worker_write": {"thread": "worker", "syscalls": 8}
29512              },
29513              "edges": [ {"before": "main_write", "after": "worker_write", "strength": "hard"} ]
29514            }"#,
29515        );
29516        let main = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29517        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29518
29519        // Anchors resolve to the addressed (thread, count) and nothing else.
29520        assert_eq!(
29521            hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 47),
29522            vec!["main_write".to_string()]
29523        );
29524        assert_eq!(
29525            hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 8),
29526            vec!["worker_write".to_string()]
29527        );
29528        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 8).is_empty());
29529        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 47).is_empty());
29530        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 7).is_empty());
29531
29532        // Before its gating BEFORE anchor fires, the AFTER anchor is blocked and
29533        // the BEFORE anchor is free (it gates nothing).
29534        assert!(hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
29535        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("main_write"));
29536
29537        // Firing the BEFORE anchor opens the gate exactly once.
29538        assert!(hb.fired.insert("main_write".to_string()));
29539        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
29540    }
29541
29542    /// A soft edge never parks its AFTER thread, and `spawn_ordinal` addressing
29543    /// resolves against the observed spawn order (index 0 = root).
29544    #[test]
29545    fn hb_runtime_soft_edge_and_spawn_ordinal_resolution() {
29546        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
29547            r#"{
29548              "version": 1,
29549              "threads": {
29550                "root":  {"spawn_ordinal": 0},
29551                "child": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}
29552              },
29553              "events": {
29554                "a": {"thread": "root",  "syscalls": 3},
29555                "b": {"thread": "child", "syscalls": 4}
29556              },
29557              "edges": [ {"before": "a", "after": "b", "strength": "soft"} ]
29558            }"#,
29559        );
29560        // A soft edge biases but never hard-blocks, so its AFTER is never parked.
29561        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("b"));
29562
29563        // spawn_ordinal is unresolved until threads are observed at creation time.
29564        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
29565        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
29566        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3).is_empty());
29567        hb.note_spawn(root); // index 0 -> root
29568        hb.note_spawn(child); // index 1 -> first spawned child
29569        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3), vec!["a".to_string()]);
29570        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
29571        // note_spawn is idempotent, so a re-registration does not shift indices.
29572        hb.note_spawn(root);
29573        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
29574    }

29576    /// A thread with an emulated sleep filed as its request, the way
29577    /// `handle_pause` and `nanosleep` file one, parked in the timed waiters at
29578    /// its deadline unless `queued`, which leaves it on the run queue with the
29579    /// request not yet admitted.
29580    fn filed_sleep(
29581        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
29582        deadline: LogicalTime,
29583        fyi: &str,
29584        queued: bool,
29585    ) -> DetTid {
29586        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
29587        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
29588        let mut request = Resources::new(target);
29589        request.insert(ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline), Permission::W);
29590        request.fyi(fyi);
29591        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
29592        if queued {
29593            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
29594        } else {
29595            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, target);
29596        }
29597        target
29598    }
29599
29600    /// A sleeper's kernel signal state: `caught` handled, `ignored` set to
29601    /// `SIG_IGN`, the rest at their default action; `blocked` its mask and
29602    /// `pending` its pending set.
29603    fn sleeper_state(caught: u64, ignored: u64, blocked: u64, pending: u64) -> KernelSignalState {
29604        KernelSignalState {
29605            caught,
29606            ignored,
29607            blocked,
29608            pending,
29609            thread_pending: pending,
29610            ..Default::default()
29611        }
29612    }
29613
29614    fn set_sleeper_state(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid, state: KernelSignalState) {
29615        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(target, state);
29616    }
29617
29618    /// Records `signals` as sent to `target` in one sender turn, each made
29619    /// pending as the kernel queues it, then installs `at_drain` (if any) as the
29620    /// state the drain reads and drains.
29621    fn send_cross_task(
29622        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
29623        target: DetTid,
29624        signals: &[i32],
29625        at_drain: Option<KernelSignalState>,
29626    ) {
29627        for signal in signals {
29628            if let Some(state) = scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.get_mut(&target) {
29629                state.pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
29630                state.thread_pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
29631            }
29632            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(*signal));
29633        }
29634        if let Some(state) = at_drain {
29635            set_sleeper_state(scheduler, target, state);
29636        }
29637        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
29638        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
29639    }
29640
29641    fn assert_sleep_parked(
29642        scheduler: &Scheduler,
29643        target: DetTid,
29644        deadline: LogicalTime,
29645        case: &str,
29646    ) {
29647        assert_eq!(
29648            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
29649            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
29650            "{case}"
29651        );
29652        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
29653        assert!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target).is_some(), "{case}");
29654    }
29655
29656    fn assert_sleep_woken(scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid, signals: &[i32], case: &str) {
29657        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty(), "{case}");
29658        assert_eq!(
29659            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
29660            vec![target],
29661            "{case}"
29662        );
29663        assert_eq!(
29664            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
29665            signals
29666                .iter()
29667                .map(|signal| SigWrapper(*signal))
29668                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
29669            "{case}"
29670        );
29671        assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{case}");
29672    }

29674    /// A cross-task signal that is caught, or whose default action terminates
29675    /// the process, ends a `pause` parked in the timed waiters at
29676    /// `INDEFINITE`: the request becomes the signal set and the thread is
29677    /// queued, so its turn answers `Signaled`. Before the fix the signal was
29678    /// never recorded and the pause slept forever
29679    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
29680    #[test]
29681    fn a_caught_or_fatal_cross_task_signal_ends_a_parked_pause() {
29682        for (signal, caught) in [(libc::SIGUSR1, true), (libc::SIGTERM, false)] {
29683            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
29684            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
29685            let case = format!("signal {signal}, caught={caught}");
29686            assert_eq!(
29687                scheduler.signal_sleep(target),
29688                Some(SignalSleep::Pause),
29689                "{case}"
29690            );
29691            let caught_set = if caught { kernel_signal_bit(signal) } else { 0 };
29692            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught_set, 0, 0, 0));
29693            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
29694            assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[signal], &case);
29695        }
29696    }
29697
29698    /// A pause whose request is filed but still queued, not yet admitted to
29699    /// the timed waiters, is ended in place: it stays queued exactly once with
29700    /// the signal set as its request.
29701    #[test]
29702    fn a_cross_task_signal_ends_a_pause_still_on_the_run_queue() {
29703        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
29704        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, true);
29705        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
29706        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
29707        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], "queued pause");
29708    }

29710    /// `sigchld_family` with two children of the parent process, 200 and 201,
29711    /// whose notifications the child-exit ledger owns.
29712    fn owned_sigchld_family() -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid, [DetPid; 2]) {
29713        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
29714        let children = [200, 201].map(DetPid::from_raw);
29715        for child in children {
29716            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.exit_status.insert(
29717                child,
29718                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
29719                    code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
29720                    pid: child.as_raw(),
29721                    uid: 0,
29722                    status: 0,
29723                },
29724            );
29725            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
29726        }
29727        (scheduler, parent, creator, children)
29728    }

29730    /// The `ChildExit` timer of `child` sends its copy, as `signal_guest`
29731    /// records it in the send window.
29732    fn timer_sends(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) {
29733        assert_eq!(
29734            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
29735            Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send)
29736        );
29737        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(parent, Some(child));
29738    }
29739
29740    fn dequeue(
29741        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
29742        thread: DetTid,
29743        copy: child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy,
29744    ) -> child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer {
29745        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
29746            thread,
29747            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue { copy, admits: true },
29748        )
29749    }
29750
29751    fn delivers(child: DetPid) -> child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer {
29752        child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Deliver(
29753            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
29754                code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
29755                pid: child.as_raw(),
29756                uid: 0,
29757                status: 0,
29758            },
29759        ))
29760    }
29761
29762    /// The scheduler's copy for child 201 is sent while the kernel's late copy
29763    /// for child 200, already notified, is pending: Linux keeps the first
29764    /// copy's siginfo and does not queue the second, so the dequeue shows
29765    /// child 200's exit. It stands for child 201, with its siginfo, and is not
29766    /// dropped; classified by its siginfo it was dropped as child 200's
29767    /// duplicate, and child 201's notification was lost (the design check of
29768    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
29769    #[test]
29770    fn a_send_coalesced_into_a_pending_kernel_copy_is_delivered_for_its_own_child() {
29771        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
29772        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
29773        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
29774        assert_eq!(
29775            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
29776            delivers(first)
29777        );
29778        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
29779        assert_eq!(
29780            dequeue(
29781                &mut scheduler,
29782                creator,
29783                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
29784            ),
29785            delivers(second)
29786        );
29787        assert_eq!(
29788            dequeue(
29789                &mut scheduler,
29790                creator,
29791                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: second }
29792            ),
29793            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
29794            "child 201's own late kernel copy is the duplicate"
29795        );
29796    }
29797
29798    /// A kernel copy taken while another child's send is in the window does
29799    /// not stand for its own child when that child is not yet notified: its
29800    /// timer still sends its own copy, as it does when host timing posts the
29801    /// kernel copy after the send and it coalesces. A SIGKILL cohort's copy,
29802    /// which names a member host timing chooses, likewise. Retiring the named
29803    /// child made its timer send or not by host timing, and `--verify-strict`
29804    /// of `a_cross_process_sigkill_verifies_at_bitwise_parity` diverged.
29805    #[test]
29806    fn a_kernel_copy_in_the_window_leaves_an_unnotified_child_its_own_timer() {
29807        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
29808        let (_, _, _, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
29809        for (cohort, named) in [(false, second), (true, first), (true, second)] {
29810            let case = format!("cohort={cohort}, named {named}");
29811            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
29812            if cohort {
29813                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.join_cohort(first, 7);
29814                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.join_cohort(second, 7);
29815            }
29816            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
29817            assert_eq!(
29818                dequeue(
29819                    &mut scheduler,
29820                    creator,
29821                    DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: named }
29822                ),
29823                delivers(first),
29824                "{case}"
29825            );
29826            assert_eq!(
29827                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, second),
29828                Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send),
29829                "{case}"
29830            );
29831        }
29832    }

29834    /// A futex wait's question before it parks (`PrivatePending`) counts only
29835    /// a guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` the schedule recorded: not the
29836    /// scheduler's send in the window, which a sleep's question
29837    /// (`PlacedPending`) counts and a futex wait holds, and not a recorded copy
29838    /// when a host-timed source can post `SIGCHLD` to the process
29839    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
29840    #[test]
29841    fn a_futex_waits_question_counts_only_a_recorded_private_sigchld() {
29842        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
29843        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
29844        let (mut scheduler, parent, _, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
29845        let ask = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, control| {
29846            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, control)
29847        };
29848        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
29849        assert_eq!(
29850            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
29851            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
29852            "a sleep counts the window's send"
29853        );
29854        assert_eq!(
29855            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
29856            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
29857            "a futex wait does not"
29858        );
29859        ask(
29860            &mut scheduler,
29861            ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: parent },
29862        );
29863        assert_eq!(
29864            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
29865            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
29866            "a recorded private copy"
29867        );
29868        scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
29869            parent,
29870            HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
29871            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
29872        );
29873        assert_eq!(
29874            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
29875            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
29876            "a host-timed source can post SIGCHLD too"
29877        );
29878    }

29880    /// A claimed `SIGCHLD` (`ClaimedDelivery`) marks the claiming thread's
29881    /// delivery placed, so its turn is granted rather than deferred behind a
29882    /// runnable sibling: deferred, a sibling that yields until the handler runs
29883    /// held the handler back for ever (the Claude review of
29884    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4229's fix).
29885    #[test]
29886    fn a_claimed_sigchld_delivery_is_placed() {
29887        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
29888        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
29889        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
29890        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
29891        assert_eq!(
29892            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::ClaimedDelivery),
29893            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
29894        );
29895        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
29896    }
29897
29898    /// A signal sent to a thread whose `SIGCHLD` delivery is deferred
29899    /// (`sigchld_deferred`) re-admits that delivery, placed, with its request
29900    /// untouched: the kernel delivers the new signal after it, and a sibling
29901    /// that never stops running would hold both back for ever. Before, the
29902    /// thread was found in no pool, reported gone, and the send panicked.
29903    #[test]
29904    fn a_signal_to_a_thread_with_a_deferred_sigchld_delivery_readmits_it() {
29905        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
29906        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
29907        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
29908        let mut delivery = Resources::new(target);
29909        delivery.insert(
29910            ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)),
29911            Permission::RW,
29912        );
29913        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(delivery));
29914        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
29915        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
29916        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
29917        scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(target);
29918        // A runnable sibling keeps step 2e from re-admitting it.
29919        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
29920        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&target));
29921        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGALRM);
29922        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&target));
29923        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target));
29924        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
29925        assert_eq!(
29926            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
29927            vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)],
29928            "the deferred delivery's request is untouched"
29929        );
29930    }

29932    /// `WindowUnusable` answers whether the asking thread's process gave up
29933    /// the send window: false while every thread that could take its
29934    /// `SIGCHLD` does so at a committed point, true once one entered a blocking
29935    /// call outside the schedule with `SIGCHLD` unblocked, and false on a
29936    /// backend that does not model signal targets
29937    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4229).
29938    #[test]
29939    fn window_unusable_reports_an_outside_taker() {
29940        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
29941        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
29942        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
29943        let ask = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
29944            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::WindowUnusable)
29945        };
29946        assert_eq!(ask(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false));
29947        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(0), false);
29948        assert!(!scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent));
29949        assert_eq!(ask(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true));
29950        scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
29951        assert_eq!(ask(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false));
29952    }

29954    /// A background read by `thread` of descriptor `fd` in the table `thread`
29955    /// created (`Scheduler::background_reads`).
29956    fn background_read(
29957        op: ExternalOpId,
29958        thread: DetTid,
29959        fd: i32,
29960        signals: BackgroundReadSignals,
29961    ) -> BackgroundRead {
29962        BackgroundRead {
29963            op,
29964            files: detcore_model::fd::FilesId::initial(thread),
29965            fd,
29966            signals,
29967        }
29968    }
29969
29970    /// Under record and replay, `WindowUnusable` also says no while another
29971    /// thread of the process is outside the schedule in a call that could take
29972    /// its `SIGCHLD` (`outside_call_may_take_sigchld`): one sleeping with
29973    /// `SIGCHLD` unblocked or under an unknown mask, or a background read of a
29974    /// signalfd that reads `SIGCHLD` or whose signals are unknown, which they
29975    /// become when a `signalfd4` for `SIGCHLD` follows the read's start. A
29976    /// sibling that blocks `SIGCHLD` and reads a signalfd for other signals
29977    /// cannot, and run mode is unchanged
29978    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4343).
29979    #[test]
29980    fn window_unusable_waits_for_an_outside_call_that_may_take_sigchld() {
29981        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
29982        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
29983        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
29984        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
29985        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
29986        let ask = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
29987            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::WindowUnusable)
29988        };
29989        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
29990        scheduler.signalfd_masks.insert(parent, chld | usr2);
29991        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(parent, Some(chld | usr2), true);
29992        assert_eq!(ask(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true));
29993
29994        let op = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
29995        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(parent, op);
29996        scheduler
29997            .blocked
29998            .out_of_scheduler_masks
29999            .insert(parent, Some(chld | usr2));
30000        scheduler.background_reads.insert(
30001            parent,
30002            background_read(op, parent, 9, BackgroundReadSignals::Signalfd(usr2)),
30003        );
30004        assert_eq!(
30005            ask(&mut scheduler),
30006            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30007            "a sibling blocking SIGCHLD and reading a signalfd for SIGUSR2 only"
30008        );
30009        scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, usr2);
30010        assert_eq!(
30011            ask(&mut scheduler),
30012            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30013            "a signalfd4 for SIGUSR2 only, after the read began"
30014        );
30015        scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
30016        assert_eq!(
30017            ask(&mut scheduler),
30018            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30019            "a signalfd4 for SIGCHLD after the read began may have re-armed its descriptor"
30020        );
30021        for read in [
30022            BackgroundReadSignals::Signalfd(chld | usr2),
30023            BackgroundReadSignals::Unknown,
30024        ] {
30025            scheduler
30026                .background_reads
30027                .insert(parent, background_read(op, parent, 9, read));
30028            assert_eq!(
30029                ask(&mut scheduler),
30030                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30031                "a sibling reading a signalfd for {read:?}"
30032            );
30033        }
30034        scheduler.background_reads.insert(
30035            parent,
30036            background_read(
30037                ExternalOpId::new(parent, 6),
30038                parent,
30039                9,
30040                BackgroundReadSignals::Signalfd(chld),
30041            ),
30042        );
30043        assert_eq!(
30044            ask(&mut scheduler),
30045            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30046            "a signalfd read that has ended, the sibling now in another call"
30047        );
30048        scheduler.background_reads.remove(&parent);
30049        for mask in [Some(usr2), None] {
30050            scheduler
30051                .blocked
30052                .out_of_scheduler_masks
30053                .insert(parent, mask);
30054            assert_eq!(
30055                ask(&mut scheduler),
30056                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30057                "a sibling outside the schedule under mask {mask:?}"
30058            );
30059        }
30060        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = false;
30061        assert_eq!(
30062            ask(&mut scheduler),
30063            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30064            "run mode claims as before"
30065        );
30066    }
30067
30068    /// A background read is judged at its grant but enters the kernel later, so
30069    /// a later turn's `close`, `close_range`, `dup2` or `dup3` of its
30070    /// descriptor number may hand it another description, a signalfd for
30071    /// SIGCHLD among them: that read then counts as one that may take SIGCHLD
30072    /// (`note_descriptors_replaced`). Another number, or the same number in
30073    /// another descriptor table, leaves it alone. A read
30074    /// of a descriptor that was not a signalfd at its grant does not count
30075    /// until then (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4410).
30076    #[test]
30077    fn a_background_reads_descriptor_replaced_before_it_runs_may_take_sigchld() {
30078        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30079        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30080        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
30081        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
30082        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
30083        let ask = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
30084            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::WindowUnusable)
30085        };
30086        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
30087        scheduler.signalfd_masks.insert(parent, chld | usr2);
30088        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(parent, Some(chld | usr2), true);
30089        let op = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
30090        let table = detcore_model::fd::FilesId::initial(parent);
30091        let other_table = detcore_model::fd::FilesId::initial(creator);
30092        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(parent, op);
30093        scheduler
30094            .blocked
30095            .out_of_scheduler_masks
30096            .insert(parent, Some(chld | usr2));
30097        for (read, label) in [
30098            (BackgroundReadSignals::NotSignalfd, "a read of a pipe"),
30099            (
30100                BackgroundReadSignals::Signalfd(usr2),
30101                "a read of a signalfd for SIGUSR2 only",
30102            ),
30103        ] {
30104            scheduler
30105                .background_reads
30106                .insert(parent, background_read(op, parent, 9, read));
30107            assert_eq!(
30108                ask(&mut scheduler),
30109                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30110                "{label}"
30111            );
30112            scheduler.note_descriptors_replaced(table, 3, 8);
30113            scheduler.note_descriptors_replaced(table, 10, 10);
30114            scheduler.note_descriptors_replaced(other_table, 9, 9);
30115            assert_eq!(
30116                ask(&mut scheduler),
30117                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30118                "{label}, other descriptors, or the same number in another table, replaced"
30119            );
30120            scheduler.note_descriptors_replaced(table, 9, 9);
30121            assert_eq!(
30122                ask(&mut scheduler),
30123                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30124                "{label}, its descriptor replaced before the read runs"
30125            );
30126        }
30127        scheduler.background_reads.insert(
30128            parent,
30129            background_read(op, parent, 9, BackgroundReadSignals::NotSignalfd),
30130        );
30131        scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
30132        assert_eq!(
30133            ask(&mut scheduler),
30134            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
30135            "a signalfd4 cannot turn a read of a pipe into one of a signalfd"
30136        );
30137        scheduler.note_descriptors_replaced(table, 0, u32::MAX);
30138        assert_eq!(
30139            ask(&mut scheduler),
30140            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30141            "close_range over every descriptor"
30142        );
30143    }

30145    /// A thread a guest sent a thread-directed `SIGCHLD` takes that copy from
30146    /// its private queue first, whatever its siginfo says: it is delivered as
30147    /// it is and granted, and the send window and the ledger are left for the
30148    /// shared queue's copy. A flush and the thread's exit forget the record.
30149    #[test]
30150    fn a_private_sigchld_leaves_the_send_window_alone() {
30151        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30152        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30153        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30154        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30155        let private_sent = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid| {
30156            scheduler
30157                .child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target })
30158        };
30159        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30160        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
30161        assert_eq!(
30162            dequeue(
30163                &mut scheduler,
30164                creator,
30165                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
30166            ),
30167            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded,
30168            "a forged child-exit siginfo claims nothing"
30169        );
30170        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&creator));
30171        assert_eq!(
30172            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
30173            delivers(first),
30174            "the window is still the shared copy's"
30175        );
30176
30177        // A `tkill`/`tgkill` copy (`SI_TKILL`) consumes the record the same way.
30178        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30179        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
30180        assert_eq!(
30181            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Thread),
30182            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
30183        );
30184        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&creator));
30185        assert_eq!(
30186            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
30187            delivers(second)
30188        );
30189
30190        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
30191        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
30192        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
30193        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
30194        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&creator, &parent, MmId::initial(creator));
30195        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
30196    }

30198    /// A thread of the process outside the schedule takes the woken decision
30199    /// away from the send window only if it could take the copy: its recorded
30200    /// mask is unknown or leaves SIGCHLD unblocked, or its process holds a
30201    /// signalfd for SIGCHLD: the woken path then never ends the sleep for it.
30202    /// One whose recorded mask blocks it, such as a sibling in a
30203    /// `sigsuspend` that blocks SIGCHLD, does not (the Claude re-checks of
30204    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
30205    #[test]
30206    fn only_an_outside_thread_that_could_take_sigchld_holds_the_woken_decision() {
30207        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30208        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30209        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
30210        for (mask, signalfd, answer) in [
30211            (Some(chld), false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)),
30212            (Some(0), false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
30213            (None, false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
30214            (Some(chld), true, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
30215        ] {
30216            let case = format!("mask={mask:?}, signalfd={signalfd}");
30217            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30218            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30219            scheduler
30220                .blocked
30221                .external_io_blockers
30222                .insert(creator, ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1));
30223            scheduler
30224                .blocked
30225                .out_of_scheduler_masks
30226                .insert(creator, mask);
30227            if signalfd {
30228                scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
30229            }
30230            scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, mask, true);
30231            assert_eq!(
30232                scheduler
30233                    .child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
30234                answer,
30235                "{case}"
30236            );
30237        }
30238    }

30240    /// A guest's process-directed SIGCHLD joins the window in its sender's
30241    /// turn. Queued first, it keeps its siginfo, as Linux keeps the
30242    /// first-queued copy's; the child sent after it is still notified by that
30243    /// delivery, and its late kernel copy is dropped. Queued after a child's
30244    /// copy, the delivery carries the child's siginfo.
30245    #[test]
30246    fn a_guest_copy_queued_first_keeps_its_siginfo() {
30247        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30248        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30249        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30250        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30251        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30252            creator,
30253            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
30254        );
30255        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30256        assert_eq!(
30257            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Other),
30258            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Unowned)
30259        );
30260        assert_eq!(
30261            dequeue(
30262                &mut scheduler,
30263                parent,
30264                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
30265            ),
30266            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true)
30267        );
30268        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30269        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30270            creator,
30271            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
30272        );
30273        assert_eq!(
30274            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
30275            delivers(second)
30276        );
30277    }

30279    /// A parent-death SIGCHLD, sent by Detcore itself, queued before a
30280    /// child's timer copy keeps its siginfo, as Linux keeps the first-queued
30281    /// copy's: the one pending signal is delivered as it is, and the child is
30282    /// notified by it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4440). Any
30283    /// other scheduler copy that names no child (a timer's, an untracked
30284    /// child's) is delivered with the owned child's siginfo, as before
30285    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4482).
30286    #[test]
30287    fn a_scheduler_copy_queued_first_keeps_its_siginfo() {
30288        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30289        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30290        let (mut scheduler, parent, _, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30291        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_parent_death_send(parent);
30292        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30293        assert_eq!(
30294            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Other),
30295            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Unowned)
30296        );
30297        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(parent, None);
30298        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30299        assert_eq!(
30300            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Other),
30301            delivers(second)
30302        );
30303    }

30305    /// An `rt_sigtimedwait` that fails with EFAULT took a signal before its
30306    /// siginfo copy-out faulted if `SIGCHLD` is gone from the queue it would
30307    /// come from: the private record, which that queue serves first, or else
30308    /// the window. Still pending (a fault reading the inputs), nothing is
30309    /// taken (the Codex re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
30310    #[test]
30311    fn a_faulted_wait_takes_only_the_copy_gone_from_its_queue() {
30312        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30313        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30314        let faulted = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, private_pending: bool, shared_pending: bool| {
30315            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30316                creator,
30317                ChildExitSigchldControl::WaitFaulted {
30318                    private_pending,
30319                    shared_pending,
30320                },
30321            )
30322        };
30323        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30324        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30325            creator,
30326            ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: creator },
30327        );
30328        faulted(&mut scheduler, true, false);
30329        assert!(
30330            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator),
30331            "an input fault"
30332        );
30333        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, true);
30334        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
30335        assert!(
30336            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
30337            "the private queue went first"
30338        );
30339        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, true);
30340        assert!(
30341            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
30342            "still pending"
30343        );
30344        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, false);
30345        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
30346    }

30348    /// A guest's send records its copy before the physical send and undoes
30349    /// the record if the send fails: a new private record is removed (one
30350    /// that was already there, for a copy still pending, stays), and the
30351    /// shared send's window entry is dropped.
30352    #[test]
30353    fn a_failed_guest_send_undoes_its_record() {
30354        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30355        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30356        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
30357        let private = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
30358            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30359                parent,
30360                ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: creator },
30361            )
30362        };
30363        assert_eq!(
30364            private(&mut scheduler),
30365            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)
30366        );
30367        assert_eq!(
30368            private(&mut scheduler),
30369            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
30370            "coalesced"
30371        );
30372        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30373            parent,
30374            ChildExitSigchldControl::SendFailed {
30375                private: Some(creator),
30376                shared: None,
30377            },
30378        );
30379        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
30380
30381        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30382            creator,
30383            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
30384        );
30385        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
30386        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
30387            creator,
30388            ChildExitSigchldControl::SendFailed {
30389                private: None,
30390                shared: Some(parent),
30391            },
30392        );
30393        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
30394    }

30396    /// Two sends with no dequeue between them are one pending signal: one
30397    /// delivery stands for both children, and each one's later kernel copy is
30398    /// dropped, deterministically.
30399    #[test]
30400    fn two_sends_with_no_dequeue_between_are_one_delivery() {
30401        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30402        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30403        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30404        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30405        assert_eq!(
30406            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
30407            delivers(first)
30408        );
30409        for child in [second, first] {
30410            assert_eq!(
30411                dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child }),
30412                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
30413                "child {child}"
30414            );
30415        }
30416    }

30418    /// Setting `SIGCHLD` to `SIG_IGN` or `SIG_DFL` flushes the pending signal:
30419    /// the send window empties, a woken sleep no longer counts the copy, and
30420    /// the child's later kernel copy is dropped.
30421    #[test]
30422    fn a_flush_empties_the_send_window() {
30423        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30424        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30425        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30426        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30427        assert_eq!(
30428            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
30429            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)
30430        );
30431        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
30432        assert_eq!(
30433            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
30434            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
30435        );
30436        assert_eq!(
30437            dequeue(
30438                &mut scheduler,
30439                creator,
30440                child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
30441            ),
30442            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true)
30443        );
30444    }

30446    /// The `ChildExit` timer commits a deferred delivery as its child's
30447    /// notification only if the ledger did not match that delivery to another
30448    /// child's exit.
30449    #[test]
30450    fn the_timer_lets_only_an_unattributed_deferred_delivery_stand_in() {
30451        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _children) = owned_sigchld_family();
30452        scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(creator);
30453        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.insert(creator);
30454        assert_eq!(scheduler.deferred_child_exit_sigchld(parent, creator), None);
30455        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.remove(&creator);
30456        assert_eq!(
30457            scheduler.deferred_child_exit_sigchld(parent, creator),
30458            Some(creator)

30462    /// A delivery of a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sent is admitted by a mark for
30463    /// the very thread whose dequeue took it. In the two-child order a
30464    /// sibling's delivery of the first copy and the sleeper's of the second are
30465    /// each granted although another thread is runnable; before, both shared
30466    /// one mark for the process, and the second was deferred forever (the
30467    /// Claude re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131). A
30468    /// dequeue with no send in the window marks nothing, and a woken sleep is
30469    /// told no copy is pending while a thread of the process is in a call
30470    /// outside the schedule, which could take it at host time.
30471    #[test]
30472    fn each_scheduler_sigchld_copy_admits_only_the_thread_that_took_it() {
30473        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30474        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
30475        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30476        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30477        let placed = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
30478            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending)
30479        };
30480        let admitted = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid| {
30481            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
30482            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
30483            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(thread), Some(thread));
30484            let admitted = scheduler
30485                .block_for_one_resource(
30486                    thread,
30487                    &ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)),
30488                    &Permission::W,
30489                    None,
30490                    None,
30491                    &Ivar::new(),
30492                )
30493                .is_ok();
30494            if scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress() {
30495                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
30496            }
30497            scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(parent);
30498            scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator);
30499            scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.clear();
30500            admitted
30501        };
30502        assert_eq!(
30503            placed(&mut scheduler),
30504            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
30505        );
30506        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30507        assert_eq!(placed(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true));
30508        dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler);
30509        assert_eq!(
30510            placed(&mut scheduler),
30511            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
30512        );
30513        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30514        dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler);
30515        assert!(admitted(&mut scheduler, parent), "the leader's copy 1");
30516        assert!(admitted(&mut scheduler, creator), "the creator's copy 2");
30517        dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Other);
30518        assert!(
30519            !admitted(&mut scheduler, creator),
30520            "no send was in the window"
30521        );
30522
30523        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(parent, None);
30524        scheduler
30525            .blocked
30526            .external_io_blockers
30527            .insert(parent, ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1));
30528        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(parent, None, true);
30529        assert_eq!(
30530            placed(&mut scheduler),
30531            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
30532        );
30533    }
30534
30535    /// A process a thread of which could take SIGCHLD outside the schedule
30536    /// does not attribute it through the send window: one a thread of which
30537    /// was granted a blocking I/O call while the process held a signalfd for
30538    /// SIGCHLD, or a blocking call that leaves SIGCHLD unblocked. A send recorded before is
30539    /// forgotten at the next dequeue, which the siginfo decides as before the
30540    /// window: the kernel's late copy of a notified child is its duplicate,
30541    /// not a send it absorbed. Through the window, an outside reader's
30542    /// dequeue, reported after it rejoined, took a send it never held, and one
30543    /// SIGCHLD was delivered twice (the Claude re-check of
30544    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131 at f37277ef).
30545    #[test]
30546    fn a_process_that_could_take_sigchld_outside_the_schedule_does_not_use_the_window() {
30547        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
30548        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
30549        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
30550        for outside in ["signalfd", "blocker"] {
30551            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
30552            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
30553            assert_eq!(
30554                dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
30555                delivers(first),
30556                "{outside}"
30557            );
30558            assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent), "{outside}");
30559            match outside {
30560                "signalfd" => {
30561                    scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
30562                    assert!(
30563                        scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent),
30564                        "an unread signalfd"
30565                    );
30566                    scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), true);
30567                }
30568                _ => scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(0), true),
30569            }
30570            assert!(!scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent), "{outside}");
30571            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
30572            assert_eq!(
30573                dequeue(
30574                    &mut scheduler,
30575                    creator,
30576                    DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
30577                ),
30578                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
30579                "{outside}: the siginfo decides"
30580            );
30581            assert!(
30582                !scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
30583                "{outside}"
30584            );
30585            assert!(
30586                !scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator),
30587                "{outside}: no mark for the taker"
30588            );
30589        }
30590        // A blocker whose mask blocks SIGCHLD cannot take it, nor can a
30591        // `sigsuspend` with such a mask read the process's signalfd.
30592        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
30593        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), true);
30594        assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent));
30595        scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
30596        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), false);
30597        assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent));
30598    }
30599
30600    /// A signal the scheduler sends itself (a child exit's `SIGCHLD`, a timer's
30601    /// `SIGALRM`) to a thread whose `pause` or `nanosleep` request is filed but
30602    /// still queued, not yet parked, ends it in place: its request becomes the
30603    /// signal and it is requeued at the front of its band, ahead of a sibling
30604    /// already queued, so it is the next to resume and dequeue the signal. That
30605    /// turn is granted at once (`woken_sleeps`). Its `SIGCHLD` delivery is
30606    /// placed (`sigchld_ready`, which a mark the child-exit timer set survives
30607    /// too) and it is a `sigchld_takers` thread, resumed first, as a woken
30608    /// futex waiter is (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333). Its own
30609    /// turn then decides whether the signal ends the call (`sleep_signal`).
30610    /// Before, the queued sleep was left alone, and a pause parked with the
30611    /// signal gone by, a false deadlock
30612    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126). Left alone: a queued
30613    /// sleep where the backend does not report the guest's signal state
30614    /// (`models_signal_targets` unset), and a `nanosleep` whose deadline has
30615    /// passed, which completes at its admission.
30616    #[test]
30617    fn a_scheduler_signal_ends_a_sleep_still_on_the_run_queue() {
30618        let future = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
30619        for (models_signal_targets, deadline, fyi, delivery_placed, woken) in [
30620            (true, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false, true),
30621            (true, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, true, true),
30622            (true, future, NANOSLEEP_FYI, true, true),
30623            (false, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false, false),
30624            (
30625                true,
30626                LogicalTime::from_nanos(0),
30627                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
30628                false,
30629                false,
30630            ),
30631        ] {
30632            let case = format!(
30633                "{fyi} until {deadline:?}, models_signal_targets={models_signal_targets}, \
30634                 delivery_placed={delivery_placed}"
30635            );
30636            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30637            scheduler.models_signal_targets = models_signal_targets;
30638            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, true);
30639            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
30640                target,
30641                sleeper_state(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0, 0, 0),
30642            );
30643            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
30644            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
30645            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
30646            if delivery_placed {
30647                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(target);
30648            }
30649            // The send, as `send_guest_signal` makes it: its copy is committed
30650            // to the shared queue (the send window).
30651            assert!(scheduler.note_group_send(target, Signal::SIGCHLD, false));
30652            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
30653            assert_eq!(
30654                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
30655                vec![target, sibling],
30656                "{case}"
30657            );
30658            assert_eq!(
30659                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
30660                delivery_placed || woken,
30661                "{case}"
30662            );
30663            assert_eq!(
30664                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target),
30665                woken,
30666                "{case}"
30667            );
30668            if woken {
30669                assert_eq!(
30670                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
30671                    vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)],
30672                    "{case}"
30673                );
30674                assert!(scheduler.blocked.woken_sleeps.contains(&target), "{case}");
30675            } else {
30676                assert_eq!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target), vec![], "{case}");
30677                assert!(!scheduler.blocked.woken_sleeps.contains(&target), "{case}");
30678            }
30679        }
30680    }
30681
30682    /// A parked `pause` or `nanosleep` that the scheduler's own `SIGCHLD` wakes,
30683    /// caught and unblocked, with its copy committed to the sleeper by the
30684    /// schedule, is resumed first, ahead of a sibling in a higher band, so it is
30685    /// the thread that takes the process-directed copy. Before, it was requeued
30686    /// at the back of its band and unmarked: the sibling resumed first and took
30687    /// the copy, and a `pause` that then found no signal for itself never
30688    /// returned (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4333). So is one
30689    /// woken for a host-timed `SIGCHLD`, which its own turn ends on the wake.
30690    ///
30691    /// Its delivery is placed only when the copy is committed to it: one woken
30692    /// for a host-timed `SIGCHLD` with no committed copy is a taker but keeps
30693    /// no `sigchld_ready` mark, since a thread outside the schedule may take
30694    /// that copy and leave no delivery to consume it. With a committed copy it
30695    /// is placed whether or not `SIGCHLD` is also host-timed.
30696    ///
30697    /// Every case wakes the sleep to the front of its band, ahead of a peer
30698    /// queued earlier there, but these make it no taker and leave no mark,
30699    /// because the sleep's own turn does not end for them and parks it again
30700    /// (the Codex reviews of 4333): a `SIGALRM`; a `SIGCHLD` its mask blocks,
30701    /// or one left at its default action, which ignores it; and a `SIGCHLD`
30702    /// with no committed copy, whether the process's send window is unusable
30703    /// (a thread could take it outside the schedule) or no send entered it.
30704    /// Where the window is unusable the sleep's own turn may still claim the
30705    /// copy (`syscalls::signal::claim_pending_sigchld`), which places its
30706    /// delivery itself rather than through this mark.
30707    #[test]
30708    fn a_scheduler_sigchld_resumes_a_parked_sleep_first() {
30709        #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
30710        enum Copy {
30711            /// A group send noted in a usable send window.
30712            Committed,
30713            /// A group send while a thread could take SIGCHLD outside the
30714            /// schedule: the window is unusable.
30715            Unusable,
30716            /// No send entered the window.
30717            Uncommitted,
30718            /// No send entered the window, but SIGCHLD is host-timed for the
30719            /// sleeper.
30720            HostTimed,
30721            /// SIGCHLD is host-timed for the sleeper, and a group send came
30722            /// while the window is unusable: no copy is committed.
30723            HostTimedUnusable,
30724            /// SIGCHLD is host-timed for the sleeper, and a group send was
30725            /// noted in a usable window: the copy is committed.
30726            HostTimedCommitted,
30727        }
30728        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
30729        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
30730        let pause = (PAUSE_FYI, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE);
30731        let nanosleep = (NANOSLEEP_FYI, LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000_000_000));
30732        for ((fyi, deadline), signal, state, copy, takes) in [
30733            (
30734                pause,
30735                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30736                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30737                Copy::Committed,
30738                true,
30739            ),
30740            (
30741                nanosleep,
30742                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30743                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30744                Copy::Committed,
30745                true,
30746            ),
30747            (
30748                pause,
30749                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30750                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30751                Copy::HostTimed,
30752                true,
30753            ),
30754            (
30755                nanosleep,
30756                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30757                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30758                Copy::HostTimedUnusable,
30759                true,
30760            ),
30761            (
30762                pause,
30763                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30764                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30765                Copy::HostTimedCommitted,
30766                true,
30767            ),
30768            (
30769                pause,
30770                Signal::SIGALRM,
30771                sleeper_state(alrm, 0, 0, 0),
30772                Copy::Uncommitted,
30773                false,
30774            ),
30775            (
30776                pause,
30777                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30778                sleeper_state(chld, 0, chld, 0),
30779                Copy::Committed,
30780                false,
30781            ),
30782            (
30783                pause,
30784                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30785                sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0),
30786                Copy::Committed,
30787                false,
30788            ),
30789            (
30790                pause,
30791                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30792                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30793                Copy::Unusable,
30794                false,
30795            ),
30796            (
30797                pause,
30798                Signal::SIGCHLD,
30799                sleeper_state(chld, 0, 0, 0),
30800                Copy::Uncommitted,
30801                false,
30802            ),
30803        ] {
30804            let case = format!(
30805                "{fyi} woken by {signal:?}, caught {:#x} blocked {:#x}, {copy:?}",
30806                state.caught, state.blocked
30807            );
30808            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30809            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
30810            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(target, state);
30811            match copy {
30812                Copy::Committed => {
30813                    assert!(scheduler.note_group_send(target, signal, false), "{case}");
30814                }
30815                Copy::Unusable => {
30816                    scheduler.note_outside_blocker(target, Some(0), false);
30817                    assert!(scheduler.note_group_send(target, signal, false), "{case}");
30818                }
30819                Copy::Uncommitted => {}
30820                Copy::HostTimed => {
30821                    scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
30822                }
30823                Copy::HostTimedUnusable => {
30824                    scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
30825                    scheduler.note_outside_blocker(target, Some(0), false);
30826                    assert!(scheduler.note_group_send(target, signal, false), "{case}");
30827                }
30828                Copy::HostTimedCommitted => {
30829                    scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
30830                    assert!(scheduler.note_group_send(target, signal, false), "{case}");
30831                }
30832            }
30833            // A sibling queued earlier in the sleeper's own band, which the
30834            // wake must not follow, and one in a higher band.
30835            let peer = DetTid::from_raw(102);
30836            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, peer);
30837            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(peer);
30838            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
30839            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
30840            scheduler
30841                .priorities
30842                .insert(sibling, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
30843            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
30844            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, signal);
30845            assert_eq!(
30846                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
30847                vec![SigWrapper::from(signal)],
30848                "{case}"
30849            );
30850            assert!(scheduler.blocked.woken_sleeps.contains(&target), "{case}");
30851            let band: Vec<DetTid> = scheduler
30852                .run_queue
30853                .tids()
30854                .copied()
30855                .filter(|tid| *tid != sibling)
30856                .collect();
30857            assert_eq!(band, vec![target, peer], "{case}: front of its band");
30858            assert_eq!(
30859                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target),
30860                takes,
30861                "{case}"
30862            );
30863            // Placed only for a committed copy: a host-timed one with no
30864            // committed copy may be taken outside the schedule, leaving no
30865            // delivery to consume the mark.
30866            assert_eq!(
30867                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
30868                takes && matches!(copy, Copy::Committed | Copy::HostTimedCommitted),
30869                "{case}"
30870            );
30871            let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
30872            assert_eq!(selected, if takes { target } else { sibling }, "{case}");
30873            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
30874        }
30875    }

30877    /// Signals a pause does not return for leave it parked: one its mask
30878    /// blocks, one set to `SIG_IGN`, and `SIGWINCH` and `SIGCONT` with their
30879    /// default action, which ignores them. In a batch with one that does end
30880    /// it, only that one is delivered as the wake's signal set.
30881    #[test]
30882    fn a_blocked_or_ignored_cross_task_signal_leaves_a_pause_parked() {
30883        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30884        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
30885        let state = sleeper_state(
30886            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
30887            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
30888            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGHUP),
30889            0,
30890        );
30891        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, state);
30892        let quiet = [libc::SIGHUP, libc::SIGUSR2, libc::SIGWINCH, libc::SIGCONT];
30893        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &quiet, None);
30894        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "quiet signals");
30895
30896        let mut batch = quiet.to_vec();
30897        batch.push(libc::SIGUSR1);
30898        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &batch, None);
30899        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "batch with SIGUSR1");
30900    }

30902    /// A signal recorded in the sender's turn but no longer pending at the
30903    /// drain does not end the sleep: a caught `SIGTSTP` that the same turn's
30904    /// `SIGCONT` cancelled, or a `SIGUSR1` flushed when its disposition became
30905    /// `SIG_IGN` and then a handler again. Linux would leave the sleep asleep.
30906    #[test]
30907    fn a_cross_task_signal_withdrawn_before_the_drain_leaves_the_sleep_parked() {
30908        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
30909        for (fyi, deadline) in [
30910            (PAUSE_FYI, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
30911            (NANOSLEEP_FYI, deadline),
30912        ] {
30913            let caught = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
30914            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30915            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
30916            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0));
30917            send_cross_task(
30918                &mut scheduler,
30919                target,
30920                &[libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGCONT],
30921                Some(sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0)),
30922            );
30923            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, deadline, fyi);
30924        }
30925    }

30927    /// A signal that is unblocked and ignored when it is sent is discarded by
30928    /// Linux at generation, so a handler installed later in the sender's turn
30929    /// does not make it end the sleep, although ptrace left it pending.
30930    #[test]
30931    fn a_signal_ignored_when_sent_never_ends_the_sleep() {
30932        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
30933        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30934        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
30935        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, 0, 0));
30936        send_cross_task(
30937            &mut scheduler,
30938            target,
30939            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
30940            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
30941        );
30942        assert_sleep_parked(
30943            &scheduler,
30944            target,
30945            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
30946            "ignored when sent",
30947        );
30948
30949        // Blocked when sent, it is kept pending and does end the sleep once it
30950        // is caught and unblocked, as Linux delivers it.
30951        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30952        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
30953        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, usr1, 0));
30954        send_cross_task(
30955            &mut scheduler,
30956            target,
30957            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
30958            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
30959        );
30960        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "blocked when sent");
30961    }
