30963    /// The signals a gated wait holds are never recorded for a sleep, although
30964    /// caught and pending, unless a guest's thread-directed copy of `SIGCHLD`
30965    /// is recorded (below): `SIGCHLD`, and a signal a host-timed source armed by
30966    /// the guest can post to its process, as for a parked futex waiter. The
30967    /// kernel can post either at a host-chosen moment, so neither the pending
30968    /// bit nor the recorded send could tell whether a later guest call, a
30969    /// `sigaction(SIG_IGN)` or a `SIGCONT`, took the guest's copy back.
30970    #[test]
30971    fn a_held_signal_never_ends_the_sleep() {
30972        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
30973        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
30974        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
30975        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
30976        scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr2);
30977        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(chld | usr2, 0, 0, 0));
30978        for signal in [libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2] {
30979            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(signal));
30980            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{signal}");
30981        }
30982        send_cross_task(
30983            &mut scheduler,
30984            target,
30985            &[libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2],
30986            None,
30987        );
30988        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "held signals");
30989    }
30990
30991    /// A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD`, recorded in the sender's turn
30992    /// (`private_sent`), is in the sleeper's private queue, which only committed
30993    /// guest sends fill, so it is not held: caught and unblocked, it ends the
30994    /// sleep. It stays held where a host-timed source can post `SIGCHLD` to the
30995    /// sleeper's process, and a default-ignored one, or a caught one the
30996    /// sleeper's mask blocks, never ends it
30997    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
30998    #[test]
30999    fn a_guests_thread_directed_sigchld_ends_the_sleep() {
31000        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
31001        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
31002        for (caught, blocked, host_timed, woken) in [
31003            (chld, 0, false, true),
31004            (chld, 0, true, false),
31005            (0, 0, false, false),
31006            (chld, chld, false, false),
31007        ] {
31008            let case = format!("caught={caught:#x}, blocked={blocked:#x}, host_timed={host_timed}");
31009            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31010            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
31011            if host_timed {
31012                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
31013            }
31014            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught, 0, blocked, 0));
31015            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
31016                target,
31017                ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
31018            );
31019            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGCHLD], None);
31020            if woken {
31021                assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGCHLD], &case);
31022            } else {
31023                assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, &case);
31024            }
31025        }
31026    }

31028    /// A state the drain cannot read never invents an interruption: a thread
31029    /// that is gone is left to its retirement, and a live one ends the run with
31030    /// a diagnostic.
31031    #[test]
31032    fn an_unreadable_sleeper_state_never_wakes_the_sleep() {
31033        for failure in [
31034            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
31035            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Unreadable(reverie::Errno::EMFILE),
31036        ] {
31037            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31038            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
31039            scheduler.test_sleeper_read_failures.insert(target, failure);
31040            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
31041            let case = format!("{failure:?}");
31042            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, &case);
31043            assert_eq!(
31044                scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_some(),
31045                failure != sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
31046                "{case}"
31047            );
31048        }
31049    }

31051    /// A default stop ends a pause, which Linux then restarts once the process
31052    /// continues (`Detcore::handle_pause` returns `ERESTARTNOHAND`), but never a
31053    /// `nanosleep`, whose restart would have to keep its deadline: the stop
31054    /// takes effect when the sleep ends. A caught or fatal signal ends both.
31055    #[test]
31056    fn a_default_stop_ends_a_pause_but_not_a_nanosleep() {
31057        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
31058        for signal in [libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGSTOP] {
31059            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31060            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
31061            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
31062            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
31063            assert_sleep_woken(
31064                &scheduler,
31065                target,
31066                &[signal],
31067                &format!("pause, signal {signal}"),
31068            );
31069
31070            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31071            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
31072            assert_eq!(
31073                scheduler.signal_sleep(target),
31074                Some(SignalSleep::Nanosleep { deadline })
31075            );
31076            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
31077            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
31078            assert_sleep_parked(
31079                &scheduler,
31080                target,
31081                deadline,
31082                &format!("nanosleep, signal {signal}"),
31083            );
31084        }
31085        for (signal, caught) in [(libc::SIGUSR1, true), (libc::SIGTERM, false)] {
31086            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31087            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
31088            let caught_set = if caught { kernel_signal_bit(signal) } else { 0 };
31089            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught_set, 0, 0, 0));
31090            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
31091            assert_sleep_woken(
31092                &scheduler,
31093                target,
31094                &[signal],
31095                &format!("nanosleep, signal {signal}"),
31096            );
31097        }
31098    }

31100    /// A signal drained once a `nanosleep`'s deadline has passed leaves the
31101    /// sleep to complete normally at its timed pop, as Linux completes a sleep
31102    /// whose timer has fired; the signal is delivered as the call returns.
31103    #[test]
31104    fn a_cross_task_signal_after_a_nanosleep_deadline_leaves_it_to_complete() {
31105        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
31106        for committed in [deadline, deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1)] {
31107            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31108            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI, false);
31109            scheduler.committed_time = committed;
31110            let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
31111            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, 0));
31112            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], None);
31113            assert_sleep_parked(
31114                &scheduler,
31115                target,
31116                deadline,
31117                &format!("committed {committed}"),
31118            );
31119        }
31120    }

31122    /// What is not recorded at all: a `SIGKILL`, which the kernel acts on for
31123    /// a traced thread without the thread running, as before; a sleep request
31124    /// that is neither a tagged `pause` nor a tagged `nanosleep`; and any sleep
31125    /// on a backend that does not report the guest's signal state, which keeps
31126    /// its previous behavior.
31127    #[test]
31128    fn sleeps_that_cross_task_signals_do_not_reach() {
31129        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31130        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
31131        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGKILL));
31132        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "SIGKILL");
31133
31134        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
31135        for (deadline, fyi) in [
31136            (deadline, ""),
31137            (deadline, PAUSE_FYI),
31138            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, ""),
31139        ] {
31140            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
31141            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
31142            assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{deadline} {fyi:?}");
31143            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGTERM));
31144            assert!(
31145                scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(),
31146                "{deadline} {fyi:?}"
31147            );
31148        }
31149
31150        for (deadline, fyi) in [
31151            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
31152            (deadline, NANOSLEEP_FYI),
31153        ] {
31154            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(
31155                &Config {
31156                    sequentialize_threads: true,
31157                    ..Config::default()
31158                }
31159                .with_backend(|backend| backend.supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption = false),
31160            );
31161            assert!(!scheduler.models_signal_targets);
31162            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
31163            assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{fyi}");
31164            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(libc::SIGTERM));
31165            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{fyi}");
31166        }
31167    }

31169    #[test]
31170    fn backoff_sleep_doubles_each_round_then_caps() {
31171        let got: Vec<u64> = (1..=15).map(backoff_sleep_micros).collect();
31172        assert_eq!(
31173            got,

31179    /// File the exact owner-turn snapshot without registering a real host PID.
31180    fn in_guest_alarm_sleep(
31181        deadline: LogicalTime,
31182        fyi: &str,
31183        snapshot: crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm,
31184        queued: bool,
31185    ) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, Resources) {
31186        let config = Config {
31187            sequentialize_threads: true,
31188            ..Config::default()
31189        }
31190        .with_backend(|backend| *backend = BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST);
31191        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
31192        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, queued);
31193        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(target, target, true);
31194        scheduler
31195            .exec_incarnations
31196            .insert(target, MmId::initial(target));
31197        let mut request = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
31198            .req
31199            .try_read()
31200            .unwrap()
31201            .unwrap();
31202        request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm = Some(snapshot);
31203        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request.clone()));
31204        (scheduler, target, request)
31205    }
31206
31207    fn default_sleep_alarm_snapshot() -> crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm {
31208        crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm {
31209            disposition: crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Default,
31210            blocked: false,
31211        }
31212    }
31213
31214    /// An in-guest SIGALRM sleep is recognized from the backend's
31215    /// `virtualizes_guest_sigalrm` fact, not from its whole capability set
31216    /// being in-guest LiteInst's: any backend that keeps SIGALRM virtual has
31217    /// such sleeps, and one that does not, has none (audit step A9 of
31218    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4485).
31219    #[test]
31220    fn an_in_guest_sigalrm_sleep_follows_the_virtual_sigalrm_capability() {
31221        let (mut scheduler, target, original) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
31222            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
31223            PAUSE_FYI,
31224            default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
31225            false,
31226        );
31227        let mm = scheduler.exec_incarnations.get(&target).copied();
31228        assert!(scheduler.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(target).is_some());
31229        let mut virtual_ptrace = BackendCapabilities::PTRACE;
31230        virtual_ptrace.virtualizes_guest_sigalrm = true;
31231        scheduler.backend = virtual_ptrace;
31232        assert!(scheduler.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(target).is_some());
31233        let mut physical_liteinst = BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST;
31234        physical_liteinst.virtualizes_guest_sigalrm = false;
31235        scheduler.backend = physical_liteinst;
31236        assert!(scheduler.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(target).is_none());
31237        assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(target, target, mm, &original));
31238    }
31239
31240    /// Drive the real pop, diversion and typed grant boundaries directly,
31241    /// so an unexpected rejection cannot send a physical signal to a fake PID.
31242    /// Guest probes exercise the complete dispatcher against real targets.
31243    #[test]
31244    fn in_guest_one_shot_alarm_grants_fatal_sleep_without_host_send() {
31245        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
31246        for (deadline, fyi) in [
31247            (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
31248            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(20), NANOSLEEP_FYI),
31249        ] {
31250            for normal_due in [true, false] {
31251                let (mut scheduler, target, original) =
31252                    in_guest_alarm_sleep(deadline, fyi, default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(), false);
31253                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_alarm(
31254                    expiry,
31255                    target,
31256                    target,
31257                    Signal::SIGALRM,
31258                    LogicalTime::ZERO,
31259                );
31260                let (event_ns, TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, tid, signal)) =
31261                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.pop().unwrap()
31262                else {
31263                    panic!("the alarm must expire before its sleep");
31264                };
31265                assert_eq!(event_ns, expiry);
31266                assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_state(target), None);
31267                // Models empty-queue dispatch with committed_time still behind
31268                // the event, as well as the ordinary due-event path.
31269                scheduler.committed_time = if normal_due {
31270                    expiry
31271                } else {
31272                    LogicalTime::ZERO
31273                };
31274                let turn_before = scheduler.turn;
31275                let committed_before = scheduler.committed_time;
31276                let observed_now = if normal_due {
31277                    expiry
31278                } else {
31279                    expiry + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1)
31280                };
31281                assert!(scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31282                    event_ns,
31283                    id,
31284                    tid.tid(),
31285                    match signal {
31286                        timed_waiters::TimerSignal::Send(signal) => signal,
31287                        other => panic!("an alarm sends a deliverable signal, not {other}"),
31288                    },
31289                    observed_now
31290                ));
31291                assert_eq!(
31292                    scheduler.turn, turn_before,
31293                    "diversion is not an extra guest grant"
31294                );
31295                assert_eq!(scheduler.committed_time, committed_before);
31296                assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
31297                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
31298                assert_eq!(
31299                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
31300                    None
31301                );
31302                assert_eq!(
31303                    scheduler
31304                        .run_queue
31305                        .tids()
31306                        .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
31307                        .count(),
31308                    1
31309                );
31310
31311                // A later signal and even a direct generic substitution cannot
31312                // steal the typed response from the consumed alarm.
31313                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
31314                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
31315                let mut generic = Resources::new(target);
31316                generic.insert(
31317                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)),
31318                    Permission::W,
31319                );
31320                scheduler.force_unblock_thread(target, generic);
31321                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
31322                assert_eq!(
31323                    scheduler
31324                        .run_queue
31325                        .tids()
31326                        .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
31327                        .count(),
31328                    1
31329                );
31330
31331                let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
31332                assert!(scheduler.unblock_guest(target, &response).is_ok());
31333                assert_eq!(
31334                    scheduler.turn,
31335                    turn_before + 1,
31336                    "the fatal continuation consumes exactly one ordinary grant"
31337                );
31338                assert!(matches!(
31339                    response.try_read(),
31340                    Some(SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm)
31341                ));
31342                assert!(scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
31343                    target,
31344                    target,
31345                    Some(MmId::initial(target)),
31346                    &original,
31347                ));
31348                assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
31349                assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
31350            }
31351        }
31352    }

31354    #[test]
31355    fn in_guest_ignored_and_blocked_alarm_preserve_filed_or_parked_sleep() {
31356        use crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm;
31357        use crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition;
31358        for snapshot in [
31359            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
31360                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Ignored,
31361                blocked: false,
31362            },
31363            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
31364                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Default,
31365                blocked: true,
31366            },
31367            InGuestSleepSigalrm {
31368                disposition: SigalrmSleepDisposition::Handled,
31369                blocked: true,
31370            },
31371        ] {
31372            for (deadline, fyi) in [
31373                (LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI),
31374                (LogicalTime::from_nanos(20), NANOSLEEP_FYI),
31375            ] {
31376                for queued in [false, true] {
31377                    let (mut scheduler, target, _) =
31378                        in_guest_alarm_sleep(deadline, fyi, snapshot, queued);
31379                    assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31380                        LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
31381                        timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
31382                        target,
31383                        Signal::SIGALRM,
31384                        LogicalTime::ZERO
31385                    ));
31386                    // This method is the wake half after a successful physical
31387                    // send. Kernel pending semantics belong to the guest probes.
31388                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGALRM);
31389                    assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), queued);
31390                    assert_eq!(
31391                        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
31392                        (!queued).then_some(deadline)
31393                    );
31394                    assert_eq!(
31395                        scheduler.next_turns[&target]
31396                            .req
31397                            .try_read()
31398                            .unwrap()
31399                            .unwrap()
31400                            .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep(),
31401                        Some((snapshot, deadline))
31402                    );
31403                    assert!(!scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target));
31404                }
31405            }
31406        }
31407    }

31409    #[test]
31410    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_other_identities_and_rearmed_timers() {
31411        let (mut scheduler, target, _) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
31412            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
31413            PAUSE_FYI,
31414            default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
31415            false,
31416        );
31417        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
31418        for (id, signal) in [
31419            (
31420                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(target, 1),
31421                Signal::SIGALRM,
31422            ),
31423            (
31424                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit {
31425                    child: DetPid::from_raw(200),
31426                    parent: target,
31427                },
31428                Signal::SIGALRM,
31429            ),
31430            (
31431                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
31432                Signal::SIGALRM,
31433            ),
31434            (timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target), Signal::SIGUSR1),
31435        ] {
31436            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31437                expiry,
31438                id,
31439                target,
31440                signal,
31441                LogicalTime::ZERO
31442            ));
31443        }
31444        for interval in [LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::from_nanos(5)] {
31445            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_alarm(
31446                expiry,
31447                target,
31448                target,
31449                Signal::SIGALRM,
31450                interval,
31451            );
31452            if interval != LogicalTime::ZERO {
31453                assert!(matches!(
31454                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.pop(),
31455                    Some((_, TimedEvent::SignalEvt(..)))
31456                ));
31457            }
31458            assert!(
31459                scheduler
31460                    .blocked
31461                    .timed_waiters
31462                    .alarm_state(target)
31463                    .is_some(),
31464                "unconsumed one-shot or rearmed recurring identity"
31465            );
31466            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31467                expiry,
31468                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
31469                target,
31470                Signal::SIGALRM,
31471                LogicalTime::ZERO
31472            ));
31473        }
31474        assert_eq!(
31475            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
31476            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE)
31477        );
31478        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
31479    }

31481    #[test]
31482    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_unqualified_requests_and_states() {
31483        let expiry = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
31484        for case in 0..10 {
31485            let (mut scheduler, target, mut request) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
31486                LogicalTime::from_nanos(20),
31487                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
31488                default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
31489                false,
31490            );
31491            match case {
31492                0 => scheduler.backend = Config::default().backend,
31493                1 => request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm = None,
31494                2 => request.fyi = String::new(),
31495                3 => request.insert(ResourceID::TraceReplay, Permission::W),
31496                4 => {
31497                    scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
31498                }
31499                5 => scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(target),
31500                6 => {
31501                    scheduler
31502                        .thread_tree
31503                        .add_child(target, DetTid::from_raw(101), false);
31504                }
31505                7 => {
31506                    let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
31507                    hb.parked.insert(target);
31508                    scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
31509                }
31510                8 => {
31511                    scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(target);
31512                    scheduler
31513                        .blocked
31514                        .timed_waiters
31515                        .insert(LogicalTime::from_nanos(21), target);
31516                }
31517                9 => {
31518                    request.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm.as_mut().unwrap().disposition =
31519                        crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Handled;
31520                }
31521                _ => unreachable!(),
31522            }
31523            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
31524            assert!(
31525                !scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31526                    expiry,
31527                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
31528                    target,
31529                    Signal::SIGALRM,
31530                    LogicalTime::ZERO
31531                ),
31532                "case {case}"
31533            );
31534            assert!(
31535                !scheduler.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(target),
31536                "case {case}"
31537            );
31538        }
31539    }

31541    #[test]
31542    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_excludes_sleep_deadline_equality_and_already_ahead_time() {
31543        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(20);
31544        for (committed, event_ns, observed_now) in [
31545            (LogicalTime::ZERO, deadline, LogicalTime::ZERO),
31546            (
31547                LogicalTime::ZERO,
31548                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
31549                LogicalTime::ZERO,
31550            ),
31551            (deadline, LogicalTime::from_nanos(10), LogicalTime::ZERO),
31552            (
31553                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
31554                LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
31555                LogicalTime::ZERO,
31556            ),
31557            // A control hook crossed the sleep deadline while committed_time
31558            // and the popped event still lag. The clock must not rewind into
31559            // permission to interrupt a completed sleep.
31560            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::from_nanos(10), deadline),
31561            (
31562                LogicalTime::ZERO,
31563                LogicalTime::from_nanos(10),
31564                deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
31565            ),
31566        ] {
31567            let (mut scheduler, target, _) = in_guest_alarm_sleep(
31568                deadline,
31569                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
31570                default_sleep_alarm_snapshot(),
31571                false,
31572            );
31573            scheduler.committed_time = committed;
31574            assert!(!scheduler.divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
31575                event_ns,
31576                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(target),
31577                target,
31578                Signal::SIGALRM,
31579                observed_now
31580            ));
31581            assert_eq!(
31582                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(target),
31583                Some(deadline)
31584            );
31585            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
31586        }
31587    }

31646            target,
31647            target,

31651        scheduler.exec_incarnations.insert(target, mm);
31652        scheduler.parked.running = None;

31654            target,
31655            target,
31656            Some(mm),

31707#[cfg(test)]
31708mod poll_wake_tests {
31709    use super::*;
31710
31711    /// Where the record of copies discarded at send is kept, a standard signal
31712    /// wakes a poll at the drain if its mask leaves it unblocked, whatever the
31713    /// disposition is now (a sender's `SIG_IGN` in the same slice does not undo
31714    /// the wake Linux keeps; arm A1). A real-time signal keeps the disposition
31715    /// test (arm A11), and the backend's preemption signal never wakes it
31716    /// (R2b-1 rule 1, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4273).
31717    #[test]
31718    fn a_standard_signal_wakes_a_poll_by_its_mask_alone() {
31719        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
31720        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
31721        let rt = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGRTMIN());
31722        let perf = kernel_signal_bit(reverie::PERF_EVENT_SIGNAL as libc::c_int);
31723        let state = KernelSignalState {
31724            ignored: usr1 | rt,
31725            blocked: usr2,
31726            ..Default::default()
31727        };
31728        let wakes = poll_wake_signals(&state, true);
31729        assert_ne!(wakes & usr1, 0, "an ignored standard signal still wakes");
31730        assert_eq!(wakes & usr2, 0, "a blocked one does not");
31731        assert_eq!(wakes & rt, 0, "an ignored real-time one does not");
31732        assert_eq!(wakes & perf, 0, "the preemption signal never does");
31733        // Without the record, the disposition decides, as before.
31734        assert_eq!(poll_wake_signals(&state, false) & usr1, 0);
31735    }
31736}
